words.ex_cn: 洗手可以杀死病菌。
words.en: A germ is a very small organism that causes disease.

words.ex: Histology is the study of the microscopic structure of tissues.
words.ex_cn: 组织学是研究组织显微结构的一门学科。
words.en: Histology is the study of the microscopic structure of tissues.

words.ex: Hormones control growth and mood in the body.
words.ex_cn: 荷尔蒙控制身体的生长和情绪。
words.en: A hormone is a chemical substance produced in the body that controls and regulates the activity of certain cells or organs.

words.tr: adj. 无知觉的；无生命力的
words.ex: The statue remained insentient, unaffected by the passing years.
words.ex_cn: 雕像依旧无知觉，不受岁月流逝的影响。
words.en: Lacking consciousness or the ability to perceive.

words.ex: The latency period for this disease can be several years.
words.ex_cn: 这种疾病的潜伏期可以长达数年。
words.en: Latency refers to the state of being latent or the period of time that elapses between a stimulus and the response to it, especially in the context of diseases or computing.

words.ex: The cell has a thin membrane.
words.ex_cn: 细胞有一层薄薄的膜。
words.en: A membrane is a thin layer of tissue or material that covers or lines a part of the body, or separates one area from another.

words.ex: His metabolism is very fast.
words.ex_cn: 他的新陈代谢非常快。
words.en: Metabolism is the set of life-sustaining chemical transformations within the cells of living organisms.

words.ex: The microbe causes sickness.
words.ex_cn: 这种微生物会引起疾病。
words.en: A microbe is a very small living thing, which you can only see if you use a microscope. Some microbes can cause diseases.

words.ex: A microorganism can cause sickness.
words.ex_cn: 微生物会导致疾病。
words.en: A microorganism is a very small living thing that you can only see with a microscope.

words.ex: He looks at the bug through a microscope.
words.ex_cn: 他通过显微镜观察这只虫子。
words.en: An instrument used for viewing objects that are too small to be seen by the naked eye, especially one that uses a combination of lenses to produce a magnified image.

words.ex: The bread became moldy in the warm kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 面包在温暖的厨房里发霉了。
words.en: Something that is moldy is covered with mold.

words.ex: The virus can mutate quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒可以迅速变异。
words.en: If an animal or plant mutates, or something mutates it, it develops different characteristics as the result of a change in its genes.

words.tr: n. 生物体；有机体；有机组织；
words.ex: A bacterium is a simple organism.
words.ex_cn: 细菌是一种简单的生物体。
words.en: An organism is a living thing that has an organized structure, can react to stimuli, reproduce, grow, adapt, and maintain homeostasis.

words.ex: He loves paleontology and finds dinosaur bones.
words.ex_cn: 他热爱古生物学，寻找恐龙骨头。
words.en: The branch of science concerned with fossil animals and plants.

words.ex: Plants use sunlight for photosynthesis.
words.ex_cn: 植物利用阳光进行光合作用。
words.en: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants and some other organisms use sunlight to synthesize foods from carbon dioxide and water.

words.ex: His physiological response to stress is very strong.
words.ex_cn: 他对压力的生理反应非常强烈。
words.en: Physiological refers to the normal functions of living organisms and their parts, or to the branch of biology that deals with these functions.

words.ex: The virus can propagate quickly among people.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒可以在人群中迅速传播。
words.en: To propagate something means to spread it and encourage more people to believe in it or support it.

words.ex: The propagation of the rumor spread quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这个谣言的传播很快。
words.en: The act of spreading something, especially information or ideas, or the process by which plants or animals produce more of their own kind.

words.ex: The recessive gene is often masked by a dominant gene.
words.ex_cn: 隐性基因常常被显性基因所掩盖。
words.en: In genetics, a recessive gene is one that is expressed only when there is no dominant gene present.

words.ex: The synergic team worked well together.
words.ex_cn: 这个协作的团队合作得很好。
words.en: Involving interaction or cooperation between two or more organizations, substances, or other agents to produce a combined effect greater than the sum of their separate effects.

words.ex: The doctor examined the tissue under a microscope.
words.ex_cn: 医生在显微镜下检查了组织。
words.en: Tissue is a group of cells that have a similar structure and that work together to perform a specific function.

words.ex: The viral infection made him feverish for three days.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒引起的感染让他发烧了三天。
words.en: Relating to or caused by a virus; becoming very popular by circulating quickly from person to person, especially on the internet.

words.ex: The virus made many people sick.
words.ex_cn: 这个病毒让很多人病了。
words.en: A virus is a very small organism that causes infectious diseases in people, animals, and plants.

words.ex: Fish and birds are vertebrates.
words.ex_cn: 鱼和鸟是脊椎动物。
words.en: A vertebrate is an animal that has a spine or backbone.

words.ex: Anaerobic bacteria can live without oxygen.
words.ex_cn: 无氧细菌可以在没有氧气的情况下生存。
words.en: relating to or requiring an absence of free oxygen

words.ex: Interest will accrue over time.
words.ex_cn: 利息会随着时间积累。
words.en: If money or interest accrues, it gradually increases in amount over a period of time.

words.tr:
adj. 近似的；大约的；
v. 接近；
words.ex: The approximate cost is $50.
words.ex_cn: 费用大约是50美元。
words.en: An approximate number, time, or position is close to the correct number, time, or position, but is not exact.

words.ex: The company hired an expert to do an audit.
words.ex_cn: 公司聘请了一位专家进行审计。
words.en: An audit is an official examination of the accounts of a business or organization to check that they are accurate and correct.

words.ex: She works out to augment her strength.
words.ex_cn: 她锻炼以增强力量。
words.en: If you augment something, you make it larger, stronger, or more effective by adding something to it.

words.ex: An axiom is a fact that everyone accepts.
words.ex_cn: 公理是一个大家普遍接受的事实。
words.en: An axiom is a statement or proposition which is regarded as being established, accepted, or self-evidently true.

words.tr:
v. 促进；使增长；
n. 提高；增强；
words.ex: Exercise can boost your energy.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以促进你的精力。
words.en: If one thing boosts another, it causes it to increase, improve, or be more successful.

words.ex: The course covers a wide breadth of topics.
words.ex_cn: 这门课程涵盖了广泛的主题。
words.en: The distance or measurement from side to side of something; width.

words.tr:
n. 预算；预算金额；
adj. 廉价的；花钱少的；
v. 为 ... 做预算；
words.ex: We made a budget for our vacation.
words.ex_cn: 我们为旅行制定了一个预算。
words.en: A budget is a plan that shows how much money a person or organization will earn and how much they will need or be able to spend.

words.ex: The bulk of the students passed the exam.
words.ex_cn: 大部分学生通过了考试。
words.en: The bulk of something is most of it. The bulk of something is its size, especially when it is very large.

words.tr: n. 微积分学；（人体内的）结石
words.ex: He is learning calculus at school.
words.ex_cn: 他正在学校学习微积分。
words.en: Calculus is a branch of mathematics that deals with the finding and properties of derivatives and integrals of functions, by methods originally based on the summation of infinitesimal differences.

words.ex: The scientist calibrates the scale every morning.
words.ex_cn: 科学家每天早上标定秤。
words.en: To calibrate something means to mark or adjust it so that it can be used for measuring accurately.

words.ex: He used calipers to measure the small wire.
words.ex_cn: 他用卡尺测量那根细线。
words.en: Calipers are a device used to measure the distance between two opposite sides of an object.

words.ex: The government does a census every ten years.
words.ex_cn: 政府每十年进行一次人口普查。
words.en: A census is an official count or survey of a population, typically recording various details of individuals.

words.ex: The circumference of the circle is 31.4 cm.
words.ex_cn: 这个圆的周长是31.4厘米。
words.en: The circumference of a circle is the distance around it.

words.tr: n. 球果；松球；圆锥体；圆锥形物；
words.ex: The pine tree dropped a brown cone on the ground.
words.ex_cn: 松树掉下一个棕色的球果在地上。
words.en: A cone is a shape with a circular base that narrows to a point at the top.

words.tr:
adj. 对角线的；斜的
n. 对角线；斜线
words.ex: The square has two diagonal lines.
words.ex_cn: 这个正方形有两条对角线。
words.en: A diagonal line or movement goes in a sloping direction, for example, from one corner of a square across to the opposite corner.

words.ex: The teacher drew a diagram to explain the water cycle.
words.ex_cn: 老师画了一个图表来解释水循环。
words.en: A diagram is a simple drawing which consists mainly of lines and is used, for example, to explain how a machine works.

words.ex: The diameter of the circle is 10 cm.
words.ex_cn: 这个圆的直径是10厘米。
words.en: A straight line passing from side to side through the center of a body or figure, especially a circle or sphere.

words.tr: n. 从0到9的任一数字；手指；脚趾；
words.ex: The password has four digits.
words.ex_cn: 这个密码有四位数字。
words.en: A digit is a written symbol for any of the numbers 0 to 9.

words.ex: The dimension of the box is 10 cm by 5 cm.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子的尺寸是10厘米乘5厘米。
words.en: A dimension is a measurement of something in a particular direction, or the scope or scale of something.

words.ex: The diminution of water in the lake is obvious.
words.ex_cn: 湖中水量的减少是显而易见的。
words.en: A diminution of something is its reduction in size, importance, or intensity.

words.ex: The track is elliptical in shape.
words.ex_cn: 这个跑道是椭圆形的。
words.en: Something that is elliptical has the shape of an ellipse or is characterized by the omission of words that are understood to be obvious.

words.ex: The equation is easy to solve.
words.ex_cn: 这个方程式很容易解。
words.en: An equation is a mathematical statement that asserts the equality of two expressions.

words.tr: n. 阐述者；拥护者；代表者；指数
words.ex: He is the exponent of modern education reform.
words.ex_cn: 他是现代教育改革的阐述者。
words.en: An exponent is someone who supports and explains a particular idea, theory, or system, or a symbol that shows how many times a number is to be multiplied by itself.

words.ex: The population is growing exponentially.
words.ex_cn: 人口正在呈指数增长。
words.en: If something increases exponentially, it becomes larger at a faster and faster rate.

words.ex: The expression is factorable into two simple parts.
words.ex_cn: 这个表达式可以分解为两个简单的部分。
words.en: Capable of being factored, especially in mathematics, referring to expressions that can be broken down into products of simpler expressions.

words.ex: The company used a new formula to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 公司使用了一个新方案来解决问题。
words.en: A formula is a plan or method that is used to achieve a particular goal, especially in science or mathematics.

words.ex: The frequency of the radio station is 101.5 MHz.
words.ex_cn: 这个电台的频率是101.5兆赫。
words.en: The rate at which something happens or is repeated over a particular period of time.

words.ex: The bee built a hexagon with wax.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂用蜡建造了一个六边形。
words.en: A hexagon is a six-sided polygon.

words.ex: The hypotenuse is the longest side of a right triangle.
words.ex_cn: 斜边是直角三角形中最长的一条边。
words.en: The side opposite the right angle in a right-angled triangle.

words.ex: The temperature increases by one increment every hour.
words.ex_cn: 温度每小时增加一个单位。
words.en: An increment is an amount by which something increases or is increased.

words.tr: n. 指标；索引；指数；“index”的复数
words.ex: The company tracks key indices to measure performance.
words.ex_cn: 该公司追踪关键指标以衡量表现。
words.en: Indices are used to measure or indicate something, such as economic health or the performance of a stock market.

words.tr: adj. 不能减缩的；无法减轻的
words.ex: This fraction is irreducible.
words.ex_cn: 这个分数是最简形式。
words.en: If you describe something as irreducible, you mean that it cannot be made smaller or simpler.

words.ex: The bacteria multiply quickly.
words.ex_cn: 细菌迅速增加。
words.en: If you multiply one number by another, you add the first number to itself as many times as is indicated by the second number. For example, 2 multiplied by 3 is equal to 6.

words.ex: The ball follows a parabola when thrown.
words.ex_cn: 球被扔出时沿着抛物线运动。
words.en: A parabola is a symmetrical open plane curve formed by the intersection of a cone with a plane parallel to its side.

words.tr:
adj. 平行的；
n. 类似的事物；
words.ex: The two lines are parallel and never meet.
words.ex_cn: 这两条线是平行的，永远不会相交。
words.en: Something that is parallel to something else is similar to it in many ways, or happens at the same time as it.

words.ex: The teacher changed the parameter to make the test easier.
words.ex_cn: 老师更改了参数，使测试更容易。
words.en: A parameter is a limit or boundary which defines the scope of a particular process or activity.

words.ex: The new policy has a wide radius of influence.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策的影响范围很广。
words.en: A straight line from the center to the circumference of a circle or sphere.

words.ex: The box has a rectangle shape.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子是长方形的。
words.en: A rectangle is a four-sided flat shape where every interior angle is a right angle (90°). Opposite sides are parallel and of equal length.

words.ex: His comment was tangential to the main topic.
words.ex_cn: 他的评论离题了。
words.en: If you describe something as tangential, you mean that it has only a slight or indirect connection with the thing you are concerned with, and is therefore not worth considering seriously.

words.ex: The vertex of the triangle is at the top.
words.ex_cn: 三角形的顶点在顶部。
words.en: The highest point of something; the top or apex.

words.ex: The tree grows in a vertical line.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树垂直生长。
words.en: Something that is vertical stands or points straight up.

words.tr: n. 数字命理学；数字占卜术
words.ex: He believes in numerology and checks his lucky numbers every day.
words.ex_cn: 他相信数字命理学，每天都会查看自己的幸运数字。
words.en: Numerology is the study of the purported divine, mystical or other special relationships between a number and some coinciding observed (or perceived) events.

words.tr: n. 四边形；四方院子；方形庭院
words.ex: The garden is shaped like a quadrangle.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园呈四边形。
words.en: A quadrangle is a four-sided plane figure, especially a square or rectangle. In architecture, it refers to a square or rectangular courtyard enclosed by buildings.

words.ex: She accentuates the first syllable when she says the word.
words.ex_cn: 她说这个词时重读第一个音节。
words.en: To accentuate something means to emphasize it or make it more noticeable.

words.tr: n. 行话；暗号； 隐语
words.ex: The boys use street argot to talk secretly.
words.ex_cn: 这些男孩用街头黑话秘密交谈。
words.en: A specialized language or set of expressions used by a particular group, especially thieves or other criminals.

words.ex: He can articulate his ideas clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他能清楚地表达自己的想法。
words.en: If you describe someone as articulate, you mean that they are able to express their thoughts and ideas easily and clearly.

words.tr: adj. 两种语言的；用两种语言的；
words.ex: He is a bilingual student who speaks English and Spanish.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个会说英语和西班牙语的双语学生。
words.en: A bilingual person is someone who can speak two languages equally well.

words.ex: I can't swim.
words.ex_cn: 我不会游泳。
words.en: Cannot; used to indicate that something is not possible or allowed.

words.tr: n. 迂回累赘的陈述；遁词
words.ex: He used circumlocution to avoid answering the question.
words.ex_cn: 他用绕圈子的说法来避免回答问题。
words.en: Circumlocution is the use of many words where fewer would do, especially in a deliberate attempt to be vague or evasive.

words.ex: He uses colloquial words when talking with friends.
words.ex_cn: 他和朋友聊天时使用口语化的词语。
words.en: Colloquial language is informal language that is used in ordinary conversation rather than in writing or formal speech.

words.ex: He speaks a local dialect in his village.
words.ex_cn: 他在村子里说一种地方方言。
words.en: A dialect is a form of a language that is spoken in a particular area and that uses some of its own words, grammar, and pronunciations.

words.ex: His discourse on climate change was clear and logical.
words.ex_cn: 他关于气候变化的论述清晰而有逻辑。
words.en: Discourse is spoken or written communication between people, especially serious discussion of a particular subject.

words.tr:
v. 慢吞吞地说；拉长语调说话
n. 慢吞吞拉长调子的说话方式
words.ex: He speaks with a slow drawl.
words.ex_cn: 他说话慢吞吞的。
words.en: To speak slowly with vowels greatly prolonged.

words.ex: He practiced elocution to speak clearly in public.
words.ex_cn: 他练习雄辩术以便在公众场合清晰演讲。
words.en: The skill of clear and expressive speech, especially of distinct pronunciation and articulation.

words.ex: His eloquence moved everyone in the room.
words.ex_cn: 他的雄辩打动了房间里每一个人。
words.en: The ability to speak or write in a way that is fluent, persuasive, and expressive.

words.tr: v. （清楚地）发音；清楚地表明；阐明
words.ex: He tries to enunciate each word clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他努力清晰地发出每个单词的音。
words.en: To enunciate means to pronounce words clearly and distinctly, or to state something clearly and in detail.

words.tr: v. 含糊其辞；说模棱两可的话
words.ex: He equivocates when asked about the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 当被问到错误时，他含糊其辞。
words.en: If you equivocate, you use ambiguous language in order to deceive people or to avoid speaking directly about something.

words.ex: He used equivocation to avoid answering the question.
words.ex_cn: 他用模棱两可的话来避免回答问题。
words.en: The use of ambiguous language to conceal the truth or to avoid committing oneself.

words.ex: He learned the etymology of the word 'phone'.
words.ex_cn: 他学习了单词 'phone' 的词源。
words.en: Etymology is the study of the origin of words and the way in which their meanings have changed throughout history.

words.ex: He used a euphemism to say he lost his job.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个委婉语来表示他失业了。
words.en: A euphemism is a polite word or expression that is used to refer to things which people may find upsetting or embarrassing to talk about.

words.tr:
n. 高谈阔论；长篇大论；大声斥责的讲话
v. 作长篇大论；高谈阔论；猛烈的批评或训斥
words.ex: The politician gave a long harangue about taxes.
words.ex_cn: 这位政客就税收问题发表了一番长篇高谈阔论。
words.en: A harangue is a lengthy and aggressive speech, especially one delivered in public.

words.ex: He used an idiom to explain his idea.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个成语来解释他的想法。
words.en: An idiom is a group of words in a fixed order that have a particular meaning that is different from the meanings of each word on its own.

words.ex: The witch whispered an incantation to make the spell work.
words.ex_cn: 女巫低声念出一句咒语，让魔法生效。
words.en: An incantation is a series of words that are believed to have magical power when they are spoken.

words.tr:
n. 影射；暗指
v. 旁敲侧击地表达；含沙射影
words.ex: He made an innuendo about her being late.
words.ex_cn: 他暗示她迟到了。
words.en: An indirect or subtle, usually derogatory implication in expression; an insinuation.

words.ex: It's an irony that the fire station burned down.
words.ex_cn: 消防站着火了，这真是讽刺。
words.en: Irony is a subtle form of humor which involves saying things that you do not mean.

words.ex: He used too much jargon in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中用了太多行话。
words.en: Special words or expressions that are used by a particular profession or group and are difficult for others to understand.

words.ex: He is interested in linguistic patterns in children.
words.ex_cn: 他对儿童的语言模式感兴趣。
words.en: Relating to language or linguistics.

words.ex: He is studying linguistics at university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学学习语言学。
words.en: Linguistics is the scientific study of language and its structure, including the study of morphology, syntax, phonetics, and semantics.

words.tr: adj. 话多的；健谈的；喋喋不休的
words.ex: He is a loquacious man who talks all day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个整天喋喋不休的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as loquacious, you mean that they talk a lot.

words.tr: n. 荒唐的用词错误；被误用的词
words.ex: He said 'a wise man' instead of 'a whale of a man'—that was a malapropism.
words.ex_cn: 他说了‘a wise man’而不是‘a whale of a man’——那就是一个用词不当。
words.en: The mistaken use of a word in place of a similar-sounding one, often with unintentionally amusing effect, as in 'dance a flamingo' (instead of flamenco).

words.tr: n. 误称…之名；不当之名
words.ex: Calling a tomato a vegetable is a misnomer.
words.ex_cn: 把番茄称为蔬菜是一种错误的称呼。
words.en: A misnomer is a name that is wrongly or unsuitably applied to someone or something.

words.ex: The internet created many new neologisms like 'selfie' and 'blog'.
words.ex_cn: 互联网创造了许多新词，比如'selfie'和'blog'。
words.en: A neologism is a newly coined word or expression that may be in the process of entering common use, but has not yet been accepted into mainstream language.

words.ex: He gave an oration at the ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他在仪式上发表了演讲。
words.en: A formal speech, especially one given on a ceremonial occasion.

words.ex: In everyday parlance, people call it a phone.
words.ex_cn: 在日常用语中，人们称它为电话。
words.en: A particular way of speaking or using words, especially a way common to those with a particular job or interest.

words.ex: The teacher used phonetic symbols to help students pronounce words correctly.
words.ex_cn: 老师使用语音符号帮助学生正确发音。
words.en: Phonetic means relating to the sounds of speech or the study of these sounds.

words.ex: He used 'in' as a preposition in the sentence.
words.ex_cn: 他在句子中用 'in' 作为介词。
words.en: A preposition is a word such as 'by', 'for', 'into', or 'with' which usually has a noun group as its object.

words.tr:
n. 双关语
v. 说双关语
words.ex: He made a bad pun and everyone groaned.
words.ex_cn: 他开了个蹩脚的玩笑，大家都皱起了眉头。
words.en: A pun is a clever and amusing use of a word or phrase with two meanings, or of words with the same sound but different meanings.

words.tr: n. 修辞学；花言巧语；华丽的文辞；
words.ex: He studied rhetoric to improve his speaking skills.
words.ex_cn: 他学习修辞学以提高自己的演讲能力。
words.en: Rhetoric is the art or study of using language effectively and persuasively.

words.tr:
n. 韵文；
v. 押韵；
words.ex: The poem has a simple rhyme.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗有一段简单的韵文。
words.en: A rhyme is a repetition of similar sounds in the final stressed syllables and any following syllables of two or more words, most often used in poetry.

words.ex: The doctor used medical terminology to explain the illness.
words.ex_cn: 医生使用医学术语来解释这种疾病。
words.en: The set of terms and expressions used in a particular subject, field, or profession.

words.ex: The word 'bank' has different semantic meanings.
words.ex_cn: 单词 'bank' 有不同的语义含义。
words.en: Semantic is used to describe something that relates to the meanings of words and sentences.

words.tr: n. 长篇抨击激烈演说
words.ex: He went on a tirade about slow internet.
words.ex_cn: 他大发雷霆，抱怨网速太慢。
words.en: A tirade is a long, angry speech of criticism or accusation.

words.ex: He gave a verbal warning instead of a written one.
words.ex_cn: 他给了一个口头警告，而不是书面的。
words.en: Relating to or in the form of words.

words.tr:
adj. 本国的；地方的
n. 方言；土语
words.ex: He wrote the poem in the vernacular language.
words.ex_cn: 他用本国语言写了这首诗。
words.en: The vernacular is the language or dialect spoken by the ordinary people in a particular country or region.

words.tr: n. 韵律；节奏；抑扬顿挫
words.ex: The dancer moved with a steady cadence.
words.ex_cn: 舞者以稳定的节奏舞动。
words.en: The rhythm or sequence of sounds or movements in speech, music, dance, etc.

words.tr:
adj. 同源的；同语系的
n. 同家族的人；同源词
words.ex: English 'mother' and German 'Mutter' are cognate.
words.ex_cn: 英语的 'mother' 和德语的 'Mutter' 是同源词。
words.en: Cognate refers to words or languages that have a common origin or are related in their development.

words.ex: The word 'lead' is a homograph.
words.ex_cn: 单词 'lead' 是一个同形异义词。
words.en: A homograph is one of a group of words that have the same spelling but differ in origin, meaning, or pronunciation.

words.ex: He uses simple lexical items in his writing.
words.ex_cn: 他在写作中使用简单的词汇项。
words.en: Relating to the words or vocabulary of a language.

words.ex: She has a lingual talent for learning new languages.
words.ex_cn: 她有语言学习的天赋。
words.en: Relating to the tongue or language.

words.ex: He used a common locution in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中使用了一个常见的表达方式。
words.en: A particular style or manner of speaking; a phrase or expression.

words.tr: n. 语文学；语言学；文献学
words.ex: He loves philology because it helps him understand old texts.
words.ex_cn: 他热爱语言学，因为它帮助他理解古文。
words.en: Philology is the study of language in written historical sources; it is a combination of literary studies, history and linguistics.

words.tr: n. 感叹词；插入之语词
words.ex: He shouted 'Wow!' as an interjection.
words.ex_cn: 他喊了一声‘哇！’作为感叹词。
words.en: An interjection is a word or phrase that expresses a strong feeling or emotion, such as surprise, pleasure, or anger, and is often used in speech to interrupt or emphasize a statement.

words.tr: adj. 按字母顺序的；字母的；
words.ex: The names are listed in alphabetical order.
words.ex_cn: 这些名字是按字母顺序排列的。
words.en: In the order of the letters of the alphabet.

words.ex: He checked the glossary for the meaning of new words.
words.ex_cn: 他查阅了术语表以了解新词的含义。
words.en: A glossary is a list of terms in a particular domain of knowledge with the definitions for those terms.

words.ex: He looked up the word in his lexicon.
words.ex_cn: 他在词典里查了这个词。
words.en: The vocabulary of a person, language, or branch of knowledge.

words.tr:
adj. 逐字的；一字不差的
adv. 逐字地；一字不差地
words.ex: He repeated the words verbatim.
words.ex_cn: 他一字不差地重复了那些话。
words.en: Using exactly the same words as were used originally.

words.tr: n. 交织字母；花押字（某人姓名首字母构成的图案，缝制于个人衣物等上）
words.ex: She sewed her monogram on the pillow.
words.ex_cn: 她在枕头上缝上了她的姓名首字母图案。
words.en: A monogram is a motif made by overlapping or combining two or more letters or other graphemes to form one symbol.

words.ex: He learned proper orthography in elementary school.
words.ex_cn: 他在小学学习了正确的正字法。
words.en: Orthography is the conventional spelling system of a language.

words.ex: He said 'flamingo' instead of 'flying machine'—that was a spoonerism.
words.ex_cn: 他说了'flamingo'而不是'flying machine'——那是一个首音互换。
words.en: A spoonerism is a mistake in speech in which the initial sounds or letters of two or more words are accidentally swapped, often with a humorous effect.

words.ex: He called the test a 'silent scream', which is an oxymoron.
words.ex_cn: 他把这次考试称为‘无声的尖叫’，这是一个矛盾修辞法。
words.en: An oxymoron is a figure of speech in which apparently contradictory terms appear in conjunction.

words.ex: The big black bug bit the brave boy.
words.ex_cn: 大黑虫咬了勇敢的男孩。
words.en: Alliteration is the occurrence of the same letter or sound at the beginning of adjacent or closely connected words.

words.ex: The word 'it's' has an apostrophe.
words.ex_cn: 单词 'it's' 中有一个撇号。
words.en: An apostrophe is a punctuation mark used to indicate either possession or the omission of letters or numbers.

words.tr:
n. 星号
v. 给…注上星号
words.ex: She put an asterisk next to the word.
words.ex_cn: 她在那个词旁边加了一个星号。
words.en: An asterisk is a symbol (*) used in text to indicate a footnote or to highlight something important.

words.ex: She wrote: 'I love reading.'
words.ex_cn: 她写道：‘我喜欢阅读。’
words.en: A colon is a punctuation mark consisting of two equally sized dots centered on the same vertical line. It is also used to refer to the part of the large intestine that extends from the cecum to the rectum.

words.ex: He wrote, 'I love apples, bananas, and oranges.'
words.ex_cn: 他写道：'我喜欢苹果、香蕉和橙子。'
words.en: A comma is a punctuation mark (,) used to indicate a pause or to separate items in a list.

words.tr: n. 省略号；省略；省略符号
words.ex: He used an ellipsis to show he stopped talking.
words.ex_cn: 他用了省略号来表示他停止了说话。
words.en: An ellipsis is a set of three dots (...) used in writing to indicate an omission of words or a pause.

words.ex: She wrote mother-in-law with a hyphen.
words.ex_cn: 她写 mother-in-law 时用了连字符。
words.en: A hyphen is a short line (-) used to connect the parts of a compound word or the parts of a word that has been split at the end of a line.

words.tr: n. 圆括号；插入语；插入成分；附带
words.ex: Put the numbers in parenthesis.
words.ex_cn: 把数字放在圆括号里。
words.en: A word, clause, or sentence inserted as an explanation or afterthought into a passage that is grammatically complete without it, in writing usually marked off by round or square brackets.

words.tr: adj. 时代错误的；落伍的；过时的
words.ex: Wearing a horse-drawn carriage in modern times is anachronistic.
words.ex_cn: 在现代穿马车是过时的。
words.en: Something that is anachronistic is out of its proper time in history, or seems to belong to a different time.

words.ex: My ancestor came from China a hundred years ago.
words.ex_cn: 我的祖先一百年前来自中国。
words.en: An ancestor is a person from whom one is descended, typically more remote than a grandparent.

words.ex: He learned about his ancestry from his grandmother.
words.ex_cn: 他从祖母那里了解了自己的血统。
words.en: Your ancestry is the series of ancestors from whom you are descended.

words.tr: n. 年鉴；编年史；历史记载；年报
words.ex: The annals of history record many great kings.
words.ex_cn: 历史年鉴记录了许多伟大的国王。
words.en: A chronological record of events, especially those of a particular organization, institution, or community.

words.tr:
adj. （《圣经》中所说的大洪水前的）古老的；过时的
n.  年迈的人；不合时宜的人
words.ex: He uses an antediluvian typewriter to write letters.
words.ex_cn: 他用一台远古的打字机写信。
words.en: Belonging to the time before the biblical Flood; very old or old-fashioned.

words.tr:
adj. 古老的；
n. 古董；
words.ex: He bought an antique chair from the old market.
words.ex_cn: 他从旧市场买了一把古老的椅子。
words.en: Something that is antique is old and often valuable because it is rare or well made.

words.ex: The ruins show the antiquity of this civilization.
words.ex_cn: 这些废墟展示了这个文明的古老。
words.en: The ancient past, especially the period before the Middle Ages.

words.ex: He loves archaeology and digs old artifacts.
words.ex_cn: 他热爱考古学，挖掘古代文物。
words.en: Archaeology is the study of the societies and peoples of the past by examining the remains of their buildings, tools, and other objects.

words.tr:
adj. 同年代的
n. 同时代的人
words.ex: The two ancient temples are coeval.
words.ex_cn: 这两座古代神庙是同时期的。
words.en: Having the same age or date of origin; contemporary.

words.ex: The derivation of this word is from Latin.
words.ex_cn: 这个词的起源是拉丁语。
words.en: Derivation refers to the process by which a word is formed from another word or from a root, especially by the addition of an affix.

words.ex: He is a descendant of the first king.
words.ex_cn: 他是第一位国王的后裔。
words.en: A person, plant, or animal that is descended from a particular ancestor.

words.ex: Workers excavate the old ruins with shovels.
words.ex_cn: 工人们用铲子挖掘古代遗址。
words.en: To excavate means to dig in the ground in order to find things that have been buried there, such as archaeological remains.

words.ex: There are only two extant copies of the ancient book.
words.ex_cn: 这本古书现存只有两份。
words.en: If something is extant, it is still in existence, in spite of being very old.

words.ex: The genesis of the story is a simple dream.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事的起源是一个简单的梦。
words.en: The origin or mode of formation of something.

words.ex: The glacial landscape was covered in snow.
words.ex_cn: 冰河地貌被雪覆盖着。
words.en: relating to, resulting from, or denoting the presence or agency of ice, especially in the form of glaciers.

words.ex: The ancient Egyptians used hieroglyph to write messages.
words.ex_cn: 古埃及人用象形文字来书写信息。
words.en: A hieroglyph is a character of the ancient Egyptian writing system, which consists of pictures or symbols representing words or sounds.

words.ex: The ancient Egyptians used hieroglyphic to write messages.
words.ex_cn: 古埃及人用象形文字书写信息。
words.en: Hieroglyphic refers to a system of writing that uses pictures or symbols to represent words or sounds, especially the ancient Egyptian writing system.

words.ex: The castle is a medieval building.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡是一座中世纪的建筑。
words.en: Relating to the Middle Ages, the period in European history from about the 5th century to the 15th century.

words.ex: People in the Neolithic age used stone tools.
words.ex_cn: 新石器时代的人们使用石器。
words.en: Relating to or denoting the later part of the Stone Age, when ground or polished stone weapons and implements prevailed.

words.ex: Paleolithic people used stone tools.
words.ex_cn: 旧石器时代的人使用石器。
words.en: The Paleolithic period is the earliest part of the Stone Age, preceding the Mesolithic and Neolithic periods.

words.ex: The cave paintings are prehistoric.
words.ex_cn: 这些洞穴壁画是史前的。
words.en: Belonging to or existing in times before recorded history.

words.ex: The preliterate society told stories by speaking.
words.ex_cn: 这个前识字社会通过口述来讲述故事。
words.en: Relating to a society or culture that has not yet developed a written language.

words.ex: The provenance of this ancient vase is unknown.
words.ex_cn: 这个古花瓶的起源未知。
words.en: The place of origin or earliest known history of something.

words.tr: adj. 北欧古字的；卢恩文的；神秘的
words.ex: He found an old stone with runic letters.
words.ex_cn: 他发现了一块刻有如尼文字的古老石头。
words.en: Runic refers to the ancient alphabets used by Germanic peoples before the adoption of the Latin alphabet, or something resembling these alphabets.

words.ex: They unearthed an old coin in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 他们在花园里挖出了一枚旧硬币。
words.en: To unearth something means to find it by digging in the ground or to discover something that was hidden or unknown.

words.ex: The government decided to abolish the old law.
words.ex_cn: 政府决定废除这项旧法律。
words.en: If someone in authority abolishes a system or practice, they formally put an end to it.

words.ex: The abolition of slavery took many years.
words.ex_cn: 废除奴隶制花了许多年。
words.en: The act of officially ending or stopping something, such as a system, practice, or institution.

words.ex: The court acquitted him of all charges.
words.ex_cn: 法院宣告他无罪。
words.en: If someone is acquitted of a crime in a court of law, they are formally declared not to have committed the crime.

words.tr: n. 宣告无罪；无罪的判决
words.ex: The court gave him an acquittal after the trial.
words.ex_cn: 审判后，法院宣布他无罪。
words.en: An acquittal is a formal declaration in a court of law that someone who has been accused of a crime is not guilty.

words.tr: n. 不在犯罪现场证明；辩解；托辞
words.ex: He gave an alibi that he was at home.
words.ex_cn: 他提供了一个他在家的不在场证明。
words.en: An alibi is a form of defense used in criminal procedure wherein a defendant attempts to prove that he or she was in some other place at the time the alleged offense was committed.

words.ex: The amendment changed the old law.
words.ex_cn: 这项修正案改变了旧法律。
words.en: An amendment is a change or addition to a law or document.

words.tr:
n. 吸引力；上诉；
v. 吸引；诉请；呼吁；
words.ex: The appeal of the beach drew many tourists.
words.ex_cn: 海滩的吸引力吸引了许多游客。
words.en: If you appeal to someone to do something, you make a serious and urgent request to them. If you appeal against a decision or sentence, you formally ask a court or other authority to change it. If something appeals to you, you like it or it interests you.

words.ex: I couldn't apprehend the math lesson because it was too fast.
words.ex_cn: 我无法理解这节数学课，因为讲得太快了。
words.en: If the police apprehend someone, they catch them and arrest them.

words.ex: The police arrested the thief last night.
words.ex_cn: 警察昨晚逮捕了那个小偷。
words.en: If the police arrest you, they take charge of you and take you to a police station, because they believe you may have committed a crime.

words.tr: n. 律师；辩护律师；代理人
words.ex: The attorney helped the man with his case.
words.ex_cn: 律师帮助那个人处理了他的案件。
words.en: An attorney is a lawyer who is qualified to represent a client in court.

words.tr: adj. 真正的；真实的；真迹的；可靠的；
words.ex: This is an authentic painting by Picasso.
words.ex_cn: 这是一幅毕加索的真迹。
words.en: If something is authentic, it is real, true, or what people say it is.

words.tr:
n. 保释（金）
v. 保释；（往外）舀水
words.ex: He paid bail to get out of jail.
words.ex_cn: 他交了保释金以便出狱。
words.en: Bail is a sum of money that a person who has been accused of a crime pays to a law court so that they can be released until their trial. The payment is a way of making sure that the accused will return to court for trial.

words.ex: He sat on the bench in the park.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在公园的长凳上。
words.en: A bench is a long seat for several people, typically made of wood or metal.

words.tr: v. 承诺；犯（罪、错）；（公开地）表达意见；
words.ex: He commit to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他承诺帮助他的朋友。
words.en: To commit means to carry out or perpetrate a mistake, crime, or immoral act; or to pledge or bind oneself to a certain course of action.

words.ex: The constitution protects the rights of all citizens.
words.ex_cn: 宪法保护所有公民的权利。
words.en: The constitution of a country or organization is the system of laws which formally states people's rights and duties.

words.ex: He is studying constitutional law at university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学学习宪法。
words.en: Relating to the constitution of a country or organization; in accordance with a political constitution.

words.tr:
v. 定罪；宣判有罪
n. 罪犯；囚犯
words.ex: The court convicted him of theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院判定他犯有盗窃罪。
words.en: If someone is convicted of a crime, they are found guilty of that crime in a court of law.

words.ex: His conviction that honesty is important never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他坚信诚实很重要，从未改变。
words.en: A conviction is a strong belief or opinion, or the state of being found guilty of a crime in a court of law.

words.ex: The case will be heard in court next week.
words.ex_cn: 这个案件将于下周在法院审理。
words.en: A court is a place where legal matters are decided by a judge and jury or by a magistrate.

words.ex: The defendant spoke calmly in court.
words.ex_cn: 被告在法庭上平静地发言。
words.en: A defendant is a person or entity against whom a criminal or civil action is brought in a court of law.

words.ex: The police will detain the suspect for questioning.
words.ex_cn: 警察将扣留嫌疑人进行审问。
words.en: If someone is detained, they are officially held in a place, especially a prison, and are not allowed to leave.

words.tr: v. 制定（法律）；通过（法律）；扮演（角色）
words.ex: The government will enact a new law next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将颁布一项新法律。
words.en: To enact a law or rule means to make it official by passing it through a legislative body.

words.ex: The evidence helps to exculpate him.
words.ex_cn: 这些证据有助于为他开脱。
words.en: To remove blame from someone; to declare or prove someone not guilty of wrongdoing.

words.tr: v. 确定无罪；免除（罪责）
words.ex: The new evidence helped to exonerate him.
words.ex_cn: 新的证据帮助他洗清了罪名。
words.en: If someone is exonerated, they are proved to be not guilty of a crime or responsible for something bad that happened.

words.ex: The felon went to prison for stealing.
words.ex_cn: 这名重罪犯因偷窃而入狱。
words.en: A felon is someone who is guilty of committing a felony, which is a serious crime such as murder or rape.

words.ex: He was arrested for a felony last month.
words.ex_cn: 他上个月因重罪被逮捕了。
words.en: A felony is a serious crime such as murder or robbery.

words.ex: He felt guilt after lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他在对朋友撒谎后感到内疚。
words.en: Guilt is an unhappy feeling that you have because you have done something wrong or think that you have done something wrong.

words.ex: He felt guilty for lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他因为对朋友撒谎而感到有罪。
words.en: If you feel guilty, you feel unhappy because you believe that you have done something wrong or have failed to do something which you should have done.

words.ex: It is illegal to drive without a license.
words.ex_cn: 无证驾驶是非法的。
words.en: If something is illegal, the law says that it is not allowed.

words.ex: His handwriting is illegible.
words.ex_cn: 他的字迹无法辨认。
words.en: If something is illegible, it is impossible to read because the letters or characters are not clear, are not formed properly, or are obscured in some way.

words.ex: The illegitimate business was shut down by the police.
words.ex_cn: 这个非法的生意被警察关闭了。
words.en: An illegitimate child is one whose parents were not married to each other when the child was born. Something that is illegitimate is not allowed by the rules or laws.

words.ex: The police seized illicit drugs from the suspect.
words.ex_cn: 警察从嫌疑人那里没收了非法毒品。
words.en: Illicit activities or substances are not allowed by law or by social or religious custom.

words.tr: v. 监禁；禁闭；把...嵌在墙上
words.ex: He was immured in the old tower for years.
words.ex_cn: 他被囚禁在那座旧塔里多年。
words.en: To confine someone within or as if within walls; imprison.

words.ex: The man was incarcerated for stealing.
words.ex_cn: 这个人因偷窃而被监禁。
words.en: If people are incarcerated, they are kept in a prison or other place.

words.ex: He tried to inculpate his friend for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他试图把错误归咎于他的朋友。
words.en: To inculpate someone means to accuse them of a crime or to make them seem guilty of it.

words.ex: The court will indict him for theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院将对他提起盗窃指控。
words.en: If someone is indicted for a crime, they are officially charged with it.

words.ex: He got a fine for a small infraction.
words.ex_cn: 他因一个小违规行为被罚款。
words.en: An infraction is a violation or infringement of a law, agreement, or set of rules.

words.tr:
v. 做实习生；扣留
n. 实习生
words.ex: He is interning at a hospital this summer.
words.ex_cn: 他今年夏天在医院做实习生。
words.en: An intern is someone who works in a temporary position with an emphasis on on-the-job training rather than merely employment, often to gain experience in a particular field.

words.tr: adj. 司法的；法庭的；审判的；
words.ex: The judicial system protects people's rights.
words.ex_cn: 司法系统保护人民的权利。
words.en: Judicial means relating to the legal system and to judgments made in a court of law.

words.tr: n. 管辖权；司法权；裁判权；
words.ex: The court has jurisdiction over this case.
words.ex_cn: 法院对这个案件有管辖权。
words.en: The official power to make legal decisions and judgments.

words.tr: v. 制定法律；用立法规定
words.ex: The government will legislate new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将制定新规则。
words.en: To legislate means to make or enact laws.

words.ex: The new legislation bans plastic bags.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法规禁止使用塑料袋。
words.en: Legislation refers to the process of making or enacting laws by a government or other authority.

words.ex: The legislature passed a new law last week.
words.ex_cn: 立法机构上周通过了一项新法律。
words.en: A legislature is the part of a country's government that is responsible for making laws.

words.ex: He is facing litigation over the contract.
words.ex_cn: 他因合同问题面临诉讼。
words.en: Litigation is the process of taking legal action or bringing a lawsuit in a court of law.

words.tr: n. 渎职；不法行为；不正当
words.ex: The mayor was fired for malfeasance.
words.ex_cn: 市长因渎职被解雇了。
words.en: Malfeasance is the act of committing an illegal or wrongful act, especially by a public official.

words.ex: The nefarious thief stole money from the poor.
words.ex_cn: 那个极坏的贼从穷人那里偷了钱。
words.en: If you describe an activity as nefarious, you mean that it is wicked and immoral.

words.ex: The city passed an ordinance to stop littering.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市通过了一项禁止乱扔垃圾的法令。
words.en: An ordinance is an authoritative rule, law, decree, or command.

words.ex: He got a penalty for breaking the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他因违反规则而受到惩罚。
words.en: A penalty is a punishment that is imposed on someone for doing something that is against the rules or the law.

words.tr: v. 对…予以惩罚；使处于不利地位
words.ex: The teacher will penalize students who cheat.
words.ex_cn: 老师会惩罚作弊的学生。
words.en: To penalize someone means to punish them or make them suffer in some way because they have done something wrong.

words.ex: He will perjure himself in court.
words.ex_cn: 他将在法庭上作伪证。
words.en: If someone perjures themselves in a court of law, they lie, even though they have promised to tell the truth.

words.ex: He was charged with perjury after lying in court.
words.ex_cn: 他在法庭上撒谎后被控伪证罪。
words.en: The crime of telling a lie in a court of law after having sworn to tell the truth.

words.ex: The court will prosecute him for theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院将因盗窃罪起诉他。
words.en: To prosecute means to institute legal proceedings against someone or to carry on a legal action against a defendant in a court of law. It also means to continue with or carry on an activity or enterprise.

words.ex: The prosecution brought evidence against the suspect.
words.ex_cn: 起诉方提供了针对嫌疑人的证据。
words.en: The act or process of holding a trial against a person who is accused of a crime to see if they are guilty.

words.tr:
v. 缓期执行；暂缓处刑
n. 缓刑；暂缓
words.ex: The judge gave him a reprieve until next month.
words.ex_cn: 法官给了他一个延期，直到下个月。
words.en: If someone who has been sentenced in a court is given a reprieve, their punishment is officially delayed or cancelled.

words.ex: The respondent answered all the questions honestly.
words.ex_cn: 这位调查对象诚实地回答了所有问题。
words.en: A respondent is someone who replies to something such as a survey or set of questions.

words.ex: The statute says drivers must stop at red lights.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律规定司机必须在红灯时停车。
words.en: A statute is a formal written law of a country or state, enacted by its legislative authority.

words.tr: adj. 法定的；依照法规的；
words.ex: The statutory minimum wage is $10 per hour.
words.ex_cn: 法定最低工资是每小时10美元。
words.en: Statutory means relating to rules or laws which have been formally written down.

words.tr:
v. 以传票传唤；传讯
n. 传票
words.ex: The court subpoenaed the witness to appear next Monday.
words.ex_cn: 法院传唤证人下周一出庭。
words.en: A subpoena is a legal document ordering someone to attend a court of law and give evidence as a witness.

words.ex: He was punished for treason against the king.
words.ex_cn: 他因对国王叛国而受到惩罚。
words.en: Treason is the crime of betraying your country, for example by helping its enemies or by trying to remove its government using violence.

words.ex: The tribunal decided the case quickly.
words.ex_cn: 法庭迅速作出了裁决。
words.en: A tribunal is a special court or committee that is officially chosen to examine a particular problem or situation.

words.tr: n. 出庭律师；法律顾问
words.ex: The barrister spoke clearly in court.
words.ex_cn: 律师在法庭上清晰地发言。
words.en: A barrister is a type of lawyer in the UK and some other countries who has the right to speak and argue as an advocate in higher law courts.

words.ex: The police caught the culprit who stole the bike.
words.ex_cn: 警察抓住了偷自行车的罪犯。
words.en: A culprit is someone who has done something wrong or illegal.

words.ex: The king issued an edict to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 国王发布了一项法令来停止战争。
words.en: An edict is an official order or proclamation issued by a person in authority.

words.ex: The detective used forensic evidence to solve the case.
words.ex_cn: 侦探使用法医证据破了案。
words.en: Relating to or denoting the application of scientific methods and techniques to the investigation of crime.

words.ex: He loves studying jurisprudence to understand laws better.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢学习法学以更好地理解法律。
words.en: Jurisprudence is the study of law and the principles on which law is based.

words.ex: The maleficent storm destroyed many homes.
words.ex_cn: 这场有害的风暴摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: Causing harm or destruction, especially by supernatural means.

words.tr:
n. 手铐；镣铐
v. 上手铐；束缚
words.ex: The prisoner wore manacles on his wrists.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯的手腕上戴着镣铐。
words.en: Manacles are metal devices attached to a person's wrists in order to prevent them from moving or escaping.

words.tr: n. 骚动；破坏；故意的伤害罪
words.ex: The storm caused mayhem in the city.
words.ex_cn: 风暴在城市中造成了混乱。
words.en: Violent or extreme disorder; chaos.

words.tr:
n. 诉讼当事人
adj. 有关诉讼的
words.ex: The litigant spoke clearly in court.
words.ex_cn: 这位诉讼当事人在法庭上清晰地发言。
words.en: A litigant is a person who is involved in a lawsuit.

words.ex: The plaintiff sued the company for damages.
words.ex_cn: 原告起诉该公司要求赔偿。
words.en: A plaintiff is a person who brings a case against another in a court of law.

words.ex: The police caught the malefactor who stole the money.
words.ex_cn: 警察抓到了偷钱的罪犯。
words.en: A malefactor is someone who has committed a crime or done something wrong.

words.ex: The law is retroactive and covers last year.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律具有追溯效力，适用于去年。
words.en: If a decision, action, or law is retroactive, it is intended to take effect from a date before it was actually made.

words.tr:
n. 司法部；司法制度；法官（总称）
adj. 司法的；法院的；法官的
words.ex: The judiciary made a fair decision.
words.ex_cn: 司法部做出了公正的裁决。
words.en: The judiciary is the system of courts that interprets and applies the law in the name of the state.

words.ex: He studies penology to understand prison systems.
words.ex_cn: 他研究刑罚学以了解监狱系统。
words.en: Penology is the study of the processes devised and adopted for the punishment and prevention of crime, and the treatment of offenders.

words.ex: He returned to prison because of recidivism.
words.ex_cn: 他因再犯而重返监狱。
words.en: Recidivism is the act of repeating an undesirable behavior after having experienced negative consequences of that behavior.

words.ex: The prosecutor read the indictment in court.
words.ex_cn: 检察官在法庭上宣读了起诉状。
words.en: An indictment is a formal accusation that someone has committed a crime.

words.tr:
n. 无政府主义者
adj. 信奉无政府主义的
words.ex: He is an anarchist who hates all governments.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名无政府主义者，憎恨所有政府。
words.en: An anarchist is a person who believes in or tries to bring about anarchy.

words.ex: The country fell into anarchy after the war.
words.ex_cn: 战争之后，这个国家陷入了混乱。
words.en: Anarchy is a state of disorder due to absence or nonrecognition of authority or other controlling systems.

words.ex: The teacher chose an arbitrary number to start the game.
words.ex_cn: 老师随意选了一个数字来开始游戏。
words.en: If you describe an action, rule, or decision as arbitrary, you think that it is not based on any principle, plan, or system. It often seems unfair because of this.

words.tr: n. 优势；支配地位；支配力量
words.ex: The king's ascendancy lasted for twenty years.
words.ex_cn: 国王的统治持续了二十年。
words.en: If one group has ascendancy over another group, it has more power or influence than the other group.

words.ex: The authoritarian leader controls everything.
words.ex_cn: 这位专制的领导人控制一切。
words.en: An authoritarian government or leader has complete power and control over the people and does not allow political opposition.

words.tr: n. 专制制度；独裁制度；专制国家
words.ex: The autocracy was overthrown by a popular revolution.
words.ex_cn: 独裁政府被一场民众革命推翻了。
words.en: Autocracy is a system of government in which a country is ruled by a person or group with total power.

words.ex: The autocrat rules the country with no elections.
words.ex_cn: 独裁者在没有选举的情况下统治国家。
words.en: An autocrat is a ruler who has absolute power.

words.tr: adj. 自治的；有自治权的；自主的；
words.ex: The region has autonomous control over its education system.
words.ex_cn: 这个地区对其教育系统拥有自治权。
words.en: An autonomous organization, country, or region is independent and has the freedom to govern itself.

words.tr: n. 自主权；自治权；自治；
words.ex: The region demands autonomy from the central government.
words.ex_cn: 该地区要求从中央政府获得自主权。
words.en: Autonomy is the ability or condition of being self-governing; independence in one's thoughts or actions.

words.tr:
v. 进行无记名投票 
n. 无记名投票
words.ex: He cast his ballot in the election.
words.ex_cn: 他在选举中投了票。
words.en: A ballot is a process of voting, in writing and typically in secret. It is also the piece of paper on which you mark your vote.

words.tr: n. 官僚主义；官僚机构
words.ex: He hates the bureaucracy in government offices.
words.ex_cn: 他讨厌政府办公室里的官僚主义。
words.en: Bureaucracy refers to a system of government or business that has many complicated rules and ways of doing things.

words.tr: n. 政治阴谋小集团；秘密团体
words.ex: The cabal plotted to overthrow the government.
words.ex_cn: 这个阴谋集团策划推翻政府。
words.en: A cabal is a small group of people who are involved in secret plans to achieve political or social change, often by illegal or dishonest methods.

words.ex: He kept the dishes in the cabinet.
words.ex_cn: 他把盘子放在储藏柜里。
words.en: A cabinet is a piece of furniture with doors and shelves or drawers, used for storing or showing things. In politics, a cabinet is a group of people who are chosen by a head of state to give advice and to help set government policy.

words.tr: n. 候选人的资格（或身份）
words.ex: He applied for the job because of his strong candidacy.
words.ex_cn: 他申请了这份工作，因为他的候选人资格很强。
words.en: Candidacy is the state of being a candidate in an election.

words.tr: n. 政党会议；核心小组会议；特别利益集团
words.ex: The caucus decided on a new strategy for the upcoming election.
words.ex_cn: 党团会议决定了一项新的选举策略。
words.en: A caucus is a meeting of the members of a political party to select candidates or decide policy.

words.ex: The company wants centralization for better control.
words.ex_cn: 公司希望集中管理以更好地控制。
words.en: The process or policy of concentrating control of an organization or activity under a single authority.

words.ex: He quit his job because of coercion from his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他因为老板的强迫而辞了工作。
words.en: The act of persuading someone to do something by using force or threats.

words.ex: The despotic king ruled with fear.
words.ex_cn: 这位专制的国王用恐惧统治。
words.en: If you say that someone is despotic, you are emphasizing that they use their power over other people in a very unfair or cruel way.

words.tr: n. 专制统治；独裁制；暴政
words.ex: The king ruled with despotism.
words.ex_cn: 国王以专制统治。
words.en: Despotism is a form of government in which a single entity rules with absolute power. The ruling entity may be an individual, as in an autocracy, or a group, as in an oligarchy.

words.tr:
v. （因发言冗长）妨碍（会议的进程）
n. （议会中为拖延表决的）冗长演说
words.ex: The senator used a filibuster to delay the vote on the bill.
words.ex_cn: 参议员使用阻挠议事行动来拖延对该法案的投票。
words.en: A filibuster is a tactic used in a legislative assembly to prevent a measure from being brought to a vote. It is most commonly associated with the U.S. Senate, where a senator or a group of senators may extend debate on a proposal indefinitely to delay or entirely prevent a decision on it.

words.tr: n. 老人统治；老人政治；老人政府
words.ex: The village was ruled by a gerontocracy, with all major decisions made by the eldest members.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄由一群老人统治，所有重大决策都由最年长的成员做出。
words.en: A gerontocracy is a society, organization, or group that is governed by old people.

words.ex: The country seeks hegemony over its neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家试图对邻国实现霸权。
words.en: Hegemony refers to the dominance or leadership of one group or state over others, especially in a political or cultural context.

words.ex: The imperious queen demanded immediate obedience.
words.ex_cn: 这位专横的女王要求立即服从。
words.en: If you describe someone as imperious, you mean that they have a proud manner and expect to be obeyed.

words.tr: n. 空位期；过渡期；间歇
words.ex: The interregnum between the old king's death and the new king's coronation was marked by political instability.
words.ex_cn: 老国王去世和新国王加冕之间的空位期伴随着政治不稳定。
words.en: An interregnum is a period when a country or organization does not have a leader or a government because the previous leader or government has left and a new one has not yet started.

words.tr: n. 玩忽职守；治疗失当；营私舞弊
words.ex: The doctor was sued for medical malpractice.
words.ex_cn: 这位医生因医疗过失被起诉。
words.en: Improper, illegal, or negligent professional activity or treatment, especially by a medical practitioner, lawyer, or public official.

words.ex: The country still has a monarchy with a king as the head of state.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家仍然实行君主制，国王是国家元首。
words.en: A monarchy is a form of government in which a country is ruled by a monarch, such as a king or queen.

words.tr: n. 寡头政治；寡头统治集团；寡头统治的国家
words.ex: The country is ruled by an oligarchy of wealthy businessmen.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家由一群富有的商人寡头统治。
words.en: A form of government in which all power is vested in a few persons or in a dominant class or clique; government by the few.

words.ex: He works in a laboratory on Fridays.
words.ex_cn: 他在星期五去实验室工作。
words.en: A laboratory is a place equipped for scientific research, experiments, or teaching.

words.tr: n. 富豪；财阀；财阀政治；富豪统治
words.ex: The country is often criticized for being a plutocracy where wealth determines political power.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家经常因为财富决定政治权力的富豪统治而受到批评。
words.en: A plutocracy is a society or system that is ruled or controlled by people of great wealth or income.

words.ex: The new regime changed the tax laws.
words.ex_cn: 新的管理制度改变了税法。
words.en: A regime is the set of rules or the way that a country or organization is governed, especially when it is considered to be strict or unfair.

words.ex: The queen's reign lasted 70 years.
words.ex_cn: 女王的统治持续了70年。
words.en: The period during which a sovereign rules; to hold royal office; to prevail

words.tr: n. 投票；选举权；参政权
words.ex: Women won suffrage in 1920.
words.ex_cn: 女性在1920年获得了选举权。
words.en: Suffrage is the right to vote in political elections.

words.ex: The theocracy ruled with an iron fist.
words.ex_cn: 神权政体以铁腕统治。
words.en: A theocracy is a form of government in which a deity is recognized as the supreme civil ruler, the deity's laws being interpreted by ecclesiastical authorities.

words.ex: The people rose up against the tyranny of the king.
words.ex_cn: 人民反抗了国王的暴虐。
words.en: Tyranny is cruel and unfair treatment by someone with power over other people, or a government in which a single ruler has absolute power.

words.tr: n. 妇女当政；女权政治
words.ex: In ancient myths, gynaecocracy was often depicted as a utopian society where women held all the power.
words.ex_cn: 在古代神话中，女性统治常被描绘为一个乌托邦社会，其中女性掌握所有权力。
words.en: A society or government ruled by women.

words.tr: n. 女家长制；女族长制；母权制
words.ex: In some cultures, matriarchy is the dominant social system.
words.ex_cn: 在一些文化中，母权制是主导的社会体系。
words.en: A matriarchy is a social system in which females hold the primary power positions in roles of political leadership, moral authority, social privilege, and control of property.

words.ex: Polyandry is a rare form of marriage in which one woman is married to several men.
words.ex_cn: 一妻多夫制是一种罕见的婚姻形式，其中一个女人与几个男人结婚。
words.en: Polyandry is a form of marriage in which a woman has more than one husband at the same time.

words.tr: n. 平民制定法；公民投票
words.ex: The government decided to hold a plebiscite to decide the future of the region.
words.ex_cn: 政府决定举行公民投票来决定该地区的未来。
words.en: A plebiscite is a direct vote by the electorate on an important public question such as a change in the constitution.

words.tr: n. 公民投票；全民公决；
words.ex: The country held a referendum to decide on the new law.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家举行了公民投票来决定新法律。
words.en: A referendum is a direct vote in which an entire electorate is invited to vote on a particular proposal. This may result in the adoption of a new law.

words.ex: He bought a franchise to open a coffee shop.
words.ex_cn: 他购买了一个特许经营权来开一家咖啡店。
words.en: A franchise is an authorization granted by a government or company to an individual or group enabling them to carry out specified commercial activities, e.g., acting as an agent for a company's products.

words.ex: The municipality cleaned the streets last week.
words.ex_cn: 这个自治市上周清理了街道。
words.en: A municipality is a city or town that has its own government to manage local affairs.

words.tr: n. 联邦；共和国；联合体；
words.ex: Australia is a member of the Commonwealth.
words.ex_cn: 澳大利亚是联邦的成员。
words.en: A commonwealth is a traditional English term for a political community founded for the common good. Historically, it has been synonymous with 'republic'.

words.tr: n. 联邦；共和国；联合体；
words.ex: Australia is a member of the Commonwealth.
words.ex_cn: 澳大利亚是联邦的成员。
words.en: A commonwealth is a traditional English term for a political community founded for the common good. Historically, it has been synonymous with 'republic'.

words.tr:
n. 异教徒；无宗教信仰者
adj. 异教的；异教徒的；无宗教信仰的
words.ex: He lived in a pagan village long ago.
words.ex_cn: 他很久以前住在一个异教村庄里。
words.en: A pagan is someone who worships many gods or no god, especially one who belongs to a religion that existed before Christianity.

words.tr: n. 取消前言；改变论调
words.ex: His recantation of the controversial statement surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他改变了那个有争议的言论，这让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The act of publicly stating that you no longer believe something that you previously believed, especially in religion.

words.tr: v. 弥补；兑换；付清；赎回；履行
words.ex: He worked hard to redeem his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作来弥补自己的错误。
words.en: To redeem something means to get it back by paying a sum of money or by doing something to compensate for a fault or mistake.

words.ex: His apology was redemptive and helped heal their friendship.
words.ex_cn: 他的道歉具有救赎意义，帮助修复了他们的友谊。
words.en: Redemptive actions or processes are intended to save someone from evil, suffering, or failure.

words.ex: He practices his religion every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周日都实践自己的宗教信仰。
words.en: Religion is the belief in and worship of a superhuman controlling power, especially a personal God or gods.

words.tr:
n. 叛徒；变节者；叛教者
adj. 背叛的；变节的
v. 背叛
words.ex: He is a renegade who left the team suddenly.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个突然离开团队的叛徒。
words.en: A renegade is a person who deserts and betrays an organization, country, or set of principles.

words.ex: The temple is a sacred place for believers.
words.ex_cn: 这座寺庙对信徒来说是神圣的地方。
words.en: Something that is sacred is considered to be holy or connected with God or a god.

words.tr: n. 宗派主义；教派主义
words.ex: The conflict grew because of sectarianism.
words.ex_cn: 由于宗派主义，冲突加剧了。
words.en: Sectarianism is strong support for the religious or political group that you belong to, often combined with a dislike or hatred of other groups.

words.tr:
v. 牺牲；
n. 牺牲（品）；
words.ex: He sacrificed his time to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他牺牲了自己的时间来帮助朋友。
words.en: If you sacrifice something that is valuable or important, you give it up, usually to obtain something else for yourself or for other people.

words.tr: n. 亵渎；亵圣；悖理逆天的行为
words.ex: He committed sacrilege by breaking the holy statue.
words.ex_cn: 他砸了圣像，犯下了亵渎之罪。
words.en: If someone's behaviour or actions are described as sacrilege, they are considered to show a lack of respect for something that is regarded as holy or very important.

words.tr: adj. 亵渎神圣的；大不敬的
words.ex: He made a sacrilegious joke about the church.
words.ex_cn: 他开了一个关于教堂的亵渎神明的玩笑。
words.en: If someone's behaviour or actions are sacrilegious, they show great disrespect towards something holy or something that people think should be respected.

words.ex: She lived a saintly life, always helping others.
words.ex_cn: 她过着圣洁的生活，总是帮助他人。
words.en: If you describe someone as saintly, you mean that they are extremely kind, patient, and unselfish.

words.ex: They pray to sanctify the new home.
words.ex_cn: 他们祈祷来圣化这个新家。
words.en: To sanctify something means to make it holy or to purify it, often through a religious ceremony or blessing.

words.ex: He reads scripture every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上读经文。
words.en: The sacred writings of a religion; often used to refer to the Bible.

words.ex: He studied theology at a prestigious seminary.
words.ex_cn: 他在一所著名的神学院学习神学。
words.en: A seminary is a college for training people to become priests or ministers.

words.tr: n. 神龛；神社；圣地；圣殿
words.ex: People visit the shrine to pray.
words.ex_cn: 人们去神社祈祷。
words.en: A shrine is a place of worship which is associated with a particular holy person or object.

words.ex: He made an investment in a small business.
words.ex_cn: 他投资了一家小企业。
words.en: An investment is an amount of money that you invest in something.

words.ex: He believes in atheism and does not follow any religion.
words.ex_cn: 他信仰无神论，不信仰任何宗教。
words.en: The belief that there is no God or gods.

words.ex: He looks up to his favorite singer as an idol.
words.ex_cn: 他把自己最喜欢的歌手当作偶像。
words.en: An idol is a person or thing that is greatly admired, loved, or revered.

words.ex: The investiture ceremony was held in the grand cathedral.
words.ex_cn: 授职仪式在宏伟的大教堂举行。
words.en: An investiture is a ceremony in which someone is given an official title or rank.

words.ex: He shouted a malediction at the thief.
words.ex_cn: 他对着小偷咒骂了一句。
words.en: A malediction is a curse or the act of uttering a curse.

words.ex: The monks live in a quiet monastery.
words.ex_cn: 僧侣们住在一座安静的修道院里。
words.en: A monastery is a building or collection of buildings in which monks live and work.

words.ex: The priest offered the oblation to the altar.
words.ex_cn: 牧师将祭品献给了祭坛。
words.en: An oblation is something that is offered to a god or to a religious purpose, especially as part of a ceremony.

words.ex: The Pantheon is an ancient temple in Rome.
words.ex_cn: 万神庙是罗马的一座古代神庙。
words.en: A pantheon is a group of particularly respected, famous, or important people, or a temple dedicated to all the gods of a particular polytheistic religion.

words.ex: He received the sacrament on Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他在周日领受了圣礼。
words.en: A sacrament is a Christian religious ceremony or ritual regarded as imparting divine grace, such as baptism, the Eucharist, and (in the Roman Catholic and many Orthodox Churches) penance and anointing of the sick.

words.ex: The sect held unusual beliefs that differed from the main religion.
words.ex_cn: 这个派别的信仰与主流宗教不同。
words.en: A sect is a group of people who have different religious beliefs from other people in the same religion.

words.tr: n. （西印度群岛人、尤其是海地人信奉的）伏都教
words.ex: He believes in voodoo and wears a charm for luck.
words.ex_cn: 他相信伏都教，戴一个护身符求好运。
words.en: Voodoo is a religion practiced chiefly in Haiti and other parts of the Caribbean, involving the worship of spirits and the use of magic.

words.tr: n. 阿拉贝斯克舞姿；阿拉伯式花纹
words.ex: The artist used arabesque patterns to decorate the walls.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家使用蔓藤花纹来装饰墙壁。
words.en: An arabesque is a complex, ornate design of intertwined flowing lines, originally found in Arabic art, or a ballet position in which the dancer stands on one leg with the other leg extended behind.

words.tr:
adj. 先锋的；前卫的
n. 先锋派；前卫
words.ex: The artist uses avant-garde styles in her paintings.
words.ex_cn: 这位艺术家在她的画作中使用前卫的风格。
words.en: Avant-garde is used to describe people or works that are experimental or innovative, particularly in the arts.

words.tr:
n. 半身像；胸部；搜捕
v. 打碎；搜捕
adj. 破产的；打碎的
words.ex: The museum has a marble bust of the ancient king.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆里有一座古代国王的大理石半身像。
words.en: A bust is a sculpture of a person's head, shoulders, and chest. As a verb, to bust means to break something, to arrest someone, or to go bankrupt.

words.ex: He practices calligraphy every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上练习书法。
words.en: Calligraphy is the art of producing decorative handwriting or lettering with a pen or brush.

words.tr: n. 小配角；小品文；浮雕宝石
words.ex: She appeared in a cameo role in the film.
words.ex_cn: 她在电影中扮演了一个配角。
words.en: A cameo is a small but noticeable part in a film or play, often played by a famous actor or actress. It can also refer to a piece of jewelry consisting of a raised design on a background of a different color.

words.ex: My brother watches cartoon every evening.
words.ex_cn: 我弟弟每天晚上看卡通片。
words.en: A cartoon is a humorous drawing or series of drawings in a newspaper or magazine, or a film made using animation techniques.

words.ex: He carved the meat with a sharp knife.
words.ex_cn: 他用一把锋利的刀切开了肉。
words.en: To carve means to cut into a hard material in order to produce an object, design, or inscription.

words.tr:
n. 陶瓷制品；陶瓷器；
adj. 陶质的；制陶的；
words.ex: He bought a ceramic bowl at the market.
words.ex_cn: 他在市场上买了一个陶瓷碗。
words.en: Ceramic is a hard material that is made by baking clay or similar substances at high temperatures. It is used to make things such as tiles, dishes, and statues.

words.tr: n. 制陶艺术；制陶工艺；
words.ex: He learned ceramics from his grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 他从祖父那里学习了制陶艺术。
words.en: The art of making objects by shaping pieces of clay and then baking them until they are hard.

words.tr:
n. 明显的伪装；装模作样
(~s：看手势猜字谜游戏)
words.ex: His apology was a charade to hide his true feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他的道歉是一种明显的伪装，为了隐藏他真实的情感。
words.en: A charade is a situation in which people pretend that something is true when it clearly is not, or a game in which one team acts out a word or phrase for the other team to guess.

words.tr:
v. 追逐；
n. 追逐；
words.ex: The dog chases the cat every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗每天早上追逐猫。
words.en: To chase someone or something means to quickly follow them or it in order to catch them.

words.tr: n. 编舞艺术；舞蹈编排；
words.ex: The dancer praised the choreography of the ballet.
words.ex_cn: 这位舞者称赞了这部芭蕾舞的编舞艺术。
words.en: Choreography is the art of designing sequences of movements in which motion, form, or both are specified. Choreography may also refer to the design itself. A choreographer is one who creates choreographies by practicing the art of choreography.

words.tr: n. 拼贴画；拼贴艺术；杂烩
words.ex: He made a collage from old magazine pictures.
words.ex_cn: 他用旧杂志的图片做了一幅拼贴画。
words.en: A collage is a picture that has been made by sticking pieces of colored paper, cloth, or photographs onto a surface.

words.ex: The wizard conjure a fireball with ancient words.
words.ex_cn: 巫师用古老的咒语召唤出一个火球。
words.en: If you conjure something out of nothing, you make it appear as if by magic.

words.ex: She washed the crockery after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 她晚饭后洗了餐具。
words.en: Crockery refers to plates, dishes, cups, and other similar items, especially ones made of earthenware or china.

words.ex: The daguerreotype was one of the earliest photographic processes.
words.ex_cn: 银版照相法是最早的摄影方法之一。
words.en: An early photographic process employing an iodine-sensitized silvered plate and mercury vapor.

words.tr: v. 加浮雕花纹于；饰以浮饰；使凸出
words.ex: He embosses the card with his name.
words.ex_cn: 他把名字压印在卡片上。
words.en: To decorate a surface by making raised designs or patterns on it.

words.tr: v. 刺绣；绣（花）；加以渲染（或润色）
words.ex: She embroiders flowers on the pillow.
words.ex_cn: 她在枕头上刺绣花朵。
words.en: To embroider means to decorate cloth or other material by sewing patterns or pictures on it with colored threads.

words.ex: He brushed his teeth to protect the enamel.
words.ex_cn: 他刷牙以保护牙釉质。
words.en: A hard, glossy substance that is applied to metal, glass, or pottery for decoration or protection.

words.ex: He engraves his name on the ring.
words.ex_cn: 他把名字刻在戒指上。
words.en: To engrave means to cut or carve a design or letters into a hard surface, or to be strongly impressed in someone's memory.

words.tr:
n. 蚀刻版画
v. 蚀刻；凿刻；“etch”的现在分词
words.ex: The museum displayed a collection of etchings from the 18th century.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆展出了18世纪的蚀刻版画收藏。
words.en: An etching is a picture printed from a metal plate that has had a design cut into it with acid.

words.ex: He bought a small figurine from the market.
words.ex_cn: 他从市场上买了一个小雕像。
words.en: A figurine is a small ornamental statuette.

words.ex: The jeweler crafted a delicate filigree pendant.
words.ex_cn: 珠宝匠制作了一个精致的金银丝细工吊坠。
words.en: Filigree is ornamental work of fine (typically gold or silver) wire formed into delicate tracery.

words.tr:
n. 壁画
v. 作壁画
words.ex: The artist painted a fresco on the church wall.
words.ex_cn: 这位艺术家在教堂的墙上画了一幅湿壁画。
words.en: A fresco is a picture that is painted on a plastered wall when the plaster is still wet.

words.ex: He put together a jigsaw puzzle on the table.
words.ex_cn: 他在桌子上拼了一幅拼图。
words.en: A jigsaw puzzle is a puzzle consisting of small irregularly cut pieces that are to be fitted together to form a picture.

words.ex: He performed a mime on the street.
words.ex_cn: 他在街上表演了哑剧。
words.en: A mime is a form of performance art where the performer uses gestures and movements without speech to convey a story or emotion. As a verb, to mime means to imitate or mimic actions or expressions without using words.

words.ex: The ballroom was filled with couples dancing the minuet.
words.ex_cn: 舞厅里充满了跳小步舞的情侣。
words.en: A minuet is a slow, stately ballroom dance for two in triple time, popular especially in the 18th century.

words.tr: n. 蒙太奇；画面剪辑；合成画；大杂烩
words.ex: The movie ends with a montage of old photos.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影以一组旧照片的蒙太奇结尾。
words.en: A montage is a technique in film editing in which a series of short shots are edited into a sequence to condense space, time, and information.

words.tr: n. 缝纫；刺绣；针线活；缝制品；绣制品
words.ex: She does needlework every evening.
words.ex_cn: 她每天晚上做针线活。
words.en: Needlework is the activity of sewing or the things that are sewn.

words.tr:
n. 哑剧；（英）圣诞童话剧
v. 打手势；演哑剧
words.ex: The children laughed at the clown's pantomime.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们笑了，因为小丑的哑剧表演。
words.en: Pantomime is a type of entertainment where performers express a story or represent characters through gestures and body movements without using speech.

words.ex: The petroglyphs were carved by ancient civilizations.
words.ex_cn: 这些岩石雕刻是由古代文明刻制的。
words.en: A petroglyph is a carving or inscription on a rock surface, especially one made by prehistoric people.

words.tr:
n. 单脚尖旋转
v. 用脚尖旋转；表演旋转舞
words.ex: She executed a perfect pirouette.
words.ex_cn: 她完成了一个完美的单脚尖旋转。
words.en: In ballet, a pirouette is a turn or spin on one foot, typically with the raised foot touching the knee of the supporting leg.

words.tr: n. 陶器；制陶手艺；陶器作坊；
words.ex: He makes pottery in his backyard studio.
words.ex_cn: 他在后院的工作室制作陶器。
words.en: Objects such as pots, dishes, and vases that are made out of clay and then baked at high temperatures to make them hard.

words.ex: The scientist used a sampler to collect water from the river.
words.ex_cn: 科学家使用采样器从河中采集水样。
words.en: A sampler is a piece of embroidery worked in various stitches as a specimen of skill, typically containing the alphabet, some verses, or the maker's name.

words.ex: He has a sartorial style that impresses everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种令人印象深刻的服装风格。
words.en: Sartorial relates to tailoring, clothes, or style of dress.

words.ex: He sculpted a statue from clay.
words.ex_cn: 他用黏土雕刻了一座雕像。
words.en: To sculpt means to create or represent something by carving, casting, or other shaping techniques.

words.ex: The circus had a sideshow with magic tricks.
words.ex_cn: 马戏团有一个包含魔术表演的穿插表演。
words.en: A sideshow is a small show or performance that is separate from but related to the main event, often providing entertainment or additional attractions.

words.tr:
n. 组雕
adj. 雕塑艺术的
words.ex: The museum's collection includes a vast array of ancient statuary.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆的收藏包括大量的古代雕像。
words.en: Statuary refers to statues collectively, or the art of making statues.

words.tr:
n. 针脚；缝线；一针
v. 缝；缝合
words.ex: She sews a stitch to fix the tear.
words.ex_cn: 她缝一针来补破洞。
words.en: A stitch is a piece of thread that has been used to sew the edges of a wound together. It can also refer to a loop of thread or yarn resulting from a single pass or movement of the needle in sewing, knitting, or crocheting.

words.tr:
n. 滑稽拙劣的模仿；嘲弄；歪曲
v. 滑稽化；嘲弄
words.ex: The trial was a travesty of justice.
words.ex_cn: 这场审判是对正义的嘲弄。
words.en: If you describe something as a travesty of another thing, you mean that it is a very bad representation of that other thing.

words.tr: adj. 多方面的；有多种技能的；
words.ex: He is a versatile player who can play many positions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名多方面的运动员，能打多个位置。
words.en: Able to adapt or be adapted to many different functions or activities.

words.tr: n. 木刻；木刻印版；木版画
words.ex: The artist created a beautiful woodcut of the landscape.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家创作了一幅美丽的风景木刻画。
words.en: A woodcut is a picture or design printed from a block of wood that has been carved with a knife or chisel.

words.tr: n. 编号作品；乐曲；艺术作品
words.ex: The composer's latest opus has received critical acclaim.
words.ex_cn: 这位作曲家的最新作品获得了评论界的好评。
words.en: An opus is a creative work, especially a musical composition or set of compositions numbered in order of publication.

words.tr:
adj. 有图画的；图示的
n. 画报
words.ex: The book has a pictorial guide to plants.
words.ex_cn: 这本书有一本植物的图解指南。
words.en: A pictorial representation or image is one that is made using pictures or shows things in a way that pictures do.

words.ex: They danced the tango at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他们在聚会上跳了探戈舞。
words.en: A ballroom dance of Latin American origin in 2/4 or 4/4 time with a basic pattern of step-step-step-step-close and characterized by long pauses and stylized body positions.

words.tr:
adj. 洛可可式的；旧式的；过分修饰的
n. 洛可可式
words.ex: The room has rococo decorations with lots of curves and gold.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间有大量曲线和金色的洛可可装饰。
words.en: Rococo is a style of architecture, music, and art that emerged in France in the early 18th century, characterized by elaborate ornamentation and asymmetrical values.

words.tr:
n. 音高；球场；程度（最高点）；宣传论点；
v. 扎营；
words.ex: The singer changed the pitch of her voice.
words.ex_cn: 歌手改变了她声音的音高。
words.en: Pitch can refer to the highness or lowness of a sound, the act of throwing something, or a thick, black, sticky substance used for paving roads or waterproofing.

words.ex: The room has good acoustic properties.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间有良好的声音效果。
words.en: Relating to sound or the sense of hearing.

words.ex: She sang a beautiful aria at the opera.
words.ex_cn: 她在歌剧上唱了一段优美的咏叹调。
words.en: An aria is a song for one voice in an opera, often expressing a character's emotions.

words.tr: adj. 没有韵律的；心律不齐的
words.ex: His heart beats in an arrhythmic pattern.
words.ex_cn: 他的心跳呈不规则节律。
words.en: If someone has an arrhythmic heartbeat, the beats of their heart are not regular.

words.ex: The piece is an example of atonal music.
words.ex_cn: 这首作品是无调音乐的一个例子。
words.en: Atonal music is music that lacks a tonal center or key.

words.ex: He sang a old ballad about love and war.
words.ex_cn: 他唱了一首关于爱情与战争的老民谣。
words.en: A ballad is a type of song that tells a story, often a folk song or a slow romantic song.

words.tr: n. 大胆的尝试；精湛的技艺
words.ex: Her bravura performance left the audience in awe.
words.ex_cn: 她精湛的表演让观众惊叹不已。
words.en: A bravura performance is one that is very skillful and exciting.

words.ex: The cacophonous noise made her cover her ears.
words.ex_cn: 刺耳的噪音让她捂住了耳朵。
words.en: If you describe a mixture of sounds as cacophonous, you mean that they are loud and unpleasant.

words.ex: The cacophony of car horns made it hard to think.
words.ex_cn: 汽车喇叭的刺耳噪音让人难以思考。
words.en: A cacophony is a mixture of loud and usually unpleasant sounds.

words.ex: He plays the cello every evening.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上拉大提琴。
words.en: A cello is a large stringed instrument of the violin family, tuned an octave below the viola.

words.ex: The choir sings every Sunday in church.
words.ex_cn: 唱诗班每周日在教堂唱歌。
words.en: A choir is a group of people who sing together, especially in a church or school.

words.ex: The guitarist played a C major chord.
words.ex_cn: 吉他手弹了一个C大和弦。
words.en: A chord is a group of three or more musical notes played together.

words.tr:
v. 合唱；异口同声地说
n. 合唱团；合唱
words.ex: They chorus when the song reaches the bridge.
words.ex_cn: 当歌曲进行到桥段时，他们一起合唱。
words.en: A chorus is a part of a song which is repeated after each verse, or a group of people who sing together.

words.tr:
adj. 响亮清晰的
n. 号角
words.ex: The clarion call for change inspired everyone.
words.ex_cn: 那声清晰的变革号召激励了每个人。
words.en: A clarion is a type of trumpet with a clear, shrill tone, used historically for signaling or in military contexts. It can also refer to something that is loud and clear, especially in the context of a call to action.

words.ex: The coda of the symphony brought the concert to a powerful conclusion.
words.ex_cn: 交响乐的终曲为音乐会带来了强有力的结束。
words.en: The concluding passage of a piece or movement, typically forming an addition to the basic structure.

words.ex: He is a composer who writes music for movies.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位为电影作曲的作曲家。
words.en: A composer is a person who writes music, especially classical music.

words.ex: He plays a violin concerto at the concert.
words.ex_cn: 他在音乐会上演奏一首小提琴协奏曲。
words.en: A concerto is a musical composition usually composed in three parts or movements, in which one solo instrument is accompanied by an orchestra.

words.ex: The plants grow in the conservatory.
words.ex_cn: 植物在温室里生长。
words.en: A conservatory is a room with glass walls and a glass roof, which is built on the side of a house. It is used as a sun lounge or for growing plants. It can also refer to a school where people are trained in music or acting.

words.tr: n. 声音渐增；高潮；顶峰
words.ex: The music reached a loud crescendo at the end.
words.ex_cn: 音乐在结尾处达到响亮的高潮。
words.en: A crescendo is a gradual increase in loudness or intensity in music, or any situation where there is a gradual increase in intensity.

words.tr: n. 挽歌；哀歌；忧伤的歌
words.ex: They sang a slow dirge at the funeral.
words.ex_cn: 他们在葬礼上唱了一首缓慢的哀歌。
words.en: A dirge is a slow, sad song or piece of music, sometimes played at a funeral.

words.tr: n. 音乐唱片分类目录；录音作品目录
words.ex: The discography includes all of the artist's albums and singles.
words.ex_cn: 这份唱片目录包括了这位艺术家的所有专辑和单曲。
words.en: A discography is a list or catalog of musical recordings by a particular artist or group.

words.ex: He sang a short ditty while walking home.
words.ex_cn: 他一边走回家一边唱了一首小曲。
words.en: A ditty is a short simple song.

words.ex: They sing a duet at the school concert.
