words.ex: He threw away a trifle of money on candy.
words.ex_cn: 他花了一点钱买糖果。
words.en: A trifle is something that is considered to have little importance, value, or significance. It can also refer to a small amount of something. As a verb, to trifle means to treat someone or something without seriousness or respect.

words.tr: n. 琐事；微不足道的东西；各种科目知识
words.ex: He loves to share trivia at dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在晚餐时分享冷知识。
words.en: Trivia refers to unimportant matters or pieces of information that are considered to be of little value or significance.

words.ex: The mistake was trivial and didn't affect the result.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误不重要，没有影响结果。
words.en: If you describe something as trivial, you mean that it is not important or significant, or is not worth serious consideration.

words.ex: He made a venial mistake in the report.
words.ex_cn: 他在报告中犯了一个可以原谅的错误。
words.en: If you describe a wrong action as venial, you mean that it is not very serious or grave, and therefore easy to forgive.

words.ex: The pond is shallow, so you can see the bottom.
words.ex_cn: 这个池塘很浅，所以你能看到底部。
words.en: If something is shallow, it does not extend far down from the top surface.

chapters.name: Word List 20 属性 程度

words.ex: He gave an absolute yes to the offer.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个提议给出了完全肯定的回答。
words.en: Absolute means complete and total, or not limited in any way.

words.tr: adj. 深不可测的；极坏的；糟透的
words.ex: The abysmal depth of the ocean scared the divers.
words.ex_cn: 海洋的深不可测吓到了潜水员。
words.en: If you describe a situation or the condition of something as abysmal, you think that it is very bad or poor in quality.

words.tr: adj. 绝对的；确定无疑的；分类的
words.ex: He gave a categorical no to the offer.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个提议给出了明确的拒绝。
words.en: If you are categorical about something, you state your views very definitely and firmly.

words.ex: The teacher gave a comprehensive review before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 老师在考试前给了一个全面的复习。
words.en: Something that is comprehensive includes everything that is needed or relevant.

words.tr:
v. 完成；使完美；圆房
adj. 完美的；至上的；圆满的
words.ex: He consummated the deal with a handshake.
words.ex_cn: 他用握手完成了这笔交易。
words.en: To consummate means to make something complete or perfect, often used in the context of a marriage or an agreement. It can also describe someone who is extremely skilled in a particular area.

words.ex: He led a dissolute life after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后过着放荡的生活。
words.en: If you describe someone as dissolute, you mean they behave in a way that is considered immoral because they do things such as drink or have sex too much.

words.ex: The company made drastic cuts to save money.
words.ex_cn: 公司进行了急剧的削减以节省资金。
words.en: If you describe a change or action as drastic, you mean that it is extreme and often severe.

words.ex: His egregious mistake cost the team the game.
words.ex_cn: 他严重的错误让球队输掉了比赛。
words.en: An egregious error or failure is extremely bad and noticeable.

words.ex: He read the book in its entirety.
words.ex_cn: 他从头到尾读了这本书。
words.en: The whole of something, especially when considered as a single unit.

words.ex: The car exceeded the speed limit.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车超过了限速。
words.en: To be greater in quantity, degree, or intensity than something else.

words.tr:
n. 过量；过度；超过；
adj. 多余的；
words.ex: The excess of sugar in his diet caused health problems.
words.ex_cn: 他饮食中糖分过量导致了健康问题。
words.en: An excess of something is a larger amount than is needed, allowed, or usual.

words.ex: The report gives an exhaustive list of all the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这份报告给出了所有规则的详尽列表。
words.en: If you describe a study, search, or list as exhaustive, you mean that it is very thorough and complete.

words.tr: adj. 过度的；过高的；过分的；
words.ex: The restaurant charged an exorbitant price for a small salad.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅对一份小沙拉要了过高的价格。
words.en: If you describe something such as a price or fee as exorbitant, you are emphasizing that it is much higher than it should be.

words.ex: The book has a finite number of pages.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的页数是有限的。
words.en: Something that is finite has a definite fixed size or extent.

words.ex: The gross income of the company is $5 million.
words.ex_cn: 公司的总收入是500万美元。
words.en: If you describe something as gross, you mean it is very obvious, unacceptable, or unpleasant.

words.ex: He spent inordinate time on video games.
words.ex_cn: 他花了过多的时间玩电子游戏。
words.en: If you describe something as inordinate, you are emphasizing that it is unusually or excessively large in amount or degree.

words.ex: The inquisitive child asked many questions about the stars.
words.ex_cn: 这个好奇的孩子问了很多关于星星的问题。
words.en: If you describe someone as inquisitive, you mean that they are interested in a lot of different things and want to find out more about them.

words.ex: The vase remained intact after the fall.
words.ex_cn: 花瓶从高处摔下后依然完整无缺。
words.en: Something that is intact is complete and has not been damaged or changed.

words.ex: Honesty is an integral part of a good relationship.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是良好关系中不可或缺的一部分。
words.en: Something that is integral is very important or necessary. If something is an integral part of a whole, it is an essential part of that whole.

words.ex: He tried to integrate into the new school community.
words.ex_cn: 他试图融入新的学校群体。
words.en: If someone integrates into a social group, or is integrated into it, they behave in such a way that they become part of the group or are accepted into it.

words.ex: He showed maturity when he apologized for his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 当他为自己的错误道歉时，表现出了成熟。
words.en: Maturity is the state of being fully developed or grown, or the time when a financial arrangement becomes ready to be paid.

words.tr: adj. 爱发号施令的；多管闲事的
words.ex: The officious clerk refused to help unless I filled out another form.
words.ex_cn: 那位爱多管闲事的职员拒绝帮忙，除非我再填一份表格。
words.en: If you describe someone as officious, you are critical of them because they are eager to tell people what to do when you think they should not.

words.tr: adj. 无所不在的；遍及各处的
words.ex: The smell of bread is omnipresent in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 早晨面包的香味无处不在。
words.en: If you describe something as omnipresent, you mean that it seems to be everywhere at the same time.

words.ex: The child suffered from overexposure to the sun.
words.ex_cn: 孩子因暴晒而受苦。
words.en: Exposure to an excessive amount of something, especially to something harmful or to the public eye.

words.tr: v. 伸得过长；做得过火；走过头
words.ex: He overreachs his authority and makes bad decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他越权行事，做出了错误的决定。
words.en: If you say that someone overreaches themselves, you mean that they fail at something because they are trying to do more than they are able to.

words.tr: adj. 过分劳累的；过度兴奋的；过分紧张的
words.ex: He felt overwrought after working 16 hours straight.
words.ex_cn: 他连续工作了16个小时，感到精疲力尽。
words.en: If someone is overwrought, they are very upset and are not thinking or behaving calmly or sensibly.

words.ex: She pampered her baby with warm baths and soft blankets.
words.ex_cn: 她用温水浴和柔软的毯子细心照顾她的婴儿。
words.en: To treat someone very kindly, often too kindly, by letting them have or do whatever they want.

words.ex: He only read the partial report.
words.ex_cn: 他只读了部分报告。
words.en: If you describe something as partial, you mean that it is not complete or whole.

words.tr: adj. 放任的；纵容的；许可的
words.ex: Her parents are permissive and let her stay out late.
words.ex_cn: 她的父母很宽容，让她很晚才回家。
words.en: A permissive person, society, or system allows people a lot of freedom to do what they want.

words.tr:
adj. 全体参加的；无限的；完全的
n. 全会；全体会议
words.ex: The plenary session started at 9 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 全体会议在上午九点开始。
words.en: A plenary session or meeting is one that is attended by everyone who has the right to attend.

words.ex: The garden was in a state of plenitude, with flowers blooming everywhere.
words.ex_cn: 花园里繁花似锦，处处充满生机。
words.en: The state of being full or complete; abundance.

words.ex: There is a plentitude of food at the party.
words.ex_cn: 聚会上食物非常多。
words.en: Plentitude refers to a large or sufficient quantity or supply of something.

words.ex: There is a plethora of choices on the menu.
words.ex_cn: 菜单上有太多的选择。
words.en: A plethora of something is a very large quantity of it, especially an amount that is greater than you need, want, or can cope with.

words.ex: He left school at 15, which was too premature.
words.ex_cn: 他15岁就离开了学校，这太早了。
words.en: Happening or done before the usual or expected time; not fully developed or mature.

words.tr: adj. 过分拘谨的；装正经的
words.ex: She is prudish about wearing shorts in public.
words.ex_cn: 她对在公共场合穿短裤感到拘谨。
words.en: If you describe someone as prudish, you mean that they are too easily shocked by things relating to sex.

words.tr: adj. 泛滥的；猖獗的；蔓生的
words.ex: Rumors are rampant in the small town.
words.ex_cn: 谣言在这个小镇上四处流传。
words.en: If you describe something bad, such as a crime or disease, as rampant, you mean that it is very common and is increasing in an uncontrolled way.

words.ex: The company announced redundancy due to low profits.
words.ex_cn: 公司因利润低下宣布裁员。
words.en: Redundancy refers to the state of being not or no longer needed or useful; the inclusion of extra components which are not strictly necessary to functioning, in case of failure in other components; or the dismissal of employees from work for being no longer necessary.

words.ex: The extra chair is redundant because we have enough seats.
words.ex_cn: 这把额外的椅子是多余的，因为我们已经有足够的座位了。
words.en: If you are made redundant, your employer tells you to leave because your job is no longer necessary or because there is no more work for you.

words.ex: It was sheer luck that he won the game.
words.ex_cn: 他赢了比赛完全是运气。
words.en: Sheer is used to emphasize that a state or situation is complete and does not involve or is not mixed with anything else.

words.ex: He felt satiety after eating a large meal.
words.ex_cn: 他吃完一顿大餐后感到饱足。
words.en: Satiety is the state of being completely satisfied, especially with food or pleasure, so that you could not have any more.

words.tr: adj. 完全的；荒凉的；光秃秃的；僵硬的；严厉的
words.ex: There was a stark difference between the two results.
words.ex_cn: 这两个结果之间有完全的差异。
words.en: Stark means complete, severe, or obvious in a way that is impossible to avoid noticing.

words.ex: The supreme leader makes the final decision.
words.ex_cn: 至上的领导人做出最终决定。
words.en: If you say that something is supreme, you mean that it is the most important or the best of its kind.

words.tr:
v. 使饮食过度；吃得过量；过分沉溺
n. 过量；过度
words.ex: He surfeited on pizza and felt sick.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多披萨，感到恶心。
words.en: An excessive amount of something, especially food or drink.

words.ex: The farm has a surplus of apples this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年农场苹果过剩。
words.en: A surplus is an amount of something that is extra or more than what is needed.

words.ex: The synthesis of ideas helped solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 这些想法的综合帮助解决了问题。
words.en: The act of combining different ideas, influences, or objects into a new and coherent whole.

words.tr: adj. 违背良心的；无节制的；过度的
words.ex: The prices they were charging were unconscionable.
words.ex_cn: 他们收取的价格是不合理的。
words.en: If you describe something as unconscionable, you mean that it is morally unacceptable, often because it is too large, too extreme, or too severe.

words.tr: v. 喊价过低；出价过低；出较低的价钱
words.ex: He underbid the other contractors to win the job.
words.ex_cn: 他以更低的报价击败了其他承包商，赢得了这份工作。
words.en: To bid lower than another, especially in a competitive situation such as an auction or a tender.

words.tr: adj. 没有减轻的；十足的；绝对的
words.ex: The criticism was unmitigated and harsh.
words.ex_cn: 批评是全然的严厉。
words.en: If you describe something as unmitigated, you are emphasizing that it is completely bad or good, without any qualification.

words.tr: adj. 不合格的；没资格的；完全的；绝对的
words.ex: He is unqualified for the job.
words.ex_cn: 他没有资格胜任这份工作。
words.en: If you are unqualified for something, you do not have the qualifications that are needed for it. It can also mean complete or total, without any doubt or limitation.

words.tr: adj. 未被预订的；无保留的；不隐瞒的
words.ex: He gave an unreserved apology.
words.ex_cn: 他毫无保留地道歉了。
words.en: If you describe someone's feelings or behaviour as unreserved, you mean that they have expressed their feelings or done something in a very open and full way.

words.ex: It was an utter mistake.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个完全的错误。
words.en: To say something or to make a sound with your voice; complete or absolute.

words.ex: He is a thoroughgoing supporter of environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的彻底支持者。
words.en: If you describe someone as thoroughgoing, you mean that they are very thorough and complete in what they do.

words.ex: He reads the unabridged version of the novel.
words.ex_cn: 他读这部小说的完整版。
words.en: An unabridged book, speech, or article is in its original form and has not been made shorter.

words.tr: adj. 未经缓和的；无节制的；没有调和好的
words.ex: He gave an untempered response to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题做出了毫无节制的回应。
words.en: Not moderated or controlled; not tempered.

words.tr: adj. 二年级学生的；一知半解的；自信但幼稚浅薄的
words.ex: His sophomoric remarks showed a lack of depth in understanding.
words.ex_cn: 他一知半解的评论显示了他理解上的浅薄。
words.en: If you describe something as sophomoric, you mean that it is silly and immature, often in a way that is typical of a young person who is trying to be clever or funny.

words.ex: He is still immature and often cries when upset.
words.ex_cn: 他仍然不成熟，生气时经常哭。
words.en: If you describe someone as immature, you are criticizing them because they do not behave in a sensible or responsible way, or because they have not developed emotionally or mentally to the level that is normal for their age.

words.ex: He is overly careful with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他花钱过于谨慎。
words.en: To an excessive degree.

chapters.name: Word List 20 属性 持续

words.ex: He has a chronic cough that lasts for months.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个持续数月的慢性咳嗽。
words.en: A chronic illness or condition lasts for a long time and cannot be cured, but it can usually be controlled.

words.ex: His speech was coherent and easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲连贯且易于理解。
words.en: If something is coherent, it is well planned, so that it is clear and sensible and all its parts go well with each other.

words.ex: The duration of the movie is two hours.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的持续时间是两小时。
words.en: The duration of an event or state is the time during which it happens or exists.

words.ex: He cares only about earthly things like money and fame.
words.ex_cn: 他只关心金钱和名声这样的现世之物。
words.en: Of or relating to the earth or human life on earth.

words.tr: adj. 持久的；不朽的； v. 忍受；“endure”的现在分词；
words.ex: This is an enduring friendship.
words.ex_cn: 这是一段持久的友谊。
words.en: Lasting for a long time; continuing or enduring over a period of time.

words.ex: The Industrial Revolution was a new epoch in history.
words.ex_cn: 工业革命是历史上一个新时代。
words.en: An epoch is a period of time in history or a person's life, typically one marked by notable events or particular characteristics.

words.ex: The stars seem eternal in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中的星星看起来是永久的。
words.en: If something is eternal, it lasts forever.

words.tr: adj. 永久的；永恒的；经久不变的
words.ex: The love between them is everlasting.
words.ex_cn: 他们之间的爱是永恒的。
words.en: Something that is everlasting lasts forever or for a very long time.

words.ex: That park was in its heyday in the 1990s.
words.ex_cn: 那个公园在20世纪90年代是它的鼎盛时期。
words.en: The period of a person's or thing's greatest success, popularity, or vigor.

words.ex: Hitherto, no one has solved the problem.
words.ex_cn: 迄今为止，没有人解决过这个问题。
words.en: Until now or until the point in time under discussion.

words.ex: Legends say that some heroes are immortal.
words.ex_cn: 传说有些英雄是不死的。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as immortal, you mean that they are so famous or popular that they will be remembered for a very long time.

words.tr: adj. 不断的；不停的；连续的
words.ex: The baby cried with incessant noise.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿不停地哭闹。
words.en: If you say that something is incessant, you are emphasizing that it continues without stopping.

words.ex: The stars seem to go on to infinity.
words.ex_cn: 星星似乎延伸到无限。
words.en: Infinity is a concept of something that is unlimited, endless, without bound.

words.tr: adj. 持久的；恒久的； v. 持续；“last”的现在分词；
words.ex: The friendship between them is lasting.
words.ex_cn: 他们之间的友谊是持久的。
words.en: Something that is lasting continues to exist or have an effect for a very long time.

words.tr:
n. 租契；
v. 出租；
words.ex: He signed a lease for the apartment.
words.ex_cn: 他签了公寓的租契。
words.en: A lease is a legal agreement by which the owner of a building, a piece of land, or something such as a car allows someone else to use it for a period of time in return for money.

words.ex: The millennium began in the year 2000.
words.ex_cn: 一千年始于2000年。
words.en: A millennium is a period of one thousand years.

words.tr: adj. 多年生的；反复出现的；
words.ex: These perennial flowers bloom every year.
words.ex_cn: 这些多年生的花每年都会开花。
words.en: A perennial plant is one that lives for more than two years, often flowering and producing seeds multiple times over its lifespan.

words.ex: The permanence of the statue reminds us of history.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像的永久性让我们想起历史。
words.en: The state or quality of lasting or remaining unchanged indefinitely.

words.ex: He made a permanent change to his lifestyle.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的生活方式做出了永久的改变。
words.en: Something that is permanent exists or happens all the time, or exists for a long time without changing.

words.ex: The machine makes a perpetual noise.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器发出持续的噪音。
words.en: Something that is perpetual continues indefinitely or for a very long time without interruption.

words.tr: v. 使（尤指不好的情形、体系、信仰）持续、长存；
words.ex: The system perpetuates inequality among the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这个体系使贫困人群的不平等持续存在。
words.en: To perpetuate something means to cause it to continue, especially for a long time.

words.ex: The perpetuation of bad habits hurts progress.
words.ex_cn: 坏习惯的延续会阻碍进步。
words.en: The act of causing something to continue indefinitely or the state of being continued indefinitely.

words.tr:
adj. 连续的；连环的
n. 连续剧；连载小说
words.ex: He watched the serial episodes every night.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上观看连续的剧集。
words.en: A serial is a story or play that is broadcast on television or radio in several parts at fixed times, or a story that is published in a magazine or newspaper in several parts.

words.tr: adj. 持久的；持续不变的； v. 维持；支撑；“sustain”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The team showed sustained effort throughout the game.
words.ex_cn: 整个比赛中，这支队伍都展现了持久的努力。
words.en: Continuing for an extended period or without interruption.

words.ex: The teacher has a long tenure at the school.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师在学校有很长的任期。
words.en: The period during which an office is held; the status of holding one's position on a permanent basis.

words.ex: The rain was unremitting all day.
words.ex_cn: 雨一整天都没有停过。
words.en: If you describe someone's effort or activity as unremitting, you mean that it is continued without stopping or becoming less intense.

words.tr: adj. 保留的； v. 保留；“reserve”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The seats are reserved for students.
words.ex_cn: 这些座位是为学生保留的。
words.en: If something is reserved, it is kept specially for a particular purpose or person.

words.ex: The volcano began to disgorge lava.
words.ex_cn: 火山开始喷出岩浆。
words.en: If something disgorges its contents or if it is disgorged, its contents come out, often in a sudden and violent way.

words.ex: The air was filled with the effluvia of decaying organic matter.
words.ex_cn: 空气中充满了腐烂有机物的臭气。
words.en: Effluvia refers to unpleasant or harmful odors or fumes that are emitted from something, typically waste or decaying matter.

words.ex: The fetid smell came from the old trash.
words.ex_cn: 那股恶臭来自旧垃圾。
words.en: Having an extremely unpleasant smell.

words.tr: adj. 明目张胆的；丑恶可耻的；公然的
words.ex: He made a flagrant mistake during the game.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中犯了一个明显的错误。
words.en: If you describe an action as flagrant, you mean that it is done in an open and obvious way and is intended to shock or offend people.

words.ex: The old library had a fusty smell.
words.ex_cn: 那间旧图书馆有一股发霉的味道。
words.en: If you describe something as fusty, you mean that it is old-fashioned and not interesting or exciting.

words.ex: The movie showed a gruesome accident.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了一起令人毛骨悚然的事故。
words.en: Something that is gruesome is extremely unpleasant and shocking, especially because it involves death or injury.

words.ex: The malodor from the garbage was unbearable.
words.ex_cn: 垃圾的恶臭让人难以忍受。
words.en: An unpleasant or offensive smell.

words.ex: The malodor from the garbage was unbearable.
words.ex_cn: 垃圾的恶臭让人难以忍受。
words.en: An unpleasant or offensive smell.

words.tr: adj. 沙哑的；粗声的；喧闹的
words.ex: His raucous voice made it hard to understand him.
words.ex_cn: 他沙哑的声音让他很难被听清楚。
words.en: A raucous sound is loud and harsh.

words.ex: The surface of the wood roughened over time.
words.ex_cn: 随着时间的推移，木头的表面变得粗糙了。
words.en: To make or become rough.

words.tr: adj. 粗糙的；淫秽的；困难重重的
words.ex: The scabrous surface of the old book felt rough to the touch.
words.ex_cn: 这本旧书的粗糙表面摸起来很粗糙。
words.en: If you describe something as scabrous, you mean that it is rough and covered with small points or lumps, or that it is difficult to deal with because it is complicated or unpleasant.

words.ex: The amplitude of the sound is very high.
words.ex_cn: 声音的振幅非常高。
words.en: The extent or range of a quality, property, process, or phenomenon: magnitude.

words.ex: He uses an astronomical telescope to watch stars.
words.ex_cn: 他用一架天文望远镜观察星星。
words.en: If you describe an amount, especially the cost of something as astronomical, you are emphasizing that it is very large indeed.

words.ex: The statue was colossal, taller than the building.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像巨大，比大楼还高。
words.en: If you describe something as colossal, you are emphasizing that it is very large.

words.ex: The elephant is enormous.
words.ex_cn: 这头大象非常巨大。
words.en: If you describe something as enormous, you are emphasizing that it is extremely large in size or amount.

words.ex: The elephant was gargantuan compared to the dog.
words.ex_cn: 这只大象比起狗来说巨大无比。
words.en: If you say that something is gargantuan, you are emphasizing that it is very large.

words.ex: The mountain is immense.
words.ex_cn: 这座山非常巨大。
words.en: Extremely large or great, especially in scale or degree.

words.tr: n. 广大；巨大；浩瀚无垠
words.ex: The immensity of the ocean surprised him.
words.ex_cn: 海洋的浩瀚让他感到惊讶。
words.en: The quality or state of being immense; vastness or hugeness.

words.tr: adj. 坚不可摧的；不可战胜的
words.ex: The castle was impregnable during the war.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡在战争期间固若金汤。
words.en: An impregnable building or place is so strong and secure that it cannot be entered or captured by force.

words.ex: Her irrepressible laugh filled the room.
words.ex_cn: 她抑制不住的笑声充满了房间。
words.en: If someone is irrepressible, they are full of energy and enthusiasm and cannot be controlled or stopped.

words.tr:
n. 猛玛（象）；庞然大物；
adj. 巨大的；庞大的；
words.ex: The mammoth lived in cold areas long ago.
words.ex_cn: 猛犸象很久以前生活在寒冷地区。
words.en: If you describe something as mammoth, you are emphasizing that it is extremely large.

words.tr: adj. 大规模的；大而重的；
words.ex: The company launched a massive advertising campaign.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司发起了一场大规模的广告活动。
words.en: Something that is massive is extremely large in size, amount, or extent.

words.ex: He lives in a big metropolis with many tall buildings.
words.ex_cn: 他住在一个有很多高楼的大都市里。
words.en: A metropolis is a very large city, often the most important city in a country or area.

words.tr: adj. 大都市的；大城市的；
words.ex: He lives in a metropolitan city like New York.
words.ex_cn: 他住在纽约这样的大都市。
words.en: Relating to or denoting a metropolis or large city, especially as the main city of a country or region.

words.tr:
adj. 巨大的；强大的；
adv. 非常；
words.ex: The mighty river flows through the valley.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的河流流经山谷。
words.en: Possessing great power, strength, or force; formidable.

words.tr: adj.  独块巨石的；整体的；庞大的；单一的；统一的
words.ex: The ancient temple was built from a monolithic stone.
words.ex_cn: 这座古代神庙是由一块巨石建成的。
words.en: A monolithic structure is extremely large and made of one piece or one type of material.

words.ex: The monster made a monstrous sound.
words.ex_cn: 这个怪物发出了巨大的声音。
words.en: If you describe something as monstrous, you mean that it is extremely large or that it is extremely unpleasant or wrong.

words.ex: The project was a monumental task.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目是一项巨大的任务。
words.en: If you describe something as monumental, you are emphasizing that it is very large and impressive, or that it is of great importance or significance.

words.ex: The mountainous region has many hiking trails.
words.ex_cn: 这个多山的地区有许多徒步小径。
words.en: A mountainous area has a lot of mountains.

words.tr: adj. 无可匹敌的；盖世无双的
words.ex: Her singing is peerless.
words.ex_cn: 她的歌唱无人能及。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as peerless, you mean that they are better than any other person or thing of the same type.

words.ex: The predominant color in the room is blue.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的主导颜色是蓝色。
words.en: If something is predominant, it is more important, noticeable, or powerful than the other things in a situation.

words.tr: v. 占主导地位；占支配地位；
words.ex: English predominate in this region.
words.ex_cn: 英语在这个地区占主导地位。
words.en: If one type of person or thing predominates in a group, there is more of that type than of any other.

words.tr: adj. 惊人的；巨大的；奇异的；巨大的；
words.ex: He showed a prodigious memory for names.
words.ex_cn: 他对名字有着惊人的记忆力。
words.en: If you describe something as prodigious, you are emphasizing that it is very large or impressive.

words.tr: adj. 强有力的；强盛的；有势力的
words.ex: The puissant ruler commanded respect from all his subjects.
words.ex_cn: 这位强大的统治者赢得了所有臣民的尊敬。
words.en: Having great power or influence; potent.

words.ex: The view from the mountain was stupendous.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色令人惊叹。
words.en: Something that is stupendous is extremely impressive or large.

words.ex: The company made a titanic effort to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司做出了巨大的努力来按时完成项目。
words.en: If you describe something as titanic, you mean that it is very big or important, and usually that it involves very powerful forces.

words.ex: One aspect of learning English is practicing speaking.
words.ex_cn: 学习英语的一个方面是练习口语。
words.en: An aspect of something is one of the parts of its character or nature.

words.tr: adj. 容量大的；广阔的；宽敞的
words.ex: The capacious room can hold many people.
words.ex_cn: 这个宽敞的房间可以容纳很多人。
words.en: Capacious means having a lot of space inside; roomy.

words.ex: The house has a commodious living room.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子有一个宽敞的客厅。
words.en: A commodious room or building is large and has a lot of space.

words.ex: He used a compass to find north.
words.ex_cn: 他用指南针找北方。
words.en: A compass is an instrument that you use for finding directions. It has a dial and a magnetic needle that always points to the north.

words.tr: n. 听力所及的范围；可听距离
words.ex: Keep your voice down; I don't want anyone within earshot to hear our conversation.
words.ex_cn: 小声点；我不想让听力所及范围内的任何人听到我们的谈话。
words.en: The range within which one can hear or be heard.

words.tr: adj. 基督教大联合的；普世的；普遍的
words.ex: The ecumenical movement seeks to promote unity among all Christian churches.
words.ex_cn: 普世运动旨在促进所有基督教会之间的团结。
words.en: Ecumenical is used to describe something that is concerned with promoting unity among the world's different Christian churches.

words.ex: Malaria is endemic in some parts of Africa.
words.ex_cn: 疟疾在非洲某些地区是地方性的。
words.en: If a disease or condition is endemic in a particular area, it is frequently or regularly found among the people living there.

words.tr: adj. 包容的；包含全部费用的；
words.ex: The school is inclusive and welcomes all students.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校是包容的，欢迎所有学生。
words.en: Inclusive is used to describe something that is designed to include all types of people, things, or ideas, and to treat them all fairly and equally.

words.ex: The indigenous people live in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 本土居民住在森林里。
words.en: Indigenous people or things belong to the country in which they are found, rather than coming there or being brought there from another country.

words.ex: The meeting felt interminable.
words.ex_cn: 这场会议感觉没完没了。
words.en: If you describe something as interminable, you are emphasizing that it continues for a very long time and indicating that you find it boring or annoying.

words.ex: His ken does not include quantum physics.
words.ex_cn: 他的知识范围不包括量子物理。
words.en: Ken is the range of one's knowledge or understanding.

words.tr: adj. 有限的； v. 限制；“limit”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: We have limited time to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 我们完成这个项目的时间是有限的。
words.en: If something is limited, there is only a certain amount of it.

words.ex: The view from the hill is panoramic.
words.ex_cn: 从山上望去，景色一览无余。
words.en: A panoramic view or picture is one that shows a wide area of land or sea.

words.tr: n. 视角；观点；（对事物的）合理判断；
words.ex: His perspective on life is very positive.
words.ex_cn: 他对生活的看法非常积极。
words.en: A particular attitude towards or way of regarding something; a point of view.

words.ex: The smell of bread pervades the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 面包的香味弥漫在整个厨房里。
words.en: If something pervades a place or thing, it is present throughout it.

words.ex: He was born in the province of Guangdong.
words.ex_cn: 他出生在广东省。
words.en: A province is a large area of a country that has its own administration and often its own culture.

words.ex: This book is about the realm of artificial intelligence.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是关于人工智能领域的。
words.en: A realm is a country ruled by a king or queen, or an area of activity, interest, or knowledge.

words.ex: The scope of this project includes three cities.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目的范围包括三个城市。
words.en: The range of one's perceptions, thoughts, or actions.

words.ex: The new house has a spacious living room.
words.ex_cn: 这所新房子有一个宽敞的客厅。
words.en: A spacious room, building, or place is large in size or area, so that you can move around freely in it.

words.tr:
n. 时距；跨度；
v. 跨越；
words.ex: The span of his career was 40 years.
words.ex_cn: 他职业生涯的时距是40年。
words.en: The extent or measure of space between two points or extremities, as of a bridge or a roof; the full extent, stretch, or reach of anything.

words.tr: adj. 蔓延的；杂乱无序伸展的； v. “sprawl”的现在分词；
words.ex: The sprawling city has many neighborhoods.
words.ex_cn: 这座蔓延的城市有许多社区。
words.en: If you describe something as sprawling, you mean that it covers a large area of land.

words.ex: The rule subsumes all similar cases.
words.ex_cn: 这个规则涵盖所有类似的情况。
words.en: If something is subsumed within a larger group or class, it is included within it, rather than being considered as something separate.

words.tr:
n. 系绳；系链；界限
v. 用绳拴住
words.ex: The horse was tied to the post with a tether.
words.ex_cn: 这匹马被用拴绳系在了柱子上。
words.en: A tether is a rope or chain used to tie an animal to a post or other fixed point so that it cannot move away.

words.tr: adj. 线性的；一维的；一度空间的
words.ex: The line is unidimensional.
words.ex_cn: 这条线是一维的。
words.en: Involving or having only one dimension.

words.ex: The country made a unilateral decision to close the border.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家单方面决定关闭边境。
words.en: Involving only one group or country.

words.ex: The hikers enjoyed a beautiful vista from the mountain top.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者们从山顶欣赏到了美丽的景色。
words.en: A vista is a pleasing view, especially one seen through a long, narrow opening.

words.ex: The park is within the precinct of the city center.
words.ex_cn: 这个公园位于市中心的范围内。
words.en: A precinct is a part of a city or town that has its own police force, or a division of a city for police or voting purposes.

words.ex: He feels comfortable in his artistic milieu.
words.ex_cn: 他在他的艺术环境中感到自在。
words.en: The milieu is the environment or setting in which something happens or develops.

words.ex: They walked abreast down the street.
words.ex_cn: 他们并肩走在街上。
words.en: If people or things are abreast, they are lined up next to each other, side by side, and often facing the same direction.

words.ex: The circles are concentric and share the same center.
words.ex_cn: 这些圆是同心的，拥有同一个中心。
words.en: Having a common center, as circles or spheres.

words.ex: The teacher will delimit the scope of the exam.
words.ex_cn: 老师将限定考试的范围。
words.en: If you delimit something, you fix or establish its limits.

words.ex: The treaty will demarcate the new borders between the two countries.
words.ex_cn: 条约将划定两国之间的新边界。
words.en: To set the boundaries or limits of something.

words.ex: The distal end of the bone is broken.
words.ex_cn: 骨头的远端断了。
words.en: Situated away from the center of the body or from the point of attachment.

words.ex: She is a grounded individual who always makes thoughtful decisions.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个理性的人，总是做出深思熟虑的决定。
words.en: If you say that someone is grounded, you mean that they are sensible and reasonable, and that they understand the importance of ordinary things in life.

words.tr: v. 置于…之间；插入；插嘴；介入
words.ex: The mediator tried to interpose before the situation escalated.
words.ex_cn: 调解人试图在局势升级之前进行干预。
words.en: If you interpose something between two people or things, you place it between them. If you interpose, you interrupt with a comment or question.

words.ex: He juxtaposes old photos with new ones.
words.ex_cn: 他把老照片和新照片放在一起。
words.en: To place or deal with close together for contrasting effect.

words.ex: The car made a lateral move to avoid the dog.
words.ex_cn: 汽车横向移动以避开狗。
words.en: Relating to the side or sides; situated at or extending to the side.

words.ex: The nethermost part of the cave was filled with water.
words.ex_cn: 洞穴的最下面部分充满了水。
words.en: The nethermost part of something is the lowest or deepest part of it.

words.tr: n. 商机；理想的工作或生活；
words.ex: He found a niche in selling eco-friendly phone cases.
words.ex_cn: 他在销售环保手机壳方面找到了商机。
words.en: A niche is a hollow area in a wall which has been made to hold a statue, or a comfortable or suitable position in life or employment.

words.ex: The obverse of the coin features the head of the queen.
words.ex_cn: 硬币的正面印有女王的头像。
words.en: The obverse of something is the main or most obvious part of it, or the side of it that is most often seen or used.

words.tr: adj. 西洋的；西方的；欧美的；
words.ex: He likes occidental music more than traditional Chinese music.
words.ex_cn: 他更喜欢西洋音乐而不是中国传统音乐。
words.en: Relating to the countries of the West, especially Europe and America.

words.tr:
adj. 舞台后面的；后台的；台下的
adv. 舞台后面地；后台地；幕后地
words.ex: The actor waited offstage before his turn.
words.ex_cn: 演员在幕后等待上场。
words.en: Offstage refers to the area of a theater that is not visible to the audience, often used by performers and crew when not on stage.

words.tr: n. 出口；发泄途径；经销店；折扣店
words.ex: The river flows out through an outlet.
words.ex_cn: 河水通过一个出口流出。
words.en: An outlet is a hole or pipe through which liquid or air can flow out, or a point in a wall where you can connect electrical equipment to the electricity supply.

words.ex: The proximate cause of the accident was bad weather.
words.ex_cn: 事故的直接原因是恶劣天气。
words.en: If something is proximate, it is nearest in space, time, or relationship.

words.ex: She snuggled the baby in a blanket.
words.ex_cn: 她用毯子把宝宝裹得舒舒服服。
words.en: To snuggle means to settle or move into a warm, comfortable position, especially close to someone else for affection or warmth.

words.ex: The subterranean tunnel connects two buildings.
words.ex_cn: 这条地下的隧道连接着两栋大楼。
words.en: Existing, occurring, or done under the earth's surface.

words.tr: v. 置于某物之上；添加
words.ex: He superimposes a map on the photo.
words.ex_cn: 他把地图叠加在照片上。
words.en: To superimpose something means to place or lay one thing over another, typically so that both are still evident.

words.ex: His ulterior motive was to get money.
words.ex_cn: 他别有用心，目的是弄到钱。
words.en: If you say that someone has an ulterior motive for doing something, you believe that they have a hidden reason for doing it.

words.tr: adj. 根本的；潜在的； v. “underlie”的现在分词；
words.ex: The underlying cause of the problem is poverty.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题的根本原因是贫困。
words.en: An underlying thing is the thing that is the most important or basic, although it is not easily noticed or stated directly.

words.ex: The park is in the vicinity of my house.
words.ex_cn: 公园在我家附近。
words.en: The area or region near or about a place; the surrounding district.

words.ex: He lives in the nether world of dreams.
words.ex_cn: 他生活在梦境的地下世界。
words.en: Situated or occurring below or beneath something else.

words.ex: He bought a new accessory for his phone.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的手机买了一个新配件。
words.en: An accessory is something such as a bag or piece of jewelry that you wear or carry because it is attractive.

words.ex: He added an addendum to the contract.
words.ex_cn: 他在合同后加了一个附录。
words.en: An addendum is an additional section at the end of a book or document that provides further information or corrections.

words.tr:
n. 附属物；
adj. 附属的；
words.ex: The printer is an adjunct to the computer.
words.ex_cn: 打印机是电脑的附属物。
words.en: Something that is added or attached to something else but is not essential to it.

words.tr: n. 附加物；附属物；附属肢体
words.ex: The crab has an appendage that looks like a claw.
words.ex_cn: 螃蟹有一个看起来像钳子的附属物。
words.en: An appendage is something that is joined to or connected with something larger or more important.

words.tr:
adj. 辅助的；附属的
n. 辅助物；附属物；助动词
words.ex: He used an auxiliary verb to form the past tense.
words.ex_cn: 他使用了一个助动词来构成过去时。
words.en: An auxiliary is a person or thing that provides additional help or support.

words.ex: The factory makes cheese, and whey is a by-product.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂生产奶酪，乳清是副产品。
words.en: A by-product is something that is produced as a result of making something else, or something unexpected that happens as a result of something.

words.ex: The loan requires collateral documents.
words.ex_cn: 这笔贷款需要附属文件。
words.en: Collateral is something pledged as security for repayment of a loan, to be forfeited in the event of a default.

words.ex: The cheese is a derivative of milk.
words.ex_cn: 这种奶酪是牛奶的派生物。
words.en: A derivative is something which has been developed or obtained from something else.

words.tr: adj. 有附带条件的；有附文的；临时的
words.ex: The agreement was provisory and subject to change.
words.ex_cn: 该协议是附带条件的，可能会发生变化。
words.en: A provisory measure or arrangement is one that is made or done for the time being, especially until something more permanent can be arranged.

words.ex: The big company owns a subsidiary that makes phones.
words.ex_cn: 这家大公司拥有一家生产手机的附属公司。
words.en: A subsidiary is a company which is part of a larger and more important company.

words.ex: The small river flows into the main river as a tributary.
words.ex_cn: 这条小河作为支流汇入主河。
words.en: A tributary is a stream or river that flows into a larger stream or main stem (or parent) river or a lake. A tributary does not flow directly into a sea or ocean.

words.tr: n. 副官；助理；人事行政参谋
words.ex: The adjutant helped the general with his papers.
words.ex_cn: 副官帮将军处理文件。
words.en: An adjutant is an officer in the army who deals with administrative work, or an assistant to a senior officer.

words.ex: He will append his name to the list.
words.ex_cn: 他将在名单上加上他的名字。
words.en: To add something to the end of a piece of writing.

words.tr:
v. 补充；与…相辅相成；
n. 补足物；补语；余角；
words.ex: The red scarf complements her blue coat.
words.ex_cn: 这条红围巾补充了她的蓝外套。
words.en: To complement something means to make it complete or perfect by adding something to it.

words.ex: He added a codicil to his will, specifying additional bequests.
words.ex_cn: 他在遗嘱中添加了一个附录，指定了额外的遗产分配。
words.en: A codicil is an addition or supplement that explains, modifies, or revokes a will or part of one.

words.tr: n. 附言；附录；补充说明
words.ex: He added a postscript to his letter.
words.ex_cn: 他在信后加了一段附言。
words.en: A postscript is a note appended to a finished letter, article, or book.

words.tr:
n. 标签；标记；
v. 加标签于；
words.ex: The tag on the shirt says 'wash cold'.
words.ex_cn: 衬衫上的标签写着‘冷水洗涤’。
words.en: A tag is a small piece of card, cloth, or plastic which is attached to an object or person and has information about that object or person on it. A tag can also be a word or phrase that is used to describe or identify something, especially in a computer file or on a website.

words.ex: The appendix contains extra data for the report.
words.ex_cn: 附录包含了报告的额外数据。
words.en: An appendix is a section at the end of a book that contains additional information. It can also refer to the small tube attached to the large intestine in the human body, known as the vermiform appendix.

words.ex: The cost of lunch was incidental to the main expense.
words.ex_cn: 午餐的费用是主要开销的附带部分。
words.en: If one thing is incidental to another, it is less important than the other thing or is not a major part of it.

words.tr:
n. 中尉；副官
adj. 副的
words.ex: The subaltern followed the officer's order.
words.ex_cn: 下级士兵遵从了军官的命令。
words.en: A subaltern is someone who has a lower rank or position in an organization, especially in the armed forces.

words.ex: His opinion is subordinate to the manager's.
words.ex_cn: 他的意见比经理的次要。
words.en: If someone is your subordinate, they have a less important position than you in the organization that you both work for.

words.ex: The church has a byzantine dome with gold mosaics.
words.ex_cn: 这座教堂有一个拜占庭风格的穹顶，饰有金色马赛克。
words.en: If you describe a system or process as byzantine, you are criticizing it because it is complicated and difficult to understand.

words.ex: Too many rules can complicate the game.
words.ex_cn: 太多的规则会使游戏变得复杂。
words.en: To make something more difficult to understand or deal with by adding more parts or details.

words.tr:
adj. 精心制作的；详尽的；
v. 精心制作；详尽阐述；
words.ex: She wore an elaborate dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件精心制作的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: To elaborate means to add more details to something that has already been said or written, making it more complex or detailed. As an adjective, it describes something that is very complex and detailed.

words.tr: adj. 密封的；不透气的；与外界隔绝的
words.ex: The container was hermetic to ensure the contents stayed fresh.
words.ex_cn: 这个容器是密封的，以确保内容物保持新鲜。
words.en: If something is hermetic, it is so tightly sealed that no air can get in or out.

words.tr: adj. 难以辨认的；无法破译的
words.ex: The handwriting was so indecipherable that even the author couldn't read it.
words.ex_cn: 这字迹太难辨认了，连作者自己都读不出来。
words.en: If writing or speech is indecipherable, it is impossible to understand because the words and letters cannot be recognized or understood.

words.ex: The glass has opacity so we cannot see through it.
words.ex_cn: 这玻璃不透明，所以我们看不到它后面的东西。
words.en: Opacity refers to the quality of being difficult to see through or understand, often due to a lack of transparency or clarity.

words.ex: His words had a profound effect on her life.
words.ex_cn: 他的话对她的生活产生了深远的影响。
words.en: If you describe something as profound, you mean that it is very great or intense.

words.tr:
adv. 光明正大地
adj. 光明正大的
words.ex: He always plays aboveboard in business.
words.ex_cn: 他在商业中总是光明正大。
words.en: If something is aboveboard, it is done in an honest and open way without any attempt to deceive.

words.ex: The judge was disinterested in the case.
words.ex_cn: 法官对这个案件持客观态度。
words.en: If someone is disinterested in something, they have no personal involvement or investment in it and are therefore able to judge it fairly.

words.ex: He bought equity in a tech company.
words.ex_cn: 他购买了一家科技公司的股票。
words.en: Equity is the quality of being fair and impartial.

words.tr:
adv. 甚至；甚至于；
adj. 平坦的；
words.ex: He didn't even say goodbye.
words.ex_cn: 他甚至连再见都没说。
words.en: Even is used to emphasize something that is surprising or unlikely. It can also describe something that is flat, smooth, or level, or something that is equal in amount, degree, or value.

words.ex: The judge was evenhanded in treating both sides.
words.ex_cn: 法官对双方都公平对待。
words.en: Treating everyone equally and fairly.

words.tr: adj. 公正的；不偏不倚的；
words.ex: The judge was impartial in the trial.
words.ex_cn: 法官在审判中是公正的。
words.en: Someone who is impartial is not directly involved in a particular situation, and is therefore able to give a fair opinion or decision about it.

words.tr:
adj. 客观的；
n. 目标；目的；
words.ex: He gave an objective opinion about the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影给出了一个客观的看法。
words.en: An objective is something that you plan to do or achieve.

words.ex: The judge made an equitable decision.
words.ex_cn: 法官做出了一个公平的决定。
words.en: Fair and impartial; treating everyone equally.

words.ex: The judge gave an unbiased decision.
words.ex_cn: 法官作出了无偏见的判决。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as unbiased, you mean they are fair and not likely to support one particular person or group involved in something.

words.ex: The judge showed impartiality in the trial.
words.ex_cn: 法官在审判中表现出公平。
words.en: Impartiality is the quality of being unbiased or not favoring one side over another.

words.tr: adj. 不受个人感情影响的；没有人情味的；
words.ex: The judge gave an impersonal decision based on the law.
words.ex_cn: 法官基于法律作出了不受个人感情影响的判决。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as impersonal, you mean that they do not show any emotion about the person they are dealing with.

words.ex: Oil helps to lubricate the engine parts.
words.ex_cn: 油有助于润滑发动机部件。
words.en: To apply a substance such as oil or grease to (something) in order to minimize friction and allow smooth movement.

words.ex: The lubricious surface made it difficult to gain traction.
words.ex_cn: 光滑的表面使它很难获得牵引力。
words.en: If you describe something as lubricious, you mean that it is smooth and slippery or that it is sexually suggestive or lustful.

words.tr: adj. 缎子似的；光滑的；柔软的
words.ex: The dress had a satiny texture that felt luxurious against the skin.
words.ex_cn: 这件衣服有一种光滑的质感，与皮肤接触时感觉很奢华。
words.en: Having a smooth, glossy surface resembling satin.

words.tr:
adj. 光滑的；圆滑的；熟练的；华而不实的
n. 浮油层；光滑之处
v. 使平滑
words.ex: The ice on the road was slick.
words.ex_cn: 路上的冰很光滑。
words.en: If something is slick, it is done smoothly and efficiently, often in a way that is intended to be impressive.

words.ex: The floor is slippery after it rains.
words.ex_cn: 下雨后地板很滑。
words.en: Something that is slippery is smooth, wet, or oily and is therefore difficult to walk on or to hold.

words.tr:
adj. 平滑的；平坦的；
v. 使平滑；
words.ex: The glass surface is smooth.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃表面是平滑的。
words.en: Having an even and regular surface or consistency; free from projections, indentations, or roughness.

words.tr: n. 恶作剧；开玩笑；戏谑
words.ex: He played a prank on his friend with a fake spider.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个假蜘蛛捉弄了他的朋友。
words.en: A prank is a trick or practical joke that is played on someone, often to make them look foolish or to amuse others.

words.ex: It's preposterous to think cats can drive cars.
words.ex_cn: 认为猫会开车是极其荒谬的。
words.en: If you describe something as preposterous, you mean that it is extremely unreasonable and foolish.

words.ex: He wore a weird hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶怪异的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as weird, you mean that they are strange, unusual, or mysterious.

words.ex: The movie was fantastic!
words.ex_cn: 这部电影极好！
words.en: If you describe something as fantastic, you are emphasizing that you think it is very good or that you like it a lot.

words.tr: adj. 梦幻的；荒诞不经的
words.ex: His chimerical dream of flying without wings never came true.
words.ex_cn: 他那不切实际的、不用翅膀就能飞翔的梦想从未实现。
words.en: If you describe something as chimerical, you mean that it is imagined or hoped for but unlikely to be real or practical.

words.tr: n. 滑稽；丑态；插科打诨
words.ex: The play was filled with buffoonery to entertain the audience.
words.ex_cn: 这部戏充满了滑稽表演，以娱乐观众。
words.en: Buffoonery refers to behavior that is ridiculous but amusing, often involving silly jokes or actions.

words.ex: The two groups are discrete and do not overlap.
words.ex_cn: 这两个群体是分离的，没有重叠。
words.en: Something that is discrete is separate and distinct in form or concept.

words.tr: adj. 暂时的；临时的；期间的；
words.ex: He is the interim manager until a new one is hired.
words.ex_cn: 在招聘到新的经理之前，他是临时经理。
words.en: An interim is a period of time between one event, process, or period and another, especially one of temporary nature.

words.tr: adj. 断断续续的；间歇的
words.ex: The rain is intermittent today.
words.ex_cn: 今天雨断断续续地下。
words.en: Something that is intermittent happens occasionally rather than continuously.

words.ex: Many people lost jobs during the recession.
words.ex_cn: 在经济不景气期间，许多人失去了工作。
words.en: A recession is a period when the economy of a country is not doing well, industrial production and business activity are at a low level, and many people are unemployed.

words.ex: The patient experienced remittent fever throughout the night.
words.ex_cn: 病人整晚都经历着弛张热。
words.en: A remittent condition, especially a fever, is one that temporarily abates in severity but does not cease entirely.

words.tr:
v. 拼写；意味着；
n. 一段时间；
words.ex: Can you spell your name?
words.ex_cn: 你能拼出你的名字吗？
words.en: If you spell a word, you write or speak each letter in the correct order.

words.tr: adj. 不定时发生的；时有时无的；零星的
words.ex: He makes sporadic visits to his grandparents.
words.ex_cn: 他时不时去看望他的祖父母。
words.en: occurring at irregular intervals or only in a few places; scattered or isolated

words.ex: His answer was apt for the question.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答对这个问题很恰当。
words.en: If someone is apt to do something, they often do it and so it is likely that they will do it again.

words.tr: adj. 轻率的；肤浅的；易做到的
words.ex: He gave a facile answer to the hard question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个难题给出了一个简单的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone's arguments or suggestions as facile, you are criticizing them because their ideas are too simple and indicate a lack of careful, intelligent thinking.

words.ex: This lock is foolproof and easy to use.
words.ex_cn: 这个锁是万无一失的，而且容易使用。
words.en: A foolproof plan, system, or method is so well designed that it cannot go wrong or be used wrongly.

words.ex: The handwriting is legible and easy to read.
words.ex_cn: 字迹清晰，容易辨认。
words.en: If writing or print is legible, it is clear enough to read.

words.ex: The teacher gave a lucid explanation of the math problem.
words.ex_cn: 老师对这道数学题做了一个易懂的解释。
words.en: If someone is lucid, they are able to understand things clearly and think clearly, especially when they have been very ill or confused.

words.ex: She readily agreed to help me.
words.ex_cn: 她很容易就同意帮我了。
words.en: If you do something readily, you do it in a way which shows that you are very willing to do it.

words.ex: The instructions were straightforward and easy to follow.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明很简单，容易遵循。
words.en: If you describe something as straightforward, you approve of it because it is easy to do or understand.

words.ex: His knowledge of history is superficial.
words.ex_cn: 他对历史的了解是表面的。
words.en: If you describe someone as superficial, you disapprove of them because they do not think deeply, and have little understanding of anything serious or important.

words.tr: n. 表面性的事物；肤浅
words.ex: Her work is often criticized for its superficiality.
words.ex_cn: 她的作品经常因为浅薄而受到批评。
words.en: Superficiality refers to the quality of being superficial, that is, concerned only with the obvious or apparent aspects of something, not with the deeper or more important aspects.

words.tr: adj. 要求不高的；不苛求的；不费力的
words.ex: She found the job surprisingly undemanding.
words.ex_cn: 她发现这份工作出乎意料地要求不高。
words.en: If you describe something as undemanding, you mean that it is not difficult or challenging, and is therefore easy to do or deal with.

words.tr:
adj. 自家织的；朴素的
n. 手织品
words.ex: He wore a homespun shirt to the fair.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着一件自织的衬衫去赶集。
words.en: Homespun refers to something that is simple, plain, and not sophisticated, often made at home.

words.ex: The book has a compact design.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的设计很紧凑。
words.en: A compact object or substance is small and dense, with all its parts closely packed together.

words.ex: He gave a concise answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了简明的回答。
words.en: Something that is concise says everything that is necessary without using any unnecessary words.

words.tr: adj. 言简意赅的；简明扼要的；凝练的
words.ex: He gave a laconic reply: 'Yes.'
words.ex_cn: 他简短地回答：‘是的。’
words.en: If you describe someone as laconic, you mean that they use very few words to say something, so that they seem casual or unfriendly.

words.ex: The pithiness of his speech impressed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他讲话的有力之处让所有人都印象深刻。
words.en: The quality of being concise and meaningful in expression.

words.tr: adj. 言简意赅的；精练的
words.ex: He gave a pithy answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了简洁有力的回答。
words.en: A pithy statement or piece of writing is short, clear, and full of meaning.

words.tr:
n. 平原；
adj. 简单明了的；朴素的；
words.ex: The cows graze on the plain.
words.ex_cn: 牛在平原上吃草。
words.en: If something is plain, it is easy to see, hear, or understand.

words.tr: v. 重述要点；简要回顾
words.ex: Can you recapitulate the main points of the lecture?
words.ex_cn: 你能重述一下讲座的主要要点吗？
words.en: If you recapitulate something, you say it again briefly, or you give a summary of it.

words.ex: He drew a simple schematic of the circuit.
words.ex_cn: 他画了一个电路的简单示意图。
words.en: A schematic diagram or representation is a simple drawing that uses symbols to show the parts of something and how they are connected.

words.tr: v.  系统化；图形化；扼要表示
words.ex: The professor tried to schematize the complex process for his students.
words.ex_cn: 教授试图为学生们系统化复杂的流程。
words.en: To arrange or represent something according to a plan, system, or scheme.

words.tr: adj. 说教的；过分认真的；简洁的；富于警句的
words.ex: His speech was full of sententious remarks.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲中充满了简洁精炼的格言。
words.en: If you describe someone as sententious, you mean that they try to appear wise, intelligent, and moral, but in a way that is often perceived as pompous or insincere.

words.ex: He gave a succinct answer.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个简洁的回答。
words.en: Something that is succinct expresses facts or ideas clearly and in few words.

words.ex: Her terse reply left no room for further discussion.
words.ex_cn: 她简洁的回答没有留下进一步讨论的余地。
words.en: A terse statement or comment is brief and to the point, often seeming rude or unfriendly because of its brevity.

words.ex: The brevity of his speech surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他讲话的短暂让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: Brevity is the use of only a few words to say something, or the quality of being short in time.

words.ex: The old computer is antiquated and slow.
words.ex_cn: 这台旧电脑过时且缓慢。
words.en: Something that is antiquated is old-fashioned or outdated and no longer suitable for modern conditions or purposes.

words.tr: n. 人工制品；手工艺品；加工品
words.ex: The museum has an ancient artifact.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆里有一件古代文物。
words.en: An artifact is an object that is made by a person, especially something of historical or cultural interest.

words.ex: The museum displays ancient artifacts from Egypt.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆展出了来自埃及的古代文物。
words.en: An artifact is an object that is made by a person, especially something of historical or cultural interest.

words.ex: He is a conservative man who likes old traditions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢古老传统的保守男子。
words.en: A conservative person or group is one that does not like changes or new ideas, especially in politics or religion.

words.ex: He wears conventional clothes to work.
words.ex_cn: 他穿传统服装去上班。
words.en: Conventional ideas, methods, or systems are the ones that are generally accepted and used, and that have been used for a long time.

words.ex: His work is a critique of social conformism.
words.ex_cn: 他的作品是对社会因循守旧的批判。
words.en: Conformism is the tendency to conform to established customs, attitudes, or norms.

words.ex: The old house looked dilapidated after years of neglect.
words.ex_cn: 这所老房子因多年疏于维护而显得残破。
words.en: A building that is dilapidated is old and in a generally bad condition.

words.tr: v. （使）成化石；变陈腐；（使）僵化
words.ex: The old tree fossilized over millions of years.
words.ex_cn: 这棵老树在数百万年中变成了化石。
words.en: To fossilize means to become or cause to become a fossil, or to become fixed and unable to change or develop.

words.tr: adj. 灰白的；须发斑白的
words.ex: The old man had a hoary beard.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人有一头灰白的胡须。
words.en: If you describe something as hoary, you mean that it is old and often repeated and therefore not interesting or original.

words.ex: This custom has existed from time immemorial.
words.ex_cn: 这个习俗从远古时代就存在了。
words.en: Something that is immemorial has existed or been happening for such a long time that it cannot be remembered.

words.ex: His moralistic tone made the lecture boring.
words.ex_cn: 他那说教的语调让讲座变得无聊。
words.en: If you describe someone as moralistic, you are critical of them for making harsh judgments of other people's behavior based on their own beliefs about what is right and wrong.

words.tr: adj. 被虫蛀的；破旧的；过时的
words.ex: The moth-eaten coat looked out of place in the modern setting.
words.ex_cn: 这件虫蛀的外套在现代环境中显得格格不入。
words.en: Something that is moth-eaten is old and in bad condition, often because it has been eaten by moths or because it is very old and has not been looked after well.

words.ex: The technology is becoming obsolescent as newer models are introduced.
words.ex_cn: 随着新模型的推出，这项技术正在变得过时。
words.en: Becoming obsolete or going out of use.

words.tr: adj. 过时的；老式的； v. “outmode”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: This phone is outmoded and needs to be replaced.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机已经过时了，需要更换。
words.en: If you describe something as outmoded, you mean that you think it is old-fashioned and no longer useful or relevant to modern life.

words.ex: The forest remained pristine and untouched.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林保持原始且未被破坏。
words.en: Something that is pristine is in its original condition and has not been spoiled or damaged.

words.tr:
adj. 反动的；保守的
n. 反动派；保守人士
words.ex: The reactionary government banned free speech.
words.ex_cn: 这个反动政府禁止了言论自由。
words.en: A reactionary person or group tries to prevent changes in the political or social system of their country.

words.ex: The guard asked for the shibboleth before letting us in.
words.ex_cn: 守卫在让我们进去之前问了口令。
words.en: A shibboleth is a custom, principle, or belief distinguishing a particular class or group of people, especially a long-standing one regarded as outmoded or no longer important.

words.tr: adj. 在商店中陈列旧了的
words.ex: The shopworn phrase no longer resonates with today's audience.
words.ex_cn: 这个陈旧的短语不再引起当今观众的共鸣。
words.en: If something is shopworn, it has become less attractive or valuable because it has been on display or for sale in a shop for a long time.

words.tr:
n. 刻板印象；陈规老套
v. 对…存有成见；把…模式化
words.ex: He broke the stereotype that boys cannot cry.
words.ex_cn: 他打破了男孩不能哭的刻板印象。
words.en: A stereotype is a fixed general image or set of characteristics that a lot of people believe represent a particular type of person or thing.

words.ex: The timeworn furniture in the attic looked like it belonged to another era.
words.ex_cn: 阁楼上的陈旧家具看起来像是属于另一个时代。
words.en: Something that is timeworn is old and often used or repeated so much that it is no longer interesting or effective.

words.ex: The old building was in a state of decrepitude.
words.ex_cn: 这座老建筑处于一种破败的状态。
words.en: Decrepitude refers to the state of being old and in poor condition, especially as a result of age or long use.

words.tr: adj. 教条的；武断的；固执己见的
words.ex: He is dogmatic about his beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己信念非常固执。
words.en: If you say that someone is dogmatic, you are critical of them because they are convinced that they are right, and refuse to consider that other opinions might also be justified.

words.ex: He used a cliche to describe the sunset.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个陈词滥调来形容日落。
words.en: A cliché is an idea or phrase that has been used so much that it is no longer interesting or effective.

words.ex: The word 'thou' is archaic in modern English.
words.ex_cn: ‘thou’这个词在现代英语中是过时的。
words.en: Very old or old-fashioned.

words.tr: adj. 过时的；已过盛年的
words.ex: The fashion styles of the 1980s are now considered passé.
words.ex_cn: 20世纪80年代的时尚风格现在被认为已经过时了。
words.en: No longer fashionable or in vogue; out of date.

words.ex: The room was devoid of any furniture.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间里全无家具。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is devoid of a quality or thing, you are emphasizing that they have none of it.

words.tr:
adj. 脱离肉体的；无实体的；不具形体的
v. 使脱离肉体；“disembody”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The voice sounded disembodied, echoing through the empty room.
words.ex_cn: 那声音听起来空洞无物，在空荡的房间里回响。
words.en: If you describe a voice or a form as disembodied, you mean that it is not connected to a physical body.

words.ex: The cat has a fluffy tail.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫有一条蓬松的尾巴。
words.en: Something that is fluffy is soft and light, with many small, loose pieces or parts.

words.ex: The milk is frothy after being steamed.
words.ex_cn: 牛奶经过蒸汽处理后变得泡沫丰富。
words.en: Frothy describes something that is full of or covered with a mass of small bubbles, or something that is light and entertaining but not serious.

words.tr: adj. 非实体的；非物质的；无形体的
words.ex: The ghost is incorporeal and cannot be touched.
words.ex_cn: 这个幽灵是无形的，无法被触碰。
words.en: Not composed of matter; having no material existence.

words.ex: His excuse was insubstantial and unconvincing.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口是无实质的，毫无说服力。
words.en: If something is insubstantial, it is not solid, large, or strong, and therefore often seems unsatisfactory or unimportant.

words.tr: n. 不可触知性；无形；不能把握
words.ex: The intangibility of emotions makes them difficult to measure.
words.ex_cn: 情感的无形性使得它们难以测量。
words.en: The quality of being intangible; not having physical presence or not being able to be touched.

words.tr: adj. 空洞的；枯燥乏味的；不成熟的；缺乏营养的
words.ex: His jejune remarks made no sense to the audience.
words.ex_cn: 他幼稚的言论让听众无法理解。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as jejune, you are criticizing them for being very simple and unsophisticated.

words.tr: adj. 唐吉诃德式的；不切实际的
words.ex: He made a quixotic effort to fix the broken bridge with sticks and glue.
words.ex_cn: 他用树枝和胶水试图修复那座破桥，这真是异想天开。
words.en: If you describe someone's ideas or plans as quixotic, you mean that they are imaginative or hopeful but unrealistic.

words.ex: Their agreement was tenuous and easily broken.
words.ex_cn: 他们的协议很脆弱，容易破裂。
words.en: If you describe something such as a connection, a reason, or someone's position as tenuous, you mean that it is very uncertain or weak.

words.ex: He is learning theoretical physics at university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学学习理论物理。
words.en: A theoretical study or explanation is based on or uses the ideas and abstract principles of a subject, rather than the practical aspects or uses of it.

words.tr: adj. 充满蒸气的；似蒸气的
words.ex: The novel is filled with vaporous descriptions of imaginary lands.
words.ex_cn: 这部小说充满了对虚构土地的空想描述。
words.en: Something that is vaporous is like vapor or is full of vapor.

words.ex: The void on the page made the text look empty.
words.ex_cn: 页面上的空白让文字看起来空荡荡的。
words.en: If you describe a situation or a feeling as a void, you mean that it seems empty because there is nothing interesting or worthwhile about it.

words.ex: The child told a fanciful story about flying dragons.
words.ex_cn: 孩子讲了一个关于会飞的龙的富于幻想的故事。
words.en: If you describe an idea as fanciful, you mean that it is imaginative rather than reasonable or practical.

words.ex: His sojourn in Paris lasted two years.
words.ex_cn: 他在巴黎旅居了两年。
words.en: A sojourn is a temporary stay in a place.

words.tr:
n. 狂风；暴风雪；大喊大叫
v. 狂风吹袭；哇哇地叫嚷
words.ex: A sudden squall knocked over the small boat.
words.ex_cn: 一阵突如其来的狂风掀翻了小船。
words.en: A squall is a sudden, violent gust of wind or a localized storm, especially one bringing rain, snow, or sleet. It can also refer to a loud, harsh cry or scream.

words.ex: The comedian adlibbed a few jokes to fill the time.
words.ex_cn: 喜剧演员即兴讲了几个笑话来填补时间。
words.en: To speak or perform without previously preparing one's words.

words.tr: adj. 短暂的；朝生暮死的
words.ex: The flowers are ephemeral and last only one day.
words.ex_cn: 这些花是短暂的，只持续一天。
words.en: Something that is ephemeral lasts for only a very short time.

words.tr: adj. 即席的；临时的；无准备的；不用讲稿的
words.ex: He gave an extemporaneous speech at the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上做了一次即兴演讲。
words.en: spoken or done without preparation

words.tr: v. 即兴而作；即席演说；当场表演
words.ex: She extemporized a speech on the spot.
words.ex_cn: 她当场即兴演讲。
words.en: To extemporize means to compose, perform, or produce something such as a speech or a piece of music on the spur of the moment, without preparation.

words.tr: adj. 短暂的； v. “fleet”的现在分词；
words.ex: The smile was fleeting.
words.ex_cn: 那个微笑是短暂的。
words.en: If you describe something as fleeting, you mean that it lasts only for a very short time.

words.tr: adj. 短暂的； v. “fleet”的现在分词；
words.ex: The smile was fleeting.
words.ex_cn: 那个微笑是短暂的。
words.en: If you describe something as fleeting, you mean that it lasts only for a very short time.

words.tr:
n. 衣柜；壁橱；贮藏室
adj. 隐藏的
words.ex: He keeps his shirts in the closet.
words.ex_cn: 他把衬衫放在壁橱里。
words.en: A closet is a small room or space in a house or apartment where clothes, shoes, and other items are stored.

words.ex: The cardinals met in conclave to elect a new pope.
words.ex_cn: 红衣主教们秘密开会选举新教皇。
words.en: A conclave is a private meeting at which the discussions are kept secret, especially a meeting of Roman Catholic cardinals to elect a new pope.

words.ex: The document is confidential and cannot be shared.
words.ex_cn: 这份文件是机密的，不能分享。
words.en: If you talk to someone in a confidential way, you talk to them quietly because what you are saying is secret or private.

words.tr:
adj. 秘密的；隐蔽的
n. （动物可藏身的）小树丛
words.ex: He made a covert plan to leave without telling anyone.
words.ex_cn: 他秘密制定了一个不告诉任何人就离开的计划。
words.en: Covert activities or situations are secret or hidden.

words.tr: adj. 隐秘的；秘密的；隐晦的
words.ex: He gave a cryptic answer and left.
words.ex_cn: 他给了一个神秘的回答，然后离开了。
words.en: If you describe something as cryptic, you mean that it is mysterious or difficult to understand.

words.tr: v. 对（机密文件等）销密
words.ex: The government decided to declassify the documents after 30 years.
words.ex_cn: 政府决定在30年后解密这些文件。
words.en: To declassify information means to officially state that it is no longer secret.

words.ex: He tried to eavesdrop on their conversation.
words.ex_cn: 他试图偷听他们的对话。
words.en: To eavesdrop means to listen secretly to other people's conversations.

words.ex: He enciphers his messages with a simple code.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个简单的密码加密他的信息。
words.en: To convert (a message or information) into a cipher or code.

words.ex: He gave a furtive look around before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他离开前偷偷看了一眼四周。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as furtive, you disapprove of them behaving as if they want to keep something secret or hidden.

words.ex: The map has an indicative arrow to show the way.
words.ex_cn: 这张地图上有一个指示方向的箭头。
words.en: If one thing is indicative of another, it suggests what the other thing is likely to be.

words.tr:
adj. 超自然的；神秘的；隐藏的
v. 掩蔽
n. 神秘的事物；神秘学
words.ex: He is interested in the occult.
words.ex_cn: 他对神秘学感兴趣。
words.en: Relating to mystical, supernatural, or magical powers, practices, or phenomena.

words.tr:
v. 潜行以觅食；窥伺；逡巡于
n. 悄然潜行；四处觅食；徘徊
words.ex: The cat will prowl around the house at night.
words.ex_cn: 猫会在晚上在房子周围徘徊。
words.en: To move around quietly in a place trying not to be seen or heard, especially when you are looking for something or someone.

words.ex: The police discovered a scheme to steal money.
words.ex_cn: 警方发现了一个偷钱的阴谋。
words.en: A scheme is a plan or arrangement, especially one produced by a government or other organization, or a secret plan to do something, especially something illegal or dishonest.

words.tr: adj. 遮遮掩掩的；守口如瓶的；
words.ex: He gave a secretive smile and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他露出一个遮遮掩掩的微笑，然后走开了。
words.en: If you are secretive, you like to have secrets and to keep your knowledge, feelings, or intentions hidden.

words.tr: v. 侧向移动；悄悄贴近
words.ex: She sidled up to him and whispered in his ear.
words.ex_cn: 她侧身悄悄靠近他，在他耳边低语。
words.en: To move sideways or obliquely, especially in a stealthy or furtive manner.

words.tr:
adj. 偷偷摸摸的；暗中的
v. 溜；偷偷地做；“sneak”的现在分词
words.ex: She had a sneaking suspicion that he was lying.
words.ex_cn: 她有一种偷偷的怀疑，认为他在撒谎。
words.en: If you have a sneaking feeling about something, you have a slight suspicion or awareness of it, often without being able to explain why.

words.tr: n. 秘密行动；偷偷摸摸
words.ex: The cat moved in stealth to catch the mouse.
words.ex_cn: 猫悄悄地移动去抓老鼠。
words.en: Stealth is the action of moving or behaving in a secretive way in order to avoid being noticed.

words.tr: adj. 秘密的；鬼鬼祟祟的；偷偷摸摸的
words.ex: He gave a surreptitious glance at his phone during class.
words.ex_cn: 他在上课时偷偷瞥了一眼手机。
words.en: If something is done surreptitiously, it is done secretly, often because it would not be approved of.

words.tr: adj. 神秘的；不可思议的；
words.ex: The uncanny silence in the forest made him nervous.
words.ex_cn: 森林里那神秘的寂静让他感到紧张。
words.en: If you describe something as uncanny, you mean that it is strange and difficult to explain.

words.tr:
n. 搭线窃听装置；窃听或偷录
v. 用窃听器监听；在…装窃听器
words.ex: The police installed a wiretap on the suspect's phone.
words.ex_cn: 警方在嫌疑人的电话上安装了窃听装置。
words.en: A wiretap is a device used to listen secretly to other people's telephone conversations, or the act of using such a device.

words.tr:
adj. 每两年一次的；二年生的
n. 二年生植物
words.ex: The biennial art show attracts many visitors.
words.ex_cn: 每两年一次的艺术展吸引了很多参观者。
words.en: Happening every two years or lasting for two years.

words.ex: He makes frequent trips to the city.
words.ex_cn: 他经常去城市。
words.en: If something is frequent, it happens often.

words.tr: adj. 每日的；平凡的；平常的
words.ex: He drinks coffee every quotidian morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都喝咖啡。
words.en: Something that is quotidian occurs every day or is very common and ordinary.

words.tr: adj. 有节奏的；有韵律的；
words.ex: The children danced to the rhythmic beat.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们随着有节奏的节拍跳舞。
words.en: A rhythmic sound or movement has a clear and regular pattern that is repeated.

words.ex: The phone vibrates when it receives a call.
words.ex_cn: 当手机收到电话时，它会震动。
words.en: To vibrate means to move rapidly to and fro or up and down; to oscillate.

words.ex: Her garrulity made it difficult for anyone to get a word in edgewise.
words.ex_cn: 她的多嘴多舌让任何人几乎无法插话。
words.en: Garrulity is the quality of being excessively talkative, especially about trivial matters.

words.tr: adj. 絮聒的；饶舌的；多嘴的
words.ex: He is garrulous and talks too much.
words.ex_cn: 他话很多，说个不停。
words.en: If you describe someone as garrulous, you mean that they talk a lot, especially about things that are not important.

words.tr: adj. 迂回曲折的；转弯抹角的
words.ex: The politician used a periphrastic response to avoid directly answering the question.
words.ex_cn: 这位政治家用一种迂回的回答来避免直接回答问题。
words.en: If someone uses periphrastic language, they express something in an indirect way, using more words than necessary.

words.ex: The phrase 'free gift' is pleonastic because 'gift' implies something given without charge.
words.ex_cn: 短语'免费礼物'是冗言的，因为'礼物'本身就意味着不收费。
words.en: Using more words than are necessary to convey meaning, often to the point of redundancy.

words.ex: His prolix speech made everyone bored.
words.ex_cn: 他冗长的演讲让所有人都感到无聊。
words.en: Using or containing too many words; tediously lengthy.

words.tr: n. 冗长无聊的废话；繁琐的程序；一连串的无聊举动
words.ex: He went on a rigmarole about his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他滔滔不绝地讲述他的童年。
words.en: A rigmarole is a long and complicated process that seems unnecessary and is often annoying.

words.ex: The long meeting was tedious.
words.ex_cn: 这场漫长的会议很沉闷。
words.en: If you describe something such as a job, task, or situation as tedious, you mean it is boring and rather frustrating.

words.ex: He used too much verbiage in his email.
words.ex_cn: 他在邮件中用了太多的冗词。
words.en: Verbiage refers to an overabundance of words in writing or speech, often seen as unnecessary or overly complex.

words.ex: He gave a verbose answer to the simple question.
words.ex_cn: 他对简单的问题给出了冗长的回答。
words.en: Using or containing more words than are necessary; long-winded.

words.tr: v. 痛击；痛斥；冗长地解释
words.ex: He belabored the point until everyone was bored.
words.ex_cn: 他反复讨论那个观点，直到大家都感到厌烦。
words.en: To argue or discuss (a subject) in excessive detail; to attack or criticize (someone) persistently.

words.ex: He took a circuitous route to avoid the traffic.
words.ex_cn: 他绕了远路以避开交通拥堵。
words.en: A circuitous route, journey, or piece of writing is longer than it needs to be because it is not direct.

words.tr: adj. (行文说话等)委婉曲折的；拐弯抹角的
words.ex: His circumlocutory speech made it difficult to understand his point.
words.ex_cn: 他拐弯抹角的讲话让人难以理解他的观点。
words.en: Using many words where fewer would do, especially in a deliberate attempt to be vague or evasive.

words.tr:
v. 说傻话；胡说；淌口水；流鼻涕
n. 胡言乱语；糊涂话
words.ex: He was so tired that he started to drivel incoherently.
words.ex_cn: 他太累了，开始胡言乱语。
words.en: If you describe what someone says as drivel, you mean that it is nonsense.

words.tr: adj. 气长的；啰嗦的；冗长的
words.ex: His long-winded speech made everyone sleepy.
words.ex_cn: 他冗长的演讲让所有人都犯困。
words.en: If you describe something that someone says or writes as long-winded, you are critical of it because it is too long, often because the same thing is said more than once.

words.ex: The judge criticized the lawyer for his prolixity in the court.
words.ex_cn: 法官批评了律师在法庭上的冗长发言。
words.en: Prolixity refers to the use of too many words to express an idea, making speech or writing tediously lengthy.

words.ex: The river has a sinuous path through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这条河在森林中蜿蜒流淌。
words.en: Something that is sinuous has many smooth turns and curves.

words.ex: The extra words are superfluous.
words.ex_cn: 这些额外的词是多余的。
words.en: Something that is superfluous is unnecessary or no longer needed.

words.tr: adj. 宽松的；容积大的；部头大的；卷数多的
words.ex: She wore a voluminous dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条宽松的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is voluminous is very large or contains a lot of things.

words.tr: adj. 蜿蜒的； v. “wind”的现在分词；
words.ex: The winding road goes through the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这条蜿蜒的道路穿过山脉。
words.en: A winding path, road, river, etc. repeatedly turns in different directions.

words.ex: It is a windy day today.
words.ex_cn: 今天是多风的一天。
words.en: If it is windy, the wind is blowing a lot.

words.ex: The verbosity of the report made it difficult to understand.
words.ex_cn: 报告的冗长使得它难以理解。
words.en: Verbosity is the quality of using more words than needed; wordiness.

words.tr: adj. 话多的；健谈的；喋喋不休的
words.ex: He is a loquacious man who talks all day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个整天喋喋不休的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as loquacious, you mean that they talk a lot.

words.tr: n. 冗长的文章；砂浆层
words.ex: He wrote a long screed about politics.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一篇关于政治的长篇大论。
words.en: A long and often tedious speech or piece of writing.

words.ex: He is harping on about the same mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他一直在唠叨同一个错误。
words.en: To keep talking or complaining about something in a way that is annoying.

words.tr: n. 连祷文；枯燥冗长的陈述
words.ex: The meeting was filled with a litany of complaints.
words.ex_cn: 会议充斥着冗长的抱怨。
words.en: A litany is a form of prayer in which a series of petitions are recited by a leader with responses from the congregation. It can also refer to any long, tedious account or recital.

words.ex: Her loquacity made it difficult to get a word in edgewise.
words.ex_cn: 她的多话使得别人很难插上话。
words.en: The quality of talking a great deal; talkativeness.

words.tr: adj. 可延展的；易于塑造的
words.ex: The gold is ductile and can be drawn into thin wires.
words.ex_cn: 金具有延展性，可以拉成细丝。
words.en: A ductile material is one that can be stretched into a wire or hammered into a thin sheet without breaking.

words.tr: n. 展延性；柔软性；顺从
words.ex: Gold is prized for its ductility and ability to be drawn into thin wires.
words.ex_cn: 黄金因其延展性好，能被拉成细丝而受到珍视。
words.en: Ductility is the ability of a material to be drawn or plastically deformed without fracture; it is therefore a measure of a material's ability to undergo deformation under tensile stress.

words.ex: The floppy ears of the dog waved when it ran.
words.ex_cn: 狗的松垂耳朵在它跑时晃动。
words.en: Something that is floppy is loose and soft, often hanging or bending in a way that suggests it lacks stiffness.

words.tr: adj. 细长而弯曲的；瘦削的；平直的；稀疏的
words.ex: Her lank hair hung down to her waist.
words.ex_cn: 她那细长柔软的头发垂到了腰部。
words.en: If someone is lank, they are tall and thin in a way that is not attractive.

words.tr:
adj. 柔软的；可塑的；易弯曲的；有弹性的
v. 使柔软；把（火炮）系在前车上；做热身运动
n. （拖炮车的）前车
words.ex: The gymnast's body is remarkably limber.
words.ex_cn: 这位体操运动员的身体非常柔软。
words.en: Capable of moving or bending easily; flexible.

words.tr: adj. 易弯的；柔软的；动作轻盈的
words.ex: The dancer is lithe and moves gracefully.
words.ex_cn: 这位舞者身材柔韧，动作优雅。
words.en: A person or animal that is lithe is thin, supple, and graceful.

words.ex: The plastic is pliable and easy to bend.
words.ex_cn: 这种塑料柔韧，容易弯曲。
words.en: A pliable object or material is easy to bend or shape without breaking.

words.tr: adj. 顺从的；易屈服的；柔软的；易弯曲的
words.ex: He is a yielding student who always follows the teacher's rules.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个顺从的学生，总是遵守老师的规则。
words.en: A yielding person or thing is one that is flexible or compliant, often bending or giving way under pressure.

words.tr: n. 读者（数）；高级讲师职位
words.ex: The newspaper has a large readership.
words.ex_cn: 这份报纸拥有大量的读者。
words.en: The number or type of people who read a particular newspaper, magazine, or book.

words.tr: adj. 用不完的；无穷无尽的；
words.ex: The sun provides an inexhaustible source of energy.
words.ex_cn: 太阳提供一种用不完的能量来源。
words.en: If you describe something as inexhaustible, you are emphasizing that there is a very large quantity of it and that it is not likely to be used up or to run out.

words.ex: He didn't care about an iota of the details.
words.ex_cn: 他对这些细节的极小量都不在意。
words.en: An iota is an extremely small amount of something.

words.tr: n. 少量；一点点；一小份
words.ex: He had a modicum of common sense.
words.ex_cn: 他有一点点常识。
words.en: A modicum of something, especially something that is good or desirable, is a small but useful or significant amount of it.

words.tr:
n. 浅薄的知识；一知半解；微量
v.  充内行；“smatter”的现在分词
words.ex: He has a smattering of knowledge in many subjects.
words.ex_cn: 他在许多科目上只有一知半解的知识。
words.en: A smattering of something is a small amount of it or a few things about it.

words.ex: Smartphones are ubiquitous in modern life.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机在现代生活中无处不在。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as ubiquitous, you mean that they seem to be everywhere.

words.ex: I have a whit of patience left.
words.ex_cn: 我只剩下一点点耐心了。
words.en: A whit is a very small amount of something, used especially in negative expressions to mean 'not at all'.

words.ex: A bevy of birds flew over the lake.
words.ex_cn: 一群鸟飞过湖面。
words.en: A bevy of people or things is a group of them, especially a group of women or girls.

words.tr: n. 极漫长的时期；永世；千万年
words.ex: This rock has been here for an eon.
words.ex_cn: 这块岩石已经在这里存在了亿万年。
words.en: An eon is an extremely long period of time.

words.ex: She coordinates the team's schedule.
words.ex_cn: 她协调团队的安排。
words.en: If you coordinate an activity, you organize the various people and things involved in it. If you coordinate the different parts of your body, you make them work together efficiently.

words.ex: Fish abound in this river.
words.ex_cn: 这条河里鱼很多。
words.en: If things abound, or if a place abounds with things, there are very large numbers of them.

words.ex: There is an abundance of food at the party.
words.ex_cn: 聚会上食物非常丰富。
words.en: A very large quantity of something.

words.ex: The forest has abundant water and trees.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林水源和树木都很丰富。
words.en: If something is abundant, there is a lot of it or it is very common.

words.ex: The water supply is adequate for the village.
words.ex_cn: 供水对这个村庄来说是足够的。
words.en: If something is adequate, there is enough of it or it is good enough to be used or accepted.

words.ex: His family's affluence allowed him to travel the world.
words.ex_cn: 他家的富裕让他能环游世界。
words.en: Affluence is the state of having a lot of money or owning many things.

words.ex: The affluent family bought a big house by the lake.
words.ex_cn: 这个富裕的家庭在湖边买了一栋大房子。
