words.en: Having a great deal of money; wealthy.

words.ex: This is a good example of teamwork.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个团队合作的好例子。
words.en: An example is a particular instance of something that is representative of a group or used to illustrate a point.

words.ex: He ate a chunk of cheese for lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午餐吃了一大块奶酪。
words.en: A chunk of something is a large piece or amount of it.

words.ex: He has a considerable amount of money.
words.ex_cn: 他有相当多的钱。
words.en: Considerable means large in size, amount, or extent.

words.ex: He wrote copious notes during the lecture.
words.ex_cn: 他在讲座期间写了大量的笔记。
words.en: Something that is copious exists in large amounts.

words.tr: n. 丰饶的山羊角；聚宝盆；丰饶角
words.ex: The Thanksgiving table had a cornucopia of fruits and vegetables.
words.ex_cn: 感恩节的餐桌上摆满了水果和蔬菜的丰饶山羊角。
words.en: A cornucopia is a symbol of abundance and nourishment, commonly represented as a large horn-shaped container overflowing with produce, flowers, or nuts.

words.ex: The linguist analyzed the English corpus to find common phrases.
words.ex_cn: 语言学家分析了英语语料库以寻找常用短语。
words.en: A corpus is a large collection of written or spoken texts that is used for language research.

words.ex: He has a dual role as teacher and coach.
words.ex_cn: 他同时担任老师和教练的双重角色。
words.en: Having two parts or aspects.

words.ex: The exodus of people from the city happened after the flood.
words.ex_cn: 洪水之后，大批人离开了这座城市。
words.en: An exodus is a situation in which many people leave a place at the same time.

words.ex: The fecundity of the rabbits helped them grow quickly.
words.ex_cn: 兔子的高繁殖力帮助它们迅速增长。
words.en: The ability to produce an abundance of offspring or new growth; fertility.

words.tr: adj. 过分虚伪而令人生厌的
words.ex: He gave her a fulsome compliment.
words.ex_cn: 他给了她一段过分的赞美。
words.en: If you describe expressions of praise, apology, or gratitude as fulsome, you disapprove of them because they are exaggerated and elaborate, so that they sound insincere.

words.tr:
n. 供过于求；过量
v. 使充满；过量供应
words.ex: The market has a glut of cheap phones.
words.ex_cn: 市场上廉价手机泛滥。
words.en: An excessive supply of something, more than is needed, wanted, or can be used; to supply or fill to excess.

words.ex: The difference between the two values is infinitesimal.
words.ex_cn: 这两个值之间的差异极微。
words.en: Something that is infinitesimal is extremely small.

words.ex: The luxuriant forest had thick trees and deep green leaves.
words.ex_cn: 这片茂密的森林有茂盛的树木和深绿色的叶子。
words.en: Luxuriant is used to describe something that is rich in growth, abundance, or opulence.

words.ex: The garden has manifold flowers.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园里有繁多的花朵。
words.en: If something is manifold, it has many different parts, features, or forms.

words.tr:
adj. 无数的；
n. 无数；
words.ex: There are myriad stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中有无数的星星。
words.en: A myriad of things or people is a very large number of them.

words.ex: The score was nil at the end of the game.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束时分数为零。
words.en: Nothing or none; used to indicate the absence of something.

words.ex: There are numerous books on the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 书架上有许多书。
words.en: If people or things are numerous, they exist or are present in large numbers.

words.ex: The palace had opulent carpets and golden chandeliers.
words.ex_cn: 宫殿里有华丽的地毯和金色的吊灯。
words.en: Having or displaying great wealth or richness.

words.tr: adj. 没有用的；不必要的；多余的
words.ex: The meeting was deemed otiose as it did not address any new issues.
words.ex_cn: 这次会议被认为是多余的，因为它没有解决任何新问题。
words.en: If you describe something as otiose, you mean that it serves no practical purpose or has no effect.

words.tr: adj. 充满...的；挤满人的；拥挤的； v. 包装；“pack”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The bus was packed with people.
words.ex_cn: 公交车上挤满了人。
words.en: Filled with a large number of people or things.

words.tr: n. 微薄的工资；极少的报酬
words.ex: He lived on a pittance during his early career.
words.ex_cn: 他在职业生涯初期靠微薄的收入生活。
words.en: A very small or inadequate amount of money paid to someone as an allowance or wage.

words.tr: adj. 人口众多的；人口密集的
words.ex: China is a populous country.
words.ex_cn: 中国是一个人口众多的国家。
words.en: If a place is populous, it has a large population.

words.ex: He is a prolific writer who publishes books every year.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位多产的作家，每年都会出版书籍。
words.en: A prolific artist, writer, or composer produces a large number of works of art, books, or pieces of music.

words.ex: The rarefaction of the air at high altitudes makes breathing difficult.
words.ex_cn: 高海拔地区空气稀薄，使得呼吸困难。
words.en: Rarefaction is the process or result of making or becoming less dense or compact.

words.ex: He caught a scad while fishing at the pier.
words.ex_cn: 他在码头钓鱼时捕到一条竹荚鱼。
words.en: A large number or amount of something.

words.ex: He has scads of toy cars.
words.ex_cn: 他有大量的玩具车。
words.en: If you refer to scads of things or people, you are emphasizing that there are a lot of them.

words.ex: This segment of the book is very interesting.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的这一部分非常有趣。
words.en: A segment of something is one of the parts into which it is divided or from which it is formed.

words.ex: The serried ranks of the audience applauded enthusiastically.
words.ex_cn: 密集的观众行列热情地鼓掌。
words.en: If people or things are serried, they are standing or arranged closely together in rows.

words.tr: adj. 重大的；重要的；影响明显的；
words.ex: This discovery is a significant step forward.
words.ex_cn: 这一发现是一个重大的进步。
words.en: Something that is significant is important or large enough to be noticed or to have an effect.

words.tr: v. （使）回转；（使）侧滑n. 大量；许多v. 杀死；杀害；残害；宰杀；“slay”的过去式
words.ex: The car slewed around the corner.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在拐角处突然转向。
words.en: To kill someone or something in a violent way; to turn or slide violently or uncontrollably in a particular direction.

words.tr: adj. 单独的；独唱的；独奏的；
words.ex: He played a solo guitar piece at the concert.
words.ex_cn: 他在音乐会上演奏了一首独奏吉他曲。
words.en: A solo is a piece of music or a performance done by one person alone, without any accompaniment.

words.tr: n. 泛滥；猛涨；大批；一连串
words.ex: A spate of rain flooded the streets.
words.ex_cn: 一场暴雨淹没了街道。
words.en: A spate of things, especially unpleasant ones, is a large number of them that happen or appear within a short period of time.

words.ex: One apple will suffice for now.
words.ex_cn: 一个苹果现在就足够了。
words.en: If something suffices, it is enough to achieve a purpose or to fulfill a need.

words.ex: We have sufficient food for the trip.
words.ex_cn: 我们有足够的食物用于这次旅行。
words.en: If something is sufficient for a particular purpose, there is enough of it for the purpose.

words.tr: n. 多余物；过剩品；多余
words.ex: The superfluity of clothes made her room messy.
words.ex_cn: 过多的衣服让她的房间乱糟糟的。
words.en: Superfluity refers to an unnecessarily large amount of something, more than is needed.

words.tr:
n. 人群；一大群；众多
v. 群集；挤满；涌进
words.ex: A throng of people waited outside the store.
words.ex_cn: 一大群人站在商店外面等候。
words.en: A large, densely packed crowd of people or animals.

words.tr: adj. 无穷尽的；经久不衰的；永远可靠的
words.ex: Her unfailing smile made everyone feel welcome.
words.ex_cn: 她永不消失的微笑让每个人都感到受欢迎。
words.en: If you describe someone's good qualities or behaviour as unfailing, you mean that they never change.

words.ex: There are untold stories behind this war.
words.ex_cn: 这场战争背后有着数不清的故事。
words.en: If you refer to an amount as untold, you are emphasizing that it is very large, usually so large that it cannot be measured or counted.

words.ex: Beijing is a transport hub in China.
words.ex_cn: 北京是中国的交通中心。
words.en: A hub is the central part of a wheel, rotating on or with the axle, and from which the spokes radiate. It can also refer to a central point of activity or interest.

words.ex: The fence marks the perimeter of the garden.
words.ex_cn: 围栏标出了花园的边界。
words.en: The perimeter of an area or object is the total length of its sides or outer boundary.

words.ex: The room was devoid of any furniture.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间里全无家具。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is devoid of a quality or thing, you are emphasizing that they have none of it.

words.tr: adj. 无价的；无法估计的
words.ex: Her kindness is inestimable.
words.ex_cn: 她的善良是无法估量的。
words.en: If you describe the value, benefit, or importance of something as inestimable, you mean that it is extremely great and cannot be calculated.

words.ex: The witch stirred a magic potion.
words.ex_cn: 女巫搅拌了一瓶魔药。
words.en: A potion is a liquid that is believed to have magical or medicinal properties.

words.ex: A quorum must be present to conduct official business.
words.ex_cn: 必须有法定人数在场才能进行正式业务。
words.en: A quorum is the minimum number of people that must be present at a meeting before it can officially begin and before official decisions can be taken.

words.tr: adj. 慷慨的；优厚的； 大方的
words.ex: He gave a munificent donation to the school.
words.ex_cn: 他向学校捐赠了一笔慷慨的款项。
words.en: If you describe someone as munificent, you mean that they are very generous, often in the form of giving money or gifts.

words.tr: n. 大量；丰富；慷慨；浪费
words.ex: There is a profusion of flowers in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 花园里有大量花朵。
words.en: If there is a profusion of something or it occurs in profusion, there is a very large quantity or variety of it.

words.ex: The table was replete with food.
words.ex_cn: 桌子上摆满了食物。
words.en: If you are replete with something, you have a lot of it and it fills you up.

words.tr: adj. 俗艳的；花哨的；过分装饰的
words.ex: The room was decorated in a garish pink that hurt the eyes.
words.ex_cn: 房间被装饰成刺眼的粉红色，令人眼睛不适。
words.en: If you describe something as garish, you mean that it is excessively bright, colorful, or elaborate in a way that is considered tasteless or unattractive.

words.ex: The room was decorated with gaudy colors that hurt the eyes.
words.ex_cn: 房间用俗丽的颜色装饰，刺眼。
words.en: If you describe something as gaudy, you mean that it is very brightly coloured and showy, but not in an attractive way.

words.tr: adj. 俗气的；华而不实的；虚有其表的
words.ex: The decoration was meretricious and lacked any real artistic merit.
words.ex_cn: 装饰俗气，缺乏真正的艺术价值。
words.en: Something that is meretricious is attractive in a showy or cheap way, often without having any real value or quality.

words.tr: adj. 俗丽而不值钱的；花里胡哨的
words.ex: She wore a tawdry dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿着一件俗丽的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe something as tawdry, you mean that it is showy and bright but of very poor quality.

words.tr:
adj. 虚有其表的；花哨而无价值的
n. 中看不中用的东西
words.ex: The expensive gadget turned out to be mere trumpery.
words.ex_cn: 这个昂贵的装置原来只是中看不中用的东西。
words.en: Something that is showy but of little value or use; nonsense or trivialities.

words.ex: His antic behavior made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他滑稽的行为让大家都笑了。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as antic, you mean that it is strange and foolish in a way that is amusing.

words.ex: He believes education is his birthright.
words.ex_cn: 他认为教育是他的天赋权利。
words.en: A birthright is a right, privilege, or possession that a person has from birth, especially as a descendant of a particular family or social class.

words.tr: adj. 古怪的；暴躁的；有毛病的
words.ex: He is cranky when he doesn't sleep well.
words.ex_cn: 他睡眠不好时会脾气暴躁。
words.en: If you describe someone as cranky, you mean they are bad-tempered and irritable.

words.tr: n. 奇事；巧合；怪癖；奇行
words.ex: His habit of talking to his plants is a strange quirk.
words.ex_cn: 他跟植物说话的习惯是一个奇怪的奇事。
words.en: A quirk is a peculiar habit or aspect of a person's character, or an unexpected twist in a situation or story.

words.tr:
n. 特点；特性；
adj. 典型的；特有的；
words.ex: Honesty is a key characteristic of a good friend.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是一个好朋友的关键特点。
words.en: A characteristic is a quality or feature that is typical of someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 卓越的；杰出的；罕见的；特别的；
words.ex: She is an exceptional student who always gets top grades.
words.ex_cn: 她是一名卓越的学生，总是取得最高分。
words.en: An exceptional person or thing has some unusual quality or ability that makes them different from others.

words.tr: n. 专门知识；专门技能；
words.ex: His expertise in computers helps the team solve problems.
words.ex_cn: 他在计算机方面的专门知识帮助团队解决问题。
words.en: Expertise is special skill or knowledge that is acquired by training, study, or practice.

words.tr:
n. 特征；报刊特写；
v. 以…为特色；是…的重要组成；
words.ex: The main feature of this phone is its long battery life.
words.ex_cn: 这款手机的主要特征是续航时间长。
words.en: A feature of something is an interesting or important part or characteristic of it.

words.ex: The hallmark of a good teacher is patience.
words.ex_cn: 好老师的标志是耐心。
words.en: A hallmark is a distinctive characteristic or attribute that is typical of a particular person or thing.

words.tr:
n. 个人；
adj. 个别的；单独的；
words.ex: Each individual has the right to speak freely.
words.ex_cn: 每个人都有权自由发言。
words.en: An individual is a person considered separately from their society or community. As an adjective, it describes something that is single, separate, or unique to a person or thing.

words.tr: n. 实际知识；技术；窍门
words.ex: He has the know-how to fix the machine.
words.ex_cn: 他有修理这台机器的诀窍。
words.en: Practical knowledge or expertise in a particular field or area.

words.ex: The artist carefully drew the lineaments of the face.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家仔细地勾勒出脸部的轮廓。
words.en: The features or characteristics of a face, especially when considered as an indication of character or identity.

words.ex: His painting shows great originality.
words.ex_cn: 他的画作展现了极大的独创性。
words.en: The quality of being new and original in a way that is not derived from something else.

words.ex: It is the president's prerogative to make final decisions.
words.ex_cn: 做最终决定是总统的特权。
words.en: A prerogative is a right or privilege exclusive to a particular individual or class.

words.ex: Going first is a privilege, not a right.
words.ex_cn: 优先权是一种特权，而不是权利。
words.en: A privilege is a special right or advantage that only one person or group has.

words.ex: This painting is unique because no other like it exists.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是独特的，因为没有其他类似的。
words.en: Something that is unique is the only one of its kind.

words.ex: His physiognomy showed kindness and calm.
words.ex_cn: 他的相貌展现出善良与平静。
words.en: The physiognomy of a person or animal is their face, especially when this is considered in relation to their character or temperament.

words.tr:
n. 纤毛虫
adj. 有纤毛的；具缘毛的
words.ex: The ciliate protozoa are characterized by the presence of cilia.
words.ex_cn: 纤毛原生动物的特点是具有纤毛。
words.en: Having cilia; relating to or characteristic of ciliates.

words.tr: adj. 圆圈的；环形的；循环的；
words.ex: The table has a circular top.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子有一个圆形的桌面。
words.en: Something that is circular is shaped like a circle.

words.tr: n. 结构；布局；配置；外形
words.ex: The configuration of the computer is very simple.
words.ex_cn: 这台电脑的配置非常简单。
words.en: The arrangement of parts or elements in a particular form, figure, or combination.

words.ex: They erect a flagpole in the park.
words.ex_cn: 他们在公园里竖立一根旗杆。
words.en: If people erect something such as a building, bridge, or barrier, they build it or create it.

words.ex: The old building has a beautiful facade with stone pillars.
words.ex_cn: 这栋老建筑有一个带有石柱的漂亮正面。
words.en: The front of a building, especially an imposing or decorative one. Also, a superficial appearance or illusion of something.

words.ex: The diamond has many smooth facets.
words.ex_cn: 这颗钻石有许多光滑的小平面。
words.en: A particular aspect or feature of something.

words.ex: He spoke in the guise of a friend.
words.ex_cn: 他以朋友的伪装说话。
words.en: An external form, appearance, or manner of presentation, typically concealing the true nature of something.

words.ex: The graph shows a linear relationship between time and distance.
words.ex_cn: 这张图显示了时间与距离之间的线性关系。
words.en: Linear means involving or relating to a straight line or lines.

words.ex: The osseous tissue supports the body.
words.ex_cn: 骨组织支撑身体。
words.en: Of, relating to, or consisting of bone.

words.ex: His ostensible reason for leaving was sickness.
words.ex_cn: 他离开的表面原因是生病。
words.en: An ostensible reason or purpose seems to be the real one, but it is not.

words.tr: n. 铜绿锈；（金属表面的）绿锈；（旧木器等表面）年久而产生的光泽；（有点儿…的）样子
words.ex: The patina on the old bronze statue added to its charm.
words.ex_cn: 旧青铜雕像上的铜绿增添了它的魅力。
words.en: A patina is a thin layer that forms on the surface of something, especially metal, often as a result of age or exposure to the air, and that is usually green or brown.

words.tr:
adj. 垂直的；笔直的
n. 垂直线
words.ex: The lines are perpendicular to each other.
words.ex_cn: 这些线互相垂直。
words.en: At right angles to the plane of the horizon or a base line; vertical.

words.tr:
n. 辫子；辫状物；发辫
v. 将…编成辫
words.ex: She wore her hair in a neat plait.
words.ex_cn: 她把头发编成了整齐的辫子。
words.en: A plait is a length of hair that has been twisted over and under other pieces of hair to form one thick length. To plait hair means to twist three or more lengths of hair over and under each other to form one thick length.

words.tr: adj. 难看的；不悦目的；不雅观的
words.ex: The construction site was an unsightly mess.
words.ex_cn: 建筑工地看起来一片狼藉，很不雅观。
words.en: If you describe something as unsightly, you mean that it is unattractive to look at.

words.tr:
v. 梳理；“hackle”的第三人称单数
n. （猫狗等动物的）后颈毛；厌烦；恼怒
words.ex: The dog's hackles rose as it sensed danger.
words.ex_cn: 狗感觉到危险时颈部的毛竖了起来。
words.en: The hackles are the hairs along the back of an animal's neck, which rise when the animal is angry or frightened. In humans, the term can also refer to a state of anger or irritation.

words.ex: He avoids eating sugar to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他避免吃糖以保持健康。
words.en: If you avoid something, you take action in order to prevent it from happening to you.

words.ex: The portly man walks slowly with a cane.
words.ex_cn: 这位胖胖的男人拄着拐杖慢慢走。
words.en: If you describe someone as portly, you mean that they are fat in a dignified way.

words.tr: adj. （多）肌腱的；坚韧的；肌肉强壮有力的
words.ex: He had a sinewy build, with muscles that stood out clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他肌肉发达，肌肉线条清晰可见。
words.en: Having or consisting of sinews; muscular and strong.

words.ex: The incrustation on the pipe needed to be removed to restore proper flow.
words.ex_cn: 管子上的硬壳需要被清除以恢复正常的流动。
words.en: An incrustation is a hard outer layer or covering that forms on something, often as a result of a chemical reaction or the accumulation of material.

words.tr: n. 受公众注意的程度；简介；轮廓；
words.ex: The celebrity's profile rose after the TV interview.
words.ex_cn: 这位名人经过电视采访后，受公众注意的程度提高了。
words.en: A profile is a side view of something, especially a person's face, or a brief description of someone or something.

words.ex: The old eggs began to addle in the heat.
words.ex_cn: 这些旧鸡蛋在热中开始腐臭。
words.en: If something addles someone's mind or brain, it confuses them and makes them unable to think clearly.

words.tr:
n. 熏香；熏香的烟
v. 使愤怒；激怒
words.ex: The smell of incense fills the room.
words.ex_cn: 香火的气味充满了房间。
words.en: Incense is a substance that is burned for its pleasant smell, often used in religious ceremonies. As a verb, to incense means to make someone very angry.

words.tr: adj. 芬香的；特别美味的
words.ex: The scent of the ambrosial flowers filled the air.
words.ex_cn: 芬芳馥郁的花香弥漫在空气中。
words.en: Something that is ambrosial is extremely pleasant to taste or smell, often described as divine or heavenly.

words.tr: adj. 开胃的；促进食欲的
words.ex: The smell of the food was appetizing.
words.ex_cn: 食物的香味很诱人。
words.en: If you describe food as appetizing, you mean that it looks or smells good and makes you want to eat it.

words.ex: The aroma of fresh bread filled the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 新鲜面包的香味充满了厨房。
words.en: An aroma is a strong, pleasant smell.

words.ex: The flowers are aromatic and fill the garden with scent.
words.ex_cn: 这些花是芳香的，使花园充满香气。
words.en: Having a pleasant and distinctive smell.

words.ex: The water in the swamp is brackish.
words.ex_cn: 沼泽里的水是微咸的。
words.en: Brackish water is slightly salty, as is the mixture of river water and seawater in estuaries.

words.tr:
adj. 甜得发腻的；令人腻烦的
v. 感到腻烦；“cloy”的现在分词
words.ex: The cloying sweetness of the cake made me sick.
words.ex_cn: 蛋糕过于甜腻的味道让我感到恶心。
words.en: If you describe something as cloying, you mean that it is so sweet or sentimental that it is unpleasant.

words.tr: adj. 浓烈的；醇厚的；圆润的（音质）
words.ex: The wine had a full-bodied flavor with hints of blackberry and oak.
words.ex_cn: 这款酒口感浓郁，带有黑莓和橡木的香气。
words.en: Having a rich, strong flavor or quality.

words.ex: The art of wine tasting involves the science of gustation.
words.ex_cn: 品酒的艺术涉及味觉的科学。
words.en: Gustation is the act or faculty of tasting, the sense by which the qualities and flavor of a substance are distinguished by the taste buds.

words.ex: The gustatory sense helps us taste food.
words.ex_cn: 味觉帮助我们品尝食物。
words.en: Relating to the sense of taste.

words.tr: adj. 美味的；甘美的；满足感官的；性感的
words.ex: The fruit was luscious and sweet.
words.ex_cn: 这种水果甘甜可口。
words.en: If you describe something as luscious, you mean that it is very pleasant to taste, smell, look at, or listen to.

words.tr: adj. 散发气味的；香的；臭的
words.ex: The odoriferous flowers filled the room with their sweet scent.
words.ex_cn: 芬芳的花朵用它们的甜香充满了房间。
words.en: Having or giving off a smell, especially a pleasant one.

words.ex: The dog uses olfaction to find the hidden toy.
words.ex_cn: 狗用嗅觉找到藏起来的玩具。
words.en: The sense of smell, or the act of smelling.

words.tr: adj. 有...气味的；令人想起...的
words.ex: The garden is redolent of roses.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园弥漫着玫瑰的香气。
words.en: Strongly reminiscent or suggestive of something.

words.ex: The garden was filled with the redolence of blooming roses.
words.ex_cn: 花园里充满了盛开的玫瑰的芬芳。
words.en: a pleasant smell

words.ex: The soup is tasty and hot.
words.ex_cn: 这汤美味又热。
words.en: If you describe food as tasty, you mean that it has a pleasant and attractive flavour.

words.ex: She bought an unscented lotion to avoid skin irritation.
words.ex_cn: 她买了一瓶无香味的乳液，以避免皮肤刺激。
words.en: Not having a scent or fragrance.

words.ex: The flower has a sweet fragrance.
words.ex_cn: 这朵花有一种甜美的香味。
words.en: A fragrance is a pleasant smell, especially that of a flower or perfume.

words.ex: The cactus has succulent leaves to store water.
words.ex_cn: 仙人掌有多汁的叶子来储存水分。
words.en: (of food) tender, juicy, and tasty; (of a plant) having thick, fleshy tissues adapted to water storage.

words.tr: adj. 似麝香的；有麝香味的
words.ex: The musky smell came from the old woods.
words.ex_cn: 那股麝香般的气味来自那片老树林。
words.en: Having the smell or qualities of musk.

words.ex: The wound was cleaned with saline water.
words.ex_cn: 伤口用盐水清洗。
words.en: Saline is used to describe something that contains salt or is related to salt.

words.ex: The soup was palatable after adding salt.
words.ex_cn: 加了盐后，汤变得可口美味了。
words.en: If you describe food or drink as palatable, you mean that it tastes pleasant.

words.tr:
adj. 咸的；辛辣的；好吃的；好闻的
n. 咸味小吃
words.ex: The savory snack made her thirsty.
words.ex_cn: 这道咸味小吃让她口渴了。
words.en: Savory food is pleasantly salty or spicy and not sweet in taste.

words.tr:
v. 品味；细品；享用；体会
n. 风味；滋味
words.ex: He savord the taste of the chocolate slowly.
words.ex_cn: 他慢慢地品味着巧克力的味道。
words.en: To enjoy or appreciate (something) completely.

words.ex: The small room was cosy with a warm blanket and a cup of tea.
words.ex_cn: 这个小房间铺着温暖的毯子，喝着热茶，非常舒适。
words.en: A place or situation that is cosy is comfortable and warm.

words.ex: The little cabin is cozy and warm.
words.ex_cn: 这座小木屋舒适又温暖。
words.en: A place that is cozy is comfortable and warm.

words.ex: The calorific value of the food is high.
words.ex_cn: 这种食物的发热量很高。
words.en: Calorific refers to the amount of energy contained in food or fuel, which is determined by the heat it produces when it is burned.

words.tr: adj. 微温的；不冷不热的；不热情的
words.ex: The water is lukewarm, so I didn't swim.
words.ex_cn: 水是温的，所以我没游泳。
words.en: If you describe something as lukewarm, you mean that it is only slightly warm, or that it is not very enthusiastic or interested.

words.tr:
adj. 温暖舒适的；紧密的；紧身的；贴身的
n. 酒馆内的雅间
words.ex: The cottage was snug and warm, perfect for a winter retreat.
words.ex_cn: 这间小屋舒适温暖，是冬季度假的完美之地。
words.en: If you feel snug or are in a snug place, you are very warm and comfortable, especially because you are protected from cold or danger.

words.tr: adj. 微温的；不冷不热的；不热情的
words.ex: He drank the tepid water slowly.
words.ex_cn: 他慢慢地喝着温吞的水。
words.en: Slightly warm; lukewarm. Also, showing little enthusiasm.

words.tr: adj. 易变化的；不稳定的
words.ex: The labile emotions of the character made the story unpredictable.
words.ex_cn: 这个角色易变的情绪使得故事变得不可预测。
words.en: If you describe someone as labile, you mean that their emotions or behavior are unstable and can change quickly.

words.tr: adj. 像海绵的；松软多孔的
words.ex: The bread is spongy and soft.
words.ex_cn: 这种面包松软有弹性。
words.en: Something that is spongy is soft and full of holes, like a sponge.

words.tr: adj. 不可靠的；不稳固的；无根据的；不佳的
words.ex: The building's structure was found to be unsound.
words.ex_cn: 这座建筑的结构被发现是不牢靠的。
words.en: If something or someone is unsound, they are not in a good condition or are not based on good reasons.

words.ex: He has an abiding love for music.
words.ex_cn: 他对音乐有着持久的热爱。
words.en: If you have an abiding feeling for someone or something, you have a feeling that lasts for a long time.

words.tr: adj. 恒定的；不变的；持续的；
words.ex: The temperature is constant in this room.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间的温度是恒定的。
words.en: Something that is constant happens all the time or is always there.

words.tr: adj. 根深蒂固的；生染的； v. “ingrain”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: His ingrained habits are hard to change.
words.ex_cn: 他根深蒂固的习惯很难改变。
words.en: If something is ingrained, it is firmly established and therefore difficult to change.

words.tr: n. 林波舞；不稳定状态；中间过渡状态
words.ex: The project is currently in limbo while we wait for approval.
words.ex_cn: 该项目目前处于待批准的中间状态。
words.en: A situation of uncertainty or neglect, especially one regarded as being in a state of waiting or not progressing.

words.ex: The sheep graze on a high plateau.
words.ex_cn: 羊群在高高原上吃草。
words.en: A plateau is a large area of high and fairly flat land. It can also refer to a period during which there are no large changes.

words.tr: adj. 摇摇欲坠的；破烂不堪的
words.ex: The old house was ramshackle and needed repair.
words.ex_cn: 那栋老房子摇摇欲坠，需要修理。
words.en: A ramshackle building or vehicle is in very bad condition and in danger of falling down.

words.ex: He is steadfast in his beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己信念坚定不移。
words.en: If someone is steadfast, they are very loyal and constant in their attitudes or actions.

words.ex: The body maintains homeostasis to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 身体保持稳态以保持健康。
words.en: The ability or tendency of an organism or cell to maintain internal equilibrium by adjusting its physiological processes.

words.ex: She maintained an unfaltering gaze throughout the presentation.
words.ex_cn: 她在整个演讲过程中始终保持坚定的目光。
words.en: If you describe someone's attitude or behaviour as unfaltering, you mean that it is strong and firm and does not weaken.

words.tr: adj. 不可改变的；永恒不变的
words.ex: The password is immutable and cannot be changed.
words.ex_cn: 密码是不可更改的。
words.en: If you say that something is immutable, you mean that it cannot be changed at all.

words.ex: The injured man was immobile after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，这名受伤的人无法移动。
words.en: If something is immobile, it is not moving or cannot move.

words.ex: The law gives antecedence to the oldest claim.
words.ex_cn: 法律给予最古老的主张优先权。
words.en: The fact or condition of being antecedent; precedence in time or order.

words.ex: He antedated the contract by one week.
words.ex_cn: 他把合同的日期提前了一周。
words.en: To be of an earlier date than something else; to precede in time.

words.tr: adj. 前面的；前部的；较早的
words.ex: The anterior part of the brain controls movement.
words.ex_cn: 大脑的前部控制运动。
words.en: Located before or at the front of something.

words.tr: adj. 迟来的；来得太迟的
words.ex: She sent a belated birthday card to her friend.
words.ex_cn: 她给朋友寄了一张迟到的生日卡片。
words.en: If you describe something as belated, you mean that it is late or delayed.

words.ex: The continuation of the project depends on funding.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目的继续取决于资金。
words.en: The act of continuing something or the state of being continued.

words.tr: v. 接着发生；因而产生
words.ex: The storm ended, and peace ensued.
words.ex_cn: 风暴结束后，和平随之而来。
words.en: If something ensues, it happens immediately after another event, usually as a result of it.

words.ex: Heretofore, he did not understand the problem.
words.ex_cn: 到目前为止，他不明白这个问题。
words.en: Up to this time; until now.

words.ex: He visited his natal village for the first time.
words.ex_cn: 他第一次回到了自己的出生村庄。
words.en: Relating to the place or time of one's birth

words.ex: The book is overdue at the library.
words.ex_cn: 这本书在图书馆逾期了。
words.en: If you say that a change or an event is overdue, you mean that you think it should have happened before now.

words.tr: adj. 最重要的； v. “override”的现在分词；
words.ex: The overriding goal is to keep everyone safe.
words.ex_cn: 最重要的目标是确保每个人的安全。
words.en: An overriding issue or feeling is more important than any other.

words.ex: The penultimate chapter is the second to last.
words.ex_cn: 倒数第二章是倒数第二。
words.en: Penultimate is used to describe something that is second to the last in a series.

words.tr: adj. （时间、次序）较后的；后面的；背面的；
words.ex: The posterior chapter explains the final result.
words.ex_cn: 后面的章节解释了最终结果。
words.en: Located behind a part or toward the rear of something.

words.ex: The rain precedes the storm.
words.ex_cn: 雨先于风暴来临。
words.en: If one event or period of time precedes another, it happens before it.

words.ex: He read the previous chapter last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚读了前一章。
words.en: Existing or occurring before in time or order.

words.tr: adj. 首要的；主要的；基本的；最好的；
words.ex: This is the prime reason for the delay.
words.ex_cn: 这是延误的首要原因。
words.en: Prime is used to describe something that is of the best possible quality, or the most important or basic part of something.

words.tr: n. 需优先考虑的事；优先权；
words.ex: Homework is my top priority.
words.ex_cn: 作业是我最需要优先考虑的事。
words.en: If something is a priority, it is the most important thing you have to do or deal with, or must be done or dealt with before everything else you have to do.

words.tr:
n. 长队；
v. 排队；
words.ex: There is a long queue at the ticket counter.
words.ex_cn: 售票处排着一条长队。
words.en: A queue is a line of people or vehicles waiting for something.

words.ex: The steps must be followed in sequential order.
words.ex_cn: 这些步骤必须按顺序进行。
words.en: Sequential means relating to or following in a sequence.

words.ex: The two events happened simultaneously.
words.ex_cn: 这两个事件同时发生了。
words.en: Happening, existing, or done at the same time.

words.ex: He failed the test, but subsequent efforts helped him pass.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格，但随后的努力让他通过了。
words.en: Following in time or order; succeeding.

words.tr: adj. 同时发生的；同步的；
words.ex: The two events happened synchronous.
words.ex_cn: 这两个事件同时发生。
words.en: Happening or existing at the same time.

words.tr: adj. 最终的；最后的；极端的；
words.ex: This is the ultimate solution to the problem.
words.ex_cn: 这是这个问题的最终解决方案。
words.en: You use ultimate to describe the final result or aim of a long series of events.

words.tr: adj. 不合时宜的；过早发生的
words.ex: His untimely death shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他突如其来的去世让所有人都感到震惊。
words.en: If you describe an event as untimely, you mean that it happened earlier than it should, or sooner than you expected.

words.ex: The foreword explains why the book was written.
words.ex_cn: 序言解释了这本书为何被撰写。
words.en: A foreword is a short introduction at the beginning of a book, usually written by someone other than the author.

words.ex: With hindsight, I should have saved more money.
words.ex_cn: 事后看来，我本该多存些钱。
words.en: The understanding of a situation or event only after it has happened or developed.

words.tr: n. 事先形成的看法；先入之见；成见
words.ex: He had a preconception that all teachers are strict.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个先入为主的观念，认为所有老师都很严格。
words.en: An idea or opinion that is formed before you have enough information or experience, or a bias that prevents objective consideration of an issue.

words.ex: The bus stops at the terminal at 9 PM.
words.ex_cn: 公交车晚上9点到达终点站。
words.en: A terminal is a place where vehicles, passengers, or goods begin or end a journey. It can also refer to a computer device at which a user enters data or commands.

words.ex: The storm anteceded the flood.
words.ex_cn: 风暴发生在洪水之前。
words.en: To go before in time or order; precede.

words.tr: n. 前情；先行词；祖先；经历；“antecedent”的复数
words.ex: The antecedents of the conflict go back to last year.
words.ex_cn: 这场冲突的前情可以追溯到去年。
words.en: An antecedent is a thing or event that existed before or logically precedes another.

words.ex: Is this your book?
words.ex_cn: 这是你的书吗？
words.en: Belonging to or associated with the person or people that the speaker is addressing.

words.ex: The company got a lot of publicity from the TV ad.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司从电视广告中获得了大量宣传。
words.en: Publicity is the activity of making sure that someone or something attracts a lot of interest or attention from the public, especially by providing information about them in newspapers, on television, etc.

words.ex: The celebrity smiled at the fans outside the theater.
words.ex_cn: 这位名人向剧院外的粉丝微笑。
words.en: A celebrity is a famous person, especially in entertainment or sports.

words.tr: adj. 引人注意的； v. “arrest”的现在分词；
words.ex: She wore an arresting red dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件引人注目的红色连衣裙去参加派对。
words.en: If something is arresting, it is very attractive or striking in a way that draws your attention.

words.tr: adj. 著名的； v. 庆祝；“celebrate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is a celebrated painter in China.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位在中国著名的画家。
words.en: A celebrated person or thing is famous and much admired.

words.ex: The red hat was conspicuous in the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 那顶红帽子在人群中非常显眼。
words.en: Something that is conspicuous is very obvious or easy to notice.

words.ex: The dignitary gave a speech at the ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 这位显要人物在仪式上发表了演讲。
words.en: A dignitary is a person who has an important position in a society or an organization.

words.tr:
n. 不信任；名誉丧失；信誉丧失
v. 不信；败坏名声；使丢脸
words.ex: His lies brought discredit to the company.
words.ex_cn: 他的谎言使公司失去了信任。
words.en: To discredit someone or something means to cause them to lose people's respect or trust.

words.ex: The scandal brought the company into disrepute.
words.ex_cn: 这起丑闻使该公司声名狼藉。
words.en: If someone or something is in disrepute, they have a bad reputation because people think they have done something bad or wrong.

words.ex: This painting has a distinctive style.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画有独特的风格。
words.en: Something that is distinctive has a special quality or feature which makes it easily recognizable and different from other things of the same type.

words.tr: v. 区分；“distinguish”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 卓越的；著名的；
words.ex: He distinguished the fake coin from the real one.
words.ex_cn: 他把假硬币和真硬币区分开来。
words.en: If you describe a person or their work as distinguished, you mean that they have been very successful in their career and have a good reputation.

words.ex: He is a man of great eminence in science.
words.ex_cn: 他在科学界享有很高的声望。
words.en: Eminence refers to a position of great distinction or superiority, especially in a particular field or profession.

words.ex: He is an eminent scientist who won the Nobel Prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位获得诺贝尔奖的杰出科学家。
words.en: An eminent person is well-known and respected, especially because they are good at their profession.

words.ex: He lost his car because of forfeiture.
words.ex_cn: 他因为没收而失去了他的车。
words.en: The act of losing or giving up something as a penalty for wrongdoing.

words.ex: He is an illustrious scientist who won many awards.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位杰出的科学家，获得过许多奖项。
words.en: If you describe someone as illustrious, you mean that they are very well known because they have a high position in society or they have done something impressive.

words.ex: He accepted a nominal fee for the service.
words.ex_cn: 他为这项服务收取了微不足道的费用。
words.en: If you say that something is nominal, you mean that it is very small in comparison to the real value or importance of something.

words.ex: His notability comes from winning the science prize.
words.ex_cn: 他的知名度来自赢得科学奖。
words.en: The quality of being worthy of attention or notice; prominence.

words.ex: Her performance was phenomenal.
words.ex_cn: 她的表现非常非凡。
words.en: If you describe something as phenomenal, you think it is extremely good or impressive.

words.tr: adj. 杰出的；卓越的；出类拔萃的
words.ex: He is a pre-eminent scientist in his field.
words.ex_cn: 他是该领域最杰出的科学家。
words.en: If someone or something is pre-eminent in a group, they are more important, powerful, or capable than other people or things in the group.

words.ex: The university has great prestige for its research.
words.ex_cn: 这所大学因其研究而享有很高的声望。
words.en: The widespread respect and admiration felt for someone or something on the basis of a perception of their achievements or quality.

words.tr: adj. 享有声望的；声望很高的；
words.ex: He got into a prestigious university.
words.ex_cn: 他进入了一所享有声望的大学。
words.en: A prestigious institution, job, or activity is respected and admired because it is considered to be of very high quality.

words.tr: adj. 突出的；杰出的；显著的；
words.ex: He is a prominent scientist in the field of medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他是医学领域的一位突出的科学家。
words.en: Someone or something that is prominent is important and well-known, or is positioned in a way that makes them easily seen or noticed.

words.tr: adv. 如谚语所说；众所周知地
words.ex: He is proverbially late for meetings.
words.ex_cn: 他开会总是习惯性地迟到。
words.en: In a manner that is well known or typical, as if it were a proverb or a well-known saying.

words.ex: He is a scientist of great renown.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位享有盛誉的科学家。
words.en: Renown is the state of being known and talked about by many people because of your achievements, qualities, or actions.

words.ex: He has a good reputation for honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他以诚实著称。
words.en: The opinion that people have about someone or something because of what has happened in the past.

words.tr:
n. 名声；名誉；名望
v. 认为；以为
words.ex: He is of good repute in his town.
words.ex_cn: 他在镇上声誉很好。
words.en: The opinion generally held of someone or something; the state of being regarded in a particular way.

words.ex: The salient point in the report is the cost increase.
words.ex_cn: 报告中最显著的要点是成本上升。
words.en: The most noticeable or important.

words.tr:
n. 信号；
v. 用信号通知；
words.ex: The traffic light is a signal to stop.
words.ex_cn: 交通灯是一个停止的信号。
words.en: A signal is a gesture, sound, or action which is intended to give a particular message to the person who sees or hears it.

words.tr: v. 告诉；讲述；“tell”的现在分词； adj. 有力的；反映情况的；
words.ex: He told me the news.
words.ex_cn: 他告诉了我这个消息。
words.en: If something is telling, it shows the true nature of a situation or someone's feelings or character in a very clear way.

words.tr: adj. 名义上的；有名无实的
words.ex: He is the titular head of the company.
words.ex_cn: 他是该公司的名义上的负责人。
words.en: Holding or constituting a purely formal position or title without any real authority.

words.tr: adj. 超越的；杰出的；卓越的
words.ex: The beauty of the sunset was transcendent.
words.ex_cn: 日落的美是超凡的。
words.en: If you describe something as transcendent, you mean that it is extremely good or impressive, often in a way that goes beyond the ordinary.

words.tr: adj. 不被注意的；被忽视的；
words.ex: The unnoticed crack in the wall grew bigger.
words.ex_cn: 墙上的那条不被注意的裂缝变大了。
words.en: If something happens or passes unnoticed, it is not seen or observed by anyone.

words.ex: The door handle was unobtrusive and blended with the wall.
words.ex_cn: 门把手不显眼，与墙壁融为一体。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as unobtrusive, you mean that they are not easily noticed or do not draw attention to themselves.

words.tr: adj. 有声望的；声誉好的
words.ex: He works for a reputable company.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家信誉良好的公司工作。
words.en: A reputable person or organization is considered to be good and trustworthy by most people.

words.tr:
adj. 据说的；号称的；有名气的
v. 认为；以为；“repute”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He is a reputed doctor in this city.
words.ex_cn: 他是这座城市里有名的医生。
words.en: Generally believed to be a particular thing, although this might not be true.

words.tr: adj. 应受尊敬的；牧师的
words.ex: The reverend priest gave a kind speech.
words.ex_cn: 这位应受尊敬的牧师发表了一番善意的讲话。
words.en: A title of respect for a clergyman.

words.tr: n. 文雅；出身高贵；有风度
words.ex: His gentility made everyone feel welcome.
words.ex_cn: 他的优雅使每个人都感到受欢迎。
words.en: Gentility refers to the quality of being genteel, which involves showing the characteristics of polite society, such as refinement, grace, and good manners.

words.ex: The criminal gained infamy for his violent crimes.
words.ex_cn: 这个罪犯因暴力犯罪而声名狼藉。
words.en: The state of being well known for some bad quality or deed.

words.ex: It was an auspicious day for their wedding.
words.ex_cn: 那天是他们婚礼的吉日。
words.en: If you describe something as auspicious, you mean that it is a sign of future success.

words.ex: He felt delectation while eating the sweet cake.
words.ex_cn: 他吃甜蛋糕时感到愉悦。
words.en: Delectation is a feeling of great pleasure and enjoyment.

words.ex: He passed the test by a fluke.
words.ex_cn: 他靠运气通过了考试。
words.en: A fluke is an unexpected stroke of good luck or a surprising success that happens by chance.

words.ex: It was fortuitous that he found his keys just before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他在出发前刚好找到钥匙，真是幸运。
words.en: If you describe something as fortuitous, you mean that it happens by chance rather than by anyone's planning or intention.

words.tr: adj. 有利的；吉祥的；吉利的
words.ex: The weather was propitious for a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 天气非常适合野餐。
words.en: If something is propitious, it is likely to lead to success, or it indicates a good chance of success.

words.ex: The country enjoys prosperity after years of peace.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家在多年的和平后迎来了繁荣。
words.en: Prosperity is a condition in which a person, community, or country is thriving and successful, especially in financial terms.

words.tr: adj. 机缘巧合的；及时的；凑巧的
words.ex: It was providential that he found the lost key.
words.ex_cn: 他找到丢失的钥匙真是幸运。
words.en: If you describe something as providential, you mean that it happens at exactly the right time, often by chance, and often in a way that is very fortunate.

words.ex: The monk recited the Beatitudes during the service.
words.ex_cn: 修道士在仪式中背诵了至福经。
words.en: Supreme blessedness or happiness.

words.ex: She felt great felicity when she won the prize.
words.ex_cn: 当她赢得奖品时，她感到极大的幸福。
words.en: Felicity is great happiness and pleasure.

words.tr:
adj. 浅黄色的；黄皮革制的
n. 浅黄色；浅黄色皮革；爱好者
v. 用软布擦亮
words.ex: The buff walls looked warm in the sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 浅黄色的墙壁在阳光下显得温暖。
words.en: A buff is a person who is very interested in and knowledgeable about a particular subject.

words.ex: The colors of the painting fade in the sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画的颜色在阳光下逐渐消失。
words.en: To gradually grow faint and disappear.

words.tr: adj. 消色差的；无彩色的
words.ex: The painting is achromatic, using only black and white.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是无色的，只用了黑色和白色。
words.en: Designed to transmit light without separating it into colors, correcting for color distortion in lenses.

words.tr:
n. 雪花石膏
adj. 白净的
words.ex: The statue is made of alabaster.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像由雪花石膏制成。
words.en: Alabaster is a type of fine-grained, translucent gypsum or calcite, typically white, used for carving or as a building material.

words.tr:
adj. 天蓝色的；蔚蓝色的
n. 天蓝色
words.ex: The sky is azure today.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天空是蔚蓝色的。
words.en: Azure is used to describe things that are bright blue in color.

words.tr: v. 使变白；（脸色）变苍白；焯
words.ex: She blanches the vegetables before freezing them.
words.ex_cn: 她在冷冻蔬菜之前先焯水。
words.en: To blanch means to make something white or pale, often by removing color or by causing it to lose color. It can also refer to the process of briefly boiling vegetables and then plunging them into cold water to halt the cooking process.

words.ex: She added bleach to the white shirt to make it brighter.
words.ex_cn: 她往白衬衫里加了漂白剂，让它更亮。
words.en: To bleach something means to make it white or pale by using a chemical or by exposing it to sunlight.

words.tr: adj. 玫瑰色的；红润的（皮肤）；美好的；有希望的（前途等）
words.ex: The sky turned rosy at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 日出时，天空变成了玫瑰色。
words.en: If you describe a situation as rosy, you mean that it seems to be full of hope and promise.

words.tr:
n. 对照；反差；对立；
v. 对比；和...形成对照；
words.ex: The contrast between light and dark is clear in the photo.
words.ex_cn: 这张照片中明暗的对照很明显。
words.en: A contrast is a great difference between two or more things which is clear when you compare them.

words.ex: He likens his job to a puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的工作比作一个拼图。
words.en: To liken something to something else is to say that they are similar in some way.

words.ex: His eccentricity makes him unique.
words.ex_cn: 他的古怪使他与众不同。
words.en: The quality of being eccentric; behaviour that is unusual, peculiar, or odd.

words.tr: n. 恶作剧；（危险而愚蠢的）冒险行为
words.ex: His funny escapade made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他那滑稽的淘气行为让大家都笑了。
words.en: An escapade is an exciting and somewhat dangerous adventure, especially one that is not very sensible or is against the rules.

words.tr:
v. 想要；
adj. 花哨的；昂贵的；
n. 爱好；
words.ex: I fancy a cup of tea.
words.ex_cn: 我想要一杯茶。
words.en: If you describe something as fancy, you mean that it is special, unusual, or elaborate, often because it has a lot of decoration or is very expensive.

words.ex: The two cultures are disparate in their traditions.
words.ex_cn: 这两种文化在传统上完全不同。
words.en: Things that are disparate are clearly different from each other in quality or type.

words.ex: There is a disparity in pay between men and women.
words.ex_cn: 男女之间的工资存在差异。
words.en: A disparity between two or more things is a noticeable difference between them.

words.tr: n. 区别；区分；优等评分；
words.ex: There is a clear distinction between right and wrong.
words.ex_cn: 对与错之间有明显的区别。
words.en: A distinction is a difference or contrast between similar things or people.

words.tr: adj. 不同的；多种多样的；
words.ex: The class has diverse students from many countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级有来自许多国家的不同学生。
words.en: If a group or range of things is diverse, it is made up of a wide variety of things.

words.ex: He joined a fraternity at university.
words.ex_cn: 他在大学加入了兄弟会。
words.en: Fraternity refers to a group of people sharing a common profession or interests, or a feeling of friendship and mutual support within a group.

words.tr: adj. 异种的；异质的；由不同成份形成的
words.ex: The class is heterogeneous, with students from many countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级是多元的，有来自许多国家的学生。
words.en: A heterogeneous group consists of many different types of things or people.

words.ex: The homogeneity of the sample made the test results reliable.
words.ex_cn: 样本的同种性使测试结果可靠。
words.en: The quality or state of being all the same or all of the same kind.

words.ex: The mixture is homogeneous and looks the same throughout.
words.ex_cn: 这种混合物是均一的，看起来处处都一样。
words.en: Something that is homogeneous is uniform in nature or character throughout.

words.tr:
n. 亲属；血缘关系
adj. 同源的；类似的
words.ex: He visited his kindred during the holiday.
words.ex_cn: 他在假期里探望了他的亲属。
words.en: If two people or things are kindred, they are similar in some way, often because they are related.

words.tr: adj. 多种的；各式各样的
words.ex: She has multifarious hobbies, like painting, singing, and gardening.
words.ex_cn: 她有很多不同的爱好，比如绘画、唱歌和园艺。
words.en: If you describe things as multifarious, you mean that they are many and of various types.

words.ex: The store offers multiple flavors of ice cream.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店提供多种口味的冰淇淋。
words.en: If something is multiple, it consists of or involves many things of the same kind.

words.tr: n. 大数目；多种多样；繁多
words.ex: There is a multiplicity of stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中有大量星星。
words.en: A multiplicity of things or people means a large number or great variety of them.

words.tr: adj. 各种各样的；杂七杂八的
words.ex: He bought sundry items at the store.
words.ex_cn: 他在商店买了各种物品。
words.en: If someone refers to sundry people or things, they are referring to several people or things that are all different from each other.

words.tr: v. 使成杂色；使多样化
words.ex: The artist variegate the wall with colorful paints.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家用彩色油漆使墙壁变得五彩斑斓。
words.en: To make something more diverse or varied in appearance by adding different colors or elements.

words.tr: adj. 无益于健康的；对身体有害的
words.ex: The air in the old factory was unsalubrious.
words.ex_cn: 旧工厂里的空气不健康。
words.en: Unsalubrious is used to describe conditions or places that are detrimental to health or well-being.

words.tr: adj. 调皮的；恶作剧的；有害的
words.ex: The mischievous boy laughed and hid his sister's shoes.
words.ex_cn: 那个顽皮的男孩笑着藏起了他姐姐的鞋子。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behaviour as mischievous, you mean that they enjoy playing tricks on people or doing things to annoy or embarrass them.

words.tr: n. 祸根；致命伤；烦扰之源；
words.ex: Smoking is the bane of his health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟是他健康的祸根。
words.en: Something that causes misery or death.

words.ex: His efforts were bootless.
words.ex_cn: 他的努力是徒劳的。
words.en: If you describe something as bootless, you mean that it is useless or does not achieve anything.

words.ex: He will deactivate his account tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会停用他的账户。
words.en: If you deactivate something, you cause it to stop working or to stop being active.

words.ex: He saw the futility of trying to fix it himself.
words.ex_cn: 他看到了自己试图修理它的无用。
words.en: The quality of being futile or ineffective.

words.tr: adj. 无能的；不起作用的
words.ex: His attempts to solve the problem were ineffectual.
words.ex_cn: 他试图解决问题的尝试是无效的。
words.en: If someone or something is ineffectual, they lack the ability or power to achieve something.

words.ex: The poison is lethal to humans.
words.ex_cn: 这种毒药对人类是致命的。
words.en: Something that is lethal can kill people or animals.

words.tr: adj. 产量少的；效果不佳的；没有收益的
words.ex: He had an unproductive day at work.
words.ex_cn: 他在工作中度过了毫无成效的一天。
words.en: If someone or something is unproductive, they do not produce very much or do not produce very good results.

words.ex: Smoking is injurious to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is injurious causes harm or damage.

words.tr: adj. 有害的；恶性的；致命的
words.ex: Smoking is a pernicious habit.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟是一种有害的习惯。
words.en: Having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way.

words.tr: adj. 致死的；瘟疫的；有害的
words.ex: The pestilent disease killed many people in the village.
words.ex_cn: 这种致死的疾病夺去了村里许多人的生命。
words.en: Something that is pestilent is likely to cause or spread a deadly disease, or is extremely harmful or unpleasant.

words.ex: The frog is poisonous.
words.ex_cn: 这只青蛙是有毒的。
words.en: Something that is poisonous will kill you or make you ill if you eat it, drink it, or absorb it.

words.ex: The water is toxic to fish.
words.ex_cn: 这种水对鱼是有毒的。
words.en: If a substance is toxic, it is poisonous.

words.ex: The snake released venom into its prey.
words.ex_cn: 蛇向猎物释放了毒液。
words.en: Venom is a poisonous substance secreted by animals such as snakes and spiders, used for defense or to kill prey.

words.ex: The virulent virus spread quickly through the town.
words.ex_cn: 这种剧毒的病毒迅速在小镇上传播。
words.en: A virulent disease or poison is extremely powerful and dangerous.

words.tr:
n. 权宜之计；应急办法
adj. 权宜的
words.ex: Closing the factory was an expedient to save money.
words.ex_cn: 关闭工厂是为了省钱的权宜之计。
words.en: An expedient action or solution to a problem is one that is convenient or practical, although it may not be morally right.

words.tr: adj. 权宜的；临时凑合的；
words.ex: He used a makeshift table made of boxes and a board.
words.ex_cn: 他用箱子和木板做了一个权宜的桌子。
words.en: A makeshift object or arrangement is one that is made or done quickly and without much skill, using whatever is available at the time.

words.ex: This temperature is the optimum for growing plants.
words.ex_cn: 这个温度是最适宜植物生长的。
words.en: The optimum is the best or most favorable condition, degree, amount, etc., for achieving a particular result.

words.tr: adj. 有益的；值得的； v. “reward”的现在分词；
words.ex: Volunteering is a rewarding experience.
words.ex_cn: 志愿服务是一种有益的经历。
words.en: Providing satisfaction or gratification; beneficial.

words.tr:
adj. 最佳的；最高级的；过度的
n. 最高级；最高程度
words.ex: This is the superlative movie I have ever seen.
words.ex_cn: 这是我见过的最棒的电影。
words.en: The superlative form of an adjective or adverb is the form that indicates that something has more of a quality than anything else in a particular group.

words.ex: The system will validate your password.
words.ex_cn: 系统将验证你的密码。
words.en: To validate something such as a claim or statement means to prove or confirm that it is true or correct.

words.ex: The salubrity of the air in the mountains helps people feel better.
words.ex_cn: 山区空气的有益健康特性让人感觉更好。
words.en: The quality of being beneficial to health; healthiness.

words.ex: The authenticity of the ancient painting was confirmed by experts.
words.ex_cn: 这幅古画的真实性得到了专家的确认。
words.en: The quality of being genuine or not corrupted from the original.

words.tr: adj. 根据事实的；真实的；
words.ex: His report is factual and accurate.
words.ex_cn: 他的报告是基于事实且准确的。
words.en: If something is factual, it is based on facts or concerns facts.

words.tr:
adj. 特指的；特殊的；挑剔的；
n. 细节；详情；
words.ex: He wants a particular book, not any other.
words.ex_cn: 他想要一本特指的书，不是别的。
words.en: You use particular to emphasize that you are talking about one thing or one kind of thing rather than other similar ones.

words.ex: He wrote a reportorial piece about the local election.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一篇关于当地选举的报道文章。
words.en: Relating to or characteristic of a reporter or the reporting of news.

words.tr: n. 自明之理；不言而喻的道理；老生常谈
words.ex: It is a truism that water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.
words.ex_cn: 水在100摄氏度沸腾，这是一个不言而喻的事实。
words.en: A truism is a statement that is obviously true and says nothing new or interesting.

words.ex: He remained unaffected by the noise.
words.ex_cn: 他没有受到噪音的影响。
words.en: If someone or something is unaffected by an event or occurrence, they are not changed by it in any way.

words.tr: adj. 貌似真实的; 可能的
words.ex: The story she told sounded verisimilar, but we later found out it was fabricated.
words.ex_cn: 她讲述的故事听起来很真实，但我们后来发现它是捏造的。
words.en: Having the appearance of truth; probable or likely.

words.tr: adj. 真实的；确实的；真正的
words.ex: It was a veritable treasure trove of old books.
words.ex_cn: 那是一个真正的旧书宝库。
words.en: You use veritable to emphasize the size, amount, or nature of something.

words.tr: adj. 未受（或不容）侵犯的；未受（或不容）亵渎的
words.ex: The sacred site remains inviolate.
words.ex_cn: 这个神圣的遗址仍然不受侵犯。
words.en: If something is inviolate, it has not been or cannot be disturbed, harmed, or profaned.

words.tr: adj. 整洁时髦的；设计精妙的
words.ex: He wears a natty suit to work every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天穿一件时髦的西装去上班。
words.en: If you describe someone as natty, you mean that their clothes are smart and fashionable.

words.tr: adj. 首要的；主要的；基本的；最好的；
words.ex: This is the prime reason for the delay.
words.ex_cn: 这是延误的首要原因。
words.en: Prime is used to describe something that is of the best possible quality, or the most important or basic part of something.

words.tr: adj. 清洁的；无瑕疵的；无过失的
words.ex: The kitchen was immaculate after she cleaned it.
words.ex_cn: 她打扫后，厨房非常干净。
words.en: If you describe something as immaculate, you mean that it is extremely clean, tidy, or neat.

words.ex: The child's innocence showed in his honest smile.
words.ex_cn: 孩子的无罪体现在他诚实的微笑中。
words.en: the state or quality of being innocent, especially freedom from sin, moral wrong, or guilt through lack of knowledge of evil

words.ex: The kitchen must be sanitary to prevent illness.
words.ex_cn: 厨房必须保持清洁以防止疾病。
words.en: relating to the conditions that affect hygiene and health, especially the supply of sewage facilities and clean drinking water

words.tr: adj. 整洁的；井然有序的
words.ex: He keeps his room shipshape.
words.ex_cn: 他把房间收拾得整整齐齐。
words.en: If something is shipshape, it is neat and tidy and everything is in its correct place.

words.ex: Her room is always tidy.
words.ex_cn: 她的房间总是很整洁。
words.en: If you describe something as tidy, you mean that it is neat and arranged in an orderly way.

words.ex: He always keeps his garden trim and neat.
words.ex_cn: 他总是把花园打理得整洁有序。
words.en: To trim something means to make it tidier or more level by cutting a small amount off it.

words.tr: adj. 被小心照料的；整齐干净的；梳洗得整洁的
words.ex: He is a well-groomed man with neat hair and clean clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他是个仪表整洁的男人，头发整齐，衣服干净。
words.en: If you describe someone as well-groomed, you mean that they are smart and neat in appearance.

words.ex: The book is a compilation of his best essays.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是他最佳文章的汇编物。
words.en: A compilation is a collection of different items, such as songs, pieces of writing, or data, that have been gathered together in one place or for one purpose.

words.ex: The editor checked the collation of the manuscript.
words.ex_cn: 编辑检查了手稿的校对。
words.en: Collation refers to the process of assembling written information into a standard order or form, or a light meal.

words.ex: The indispensability of water for life is clear.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命不可或缺是显而易见的。
words.en: The quality of being absolutely necessary or essential.

words.tr: adj. 重大的；命中注定的；决定命运的；预言性的
words.ex: It was a fateful day when he met her.
words.ex_cn: 那是他遇见她的命运般的一天。
words.en: If you describe an event or action as fateful, you mean that it has very important and often bad effects on the future.

words.tr: n. 冲击；主力；首当其冲
words.ex: The farmers bore the brunt of the drought.
words.ex_cn: 农民们承受了干旱的主要打击。
words.en: The main force or impact of something, especially something unpleasant.

words.ex: Lying has serious consequences.
words.ex_cn: 撒谎会有严重的后果。
words.en: A consequence is a result or effect of an action or condition.

words.tr: adj. 至关重要的；决定性的；
words.ex: It is crucial to drink water every day.
words.ex_cn: 每天喝水至关重要。
words.en: If you describe something as crucial, you mean it is extremely important.

words.tr: n. 关键点；最难点；症结
words.ex: The crux of the problem is money.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题的关键是钱。
words.en: The most important or difficult part of a problem or issue.

words.tr: adj. 震撼全球的；极为重大的；翻天覆地的
words.ex: The news was earthshaking for everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个消息让每个人都震惊不已。
words.en: of very great importance or significance; momentous

words.ex: He is learning elementary math at school.
words.ex_cn: 他在学校学习初级数学。
words.en: Elementary means relating to the simplest and most basic aspects of a subject.

words.ex: The elite of the city often meet at private clubs.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市的精英经常在私人俱乐部会面。
words.en: You can refer to the most powerful, rich, or talented people within a particular group, place, or society as the elite.

words.tr: adj. 必需的；基本的；本质的；
words.ex: Water is essential for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命是必需的。
words.en: Something that is essential is extremely important or absolutely necessary to a particular subject, situation, or activity.

words.tr: adj. 深远的；影响深远的
words.ex: The decision had far-reaching effects on the town.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定对这个城镇产生了深远的影响。
words.en: If you describe actions, events, or changes as far-reaching, you mean that they have a very great influence and affect a great number of things.

words.ex: The accident was fatal.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故是致命的。
words.en: If an action or event is fatal, it causes someone's death.

words.tr: adj. 基本的；基础的；根本的；
words.ex: Water is a fundamental need for life.
words.ex_cn: 水是生命的基本需求。
words.en: You use fundamental to describe things, activities, and principles that are very important or essential. They affect the basic nature of other things or are the most important element upon which other things depend.

words.ex: The door opens on a metal hinge.
words.ex_cn: 这扇门装在一个金属枢纽上。
words.en: A hinge is a piece of metal, wood, or plastic that is used to join two things together so that one of them can swing or move freely.

words.tr:
adj. 无法精确估量的
n. 无法估量的事物
words.ex: The reason for his silence is imponderable.
words.ex_cn: 他沉默的原因无法衡量。
words.en: An imponderable factor or element is one that cannot be precisely measured or assessed.

words.tr:
n. 进口；重要性；
v. 进口；
words.ex: The country increased its import of oil last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年这个国家增加了石油的进口。
words.en: To bring in (goods or services) from a foreign country for sale or use.

words.tr: n. 骨髓；精华；活力；西葫芦
words.ex: The bone marrow makes blood cells.
words.ex_cn: 骨髓制造血细胞。
words.en: The soft fatty substance in the cavities of bones, in which blood cells are produced; the essence or most vital part of something.

words.ex: The momentous decision changed his life.
words.ex_cn: 这个重要的决定改变了他的一生。
words.en: If you refer to a decision, event, or change as momentous, you mean that it is very important, often because of the effects that it will have in the future.

words.tr: adj. 最高的；至上的；最重要的；
words.ex: His safety is paramount.
words.ex_cn: 他的安全是最重要的。
words.en: Something that is paramount or of paramount importance is more important than anything else.

words.tr:
adj. 主要的；最重要的；
n. 校长；负责人；
words.ex: The principal reason for his success is hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他成功的主要原因是努力工作。
words.en: The person with the highest authority or most important position in an organization, institution, or group.

words.ex: The red light signifies stop.
words.ex_cn: 红灯表示停止。
words.en: If an event, a sign, or a symbol signifies something, it is a sign of that thing or represents that thing.

words.tr:
adj. 主要的；重要的；
n. 主要产品；主要部分；主食；
words.ex: Rice is a staple food in many Asian countries.
words.ex_cn: 大米是许多亚洲国家的主要食物。
words.en: A staple is a basic food that is eaten regularly and in such quantities that it constitutes a dominant portion of a standard diet for a given people, supplying a large fraction of energy needs and generally forming a significant proportion of the intake of other nutrients as well.

words.ex: Water is a common substance.
words.ex_cn: 水是一种常见的物质。
words.en: A substance is a particular kind of matter with uniform properties.

words.tr: adj. 本质上的；实质性的；
words.ex: The change was substantive, not just cosmetic.
words.ex_cn: 这个改变是本质上的，而不仅仅是表面上的。
words.en: Something that is substantive is significant, meaningful, or important in a way that is not just superficial or formal.

words.tr: n. 底层；下层土壤地基
words.ex: The rock layer is the substratum of the soil.
words.ex_cn: 岩石层是土壤的基底。
words.en: A substratum is an underlying layer or substance, especially one that forms a foundation or basis.

words.ex: The movie has a thematic focus on friendship.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的主题聚焦于友谊。
words.en: Relating to or constituting a theme or themes.

words.ex: The storm caused unprecedented damage.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴造成了前所未有的破坏。
words.en: If something is unprecedented, it has never happened before.

words.ex: The scientist made a breakthrough in cancer research.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家在癌症研究中取得了突破。
words.en: A breakthrough is a significant development or achievement that helps to solve a problem or improve a situation.

words.ex: This decision is pivotal for the company's future.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定对公司未来至关重要。
words.en: Of crucial importance in relation to the development or success of something else.

words.tr: v. 强加；“impose”的现在分词； adj. 壮观的；
words.ex: He imposed his rules on the team.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的规则强加给团队。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as imposing, you mean that they have an impressive appearance or manner.

words.ex: The sunset over the mountains was magnificent.
words.ex_cn: 山上的日落壮丽极了。
words.en: If you say that something or someone is magnificent, you mean that you think they are extremely good, beautiful, or impressive.

words.ex: The refulgent sun illuminated the entire room.
words.ex_cn: 灿烂的阳光照亮了整个房间。
words.en: Shining brightly; radiant.

words.ex: The queen was resplendent in her golden crown.
words.ex_cn: 女王戴着金色王冠，光彩夺目。
words.en: Something that is resplendent is very bright and attractive, often because it is richly decorated or very colorful.

words.ex: The splendor of the sunset amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 日落的壮丽让每个人都惊叹。
words.en: Splendor is the great beauty or impressive appearance of something.

words.ex: The old edifice stands near the river.
words.ex_cn: 那座古老的建筑坐落在河边。
words.en: An edifice is a large, impressive building.

words.ex: The grandeur of the palace amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 宫殿的宏伟让每个人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The quality of being grand or splendid in appearance or style.

words.tr: adj. 宏伟的；壮丽的；威严的；
words.ex: The majestic mountain stood above the clouds.
words.ex_cn: 那座宏伟的山峰耸立在云层之上。
words.en: If you describe something as majestic, you mean that it has a quality of greatness and impressiveness that often inspires admiration or awe.

words.tr: n. 露天历史剧；盛装游行（或庆典）；选美比赛
words.ex: The town held a pageant to show the history of the old kingdom.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇举办了一场露天历史剧，以展示古老王国的历史。
words.en: A pageant is a public entertainment consisting of a procession of people in elaborate, colorful costumes, or an outdoor performance of a historical scene.

words.tr: adj. 宫殿般的；宏伟的；富丽堂皇的
words.ex: He lives in a palatial house near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他住在湖边一座宏伟的房子里。
words.en: If you describe a building or a place as palatial, you mean that it is very large, impressive, or luxurious, like a palace.

words.ex: The parade had lots of pageantry with colorful costumes and flags.
words.ex_cn: 游行中有许多华丽的场面，有色彩鲜艳的服装和旗帜。
words.en: Pageantry refers to the elaborate display or ceremony, often involving a procession or parade, that is designed to impress or entertain. It is typically associated with grand public events, celebrations, or competitions that are characterized by their spectacle and showmanship.

words.ex: The king walked with pomp in the parade.
words.ex_cn: 国王在游行中以隆重的气势行走。
words.en: Pomp is the use of a lot of ceremony, fine clothes, and decorations, especially on a public or official occasion.

chapters.name: Word List 26 人及品质 抽象行为

words.tr: v. 表现；举止；一致；相称
words.ex: He comports himself with kindness.
words.ex_cn: 他以友善的方式表现自己。
words.en: If you comport yourself in a particular way, you behave in that way.

words.tr:
v. 实施；传导（电、热）；
n. 行为；举止；
words.ex: The company will conduct a survey next week.
words.ex_cn: 公司将在下周进行一项调查。
words.en: To organize and carry out a particular activity.

words.ex: His calm demeanour surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他冷静的举止让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: Demeanour refers to the way in which a person behaves towards others; their outward behaviour or bearing.

words.ex: He works in the sales department.
words.ex_cn: 他在销售部工作。
words.en: A department is one of the sections in an organization such as a government, business, or university.

words.tr:
pron. 我的（东西）；
n. 矿；
v. 采矿；
words.ex: This book is mine.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是我的。
words.en: Used to refer to a thing or things belonging to or associated with the speaker. A place where minerals are extracted from the earth. To extract minerals from the earth.

words.ex: He sat with good posture at the desk.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在书桌前，姿势端正。
words.en: Your posture is the way in which you hold your body when you are standing or sitting.

words.tr: v.  合理化； 使合理
words.ex: He tries to rationalize his bad choices.
words.ex_cn: 他试图为自己的错误选择找借口。
words.en: To rationalize something means to try to find reasons to explain or justify it, often when these reasons are not really good ones.

chapters.name: Word List 26 人及品质 高贵

words.ex: He was born in August.
words.ex_cn: 他出生在八月。
words.en: August is the eighth month of the Gregorian calendar, following July and preceding September.

words.tr:
n. 中产阶级的人；资产阶级的人
adj. 中产阶级的；追求名利的；资产阶级的
words.ex: He lives a bourgeois life with a big house and a car.
words.ex_cn: 他过着资产阶级的生活，有一栋大房子和一辆车。
words.en: If you describe people, their way of life, or their attitudes as bourgeois, you are criticizing them for caring too much about money and possessions and for being too conventional.

words.ex: He made a choice to study hard.
words.ex_cn: 他选择努力学习。
words.en: If you have a choice, you can choose between two or more things.

words.ex: He kept his dignity even when he was poor.
words.ex_cn: 即使他很穷，他依然保持尊严。
words.en: Dignity is the quality of being worthy of honor or respect.

words.tr: v. 使成贵族；使高贵；使受尊敬
words.ex: The king will ennoble the brave soldier.
words.ex_cn: 国王将封赏这位勇敢的士兵。
words.en: To ennoble someone means to make them a member of the nobility, or to make them seem morally or socially superior.

words.tr: adj. 文雅的；有教养的；上流社会的；装绅士派头的
words.ex: She spoke in a genteel way at the dinner party.
words.ex_cn: 她在晚宴上说话很文雅。
words.en: Someone who is genteel behaves in a polite and refined way, often in a manner that is considered typical of someone from a high social class.

words.ex: The imperial palace was built long ago.
words.ex_cn: 这座帝国宫殿是很久以前建造的。
words.en: relating to an empire or an emperor; majestic or superior in quality or size

words.tr: adj. 有权威的；地方法官的
words.ex: His magisterial tone left no room for argument.
words.ex_cn: 他那权威的语气让人没有反驳的余地。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior or work as magisterial, you mean that they show great authority or ability.

words.ex: The old temple felt numinous at night.
words.ex_cn: 那座古庙在晚上显得神圣神秘。
words.en: Something that is numinous is spiritual or supernatural in a way that inspires awe or reverence.

words.tr: adj. 皇家的；尊贵的；富丽堂皇的
words.ex: The queen wore a regal crown.
words.ex_cn: 女王戴着一顶威严的王冠。
words.en: If you describe something as regal, you mean that it is suitable for a king or queen, because it is very impressive or beautiful.

words.tr: adj. 势利的；谄上欺下的
words.ex: He is snobbish and ignores people who are not rich.
words.ex_cn: 他很势利，不理睬不富有的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as snobbish, you disapprove of them because they are too proud of their social status, intelligence, or taste.

words.tr: n. 至高无上；最大权力；最高地位；
words.ex: The king claimed supremacy over all other rulers.
words.ex_cn: 国王宣称自己对所有其他统治者拥有至高无上的权力。
words.en: Supremacy is the state or condition of being superior to all others in authority, power, or status.

words.tr: n. 仲裁人；公断人；权威
words.ex: He is the arbiter of the dispute.
words.ex_cn: 他是这场纠纷的仲裁者。
words.en: An arbiter is a person or agency officially appointed to settle a dispute.

words.tr: n. 权威；官方机构；权力；权威人士；当局；
words.ex: The teacher is an authority on ancient history.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师是古代史方面的权威。
words.en: The power to make decisions or enforce rules.

words.ex: The queen wore a diadem on her coronation day.
words.ex_cn: 女王在加冕日戴上了王冠。
words.en: A diadem is a crown or a headband worn as a symbol of royalty.

words.ex: The well-bred child said thank you politely.
words.ex_cn: 这个有教养的孩子礼貌地说了谢谢。
words.en: Someone who is well-bred has good manners and has been well brought up.

words.tr: n. 贵族政治；贵族统治；贵族
words.ex: The aristocracy lived in big castles long ago.
words.ex_cn: 很久以前，贵族住在巨大的城堡里。
words.en: The highest class in certain societies, especially those holding hereditary titles or offices.

words.tr: n. 岩层；地层；社会阶层
words.ex: The geologist examined the stratum for fossils.
words.ex_cn: 地质学家检查了岩层以寻找化石。
words.en: A stratum is a layer of material, naturally or artificially formed, often one of a number of parallel layers one upon another.

chapters.name: Word List 26 人及品质 活力

words.tr:
adj. 盛开的；旺盛的；非常的
v. 开花；“bloom”的现在分词
words.ex: The flowers are blooming in spring.
words.ex_cn: 花在春天盛开。
words.en: If something is described as blooming, it is growing or developing in a healthy and vigorous way, especially with reference to plants.

words.ex: The city had an economic boom after the new factory opened.
words.ex_cn: 新工厂开业后，这座城市迎来了经济繁荣。
words.en: If there is a boom in the economy, there is an increase in economic activity, for example in the amount of things that are being bought and sold.

words.tr:
adj. 动态的；有活力的；不断变化的；
n. 活力；动力；
words.ex: The game has dynamic weather that changes every hour.
words.ex_cn: 这个游戏有每小时变化的动态天气。
words.en: If you describe someone as dynamic, you approve of them because they are full of energy or full of new ideas.

words.tr: adj. 精力充沛的；热情洋溢的；
words.ex: The exuberant children ran around the park.
words.ex_cn: 那些精力充沛的孩子们在公园里跑来跑去。
words.en: If you are exuberant, you are full of energy, excitement, and cheerfulness.

words.tr: v. 繁荣兴旺；茁壮成长；
words.ex: The business flourishes in the new market.
words.ex_cn: 这家企业在新市场中繁荣兴旺。
words.en: If something flourishes, it is successful, active, or common, and developing quickly and strongly.

words.tr: adj. 盛开的；完全成熟的；全面的
words.ex: The garden is full of full-blown roses in spring.
words.ex_cn: 春天，花园里盛开着盛开的玫瑰。
words.en: completely developed or formed

words.tr: n. 活动过度；极度活跃
words.ex: The child shows hyperactivity during class.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子在课堂上表现出多动。
words.en: Hyperactivity is a state of being unusually or abnormally active.

words.ex: The lush grass looked green after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后，葱翠的草地显得格外绿。
words.en: A lush area has a lot of green, healthy plants, grass, and trees.

words.tr: adj. 精力充沛的；生气勃勃的；健壮的
words.ex: The young man sang a lusty song at the party.
words.ex_cn: 那个年轻人在派对上唱了一首嘹亮的歌。
words.en: If you describe someone as lusty, you mean that they are strong and healthy and full of energy.

words.tr: adj. 精神饱满的；勇敢的
words.ex: The mettlesome horse galloped across the field.
words.ex_cn: 这匹精神饱满的马飞奔过田野。
words.en: If you describe someone as mettlesome, you mean that they are full of courage, energy, and determination.

words.tr: adj. 棕榈（似）的；多棕榈的；繁荣的；兴旺的
words.ex: The palmy days of the town are gone.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇的繁荣岁月已经过去了。
words.en: If you describe a period of time as palmy, you mean that it was successful or prosperous.

words.tr: adj. 热情的；充满热情的；
words.ex: She is passionate about teaching children.
words.ex_cn: 她对教孩子充满热情。
words.en: Having, showing, or caused by strong feelings or beliefs.

words.ex: The city became prosperous after the new factory opened.
words.ex_cn: 新工厂开业后，这座城市变得繁荣了。
words.en: A prosperous person, place, or economy is rich and successful.

words.tr: adj.  活泼的；明快的；时髦的；没好气的
words.ex: He gave a snappy reply to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了干脆利落的回答。
words.en: If someone is snappy, they speak to people in a sharp, unfriendly way.

words.ex: She painted with great verve.
words.ex_cn: 她作画时充满热情。
words.en: If you say that someone has verve, you mean that they seem to have a lot of energy and enthusiasm.

words.ex: The children are vibrant and full of energy.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们充满活力。
words.en: If you describe something as vibrant, you mean that it is bright, lively, and full of energy.

words.ex: He uses vim to write code.
words.ex_cn: 他用 vim 编写代码。
words.en: Vim is a noun that refers to energy and enthusiasm in doing something.

words.ex: Water is vital for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命至关重要。
words.en: If you say that something is vital, you mean that it is necessary or very important.

words.tr: v. 给予 ... 生命力； 激发
words.ex: The new paint will vitalize the old house.
words.ex_cn: 新油漆会让这栋老房子焕然一新。
words.en: To give life or energy to something, making it more active or successful.

chapters.name: Word List 26 人及品质 精神

words.tr: adj. 有骑士风度的；彬彬有礼的；侠义的
words.ex: The knight was chivalrous and helped the lady.
words.ex_cn: 这位骑士有骑士精神，帮助了那位女士。
words.en: A chivalrous man is polite, kind, and unselfish, especially towards women.

words.tr: n. 倡议；主动权；自发性；措施；
words.ex: The school launched an initiative to reduce plastic use.
words.ex_cn: 学校发起了一项减少塑料使用的倡议。
words.en: An initiative is an important act or statement that is intended to solve a problem.

words.ex: The child's psyche was affected by the loud noises.
words.ex_cn: 孩子的心灵受到了嘈杂声音的影响。
words.en: The human soul, mind, or spirit.

words.ex: He finds peace through spiritual meditation.
words.ex_cn: 他通过精神上的冥想找到平静。
words.en: Relating to the human spirit or soul as opposed to material or physical things.

words.tr: adj. 内脏的；脏腑的；发自肺腑的
words.ex: He had a visceral reaction to the scary movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影有本能的恐惧反应。
words.en: Relating to deep inward feelings rather than to the intellect.

words.ex: The company follows ethical practices in hiring.
words.ex_cn: 该公司在招聘中遵循伦理规范。
words.en: Relating to moral principles or the branch of knowledge dealing with these.

words.ex: He felt psychological stress before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前感到心理压力。
words.en: Relating to the mental and emotional state of a person.

chapters.name: Word List 26 人及品质 冷淡

words.tr:
adj. 疏远的；冷淡的
adv. 远离地
words.ex: He stayed aloof during the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上保持冷淡。
words.en: Someone who is aloof is not very friendly and does not like to spend time with other people.

words.ex: The mountains look distant from here.
words.ex_cn: 从这里看，山显得很远。
words.en: If you describe something as distant, you mean that it is far away in space or time.

words.ex: He estranged his brother with harsh words.
words.ex_cn: 他用刻薄的话与兄弟疏远了。
words.en: If you estrange someone, especially a member of your family, you cause them to stop being friendly or close to you.

words.ex: This brand has an exclusive design.
words.ex_cn: 这个品牌拥有独有的设计。
words.en: Something that is exclusive is available only to particular people, and not to everyone.

words.tr: v. 禁止；不准；“forbid”的现在分词；
words.ex: The sign forbids parking here.
words.ex_cn: 这个标志禁止在这里停车。
words.en: If you describe something as forbidding, you mean it has a severe, unfriendly, or threatening appearance.

words.ex: He remained impassive when he heard the bad news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个坏消息时，他依然面无表情。
words.en: If someone is impassive, they do not show any emotion.

words.tr: adj. 不能渗透的；不受影响的
words.ex: The coat is impervious to rain.
words.ex_cn: 这件外套不透水。
words.en: If you are impervious to someone's actions, you are not affected or influenced by them.

words.tr: adj. 不感兴趣的；不关心的；
words.ex: He was indifferent to the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影不感兴趣。
words.en: If you accuse someone of being indifferent to something, you mean that they have a complete lack of interest in it.

words.tr: adj. 若无其事的；不在乎的；冷淡的
words.ex: He was nonchalant about the test result.
words.ex_cn: 他对考试结果表现得漫不经心。
words.en: If you describe someone as nonchalant, you mean that they appear not to worry or care about things and that they seem very calm.

words.ex: He was offish when I said hello.
words.ex_cn: 我跟他打招呼时，他很冷淡。
words.en: If you describe someone as offish, you mean that they are not very friendly towards other people.

words.tr:
v. 冷落；怠慢；不理睬；掐灭
n. 冷落；怠慢
adj. 短平而上翘的
words.ex: He snubbed his friend at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上冷落了朋友。
words.en: To snub someone means to deliberately ignore them or treat them with disrespect, often by refusing to acknowledge their presence or by failing to respond to a greeting or request.

words.tr: adj. 不动声色的；无动于衷的；不易激动的
words.ex: He remained stolid in the face of adversity.
words.ex_cn: 面对逆境，他依然冷漠。
words.en: If you describe someone as stolid, you mean that they do not show much emotion or are not very exciting or interesting.

words.tr: adj. 缺乏兴趣的；漠不关心的；
words.ex: He was apathetic about the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影缺乏兴趣。
words.en: If you describe someone as apathetic, you are criticizing them because they do not seem to be interested in or enthusiastic about doing anything.

words.ex: He showed apathy toward the news.
words.ex_cn: 他对这则新闻漠不关心。
words.en: Apathy is a lack of feeling, emotion, interest, or concern about something. It is a state of indifference, or the suppression of emotions such as concern, excitement, motivation, or passion.

words.tr: adj. 煮过熟了的；不动感情的
words.ex: He ate a hard-boiled egg for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他早餐吃了一个煮熟的鸡蛋。
words.en: Hard-boiled refers to eggs that have been cooked until both the white and yolk are solid, or it can describe a person who is tough and unsentimental.

words.tr: adj. 不领情的；忘恩负义的
words.ex: He was ungrateful for the gift.
words.ex_cn: 他对这份礼物毫不感激。
words.en: If you describe someone as ungrateful, you are criticizing them for not showing thanks or for being unkind to someone who has helped them or done them a favour.

chapters.name: Word List 26 人及品质 魅力

words.ex: His charisma made everyone want to follow him.
words.ex_cn: 他的超凡魅力让所有人都想追随他。
words.en: Charisma is a compelling attractiveness or charm that can inspire devotion in others.

words.ex: Her smile has a special charm.
words.ex_cn: 她的微笑有一种特别的魅力。
words.en: If you say that someone has charm, you mean that they behave in a friendly and pleasant way that makes people like them. A charm is also a small ornament that is fixed to a bracelet or necklace.

words.tr: adj. 富有魅力的；迷人的；
words.ex: She wore a glamorous dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条富有魅力的裙子去参加派对。
