words.en: If you describe someone or something as glamorous, you mean that they are more attractive, exciting, or interesting than ordinary people or things.

words.tr: adj. 风度好的；个性或外表宜人的；英俊的；貌美的；有魅力的
words.ex: He was a personable young man, always ready to help others.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个品貌兼优的年轻人，总是乐于助人。
words.en: If you describe someone as personable, you mean that they are pleasant and attractive in appearance and character.

words.tr: adj. 极好的；令人震惊的； v. “stun”的现在分词；
words.ex: She wore a stunning dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件极好的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: Extremely impressive or attractive.

chapters.name: Word List 26 人及品质 能力

words.ex: This phone is affordable for students.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机对学生来说价格合理。
words.en: If something is affordable, most people have enough money to buy it.

words.ex: The artistry of the painting amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画的艺术性让每个人都惊叹。
words.en: The skill of an artist, or the quality of being artistic.

words.ex: He has the calibre to lead the team.
words.ex_cn: 他有领导团队的能力。
words.en: The quality of someone's character or the level of their ability; the diameter of the inside of a tube, especially of a gun barrel.

words.ex: His competence in math helped him solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学方面的能力帮助他解决了这个问题。
words.en: Competence is the ability to do something well or efficiently.

words.tr: n. 工艺；手艺；行业；航空器；
words.ex: The craft of pottery takes years to learn.
words.ex_cn: 陶艺工艺需要多年才能掌握。
words.en: Skill in making things by hand; the skilled practice of a practical occupation; the skilled production of decorative or functional objects.

words.ex: He excels in math.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长数学。
words.en: To be exceptionally good at or proficient in an activity or subject.

words.tr:
n. 专长；特长
adv. 用强音
words.ex: His forte is playing the piano.
words.ex_cn: 他的强项是弹钢琴。
words.en: A thing at which someone excels.

words.ex: He felt impuissance after the failure.
words.ex_cn: 失败后，他感到无能为力。
words.en: The state or condition of being powerless or lacking strength.

words.tr: adj. 无能力的；不称职的；不能胜任的；
words.ex: He is incompetent at managing simple tasks.
words.ex_cn: 他无法胜任简单的任务。
words.en: If you describe someone as incompetent, you are criticizing them because they are unable to do their job or a task properly.

words.tr: adj. 不适当的；无能的；笨拙的
words.ex: His inept reply made the situation worse.
words.ex_cn: 他不适当的回答让情况变得更糟。
words.en: If you say that someone is inept, you are criticizing them because they do something with a complete lack of skill.

words.tr: n. 不合适；不擅长；笨拙；无能
words.ex: His ineptitude made him unsuitable for the job.
words.ex_cn: 他的不合适让他不适合这份工作。
words.en: Lack of skill or ability; incompetence.

words.ex: He has a knack for fixing bikes.
words.ex_cn: 他有修自行车的技巧。
words.en: A knack is a special skill or ability that someone has, especially one that is hard to explain or teach.

words.tr: adj. 全能的；无所不能的
words.ex: The god is omnipotent.
words.ex_cn: 这个神是无所不能的。
words.en: Having unlimited power, able to do anything.

words.tr: n. 高超的技艺；造诣；英勇；
words.ex: His prowess in basketball amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在篮球方面的高超技艺让所有人都惊叹。
words.en: Exceptional skill or ability in a particular field or activity.

words.ex: He smiled at the recollection of his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他回忆起童年时微笑了。
words.en: The act of remembering something or the ability to remember.

words.ex: This plan is viable and can be done with little money.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划是可行的，而且用很少的钱就能完成。
words.en: If something is viable, it is capable of doing what it is intended to do.

words.ex: He chose teaching as his vocation.
words.ex_cn: 他选择了教学作为自己的职业。
words.en: A vocation is a type of work that you feel you are especially suited to do and to which you give much of your time and energy.

words.ex: The machine is a clever contrivance that saves a lot of time.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器是一个节省大量时间的发明。
words.en: A contrivance is a device or plan that is used to achieve a particular result, often in a way that is clever but not always honest or straightforward.

words.tr: n. 手法；骗术；花招；诡诈
words.ex: His success was due to a bit of legerdemain in the deal.
words.ex_cn: 他的成功归功于交易中的一点小把戏。
words.en: Skillful use of one's hands when performing conjuring tricks.

chapters.name: Word List 26 人及品质 年老

words.tr: adj. 经验主义的；以经验为根据的；
words.ex: The scientist used empirical data to support her theory.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家使用经验数据来支持她的理论。
words.en: Empirical evidence or study relies on practical experience rather than theories.

words.tr: adj. 羽毛丰满的；有充分资格的；成熟的
words.ex: The young eagle is now full-fledged and can fly alone.
words.ex_cn: 这只小鹰现在已经羽毛丰满，可以独自飞翔了。
words.en: Having reached full development or maturity; fully qualified or established.

words.ex: He remained passive during the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持被动。
words.en: Accepting or allowing what happens or what others do, without active response or resistance.

words.ex: The precocious child could read before age five.
words.ex_cn: 这个早熟的孩子在五岁前就会阅读了。
words.en: A precocious child shows intelligence or skill at a very young age, especially in a way that is unusual for their age.

words.ex: The apples ripen in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 苹果在秋天成熟。
words.en: When crops ripen or when the sun ripens them, they become ripe and ready to eat.

words.tr:
adj. 富有经验的；加佐料的；风干的
v. 给 ... 调味；适应；风干；“season”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He is a seasoned cook with many years of experience.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有多年经验的熟练厨师。
words.en: If someone is seasoned, they have a lot of experience of something and are therefore able to deal with it in a confident way.

words.ex: Her senility made it difficult for her to remember recent events.
words.ex_cn: 她的衰老使她难以记住最近发生的事情。
words.en: Senility refers to the mental and physical decline associated with old age, often characterized by memory loss, confusion, and a decrease in cognitive abilities.

words.tr: adj. 年老的；衰老的；老糊涂的
words.ex: The senile man forgot his son's name.
words.ex_cn: 这位年老的男子忘记了他儿子的名字。
words.en: If someone is senile, they are behaving in a confused or strange way, and unable to remember things, because they are old.

words.tr:
adj. 领取退休金而退休的；过时的
v. 因年老而辞退；给养老金使…退休；“superannuate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The superannuated teacher still works part-time.
words.ex_cn: 这位退休的老师仍然兼职工作。
words.en: Too old to be effective or useful, especially in the context of employment.

words.tr:
adj. （尤指宗教或精神方面）超验的；超自然的
n. 超越数；超越物；抽象的普遍概念
words.ex: His transcendental philosophy influenced many thinkers.
words.ex_cn: 他的先验哲学影响了众多思想家。
words.en: Transcendental refers to something that is beyond ordinary or physical experience, often relating to spiritual or metaphysical realms.

words.tr: adj. 没有激情的；不感情用事的；平静的
words.ex: Her unimpassioned response indicated a lack of interest.
words.ex_cn: 她不动感情的回应表明了缺乏兴趣。
words.en: Not showing or feeling strong emotion; calm and rational.

chapters.name: Word List 26 人及品质 年轻幼稚

words.tr: adj. 未成熟的；无处世经验的；乳臭未干的
words.ex: The new recruits were callow and inexperienced.
words.ex_cn: 新兵们年轻而无经验。
words.en: If you describe someone as callow, you mean that they are inexperienced and immature.

words.ex: He showed filial love by taking care of his old parents.
words.ex_cn: 他通过照顾年迈的父母表现出子女的孝心。
words.en: Filial is used to describe the relationship between children and their parents, especially emphasizing the duty and respect that children should show towards their parents.

words.tr:
n. 刚长齐羽毛学飞的幼鸟
adj. 新形成的；无经验的
v. 羽毛长成；用羽毛盖上；装上羽毛；“fledge”的现在分词
words.ex: The fledgling bird tried to fly for the first time.
words.ex_cn: 这只幼鸟第一次尝试飞翔。
words.en: A fledgling is a young bird that has just grown its feathers and is learning to fly. It can also refer to a person or organization that is new and inexperienced.

words.tr:
adj. 绿色的；未熟的；无经验的；
n. 绿色；
words.ex: The leaves are green in spring.
words.ex_cn: 春天时，树叶是绿色的。
words.en: Green is the color between blue and yellow in the spectrum. It is the color of growing grass and leaves.

words.ex: The incipient fire was put out quickly.
words.ex_cn: 初期的小火被迅速扑灭了。
words.en: An incipient situation or quality is one that is just beginning to develop or become noticeable.

words.tr: adj. 婴儿的；幼稚的；孩子气的
words.ex: The infantile smile made everyone feel warm.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿般的微笑让每个人都感到温暖。
words.en: Infantile behavior or illnesses are typical of very young children.

words.tr:
adj. 青少年的；幼稚的；
n. 少年；
words.ex: The book is written for juvenile readers.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是为青少年读者撰写的。
words.en: A juvenile is a child or young person who is not yet old enough to be considered an adult.

words.ex: The nascent industry is growing quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这个新生的产业正在迅速发展。
words.en: Nascent things or processes are just beginning, and are expected to become stronger or to grow bigger.

words.tr: adj. 愚蠢的；幼稚的；孩子气的
words.ex: His puerile jokes made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他幼稚的笑话让每个人都感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as puerile, you mean that they are silly and childish.

words.tr: adj. 未充分发展的；初步的；基本的；
words.ex: His knowledge of math is rudimentary.
words.ex_cn: 他对数学的了解是初步的。
words.en: Rudimentary means relating to the basic or simplest aspects of a subject, or being in the earliest stages of development.

words.tr: n. 初进社交界的少女
words.ex: The debutante's ball was a grand affair attended by the elite of society.
words.ex_cn: 这位初次进入社交界的年轻女子的舞会是一场盛大的活动，社会精英纷纷出席。
words.en: A debutante is a young woman from a wealthy or upper-class family who is making her first formal appearance in society, typically at a debutante ball.

chapters.name: Word List 26 人及品质 热情

words.ex: He is an ardent supporter of environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的热心支持者。
words.en: An ardent person has strong feelings or enthusiasm for something.

words.ex: He is an avid reader of mystery novels.
words.ex_cn: 他热衷于阅读侦探小说。
words.en: If you say that someone is avid for something, you mean that they are very eager to get it.

words.ex: He was a fervid supporter of the cause.
words.ex_cn: 他是这一事业的热心支持者。
words.en: Having or displaying a passionate intensity.

words.ex: He spoke with fervor about his dreams.
words.ex_cn: 他充满热情地谈论自己的梦想。
words.en: Fervor is intense and passionate feeling.

words.tr: adj. 极端或过分热情的
words.ex: His perfervid speech inspired the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他那热情洋溢的演讲激励了群众。
words.en: Having or showing intense and fervent feeling or enthusiasm.

words.tr: v. 盛情招待；尽情吃喝；使欢悦
words.ex: He regaled us with stories of his travels.
words.ex_cn: 他给我们讲了他旅行的故事，让我们很开心。
words.en: To regale someone means to entertain them with stories or to provide them with a lot of enjoyable food and drink.

words.tr: adj. 兴致很高的；很有滋味的
words.ex: The party had a zesty atmosphere with lively music and dancing.
words.ex_cn: 派对气氛非常活跃，有充满活力的音乐和舞蹈。
words.en: Having a strong, pleasant, and somewhat spicy flavor or smell; lively and pleasing.

words.ex: He showed great zeal in helping others.
words.ex_cn: 他在帮助他人时表现出极大的热情。
words.en: Zeal is great enthusiasm, especially in connection with work, religion, or politics.

words.ex: He speaks with great ardor about his dreams.
words.ex_cn: 他充满热情地谈论自己的梦想。
words.en: Ardor is a strong, intense feeling of love or enthusiasm for someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 奔放的；兴高采烈的；沸腾的
words.ex: He is ebullient after winning the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得奖后非常兴奋。
words.en: If you describe someone as ebullient, you mean that they are lively and full of enthusiasm or excitement about something.

words.tr: adj. 溢于言表的；感情奔放的
words.ex: She was effusive in her praise for the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 她对老师的赞美非常热情。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as effusive, you mean that they express pleasure, gratitude, or approval in a very enthusiastic way.

words.ex: He showed great enthusiasm for learning English.
words.ex_cn: 他对学习英语表现出极大的热情。
words.en: Enthusiasm is a strong feeling of excitement and interest in something and a desire to become involved in it.

words.tr: adj. 热烈的；强烈的；热情的
words.ex: He is a fervent supporter of environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的热心支持者。
words.en: having or showing very strong and sincere feelings about something

chapters.name: Word List 26 人及品质 天赋

words.tr: adj. 先天的；天生的；生性的
words.ex: He was born with a congenital heart problem.
words.ex_cn: 他出生时就有先天性心脏病。
words.en: A congenital disease or condition exists at or from birth.

words.ex: She has a flair for painting.
words.ex_cn: 她有绘画的天赋。
words.en: If you have a flair for a particular activity, you have a natural ability to do it well.

words.tr: adj. 内在的；无所不在的
words.ex: The immanent laws of nature govern all living things.
words.ex_cn: 自然界的内在法则支配着所有生物。
words.en: Existing or operating within; inherent.

words.tr: adj. 天生的；先天的；天赋的
words.ex: He has an inborn talent for music.
words.ex_cn: 他天生就有音乐才能。
words.en: An inborn quality or ability is one that you have had naturally since birth.

words.ex: Babies have an innate ability to cry.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿生来就有哭泣的能力。
words.en: An innate quality or ability is one that you were born with, not one you have learned.

words.ex: The cat made an instinctive jump to avoid the dog.
words.ex_cn: 猫本能地跳开以躲避狗。
words.en: An instinctive feeling, action, or idea is one that you have or do without thinking or reasoning.

words.ex: Finding my lost keys while walking in the park was pure serendipity.
words.ex_cn: 在公园散步时偶然找到了丢失的钥匙，这真是易遇奇缘的运气。
words.en: The occurrence and development of events by chance in a happy or beneficial way.

chapters.name: Word List 26 人及品质 渊博

words.ex: His knowledge is encyclopedic.
words.ex_cn: 他的知识非常渊博。
words.en: Comprehensive in terms of information or knowledge, resembling or suggesting an encyclopedia.

words.ex: The erudite professor knows many ancient languages.
words.ex_cn: 这位博学的教授懂得许多古代语言。
words.en: Having or showing great knowledge or learning.

words.ex: His lectures were marked by erudition and wit.
words.ex_cn: 他的讲座以博学和机智著称。
words.en: Erudition is the quality of having or showing great knowledge or learning.

words.tr: adj. 了解情况的； v. 通知；告知；“inform”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is an informed voter who reads the news daily.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个了解情况的选民，每天阅读新闻。
words.en: If someone is informed, they know a lot about a particular subject or situation.

words.ex: He is literate and can read simple books.
words.ex_cn: 他有读写能力，能读简单的书。
words.en: A literate person is able to read and write, and has a good education.

words.tr: adj. 全知的；无所不知的
words.ex: The omniscient narrator knows everything about the characters.
words.ex_cn: 全知的叙述者了解角色的一切。
words.en: Knowing everything; having infinite awareness, understanding, and insight.

words.ex: He is a maven in the field of computer science.
words.ex_cn: 他是计算机科学领域的专家。
words.en: A maven is someone who is very knowledgeable about a particular subject.

words.ex: He is savvy about technology.
words.ex_cn: 他对技术很有见识。
words.en: If you describe someone as savvy, you mean that they show a lot of practical knowledge and ability.

words.ex: The clear sky was an auspice of good weather.
words.ex_cn: 晴朗的天空是好天气的预兆。
words.en: An auspice is a sign or omen that is believed to predict the future, often seen as favorable or supportive. It can also refer to the protection or support provided by a person or organization.

chapters.name: Word List 26 人及品质 愿望

words.tr: n. 渴望；热望；强烈的愿望； v. “crave”的现在分词；
words.ex: He has a craving for chocolate.
words.ex_cn: 他渴望吃巧克力。
words.en: A craving is a very strong desire for something.

words.ex: He is desirous of a new bike.
words.ex_cn: 他想要一辆新自行车。
words.en: Having or characterized by desire; wanting or wishing for something.

words.tr: v. 处置；清除；解决；“dispose”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He disposed of the old books.
words.ex_cn: 他处理掉了那些旧书。
words.en: If you are disposed to do something, you are willing or eager to do it.

words.tr:
n. 渴望；期望
v. 渴望；追求；“hanker”的现在分词
words.ex: He had a hankering for adventure.
words.ex_cn: 他对冒险有着强烈的渴望。
words.en: A hankering is a strong feeling of wanting something.

words.ex: He gave an intentional wrong answer to confuse the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他故意答错答案来迷惑老师。
words.en: Something that is intentional is done on purpose, not by chance.

words.tr: adj. 非自愿的；不由自主的；
words.ex: His hand moved in an involuntary way.
words.ex_cn: 他的手不自觉地动了一下。
words.en: If you make an involuntary movement or exclamation, you make it suddenly and without intending to because you are unable to control yourself.

words.tr:
n. 渴望；热望
adj. 渴望的；热望的
v. 渴望；热望；“long”的现在分词
v. 用练马绳训练马的各种步态
words.ex: Her longing for home grew stronger each day.
words.ex_cn: 她对家的渴望与日俱增。
words.en: A strong feeling of wanting something or someone.

words.ex: The prospect of a better job makes him happy.
words.ex_cn: 更好工作的前景让他感到高兴。
words.en: A prospect is the possibility that something will happen, or a view of a wide area.

words.tr: adj. 任性的；故意的；蓄意的
words.ex: The willful child refused to eat his vegetables.
words.ex_cn: 这个任性的孩子拒绝吃蔬菜。
words.en: If you describe actions or attitudes as willful, you are critical of them because they are done or expressed deliberately, especially with the intention of causing harm, or they are stubborn and unreasonable.

words.ex: He yearns for a better life.
words.ex_cn: 他渴望更好的生活。
words.en: If you yearn for something, you want it very much.

words.ex: He showed reluctance to speak in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他表现出不愿意在全班面前讲话。
words.en: Reluctance is an unwillingness to do something.

chapters.name: Word List 26 人及品质 直率

words.ex: He spoke with candor about his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他坦率地谈到了自己的错误。
words.en: the quality of being open and honest in expression; frankness.

words.tr: adj. 直截了当的；直率的；坦白的
words.ex: He is forthright about his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他坦率地承认自己的错误。
words.en: If you describe someone as forthright, you admire them because they show clearly and strongly what they think and feel.

chapters.name: Word List 26 人及品质 忠诚

words.tr: v. 犯罪；做错事；“commit”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 忠诚的；
words.ex: He was committed for stealing a car.
words.ex_cn: 他因偷车而被定罪。
words.en: If you are committed to something, you are willing to give your time and energy to it because you believe in it.

words.tr: v. 奉为神圣；贡献；奉献
words.ex: They consecrate the church with prayer and song.
words.ex_cn: 他们用祈祷和歌声将教堂奉为神圣。
words.en: To consecrate something means to officially declare it to be holy and to be used for religious purposes.

words.ex: His dedication to teaching helped many students succeed.
words.ex_cn: 他对教学的奉献帮助了许多学生取得成功。
words.en: The act of dedicating or the state of being dedicated; commitment.

words.ex: He swore fealty to the king.
words.ex_cn: 他向国王宣誓效忠。
words.en: Fealty is a formal and solemn promise of loyalty to a king, queen, or other ruler, especially in the Middle Ages.

words.tr: adj. 不奸猾的；厚道的；坦率的
words.ex: He is a guileless boy who always tells the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个纯真无邪的男孩，总是说真话。
words.en: If you describe someone as guileless, you mean that they behave openly and truthfully and do not try to deceive people.

words.ex: He is loyal to his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友忠诚。
words.en: Someone who is loyal remains firm in their friendship or support for a person or thing.

words.ex: He is a dependable friend who always helps.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个可靠的朋友，总是提供帮助。
words.en: Someone or something that is dependable can be relied on to do what you need or expect.

words.ex: He shows piety by praying every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天祈祷，表现出虔诚。
words.en: Piety is strong religious belief, or behaviour that is religious or morally correct.

words.ex: His fidelity to his friend never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的忠诚从未改变。
words.en: Fidelity is loyalty to a person, organization, or set of beliefs.

chapters.name: Word List 27 正向评价 沉着

words.ex: She sang softly to allay his fears.
words.ex_cn: 她轻声唱歌以缓解他的恐惧。
words.en: If you allay someone's fears or doubts, you stop them feeling afraid or doubtful.

words.ex: She spoke with aplomb during the interview.
words.ex_cn: 她在面试中自信地发言。
words.en: If you do something with aplomb, you do it with confidence in a relaxed way.

words.ex: He gave her a gift to appease her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他送她一份礼物来平息她的怒气。
words.en: If you try to appease someone, you try to stop them from being angry by giving them what they want.

words.ex: The soup was too bland for me.
words.ex_cn: 这汤太淡了，我不喜欢。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as bland, you mean that they are rather dull and unexciting.

words.tr: v. 组成；创作；“compose”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The team is composed of five players.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队由五名队员组成。
words.en: If someone is composed, they are calm and able to control their feelings.

words.ex: He kept his composure during the interview.
words.ex_cn: 他在面试中保持了冷静。
words.en: The state of being calm and in control of your emotions.

words.tr: adj. 无表情的（面孔）；表情冷淡的
words.ex: He delivered the punchline with a deadpan expression.
words.ex_cn: 他用面无表情的表情说出了笑点。
words.en: If you describe someone as deadpan, you mean that they appear serious and do not show emotion in their face or voice, even when they are joking or teasing.

words.tr: adj. 不动感情的；冷静的；平心静气的
words.ex: She remained dispassionate throughout the heated debate.
words.ex_cn: 她在激烈的辩论中始终保持冷静。
words.en: If you are dispassionate, you are able to act calmly and reasonably and not be influenced by your feelings or by personal opinions.

words.ex: He remained imperturbable even when the storm hit.
words.ex_cn: 即使风暴来袭，他依然镇定自若。
words.en: If you describe someone as imperturbable, you mean that they remain calm, even in disturbing or dangerous situations.

words.ex: It was impolitic to laugh at his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 笑他的错误是不妥当的。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as impolitic, you mean that it is unwise and likely to cause offence or problems, especially in social situations.

words.ex: He enjoys the leisureliness of Sunday mornings.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢星期天早上的悠闲。
words.en: The quality or state of being leisurely; unhurriedness.

words.tr: adj. 头脑冷静的；清醒的
words.ex: She is always levelheaded in a crisis.
words.ex_cn: 她在危机中总是保持冷静。
words.en: If you describe a person as levelheaded, you mean that they are calm and sensible even in difficult situations.

words.ex: He is methodical in organizing his work.
words.ex_cn: 他在安排工作时很有条理。
words.en: If you describe someone as methodical, you mean that they do things carefully, thoroughly, and in order.

words.tr: n. 漠不关心；无动于衷
words.ex: He showed nonchalance when the glass fell.
words.ex_cn: 当玻璃杯掉下来时，他表现得若无其事。
words.en: The state of being nonchalant; a casual lack of concern or indifference.

words.ex: He is phlegmatic even when things go wrong.
words.ex_cn: 即使事情出错，他依然冷静。
words.en: A phlegmatic person does not usually get emotional or excited about things.

words.tr:
n. 平衡；姿态；镇静
v. 使平衡；保持（某种姿势）
words.ex: The dancer maintained her poise on one foot.
words.ex_cn: 舞者单脚保持平衡。
words.en: If someone has poise, they are calm, dignified, and self-controlled.

words.ex: It is rational to save money for the future.
words.ex_cn: 为未来存钱是合理的。
words.en: Based on or in accordance with reason or logic.

words.tr: adj. 心智健全的；头脑清醒的；明智的
words.ex: He is still sane after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他仍然神志清醒。
words.en: If someone is sane, they are able to think and behave in a normal and rational manner.

words.ex: Despite the chaos around him, he maintained his sangfroid.
words.ex_cn: 尽管周围一片混乱，他依然保持冷静。
words.en: If you say that someone has sangfroid, you mean that they are able to remain calm in a dangerous or difficult situation.

words.tr: n. 心智健全；神志清楚；神智健全
words.ex: The doctors questioned his sanity after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，医生们质疑他的精神是否健全。
words.en: The condition of having a healthy mind and not being mentally ill.

words.tr:
adj. 安详的；安静的；镇静的
v. 给…服镇静剂
words.ex: The sedate old man sat quietly by the window.
words.ex_cn: 那位安详的老人安静地坐在窗边。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as sedate, you mean that they are quiet, calm, and dignified.

words.tr: adj. 清醒的；严肃的；素淡的；
words.ex: He stayed sober after drinking only water.
words.ex_cn: 他只喝了水，保持清醒。
words.en: If you are sober, you are not drunk. If you are sober, you are serious and thoughtful.

words.ex: He is a staid man who never wears casual clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个古板的人，从不穿休闲服。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as staid, you mean that they are serious, dull, and rather old-fashioned.

words.tr: adj. 镇定自若的；临危不乱的
words.ex: She remained unflappable even under intense pressure.
words.ex_cn: 即使在巨大的压力下，她依然保持镇定。
words.en: If you describe someone as unflappable, you mean that they stay calm in difficult or worrying situations.

words.tr: adj. 无动于衷的；坚定的；不动心的
words.ex: She remained unmoved by his pleas.
words.ex_cn: 对他的恳求，她无动于衷。
words.en: If you are unmoved by something, you are not emotionally affected by it.

chapters.name: Word List 27 正向评价 聪颖

words.ex: He has business acumen and makes smart decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他有商业洞察力，能做出明智的决定。
words.en: The ability to make good judgments and quick decisions, typically in a particular domain.

words.tr: adj. 敏锐的；急性的；严重的；
words.ex: He has an acute mind and solves problems quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他思维敏锐，能快速解决问题。
words.en: An acute problem or negative feeling is very severe.

words.ex: He is adroit at fixing broken machines.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长修理坏掉的机器。
words.en: Someone who is adroit is quick and skillful in their thoughts, behavior, or actions.

words.tr: n. 敏捷；活泼；欣然；乐意
words.ex: He answered the question with alacrity.
words.ex_cn: 他愉快地回答了问题。
words.en: If you do something with alacrity, you do it quickly and eagerly.

words.ex: He is ambidextrous and can write with both hands.
words.ex_cn: 他是左右手都灵巧的，可以用两只手写字。
words.en: Someone who is ambidextrous can use both their right and left hands equally well.

words.ex: He is an astute businessman who always makes smart decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他是个精明的商人，总是做出明智的决定。
words.en: If you describe someone as astute, you think they are clever and can see through things quickly and make good judgments.

words.ex: He is calculating the total cost.
words.ex_cn: 他正在计算总费用。
words.en: If you describe someone as calculating, you disapprove of the fact that they deliberately plan to get what they want, often by hurting or harming other people.

words.tr: adj. 精明的；老谋深算的
words.ex: He is a canny trader who always makes smart choices.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个精明的交易员，总是做出明智的选择。
words.en: A canny person is clever and able to think quickly, especially in business or politics.

words.ex: He is conversant with basic math.
words.ex_cn: 他熟悉基础数学。
words.en: If you are conversant with something, you are familiar with it and able to deal with it.

words.ex: The chef made a deft cut with the knife.
words.ex_cn: 厨师用刀熟练地切了一下。
words.en: A deft action is skilful and often quick.

words.ex: The surgeon's dexterity saved the patient's life.
words.ex_cn: 外科医生的灵巧救了病人的命。
words.en: Skill and grace in physical movement, especially in the use of the hands; adroitness.

words.tr: adj. 灵巧的（手）；熟练的；敏捷的
words.ex: He is dexterous with his hands.
words.ex_cn: 他双手很灵巧。
words.en: Someone who is dexterous is skillful with their hands.

words.ex: He made an expeditious decision to leave.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速做出了离开的决定。
words.en: If you describe something as expeditious, you mean that it is done quickly and efficiently.

words.tr: adj. 讲究实际的；头脑清晰的；不感情用事的
words.ex: He is hardheaded and won't change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很固执，不会改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as hardheaded, you mean that they are practical and determined to get what they want, and do not let emotions or other people's opinions affect them.

words.tr: adj. 有独创性的；巧妙的；
words.ex: The child came up with an ingenious way to solve the puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子想出了一个有独创性的方式来解决这个谜题。
words.en: Something that is ingenious is very clever and involves new ideas, methods, or equipment.

words.ex: His ingenuity solved the problem with a simple tool.
words.ex_cn: 他的独创力用一个简单的工具解决了问题。
words.en: Ingenuity is the ability to think of clever and original ways to solve problems.

words.ex: His intellect helps him solve difficult problems.
words.ex_cn: 他的智力帮助他解决难题。
words.en: The ability to understand and think in a logical way about things.

words.tr:
adj. 智力的；
n. 知识分子；
words.ex: He is an intellectual person who loves solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个热爱解决数学问题的智力型人。
words.en: An intellectual is someone who spends a lot of time studying and thinking about complicated ideas.

words.tr: adj. 明智的；有见识的；判断正确的
words.ex: He made a judicious choice about which book to buy.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了一个明智的买书决定。
words.en: If you describe an action or decision as judicious, you approve of it because you think that it shows good judgment and sense.

words.ex: His judiciousness in decision-making has earned him respect.
words.ex_cn: 他在决策中的明智为他赢得了尊重。
words.en: The quality of having or showing good judgment; prudence.

words.tr: adj. 灵活的；敏捷的；机敏的
words.ex: The cat is nimble and jumps over the fence.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫很敏捷，跳过了篱笆。
words.en: Someone who is nimble is able to move their fingers, hands, or legs quickly and easily.

words.ex: The detective managed to outfox the criminal.
words.ex_cn: 侦探设法智胜了罪犯。
words.en: To outfox someone means to defeat them by being more clever or cunning than they are.

words.ex: He outwit the opponent with a clever trick.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个聪明的计策胜过了对手。
words.en: To outwit someone means to use your intelligence or a clever trick to defeat them or gain an advantage over them.

words.tr: n. （文章语言表达等的）明晰；简明
words.ex: The perspicuity of her writing made it easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 她写作的明晰性使得文章易于理解。
words.en: The quality of being clear and easy to understand.

words.ex: He is proficient in playing the piano.
words.ex_cn: 他弹钢琴很熟练。
words.en: If you are proficient in something, you can do it well because you have learned how to do it.

words.tr: adj. 有先见之明的；深谋远虑的
words.ex: He is a provident man who saves money for the future.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个有远见的人，会为未来存钱。
words.en: Making provision for the future; exercising foresight or forethought.

words.ex: I am ready for the test.
words.ex_cn: 我准备好考试了。
words.en: If you are ready, you are prepared for something or are in a suitable state to do or deal with it.

words.tr: adj. 资源丰富的；机敏的；足智多谋的
words.ex: He is a resourceful man who can fix anything with little material.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个资源丰富的男人，能用很少的材料修好任何东西。
words.en: If someone is resourceful, they are good at finding ways of dealing with problems.

words.tr: adj. 精明练达的；有远见的；有洞察力的
words.ex: He is a sagacious man who always makes wise choices.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个睿智的人，总是做出明智的选择。
words.en: Having or showing keen mental discernment and good judgment; shrewd.

words.ex: She added sage to the stuffing for Thanksgiving dinner.
words.ex_cn: 她在感恩节晚餐的填料中加入了鼠尾草。
words.en: A sage is a person who is regarded as being very wise, especially someone who is known for their good judgment and deep understanding of life.

words.ex: Her sagacity in business matters was widely recognized.
words.ex_cn: 她在商业事务上的睿智广为人知。
words.en: The quality of being sagacious; wisdom and good judgment.

words.ex: He gave a sapient nod, indicating he understood the situation.
words.ex_cn: 他聪明地点了点头，表示他理解了情况。
words.en: Having or showing great wisdom or sound judgment.

words.tr: v. 闪烁；发火花；焕发才智
words.ex: The diamonds on her necklace scintillated under the light.
words.ex_cn: 她项链上的钻石在灯光下闪闪发光。
words.en: To emit sparks or to sparkle; to twinkle; to be brilliant or lively in conversation or performance.

words.tr: adj. 明智的；有判断力的；恰当的；合理的；
words.ex: It is sensible to wear a coat in cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 在寒冷的天气里穿外套是明智的。
words.en: A sensible person is able to make good judgments and decisions based on reason rather than emotion.

words.tr: adj. 精明的；敏锐的；机灵的；
words.ex: He made a shrewd decision to buy the house low.
words.ex_cn: 他精明地决定低价买下这栋房子。
words.en: A shrewd person is able to understand and judge a situation quickly and to use this understanding to their own advantage.

words.tr: n. 技巧；敏捷手法；策略；戏法
words.ex: The magician used sleight to make the coin disappear.
words.ex_cn: 魔术师用技巧让硬币消失了。
words.en: Skill in using the hands, especially in performing tricks.

words.tr: adj. 聪明的；时髦的；衣冠楚楚的；
words.ex: He is a smart student who solves math problems quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个聪明的学生，能快速解决数学问题。
words.en: If you describe someone as smart, you mean that they are clean, tidy, and stylish in their appearance.

words.ex: He answered the question with tact.
words.ex_cn: 他机智地回答了这个问题。
words.en: If you describe what someone says or does as tact, you mean that it is polite, considerate, and shows an understanding of other people's feelings.

words.ex: His virtuosity on the piano amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在钢琴上的精湛技艺让所有人惊叹。
words.en: Great skill in music or another artistic pursuit.

words.ex: He is a man of great wit.
words.ex_cn: 他是个极具机智的人。
words.en: Wit is the ability to use words or ideas in a quick, clever, and amusing way.

chapters.name: Word List 27 正向评价 功效

words.ex: This rule is applicable to all students.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则适用于所有学生。
words.en: If something is applicable to a particular situation, it is relevant or suitable for that situation.

words.ex: This medicine is efficacious for colds.
words.ex_cn: 这种药对感冒有效。
words.en: An efficacious method or treatment is one that has the ability to produce a desired effect or result.

words.ex: The efficacy of the medicine is clear.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物的效果是明显的。
words.en: The ability to produce a desired or intended result.

words.tr:
adj. 起作用的；运作中的
n. 技工；密探；特工
words.ex: The operative plan is to start tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 实施的计划是明天开始。
words.en: An operative system or plan is one that is in use or being used. An operative is someone who works for a government agency or a private company, often doing secret or confidential work.

words.ex: His advice was effectual in solving the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他的建议在解决问题上是有效的。
words.en: Producing or able to produce a desired effect; effective.

words.tr: adj. 无力的；虚弱的；阳痿的
words.ex: He felt impotent after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到无能为力。
words.en: If someone feels impotent, they feel that they have no power to influence people or events.

chapters.name: Word List 27 正向评价 和蔼

words.tr: adj. 谦恭有礼的；和蔼可亲的
words.ex: He is an affable man who always smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个和蔼可亲的人，总是面带微笑。
words.en: Someone who is affable is pleasant and friendly.

words.ex: Her affability made her a favorite among the customers.
words.ex_cn: 她的亲切使她成为顾客们的最爱。
words.en: The quality of being affable; friendliness and approachability.

words.tr: adj. 和蔼可亲的；亲切友好的
words.ex: He is an amiable man who always smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个和蔼可亲的人，总是面带微笑。
words.en: Someone who is amiable is friendly and pleasant to be with.

words.ex: They had an amicable talk after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 争吵之后，他们进行了一次友好的交谈。
words.en: When people have an amicable relationship, they are pleasant towards each other and solve their problems without arguing.

words.ex: The treaty established amity between the two nations.
words.ex_cn: 该条约确立了两国之间的友好关系。
words.en: A friendly relationship between people or countries.

words.ex: The benevolent man gave food to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这位慈善的人给穷人提供了食物。
words.en: If you describe a person in authority as benevolent, you mean that they are kind and fair.

words.ex: The benign teacher always helped students after class.
words.ex_cn: 这位仁慈的老师总是在课后帮助学生。
words.en: A benign substance or process does not have any harmful effects.

words.ex: His bonhomie made everyone feel welcome.
words.ex_cn: 他的温和让每个人都感到受欢迎。
words.en: A cheerful and friendly manner; geniality.

words.tr:
n. 天主教徒；
adj. 天主教的；
words.ex: He is a catholic who goes to church every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名每周日都去教堂的天主教徒。
words.en: If you describe a collection of things or people as catholic, you are emphasizing that it is varied and includes many different types of things or people.

words.tr: adj. 仁慈的；慈善事业的；
words.ex: She gave charitable donations to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 她向穷人捐赠了仁慈的善款。
words.en: A charitable organization or activity helps and supports people who are ill, very poor, or who have disabilities.

words.ex: The judge showed clemency and reduced the sentence.
words.ex_cn: 法官表现出宽大，减轻了刑罚。
words.en: Clemency is kindness and forgiveness, especially towards someone who could be punished severely.

words.ex: The clement teacher gave students extra time.
words.ex_cn: 这位仁慈的老师给了学生更多时间。
words.en: Mild or merciful in disposition or character; lenient; compassionate.

words.tr: adj. 兼容的；可和谐共存的；
words.ex: This printer is compatible with my computer.
words.ex_cn: 这个打印机与我的电脑兼容。
words.en: If things, for example, systems, ideas, and beliefs, are compatible, they work well together or can exist together successfully.

words.ex: The weather was congenial for a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 天气非常适合野餐。
words.en: A congenial person, place, or environment is pleasant because it suits your character or nature.

words.ex: He is an equable man who never gets angry.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个性情恬静的人，从不生气。
words.en: If you describe someone as equable, you mean that they are calm, cheerful, and fair with other people, even in difficult circumstances.

words.ex: He is even-tempered and never gets angry easily.
words.ex_cn: 他性格平和，从不轻易发脾气。
words.en: If someone is even-tempered, they are usually calm and do not easily get angry or upset.

words.ex: His familiarity with the city helped him find the way.
words.ex_cn: 他对这座城市的熟悉帮助他找到了路。
words.en: A thorough knowledge or mastery of a subject, place, or situation, often gained through experience.

words.ex: The twin boys are fraternal twins.
words.ex_cn: 这两个男孩是异卵双胞胎。
words.en: Fraternal is used to describe feelings or actions that are like those of a brother towards his brothers or sisters.

words.tr: adj. 温和的；文雅的；温柔的；
words.ex: The mother gave a gentle hug to her child.
words.ex_cn: 母亲给了孩子一个温和的拥抱。
words.en: Someone who is gentle is kind and calm, and does not behave in a violent or harsh way.

words.ex: He showed goodwill by helping his neighbor for free.
words.ex_cn: 他通过免费帮助邻居表现出善意。
words.en: A friendly or cooperative attitude or feeling towards others, especially in a business context.

words.tr: adj. 亲切的；和蔼的；仁慈的
words.ex: She was gracious and thanked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 她很友善，感谢了每一个人。
words.en: If you describe someone, especially someone you think is superior to you, as gracious, you mean that they are very well-mannered and pleasant.

words.tr: adj. 人道的；仁慈的；人文的
words.ex: The shelter treats animals in a humane way.
words.ex_cn: 这个收容所以人道的方式对待动物。
words.en: If you describe something as humane, you mean that it is good and kind, especially because it decreases suffering.

words.ex: The judge showed leniency toward the first-time offender.
words.ex_cn: 法官对初犯表现出了宽大。
words.en: Leniency is the quality of being more merciful or tolerant than expected.

words.tr: adj. 宽厚的；仁慈的；不严格的；
words.ex: The teacher was lenient with students who were late.
words.ex_cn: 老师对迟到的学生很宽厚。
words.en: If you are lenient with someone, you are not strict in the way you treat them, especially when they have done something wrong.

words.tr: adj. 外向的；即将离职的；往外去的；
words.ex: He is an outgoing boy who loves talking to new people.
words.ex_cn: 他是个外向的男孩，喜欢和新朋友聊天。
words.en: Someone who is outgoing is very friendly and likes meeting and talking to people.

words.tr:
adj. 给人良好印象的；令人喜爱的；吸引人的
v. 使预先具有（某种思想）；使…先怀偏见；使产生偏爱；“prepossess”的现在分词
words.ex: She had a prepossessing smile that could light up a room.
words.ex_cn: 她有一个迷人的微笑，能照亮整个房间。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as prepossessing, you mean that they have a quality that makes you like or approve of them immediately.

words.ex: He is a sociable man who likes to talk with friends.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢和朋友聊天的外向的人。
words.en: A sociable person is friendly and enjoys being with other people.

words.tr:
adj. 柔和的；减弱的；郁郁不乐的
v. 征服；克制；制服；“subdue”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The room had subdued lights.
words.ex_cn: 房间里灯光柔和。
words.en: If a color or light is subdued, it is not very bright.

words.ex: The beneficent man gave food to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这位仁慈的人给穷人提供了食物。
words.en: A beneficent person or organization helps people or results in something good.

words.ex: His geniality made everyone feel welcome.
words.ex_cn: 他的和蔼可亲让每个人都感到受欢迎。
words.en: The quality of being friendly and cheerful.

chapters.name: Word List 27 正向评价 活泼

words.ex: The children love watching animated movies.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们喜欢看动画电影。
words.en: Animated means full of life or excitement, or made to appear to move as if by magic or technology.

words.ex: My son loves watching cartoon animation.
words.ex_cn: 我儿子喜欢看卡通动画。
words.en: Animation is the process of making films in which drawings or puppets appear to move.

words.ex: He took a brisk walk in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 他早上轻快地散步。
words.en: If someone or something is brisk, they are quick and lively in their actions or movements.

words.tr: v. 使有生气；使活跃；使快活
words.ex: The music enlivened the party.
words.ex_cn: 音乐让派对更热闹了。
words.en: To make something more interesting, exciting, or cheerful.

words.ex: The expansive desert stretches for miles.
words.ex_cn: 广阔的沙漠延伸数英里。
words.en: If you describe something such as a period of time or a piece of writing as expansive, you mean that it is very long or detailed.

words.ex: The story had a graphic description of the battle.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事对战斗的描述非常生动。
words.en: A graphic is a visual representation of data or information, such as a chart, diagram, or picture.

words.tr: adj. 活泼的；神气的；意气洋洋的；有生气的
words.ex: She is perky after drinking coffee.
words.ex_cn: 她喝完咖啡后精神抖擞。
words.en: Someone who is perky is cheerful and lively.

words.ex: She had a puckish grin on her face when she hid his keys.
words.ex_cn: 她藏起他的钥匙时，脸上露出了淘气的笑容。
words.en: If you describe someone as puckish, you mean that they playfully cause trouble or behave in a mischievous way.

words.tr: adj. 活泼的；有趣的；略带淫秽的
words.ex: The novel was full of racy dialogue.
words.ex_cn: 这部小说充满了生动的对话。
words.en: If you describe something as racy, you mean that it is exciting, lively, and slightly shocking, especially because it is related to sex.

words.ex: The city is known for its vibrancy and cultural diversity.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市以其活力和文化多样性而闻名。
words.en: The quality of being full of energy and life.

words.ex: The painter used vivid colors to show the forest.
words.ex_cn: 画家用鲜艳的颜色来描绘森林。
words.en: If you describe memories and descriptions as vivid, you mean that they are very clear and detailed.

words.tr: adj. 活泼的；敏捷的；充满生气的
words.ex: The old man is still spry and walks fast.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人仍然身手敏捷，走得很慢。
words.en: Someone who is spry, especially an older person, is lively and active.

words.tr: adj. 轻松愉快的；无忧无虑的；随便的；漫不经心的
words.ex: He gave a lighthearted laugh during the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上开心地笑了。
words.en: If someone is lighthearted, they are cheerful and happy.

chapters.name: Word List 27 正向评价 坚强

words.tr: adj. 通过经历而变得顽强的；坚毅的；冷酷无情的
words.ex: The hard-bitten soldier never gave up, even in the face of overwhelming odds.
words.ex_cn: 面对压倒性的劣势，这位顽强的士兵也从未放弃。
words.en: If you describe someone as hard-bitten, you mean that they have been through a lot of difficult or unpleasant experiences and are tough as a result.

words.ex: The intrepid explorer climbed the high mountain.
words.ex_cn: 这位无畏的探险家爬上了高山。
words.en: If you describe someone as intrepid, you mean that they are brave, fearless, and willing to do things that might be dangerous.

words.tr: adj. 不容亵渎的；不可侵犯的
words.ex: Her privacy is inviolable.
words.ex_cn: 她的隐私是不可侵犯的。
words.en: If a law or principle is inviolable, it must not be broken or treated without respect.

words.tr: adj. 不会受伤害的；攻不破的；固若金汤的
words.ex: The fortress was said to be invulnerable.
words.ex_cn: 这座要塞据说无懈可击。
words.en: If someone or something is invulnerable, they cannot be harmed or damaged.

words.ex: He was stouthearted and faced the storm.
words.ex_cn: 他勇敢地面对了风暴。
words.en: Having or showing courage and determination.

words.tr: n. 意志力；自愿选择；自行决断
words.ex: He did it of his own volition.
words.ex_cn: 他是出于自己的意愿做的。
words.en: The power to make your own decisions or choices.

chapters.name: Word List 27 正向评价 俭朴

words.tr: adj. 有节制的；饮食有度的
words.ex: He is abstemious with sugar and eats little dessert.
words.ex_cn: 他对糖很节制，吃很少的甜点。
words.en: Someone who is abstemious avoids doing too much of something enjoyable, especially eating or drinking.

words.tr: adj. 简朴的；严厉的；苦行的；紧缩的
words.ex: The room has austere walls with no decorations.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间的墙壁朴素，没有任何装饰。
words.en: If you describe something as austere, you approve of its plain and simple appearance.

words.tr: n. 紧缩；艰苦朴素；节俭
words.ex: The government implemented austerity measures to reduce the budget deficit.
words.ex_cn: 政府实施了紧缩措施以减少预算赤字。
words.en: Austerity is a situation in which people's living standards are reduced because of economic difficulties.

words.tr: adj. 贞洁的；忠贞的；朴素的
words.ex: She remained chaste despite the pressure.
words.ex_cn: 尽管有压力，她依然保持贞洁。
words.en: If you describe someone as chaste, you mean that they do not have sex with anyone, or they only have sex with their husband or wife.

words.ex: He is frugal with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他花钱很节俭。
words.en: If you describe someone as frugal, you mean that they are careful about spending money and use things only when they need to.

words.tr: adj. 像家般舒适的；朴素的；
words.ex: The small cabin had a homely feel with soft blankets and a warm fire.
words.ex_cn: 这座小木屋有柔软的毛毯和温暖的火炉，感觉像家一样舒适。
words.en: If you describe something as homely, you mean that it is simple and plain, often in a way that is comforting. If you describe a person as homely, you mean that they are not very attractive.

words.tr: adj. 单纯的；天真的；坦率的
words.ex: He gave an ingenuous smile when he told the truth.
words.ex_cn: 当他讲真话时，他露出了天真无邪的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as ingenuous, you mean that they are innocent, trusting, and honest, often in a way that seems naive.

words.ex: The child gave a naive smile when he believed the story.
words.ex_cn: 当孩子相信这个故事时，他露出了天真的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as naïve, you think they lack experience and so expect things to be easy or people to be honest or kind.

words.ex: His naivety made him trust strangers easily.
words.ex_cn: 他的天真使他很容易相信陌生人。
words.en: Naivety is the quality of being naive; innocence or lack of experience, wisdom, or judgment.

words.tr: adj. 谨慎的；慎重的；精明的
words.ex: He is prudent with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他在花钱时很谨慎。
words.en: If you are prudent, you are careful and avoid taking unnecessary risks.

words.ex: The company must retrench to save money.
words.ex_cn: 公司必须裁员以节省资金。
words.en: If a person or organization retrenches, they spend less money.

words.tr: v. 舍不得给；节省；克扣
words.ex: She skimped on the ingredients to save money.
words.ex_cn: 她为了省钱，在食材上克扣。
words.en: To skimp means to spend less time, money, or effort on something than is really needed, often resulting in a lower quality outcome.

words.tr: adj. 少量使用的； v. “spare”的现在分词；
words.ex: He uses sparing amounts of sugar in his tea.
words.ex_cn: 他在茶里只用很少的糖。
words.en: If you describe someone as sparing, you mean that they are careful in the way they use something, especially money or food, because there is very little of it.

words.ex: He lives a spartan life with little food and no luxuries.
words.ex_cn: 他过着简朴的生活，食物很少，也没有奢侈品。
words.en: If you describe something as spartan, you mean that it is very simple and not at all luxurious, often because it is intended to be useful or practical rather than attractive.

words.tr:
n. (从事某项活动的)规定期限
v. 吝惜；节省
words.ex: He did a short stint as a teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他短暂地当过一段时间老师。
words.en: A stint is a fixed period of time during which someone does a particular job or activity.

words.ex: She is thrifty and saves money every week.
words.ex_cn: 她很节约，每周都存钱。
words.en: If you say that someone is thrifty, you are praising them for saving money and not spending it on unnecessary things.

words.ex: The country's economy is growing fast.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家的经济正在快速增长。
words.en: The economy of a country or region is the system by which money, industry, and trade are organized.

words.ex: His frugality helped him save money for years.
words.ex_cn: 他的节俭让他多年都存下了钱。
words.en: Frugality is the quality of being careful with money or food, so that you only spend what is necessary.

words.ex: He ate a moderate amount of food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了适量的食物。
words.en: If you moderate something or if it moderates, it becomes less extreme or violent, or if you moderate a discussion, you help the people in it to reach an agreement.

words.ex: He is an assiduous student who studies every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个勤奋的学生，每天都学习。
words.en: Someone who is assiduous works hard or does things very thoroughly.

words.ex: He gave a cautionary warning about the dangerous road.
words.ex_cn: 他针对这条危险的道路给出了一个警戒性的警告。
words.en: A cautionary story or warning is intended to make people aware of the possible dangers or problems of something.

words.ex: He is chary of spending money on useless things.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意把钱花在无用的东西上。
words.en: If you are chary of doing something, you are cautious or hesitant about doing it because you are worried that it might have bad consequences.

words.tr: v. 深思熟虑；慎重考虑
words.ex: He cogitates before he answers the question.
words.ex_cn: 他在回答问题之前会深思。
words.en: To think deeply about something; to ponder or meditate.

words.ex: He is a conscientious student who always finishes his homework on time.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个尽责的学生，总是按时完成作业。
words.en: Someone who is conscientious is very careful to do their work properly.

words.tr:
adj. 深思熟虑的；故意的；
v. 深思熟虑；
words.ex: He made a deliberate choice to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他深思熟虑后决定辞去工作。
words.en: If you do something that is deliberate, you planned or decided to do it beforehand, and so it happens on purpose rather than by chance.

words.tr: adj. （言行）谨慎的；不显眼的；朴素的
words.ex: He was discreet about his personal life.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的私生活很低调。
words.en: If you are discreet, you are polite and careful in what you do or say, because you want to avoid embarrassing or offending someone.

words.ex: The teacher gave students discretion to choose their own topic.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了学生自行选择题目的权利。
words.en: Discretion is the quality of behaving in a quiet and controlled way without drawing attention to yourself or giving away personal or private information.

words.ex: He is an earnest student who always finishes his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个认真的学生，总是完成作业。
words.en: If you are earnest about something, you are serious about it and your intentions are honest and sincere.

words.tr: v. 使全神贯注；独占；垄断
words.ex: He is engrossed in reading a novel.
words.ex_cn: 他正全神贯注地读一本小说。
words.en: If something engrosses you, it interests you so much that you do not notice anything else.

words.tr: n. 正式誊写的文件；全神贯注
words.ex: The lawyer kept the engrossment of the contract in a safe box.
words.ex_cn: 律师把正式誊写的合同文件放在保险箱里。
words.en: The state of being completely absorbed or occupied by something.

words.tr: n. 先见；预见；先见之明
words.ex: He showed foresight by saving money for the future.
words.ex_cn: 他通过为未来存钱展现了远见。
words.en: The ability to predict or the action of predicting what will happen or be needed in the future.

words.tr:
adv. 小心地；谨慎地
adj. 小心的；谨慎的
words.ex: He walked gingerly on the icy path.
words.ex_cn: 他小心翼翼地走在结冰的小路上。
words.en: If you do something gingerly, you do it in a careful manner, usually because you expect it to be dangerous, unpleasant, or painful.

words.tr: adj. 不顾将来的；无远见的；不节俭的
words.ex: He is improvident and spends all his money.
words.ex_cn: 他挥霍无度，花光了所有钱。
words.en: If you describe someone as improvident, you mean that they do not think about the future and do not plan for it carefully, often spending money in a careless way.

words.tr:
n. 意图；目的；
adj. 专注的；
words.ex: His intent was to help, not to hurt.
words.ex_cn: 他的意图是帮助，而不是伤害。
words.en: If you are intent on doing something, you are determined to get it done. If you have an intent to do something, you have a plan or purpose in mind.

words.tr:
adj. 成熟的；
v. 成熟；
words.ex: He is a mature student who works full-time.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位成熟的学生，全职工作。
words.en: When something or someone matures, they become fully grown or developed. In finance, a mature investment is one that has reached the end of its term and is ready to be paid out.

words.tr: v. 测量；“measure”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 慎重的；谨慎小心的；
words.ex: He measured the length of the table.
words.ex_cn: 他测量了桌子的长度。
words.en: If you describe someone's way of speaking as measured, you mean that it is slow and deliberate, often because they are trying to hide their feelings.

words.ex: He sat in a meditative pose by the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在湖边，摆出沉思冥想的姿势。
words.en: A meditative state or process involves deep thought or concentration, often as part of a religious or spiritual practice.

words.tr: adj. 一丝不苟的；缜密的
words.ex: He is meticulous about checking his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他仔细检查作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as meticulous, you mean that they do things very carefully and with great attention to detail.

words.tr: adj. 不多的；适度的；谦虚的；
words.ex: He made a modest profit last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年的利润不多。
words.en: If you say that someone is modest, you approve of them because they do not talk much about their abilities or achievements.

words.tr: adj. 虔诚的；信神的；伪善的
words.ex: He is a pious man who prays every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个每天祈祷的虔诚的人。
words.en: Someone who is pious is very religious and moral.

words.ex: His preoccupation with video games made him ignore his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他对电子游戏的全神贯注让他忽略了作业。
words.en: If you have a preoccupation with something or someone, you think or worry about them very often and they are the main focus of your attention.

words.ex: She showed great prudence in managing her finances.
words.ex_cn: 她在理财方面表现出了极大的谨慎。
words.en: Prudence is the quality of being careful and avoiding risks.

words.tr: adj. 谨小慎微的；一丝不苟的
words.ex: He is punctilious about following every rule.
words.ex_cn: 他对遵守每一条规则都谨小慎微。
words.en: If someone is punctilious, they are very careful to behave correctly and to follow the details of rules or customs.

words.tr: adj. 全神贯注的；专心致志的
words.ex: The children were rapt during the story.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们全神贯注地听故事。
words.en: If someone is rapt, they are so interested in or fascinated by what they are seeing or hearing that they do not pay attention to anything else.

words.tr: adj. 勤勉的；勤苦工作的
words.ex: He is sedulous in practicing piano every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天勤奋地练习钢琴。
words.en: If you describe someone as sedulous, you mean that they work hard and pay great attention to detail.

words.tr: v. 研究；学习；“study”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He studied the behavior of birds in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他研究了森林中鸟类的行为。
words.en: If you describe something as studied, you mean that it is deliberate and planned, rather than natural or spontaneous.

words.tr:
adj. 幻想的；有远见的
n. 空想家；有远见的人
words.ex: He had a visionary idea about flying cars.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个关于飞行汽车的幻想想法。
words.en: A visionary is someone who has strong ideas about how things might be different in the future, especially in a way that leads to changes in society or technology.

words.ex: He was wary of strangers who offered free gifts.
words.ex_cn: 他对那些提供免费礼物的陌生人保持谨慎。
words.en: If you are wary of something or someone, you are cautious because you do not know much about them and you believe they may be dangerous or cause problems.

words.ex: He was circumspect before signing the contract.
words.ex_cn: 他在签署合同之前非常谨慎。
words.en: If you are circumspect, you think carefully about something before doing it, because there may be risks involved.

words.ex: Beware of the dog.
words.ex_cn: 当心那只狗。
words.en: to be cautious and alert to the dangers of.

words.ex: He is scrupulous about checking his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他检查作业时一丝不苟。
words.en: If you are scrupulous, you are careful, thorough, and extremely attentive to details.

words.tr: n. 假正经；过分拘谨；装规矩
words.ex: His prudery made him avoid talking about love.
words.ex_cn: 他的拘谨让他避免谈论爱情。
words.en: Prudery is behavior or attitudes that are excessively modest or proper, especially in a way that is considered old-fashioned or hypocritical.

words.ex: She is assertive when she speaks up for her rights.
words.ex_cn: 当她为自己权利发声时，表现得坚定自信。
words.en: Someone who is assertive behaves confidently and is not frightened to say what they want or believe.

words.ex: This small enterprise makes handmade toys.
words.ex_cn: 这家小企业生产手工玩具。
words.en: An enterprise is a company or business, often a large one, or a difficult or important project, especially one that involves a lot of planning and organization.

words.ex: He showed his mettle in the tough race.
words.ex_cn: 他在艰苦的比赛中展现了实力。
words.en: Mettle is the ability and determination to do something successfully in spite of difficult conditions.

words.ex: The team's morale improved after they won the game.
words.ex_cn: 球队赢了比赛后，士气提升了。
words.en: Morale is the amount of confidence and cheerfulness that a group of people have.

words.ex: He strives to finish his homework every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天努力完成作业。
words.en: If you strive to do something or strive for something, you make a great effort to do it or get it.

words.ex: The bounteous harvest pleased the farmers.
words.ex_cn: 丰收让农民们很高兴。
words.en: If you describe something as bounteous, you mean that it is large in quantity or amount and is generous or freely given.

words.ex: His generosity helped the poor family.
words.ex_cn: 他的慷慨帮助了那个贫困的家庭。
words.en: Generosity is the quality of being kind and generous.

words.ex: The climate is hospitable for growing oranges.
words.ex_cn: 这种气候适合种植橙子。
words.en: If someone is hospitable, they are friendly, welcoming, and generous to guests or strangers.

words.tr:
adj. 慷慨激昂的；热烈的
v. 激起热情；使激动；“impassion”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He gave an impassioned speech about peace.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了充满激情的关于和平的演讲。
words.en: An impassioned speech or piece of writing is one that expresses very strong feelings about something.

words.tr: n. 慷慨大方；宽大；心胸开阔
words.ex: His liberality in sharing his wealth was well-known.
words.ex_cn: 他慷慨分享财富的行为是众所周知的。
words.en: The quality of being generous and open-minded.

words.ex: He showed magnanimity by forgiving his enemy.
words.ex_cn: 他宽恕了敌人，展现了宽宏大量。
words.en: Magnanimity is the quality of being kind, generous, and forgiving, especially towards someone who has wronged you.

words.tr: adj. 宽宏大量的；有雅量的
words.ex: He was magnanimous and forgave his enemy.
words.ex_cn: 他宽宏大量，原谅了他的敌人。
words.en: If you are magnanimous, you behave kindly and generously toward someone, especially after defeating them or being treated badly by them.

words.tr: n. 宽宏大量；慷慨给与
words.ex: Her munificence in donating to charity is well known.
words.ex_cn: 她对慈善机构的慷慨捐赠是众所周知的。
words.en: Munificence is the quality of being extremely generous.

words.ex: She gave her time ungrudgingly to help the community.
words.ex_cn: 她心甘情愿地抽出时间帮助社区。
words.en: If you describe someone's attitude or behaviour as ungrudging, you mean that they are willing to do something and do not resent doing it.

words.tr: adj. 大量地给予的；不吝啬的
words.ex: She was unstinting in her praise for the volunteers.
words.ex_cn: 她对志愿者们给予了慷慨的赞扬。
words.en: If you describe someone's support or effort as unstinting, you mean that they give it generously and completely, without holding back.

words.tr: adj. 慷慨的；丰富的；充足的
words.ex: She gave a bountiful donation to the orphanage.
words.ex_cn: 她向孤儿院慷慨地捐了一笔钱。
words.en: Something that is bountiful is large in quantity or number and is freely given.

words.ex: The painting has a simple aesthetic appeal.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画有一种简单的审美吸引力。
words.en: Concerned with beauty or the appreciation of beauty.

words.tr:
adj. 诱人的；迷人的；有吸引力的
v. 诱惑；吸引；“allure”的现在分词
words.ex: The city's nightlife is alluring to many tourists.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市的夜生活对许多游客来说都极具诱惑力。
words.en: Something that is alluring is powerfully and mysteriously attractive or fascinating.

words.ex: She is a comely girl with a sweet smile.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个面容姣好、带着甜美微笑的姑娘。
words.en: Pleasant to look at; attractive.

words.tr: adj. 潇洒的；风度翩翩的；温文尔雅的
words.ex: He had a debonair manner that put everyone at ease.
words.ex_cn: 他温文尔雅的举止让每个人都感到轻松自在。
words.en: A debonair man is charming, confident, and stylish, especially in his behavior and appearance.

words.ex: The restaurant serves a famous delicacy called seafood soup.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅供应一道著名的佳肴，叫海鲜汤。
words.en: Delicacy refers to the quality of being delicate, fine, or subtle in appearance, structure, or manner. It can also denote a choice or rare food item.

words.tr: adj. 精致的；微妙的；易碎的；脆弱的；
words.ex: She wore a delicate lace dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条精致的蕾丝连衣裙去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is delicate is small and beautifully shaped. It can also be easily broken or damaged.

words.tr: v. 从事于；（使）参与；“engage”的现在分词； adj. 有趣的；
words.ex: He is engaging in community service.
words.ex_cn: 他正在从事社区服务。
words.en: An engaging person or thing is pleasant, interesting, and entertaining.

words.tr:
adj. 迷人的；吸引人的
v. 迷惑；吸引住；奴役；“enthrall”的现在分词
words.ex: The book was an enthralling tale of adventure.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是一个引人入胜的冒险故事。
words.en: If you describe something as enthralling, you mean it is so interesting and exciting that it holds your attention completely.

words.tr: adj. 精美的；细腻的；强烈的
words.ex: She wore an exquisite dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条精美的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is exquisite is extremely beautiful or pleasant, especially in a delicate or refined way.

words.tr: adj. 红润的；华丽的；过分装饰的
words.ex: Her cheeks were florid after running in the cold.
words.ex_cn: 她在寒冷中跑步后，脸颊变得红润。
words.en: If you describe something as florid, you mean that it is complicated and elaborate rather than plain and simple.

words.ex: She wore a gorgeous dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件华丽的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you say that something is gorgeous, you mean that it gives you a lot of pleasure or is very attractive.

words.ex: She walked with grace across the stage.
words.ex_cn: 她优雅地走过舞台。
words.en: Grace is the quality of being pleasant, polite, and dignified, or a period of time allowed for something to be done.

words.ex: Her lissome movements captivated the audience.
words.ex_cn: 她柔软敏捷的动作吸引了观众。
words.en: If you describe someone as lissome, you mean they are thin, supple, and graceful.

words.ex: The ornate ceiling had gold patterns and flowers.
words.ex_cn: 华丽的天花板上有金色的图案和花朵。
words.en: Something that is ornate is highly decorated with complex patterns.

words.ex: Her pulchritude was the talk of the town.
words.ex_cn: 她的美貌是全镇的话题。
words.en: Physical beauty, especially of a woman.

words.tr: adj. 如天使般美丽（或纯洁等）的
words.ex: Her seraphic smile lit up the room.
words.ex_cn: 她天使般的微笑照亮了整个房间。
words.en: Resembling or characteristic of a seraph; angelic; blissful.

words.ex: The food at this restaurant is superb.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅的食物极佳。
words.en: If something is superb, its quality is very good indeed.

words.tr: v. 接受；拿(走)；带领；乘坐；费时；吃；“take”的现在分词；
words.ex: He is taking the job offer.
words.ex_cn: 他正在接受这份工作邀请。
words.en: The act of taking something, especially by force or by a legal process.

words.tr: v. 使变形；使改观；美化
words.ex: The makeup artist transfigured the actress for the role.
words.ex_cn: 化妆师为演员的角色进行了改观。
words.en: To transform into something more beautiful or elevated.

words.tr: adj. 漂亮的；迷人的；讨人喜欢的
words.ex: The winsome girl smiled at everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个可爱的女孩对每个人微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as winsome, you mean that they are attractive and charming.

words.tr: adj. 不可言喻的；无法形容的；避讳的
words.ex: The beauty of the sunset was ineffable.
words.ex_cn: 日落的美是无法言喻的。
words.en: If you describe something as ineffable, you mean that it is so impressive or extreme that it cannot be described in words.

words.ex: The difference between the two colors is subtle.
words.ex_cn: 这两种颜色之间的区别很微妙。
words.en: Something that is subtle is not immediately obvious or noticeable, but is rather indirect or understated.

words.tr: adj. 抛光的；磨光的；擦亮的； v. 擦亮；磨光；“polish”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The polished table reflected the light.
words.ex_cn: 抛光的桌子反射着光线。
words.en: If something is polished, it has been made smooth and shiny by rubbing it with a cloth or a special substance.

words.ex: The project was completed with remarkable celerity.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目以惊人的速度完成了。
words.en: Celerity is the quality of being swift or rapid.

words.ex: Her visual acuity is remarkable for someone her age.
words.ex_cn: 对于她这个年龄的人来说，她的视力敏锐度非常出色。
words.en: Acuity refers to the ability to see, hear, or think accurately and clearly.

words.ex: He claims to have clairvoyance and can see the future.
words.ex_cn: 他声称自己有预知能力，能看到未来。
words.en: The supposed faculty of perceiving things or events in the future or beyond normal sensory contact.

words.tr: adj. 颖悟的；敏锐的；有洞察力的
words.ex: She is perspicacious and notices small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 她很敏锐，能注意到细小的错误。
words.en: Having a ready insight into and understanding of things.

words.ex: Her perspicacity helped her solve the problem quickly.
words.ex_cn: 她的洞察力帮助她迅速解决了问题。
words.en: The ability to understand and judge things quickly and accurately.

words.tr: adj. 易反应的；应答的；回答的；
words.ex: The child is responsive to his mother's voice.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子对母亲的声音反应灵敏。
words.en: If someone or something is responsive, they react quickly and favorably.

words.tr: adj. 敏感的；感情脆弱的；体贴的；善解人意的；
words.ex: He is sensitive to loud noises.
words.ex_cn: 他对大声响很敏感。
words.en: If you are sensitive to other people's needs, problems, or feelings, you understand and are aware of them.

words.ex: His sensitivity to loud noises makes him wear earplugs.
words.ex_cn: 他对噪音的敏感性让他戴耳塞。
words.en: Sensitivity is the quality or condition of being sensitive—the capacity to respond to slight changes, signals, or influences.

words.ex: The sensitization process allowed the material to react more quickly to light.
words.ex_cn: 敏化过程使材料对光的反应更快。
words.en: Sensitization refers to the process of becoming sensitive or responsive to a particular stimulus or allergen, often leading to an allergic reaction upon subsequent exposures.

words.ex: The lotion can sensitize your skin to sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 这种乳液会使你的皮肤对阳光敏感。
words.en: To make someone or something sensitive to a particular substance or condition.

words.ex: His incisive comment solved the problem quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他一针见血的评论迅速解决了问题。
words.en: An incisive remark, question, or piece of writing is very clear and direct, and shows that the person understands something very well.

words.tr: adj. 尖锐的；有力的；精辟的
words.ex: His trenchant criticism left no room for doubt.
words.ex_cn: 他尖锐的批评让人没有怀疑的余地。
words.en: If you say that someone's speech or writing is trenchant, you mean that it is very clear and effective, often in criticizing something.

words.tr: adj. 居高临下的v. 屈尊；俯就；表现出优越感；“condescend”的现在分词
words.ex: He gave a condescending smile when she asked a simple question.
words.ex_cn: 当她问了一个简单的问题时，他露出了一副屈尊俯就的微笑。
words.en: If you say that someone is condescending, you are showing your disapproval of the fact that they talk or behave in a way which shows that they think they are superior to other people.

words.ex: He showed humility after winning the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他在赢得奖品后表现出了谦逊。
words.en: Humility is the quality of being humble and not thinking that you are better than other people.

words.ex: His constant self-abasement made him seem weak and unconfident.
words.ex_cn: 他不断的自卑让他显得软弱和不自信。
words.en: Self-abasement is the act of belittling or degrading oneself, often excessively or unnecessarily.

words.tr: adj. 不装腔作势的；低调谦逊的；
words.ex: He is an unassuming man who never talks about his achievements.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个不装腔作势的人，从不谈论自己的成就。
words.en: If you describe someone as unassuming, you approve of them because they are quiet and do not try to appear important.

words.ex: He was courteous to everyone he met.
words.ex_cn: 他对遇到的每个人都很有礼貌。
words.en: Someone who is courteous is polite and respectful to other people.

words.ex: He delves into the history of ancient civilizations.
words.ex_cn: 他探究古代文明的历史。
words.en: If you delve into something, you try to discover new information about it by searching or investigating carefully.

words.ex: He shows diligence in doing his homework every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天认真完成作业。
words.en: Conscientiousness in paying proper attention to a task; giving the degree of care required in a given situation.

words.ex: He is an industrious student who studies every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个勤勉的学生，每天都学习。
words.en: Someone who is industrious works hard and is determined.

words.ex: He made a painstaking effort to fix the small details.
words.ex_cn: 他细心地努力修正每一个小细节。
words.en: If you describe someone's work as painstaking, you mean that they do it very carefully and thoroughly, often taking a long time.

words.tr: adj. 需要久坐的；惯于久坐不动的；不爱活动的；
words.ex: His sedentary job makes him sit all day.
words.ex_cn: 他的久坐工作让他整天坐着。
words.en: Someone who has a sedentary lifestyle or job sits down a lot of the time and does not take much exercise.

words.ex: They shouted, 'Welcome home!' when he walked through the door.
words.ex_cn: 当他走进门时，他们大喊：‘欢迎回家！’
words.en: A greeting used to express pleasure at someone's return to their home.

words.tr:
v. 费力地做；苦干；跋涉
n. 苦工；劳累的工作
words.ex: He toils in the field every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天在田里辛苦劳作。
words.en: If you toil, you work very hard doing something that is difficult or tiring.

words.tr: n. 苦心而成的著作；学术作品；刻苦钻研
words.ex: The professor's latest lucubration is a comprehensive study on ancient civilizations.
words.ex_cn: 教授最新的苦心之作是对古代文明的综合研究。
words.en: A lucubration is a piece of writing that is produced by someone who studies or works hard at night, often implying that it is the result of deep thought and effort.

words.ex: He is diligent in doing his homework every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都很勤奋地做作业。
words.en: Someone who is diligent works hard and is careful and thorough.

words.ex: He felt tired after the exertion of running up the hill.
words.ex_cn: 在努力跑上山后，他感到很累。
words.en: The use of physical or mental energy; hard work.

words.ex: His altruism made him donate all his money to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他的利他主义让他把所有钱捐给了穷人。
words.en: Altruism is the belief in or practice of disinterested and selfless concern for the well-being of others.

words.ex: He gave his last dollar to the homeless man, showing an altruistic heart.
words.ex_cn: 他把最后一美元给了那个无家可归的人，表现出一颗无私的心。
words.en: If you describe someone as altruistic, you mean that they show unselfish concern for the welfare of others.

words.ex: He listened to his conscience and told the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他听从了良心，说出了真相。
words.en: Your conscience is the part of your mind that tells you whether what you are doing is right or wrong.

words.tr: n. 自大的人；自负的人
words.ex: He is an egotist who only talks about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他是个只谈论自己的自恋者。
words.en: An egotist is someone who is excessively conceited or absorbed in themselves; self-seeker.

words.ex: The cat is agile and jumps high.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫很敏捷，跳得很高。
words.en: Someone who is agile can move quickly and easily.

words.ex: The cat shows great agility when jumping over the fence.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫跳过围栏时表现出极大的灵活性。
words.en: Agility is the ability to move quickly and easily.

words.tr: adj. 衣冠楚楚的；干净利落的；短小精悍的
words.ex: He was a dapper man, always impeccably dressed.
words.ex_cn: 他是个衣冠楚楚的人，总是穿着无可挑剔。
words.en: If you describe a man as dapper, you mean that he is small and neat in appearance and moves quickly and energetically.

words.tr:
adv. 迅速；
adj. 快的；迅速的；
words.ex: He runs fast.
words.ex_cn: 他跑得很快。
words.en: Moving or capable of moving at high speed.

words.ex: The navy launched a large fleet to protect the coast.
words.ex_cn: 海军派出了一支大型舰队来保护海岸。
words.en: A fleet is a group of ships or vehicles that are controlled by one company or organization and are used for a particular purpose.

words.tr:
v. 轻快地掠过；突然换位；搬家
n. 掠过；迅速飞过；偷偷搬家
words.ex: The butterfly flits from flower to flower.
words.ex_cn: 蝴蝶在花朵间飞舞。
words.en: To move quickly and lightly from one place to another.

words.tr:
v. 奔驰；飞奔
n. 奔驰；飞奔
words.ex: The horse gallops across the field.
words.ex_cn: 马在田野上疾驰。
words.en: If a horse gallops, it runs very fast so that all four legs are off the ground at the same time in each stride.

words.tr:
v. 大步走；大步跑
n. 大步慢跑；平稳、轻松的步伐
words.ex: The deer loped gracefully through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 鹿优雅地大步慢跑穿过森林。
words.en: To run or move with a long, easy stride.

words.ex: The mice scamper away when they see the cat.
words.ex_cn: 老鼠一看到猫就四处奔逃。
words.en: If people or small animals scamper somewhere, they move there quickly with small, light steps.

words.tr:
v. 疾行；掠过
n. 疾驶；飞云；飞雾；小阵雨
words.ex: The clouds scudded across the sky.
words.ex_cn: 云朵在天空中疾行。
words.en: To move quickly or suddenly, especially through the air or over a surface.

words.tr:
v. 小步疾走；急赶
n. 快跑声；疾走
words.ex: The mouse scurried under the table.
words.ex_cn: 老鼠迅速跑到了桌子底下。
words.en: If people or small animals scurry somewhere, they move there quickly and hurriedly, especially because they are frightened.

words.tr:
v. 疾走
n. 疾走
words.ex: The mouse scuttered across the floor.
words.ex_cn: 老鼠在地板上小步快跑。
words.en: To move quickly with short steps, especially because you are in a hurry or frightened.

words.tr:
v. 疾走
n. 疾走
words.ex: The mouse scuttered across the floor.
words.ex_cn: 老鼠在地板上小步快跑。
words.en: To move quickly with short steps, especially because you are in a hurry or frightened.

words.ex: The valiant soldier fought bravely to protect his team.
words.ex_cn: 这位勇敢的士兵英勇战斗以保护他的队友。
words.en: Someone who is valiant is very brave and determined, especially in a difficult situation.

words.ex: The courageous soldier made a valorous charge.
words.ex_cn: 这位勇敢的士兵进行了英勇的冲锋。
words.en: If you describe someone as valorous, you mean that they are very brave, especially in battle.

words.ex: The courageous soldier made a valorous charge.
words.ex_cn: 这位勇敢的士兵进行了英勇的冲锋。
words.en: If you describe someone as valorous, you mean that they are very brave, especially in battle.

words.tr:
adj. 竖直的；直立的；
adv. 笔直地；
words.ex: The picture is hanging upright on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画垂直地挂在墙上。
words.en: If you are sitting or standing upright, you are sitting or standing with your back straight, rather than bending or lying down.

words.tr: adj. 诚实的；说实话的；准确的
words.ex: He is a veracious person who always tells the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个诚实的人，总是说真话。
words.en: Someone who is veracious is truthful and honest.

words.ex: The veracity of his story was questioned by the police.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事的真实性受到了警方的质疑。
words.en: Veracity refers to the quality of being true or accurate.

words.ex: She gave a heartfelt thank you to her teacher.
words.ex_cn: 她向老师真诚地表达了感谢。
words.en: If you describe something such as a feeling or emotion as heartfelt, you mean that it is genuine and strongly felt.

words.tr: adj. 不真诚的；不坦率的；虚伪的
words.ex: He gave a disingenuous answer to avoid trouble.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个不真诚的回答以避免麻烦。
words.en: Someone who is disingenuous is not sincere or honest, but pretends to be so in order to deceive people.

words.ex: He showed assertiveness when speaking up in the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上发言时表现出了自信。
words.en: Assertiveness is the quality of being self-assured and confident without being aggressive.

words.ex: I assure you that everything will be fine.
words.ex_cn: 我向你保证一切都会好起来的。
words.en: If you assure someone that something is true or will happen, you tell them that it is definitely true or will definitely happen, often in order to make them less worried.

words.ex: He spoke with confidence during the presentation.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲时充满信心。
words.en: Confidence is a feeling of self-assurance arising from one's appreciation of one's own abilities or qualities.

words.tr:
n. 很容易的事；确定的事情；小菜
v. 在腰间系住；紧握住；抓牢；弄确实
words.ex: Winning the game was a cinch for him.
words.ex_cn: 对他来说，赢得比赛是轻而易举的事。
words.en: If you describe something as a cinch, you mean that it is very easy to do.

words.ex: He is diffident when he speaks in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他在全班面前说话时很腼腆。
words.en: If you are diffident, you are rather shy and do not enjoy talking about yourself or being noticed by other people.

words.ex: He is confident when he speaks in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他在全班面前说话时很自信。
words.en: If you are confident, you are certain of your abilities or of your beliefs.

words.ex: He gave me his assurance that the work would be done on time.
words.ex_cn: 他向我保证工作会按时完成。
words.en: If you give someone an assurance that something is true or will happen, you say that it is definitely true or will definitely happen, in order to make them feel less worried.

words.ex: He spoke with diffidence during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上说话时很犹豫。
words.en: Diffidence is the quality of being shy and not confident of your abilities.

chapters.name: Word List 29 负向评价 傲慢

words.ex: The imperious queen demanded immediate obedience.
words.ex_cn: 这位专横的女王要求立即服从。
words.en: If you describe someone as imperious, you mean that they have a proud manner and expect to be obeyed.

words.tr: adj. 非常自负的；自命不凡的
words.ex: He was so vainglorious that he believed his own press clippings.
words.ex_cn: 他非常自负，以至于相信了自己的新闻剪报。
words.en: If you describe someone as vainglorious, you are critical of them because they are very proud of their own status, abilities, or achievements.

words.ex: His arrogance made others dislike him.
words.ex_cn: 他的傲慢让其他人不喜欢他。
words.en: Arrogance is the quality of being arrogant, which means having or revealing an exaggerated sense of one's own importance or abilities.

words.ex: He gave an arrogant answer to the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他傲慢地回答了老师的问题。
words.en: Someone who is arrogant behaves in a proud, unpleasant way towards other people because they believe that they are more important than others.

words.tr: adj. 膨胀的；肿胀的； v. “bloat”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The dog looked bloated after eating too much food.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗吃太多食物后看起来肚子膨胀。
words.en: If someone is bloated, they are swollen and round because they have eaten too much or are suffering from a medical condition.

words.tr: adj. 傲慢的；盲目自大的
words.ex: His bumptious attitude annoyed everyone at the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他傲慢的态度让会议上的每个人都感到不快。
words.en: If you say that someone is bumptious, you are criticizing them because they are very pleased with themselves and their opinions.

words.ex: His conceit makes him ignore others' advice.
words.ex_cn: 他的自负让他忽视别人的建议。
words.en: An excessively favorable opinion of one's own abilities or worth; vanity.

words.ex: The decision was consequential for the future of the company.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定对公司未来意义重大。
words.en: Something that is consequential is important or significant, often because it has effects on other things.

words.ex: He bore the contumely with dignity.
words.ex_cn: 他以尊严承受了侮辱。
words.en: Insolent or insulting language or treatment.

words.tr: adj. 傲慢的；高傲自大的
words.ex: He gave a haughty smile when he won the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得奖品时露出了傲慢的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as haughty, you mean that they behave in a proud, unfriendly way, because they think that they are better than other people.

words.ex: He spoke with hauteur when he met the new teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他见到新老师时说话一副高傲的样子。
words.en: Hauteur is the quality of being haughty; arrogance.

words.tr: adj. 刚愎自用的；顽固的；任性的
words.ex: He is headstrong and refuses to listen.
words.ex_cn: 他很固执，不肯听别人的话。
words.en: If you refer to someone as headstrong, you are slightly critical of them because they are very determined to do what they want, and refuse to be advised by others.

words.ex: His hubris made him lose the game.
words.ex_cn: 他的傲慢让他输掉了比赛。
words.en: Hubris is excessive pride or self-confidence, often leading to downfall or failure.

words.ex: Her insolence made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 她的傲慢让每个人都感到不适。
words.en: Insolence is rude and disrespectful behavior.

words.ex: He shows narcissism by always talking about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他总是谈论自己，表现出自恋。
words.en: Narcissism is the habit of always thinking about yourself and your appearance and abilities, and believing that you are better than other people.

words.tr: adj. 傲慢的；自负的；自以为是的
words.ex: His overweening pride led to his downfall.
words.ex_cn: 他过于自信的骄傲导致了他的失败。
words.en: If you describe someone as overweening, you are criticizing them because they are too confident and think they are better than other people.

words.tr: adj. 执拗的；任性的；乖张的；故意作对的；悖理的
words.ex: He gave a perverse answer to the simple question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个简单的问题给出了一个反常的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone as perverse, you mean that they deliberately behave in an unreasonable way, especially by doing the opposite of what is expected or wanted.
