words.ex: Her pertness irritated the interviewer.
words.ex_cn: 她的傲慢惹恼了面试官。
words.en: Pertness is the quality of being pert, which means being inappropriately forward or bold.

words.tr: n.  浮华；虚夸；炫耀；自负
words.ex: His pomposity often alienated his colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 他的自大使他经常疏远同事。
words.en: Pomposity is the quality of being pompous; self-importance.

words.tr: adj. 自负的；自命不凡的；浮华的
words.ex: He gave a pompous speech with big words.
words.ex_cn: 他用华丽的词藻做了一番自大的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as pompous, you mean that they behave or speak in a very serious way because they think they are more important than they really are.

words.tr: adj. 教皇的；武断的；傲慢的
words.ex: He wore a pontifical robe during the ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他在仪式上穿了一件教皇式的长袍。
words.en: Relating to the Pope or to the office or authority of the Pope; having the pomp or dignity associated with high ecclesiastical office.

words.tr: v. 用喙整理羽毛；精心打扮；感觉良好
words.ex: The bird preens its feathers every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟每天早上梳理它的羽毛。
words.en: If a bird preens or preens itself, it cleans and arranges its feathers using its beak.

words.tr: n. 自命不凡；自称；标榜；虚荣
words.ex: His pretension made others think he was better than them.
words.ex_cn: 他的自命不凡让别人觉得他比他们强。
words.en: If you say that someone has pretensions, you mean that they claim or pretend that they are more important, intelligent, or skilled than they really are.

words.tr: adj. 自命不凡的；自负的；矫饰的
words.ex: He wore a fancy hat to seem pretentious.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶华丽的帽子，显得自命不凡。
words.en: If you describe something as pretentious, you mean that it is intended to seem important or significant, but you think it is not.

words.tr: v. 打扮；装饰；精心打扮
words.ex: She spent hours primping before the big event.
words.ex_cn: 她在重大活动前花了几个小时精心打扮。
words.en: To spend time making small adjustments to one's appearance, especially in front of a mirror.

words.tr: adj. 自私的；固执己见的；过于专注自身利益的
words.ex: He is self-absorbed and never listens to others.
words.ex_cn: 他很自私，从不听别人说话。
words.en: Someone who is self-absorbed thinks so much about themselves and their own interests that they do not notice other people or their problems.

words.tr: adj. 自鸣得意的；沾沾自喜的
words.ex: He smiled in a smug way after winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 他在赢得比赛后得意地笑了。
words.en: If you say that someone is smug, you are criticizing the fact they seem very pleased with how good, clever, or lucky they are.

words.tr: adj. 傲慢的；目空一切的；自大的
words.ex: He gave a supercilious smile when she asked a simple question.
words.ex_cn: 当她问了一个简单的问题时，他露出了傲慢的微笑。
words.en: If you say that someone is supercilious, you disapprove of them because they behave in a way that shows they think they are better than other people.

words.tr: n. 无道德原则；不诚实；不公正；无耻
words.ex: His unscrupulousness in business dealings led to his downfall.
words.ex_cn: 他在商业交易中的不择手段导致了他最终的失败。
words.en: The quality of being unscrupulous; lack of moral principles.

words.tr:
v. 使相形见绌；抢…的风头
adv. 在（或向）舞台后部
words.ex: She tried to upstage her co-star by wearing a more extravagant gown.
words.ex_cn: 她试图通过穿一件更华丽的礼服来抢走她搭档的风头。
words.en: If someone upstages you, they draw attention away from you by being more attractive or interesting.

words.tr: adj. 徒劳的；空虚的；自负的；爱慕虚荣的
words.ex: It's vain to try to fix what can't be fixed.
words.ex_cn: 试图修复无法修复的东西是徒劳的。
words.en: If you describe someone as vain, you are critical of their extreme pride in their own beauty, intelligence, or other good qualities.

chapters.name: Word List 29 负向评价 卑鄙

words.tr: adj. 徒劳的；空虚的；自负的；爱慕虚荣的
words.ex: It's vain to try to fix what can't be fixed.
words.ex_cn: 试图修复无法修复的东西是徒劳的。
words.en: If you describe someone as vain, you are critical of their extreme pride in their own beauty, intelligence, or other good qualities.

words.tr: adj. 平民的；卑贱的；卑鄙的；不光彩的
words.ex: He came from an ignoble family, but worked hard to succeed.
words.ex_cn: 他出身于平民家庭，但努力工作以取得成功。
words.en: If you describe something as ignoble, you mean that it is bad and something to be ashamed of.

words.tr: adj. 耻辱的；不名誉的；不光彩的
words.ex: He faced an ignominious defeat in the election.
words.ex_cn: 他在选举中遭遇了耻辱的失败。
words.en: If you describe an experience or action as ignominious, you mean it is embarrassing because it shows a great lack of success.

words.ex: Old sailors often got scurvy from lack of fresh fruit.
words.ex_cn: 老水手因缺乏新鲜水果而患上坏血病。
words.en: A disease caused by a deficiency of vitamin C, characterized by spongy and bleeding gums, bleeding under the skin, and extreme weakness.

words.ex: He made a sneaky move to take the cookie without being seen.
words.ex_cn: 他偷偷摸摸地拿走了饼干，没被人发现。
words.en: If you describe someone as sneaky, you disapprove of them because they do things secretly rather than openly.

words.tr: adj. 暗中的；卑劣的；人手不足的
words.ex: He was accused of using underhanded tactics to win the election.
words.ex_cn: 他被指控在选举中使用卑劣手段获胜。
words.en: If you describe someone's actions as underhanded, you are criticizing them because they are secret and dishonest.

words.tr: adj. 糟糕透顶的；恶劣的；卑鄙的
words.ex: He said a vile thing to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友说了句卑鄙的话。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is vile, you mean that they are extremely unpleasant.

words.tr: v. 行为不端；行为无礼貌
words.ex: The boy misbehaved in class.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩在课堂上行为不端。
words.en: If someone, especially a child, misbehaves, they behave in a way that is not acceptable to other people.

chapters.name: Word List 29 负向评价 卑贱

words.ex: He abased himself before the king.
words.ex_cn: 他在国王面前贬低自己。
words.en: To abase someone or something means to lower them in rank, status, or esteem.

words.ex: The refugees lived in abject poverty.
words.ex_cn: 这些难民过着凄惨的贫困生活。
words.en: Abject means extremely bad, unpleasant, and degrading.

words.ex: The currish dog barked at strangers.
words.ex_cn: 这只凶恶的狗对陌生人吠叫。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as currish, you mean that it is mean-spirited or dishonorable.

words.ex: The dog grovelled on the ground to beg for food.
words.ex_cn: 狗趴在地上乞求食物。
words.en: If you grovel, you behave in a very submissive way in order to show that you are sorry for something wrong that you have done or to try to get someone to forgive you or do something for you.

words.tr: adj. 羞愧的；卑躬屈膝的
words.ex: He looked hangdog after losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 输掉比赛后，他一副垂头丧气的样子。
words.en: If someone has a hangdog expression, they look sad, ashamed, or guilty.

words.tr: adj. 卑微的；谦逊的；虚心的；
words.ex: He lived in a humble house near the river.
words.ex_cn: 他住在河边一座简陋的房子里。
words.en: If you describe someone as humble, you mean that they do not think they are better or more important than other people.

words.ex: This product is inferior to the other one.
words.ex_cn: 这个产品比另一个差。
words.en: If one person or thing is inferior to another, they are not as good, important, or valuable as the other person or thing.

words.tr:
v. 意思；导致；打算；
n. 平均数；
adj. 低劣；平均；
words.ex: What does this word mean?
words.ex_cn: 这个词是什么意思？
words.en: If you want to know what a word, a sentence, or an expression means, you want to know what it refers to or what its significance is.

words.tr:
adj. 行乞的
n. 乞丐
words.ex: The mendicant monks wandered the streets, seeking alms.
words.ex_cn: 托钵僧在街上徘徊，寻求施舍。
words.en: A mendicant is someone who lives by asking people for money or food, especially as a member of a religious group that does this as a way of life.

words.ex: The abolition of serfdom in Russia was a significant social change.
words.ex_cn: 俄罗斯废除农奴制是一个重大的社会变革。
words.en: Serfdom is the status of peasants under feudalism, specifically relating to manorialism. It was a condition of bondage or modified slavery which developed primarily during the High Middle Ages in Europe and lasted in some countries until the mid-19th century.

words.tr: adj. 屈从的；奴隶的；逢迎的
words.ex: He gave a servile answer to his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他向老板给出了卑躬屈膝的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone as servile, you disapprove of them because they are too eager to obey someone or do things for them.

chapters.name: Word List 29 负向评价 残忍

words.tr: adj. 虐待狂的；残酷成性的
words.ex: The sadistic man laughed when the dog cried.
words.ex_cn: 那个残忍的人当狗叫时笑了。
words.en: Deriving pleasure from inflicting pain, suffering, or humiliation on others.

words.ex: The movie shows the brutality of war.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了战争的残忍。
words.en: Brutality is cruel and violent behavior, or a cruel and violent act.

words.ex: Some ancient tribes practiced cannibalism in rituals.
words.ex_cn: 一些古代部落在仪式中实行同类相食。
words.en: Cannibalism is the practice of eating the flesh of one's own species.

words.tr: adj. 残暴的；恶劣的；糟透的
words.ex: The dictator committed atrocious acts against his people.
words.ex_cn: 这位独裁者对人民犯下了残暴的罪行。
words.en: If you describe something as atrocious, you are emphasizing that its quality is very bad.

words.ex: The war caused many atrocities.
words.ex_cn: 战争造成了许多暴行。
words.en: An atrocity is a very cruel, shocking, and morally unacceptable act.

words.ex: The barbarous act shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这野蛮的行为震惊了所有人。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as barbarous, you mean that it is extremely cruel or uncivilized.

words.tr: adj. 野兽的；野兽般的；极残忍的
words.ex: The bestial treatment of the prisoners shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 对囚犯的兽性对待震惊了所有人。
words.en: If you describe behavior or a situation as bestial, you mean that it is very unpleasant or disgusting.

words.ex: The storm caused a brutal flood that destroyed many homes.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴引发了残酷的洪水，摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: A brutal act or person is cruel and violent.

words.ex: He gave a brute answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了粗暴的回答。
words.en: A brute is a person who is cruel and violent.

words.tr: adj. 铁石心肠的；无情的；起老茧的
words.ex: He was callous to his friend's pain.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的痛苦无动于衷。
words.en: A callous person or action is very cruel and shows no concern for other people or their feelings.

words.ex: Snakes are cold-blooded animals.
words.ex_cn: 蛇是冷血动物。
words.en: If you describe someone as cold-blooded, you mean that they are cruel and unfeeling.

words.ex: The feral cat lives in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 这只野生的猫生活在森林里。
words.en: A feral animal is a domestic animal that has returned to the wild, or is the offspring of such animals, and is not socialized to humans.

words.ex: The ferocious wind knocked down the tree.
words.ex_cn: 强烈的风把树吹倒了。
words.en: A ferocious animal or person is very fierce and violent.

words.tr: adj. 严厉的；严峻的；冷酷无情的；坚定的；可怕的
words.ex: He had a grim look on his face.
words.ex_cn: 他脸上带着严峻的表情。
words.en: If a situation or piece of news is grim, it is very serious, unpleasant, and depressing.

words.tr: adj. 粗鲁的；生硬的；粗哑的
words.ex: The old man gave a gruff answer.
words.ex_cn: 老人粗声粗气地回答了。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as gruff, you mean that they seem rather unfriendly or bad-tempered.

words.ex: The prison conditions were inhumane.
words.ex_cn: 监狱的条件是不人道的。
words.en: If you describe something as inhumane, you mean that it is extremely cruel.

words.ex: The unfair verdict caused public outrage.
words.ex_cn: 不公正的判决引发了公众的愤怒。
words.en: An outrage is an extremely strong reaction of anger, shock, or indignation.

words.tr: adj. 冷酷的；无情的；无怜悯心的
words.ex: The pitiless wind blew all night.
words.ex_cn: 无情的风刮了一整夜。
words.en: If you describe someone as pitiless, you mean that they are very cruel and have no pity for anyone.

words.ex: The relentless rain flooded the streets.
words.ex_cn: 无情的雨水淹没了街道。
words.en: Someone who is relentless is determined to do something and refuses to give up, even if what they are doing is unpleasant or cruel.

words.tr: adj. 暴乱的；吵闹的；欢腾的；放纵不羁的
words.ex: The riotous crowd broke windows and set fires.
words.ex_cn: 暴乱的人群砸碎了窗户并放火。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as riotous, you mean that it is noisy and lively in a rather wild way.

words.tr:
adj. 吵闹的；粗暴的
n. 凶暴的人；无赖
words.ex: The rowdy kids made noise in the library.
words.ex_cn: 那些吵闹的孩子在图书馆里制造噪音。
words.en: If you describe someone as rowdy, you mean that they are noisy, rough, and likely to cause trouble.

words.ex: His ruthlessness made him a successful but feared leader.
words.ex_cn: 他的无情使他成为一个成功但令人畏惧的领导者。
words.en: The quality of being cruel and without pity; mercilessness.

words.tr: adj. 撒旦的；恶魔的；邪恶的
words.ex: The movie had satanic symbols in the scenes.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的场景中有一些撒旦的符号。
words.en: If you describe something as satanic, you mean that it is extremely evil or wicked.

words.ex: The savage wolf howled under the moon.
words.ex_cn: 那头野性的狼在月光下嚎叫。
words.en: A savage person or animal is very fierce and violent.

words.tr: adj. 严重的；严厉的；非常困难的；
words.ex: The storm caused severe damage to the houses.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴对房屋造成了严重的破坏。
words.en: If something is severe, it is very bad or very serious.

words.tr: adj. 好战凶猛的；寻衅的；言词刻毒的
words.ex: He gave a truculent reply to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了好斗的答复。
words.en: If you say that someone is truculent, you mean that they are bad-tempered and aggressive.

words.tr: adj. 狂暴的；骚动的；动荡的；汹涌的
words.ex: The turbulent sea made the boat shake.
words.ex_cn: 汹涌的海让船摇晃。
words.en: A turbulent situation, time, or relationship is one in which there is a lot of change, confusion, and often conflict.

words.ex: He gave a vicious smile before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他离开前露出一个恶毒的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as vicious, you mean that they are violent and cruel, or that they are intended to cause someone great harm or suffering.

words.ex: The lion showed ferocity when it hunted.
words.ex_cn: 狮子在捕猎时表现出凶猛。
words.en: Ferocity refers to the state or quality of being ferocious, which means savagely fierce, cruel, or violent.

chapters.name: Word List 29 负向评价 草率

words.tr: adj. 半熟的；未完成的；不完整的
words.ex: His half-baked idea failed at once.
words.ex_cn: 他那不成熟的想法立刻失败了。
words.en: If you describe an idea or plan as half-baked, you mean that it has not been properly thought out, and so is stupid or impractical.

words.tr: adj. 马虎的；敷衍了事的
words.ex: He gave a slipshod answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个敷衍的回答。
words.en: If something is slipshod, it is done in a careless or lazy way, without attention to detail.

words.ex: He made an abrupt stop at the red light.
words.ex_cn: 他在红灯前突然停了下来。
words.en: If something happens abruptly, it happens suddenly and unexpectedly.

words.tr:
adj. 向外弯曲的；罗圈的
n. 简化式曲棍球
v. 把（球）打来打去；来回摆弄；交换；议论
words.ex: He has a bandy leg from playing football for years.
words.ex_cn: 他因为多年踢足球而有一条罗圈腿。
words.en: If you bandy words with someone, you argue or quarrel with them in an aggressive or unpleasant way.

words.tr: adj. 粗鲁的；莽撞的；唐突的
words.ex: He gave a brusque answer and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁地回答了一句，然后走开了。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as brusque, you mean that they deal with or say things quickly and shortly, so that they seem to be rude.

words.tr: n. 强迫；强制；难以抗拒的冲动
words.ex: He felt a compulsion to check the door again.
words.ex_cn: 他感到一种必须再次检查门的强迫感。
words.en: A compulsion is a very strong desire to do something, which you find difficult to control.

words.tr: adj. 匆匆的；粗略的；仓促的
words.ex: He gave the report a cursory look.
words.ex_cn: 他粗略地看了看这份报告。
words.en: A cursory glance or examination is a quick one that is not very thorough.

words.tr: adj. 简短而失礼的；唐突的
words.ex: He gave a curt reply and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他简短地回答了一句，然后走开了。
words.en: If someone is curt, they speak in a brief and rather rude way.

words.tr: adj. 爱开玩笑的；乱引人发笑的
words.ex: He gave a facetious answer when asked about his age.
words.ex_cn: 当被问到年龄时，他给出了一个开玩笑的回答。
words.en: If you say that someone is being facetious, you are criticizing them because they are making humorous remarks or saying things that they do not mean in a situation where they ought to be serious.

words.tr: adj. 轻率的；轻浮的；不严肃的
words.ex: His flippant remarks annoyed everyone at the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他轻率的言论让会议上的每个人都感到恼火。
words.en: If you describe a person or what they say as flippant, you are criticizing them because you think they are not taking something as seriously as they should.

words.tr:
adv. 向前；前进；
v. 促进；转交；
adj. 向前的；前进的；
words.ex: He walked forward to meet the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他向前走去见老师。
words.en: If you move or look forward, you move or look in a direction that is in front of you. In British English, you can also say that you are looking forward to something that is going to happen.

words.ex: He ignored the frivolous complaint and focused on the real issue.
words.ex_cn: 他忽略了这个无关紧要的投诉，专注于真正的问题。
words.en: If you describe someone as frivolous, you mean they behave in a silly or light-hearted way, rather than being serious and sensible.

words.tr: adj. 使人晕眩的；头晕的；轻浮的
words.ex: She felt giddy after spinning around.
words.ex_cn: 她转圈后感到头晕目眩。
words.en: If you feel giddy, you feel unsteady and think that you are about to fall over, usually because you are not well or because you are excited or frightened.

words.tr:
adv. 头向前地；倒栽葱地；急速地；鲁莽地
adj. 头向前的；倒栽葱的；急速的；急骤的
words.ex: He jumped headlong into the pool.
words.ex_cn: 他头向前地跳进了泳池。
words.en: If you move headlong in a particular direction, you move there very quickly and without thinking carefully about what you are doing.

words.ex: He made an impetuous decision to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他冲动地决定辞去工作。
words.en: If you describe someone as impetuous, you mean that they are likely to act quickly and suddenly without thinking or being careful.

words.tr: adj. 鲁莽的；厚颜的；冒失的；放肆无礼的
words.ex: The impudent boy talked back to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 这个鲁莽的男孩顶撞了老师。
words.en: If you describe someone as impudent, you mean they are rude or disrespectful, or they show a lack of shame about their behavior.

words.ex: He acted on impulse and bought the car.
words.ex_cn: 他一时冲动买了那辆车。
words.en: An impulse is a sudden strong desire to do something without thinking about the consequences.

words.tr: adj. 凭冲动行事的；易冲动的
words.ex: He made an impulsive decision to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他一时冲动决定辞掉工作。
words.en: If you describe someone as impulsive, you mean that they do things suddenly without thinking about them carefully first.

words.ex: His joke brought some levity to the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他的笑话为会议带来了一些轻松气氛。
words.en: Levity refers to a lack of seriousness, especially at an inappropriate time, often characterized by frivolity or lightness of manner.

words.ex: The address is 720 liberty street.
words.ex_cn: 地址是自由大街720号。
words.en: The state of being free within society from oppressive restrictions imposed by authority on one's way of life, behavior, or political views.

words.tr: adj. 未受过好教育的；粗野的
words.ex: He was rude and lowbred at the dinner party.
words.ex_cn: 他在晚宴上粗鲁且低俗。
words.en: If you describe someone as lowbred, you mean that they are rude, vulgar, or ill-mannered.

words.ex: He gave a perfunctory nod and left.
words.ex_cn: 他敷衍地点了点头，然后离开了。
words.en: If you describe something that is done as perfunctory, you mean that it is done as a duty or a formality, without much care or interest.

words.tr:
v. 加速（坏事的发生）
n. 沉淀物；冷凝物
adj. 轻率的；仓促的
words.ex: The scandal precipitated the politician's resignation.
words.ex_cn: 这起丑闻加速了这位政治家的辞职。
words.en: To cause something to happen suddenly or unexpectedly; to cause a substance to be deposited in solid form from a solution.

words.tr: adj. 轻佻的；不可靠的；易惊慌的
words.ex: The horse is skittish around loud noises.
words.ex_cn: 这匹马对大声响很敏感。
words.en: If you describe a person or animal as skittish, you mean they are easily frightened or nervous.

words.ex: He showed great temerity by challenging the expert without any preparation.
words.ex_cn: 他没有做任何准备就挑战专家，显得非常鲁莽。
words.en: If you say that someone has the temerity to do something, you are annoyed about something they have done which you think took a lot of nerve.

words.ex: He tried to gloss over his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他试图掩饰自己的错误。
words.en: To gloss over something means to treat or describe it in a way that fails to acknowledge its importance or complexity, often in order to avoid dealing with it directly.

words.tr: n. 不慎重；轻率；言行失检
words.ex: His indiscretion caused a big problem at work.
words.ex_cn: 他的轻率行为在工作中引起了大问题。
words.en: Indiscretion refers to behavior or speech that is not discreet; it can also mean a lack of good judgment or care in what one says or does.

chapters.name: Word List 29 负向评价 蠢、笨、傻

words.ex: His asinine remark made everyone laugh nervously.
words.ex_cn: 他那愚蠢的言论让所有人都尴尬地笑了。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as asinine, you mean that they are very foolish.

words.ex: He felt awkward when he forgot his friend's name.
words.ex_cn: 当他忘记朋友的名字时，他感到很尴尬。
words.en: If you describe a situation as awkward, you mean that it is embarrassing or difficult to deal with.

words.tr:
n. 愚蠢的错误；失误
v. 犯愚蠢的错误；失误；跌跌撞撞地走
words.ex: He made a big blunder in the math test.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学考试中犯了一个大错误。
words.en: A blunder is a stupid or careless mistake.

words.tr:
n. 笨活；拙劣的工作
v. 做事拙劣；把…搞糟
words.ex: He did a botch on the painting, leaving it messy.
words.ex_cn: 他把这幅画搞成了个笨活，弄得一团糟。
words.en: If you botch something that you are doing, you do it badly or clumsily.

words.tr:
adj. 牛的；似牛的；迟钝的
n. 牛；牛科动物
words.ex: The bovine grazed quietly in the field.
words.ex_cn: 那头牛在田野里安静地吃草。
words.en: Relating to or resembling cattle; slow or dull in manner.

words.tr: v. 笨拙地弄糟；笨手笨脚地走动；语无伦次
words.ex: He bumbled the presentation and forgot his lines.
words.ex_cn: 他笨拙地搞砸了演讲，忘记了台词。
words.en: To bumble is to move or act in an awkward or confused manner, often making mistakes or being inefficient.

words.ex: He is clumsy and dropped the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他很笨拙，把玻璃杯打翻了。
words.en: A clumsy person moves or handles things in a careless, awkward way, often so that things are knocked over or broken.

words.ex: His crass joke made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他愚蠢的笑话让每个人都感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as crass, you mean they are so stupid and insensitive that they offend you.

words.tr: adj. 愚笨的；癫狂的；痴傻的
words.ex: He wore a daft hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶傻气的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as daft, you mean that they are silly, foolish, or crazy.

words.ex: In his dotage, he forgot his own name.
words.ex_cn: 在他年老糊涂时，他忘记了自己名字。
words.en: Dotage is the period of life in which a person is old and weak, often used to describe a state of being overly fond or foolishly affectionate due to old age.

words.ex: She dotes on her little grandson.
words.ex_cn: 她非常疼爱她的孙子。
words.en: If you say that someone dotes on a person or a thing, you mean that they love or care about them very much and spend a lot of time with them.

words.tr: adj. 阴暗的；枯燥的；无趣的；
words.ex: The room was dull because the windows were covered.
words.ex_cn: 房间很阴暗，因为窗户被遮住了。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as dull, you mean they are not interesting or exciting.

words.ex: His fatuity made everyone laugh at him.
words.ex_cn: 他的愚蠢让大家都笑话他。
words.en: The quality of being fatuous; complacent stupidity.

words.tr: adj. 愚昧的；昏庸的；愚笨的
words.ex: His fatuous smile made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他那愚蠢的微笑让每个人都感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe a person, action, or remark as fatuous, you mean that they are extremely silly, showing a lack of intelligence or thought.

words.ex: His folly led to the loss of his job.
words.ex_cn: 他的愚蠢导致他丢了工作。
words.en: If you say that a particular action or way of behaving is folly, you mean that it is foolish.

words.tr:
n. 油炸馅饼
v. 挥霍；浪费
words.ex: He frittered away his inheritance on gambling.
words.ex_cn: 他把继承来的遗产挥霍在赌博上。
words.en: If someone fritters away time or money, they waste it on unimportant or unnecessary things.

words.tr:
v. 乱摸；摸索；笨手笨脚地做
n. 摸索；笨手笨脚
words.ex: He fumbled for his keys in the dark.
words.ex_cn: 他在黑暗中乱摸着找钥匙。
words.en: If you fumble with something, you try to hold, move, or find it with your hands in a clumsy way.

words.tr: adj. 不善交际的；不圆滑的；笨拙的
words.ex: He made a gauche comment at the dinner party.
words.ex_cn: 他在晚宴上说了个笨拙的评论。
words.en: If you describe someone as gauche, you mean that they are awkward and uncomfortable in the company of other people, especially because they lack social skills.

words.ex: His gaucherie made him awkward at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他的笨拙让他在聚会上显得很尴尬。
words.en: Gaucherie refers to a lack of grace or social awkwardness.

words.ex: The teacher's heavy-handedness made students afraid to speak.
words.ex_cn: 老师专横的做法让学生们不敢说话。
words.en: The quality of being clumsy or lacking subtlety, especially in the use of force or authority.

words.ex: He gave a ham-handed hug that made her uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他给了一个笨拙的拥抱，让她感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe someone as ham-handed, you mean they are clumsy or tactless in the way they do things.

words.tr: adj. 无知的；缺乏知识的
words.ex: He was ignorant of the basic rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对基本规则一无所知。
words.en: If you describe someone as ignorant, you mean that they do not know things they should know. If someone is ignorant of a fact, they do not know it.

words.tr:
adj. 文盲的；无知的；
n. 文盲；无知识的人；
words.ex: He is illiterate and cannot read simple signs.
words.ex_cn: 他是文盲，无法阅读简单的标识。
words.en: Someone who is illiterate cannot read or write.

words.ex: The inert gas does not react with other elements.
words.ex_cn: 这种惰性气体不与其他元素发生反应。
words.en: If someone or something is inert, they are not moving or reacting in any way.

words.tr: v. 使冲昏头脑；弄糊涂；使着迷
words.ex: He is infatuated with his new classmate.
words.ex_cn: 他迷上了他的新同学。
words.en: To inspire with a foolish or extravagant love or admiration.

words.tr: adj. 无光泽的；暗淡的；无生气的；乏善可陈的
words.ex: The paint on the car looked lackluster after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴过后，车漆显得暗淡无光。
words.en: If you describe something as lackluster, you mean that it is not exciting or not very good quality.

words.ex: He felt lethargy after eating too much junk food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃完太多垃圾食品后感到无精打采。
words.en: Lethargy is the condition or state of being lethargic; sluggishness, drowsiness, or apathy.

words.tr:
adj. 笨拙的；不机敏的；笨手笨脚的
n. 一个笨拙愚蠢的人
words.ex: He was maladroit when he dropped the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他不小心把玻璃杯打翻了。
words.en: If you describe someone as maladroit, you mean that they are clumsy or awkward, especially in social situations.

words.tr: adj. 模糊不清的；迷糊的；头脑发昏的
words.ex: The instructions were muzzy and hard to understand.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明模糊不清，难以理解。
words.en: If someone is muzzy, they are confused and unable to think clearly, often because they are tired or have drunk too much alcohol.

words.tr:
adj. 麻木的；失去知觉的
v. 使麻木；使迟钝
words.ex: His fingers felt numb after being in the cold.
words.ex_cn: 他的手指在寒冷中变得麻木。
words.en: If a part of your body is numb, you cannot feel it, usually for a short time.

words.ex: He is an oafish boy who spills his food everywhere.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个笨拙的男孩，总是把食物撒得到处都是。
words.en: If you describe someone as oafish, you disapprove of their behavior because you think that it is not intelligent, skillful, or graceful.

words.tr: adj. 钝的；愚钝的；钝角的
words.ex: The angle is obtuse, so it is larger than 90 degrees.
words.ex_cn: 这个角是钝的，所以它大于90度。
words.en: If you describe someone as obtuse, you mean that they are slow to understand things.

words.ex: He is purblind and cannot see the road.
words.ex_cn: 他视力极差，看不见路。
words.en: Lacking in insight, discernment, or understanding; obtuse.

words.tr: adj. 执拗的；难驾驭的；难以治愈的
words.ex: The refractory material can withstand high temperatures.
words.ex_cn: 这种耐火材料能承受高温。
words.en: Stubbornly resistant to authority or control; difficult to melt or work; resistant to heat.

words.ex: He made an uncouth remark at dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他在晚餐时说了句粗俗的话。
words.en: If you describe a person as uncouth, you mean that their behavior is vulgar, rude, or socially unacceptable.

words.tr: adj. 未受启蒙的；不知情的；不文明的；落后的
words.ex: He was unenlightened about the new rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对新规则一无所知。
words.en: If you describe someone as unenlightened, you mean they have not been given the necessary information or education about something, and so they do not understand it properly.

words.ex: The ungainly boy tripped over his own feet.
words.ex_cn: 这个笨拙的男孩被自己的脚绊倒了。
words.en: If you describe a person, animal, or vehicle as ungainly, you mean that they look awkward or clumsy, often because they are big.

words.tr: adj. 外行的；不谙此道的；
words.ex: The uninitiated found the technical terms hard to understand.
words.ex_cn: 外行觉得这些术语很难理解。
words.en: If you describe someone as uninitiated, you mean that they have no special knowledge or experience of a particular subject or activity.

words.tr: adj. 空虚的；茫然的；空洞的
words.ex: His vacuous smile made no sense.
words.ex_cn: 他空洞的微笑毫无意义。
words.en: If you describe someone's mind or smile as vacuous, you are critical of them because they lack intelligence, understanding, or seriousness.

words.ex: He is a dolt who doesn't understand simple math.
words.ex_cn: 他是个连简单数学都不懂的傻瓜。
words.en: A dolt is a person who is not very intelligent and who often makes mistakes.

words.ex: The dullard never understood the math lesson.
words.ex_cn: 这个愚笨的人从未理解过数学课。
words.en: A dullard is someone who is considered to be rather slow and not very intelligent.

words.tr: n. 愚笨的人；迟钝的学生
words.ex: The teacher called him a dunce for not doing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为他没做作业而称他为笨蛋。
words.en: A dunce is someone who is slow to learn or understand things.

words.ex: He called the man a moron for forgetting his keys.
words.ex_cn: 他因为那个人忘了带钥匙而叫他傻瓜。
words.en: A very stupid person.

words.tr: adj. 无知觉的；无感情的；无情的；愚钝的
words.ex: The insensate machine continued to operate without any human intervention.
words.ex_cn: 这台无生命的机器在没有人工干预的情况下继续运转。
words.en: If you describe someone as insensate, you mean that they lack human feelings and qualities, especially the ability to feel emotions.

words.tr: n. 精神错乱；精神失常；疯狂
words.ex: He was sent to a hospital because of insanity.
words.ex_cn: 他因精神错乱被送进了医院。
words.en: Insanity is the state of being seriously mentally ill; madness.

words.ex: The factory buys lumber to make furniture.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂购买木材来制造家具。
words.en: Lumber refers to wood that has been processed into beams and planks, a stage in the process of wood production. It is also used to describe the action of moving in a slow, heavy, awkward way.

words.tr:
v. 呆头呆脑地盯着
n. 呆子
words.ex: He just stood there gawking at the accident scene.
words.ex_cn: 他只是站在那里，呆呆地看着事故现场。
words.en: To gawk means to stare openly and stupidly.

words.ex: His maladroitness made him drop the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他的笨拙让他打翻了玻璃杯。
words.en: The quality or state of being maladroit; clumsiness.

words.tr: adj. 单纯的；自然的；不做作的
words.ex: Her artless smile made everyone feel at ease.
words.ex_cn: 她那天真的微笑让每个人都感到轻松。
words.en: If you describe someone as artless, you mean that they are simple and honest, and do not try to deceive other people.

words.tr: v. 把…打扮得俗里俗气
words.ex: She bedizened herself with gaudy jewelry.
words.ex_cn: 她用俗艳的珠宝打扮自己。
words.en: To bedizen means to dress or decorate in a showy or gaudy manner.

words.tr:
v. 猛冲；急奔；“dash”的现在分词
adj. 时髦的；冲劲足的
words.ex: He was dashing across the street when the car stopped.
words.ex_cn: 他正猛冲过马路时，车停了下来。
words.en: Someone who is dashing is very stylish and attractive.

words.tr: adj. 泥土的；粗俗的；朴实的
words.ex: The soil has an earthy smell after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后，土壤有一种泥土的气味。
words.en: Something that is earthy is simple and not complicated, and often relates to the natural world or to basic human needs and experiences.

words.tr: adj. 艳丽的；炫耀的；神气活现的
words.ex: He wears flamboyant clothes to stand out.
words.ex_cn: 他穿著華麗的衣服來引人注目。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is flamboyant, you mean that they are very noticeable, stylish, and exciting.

words.tr: adj. 浮华的；有纨绔习气的
words.ex: He wears fancy clothes and looks foppish.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着华丽的衣服，看起来很浮夸。
words.en: If you describe someone as foppish, you mean that they are very concerned about their clothes and appearance, often in a way that you think is silly or exaggerated.

words.ex: He wore fancy clothes out of foppery.
words.ex_cn: 他因为虚荣而穿得花里胡哨。
words.en: Foppery refers to the behavior, dress, or mannerisms of a fop; excessive concern with fashion and appearance.

words.ex: His daily routine is mundane and boring.
words.ex_cn: 他的日常生活平凡而无聊。
words.en: Something that is mundane is very ordinary and not at all interesting or unusual.

words.tr:
v. 引起（问题、危险等）；提出；
n. 姿势；
words.ex: Pollution can pose a serious threat to health.
words.ex_cn: 污染可能对健康造成严重威胁。
words.en: If you pose for a photograph or painting, you stay in a particular position so that someone can photograph you or paint you. / To pose a question or problem means to ask it or to present it.

words.ex: The provincial government opened a new school.
words.ex_cn: 省政府开设了一所新学校。
words.en: Relating to a province or provinces; having the manners, viewpoints, etc., considered characteristic of unsophisticated inhabitants of a province; narrow-minded.

words.tr: adj. 无赖的；低俗的；放荡不羁的
words.ex: The raffish man stole money from the old woman.
words.ex_cn: 那个无赖的男人从那位老太太那里偷了钱。
words.en: If you describe someone as raffish, you mean that they are unconventional and attractive in a way that is slightly disreputable.

words.tr: adj. 世俗的；非宗教的；长期的
words.ex: He lives a secular life without religion.
words.ex_cn: 他过着没有宗教的世俗生活。
words.en: Secular activities, attitudes, or things have no connection with religion.

words.tr:
v. 流涎；流口水；感情迸发
n. 口水
words.ex: The dog slobbered on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 狗的口水流到了地上。
words.en: If a person or animal slobbers, they let liquid fall from their mouth, often because they are hungry or excited.

words.tr: n. 恶言诽谤；粗俗的言语
words.ex: He replied with scurrility, calling names instead of arguing.
words.ex_cn: 他用污言秽语回应，而不是进行辩论。
words.en: Scurrility refers to the quality of being scurrilous, that is, using or containing coarse or vulgar language.

words.tr: adj. 似是而非的；貌似有理的
words.ex: His argument is specious and misleading.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点看似有理但具有误导性。
words.en: Something that is specious seems to be good, sound, or correct but is actually wrong or false.

words.ex: The temporal change of seasons affects our daily life.
words.ex_cn: 季节的时间变化影响我们的日常生活。
words.en: Relating to time as opposed to eternity; relating to worldly life as opposed to spiritual life.

words.tr: adj. 世界之外的；太阳系之外的；超俗的
words.ex: He dreams of ultramundane worlds beyond the sky.
words.ex_cn: 他梦想着天空之外的超凡世界。
words.en: Beyond the world or the material universe; spiritual or supernatural.

words.tr: adj. 非世俗的；不慕金钱的；不谙世故的
words.ex: He has an unworldly smile, like he doesn't understand money.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种超凡脱俗的微笑，好像不懂金钱。
words.en: If you describe someone as unworldly, you mean that they are not interested in material possessions or in gaining power or status, and they are often unaware of or indifferent to practical matters.

words.tr:
v. 拙劣地做；搞砸
n. 搞糟了的事情；失误
words.ex: He bungled the simple task.
words.ex_cn: 他把简单的任务搞砸了。
words.en: To bungle something means to do it badly or clumsily, often resulting in failure or mistakes.

words.tr: adj. 注意力分散的； v. “distract”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He was distracted by the loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 他被巨大的噪音分散了注意力。
words.en: If you are distracted, you are not able to concentrate because you are worried or thinking about something else.

words.tr: adj. 心不在焉的；精神恍惚的
words.ex: He is distrait and forgets his keys again.
words.ex_cn: 他心不在焉，又忘了钥匙。
words.en: If someone is distrait, they are distracted or absent-minded, often because they are thinking about something else.

words.tr: adj. 不热心的；心思不够的
words.ex: He gave a halfhearted apology and left.
words.ex_cn: 他敷衍地道了歉，然后离开了。
words.en: If someone is halfhearted about something, they do it without enthusiasm or energy.

words.ex: His inadvertence caused the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他的疏忽导致了错误。
words.en: The fact of not paying attention or making a mistake because you are not paying attention.

words.ex: He inadvertently dropped the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他非故意地打翻了玻璃杯。
words.en: If you do something inadvertently, you do it without realizing it, or by accident.

words.tr: n. 漫不经心； 漠不关心；无忧无虑
words.ex: He showed insouciance when the teacher scolded him.
words.ex_cn: 老师批评他时，他表现得毫不在意。
words.en: A feeling of not worrying about anything because you do not think anything bad will happen.

words.tr: adj. 漫不经心的；漠不关心的；无忧无虑的
words.ex: She wore an insouciant smile as she walked down the street.
words.ex_cn: 她走在街上，脸上挂着一副无忧无虑的微笑。
words.en: If you say that someone is insouciant, you mean that they are calm and seem not to worry or care about anything.

words.ex: His negligence caused the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他的疏忽导致了事故。
words.en: Negligence is failure to take proper care over something that you are responsible for, which might cause damage or loss.

words.ex: He perfunctorily finished his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他敷衍地完成了作业。
words.en: If you do something perfunctorily, you do it quickly and carelessly, without enthusiasm or attention to detail.

words.ex: The report gave a sketchy description of the event.
words.ex_cn: 这份报告对事件的描述不完备。
words.en: If something is sketchy, it is incomplete or not detailed, and possibly unreliable.

words.tr: adj. 仓促马虎的；毛躁的；潦草的
words.ex: He gave a slapdash answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个草率的回答。
words.en: If you say that something is done in a slapdash way, you mean that it is done carelessly and quickly, without much attention to detail.

words.ex: The child plays with a toy car.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在玩一辆玩具汽车。
words.en: A toy is an object for children to play with.

words.tr: adj. 不知情的；不经意的
words.ex: He was the unwitting victim of a prank.
words.ex_cn: 他是不知情的恶作剧受害者。
words.en: If someone is unwitting, they do not know or realize something.

words.tr: adj. 疏忽的；粗心的；不在意的
words.ex: He was negligent in doing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他做作业时很疏忽。
words.en: If you say that someone is negligent, you mean that they do not take enough care over something that they are responsible for.

words.tr: adj. 莽撞的；有勇无谋的
words.ex: He made a foolhardy decision to climb the mountain alone.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了一个有勇无谋的决定，独自去爬山。
words.en: If you describe behavior or an action as foolhardy, you mean that it is very risky because it shows a lack of thought or care for the possible consequences.

words.ex: The abrasive surface wore down the metal.
words.ex_cn: 磨损的表面磨耗了金属。
words.en: An abrasive substance is rough and can be used to clean surfaces or to make them smooth by rubbing. An abrasive person is someone who is harsh and rude.

words.ex: The asperity of the terrain made the hike difficult.
words.ex_cn: 地形的粗糙使得徒步旅行变得困难。
words.en: If you say something with asperity, you say it in a harsh, severe way.

words.tr: n. 废弃物（树枝、碎石等）；
words.ex: The workers cleared the brash from the construction site.
words.ex_cn: 工人们清除了建筑工地上的废弃物。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behavior as brash, you disapprove of them because you think that they are too confident and aggressive.

words.ex: He flipped the pancake with a spatula.
words.ex_cn: 他用铲子快速翻转了煎饼。
words.en: To flip something means to turn it over quickly one or more times, or to make something do this.

words.tr: adj. 性情乖戾的；脾气暴躁的
words.ex: He is grumpy when he wakes up early.
words.ex_cn: 他早起时会脾气不好。
words.en: If you say that someone is grumpy, you mean that they are bad-tempered and miserable.

words.ex: His impertinence made the teacher angry.
words.ex_cn: 他的无礼让老师生气了。
words.en: Impertinence refers to a lack of respect or rudeness, especially towards someone who is older or in a position of authority.

words.tr: adj. 傲慢的；无礼的；侮慢的
words.ex: The insolent boy talked back to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 那个无礼的男孩顶撞了老师。
words.en: If you say that someone is insolent, you mean they are rude and do not show respect for people in positions of authority.

words.ex: He made a loutish noise at the dinner table.
words.ex_cn: 他在餐桌上发出了粗鲁的噪音。
words.en: If you describe someone as loutish, you are critical of them because they behave in an impolite or aggressive way.

words.tr: adj. 侮辱的；辱骂的；鄙俗的
words.ex: He shouted opprobrious words at the driver.
words.ex_cn: 他向司机喊出辱骂的话。
words.en: Expressing scorn or criticism; conveying disgrace or shame.

words.ex: His overbearing boss always tells him what to do.
words.ex_cn: 他专横的老板总是告诉他该做什么。
words.en: If you describe someone as overbearing, you mean that they behave in a very unpleasant way because they are too confident of their own importance.

words.tr: adj. 断然的；不容置辩的；专横的
words.ex: He gave a peremptory order to leave.
words.ex_cn: 他下达了一个不容置疑的离开命令。
words.en: If someone's manner or behavior is peremptory, they are so confident and sure of their authority that they expect to be obeyed without question.

words.tr: n. 假定；推定；冒昧；放肆
words.ex: His presumption that he would win surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他以为自己会赢的这种假设让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: A presumption is something that is thought to be true because it is likely, although there is no proof.

words.ex: His ribald jokes were inappropriate for a family gathering.
words.ex_cn: 他的下流笑话不适合家庭聚会。
words.en: If you describe someone's language or behavior as ribald, you mean that it refers to sex in a rude or humorous way.

words.tr: n. 鲁莽不顾后果；鲁莽
words.ex: His recklessness caused a car accident.
words.ex_cn: 他的鲁莽导致了一场车祸。
words.en: The quality of being reckless, which means not thinking about the possible bad effects of your actions.

words.tr: adj. 粗鲁辱骂的；恶语毁谤的；下流粗俗的
words.ex: The politician was criticized for making scurrilous remarks about his opponent.
words.ex_cn: 这位政客因对对手发表下流的言论而受到批评。
words.en: If you describe something as scurrilous, you mean that it is vulgar and intended to damage someone's reputation.

words.tr: adj. 爱咬人的；爱喝叱的；脾气暴躁的
words.ex: The dog was snappish when strangers came near.
words.ex_cn: 当陌生人靠近时，这只狗爱咬人。
words.en: If someone is snappish, they speak to people in a sharp, unfriendly way.

words.tr: adj. 脾气坏的；乖戾的；傲慢的
words.ex: The surly man refused to say hello.
words.ex_cn: 那个脾气暴躁的人拒绝打招呼。
words.en: If someone is surly, they are unfriendly and bad-tempered.

words.tr: adj. 不体面的；不相配的；不适宜的
words.ex: It is unseemly to shout in a library.
words.ex_cn: 在图书馆大喊大叫是不合适的。
words.en: If you say that someone's behaviour is unseemly, you disapprove of it because it is not appropriate in a particular situation.

words.tr: adj. 庸俗的；粗俗的；粗野的；下流的
words.ex: He used a vulgar word in class.
words.ex_cn: 他在课堂上说了一个粗俗的词。
words.en: If you describe something as vulgar, you mean that it is in bad taste or of poor quality.

words.tr:
n. 野蛮人
adj. 野蛮的
words.ex: The barbarian attacked the village with a sword.
words.ex_cn: 野蛮人用剑袭击了村庄。
words.en: A barbarian is a person who is considered to be uncivilized or uncultured.

words.tr:
adj. 鲁莽的；狂妄的；轻率的
n. 狂妄的人（尤指女子）
words.ex: The madcap boy ran through the park with no hat.
words.ex_cn: 那个疯疯癫癫的男孩没戴帽子跑过了公园。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as madcap, you mean that they are full of energy and enthusiasm, but slightly crazy or uncontrolled.

words.ex: He is unlettered and cannot read or write.
words.ex_cn: 他没受过教育，不会读写。
words.en: Someone who is unlettered has not learned to read or write.

words.tr: n. 不道德行为；不法行为；
words.ex: The company was punished for its wrongdoing.
words.ex_cn: 该公司因其不道德行为受到了惩罚。
words.en: Wrongdoing refers to behavior that is morally or legally wrong.

words.tr: adj. 鲁莽的；无礼的；不相干的
words.ex: He gave an impertinent answer to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他给了老师一个鲁莽的回答。
words.en: If someone talks or behaves in a rather impolite and disrespectful way, especially towards someone who is older or in a position of authority, you can describe that person or their behaviour as impertinent.

words.tr: adj. 粗鲁的；无礼的；脾气坏的
words.ex: His churlish behavior at the meeting was uncalled for.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上的粗鲁行为是完全没有必要的。
words.en: If someone is churlish, they are rude, bad-tempered, and impolite.

words.tr: adj. 乡巴佬的；粗野的；粗鄙的
words.ex: His boorish behavior made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他粗俗的行为让所有人都感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe someone as boorish, you mean their behavior is unrefined, insensitive, or rude.

words.tr: adj. 别致的；时髦的；小巧玲珑的；活泼的；无礼的；唐突的
words.ex: She gave a pert reply to the interviewer's question.
words.ex_cn: 她对采访者的问题给出了无礼的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone as pert, you mean that they are lively and confident, and perhaps slightly disrespectful.

words.tr: v. （使）无法理解；（因吃惊）犹豫不决
words.ex: The math problem boggles my mind.
words.ex_cn: 这道数学题让我困惑不已。
words.en: If you boggle at something, you are astonished or overwhelmed by it, often because it is very complicated or large.

words.ex: The glass is brittle and breaks easily.
words.ex_cn: 这种玻璃很硬但容易碎。
words.en: If something is brittle, it is hard and easily broken.

words.tr: adj. 懦弱的；毫无志气的；
words.ex: He was craven and ran away from the fight.
words.ex_cn: 他很懦弱，逃跑了。
words.en: If you describe someone as craven, you are criticizing them for being very cowardly.

words.ex: He cringed when he heard the loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到巨大的噪音时，他畏缩了。
words.en: If you cringe at something, you feel embarrassed or disgusted, and perhaps show this feeling in your expression or by making a slight movement.

words.ex: The eerie silence made us feel scared.
words.ex_cn: 那怪异的寂静让我们感到害怕。
words.en: If you describe something as eerie, you mean that it seems strange and frightening, and makes you feel nervous.

words.ex: He was called effeminate for wearing pink.
words.ex_cn: 他因为穿粉色被说娘娘腔。
words.en: If you describe a man or his behaviour as effeminate, you mean that he behaves, looks, or sounds like a woman or girl.

words.ex: He felt emasculated after losing the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在辩论失败后感到失去了男子气概。
words.en: To emasculate someone or something means to make them weaker or less effective.

words.ex: He is too faint-hearted to speak in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他太胆小了，不敢在全班面前说话。
words.en: Lacking courage or determination; timid.

words.ex: He has flabby arms from not exercising.
words.ex_cn: 他因为不锻炼，手臂松软。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as flabby, you are criticizing them for being soft and loose rather than firm and strong.

words.tr: adj. 松弛的；软弱的；无活力的
words.ex: The leaves looked flaccid after the long dry spell.
words.ex_cn: 长时间干旱后，树叶看起来软弱无力。
words.en: Lacking firmness, resilience, or muscle tone; soft and limp.

words.tr:
adj. 轻而薄的；易坏的；不足信的
n. 复写纸；薄纸副本
words.ex: The flimsy chair broke when he sat on it.
words.ex_cn: 那把脆弱的椅子当他坐上去时就断了。
words.en: Something that is flimsy is not very strong or solid, and therefore easily damaged or destroyed.

words.ex: He didn't flinch when the needle touched his skin.
words.ex_cn: 当针碰到他的皮肤时，他没有退缩。
words.en: If you flinch, you make a small sudden movement, especially when something surprises you or hurts you.

words.ex: The old man is frail and needs help to walk.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人瘦弱，需要帮助才能走路。
words.en: Someone who is frail is not very strong or healthy.

words.tr: adj. 缺乏勇气的；怯懦的
words.ex: He was gutless and refused to speak up.
words.ex_cn: 他很懦弱，不敢站出来说话。
words.en: If you describe someone as gutless, you think they have a weak character and lack courage or determination.

words.tr:
v. 跛行；蹒跚；瘸着走
adj. 无力的；无生气的
words.ex: He limps after hurting his leg.
words.ex_cn: 他受伤后走路一瘸一拐。
words.en: If someone limps, they walk with difficulty or in an uneven way because one of their legs or feet is hurt.

words.ex: His pusillanimous behavior in the face of danger was disappointing.
words.ex_cn: 他在危险面前的懦弱行为令人失望。
words.en: If you say that someone is pusillanimous, you mean that they are timid or afraid, especially in a way that you find irritating or disappointing.

words.tr:
n. 鹌鹑；鹌鹑肉 
v. 畏缩；胆怯
words.ex: The farmer raised quail for their eggs.
words.ex_cn: 农夫饲养鹌鹑来获取它们的蛋。
words.en: If someone quails, they feel or show fear or hesitation.

words.tr: adj. 无脊椎的；没有骨气的；怯懦的
words.ex: The worm is a spineless creature.
words.ex_cn: 这条蠕虫是一种无脊椎动物。
words.en: If you describe someone as spineless, you mean that they are afraid to take action or lack determination.

words.tr: adj. 无脊椎的；没有骨气的；怯懦的
words.ex: The worm is a spineless creature.
words.ex_cn: 这条蠕虫是一种无脊椎动物。
words.en: If you describe someone as spineless, you mean that they are afraid to take action or lack determination.

words.tr: adj. 充满智慧的；明智的；英明的；
words.ex: The wise old man gave good advice.
words.ex_cn: 这位充满智慧的老人给出了很好的建议。
words.en: If you describe someone as wise, you mean that they have experience, knowledge, and good judgment.

words.ex: The maleficent storm destroyed many homes.
words.ex_cn: 这场有害的风暴摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: Causing harm or destruction, especially by supernatural means.

words.ex: The enormity of the crime shocked the whole city.
words.ex_cn: 这桩罪行的极恶震惊了整个城市。
words.en: If you refer to the enormity of something that you consider to be a problem or difficulty, you are referring to its very great size, extent, or seriousness.

words.ex: The party turned into a wild bacchanal.
words.ex_cn: 派对变成了一场狂野的狂欢。
words.en: A bacchanal is a wild and drunken celebration or party, often associated with the Roman festival of Bacchus, the god of wine.

words.ex: His humor makes everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他的幽默让大家都笑了。
words.en: The quality of being amusing or comic, especially as expressed in literature or speech.

words.ex: Parents shouldn't indulge their children's bad habits.
words.ex_cn: 父母不应该放任孩子的坏习惯。
words.en: To indulge means to allow yourself or someone else to have something enjoyable, especially more than is good for you.

words.ex: He got a driver's license last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周拿到了驾照。
words.en: A license is an official document which gives you permission to do, use, or own something.

words.tr: adj. 无辔头的；不受控制的；放纵的
words.ex: The unbridled horse ran across the field.
words.ex_cn: 那匹无辔头的马在田野上奔跑。
words.en: If you describe behaviour or feelings as unbridled, you mean that they are not controlled or limited in any way.

words.ex: The wanton destruction of the forest shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 对森林的恣意破坏让每个人都感到震惊。
words.en: If someone describes a person or their behaviour as wanton, they are critical of them for behaving in a very uncontrolled or unacceptable way, often without caring about the consequences.

words.ex: The party turned into an orgy of drinking and dancing.
words.ex_cn: 派对变成了饮酒跳舞的狂欢。
words.en: An orgy is a wild party or gathering where people behave in an unrestrained way, often involving excessive drinking, eating, or sexual activity.

words.tr: adj. 纵容的；宽厚的；溺爱的
words.ex: Her parents are indulgent and let her stay up late.
words.ex_cn: 她的父母很纵容，让她熬夜。
words.en: If you are indulgent, you treat someone with special kindness, often in a way that is not good for them.

words.tr: adj. 放纵的；无节制的；过度的
words.ex: His intemperate lifestyle led to numerous health problems.
words.ex_cn: 他放纵的生活方式导致了许多健康问题。
words.en: If you describe someone's words or behaviour as intemperate, you are critical of them because they are too extreme and uncontrolled.

words.ex: The old roue drank wine every night.
words.ex_cn: 那个老色鬼每晚都喝酒。
words.en: A man who leads a life of debauchery; a rake.

words.tr: adj. 放肆的；冒昧的；自以为是的
words.ex: He was presumptuous to ask for a raise after just one week.
words.ex_cn: 他才工作一周就要求加薪，太自以为是了。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behavior as presumptuous, you disapprove of them because they are doing something that they have no right or authority to do.

words.tr: adj. 淫秽的；败坏风俗的
words.ex: The play contains some bawdy jokes that are not suitable for children.
words.ex_cn: 这出戏包含一些不适合儿童的猥亵笑话。
words.en: Bawdy humor or language refers to jokes or remarks about sex in a way that some people find offensive.

words.ex: His libido seemed to have diminished with age.
words.ex_cn: 随着年龄的增长，他的性欲似乎有所减弱。
words.en: Libido is a person's sexual desire or energy, especially when considered as a basic life force.

words.ex: He gave a licentious speech at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上发表了一篇放荡不羁的演讲。
words.en: If you describe a person as licentious, you mean that they are very immoral in their sexual behavior.

words.tr:
n. 强烈的性欲；强烈的欲望
v. 对…有极强的性欲（或欲望）
words.ex: His lust for power ruined his relationships.
words.ex_cn: 他对权力的强烈欲望毁掉了他的关系。
words.en: Lust is a strong feeling of wanting to have or to do something, especially sexual desire.

words.tr: adj. 放荡的；肆无忌惮的；潇洒的
words.ex: He wore a rakish hat at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上戴了一顶歪斜的帽子。
words.en: If you describe someone as rakish, you mean that they are stylish and confident in a way that is slightly unconventional and possibly a little disreputable.

words.tr: adj. 感官的；肉欲的；愉悦感官的；耽于肉欲的
words.ex: The sensual smell of fresh bread made her hungry.
words.ex_cn: 新鲜面包的感官香味让她感到饥饿。
words.en: Relating to or involving gratification of the senses and physical, especially sexual, pleasure.

words.ex: He lives a sybaritic life with luxury cars and five-star meals.
words.ex_cn: 他过着奢侈的生活，有豪华汽车和五星级酒店的餐食。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as sybaritic, you mean that they are fond of luxury and pleasure.

words.tr: adj. 激起性欲的；满足感官的；撩人的
words.ex: The painting showed a voluptuous woman with flowing curves.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画描绘了一位身材性感、曲线优美的女人。
words.en: If you describe a woman as voluptuous, you mean that she has large breasts and hips and is considered sexually attractive.

words.tr: adj. 性欲的；性爱的；色情的
words.ex: The movie contains erotic scenes that are not suitable for children.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影包含不适合儿童的色情场景。
words.en: Relating to or tending to arouse sexual desire or excitement.

words.tr: adj. 肉体的；肉欲的；性欲的
words.ex: He denied any carnal desires.
words.ex_cn: 他否认有任何肉体的欲望。
words.en: Carnal is used to describe things relating to the body or to sexual desires, often in contrast to spiritual or intellectual matters.

words.ex: He used artifice to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他用诡计赢得了比赛。
words.en: Clever or cunning devices or expedients, especially as used to trick or deceive others.

words.ex: He resorted to chicanery to win the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他依靠狡辩赢得了争论。
words.en: The use of trickery to achieve a political, financial, or legal purpose.

words.ex: The crafty fox stole the chicken at night.
words.ex_cn: 那只狡猾的狐狸在夜里偷了鸡。
words.en: If you describe someone as crafty, you mean they are clever at achieving their aims by indirect or deceitful methods.

words.tr:
adj. 狡猾的；奸诈的；巧妙的
n. 奸诈；狡猾
words.ex: The cunning fox tricked the chicken.
words.ex_cn: 那只狡猾的狐狸骗了鸡。
words.en: Someone who is cunning is clever and good at deceiving others in order to get what they want.

words.ex: He is a diplomatic ambassador who handles international relations.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位处理国际关系的外交大使。
words.en: Diplomatic means relating to diplomacy or diplomats, or using skill and tact in dealing with people.

words.tr: adj. 搞两面派的；奸诈的；骗人的
words.ex: He gave a duplicitous answer to hide the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个虚伪的回答来隐藏真相。
words.en: Someone who is duplicitous is deceitful.

words.tr: n. 奸诈；欺骗；口是心非
words.ex: He showed duplicity by lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他通过对朋友撒谎表现出虚伪。
words.en: If you accuse someone of duplicity, you mean that they are deceitful.

words.ex: The cat got enmeshed in the old net.
words.ex_cn: 猫被缠在旧网里了。
words.en: To involve someone or something in a difficult situation from which it is hard to escape.

words.tr:
n. 诡计；花言巧语
v. 欺骗；诱骗；消磨
words.ex: He used a clever wile to deceive his enemies.
words.ex_cn: 他使用了一个巧妙的诡计来欺骗他的敌人。
words.en: If you say that someone uses wiles to achieve something, you mean that they use clever methods to persuade people to do what they want.

words.tr: adj. 有智虑的；精明的；有策略的
words.ex: It was politic to stay silent during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 在会议上保持沉默是明智的。
words.en: If you describe an action or decision as politic, you mean that it is sensible and likely to achieve what you want.

words.tr:
adj. 马基雅维里式的；不择手段的
n. 不择手段的政治家
words.ex: His Machiavellian tactics won him the election.
words.ex_cn: 他那不择手段的策略帮他赢得了选举。
words.en: If you describe someone as Machiavellian, you are critical of them because they often make use of cunning, deceit, or immoral means to achieve their aims.

words.tr: adj. 酸的； 苦涩的；尖刻的
words.ex: The lemon juice had an acerbic taste.
words.ex_cn: 柠檬汁有酸味。
words.en: If you say something acerbic, or harshly bitter, you are being sharply critical or sarcastic.

words.ex: His words showed great acerbity.
words.ex_cn: 他的话表现出极大的尖刻。
words.en: Acerbity refers to a sharp bitterness or severity of temper or expression.

words.tr: adj. 辛辣的；苦涩的；刺激的；尖刻的
words.ex: The smoke from the fire had an acrid smell.
words.ex_cn: 火灾的烟雾有一种刺鼻的气味。
words.en: An acrid smell or taste is strong and sharp, and usually unpleasant. It can also describe a manner or expression that is bitter or harsh.

words.ex: Their argument was acrimonious and lasted all night.
words.ex_cn: 他们的争论很尖刻，持续了一整晚。
words.en: If you say that an argument or conversation is acrimonious, you mean that it is bitter and angry because the people involved disagree with each other.

words.tr: n. 尖刻的言辞；激烈的争吵
words.ex: There was acrimony between the two neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 两个邻居之间充满了敌意。
words.en: Bitterness or ill feeling.

words.tr:
adj. 要求严格的；要求小心仔细的；苛求的
v. 强求；急需；要求；“exact”的现在分词
words.ex: He is an exacting teacher who wants perfect work.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个要求严格的老师，要求完美无缺的作业。
words.en: requiring a lot of effort, care, or attention

words.tr: adj. 过分挑剔的；苛求的
words.ex: He is finicky about what he eats.
words.ex_cn: 他对吃的东西很挑剔。
words.en: If you say that someone is finicky, you mean that they are very difficult to please because they want everything to be exactly right.

words.tr:
v. 迅速前往；“nip”的现在分词
adj. 刺骨的
words.ex: The nipping wind made it difficult to stay warm.
words.ex_cn: 刺骨的风让人难以保持温暖。
words.en: If you describe the weather as nipping, you mean that it is very cold and biting.

words.tr: adj. 刺鼻的；一语道破的
words.ex: The cheese has a pungent smell.
words.ex_cn: 这种奶酪有刺鼻的气味。
words.en: Having a sharply strong taste or smell.

words.tr:
adj. 苛刻的；尖刻的
v. 损伤；伤害；“scathe”的现在分词
words.ex: The critic wrote a scathing review of the movie.
words.ex_cn: 评论家写了一篇尖刻的电影评论。
words.en: If you say that someone is being scathing about something, you mean that they are being very critical of it.

words.ex: The school has stringent rules about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学校对作业有严格的规定。
words.en: Stringent measures, rules, or conditions are very strict or severe.

words.tr:
adj. 酸的；辛辣的；尖酸的；刻薄的
n. 甜果馅饼；骚货；妓女
words.ex: The lemon taste is too tart.
words.ex_cn: 柠檬的味道太酸了。
words.en: If something such as fruit is tart, it has a sharp taste. If someone is tart, they are sharp or cutting in their manner or speech.

words.ex: The salad was vinegared to perfection.
words.ex_cn: 这沙拉醋腌得恰到好处。
words.en: Treated with vinegar or having the characteristics of vinegar.

words.tr: adj. 刻薄的；尖刻的；恶意的
words.ex: His vitriolic words hurt everyone in the room.
words.ex_cn: 他刻薄的话伤害了房间里所有人。
words.en: If you describe someone's language or behavior as vitriolic, you disapprove of it because it is full of bitterness and hate, and so causes a lot of distress and pain.

words.tr: adj. 带酸味的；微酸的；尖刻刻薄的
words.ex: The lemonade was acidulous and sharp.
words.ex_cn: 柠檬水酸得刺口。
words.en: Slightly sour or sharp in taste or manner.

words.tr:
v. 无所事事；闲荡
adj. 懈怠的；闲散的；不做事的
words.ex: He idles away the whole afternoon.
words.ex_cn: 他整个下午都无所事事。
words.en: If you describe someone as idle, you mean they are not doing anything or they are not working hard.

words.tr: adj. 懒惰的；懒散的；好逸恶劳的
words.ex: He is indolent and never does his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他很懒，从不做作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as indolent, you mean that they are lazy.

words.ex: His indolence at work was becoming a serious issue.
words.ex_cn: 他在工作中的懒散正成为一个严重的问题。
words.en: Indolence is the state of being lazy or not wanting to do any work.

words.tr: v. 使融合；合并；“integrate”的现在分词；
words.ex: The school is integrating art into math lessons.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校正在将艺术融入数学课程中。
words.en: To combine two or more things in order to become more effective.

words.ex: The ball keeps moving because of inertia.
words.ex_cn: 球因为惯性继续移动。
words.en: Inertia is the tendency of a physical object to continue moving in a straight line at a constant speed, or to stay at rest, unless it is acted upon by a force.

words.tr: n. 大笑；笑死我了 (used to express amusement)
words.ex: He told a funny joke and got a big lol.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了个有趣的笑话，引得大家大笑。
words.en: To laugh out loud, especially in response to something humorous.

words.ex: We waited in the lounge before our flight.
words.ex_cn: 我们在登机前等在休息室里。
words.en: A lounge is a room in a house or public building where people can sit and relax. As a verb, to lounge means to lie, sit, or stand in a relaxed or lazy way.

words.ex: The rope is slack and hangs loosely.
words.ex_cn: 绳子是松弛的，垂挂着。
words.en: If something is slack, it is loose and not firmly stretched or tightly in position. It can also describe a period of low activity or a lack of effort in work or activity.

words.ex: The sloth moves very slowly in the tree.
words.ex_cn: 树懒在树上移动得非常慢。
words.en: Sloth is a disinclination to work or exert oneself; laziness, or a slow-moving tropical American mammal that lives in trees.

words.ex: The city's sprawl has covered many farmlands.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市的杂乱无序的拓展覆盖了许多农田。
words.en: If you sprawl somewhere, you sit or lie with your legs and arms spread out in a careless way.

words.ex: He lay supine on the couch, staring at the ceiling.
words.ex_cn: 他仰卧在沙发上，盯着天花板。
words.en: If you are supine, you are lying on your back. It can also describe someone who is passive or not willing to act.

words.tr: adj. 迟缓的；呆钝的；不活泼的；蛰伏的
words.ex: The cat was torpid in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 猫在阳光下懒洋洋的。
words.en: If you are torpid, you are mentally or physically inactive, especially because you are feeling lazy or sleepy.

words.ex: The cold weather put the animal into torpor.
words.ex_cn: 寒冷的天气让动物陷入麻木状态。
words.en: a state of physical or mental inactivity; lethargy.

words.tr: adj. 不修边幅的；邋遢的
words.ex: He wore slovenly clothes to work.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着邋遢的衣服去上班。
words.en: If you describe someone as slovenly, you disapprove of them because they are careless and untidy in their appearance or habits.

words.ex: The turtle moves in a sluggish way.
words.ex_cn: 乌龟移动得很缓慢。
words.en: If you describe something as sluggish, you mean that it is moving or working more slowly than usual.

words.tr: v. 嫉妒；羡慕；不乐意地做（或付出）
words.ex: He begrudges his friend's success.
words.ex_cn: 他嫉妒朋友的成功。
words.en: If you begrudge something, you feel unhappy or resentful about having to give it, do it, or allow it.

words.tr:
n. 怨恨；积怨；嫌隙
v. 勉强做；不情愿地给；吝惜
words.ex: He holds a grudge against his brother.
words.ex_cn: 他对他哥哥心怀怨恨。
words.en: A grudge is a persistent feeling of ill will or resentment resulting from a past insult or injury.

words.tr: adj. 吝啬的；小气的；少量的
words.ex: He was miserly with his money and never spent a penny on others.
words.ex_cn: 他对钱很吝啬，从不为别人花一分钱。
words.en: If you say that someone is miserly, you disapprove of them because they seem to hate spending money, and to spend as little as possible.

words.tr: n. 吝啬；小气；过度节俭
words.ex: His parsimony led to a reputation for stinginess.
words.ex_cn: 他的吝啬导致了他被认为是个小气鬼。
words.en: Parsimony is the quality of being very unwilling to spend money.

words.ex: He lives in penury after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后生活贫困。
words.en: Penury is the state of being extremely poor.

words.ex: His stinginess was well-known among his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他的吝啬在朋友中是众所周知的。
words.en: The quality of being unwilling to spend money; meanness.

words.ex: He is stingy with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他花钱很吝啬。
words.en: If you describe someone as stingy, you are criticizing them for being unwilling to spend money or to give or use a lot of something.

words.ex: He was known for being tightfisted with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他因对金钱的吝啬而闻名。
words.en: If you describe someone as tightfisted, you disapprove of them because they are unwilling to spend money.

words.tr: n. 吝啬鬼；小气鬼；守财奴
words.ex: He was known as a tightwad who never spent a penny unnecessarily.
words.ex_cn: 他以吝啬鬼闻名，从不花不必要的钱。
words.en: A tightwad is a person who is very reluctant to spend money; a miser.

words.tr: adj. 短小的；少量的；贫乏的；不足的；吝啬的
words.ex: She wore a skimpy shirt that barely covered her shoulders.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件短小的衬衫，几乎盖不住肩膀。
words.en: If you describe something as skimpy, you mean that there is not enough of it or that it is too small.

words.tr: adj. 小气的；吝啬的；太节省的
words.ex: His parsimonious nature made him unpopular among colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 他吝啬的本性使得他在同事中不受欢迎。
words.en: Someone who is parsimonious is very unwilling to spend money.

words.tr: adj. 氏族的；宗族排外的；团结心很强的
words.ex: The community was very clannish and outsiders found it hard to integrate.
words.ex_cn: 这个社区非常排外，外来者发现很难融入。
words.en: If you describe a group of people or their behavior as clannish, you mean that they often spend time together and seem unfriendly towards people who are not in the group.

words.tr: n. 派系；小集团；小圈子
words.ex: She found it hard to break into the clique at school.
words.ex_cn: 她发现很难融入学校的小圈子。
words.en: A clique is a small group of people who spend their time together and do not allow others to join them.

words.tr: n. 小团体；小圈子；志同道合的一伙
words.ex: He belongs to a small coterie of artists.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个小艺术家圈子的成员。
words.en: A coterie is a small group of people with shared interests or tastes, especially one that is exclusive of other people.

words.ex: The new mayor was accused of cronyism in his appointments.
words.ex_cn: 新市长在任命上被指控有任人唯亲的行为。
words.en: Cronyism is the practice of appointing friends and associates to positions of authority, without proper regard to their qualifications.

words.tr: adj. 不直接的；不正直的；迂回的；
words.ex: He gave a devious answer to avoid telling the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个不直接的回答，以避免说出真相。
words.en: If you describe someone as devious, you mean that they are dishonest and unfair in the way that they behave, often by using indirect methods to achieve their aims.

words.tr: n. 派系；派系斗争；内讧
words.ex: The faction argued loudly about the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 这个派别就新规定激烈争论。
words.en: A faction is a group of people within a larger group who have different opinions and beliefs from the rest of the group.

words.tr: adj. 顽固守旧的；死板保守的
words.ex: He is hidebound and refuses to change his old ways.
words.ex_cn: 他思想僵化，拒绝改变他的老办法。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as hidebound, you are criticizing them for having old-fashioned attitudes or ideas and being unwilling or unlikely to change.

words.tr: adj. 非自由主义的；思想狭隘的
words.ex: The government's illiberal policies restricted free speech.
words.ex_cn: 政府的非自由主义政策限制了言论自由。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as illiberal, you are critical of them because they do not allow or approve of much freedom or choice of action.

words.ex: The inequity in pay between men and women is wrong.
words.ex_cn: 男女薪酬之间的不公是错误的。
words.en: Inequity refers to a lack of fairness or justice in a situation or system.

words.tr:
n. 黄疸病；偏见
v. 使产生黄疸；使怀偏见
words.ex: The baby had jaundice and needed light therapy.
words.ex_cn: 这个婴儿患有黄疸，需要光疗。
words.en: Jaundice is a medical condition in which the skin and the whites of the eyes become yellow, caused by an excess of bile pigment in the blood.

words.tr:
adj. 患黄疸病的；有偏见的
v. 使产生黄疸；使怀偏见；“jaundice”的过去式
words.ex: His judgment was jaundiced by his personal dislike for the candidate.
words.ex_cn: 他对候选人的个人反感使他的判断带有偏见。
words.en: If someone has a jaundiced view of something, they see it in a negative way because they are jealous or bitter.

words.tr: adj. 倾向一方的；不平衡的；悬殊的
words.ex: The game was lopsided, and one team won by 10 points.
words.ex_cn: 这场比赛比分悬殊，一支队伍以10分获胜。
words.en: Something that is lopsided is uneven because one side is lower or heavier than the other.

words.tr: n. 裙带关系；任人唯亲
words.ex: He got the job because of nepotism.
words.ex_cn: 他因为任人唯亲而得到了这份工作。
words.en: The practice among those with power or influence of favoring relatives or friends, especially by giving them jobs.

words.tr: adj. 教区的；地方范围的；思想狭隘的
words.ex: The priest served in a small parochial church.
words.ex_cn: 牧师在一座小型教区教堂服务。
words.en: If you describe someone as parochial, you are criticizing them because you think they are too concerned with their own affairs and should be thinking about more important things.

words.ex: He showed partiality toward his favorite student.
words.ex_cn: 他对最喜欢的学生表现出偏袒。
words.en: If you have a partiality for something, you like it very much.

words.ex: He has prejudice against people from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 他对来自其他国家的人有偏见。
words.en: Prejudice is an unreasonable dislike of a particular group of people or things, or a preference for one group of people or things over another.

words.tr: adj. 倾向性的；有偏见的；有争议的
words.ex: The media's tendentious reporting often misrepresents the truth.
words.ex_cn: 媒体的带有倾向性的报道常常歪曲事实。
words.en: If something is tendentious, it expresses a particular opinion or point of view very strongly, especially one that many people disagree with.

words.ex: He was unjustly punished for a mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他因一个错误而被不公正地惩罚了。
words.en: In a manner that is not fair or just.

words.ex: He showed xenophobia toward people from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 他对来自其他国家的人表现出恐外心理。
words.en: Xenophobia is a strong feeling of dislike or fear of people from other countries.

words.ex: He hates bigotry and speaks up for everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他憎恨偏见，并为所有人发声。
words.en: Bigotry is the possession or expression of strong, unreasonable prejudices or opinions.

words.tr: adj. 派系的；与派系相关的；好争论的
words.ex: The factious group refused to cooperate with others.
words.ex_cn: 这个分裂的团体拒绝与其他人的合作。
words.en: If you describe a group or activity as factious, you mean that it is divided into groups that have strong and unfriendly disagreements.

words.ex: The teacher showed a bias for students who arrived early.
words.ex_cn: 老师对早到的学生有偏爱。
words.en: If someone is biased, they prefer one group of people to another, and behave unfairly as a result.

words.ex: He noticed the discrimination between the two prices.
words.ex_cn: 他注意到了两个价格之间的区别。
words.en: The unjust or prejudicial treatment of different categories of people, especially on the grounds of race, age, or sex.

words.tr: adj. 狭窄的； v. “cramp”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The tiny room was cramped and hard to move in.
words.ex_cn: 这个小房间很狭窄，很难活动。
words.en: If a place is cramped, it is not big enough for the people or things in it, so that it is difficult to move around or to use things properly.

words.ex: The movie had a banal plot that everyone had seen before.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的剧情平庸得让人看过了无数次。
words.en: If you describe something as banal, you do not like it because you think that it is so ordinary that it is not at all effective or interesting.

words.tr: adj. 平庸陈腐的；过于感伤的
words.ex: The movie's ending was so bathetic that it made everyone cringe.
words.ex_cn: 电影的结局如此陈腐，以至于让每个人都感到不适。
words.en: If you describe something as bathetic, you mean that it is overly sentimental or trying too hard to be serious or dramatic, often resulting in a disappointing or underwhelming effect.

words.ex: The city showed signs of decadence after the war.
words.ex_cn: 战争之后，这座城市显示出衰败的迹象。
words.en: Decadence is a situation in which a society or institution is becoming less moral and less satisfactory.

words.tr: adj. 陈腐的；陈词滥调的；老生常谈的
words.ex: His jokes are hackneyed and boring.
words.ex_cn: 他的笑话陈腐又无聊。
words.en: If you describe something as hackneyed, you mean that it is unoriginal and has been used so often that it is no longer interesting.

words.ex: The movie was mediocre and not worth watching.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影很平庸，不值得看。
words.en: If you describe something as mediocre, you mean that it is of average quality but you think it should be better.

words.ex: He refused to accept mediocrity in his work.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝在工作中接受平凡。
words.en: If you refer to the mediocrity of something, you mean that it is of average quality but you think it should be better.

words.tr: n. 陈词滥调；老生常谈；
words.ex: His speech was full of platitudes about hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了关于努力工作的陈词滥调。
words.en: A platitude is a statement that has been used so often that it is meaningless and shows a lack of original thought.

words.ex: His speech was full of trite phrases.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了陈腐的表达。
words.en: If you say that something such as an idea, remark, or story is trite, you mean that it is dull and boring because it has been said or told too many times.

words.tr:
adj. 无可名状的；难以区别的；无特征的；极普通的
n. 无以名状；不属任何类型的人
words.ex: The building was nondescript, with no special features.
words.ex_cn: 这栋建筑无可名状，没有任何特别的特征。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as nondescript, you mean that their appearance is rather dull, and not at all interesting or attractive.

words.tr: adj. 渴望获得的；贪得无厌的
words.ex: He is acquisitive and always wants more things.
words.ex_cn: 他很有占有欲，总是想要更多东西。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behavior as acquisitive, you mean they are very interested in acquiring money and possessions, often in a way that is selfish or unfair.

words.ex: His avarice knew no bounds, always seeking more wealth.
words.ex_cn: 他的贪婪无止境，总是追求更多的财富。
words.en: Avarice is extremely strong desire for money and possessions.

words.ex: He is avaricious and always wants more money.
words.ex_cn: 他贪婪，总是想要更多的钱。
words.en: If you describe someone as avaricious, you are criticizing them because they have an extremely strong desire for money and possessions.

words.ex: He covets his neighbor's car.
words.ex_cn: 他垂涎邻居的车。
words.en: If you covet something, you have a very strong desire to possess it, especially something that belongs to someone else.

words.ex: His cupidity led him to make risky investments.
words.ex_cn: 他的贪婪导致他进行了高风险的投资。
words.en: Intense desire for wealth or possessions; greed.

words.tr:
adj. 一味攫取的；贪婪的；贪心的
v. 抓紧； 领会；“grasp”的现在分词
words.ex: He was a grasping businessman who always looked for more profit.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个贪婪的商人，总是寻求更多的利润。
words.en: If you describe someone as grasping, you are criticizing them for wanting to get and keep as much money as possible, and for being unwilling to spend it.

words.ex: He was ravenous after running five miles.
words.ex_cn: 跑了五英里后，他饿极了。
words.en: If you are ravenous, you are extremely hungry.

words.tr: adj. 贪赃枉法的；腐败的
words.ex: The official was venal and took bribes.
words.ex_cn: 这位官员贪腐，接受了贿赂。
words.en: If you describe someone as venal, you disapprove of them because they are prepared to do almost anything in return for money, even things which are dishonest or immoral.

words.tr: adj. 贪吃的；贪婪的；如饥似渴的
words.ex: He is a voracious eater who finishes all the food on his plate.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个贪吃的人，总会把盘子里的所有食物吃完。
words.en: If you describe a person or their appetite for something as voracious, you mean that they want a lot of something.

words.ex: The dog's voracity was clear as it ate all the food in seconds.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗的贪吃显而易见，它几秒钟就吃光了所有食物。
words.en: The quality or state of being voracious; excessive eagerness or enthusiasm.

words.ex: He is a glutton who eats too much candy.
words.ex_cn: 他是个贪吃糖的暴食者。
words.en: A glutton is a person who eats and drinks excessively or voraciously.

words.tr: adj. 贪心的；贪婪的；渴望的
words.ex: He is covetous of his neighbor's new car.
words.ex_cn: 他垂涎邻居的新车。
words.en: If you are covetous, you have a strong desire to possess something, especially something that belongs to someone else.

words.tr: adj. 吹毛求疵的；挑剔的
words.ex: He made a captious comment about the small mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他对一个小错误发表了挑剔的评论。
words.en: Tending to find fault or raise petty objections.

words.tr:
v. 挑毛病；吹毛求疵
n. 挑剔；挑毛病
words.ex: He cavils at every small mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他挑剔每一个小错误。
words.en: If you say that someone cavils at something, you mean that they make criticisms of it that you think are unimportant or unnecessary.

words.tr: adj. 至关重要的；批判性的；关键的；危急的；临界的；
words.ex: Water is critical for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命至关重要。
words.en: If you are critical of someone or something, you show that you disapprove of them. In a critical situation, things are very serious and dangerous. A critical time or event is extremely important because it will affect future events.

words.tr: adj. 爱挑剔的；过分讲究的
words.ex: He is fastidious about keeping his room clean.
words.ex_cn: 他非常讲究保持房间整洁。
words.en: Very attentive to and concerned about accuracy and detail.

words.ex: He is fussy about his food.
words.ex_cn: 他对食物很挑剔。
words.en: Someone who is fussy is very concerned with unimportant details and is difficult to please.

words.tr: v. 挑剔；吹毛求疵；鸡蛋里挑骨头
words.ex: She tends to nitpick about small details.
words.ex_cn: 她倾向于对小细节吹毛求疵。
words.en: To nitpick means to criticize or find fault with someone or something in a petty or fussy way.

words.tr: adj. 爱挑剔的；难应付的
words.ex: She is very persnickety about her food, always looking for the best ingredients.
words.ex_cn: 她对食物非常挑剔，总是寻找最好的食材。
words.en: If you describe someone as persnickety, you think that they pay too much attention to small, unimportant details and are difficult to please.

words.tr: adj. 爱挑剔的；吹毛求疵的
words.ex: He is censorious about everyone's mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他对每个人的错误都吹毛求疵。
words.en: If you describe someone as censorious, you mean that they strongly disapprove of and criticize someone else's behavior.

words.tr:
adj. 吹毛求疵的；挑毛病的
v. 挑剔；吹毛求疵；发牢骚；“carp”的现在分词
words.ex: His constant carping criticism was tiresome.
words.ex_cn: 他那没完没了的吹毛求疵的批评令人厌烦。
words.en: If you describe someone as carping, you mean that they keep criticizing or complaining about someone or something, especially in a way you think is unnecessary or annoying.

words.ex: He was adamant about not changing his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他坚定不移地不改变主意。
words.en: If someone is adamant about something, they are determined not to change their mind about it.

words.ex: She was too closed-minded to consider new ideas.
words.ex_cn: 她思想太保守，不愿意考虑新想法。
words.en: Not willing to consider different ideas or opinions; intolerant.

words.tr: adj. 拒不服从的；藐视法庭的
words.ex: He was contumacious and refused to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他桀骜不驯，拒绝遵守规则。
words.en: If someone is contumacious, they are stubbornly or willfully disobedient to authority.

words.tr: v. 缠住；“dog”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The reporter dogged the politician everywhere.
words.ex_cn: 记者紧紧跟随这位政治家到处。
words.en: If you describe someone's actions as dogged, you mean that they are determined to continue with something even if it becomes difficult or dangerous.

words.tr:
adj. 不可挽救的；屡教不改的；不可救药的
n. 无可救药的人
words.ex: He is an incorrigible liar.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个无可救药的骗子。
words.en: If you describe someone as incorrigible, you mean that they have faults which they seem unable or unwilling to correct, even though they are aware of them.

words.ex: The problem is intractable and no one can solve it.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题很难处理，没人能解决。
words.en: If you describe a problem or a person as intractable, you mean that it is very difficult to deal with or to change.

words.tr: adj. 不妥协的；不让步的
words.ex: He is intransigent about his opinions.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的观点毫不让步。
words.en: If you describe someone as intransigent, you mean that they refuse to behave differently or to change their attitude to something.

words.ex: He is mulish and refuses to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很固执，拒绝改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as mulish, you mean they are determined to do what they want to do and will not change their mind or be persuaded to do something else.

words.tr: adj. 顽固的；执拗的；冷酷无情的
words.ex: He is obdurate and refuses to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他固执己见，拒绝改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as obdurate, you mean that they are determined not to change their mind or attitude in spite of efforts to persuade them.

words.ex: His obstinacy in refusing treatment led to his condition worsening.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝治疗的固执态度导致他的病情恶化。
words.en: The quality or state of being obstinate; stubbornness.

words.tr: adj. 执拗的；固执的；顽固的；
words.ex: He is obstinate and won't change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很执拗，不肯改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as obstinate, you are being critical of them because they are very determined to do what they want, and refuse to change their mind or be persuaded to do something else.

words.tr: adj. 固执己见的；顽固的
words.ex: He is opinionated and never changes his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很有主见，从不改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as opinionated, you mean that they have very strong opinions and refuse to accept that they may be wrong.

words.ex: He is pertinacious about finishing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持要完成作业。
