words.en: Someone who is pertinacious continues trying to do something in a very determined way, even though it is difficult or other people are against it.

words.ex: The horse's restiveness made it difficult to control during the race.
words.ex_cn: 这匹马在比赛中难以驾驭。
words.en: Restiveness refers to a state of being restless or uneasy, often due to impatience or dissatisfaction.

words.ex: He is stubborn and won't change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很顽固，不肯改变主意。
words.en: Someone who is stubborn is determined to do what they want and is very unwilling to change their mind.

words.tr: adj. 固执己见的；偏执的；执迷的
words.ex: He is bigoted and refuses to listen to others.
words.ex_cn: 他固执己见，拒绝听取别人的意见。
words.en: If you describe someone as bigoted, you mean that they are bigoted.

words.tr: adj. 顽强的；精明的；顽固的
words.ex: He is a hard-nosed manager who never gives up.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个顽强的经理，从不放弃。
words.en: If you describe someone as hard-nosed, you mean they are tough and realistic, especially in business or politics.

words.tr: adj. 判断错误的；坚持错误的
words.ex: His wrongheaded decision cost the company millions.
words.ex_cn: 他固执的决定让公司损失了数百万。
words.en: If you describe someone as wrongheaded, you mean that although they act in a determined way, their actions and ideas are based on wrong judgments.

words.ex: He jumped into the pool headfirst.
words.ex_cn: 他头朝下跳进了游泳池。
words.en: If you move headfirst in a particular direction, your head is the part of your body that is furthest forward as you are moving.

words.ex: His obduracy in the face of evidence was astounding.
words.ex_cn: 面对证据，他的执拗态度令人震惊。
words.en: Obduracy is the quality of being very determined not to change your beliefs, feelings, or actions, especially in a way that seems unreasonable.

words.ex: His story is far-fetched and not believable.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事牵强附会，不可信。
words.en: If you describe a story or idea as far-fetched, you mean that it is very unlikely to be true or practical.

words.ex: The mirror creates an illusion of a bigger room.
words.ex_cn: 镜子制造出房间更大的错觉。
words.en: An illusion is a false idea or belief, especially about yourself or your situation.

words.ex: He kneads dough every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上揉面团。
words.en: To knead is to press and stretch dough or another substance with your hands in order to make it smooth and ready to use.

words.ex: He misinformed the crowd about the time.
words.ex_cn: 他告诉人群错误的时间。
words.en: To misinform someone means to give them false or inaccurate information.

words.ex: The smile on his face was illusory.
words.ex_cn: 他脸上的微笑是虚假的。
words.en: If something is illusory, it is not real or true, although it may seem to be.

words.tr: v. 影响；“affect”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 染病的；受感动的；
words.ex: The rain affected the game.
words.ex_cn: 雨影响了比赛。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as affected, you disapprove of the fact that they behave in an unnatural way that is intended to impress other people.

words.ex: His smile belieed his true feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑掩饰了他真实的情感。
words.en: If one thing belies another, it hides the true situation and so creates a false idea or image of someone or something.

words.tr:
v. 虚张声势；唬人
n. 虚张声势；吓唬；峭壁
adj. 直率的
words.ex: He used a bluff to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他用虚张声势赢得了比赛。
words.en: If you bluff, you try to make someone believe that you will do something when you do not really intend to do it, or that you know something when you do not really know it.

words.ex: He talked with bravado, but he was scared.
words.ex_cn: 他装出勇敢的样子说话，但他其实很害怕。
words.en: A bold manner or a show of boldness intended to impress or intimidate.

words.ex: The soldier wore camouflage to hide in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 士兵穿着伪装服在森林中隐藏自己。
words.en: Camouflage is the way in which some animals are colored and shaped so that they cannot easily be seen in their natural surroundings.

words.tr:
adj. 人为的；预谋的；做作的
v. 图谋；发明；设计；设法做到；“contrive”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The story's ending felt contrived.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事的结局显得很牵强。
words.en: If you say that something someone says or does is contrived, you mean it seems false and artificial, and is not likely to fool or convince anyone.

words.tr:
n. 伪装；伪装物；
v. 伪装；掩饰；
words.ex: He wore a hat and glasses as a disguise.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了帽子和眼镜作为伪装。
words.en: To disguise means to change your appearance or behavior so that people will not recognize you, or to make something seem different from what it really is.

words.ex: He dozed off during the boring meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在无聊的会议上打起了瞌睡。
words.en: To doze means to sleep lightly or for a short period.

words.ex: His dissimulation was evident in his evasive answers.
words.ex_cn: 他闪烁其词的回答显示出了他的掩饰。
words.en: Dissimulation is the act of concealing one's true feelings, thoughts, or intentions, often by pretending to have different ones.

words.ex: He tried to extenuate his mistake by saying he was tired.
words.ex_cn: 他试图以自己累了为由减轻自己的错误。
words.en: To lessen or to try to lessen the seriousness or extent of (guilt or an offense) by providing partial excuses.

words.ex: He feigns sleep to avoid talking.
words.ex_cn: 他假装睡觉以避免交谈。
words.en: If someone feigns a particular feeling, attitude, or physical condition, they try to make other people think that they have it or are experiencing it, although this is not true.

words.tr:
adj. 假装的；不真实的
v. 假装；装作；“feign”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He feigned sleep to avoid talking.
words.ex_cn: 他假装睡觉以避免交谈。
words.en: If someone's behaviour or emotion is feigned, it is not genuine or sincere, but is pretended for effect.

words.ex: The monster was just a figment of his imagination.
words.ex_cn: 那个怪物只是他想象出来的。
words.en: A figment is something that someone imagines or invents, often something that is not real.

words.ex: He tried to gild the old box with gold paint.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用金漆把旧盒子镀金。
words.en: To cover something with a thin layer of gold or to make something seem more attractive or valuable than it really is.

words.ex: He is hypocritical when he says he hates lying but lies all the time.
words.ex_cn: 他说他讨厌撒谎，却总是撒谎，这很虚伪。
words.en: If you accuse someone of being hypocritical, you mean that they pretend to have qualities, beliefs, or feelings that they do not really have.

words.ex: His insincerity was evident in his hollow promises.
words.ex_cn: 他空洞的承诺显示了他的伪善。
words.en: The quality of not expressing genuine feelings; lack of sincerity.

words.tr: adj. 矫揉造作的；不自然的；守规矩的；彬彬有礼的
words.ex: Her mannered speech was hard to understand.
words.ex_cn: 她矫揉造作的言辞让人难以理解。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior or a work of art as mannered, you dislike it because it is elaborate or formal, and therefore seems false or artificial.

words.ex: He wore a scary mask at the Halloween party.
words.ex_cn: 他在万圣节派对上戴了一个可怕的面具。
words.en: A mask is a piece of cloth or other material that you wear over your face to hide or protect it.

words.tr: adj. 伪善的；伪装虔诚的
words.ex: His pharisaic attitude towards religion was deeply hypocritical.
words.ex_cn: 他对宗教的伪善态度非常虚伪。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as pharisaic, you are criticizing them for being hypocritical and self-righteous.

words.tr: n. 伪装；假象；虚伪的表现
words.ex: He was accused of using pretense to gain sympathy.
words.ex_cn: 他被指控利用伪装来博取同情。
words.en: A pretense is an action or way of behaving that is intended to make people believe something that is not true.

words.ex: He pretends to sleep when his mom asks him to clean his room.
words.ex_cn: 当妈妈让他打扫房间时，他假装睡觉。
words.en: If you pretend that something is the case, you act in a way that is intended to make people believe that it is the case, although in fact it is not.

words.tr: adj. 装作圣洁的；伪善的
words.ex: He gave a sanctimonious speech about honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一番关于诚实的伪善演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as sanctimonious, you disapprove of them because you think that they are trying to appear morally better than other people.

words.tr: adj. 做戏似的；不自然的；戏剧性的
words.ex: Her performance was too stagy to be believable.
words.ex_cn: 她的表演太过做作，令人难以相信。
words.en: If you describe something as stagy, you mean that it is artificial and exaggerated, like something in a play.

words.tr: n. 做作；假装；装模作样
words.ex: His laugh was an affectation to seem cool.
words.ex_cn: 他的笑声是一种装模作样的表现，以显得很酷。
words.en: An affectation is a deliberate pretense or exaggerated display of a particular quality or manner.

words.ex: He tried to gloss over his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他试图掩盖自己的错误。
words.en: To gloss over something is to try to make it seem less important or less serious than it really is.

words.ex: The witch practiced sorcery in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 女巫在森林里施展巫术。
words.en: Sorcery is the use of magic, especially black magic.

words.tr: n. 牙托； 一副假牙
words.ex: He wears a denture to eat food.
words.ex_cn: 他戴假牙来吃东西。
words.en: A denture is a removable plate or frame holding one or more artificial teeth.

words.tr:
n. 假发
v. 痛骂；严责；给…装假发
words.ex: She wore a wig to cover her bald head.
words.ex_cn: 她戴了一顶假发来遮盖她光秃的头。
words.en: A wig is a covering of false hair which you wear on your head, for example because you are bald or because you want to cover up your own hair.

chapters.name: Word List 32 正向情绪 高兴

words.ex: The weather was agreeable for a walk.
words.ex_cn: 天气令人愉悦，适合散步。
words.en: Pleasant and easy to like; willing to agree to something

words.tr: n. 便利设施；舒适条件；公共设施；
words.ex: The apartment has good amenities like a gym and a swimming pool.
words.ex_cn: 这套公寓有健身房和游泳池等便利设施。
words.en: An amenity is something that makes a place more pleasant or comfortable to live in.

words.ex: The clown amuses the children with funny tricks.
words.ex_cn: 小丑用滑稽的把戏娱乐孩子们。
words.en: If something amuses you, it makes you want to laugh or smile.

words.tr: adj. 快乐安详的；幸福的
words.ex: She had a beatific smile after the prayer.
words.ex_cn: 祈祷后，她脸上带着宁静幸福的微笑。
words.en: A beatific expression, smile, or vision shows great happiness and calmness.

words.ex: She felt pure bliss when she held her newborn baby.
words.ex_cn: 当她抱住新生儿时，感受到了无上的幸福。
words.en: Bliss is a state of complete happiness.

words.tr: adj. 极快乐的；极幸福的
words.ex: She spent a blissful afternoon in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 她在花园里度过了一个极其幸福的下午。
words.en: Extremely happy; full of joy.

words.tr: adj. 漫不经心的；无忧无虑的
words.ex: He gave a blithe smile and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他漫不经心地笑了笑，然后走开了。
words.en: If you describe someone as blithe, you mean that they are carefree and cheerful.

words.tr: v. 拥抱；包含（embrace 的现在分词）；
words.ex: She is embracing her little brother.
words.ex_cn: 她正在拥抱她的弟弟。
words.en: To hold someone closely in one's arms, especially as a sign of affection; to accept or support a belief, theory, or change willingly and enthusiastically.

words.tr:
v. 雀跃；欢跃
n. 刺山柑花蕾；雀跃；不法活动；胡闹
words.ex: The children capered around the playground.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在操场上雀跃。
words.en: A caper is a playful leap or jump. It can also refer to a prank or a mischievous act. Additionally, it denotes the pickled flower bud of the caper bush, used as a condiment.

words.tr: v. 痛饮狂欢；狂饮作乐
words.ex: They carouse every weekend at the beach.
words.ex_cn: 他们每周末都在海滩上狂欢。
words.en: To engage in a noisy, lively drinking party.

words.ex: The children cavort in the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在公园里嬉戏。
words.en: If people cavort, they leap about in a noisy and excited way because they are very happy.

words.tr: adj. 欢乐的；轻松快活的；好交际的
words.ex: The party was convivial and everyone laughed a lot.
words.ex_cn: 派对气氛友好愉快，大家都笑得很开心。
words.en: A convivial atmosphere or event is friendly and pleasant, and people enjoy being together.

words.ex: The conviviality at the party made everyone feel welcome.
words.ex_cn: 派对上的友好气氛让每个人都感到受欢迎。
words.en: Conviviality is the quality of being friendly and making people feel happy and welcome.

words.tr: v. 浪费时间；拖延；玩弄；调情
words.ex: He dallys with his homework instead of finishing it.
words.ex_cn: 他浪费时间在作业上，而不是完成它。
words.en: To dally means to act or move slowly, or to spend time idly or in trifling.

words.tr: adj. 美味的；使人愉快的
words.ex: The cake was delectable.
words.ex_cn: 这个蛋糕非常美味。
words.en: If you describe something, especially food or drink, as delectable, you mean that it is very pleasant.

words.ex: The children disported themselves in the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在公园里玩耍。
words.en: To disport means to amuse or enjoy oneself in a lively or playful way.

words.tr: n. 热情洋溢；兴高采烈
words.ex: Her ebullience was contagious, spreading joy to everyone around her.
words.ex_cn: 她的兴高采烈是有感染力的，给周围的人带来了欢乐。
words.en: Ebullience is the quality of being cheerful and full of energy.

words.ex: He felt ecstasy after winning the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得奖品后感到无比喜悦。
words.en: Ecstasy is a feeling of very great happiness.

words.tr: adj. 狂喜的；欣喜若狂的
words.ex: She was ecstatic when she won the prize.
words.ex_cn: 她赢得奖品时欣喜若狂。
words.en: If you are ecstatic, you feel very happy and full of excitement.

words.tr: adj. 相关的；有联系的； v. 关联；“relate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: This book is related to science.
words.ex_cn: 这本书与科学相关。
words.en: If two or more things are related, there is a connection between them.

words.ex: The music enraptured the whole audience.
words.ex_cn: 音乐让整个观众着迷。
words.en: To fill someone with great delight or joy.

words.tr: n. 精神欢快；兴高采烈
words.ex: He felt euphoria after winning the race.
words.ex_cn: 他在赢得比赛后感到无比兴奋。
words.en: A feeling or state of intense excitement and happiness.

words.ex: The team's victory brought a wave of exaltation.
words.ex_cn: 团队的胜利带来了一阵欣喜。
words.en: Exaltation is a feeling or state of extreme happiness or elation, often as a result of a success or achievement.

words.ex: The drug increased the patient's excitability.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物增加了病人的兴奋性。
words.en: The quality of being easily excited or prone to excitement.

words.ex: The roller coaster exhilarates the children.
words.ex_cn: 过山车让孩子们感到兴奋。
words.en: To make someone feel very happy and excited.

words.ex: He felt exhilaration after winning the race.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得比赛后感到兴奋不已。
words.en: Exhilaration is a feeling of being very happy and excited.

words.ex: His exuberance made the party fun for everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的热情洋溢让派对对每个人都很有趣。
words.en: Exuberance is the state of being full of energy, excitement, and cheerfulness, or the quality of being full of growth and vitality.

words.ex: He exults when his team wins the game.
words.ex_cn: 当他的球队赢得比赛时，他欢呼雀跃。
words.en: If you exult in a triumph or success that you have had, you feel and show great happiness and pride because of it.

words.ex: The crowd was exultant after their team won.
words.ex_cn: 球队赢了之后，人群欣喜若狂。
words.en: If you are exultant, you feel very happy and proud because of something that has happened.

words.ex: They felicitated him on his recent promotion.
words.ex_cn: 他们为他的晋升表示祝贺。
words.en: to congratulate someone

words.ex: The town was adorned with festal lights for the holiday.
words.ex_cn: 为了节日，小镇装饰上了节日的彩灯。
words.en: Festal is used to describe something that is related to a festival or is festive in nature.

words.tr: adj. 节日的；喜庆的；欢乐的
words.ex: The streets are festive during Christmas.
words.ex_cn: 圣诞节期间，街道上充满了节日气氛。
words.en: Something that is festive is special, colorful, or exciting, especially because it is connected with a festival or celebration.

words.tr:
n. 游园会；庆祝；盛大节日
v. 宴请；招待
words.ex: The town held a fete to raise money for the school.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇举办了一场集市来为学校筹款。
words.en: A fete is an outdoor event with stalls, games, and entertainments, often organized to raise money for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The garden has fragrant flowers.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园里有芳香的花。
words.en: Having a pleasant or sweet smell.

words.ex: The puppy frisks around the garden.
words.ex_cn: 小狗在花园里活蹦乱跳。
words.en: To frisk someone means to search them for weapons or illegal items by feeling their body with your hands.

words.ex: The frisky puppy was bouncing around the room.
words.ex_cn: 那只活泼的小狗在房间里蹦来蹦去。
words.en: If you describe a person or animal as frisky, you mean they are lively and playful.

words.tr:
v. 嬉戏
n. 嬉戏；欢乐的活动
words.ex: The children were frolicking in the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在公园里嬉戏。
words.en: If people or animals frolic, they play or move in a lively, happy way.

words.tr: adj. 嬉闹的；爱闹着玩的
words.ex: The children were being particularly frolicsome in the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在公园里特别嬉戏打闹。
words.en: If you describe someone as frolicsome, you mean they are lively and playful.

words.ex: The children's laughter brought gaiety to the party.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们的笑声为派对带来了欢乐。
words.en: Gaiety is a feeling, attitude, or atmosphere of liveliness and fun.

words.ex: The lambs gambol in the green field.
words.ex_cn: 小羊在绿地上嬉戏。
words.en: If animals or people gambol, they run or jump about in a playful way.

words.tr: adj. 亲切的；和蔼的；温暖的
words.ex: He is a genial man who always smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个和蔼可亲的人，总是面带微笑。
words.en: Friendly and cheerful.

words.ex: The children shouted with glee when they saw the ice cream truck.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们看到冰淇淋车时高兴地大喊。
words.en: Glee is a feeling of great happiness, usually because something good has happened.

words.tr: v. 幸灾乐祸；沾沾自喜；满足地看
words.ex: He gloats when his rival loses the game.
words.ex_cn: 当他的对手输掉比赛时，他幸灾乐祸。
words.en: To gloat means to observe or think about something with triumphant and often malicious satisfaction, gratification, or delight.

words.ex: He waits for the gratification of winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 他等待赢得比赛的满足感。
words.en: Gratification is the pleasure or satisfaction you feel when you get something you wanted or worked for.

words.ex: He gratifies his parents by getting good grades.
words.ex_cn: 他通过取得好成绩来让父母感到欣慰。
words.en: If you are gratified by something, it gives you pleasure or satisfaction.

words.ex: The hedonic treadmill theory suggests that people quickly return to a relatively stable level of happiness despite major positive or negative events.
words.ex_cn: 享乐跑步机理论认为，尽管发生了重大的积极或消极事件，人们仍会迅速回到相对稳定的幸福水平。
words.en: Hedonic relates to the pursuit of pleasure; sensual self-indulgence.

words.ex: The movie was hilarious and made us laugh a lot.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影非常搞笑，让我们笑得很开心。
words.en: If you describe something as hilarious, you mean that it is extremely funny and it makes you laugh a lot.

words.tr: v.  使中毒；使醉；使 ...陶醉
words.ex: The dirty water can intoxicate animals.
words.ex_cn: 脏水会使动物中毒。
words.en: To intoxicate someone means to make them lose control of their actions or behavior because they have drunk alcohol or taken drugs. It can also mean to make someone feel very excited and happy.

words.tr: adj. 轻松活泼的；得意洋洋的；自信满满的
words.ex: He walked with a jaunty step, clearly pleased with himself.
words.ex_cn: 他步伐轻快，显然对自己感到很满意。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as jaunty, you mean that they are full of confidence and energy.

words.ex: His jocund laughter filled the room.
words.ex_cn: 他那快活的笑声充满了整个房间。
words.en: If you describe someone as jocund, you mean that they are cheerful and happy.

words.tr:
adj. 愉快的；快乐的
v. 开玩笑；作乐
adv. 非常；很
words.ex: He is jolly at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上很快乐。
words.en: If you describe someone as jolly, you mean that they are happy and cheerful.

words.tr: adj.  快活的；愉快的；高兴的
words.ex: His jovial nature made him popular among his colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 他天性快活，这使他在同事中很受欢迎。
words.en: If you describe someone as jovial, you mean that they are happy and cheerful.

words.tr: adj. 欢腾的；欢欣鼓舞的
words.ex: The children were jubilant after winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们赢了比赛后非常高兴。
words.en: If you are jubilant, you feel extremely happy because of a success.

words.tr: n. 欢腾；欢欣鼓舞；欢庆
words.ex: There was a lot of jubilation when the team won the championship.
words.ex_cn: 当球队赢得冠军时，人们欢呼雀跃。
words.en: A feeling of great happiness and triumph.

words.tr: n. 云雀；百灵鸟；玩乐；嬉戏
words.ex: The lark sings loudly at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 云雀在日出时大声歌唱。
words.en: A lark is a small brown bird that is known for its beautiful song. It is also used to describe a carefree adventure or a playful activity.

words.ex: The children laughed with mirth.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们带着欢乐大笑。
words.en: Mirth is amusement which you express by laughing.

words.tr: n. 乐观；乐观主义；乐观精神；
words.ex: His optimism helps him stay happy even when things are hard.
words.ex_cn: 他的乐观让他即使在困难时也能保持快乐。
words.en: Optimism is a feeling of hopefulness and confidence about the future or the success of something.

words.tr: adj. 开胃的；辛辣的；刺激的；迷人的；兴奋的
words.ex: The sauce has a piquant flavor.
words.ex_cn: 这种酱汁味道辛辣可口。
words.en: Something that is piquant is pleasantly strong and sharp in taste or smell.

words.ex: The party was filled with revelry and laughter.
words.ex_cn: 派对上充满了狂欢和笑声。
words.en: Revelry is a situation in which people are enjoying themselves in a lively and noisy way, often while they are drinking alcohol.

words.tr: adj. 玫瑰色的；红润的（皮肤）；美好的；有希望的（前途等）
words.ex: The sky turned rosy at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 日出时，天空变成了玫瑰色。
words.en: If you describe a situation as rosy, you mean that it seems to be full of hope and promise.

words.tr: adj. 乐天的；自信的；红润的
words.ex: Despite the setbacks, he remained sanguine about the future.
words.ex_cn: 尽管遭遇挫折，他对未来仍然充满希望。
words.en: If you are sanguine about something, you are cheerful and confident that things will happen in the way that you want them to.

words.tr: adj. 愉快活泼的；轻快的；精力充沛的；精神矍铄的
words.ex: The old man walks sprightly every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人每天早上都轻快地走路。
words.en: Someone who is sprightly is lively and active, especially in a way that makes you feel happy.

words.tr:
n. 运输；
v. 运输；
words.ex: He uses public transport to go to work.
words.ex_cn: 他乘坐公共交通去上班。
words.en: To transport something or someone is to move them from one place to another, especially over long distances.

words.ex: The team celebrated their triumph after winning the match.
words.ex_cn: 球队在赢得比赛后庆祝了他们的胜利。
words.en: A triumph is a great success or achievement, often one that has been gained with a lot of skill or effort.

words.ex: There was an upsurge in demand for masks during the pandemic.
words.ex_cn: 疫情期间，对口罩的需求激增。
words.en: An upsurge is a sudden and usually large increase in something.

words.ex: She is a vivacious girl who laughs loudly.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个活泼的女孩，笑得很响亮。
words.en: If you describe someone as vivacious, you mean that they are lively, exciting, and attractive.

words.ex: She was elated when she won the prize.
words.ex_cn: 她获奖时非常高兴。
words.en: To make someone feel very happy and excited.

words.tr: n. 生活福利设施；便利设施；“amenity”的复数；
words.ex: The apartment has good amenities like a gym and a swimming pool.
words.ex_cn: 这套公寓有健身房和游泳池等良好的生活福利设施。
words.en: Amenities are things such as stores or sports facilities that are provided for people's convenience, enjoyment, or comfort.

words.ex: The party turned into a bacchanalian revelry.
words.ex_cn: 派对变成了狂饮作乐的狂欢。
words.en: Relating to or characteristic of the god Bacchus; marked by drunken revelry and excess.

words.ex: The carousal lasted until the early hours of the morning.
words.ex_cn: 这场喧闹的酒宴一直持续到凌晨。
words.en: A carousal is a noisy, lively drinking party or celebration.

words.tr:
v. 玩闹；轻易地取得胜利
n. 嬉闹；贪玩的人
words.ex: The children romped in the playground.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在操场上嬉戏玩耍。
words.en: To play roughly and energetically; to win easily.

words.ex: The beach was paradisiacal with white sand and blue water.
words.ex_cn: 这片海滩有白色的沙子和蓝色的海水，宛如天堂。
words.en: If you describe a place as paradisiacal, you mean that it is like paradise.

chapters.name: Word List 33 负向情绪 懊恼

words.ex: His eyes were filled with penitence as he confessed his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 当他承认自己的错误时，眼中充满了悔恨。
words.en: Penitence is the state of being sorry for having done wrong and being willing to change one's behavior.

words.tr: n. 良心的责备；后悔；悔恨
words.ex: He felt no compunction about lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他撒谎骗朋友时毫无愧疚。
words.en: A feeling of guilt or moral scruple that prevents or follows the doing of something bad.

words.tr: adj. 深感懊悔的；痛悔的；悔悟的
words.ex: He felt contrite after lying to his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他在对母亲撒谎后感到悔恨。
words.en: Feeling or expressing remorse or penitence; affected by guilt.

words.ex: He felt contrition after lying to his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他在对母亲撒谎后感到悔恨。
words.en: The state of feeling remorseful and penitent.

words.ex: The new policy has disaffected many of the employees.
words.ex_cn: 新政策使许多员工感到不满。
words.en: If something disaffects someone, it makes them lose their affection or loyalty towards a person or organization.

words.ex: The long wait disgruntles the customers.
words.ex_cn: 漫长的等待让顾客感到不满。
words.en: If you are disgruntled, you are angry or dissatisfied because something has not happened the way you wanted.

words.tr: adj. 不知悔悟的；无悔意的
words.ex: The impenitent criminal continued to commit crimes despite repeated warnings.
words.ex_cn: 尽管一再警告，那个不知悔改的罪犯仍然继续犯罪。
words.en: If you describe someone as impenitent, you mean that they are not ashamed of their bad behavior or attitudes, and they do not wish to change them.

words.ex: He has an insatiable hunger for knowledge.
words.ex_cn: 他对知识有着无法满足的渴望。
words.en: If someone is insatiable, they always want more of something and are never satisfied.

words.tr: adj. 可悲的；令人惋惜的；质量低劣的
words.ex: The situation was lamentable, with many people losing their homes.
words.ex_cn: 情况非常可悲，许多人失去了家园。
words.en: If you describe something as lamentable, you mean that it is very unfortunate or disappointing.

words.tr:
v. 呻吟；呼啸；抱怨
n. 呻吟声；萧萧声；抱怨
words.ex: He moans when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 他累了的时候会呻吟。
words.en: If you moan, you make a low sound, usually because you are unhappy or in pain.

words.tr:
adj. 忏悔的；悔过的
n. 忏悔者；悔罪者
words.ex: He sat in the church, a penitent man seeking forgiveness.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在教堂里，一个忏悔的人寻求宽恕。
words.en: Feeling or showing sorrow and regret for having done wrong; repentant.

words.ex: He felt remorse after lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他在对朋友撒谎后感到后悔。
words.en: Remorse is a strong feeling of sadness and regret about something wrong that you have done.

words.ex: He repents for lying to his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他为对母亲撒谎而悔恨。
words.en: If you repent, you feel or express sincere regret or remorse about something wrong you have done.

words.tr:
n. 重复部分；再现
v. 重演；重奏
words.ex: The song ended with a short reprise of the chorus.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌以副歌的简短重复部分结束。
words.en: A reprise is a repetition of a piece of music or a performance. It can also refer to the act of repeating something.

words.tr: adj. 真实的；真的；正确的；
words.ex: The story is true.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事是真实的。
words.en: in accordance with fact or reality

words.tr: adj. 不能再生的；顽固不化的；不悔改的
words.ex: He was an unregenerate gambler, always looking for his next bet.
words.ex_cn: 他是个顽固不化的赌徒，总是寻找下一次的赌注。
words.en: If you describe someone as unregenerate, you mean that they continue to behave in a way that you disapprove of, and they show no intention of changing their attitude or behavior.

words.tr: adj. 不思悔改的；不悔悟的
words.ex: She remained unrepentant about her actions.
words.ex_cn: 她对自己所做的事情毫无悔意。
words.en: If you describe someone as unrepentant, you mean that they are not ashamed of their beliefs or actions.

chapters.name: Word List 33 负向情绪 悲伤

words.ex: The atmosphere was funereal as the mourners gathered.
words.ex_cn: 哀悼者聚集时，气氛悲哀。
words.en: Something that is funereal is very serious and sad, and is suitable for a funeral.

words.ex: He felt deep grief after his dog died.
words.ex_cn: 他的狗去世后，他感到深深的悲痛。
words.en: Intense sorrow, especially caused by someone's death.

words.tr: adj. 痛苦的；严重的；剧烈的
words.ex: The injury caused him grievous pain.
words.ex_cn: 这次受伤给他带来了巨大的痛苦。
words.en: If you describe something such as a loss or injury as grievous, you mean that it is extremely serious or worrying in its effects.

words.tr: adj. 使人悲痛的；令人心碎的
words.ex: The story of the orphan's struggle was heartrending.
words.ex_cn: 这个孤儿奋斗的故事令人心碎。
words.en: Causing great sadness or distress.

words.ex: She mourns her dog every day.
words.ex_cn: 她每天都在哀悼她的狗。
words.en: To feel or express deep sorrow or regret for someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 可怜的；悲哀的；差劲的；令人生厌的
words.ex: The little dog looked pathetic in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 那只小狗在雨中看起来很可怜。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as pathetic, you mean that they are sad and weak or inadequate, and you feel contempt or pity for them.

words.tr: n. 怜悯；悲情；哀婉；凄楚
words.ex: The movie filled us with pathos.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影让我们充满感动。
words.en: Pathos is a quality in a work of art or literature that evokes feelings of pity or sadness.

words.ex: The violin played a plaintive melody.
words.ex_cn: 小提琴演奏了一首哀伤的旋律。
words.en: A plaintive sound or voice expresses sadness.

words.ex: The news saddened her.
words.ex_cn: 这个消息让她感到悲伤。
words.en: If something saddens you, it makes you feel sad.

words.ex: He bemoans the loss of his old car.
words.ex_cn: 他抱怨失去了他的旧车。
words.en: If you bemoan something, you express sorrow or dissatisfaction about it.

words.ex: He bewails his lost job.
words.ex_cn: 他为失去的工作而哀叹。
words.en: To express deep sorrow for; lament.

words.tr: adj. 流泪的；爱哭的；引人落泪的
words.ex: The lachrymose melody of the violin added to the somber atmosphere.
words.ex_cn: 小提琴哀伤的旋律增添了忧郁的气氛。
words.en: If you describe someone as lachrymose, you mean that they are sad or likely to cry easily.

words.tr: adj. 垂头丧气的；灰心失望的
words.ex: He looked crestfallen after losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 他输掉比赛后看起来垂头丧气。
words.en: If you are crestfallen, you are disappointed and sad because of something that has happened.

words.tr: adj. 沮丧的；泄气的；失望的
words.ex: He became despondent after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后变得沮丧。
words.en: If you are despondent, you are very unhappy because you have been experiencing difficulties that you think you will not be able to overcome.

words.ex: The sky was dismal and gray all day.
words.ex_cn: 天空一整天都是阴沉灰暗的。
words.en: If you describe something as dismal, you mean that it is very bad or depressing.

words.tr: adj. 悲哀的；忧愁的；阴沉的
words.ex: He gave a doleful look after losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 输掉比赛后，他露出悲伤的表情。
words.en: A doleful expression, sound, or manner is very sad.

words.tr: adj. 黑暗的；幽暗的；忧郁的；沮丧的
words.ex: The room was gloomy with no windows.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间没有窗户，很黑暗。
words.en: If a place is gloomy, it is almost dark so that you cannot see very well. If people are gloomy, they are unhappy and have no hope.

words.tr: v. 伤心；悲痛；使悲痛；使伤心
words.ex: He grieves for his lost dog.
words.ex_cn: 他为失去的狗感到悲痛。
words.en: To feel or express deep sorrow or distress, especially because of someone's death.

words.ex: She lamented the death of her dog.
words.ex_cn: 她哀悼她狗的去世。
words.en: If you lament something, you express your sadness, regret, or disappointment about it.

words.tr:
n. 忧愁
adj.  忧郁的
words.ex: He felt melancholy after the rain stopped.
words.ex_cn: 雨停后，他感到忧郁。
words.en: A feeling of deep sadness, typically with no obvious cause.

words.tr: adj. 郁闷的；抑郁的；孤僻的
words.ex: He was morose after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后变得忧郁。
words.en: If you describe someone as morose, you mean that they are very unhappy, bad-tempered, and unwilling to talk or be sociable.

words.ex: He sang a mournful song at the funeral.
words.ex_cn: 他在葬礼上唱了一首悲伤的歌。
words.en: If you are mournful, you are very sad.

words.ex: The plangent sound of the church bells echoed through the valley.
words.ex_cn: 教堂钟声的轰鸣声在山谷中回荡。
words.en: A plangent sound is loud, deep, and often sad.

words.tr: adj. 忧郁的；乖戾的；严肃的
words.ex: He has a saturnine mood and rarely smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他情绪阴郁，很少微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as saturnine, you mean that they are serious and unfriendly.

words.tr: adj. 痛切的；酸楚的；强烈的；尖刻的
words.ex: The letter was poignant and made her cry.
words.ex_cn: 这封信很感人，让她哭了。
words.en: A poignant piece of writing or music makes you feel sad or full of pity.

words.tr: adj. 感情脆弱的；易落泪的；多愁善感的
words.ex: She was feeling maudlin after watching the sentimental movie.
words.ex_cn: 看完那部感人的电影后，她感到非常伤感。
words.en: If you describe someone as maudlin, you mean that they are being sad and sentimental in a foolish way, perhaps because of drinking alcohol.

words.tr: v. 谴责；强烈反对；悲叹
words.ex: He deplores the violence on TV.
words.ex_cn: 他谴责电视上的暴力。
words.en: If you deplore something, you think it is very wrong or very bad.

words.tr:
v. 吸鼻子；流鼻涕；啜泣
n. 吸鼻子；流鼻涕；啜泣
words.ex: He keeps sniveling about his broken toy.
words.ex_cn: 他一直哭哭啼啼地说他的玩具坏了。
words.en: If someone snivels, they cry or sniff in a way that irritates you.

words.tr: adj. 悲哀的；可怜的；郁郁不乐的
words.ex: Her lugubrious expression made everyone feel sad.
words.ex_cn: 她那悲哀的表情让每个人都感到难过。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is lugubrious, you mean that they are sad and solemn.

chapters.name: Word List 33 负向情绪 烦躁

words.ex: He tried to agitate the workers to strike.
words.ex_cn: 他试图鼓动工人罢工。
words.en: If you agitate something, you stir it up or shake it. If something agitates you, it makes you feel anxious or upset.

words.ex: The unexpected news discombobulated her.
words.ex_cn: 突如其来的消息使她感到困惑。
words.en: To discombobulate someone means to confuse them a lot.

words.tr:
adj. 打乱的；混乱的； 扰乱的
v. 使混乱； 扰乱；“discombobulate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: She felt discombobulated after losing her keys.
words.ex_cn: 她丢了钥匙后感到非常困惑。
words.en: If you are discombobulated, you are confused and cannot think clearly, often because you have been surprised or upset by something.

words.ex: The storm disrupted the train service.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴中断了火车服务。
words.en: To disrupt a system, process, or event means to prevent it from continuing or operating in a normal way.

words.ex: He tries to foment trouble between the neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在邻居之间挑起纠纷。
words.en: If someone foments trouble or violent opposition, they cause it to develop.

words.ex: He frets about his exam results.
words.ex_cn: 他为考试成绩感到烦躁不安。
words.en: If you fret about something, you worry about it.

words.tr:
v. 磨碎；磨擦；（使）烦躁；发出磨擦声
n. 炉栅；炉箅
words.ex: The food was grated into small pieces.
words.ex_cn: 食物被擦成了小块。
words.en: To grate means to reduce food to small shreds by rubbing it on a grater. It can also mean to make a harsh, scraping sound or to cause irritation or annoyance.

words.tr:
n. 格栅
adj. 磨擦的；刺耳的
v. 磨碎；磨擦；（使）烦躁；发出磨擦声；“grate”的现在分词
words.ex: The sound of the grating metal door echoed through the hallway.
words.ex_cn: 金属门刺耳的声音在走廊里回荡。
words.en: A grating is a flat frame of metal bars or a similar structure, used to cover a hole or window, or as a partition. It can also refer to a harsh, discordant sound.

words.tr: v. 骚扰；烦扰；屡次侵扰
words.ex: He harasses his coworkers with loud jokes.
words.ex_cn: 他用大声的笑话骚扰他的同事。
words.en: If someone harasses you, they trouble or annoy you, for example by attacking you repeatedly or by causing you as many problems as they can.

words.tr: v. 不断骚扰；打扰；侵扰；
words.ex: The neighbors harry the old man with loud music every night.
words.ex_cn: 邻居们每晚用吵闹的音乐不断骚扰那位老人。
words.en: To harry someone means to repeatedly attack them or to cause them problems.

words.ex: The crowd began to heckle the speaker during the debate.
words.ex_cn: 在辩论期间，观众开始嘲笑那位演讲者。
words.en: To heckle someone means to interrupt them while they are speaking, especially in a public situation, by shouting out questions or comments, often in order to challenge or embarrass them.

words.tr: v. 大批出没于；成群滋扰；遍布于；寄生
words.ex: The bugs infest the old house.
words.ex_cn: 这些虫子侵袭了这栋老房子。
words.en: If creatures such as insects or rats infest a place, they are present in large numbers and usually cause damage or disease.

words.ex: He interrupted me while I was speaking.
words.ex_cn: 我在说话时他打断了我。
words.en: To interrupt someone means to stop them from speaking by saying or doing something, or to cause something to stop happening for a period of time.

words.ex: He was arrested for molesting a child.
words.ex_cn: 他因骚扰儿童而被逮捕。
words.en: To molest someone means to assault or harass them, especially sexually.

words.tr:
n. 荨麻
v. 激怒
words.ex: The child touched the nettle and got a rash.
words.ex_cn: 孩子碰了荨麻，皮肤起了疹子。
words.en: A nettle is a wild plant with leaves that sting when you touch them. If you are nettled by something, it makes you annoyed or angry.

words.ex: He obsesses over small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他 obsesses 于微小的错误。
words.en: If something or someone obsesses you, you think or worry about them all the time and you cannot think about anything else.

words.tr: adj. 着迷的；（受…）困扰的； v. “obsess”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is obsessed with video games.
words.ex_cn: 他着迷于电子游戏。
words.en: If someone is obsessed with a person or thing, they keep thinking about them and find it difficult to think about anything else.

words.tr: n. 痴迷；困扰；着魔；强迫观念；
words.ex: His obsession with video games made him ignore his studies.
words.ex_cn: 他对电子游戏的痴迷让他忽略了学业。
words.en: An obsession is an idea or thought that continually preoccupies or intrudes on a person's mind.

words.ex: His rude comment was a provocation to start a fight.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的评论是一种挑衅，想引发争斗。
words.en: If you describe someone's action as a provocation, you mean that it is likely to cause a reaction or argument, especially a violent or angry one.

words.tr: n. 恶心；晕眩；疑虑；不安
words.ex: The smell of the food gave her a qualm.
words.ex_cn: 食物的气味让她感到恶心。
words.en: A qualm is a feeling of uneasiness about whether what you are doing is right.

words.ex: The news roiled the financial markets.
words.ex_cn: 这个消息搅乱了金融市场。
words.en: To make (a liquid) turbid or muddy by stirring up sediment; to disturb or irritate.

words.tr: n. 煽动叛乱的言论（或行动）
words.ex: He was arrested for sedition against the government.
words.ex_cn: 他因煽动叛乱反对政府而被逮捕。
words.en: Sedition is the act of encouraging people to oppose or fight against the authority of a state or monarch.

words.tr: adj. 煽动性的；煽动叛变的
words.ex: The speech was deemed seditious and led to his arrest.
words.ex_cn: 这次演讲被认为是煽动性的，导致他被捕。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as seditious, you mean that they are likely to cause people to rebel against the authority of the state.

words.tr: adj. 紧张不安的； 心情焦躁的；易怒的
words.ex: He gets uptight when people are late.
words.ex_cn: 当别人迟到时，他会变得紧张。
words.en: If you say that someone is uptight, you mean that they are very tense, nervous, or angry about something.

words.ex: The loud noise caused him vexation.
words.ex_cn: 噪音让他感到烦恼。
words.en: The state of being annoyed, frustrated, or worried.

words.tr: adj. 使人烦恼的；令人恼火的
words.ex: The vexatious lawsuit wasted everyone's time.
words.ex_cn: 这个烦人的诉讼浪费了所有人的时间。
words.en: Causing or tending to cause annoyance, frustration, or worry.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；性急的；易激动的
words.ex: He was too hotheaded to make a good leader.
words.ex_cn: 他太性急了，不适合做领导。
words.en: If you describe someone as hotheaded, you are criticizing them for acting too quickly, without thinking of the consequences.

chapters.name: Word List 33 负向情绪 愤怒

words.ex: The loud music annoys me.
words.ex_cn: 嘈杂的音乐让我烦恼。
words.en: If someone or something annoys you, it makes you fairly angry and impatient.

words.tr:
n. 鱼饵；诱惑物
v. 下诱饵
words.ex: He used bread as bait to catch fish.
words.ex_cn: 他用面包当诱饵来钓鱼。
words.en: Bait is something which is used to attract fish or animals so that they can be caught. It can also refer to something that is offered to someone to persuade them to do something.

words.ex: He went berserk when he saw the mess in his room.
words.ex_cn: 他看到房间里的混乱时，气得发疯。
words.en: If someone goes berserk, they lose control of themselves and become very angry or violent.

words.tr: adj. 胆汁的；患胆病的；脾气暴躁的；恶心头痛的；让人恶心的
words.ex: He had a bilious complexion due to his illness.
words.ex_cn: 由于生病，他的脸色发黄。
words.en: If someone is bilious, they are bad-tempered or irritable, often because of a problem with their liver or digestion.

words.tr:
n. 刚毛；猪鬃
v. 大为恼怒；耸起毛发
words.ex: The brush has stiff bristles for cleaning pots.
words.ex_cn: 这把刷子有坚硬的刚毛，用来清洗锅具。
words.en: A bristle is a short, stiff hair, usually one of many on an animal or brush. As a verb, it can mean to react angrily or defensively, or (of hair or fur) to stand upright away from the skin, typically as a sign of anger or fear.

words.tr: adj. 脾气坏的；爱吵架的；爱发牢骚的
words.ex: The cantankerous old man yells at his neighbors every morning.
words.ex_cn: 那位脾气暴躁的老人每天早上都对邻居大喊大叫。
words.en: Someone who is cantankerous is bad-tempered and quarrels with people.

words.ex: He felt chagrin when he lost the game.
words.ex_cn: 他输掉比赛时感到懊恼。
words.en: Chagrin is a feeling of disappointment, upset, or annoyance, perhaps because of your own failure.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；暴躁的；脾气不好的
words.ex: He is a choleric man who shouts when he is angry.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个易怒的人，一生气就大喊大叫。
words.en: A choleric person is someone who gets angry very easily.

words.ex: His crabbed handwriting made it hard to read the note.
words.ex_cn: 他难辨认的笔迹让这张便条很难阅读。
words.en: If you describe someone's writing or behavior as crabbed, you mean that it is small and difficult to read or understand, often because it is written in a very small space.

words.tr:
v. 横过；穿过；交叉；
n. 十字架；十字形记号；
adj. 恼怒的；
words.ex: Please cross the street carefully.
words.ex_cn: 请小心横过街道。
words.en: To go from one side of something to the other; to place or lie across something else; to oppose.

words.tr: adj. 有怪想的；想入非非的；任性顽固的；脾气坏的
words.ex: He became increasingly crotchety in his old age.
words.ex_cn: 他在老年时变得越来越反复无常。
words.en: If you describe someone as crotchety, you mean they are bad-tempered and easily irritated.

words.tr: v. 使窘迫；使困惑；挫败
words.ex: The silly question discomfit the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 这个愚蠢的问题让老师感到窘迫。
words.en: To make someone feel uneasy or embarrassed.

words.tr: v. 燃烧；使愤怒或激动
words.ex: Her words enflamed his anger.
words.ex_cn: 她的话激起了他的愤怒。
words.en: To cause to become excited or passionate; to set on fire.

words.ex: The unfair rule enrage him.
words.ex_cn: 不公平的规则激怒了他。
words.en: To make someone extremely angry.

words.ex: The loud noise exasperates me.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让我感到烦躁。
words.en: If someone or something exasperates you, they annoy you and make you feel frustrated or impatient.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；好争吵的；活跃的
words.ex: She was a feisty woman who never backed down from a challenge.
words.ex_cn: 她是个坚强的女人，从不向挑战低头。
words.en: If you describe someone as feisty, you mean that they are tough, independent, and spirited, often willing to argue or fight.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；难驾驭的；脾气不好的
words.ex: The fractious child refused to eat his vegetables.
words.ex_cn: 这个脾气暴躁的孩子拒绝吃蔬菜。
words.en: If you describe someone as fractious, you mean they are easily upset or annoyed, and often complain.

words.tr:
n. 狂乱；狂暴；狂怒
v. 使狂乱；使狂怒
words.ex: The crowd went into a frenzy when the singer appeared.
words.ex_cn: 当歌手出现时，人群陷入了狂热。
words.en: A frenzy is a state of uncontrolled excitement or wild behavior.

words.tr:
v. 生气；用烟熏；冒烟
n. 烟雾；烟气；愤怒；烦恼
words.ex: He fumed when he saw the mess.
words.ex_cn: 他看到一团糟时生气了。
words.en: Fume refers to gas, smoke, or vapor that smells strongly or is dangerous to inhale. It can also mean to emit gas, smoke, or vapor, or to be very angry.

words.ex: He felt indignant when they blamed him for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 当他们把错误归咎于他时，他感到愤愤不平。
words.en: If you are indignant, you are shocked and angry, because you think that something is unjust or unfair.

words.ex: He felt indignation when he saw the unfair rule.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到不公平的规则时，他感到愤怒。
words.en: Indignation is a feeling of anger and surprise which you have when you think that something is wrong or unfair.

words.ex: His rude words inflamed the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话激怒了人群。
words.en: To inflame a situation or feeling means to make it much more intense or serious.

words.tr: n. 发炎；炎症；燃烧；激动
words.ex: The redness and swelling show inflammation.
words.ex_cn: 发红和肿胀表明有炎症。
words.en: Inflammation is a condition in which a part of your body becomes red, swollen, and painful as a reaction to infection or injury.

words.ex: The noise infuriates my neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 噪音让我的邻居非常生气。
words.en: To make someone extremely angry.

words.ex: He is irascible when he wakes up late.
words.ex_cn: 他起床晚时容易发怒。
words.en: If you describe someone as irascible, you mean that they become angry very easily.

words.ex: The irate customer shouted at the clerk.
words.ex_cn: 这位愤怒的顾客对店员大喊大叫。
words.en: If someone is irate, they are very angry about something.

words.ex: His voice trembled with ire.
words.ex_cn: 他的声音因愤怒而颤抖。
words.en: Anger or wrath.

words.ex: He is irritable when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 他累了的时候容易烦躁。
words.en: If someone is irritable, they are easily annoyed.

words.tr: v. 激怒；使急躁；使疼痛
words.ex: Loud noises irritate my baby.
words.ex_cn: 噪音会激怒我的宝宝。
words.en: If something irritates you, it keeps annoying you.

words.ex: The irritation on his arm hurt when he touched it.
words.ex_cn: 他手臂上的疼痛处一碰就疼。
words.en: Irritation is the feeling of annoyance, especially when something keeps happening that you do not like.

words.tr: adj. 青黑色的；苍白的；暴怒的
words.ex: His face turned livid after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他的脸变得青黑色。
words.en: If you say that someone is livid, you mean that they are extremely angry.

words.tr: adj. 喜怒无常的；情绪多变的；
words.ex: He is moody and changes his mind often.
words.ex_cn: 他喜怒无常，经常改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as moody, you mean that their feelings and behavior change frequently, and in particular that they often become depressed or angry without any warning.

words.tr:
v. 抑郁不乐；闲逛；无精打采
n. 闷闷不乐的人
words.ex: He mopes all day after losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 他输掉比赛后整天闷闷不乐。
words.en: If you mope, you spend time feeling sorry for yourself, often because you are unhappy or disappointed.

words.tr:
n. 气恼；讨厌的对象
v. （使）气恼
words.ex: It always peeves me when people are late.
words.ex_cn: 当人们迟到时，我总是很恼火。
words.en: If something peeves you, it annoys you.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；坏脾气的；乖戾的
words.ex: She had a peevish tone when she spoke.
words.ex_cn: 她说话时带着一种易怒的语气。
words.en: If you describe someone as peevish, you mean that they are easily irritated by unimportant things.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；爱发脾气的
words.ex: She was feeling pettish after a long day at work.
words.ex_cn: 工作了一整天后，她感到很易怒。
words.en: Easily irritated or annoyed; peevish.

words.tr: n. 坏脾气；性急；急躁言行
words.ex: His petulance was evident in every word he spoke.
words.ex_cn: 他的易怒在他说的每一个字中都显而易见。
words.en: Petulance is the quality of being childishly sulky or bad-tempered.

words.ex: The child's petulant behavior was a result of his frustration.
words.ex_cn: 孩子暴躁的行为是因他的沮丧所致。
words.en: If you describe someone as petulant, you mean that they get angry or annoyed in a childish or unreasonable way.

words.tr:
v. 激怒；使生气；激起
n. 怨恨；愤恨
words.ex: His rude comment piqued her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的评论激怒了她。
words.en: If something piques your interest or curiosity, it makes you interested or curious.

words.ex: He burst into rage when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他勃然大怒。
words.en: Rage is a feeling of intense anger that is difficult to control.

words.tr:
n. 暴怒；狂暴行为
v. 狂暴地乱冲
words.ex: The angry mob went on a rampage through the town.
words.ex_cn: 愤怒的暴徒在镇上肆意破坏。
words.en: A rampage is a period of violent and uncontrollable behavior by a group of people or by a single person.

words.tr: v. 使人耿耿于怀；令人怀恨
words.ex: The unfair comment still rankles him.
words.ex_cn: 那句不公平的话仍让他耿耿于怀。
words.en: If something rankles, it continues to cause you irritation, bitterness, or pain, often because you think it was unfair.

words.ex: His comments about her appearance really riled her.
words.ex_cn: 他对她外貌的评论真的激怒了她。
words.en: To make someone annoyed or irritated.

words.tr:
n. 褶边；褶饰
v. 弄皱；弄乱；扰乱
words.ex: The dress has a pink ruffle at the bottom.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子的底部有一条粉色的褶边。
words.en: To ruffle something means to disturb its smoothness or neatness, making it uneven or messy.

words.ex: He gave her a scowl when she was late.
words.ex_cn: 她迟到时，他皱了皱眉。
words.en: When someone scowls, they look at someone or something with an angry or irritated expression.

words.ex: He lost his spleen in a car accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在一场车祸中失去了脾脏。
words.en: The spleen is an organ involved in the production and removal of blood cells in most vertebrates and forming part of the immune system. It can also refer to feelings of anger or spite.

words.tr: adj. 愠怒的； 生闷气的
words.ex: He became sulky when he didn't get the toy.
words.ex_cn: 他没得到玩具时变得闷闷不乐。
words.en: Someone who is sulky is bad-tempered and unwilling to be friendly or cheerful because they are annoyed about something.

words.ex: The child threw a tantrum when he couldn't get what he wanted.
words.ex_cn: 孩子因为得不到想要的东西而发脾气。
words.en: A tantrum is an uncontrolled outburst of anger and frustration, typically in a young child.

words.tr:
n. 暴躁脾气；情绪；心情；性情
v. 使…缓和；冲淡
words.ex: He loses his temper when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 当他累了的时候，他会发脾气。
words.en: If you refer to someone's temper or say that they have a temper, you mean that they become angry very easily.

words.tr: adj. 有狂风暴雨的；狂暴的
words.ex: The tempestuous sea made the voyage dangerous.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨的海面使得航行变得危险。
words.en: If you describe a relationship or a situation as tempestuous, you mean that it is full of strong emotions, especially anger or passion.

words.ex: Her testiness was a result of lack of sleep.
words.ex_cn: 她的暴躁是不眠之夜的结果。
words.en: The quality of being easily annoyed or irritated.

words.ex: He became testy when he was asked about his past.
words.ex_cn: 当被问及他的过去时，他变得易怒。
words.en: If someone is testy, they are easily annoyed and impatient.

words.tr: adj. 怕痒的；难对付的；棘手的
words.ex: He is ticklish when someone touches his feet.
words.ex_cn: 当别人碰他的脚时，他会觉得痒。
words.en: If someone is ticklish, they are sensitive to being tickled and may laugh or squirm when touched in a certain way. It can also describe a situation that is difficult or delicate to handle.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；难以处理的；敏感的
words.ex: He is touchy about his weight.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己体重很敏感。
words.en: If you describe someone as touchy, you mean that they are easily upset, offended, or irritated.

words.ex: We sat under the umbrage of the big tree.
words.ex_cn: 我们坐在大树的树荫下。
words.en: A feeling of pique or resentment at some often fancied slight or insult.

words.tr: adj. 未受招惹而自发的；无端的
words.ex: The attack was completely unprovoked.
words.ex_cn: 这次攻击完全是毫无缘由的。
words.en: If someone's behaviour is unprovoked, it is not caused by anything someone else has done and is therefore unfair.

words.ex: The loud noise vexes my little brother.
words.ex_cn: 嘈杂的声音让我的小弟弟很烦。
words.en: If someone or something vexes you, they make you feel annoyed, puzzled, and frustrated.

words.tr: adj. 刻薄的；尖刻的；脾气坏的
words.ex: His waspish remarks stung more than he intended.
words.ex_cn: 他尖刻的评论比他预期的更伤人。
words.en: If you describe someone as waspish, you mean that they are rather bad-tempered and critical.

words.ex: His wrath scared everyone in the room.
words.ex_cn: 他的愤怒吓到了房间里的每个人。
words.en: Extreme anger.

words.tr: adj. 愤世嫉俗的；悲观的；
words.ex: He gave a cynical smile when they talked about honesty.
words.ex_cn: 当他们谈到诚实时，他露出了愤世嫉俗的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as cynical, you mean they believe that people always act selfishly.

words.tr: v. 激怒；“infuriate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: His arrogant attitude infuriated his colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 他傲慢的态度激怒了他的同事。
words.en: If something or someone infuriates you, they make you extremely angry.

words.tr: v. 激怒；“infuriate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: His arrogant attitude infuriated his colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 他傲慢的态度激怒了他的同事。
words.en: If something or someone infuriates you, they make you extremely angry.

words.ex: The movie ended with suspense, and no one knew what happened next.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影以悬念结束，没人知道接下来发生了什么。
words.en: Suspense is a state of excitement or anxiety about something that is going to happen very soon, especially something that could be either good or bad.

words.tr: n. 紧张；紧张局势；紧张关系；
words.ex: There was tension between the two friends after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 两人争吵后，彼此之间出现了紧张。
words.en: Tension is a feeling of worry and anxiety which makes it difficult for you to relax. It can also refer to the state of being stretched tight or the degree of tightness of a stretched string, wire, etc.

words.tr: v. 使心神不宁；使不安；扰乱
words.ex: The loud noise unsettled the baby.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让婴儿不安。
words.en: To make someone feel anxious or uncertain.

words.tr:
adj. 令人不安的；令人担忧的
v. 使心神不宁；使不安；扰乱；“unsettle”的现在分词
words.ex: The dark noise was unsettling.
words.ex_cn: 那黑暗中的噪音令人不安。
words.en: If something is unsettling, it makes you feel rather worried or uncertain.

words.tr:
adj. 蓝色的；
n. 蓝色；
words.ex: The sky is blue today.
words.ex_cn: 今天天空是蓝色的。
words.en: Blue is a color that is between green and violet in the spectrum of visible light. It is also used to describe something that is sad or depressed.

words.ex: The rain dampened the sound of the drums.
words.ex_cn: 雨减弱了鼓声。
words.en: To dampen something means to make it slightly wet, or to make it less strong or intense.

words.tr:
adj. 泄气的
v. 使泄气；“deflate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The balloon became deflated after the party.
words.ex_cn: 派对后气球瘪了。
words.en: If you feel deflated, you feel disappointed or less confident because something unpleasant has happened to you.

words.tr:
adj. 沮丧的；低落的；垂头丧气的
v. 使…情绪低落；使沮丧；“deject”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He felt dejected after failing the test.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格后感到沮丧。
words.en: If you are dejected, you feel miserable or unhappy, especially because you have just been disappointed by something.

words.tr: v. 使士气低落；使失去斗志
words.ex: The bad news demoralized the team.
words.ex_cn: 这个坏消息使团队士气低落。
words.en: If something demoralizes someone, it makes them lose so much confidence in what they are doing that they want to give up.

words.tr: adj. 抑郁的； v. 降低；“depress”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He felt depressed after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到抑郁。
words.en: If you are depressed, you are sad and feel that you cannot enjoy anything, because your situation is so difficult and unpleasant.

words.ex: He felt deep depression after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到深深的抑郁。
words.en: A period during which business, employment, and stock-market values decline severely or remain at a very low level of activity.

words.tr: adj. 不顾一切的；极度渴望的；绝望的；
words.ex: He made a desperate attempt to save the child.
words.ex_cn: 他不顾一切地试图救那个孩子。
words.en: If you are desperate, you are in such a bad situation that you are willing to try anything to change it.

words.tr: v. 使沮丧气馁；使灰心
words.ex: The bad news disheartened the team.
words.ex_cn: 这个坏消息使团队灰心了。
words.en: To dishearten someone means to cause them to lose hope or enthusiasm.

words.ex: He felt dismay when he saw the low grade.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到低分时，感到沮丧。
words.en: Dismay is a feeling of unhappiness and disappointment.

words.ex: He gave a dolorous look when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他露出悲伤的表情。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior or appearance as dolorous, you mean that it is very sad and depressing.

words.tr:
n. 低垂；凋萎；萎靡
v. 低垂；凋萎；萎靡
words.ex: The flowers droop in the hot sun.
words.ex_cn: 花朵在烈日下低垂。
words.en: If something droops, it hangs or leans downwards with no strength or firmness.

words.ex: The slow internet frustrates me.
words.ex_cn: 慢速的网络让我感到沮丧。
words.en: If something frustrates you, it upsets or angers you because you are unable to deal with the problems it creates.

words.ex: The phone is expensive.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机很贵。
words.en: Costing a lot of money; having a high price.

words.tr:
adj. 俯卧的；平卧的；给（悲伤等）压倒的
v. 使俯伏；使拜倒
words.ex: He fell prostrate on the ground after the race.
words.ex_cn: 比赛后，他瘫倒在了地上。
words.en: If you prostrate yourself, you lie down flat on the ground, usually in front of someone, as a way of showing respect or submission. It can also mean to be extremely tired or emotionally drained.

words.tr: adj. 面有愠色的；闷闷不乐的；阴沉的
words.ex: He gave a sullen look when his mom asked him to clean his room.
words.ex_cn: 当妈妈让他打扫房间时，他一脸阴沉。
words.en: Someone who is sullen is bad-tempered and does not speak much.

words.tr:
n. 绝望；
v. 绝望；
words.ex: He felt despair after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到绝望。
words.en: Despair is the feeling that everything is wrong and that nothing will improve.

words.tr:
adj. 沮丧的；气馁的
v. 使沮丧；使气馁；“dispirit”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He felt dispirited after losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 输掉比赛后，他感到灰心丧气。
words.en: If you are dispirited, you have lost your enthusiasm and excitement.

words.ex: The downcast eyes of the boy showed he was sad.
words.ex_cn: 男孩低垂的眼睛显示出他很难过。
words.en: If you are downcast, you are feeling sad and without hope.

words.tr: n. 布鲁斯音乐；蓝色；“blue”的复数；
words.ex: He plays the blues on his guitar every evening.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上用吉他演奏布鲁斯音乐。
words.en: A type of slow, sad music, originally from the southern US, in which the singer typically sings about their difficult life or bad luck in love.

words.ex: The violent news appalls her.
words.ex_cn: 这起暴力新闻令她震惊。
words.en: to fill with horror or dismay; shock deeply

words.ex: He is apprehensive about the test.
words.ex_cn: 他对考试感到担忧。
words.en: Anxious or fearful that something bad or unpleasant will happen.

words.ex: The children stood in awe at the sight of the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们看到山时感到敬畏。
words.en: A feeling of reverential respect mixed with fear or wonder.

words.tr: adj. 令人敬畏的；令人惊叹的
words.ex: The mountain view is awe-inspiring.
words.ex_cn: 山景令人敬畏。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as awe-inspiring, you are emphasizing that you think that they are remarkable and amazing, although sometimes rather frightening.

words.ex: The child was frightened by the bugaboo under the bed.
words.ex_cn: 孩子被床下的妖怪吓坏了。
words.en: A bugaboo is something that causes fear or worry, often unnecessarily.

words.ex: The weather was dire, with heavy rain and strong winds.
words.ex_cn: 天气非常可怕，下着大雨，刮着大风。
words.en: If you describe a situation as dire, you are emphasizing that it is very bad or serious.

words.ex: The storm was formidable and destroyed many houses.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴很可怕，摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as formidable, you mean that you feel slightly frightened by them because they are very great or impressive.

words.ex: The crime scene was grisly and made everyone feel sick.
words.ex_cn: 犯罪现场很可怕，让所有人都感到恶心。
words.en: Grisly is used to describe something that is extremely unpleasant and horrifying, often because it involves death or violence.

words.ex: The accident looked horrendous.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故看起来很可怕。
words.en: If you describe something as horrendous, you are emphasizing that it is very unpleasant or shocking.

words.tr: adj. 恐怖的；令人震惊的
words.ex: The accident was horrific.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故非常可怕。
words.en: If you say that something is horrific, you mean that it is extremely unpleasant and shocking.

words.tr: n. 梦淫妖；沉重的精神负担
words.ex: He felt like an incubus pressing on his chest at night.
words.ex_cn: 他感觉晚上有个梦魇压在胸口。
words.en: An incubus is a male demon believed to have sexual intercourse with sleeping women. In a broader sense, it can also refer to a cause of distress or anxiety.

words.tr: adj. 可怕的；恐怖的；令人毛骨悚然的
words.ex: The macabre scene in the horror movie made the audience cringe.
words.ex_cn: 恐怖电影中那可怕的场景让观众不寒而栗。
words.en: If you describe something as macabre, you mean that it is strange and horrible because it is connected with death or violence.

words.tr: n. 噩梦；不愉快的经历；
words.ex: He had a nightmare about falling from a tall building.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一个从高楼坠落的噩梦。
words.en: A nightmare is a very frightening dream.

words.tr:
n. 恐慌；
v. 感到恐慌；
words.ex: A panic spread through the crowd when the fire alarm rang.
words.ex_cn: 当火警响起时，人群陷入了恐慌。
words.en: Panic is a very strong feeling of anxiety or fear, which makes you act without thinking carefully.

words.ex: The redoubtable warrior struck fear into the hearts of his enemies.
words.ex_cn: 那位令人敬畏的战士让敌人心生恐惧。
words.en: If you describe someone as redoubtable, you have great respect for their power and strength, and you may be afraid of them as well.

words.ex: The loud noise stunned him.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让他震惊了。
words.en: To stun someone means to shock or surprise them very much.

words.tr: v. 使惊呆；使惊愕；使神志不清
words.ex: The sudden noise stupefied everyone.
words.ex_cn: 突然的噪音让所有人都惊呆了。
words.en: To stupefy someone means to make them unable to think clearly or to be surprised or shocked.

words.tr: n. 迷信；迷信观念（或思想）；
words.ex: He avoids walking under ladders because of superstition.
words.ex_cn: 他因为迷信而不愿从梯子下走过。
words.en: A superstition is a belief or practice resulting from ignorance, fear of the unknown, trust in magic or chance, or a false conception of causation.

words.ex: He felt trepidation before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前感到恐惧。
words.en: A feeling of fear or anxiety about something that may happen.

words.ex: The old house looks ugly with broken windows.
words.ex_cn: 这栋老房子有破窗户，看起来很丑陋。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is ugly, you mean that they are very unattractive and unpleasant to look at.

words.ex: He felt apprehension before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前感到焦虑。
words.en: Anxiety or fear that something bad or unpleasant will happen; understanding; the action of arresting someone.

words.tr: adj. 令人震惊的；使大吃一惊的； v. “astound”的现在分词；
words.ex: The magician's trick was astounding.
words.ex_cn: 魔术师的魔术令人震惊。
words.en: If something is astounding, it is so surprising or so impressive that it is difficult to believe.

words.tr:
adj. 糟糕的；可怕的；
adv. 非常；极其；
words.ex: The weather today is awful.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天气很糟糕。
words.en: If you say that something is awful, you mean that it is extremely unpleasant, shocking, or bad.

words.ex: He feels panic in small rooms because of claustrophobia.
words.ex_cn: 他因为幽闭恐惧症在小房间里感到恐慌。
words.en: A morbid fear of being closed in a confined space.

words.ex: He was in the throes of a difficult decision.
words.ex_cn: 他正处在艰难抉择的痛苦中。
words.en: If someone is experiencing something very unpleasant or emotionally painful, you can say that they are in the throes of it.

words.ex: The disease afflicted many people in the village.
words.ex_cn: 这种疾病使村子里许多人遭受痛苦。
words.en: If you are afflicted by pain, illness, or misfortune, it causes you great suffering and distress.

words.ex: The illness was a great affliction to her family.
words.ex_cn: 这场疾病给她的家人带来了极大的痛苦。
words.en: An affliction is something that causes pain or suffering, either physical or mental.

words.tr: v. 令委屈；令苦恼；侵害
words.ex: He feels aggrieved by the unfair decision.
words.ex_cn: 他觉得这个不公平的决定伤害了他。
words.en: To cause someone to feel distressed or troubled.

words.ex: He screamed in agony after the fall.
words.ex_cn: 他摔倒后痛苦地大叫。
words.en: Agony is very severe physical or mental pain.

words.tr: n. （身体或精神的）极度痛苦
words.ex: He felt deep anguish after losing his dog.
words.ex_cn: 失去狗后，他感到极度痛苦。
words.en: Anguish is extreme mental suffering or physical pain.

words.tr: adj. 受忧虑折磨的；饱经忧患的
words.ex: The careworn woman smiled gently at her child.
words.ex_cn: 这位面容疲惫的妇女温柔地对着她的孩子微笑。
words.en: If someone looks careworn, they look tired and worried because they have a lot of problems or responsibilities.

words.ex: He felt great distress when he lost his job.
words.ex_cn: 当他失去工作时，他感到非常忧虑。
words.en: Distress is a feeling of extreme worry, sadness, or pain.

words.tr: v. 加苦味于；使怨愤；使难受
words.ex: The unfair treatment embittered him.
words.ex_cn: 不公平的对待使他变得愤恨。
words.en: To make someone feel bitter or resentful.

words.tr: v. 使痛苦；折磨；施酷刑
words.ex: The injury excruciates him every day.
words.ex_cn: 这个伤每天让他痛苦不堪。
words.en: To cause intense pain or suffering to someone.

words.tr:
adj. 极痛苦的；极坏的；糟糕透顶的
v. 使痛苦；折磨；施酷刑；“excruciate”的现在分词
words.ex: The pain was excruciating.
words.ex_cn: 疼痛难忍。
words.en: If you describe something as excruciating, you are emphasizing that it is extremely painful, either physically or emotionally.

words.tr:
adj. 令人痛苦的；折磨人的
n. 咬；苛责；不断的苦痛
v. 啃；咬；啮；折磨；侵蚀；“gnaw”的现在分词
words.ex: He felt a gnawing hunger after skipping lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午餐没吃，感到一阵阵饥饿。
words.en: If you describe a feeling as gnawing, you mean that it causes you to feel anxious or uncomfortable over a long period of time.

words.tr:
adj. 悲痛的；令人伤心的
v. 耙地；折磨；使愁苦；“harrow”的现在分词
words.ex: The harrowing story of the survivors left a deep impression on everyone.
words.ex_cn: 幸存者的悲惨故事给每个人留下了深刻的印象。
words.en: Causing feelings of deep distress or anguish.

words.ex: The infliction of pain is illegal.
words.ex_cn: 施加痛苦是非法的。
words.en: The act of imposing something unpleasant or painful on someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 使人厌烦的；令人生气的
words.ex: The irksome noise from the construction site kept me awake all night.
words.ex_cn: 建筑工地的恼人噪音让我整晚都没睡着。
words.en: If something is irksome, it annoys you.

words.ex: He was mortified when he forgot his lines on stage.
words.ex_cn: 当他忘记舞台上的台词时，他感到非常羞愧。
words.en: To mortify someone means to cause them to feel very embarrassed or ashamed. To mortify a part of your body means to discipline it by denying it things that it wants or needs.

words.tr: n. 严酷的考验；痛苦的经历；煎熬
words.ex: He went through a long ordeal before he found peace.
words.ex_cn: 他在找到平静之前经历了一段漫长的磨难。
words.en: An ordeal is a very unpleasant and prolonged experience.

words.tr: n. 一阵剧痛；突然而强烈的情感
words.ex: He felt a pang of guilt after lying.
words.ex_cn: 他说谎后感到一阵内疚。
words.en: A pang is a sudden strong feeling of physical or emotional pain.

words.ex: He had a setback when he failed the test.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格，遇到了挫折。
words.en: A setback is an event that delays your progress or reverses some of the progress that you have made.

words.tr:
v. 阻挠；妨碍；挫败
n. 横坐板
words.ex: The rain thwarted our picnic plans.
words.ex_cn: 雨水破坏了我们的野餐计划。
words.en: If you thwart someone or thwart their plans, you prevent them from doing or getting what they want.

words.tr:
n. 痛苦；折磨；令人痛苦的东西
v. 折磨；使痛苦；烦扰；纠缠；戏弄
words.ex: The loss of his dog was a deep torment.
words.ex_cn: 失去他的狗是一种深深的痛苦。
words.en: Torment refers to severe physical or mental suffering, or to cause someone to experience such suffering.

words.tr:
n. 酷刑；拷打
v. 拷打；折磨
words.ex: The prisoner suffered from torture during the war.
words.ex_cn: 这名囚犯在战争期间遭受了酷刑。
words.en: Torture is the act of deliberately inflicting severe physical or psychological pain on someone, typically to extract information or a confession, or as a punishment.

words.tr:
n. （一阵）剧痛；（一阵）不快
v. （使）感到一阵剧痛
words.ex: He felt a twinge in his leg after running.
words.ex_cn: 他跑步后腿里一阵刺痛。
words.en: A twinge is a sudden, sharp pain or emotion.

words.ex: He felt great woe after losing his dog.
words.ex_cn: 他失去狗后感到极大的悲伤。
words.en: Woe is great sadness.

words.tr:
n. 艰辛；艰苦劳动；痛苦；分娩的阵痛
v. 辛苦工作；发生或经受阵痛
words.ex: His travail helped him succeed in the end.
words.ex_cn: 他的艰辛最终让他取得了成功。
words.en: Travail refers to painful or laborious effort, especially in the context of work or childbirth.

words.ex: The software allows you to truncate long filenames.
words.ex_cn: 该软件允许你截断过长的文件名。
words.en: To shorten something by cutting off the top or the end.

words.ex: The farmer used a harrow to break up the soil.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用耙来松土。
words.en: A harrow is a piece of farm equipment that is used to break up and smooth out the surface of the soil.

words.tr: v. 把…强加给；使遭受；使承受
words.ex: The storm inflicted heavy damage on the village.
words.ex_cn: 风暴给村庄造成了严重破坏。
words.en: If you inflict something unpleasant on someone, you make them suffer it.

words.tr:
n. 灾难；祸患；鞭子
v. 鞭打；折磨；使受苦难
words.ex: Pollution is a scourge on the environment.
words.ex_cn: 污染是对环境的祸害。
words.en: A scourge is something that causes a lot of trouble or suffering, or a whip used as an instrument of punishment.

words.ex: He felt animosity toward his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对邻居感到敌意。
words.en: Animosity is a strong feeling of dislike and anger towards someone.

words.ex: He spoke with animus against his rival.
words.ex_cn: 他带着敌意谈论他的对手。
words.en: A feeling of strong dislike or hatred.

words.ex: He has an aversion to spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他厌恶辛辣食物。
words.en: A strong dislike or disinclination towards someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 可恶的；令人憎恶的；令人痛恨的
words.ex: He finds lying to friends abhorrent.
words.ex_cn: 他认为对朋友撒谎是令人厌恶的。
words.en: If something is abhorrent to you, you hate it very much, often because you think it is immoral or wrong.

words.ex: The aggression of the army caused many deaths.
words.ex_cn: 军队的侵略导致了许多人死亡。
words.en: Aggression is a violent or hostile behavior towards another person or country.

words.ex: He gave an antagonistic reply to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了敌对的答复。
words.en: If someone is antagonistic to someone or something, they show hatred or opposition towards them.

words.ex: He felt boredom during the long meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在漫长的会议中感到无聊。
words.en: Boredom is the state of feeling bored.

words.ex: He detests eating broccoli.
words.ex_cn: 他讨厌吃西兰花。
words.en: If you detest something, you dislike it intensely.

words.ex: He resents being ignored by his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他怨恨被老板忽视。
words.en: If you resent someone or something, you feel bitter and angry about them.

words.ex: He felt resentment after being ignored by his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他被朋友忽视后感到怨恨。
words.en: Resentment is a feeling of anger or bitterness about something that you believe is unfair.

words.ex: She felt revulsion when she saw the dirty food.
words.ex_cn: 当她看到那脏兮兮的食物时，感到非常厌恶。
words.en: A sudden and intense feeling of disgust or loathing.

words.tr: adj. 味道不好的；让人不快的；难以接受的；
words.ex: The soup was unpalatable and too salty.
words.ex_cn: 这汤味道不好，太咸了。
words.en: If you describe an idea as unpalatable, you mean that you find it unpleasant and difficult to accept.

words.ex: He swore a vendetta against his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他向邻居发誓要报仇。
words.en: A vendetta is a prolonged bitter quarrel with or campaign against someone.

words.tr: n. 厌恶；憎恶；强烈的反感
words.ex: He felt loathing for the cruel teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他厌恶那个残忍的老师。
words.en: Loathing is a feeling of intense dislike or disgust.

chapters.name: Word List 35 身体特征 肥胖

words.ex: The buxom woman smiled warmly at the children.
words.ex_cn: 这位丰满的女士对孩子们温暖地笑了。
words.en: If you describe a woman as buxom, you mean that she has a full, rounded figure and is usually large-breasted.

words.tr: adj. 天使般可爱的；天使般纯真的
words.ex: The cherubic boy smiled at everyone.
words.ex_cn: 那个天使般的孩子对每个人微笑。
words.en: Having the innocence or plump prettiness of a cherub.

words.ex: The corpulent man walks slowly.
words.ex_cn: 这位肥胖的男人走得很慢。
words.en: If you describe someone as corpulent, you mean they are fat.

words.ex: His corpulence made it hard to walk fast.
words.ex_cn: 他的肥胖使他难以快走。
words.en: The state of being fat or overweight.

words.ex: The paunchy man walks slowly down the street.
words.ex_cn: 这位肚子凸出的男人慢慢地走在街上。
words.en: Having a large and protruding belly; potbellied.

words.tr:
adj. 丰满的；肥胖的
v. （使）圆胖；（使）鼓起
adv. 噗通地；直接地
words.ex: The baby has plump cheeks.
words.ex_cn: 这个婴儿有圆润的脸颊。
words.en: Having a full rounded shape; chubby.

words.tr: adj. 既胖又圆的；洪亮的
words.ex: The old man has a rotund belly.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人有一个圆滚滚的肚子。
words.en: If someone is rotund, they are round and fat.

words.tr:
v. 蹲；蹲坐；擅自占住
n. 蹲；偷住的房子；蹲坐
adj. 矮而宽的；矮胖的
words.ex: He does a squat every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上做深蹲。
words.en: If you squat, you lower yourself towards the ground, balancing on your feet with your legs bent.

words.ex: He is obese because he eats too much junk food.
words.ex_cn: 他因为吃太多垃圾食品而肥胖。
words.en: If someone is obese, they are extremely fat.

words.ex: He is a stocky man with strong arms.
words.ex_cn: 他是个身材敦实、手臂强壮的人。
words.en: A stocky person is broad and solidly built.

words.ex: The old tree has a stout trunk.
words.ex_cn: 这棵老树有一个粗壮的树干。
words.en: Someone who is stout is rather fat or heavy.

chapters.name: Word List 35 身体特征 健康

words.ex: Eating healthy food helps with longevity.
words.ex_cn: 健康饮食有助于长寿。
words.en: Longevity refers to the length or duration of an individual's life, especially when it is unusually long.

words.tr: n. 补药；滋补品；奎宁水
words.ex: He drank a tonic to feel better.
words.ex_cn: 他喝了一杯滋补剂来感觉好些。
words.en: A tonic is a medicine that makes you feel stronger, healthier, and less tired.

chapters.name: Word List 35 身体特征 强壮

words.ex: He is a brawny man who lifts heavy weights.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个强壮的男子，能举起很重的哑铃。
words.en: Someone who is brawny is strong and has big muscles.

words.ex: The burly man carried two heavy boxes easily.
words.ex_cn: 那个健壮的男人轻松地搬了两个重箱子。
words.en: A burly person is big and strong.

words.tr:
adj. 健壮的；硬朗的
v. 强拉硬拖
words.ex: He is still hale at age 80.
words.ex_cn: 他80岁了依然身体健康。
words.en: If you describe someone, especially an old person, as hale, you mean that they are healthy.

words.tr: adj. 能吃苦耐劳的；耐寒的；
words.ex: He is a hardy farmer who works in the field all day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个能吃苦耐劳的农民，整天在田里干活。
words.en: Someone who is hardy is strong and able to cope with difficult conditions.

words.tr: adj. 强健的；强壮的；结实的；
words.ex: The dog is robust and runs every day.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗很强健，每天跑步。
words.en: Strong and healthy; vigorous. (of an object) sturdy in construction.

words.ex: He is a stalwart of the environmental movement.
words.ex_cn: 他是环保运动的坚定分子。
words.en: A stalwart person is someone who is very loyal and committed to a person, belief, or cause and is not likely to change their views or behavior.

words.tr: adj. 精力充沛的；茂盛的；
words.ex: He is a vigorous man who runs every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个精力充沛的人，每天早上都跑步。
words.en: A vigorous person does things with great energy and enthusiasm. A vigorous campaign or activity is done with great energy and enthusiasm.

words.tr: adj. 有男子气概的；阳刚的；强有力的
words.ex: He is a virile man who works hard every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个精力充沛的男子，每天努力工作。
words.en: If you describe a man as virile, you mean that he has the qualities that a man is traditionally expected to have, such as strength and sexual power.

words.tr: n. 男子气概；生殖力；活力
words.ex: He shows his virility by lifting heavy weights.
words.ex_cn: 他通过举重物展示自己的阳刚之气。
words.en: Virility refers to the qualities or characteristics traditionally associated with men, such as strength, vigor, and sexual potency.

chapters.name: Word List 35 身体特征 瘦弱

words.tr: adj. 角的；有角的；尖角的；
words.ex: The angular shape of the triangle is clear.
words.ex_cn: 三角形的角形很清晰。
words.en: having angles or sharp corners; lean and bony

words.tr: adj. 体形优美的；有曲线美的
words.ex: She has a curvaceous figure.
words.ex_cn: 她身材曲线优美。
words.en: If you describe a woman as curvaceous, you think she is attractive because of the curves of her body.

words.ex: He became emaciated after months of illness.
words.ex_cn: 他生病几个月后变得瘦弱不堪。
words.en: To make or become extremely thin, especially as a result of starvation or disease.

words.ex: The sick dog showed emaciation after weeks without food.
words.ex_cn: 这只生病的狗在几周没有进食后变得骨瘦如柴。
words.en: Emaciation is the state of being extremely thin or weak, especially because of illness or lack of food.

words.tr:
adj. 瘦长难看的
v. 笨拙地移动；“gangle”的现在分词
words.ex: The tall boy is gangling as he walks.
words.ex_cn: 这个高个子男孩走路时显得笨拙。
words.en: If you describe someone as gangling, you mean that they are tall, thin, and awkward in their movements.

words.ex: The gangly boy stumbled as he walked.
words.ex_cn: 这个瘦高个男孩走路时绊倒了。
words.en: If you describe someone as gangly, you mean that they are tall, thin, and rather awkward in their movements.

words.tr: adj. 憔悴的；形容枯槁的
words.ex: He looked haggard after working all night.
words.ex_cn: 他熬了一整夜后看起来憔悴不堪。
words.en: Someone who is haggard looks exhausted and unwell, often because they have been through a very difficult or stressful experience.

words.ex: She macerated the fruit in wine overnight.
words.ex_cn: 她把水果在酒中浸泡了一整夜。
words.en: To macerate something means to soften it, or to cause it to break down, by soaking it in a liquid.

words.tr:
n. 高峰；顶峰；
v. 达到高峰；达到最高值；
words.ex: The mountain peak is covered with snow.
words.ex_cn: 这座山的高峰被雪覆盖。
words.en: The highest point or level of something; the pointed top of a mountain.

words.ex: He wears a peaky cap in winter.
words.ex_cn: 他冬天戴一顶尖顶帽子。
words.en: If someone looks peaky, they look pale and ill.

words.ex: He is puny and can't lift the box.
words.ex_cn: 他很瘦弱，举不起那个箱子。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as puny, you mean that they are small and weak.

words.ex: The tree has spindly branches reaching toward the sky.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树有细长的枝条伸向天空。
words.en: Something that is spindly is long and thin and looks as if it is weak or easily broken.

words.ex: She has a slender figure.
words.ex_cn: 她身材苗条。
words.en: Someone or something that is slender is thin and graceful.

words.tr: adj. 苗条的；体态娇美的
words.ex: He is learning Svelte to build fast websites.
words.ex_cn: 他正在学习 Svelte 来构建快速的网站。
words.en: A svelte person is attractively thin and graceful.

words.tr: adj. 修长苗条的；柳树成荫的
words.ex: She has a willowy figure and walks gracefully.
words.ex_cn: 她身材苗条，走路优雅。
words.en: If you describe a person as willowy, you mean that they are tall, thin, and graceful.

words.tr: adj. 苍白的；像尸体的；枯槁的
words.ex: His cadaverous appearance frightened the children.
words.ex_cn: 他那尸体般的惨白面容吓坏了孩子们。
words.en: If you describe someone as cadaverous, you mean they are extremely thin and pale.

words.tr: adj. 瘦弱的；憔悴的； v. “emaciate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The emaciated dog walked slowly down the street.
words.ex_cn: 那条瘦弱的狗慢慢走在街上。
words.en: Someone who is emaciated is extremely thin and weak because of illness or lack of food.

words.tr:
n. 噘嘴；发脾气；大头鱼类
v. 撅嘴
words.ex: The child made a pout when he didn't get candy.
words.ex_cn: 孩子没得到糖果时撅起了嘴。
words.en: If someone pouts, they stick out their lips, usually in order to show that they are annoyed or to make themselves sexually attractive.

words.ex: His calm demeanor made everyone feel safe.
words.ex_cn: 他平静的举止让每个人都感到安心。
words.en: The way in which a person behaves towards others; outward behavior or bearing.

words.tr:
v. 轻拍；轻触；轻敷
n. 轻拍；少量；能手；比目鱼
words.ex: He dabbed paint on the wall with a brush.
words.ex_cn: 他用刷子在墙上点了一些颜料。
words.en: To dab means to touch something lightly and quickly, often with a cloth or your fingers, in order to clean it, dry it, or apply something to it.

words.tr:
v. 打；敲打；击败；
n. 一击；跳动；
words.ex: He beat the drum loudly.
words.ex_cn: 他用力敲打鼓。
words.en: To defeat someone in a game, competition, election, or battle; to hit someone or something many times with your hand, a stick, etc.

words.tr:
n. 大头棒；攻击；威迫
v. 用重器连击；迫使
words.ex: The robber bludgeoned the guard into unconsciousness.
words.ex_cn: 劫匪用棍棒将守卫打至昏迷。
words.en: A bludgeon is a short, heavy club that is used as a weapon. To bludgeon someone means to hit them several times with a heavy object.

words.tr:
v. 撞；碰上；颠簸行进；
n. 碰撞；猛击；肿块；凸块；
words.ex: He bumped the table and spilled his drink.
words.ex_cn: 他撞到了桌子，打翻了饮料。
words.en: If you bump into something or someone, you accidentally hit them while you are moving.

words.tr: n. 烟蒂；屁股；枪托；笑柄
words.ex: He picked up the butt from the ground and threw it in the bin.
words.ex_cn: 他从地上捡起烟蒂，扔进了垃圾桶。
words.en: The end of a cigarette that is left after smoking; the part of the body that a person sits on; a person or thing that is a target for ridicule or criticism; to hit or push someone or something with the head or horns.

words.ex: The two teams clashed during the match.
words.ex_cn: 这两支队伍在比赛中发生了冲突。
words.en: A clash is a loud, harsh noise, like the clash of cymbals. It can also refer to a conflict or disagreement.

words.ex: The car crash was a serious collision.
words.ex_cn: 那场车祸是一次严重的碰撞。
words.en: A collision occurs when two or more objects come into contact with each other, often resulting in damage or a change in direction.

words.tr:
n. 接触；联系；
v. 接触；联系；
words.ex: The two balls made contact when they collided.
words.ex_cn: 两个球在碰撞时发生了接触。
words.en: Contact refers to the act of communicating with someone, especially regularly, or the state of touching something.

words.tr:
v. 蹲伏；蜷缩
n. 蹲伏；蜷缩
words.ex: The cat crouched low to catch the mouse.
words.ex_cn: 猫蹲伏下来抓老鼠。
words.en: If you crouch, you bend your legs so that you are close to the ground and leaning forward slightly.

words.ex: She cuddles her baby every night.
words.ex_cn: 她每天晚上都拥抱她的宝宝。
words.en: To hold someone or something close in your arms as a way of showing love or affection.

words.ex: Exercise can elevate your mood.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提升你的情绪。
words.en: To elevate something means to raise it to a higher position or level, either physically or in terms of its status or importance.

words.ex: He finally embraced the new idea.
words.ex_cn: 他最终接受了这个新想法。
words.en: To take someone into your arms as a sign of love or affection, or to accept something enthusiastically.

words.tr:
v. 鞭笞；鞭打
adj. 有鞭毛的；鞭状的
n. 鞭毛虫
words.ex: The bacteria flagellate to move through water.
words.ex_cn: 细菌通过鞭毛在水中移动。
