words.en: To whip or flog someone as a form of punishment or for self-discipline.

words.tr:
n. 连枷
v. 用连枷打；胡乱摆动；用力地挥动
words.ex: The farmer flails the wheat to separate the grains.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用连枷打小麦以分离谷粒。
words.en: A flail is a tool used for threshing grain, consisting of a long handle with a freely swinging stick or bar attached to it. As a verb, to flail means to wave or swing wildly; to thrash about.

words.tr:
v. 轻弹；轻击；轻拂；忽然摇动
n. 轻弹；轻拂；快速的轻打
words.ex: He flicked the light switch on.
words.ex_cn: 他 flick 了一下电灯开关。
words.en: To move or hit something with a quick, sharp movement.

words.ex: He fondled the old photo gently.
words.ex_cn: 他轻轻抚摸着那张旧照片。
words.en: To handle or touch (someone or something) in a tender and loving way.

words.ex: He gesticulates when he talks about his travels.
words.ex_cn: 当他谈论旅行时，他会用手势示意。
words.en: If you gesticulate, you make movements with your arms and hands, usually while you are describing something that is difficult to express in words.

words.ex: He made a gesture of welcome with his hands.
words.ex_cn: 他用手做了一个欢迎的姿态。
words.en: A gesture is a movement that you make with a part of your body, especially your hands, to express emotion or information.

words.ex: He will hearken to his teacher's advice.
words.ex_cn: 他会听从老师的建议。
words.en: To listen attentively or give heed to something or someone.

words.tr:
v. 举起；投掷；起伏；喘息；呕吐
n. 举；投；掷；起伏
words.ex: He heave the box onto the table.
words.ex_cn: 他把箱子举到了桌子上。
words.en: To lift or haul something heavy with great effort; to throw something forcefully; to rise and fall rhythmically or with effort.

words.ex: He gave the rope a sudden jerk to pull it up.
words.ex_cn: 他猛地一拉绳子，把它拉了上来。
words.en: If you jerk something or someone in a particular direction, or they jerk in a particular direction, they move a short distance very suddenly and quickly.

words.tr:
n. 闪光；一刹那；
v. 闪光；闪现；
words.ex: The camera captured a sudden flash of light.
words.ex_cn: 相机捕捉到了一道突然的闪光。
words.en: A flash is a sudden bright light that quickly disappears. As a verb, it means to shine brightly for a short time or to appear or pass suddenly.

words.ex: He had to lug the heavy box across the room.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不用力拖动那个沉重的箱子穿过房间。
words.en: To carry or drag something heavy with great effort.

words.tr:
n. 突然倾斜；急动；踉跄
v. 突然倾斜；急动；踉跄
words.ex: The boat made a sudden lurch to the left.
words.ex_cn: 船突然向左倾斜。
words.en: If you lurch, you move suddenly and uncontrollably in one direction.

words.ex: He carefully masticated his food before swallowing.
words.ex_cn: 他在吞咽前仔细咀嚼食物。
words.en: To chew food.

words.tr:
v. 轻推；轻触；劝说；鼓动
n. 轻推；轻触；劝说；鼓动
words.ex: He gave me a nudge to start the project.
words.ex_cn: 他轻轻推了我一下，让我开始这个项目。
words.en: If you nudge someone, you push them gently, usually with your elbow, in order to draw their attention to something.

words.ex: Her heart palpitated with excitement.
words.ex_cn: 她的心脏因兴奋而悸动。
words.en: If your heart palpitates, it beats very fast and in an irregular way, usually because you are anxious or frightened.

words.ex: He perspires heavily when he runs.
words.ex_cn: 他跑步时大量出汗。
words.en: To perspire means to produce liquid through your skin because you are hot or frightened.

words.ex: He gave her a light pinch on the arm.
words.ex_cn: 他轻轻捏了她的胳膊一下。
words.en: To pinch someone or something means to squeeze them tightly between your thumb and finger, or between two surfaces, especially in a way that causes pain.

words.tr:
v. 投入；跳入
n. 跳进；骤降
words.ex: He plunged into the cold water.
words.ex_cn: 他跳进了冰冷的水里。
words.en: If something or someone plunges in a particular direction, especially into water, they fall, rush, or throw themselves in that direction.

words.ex: He practices pugilism every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上练习拳击。
words.en: Pugilism is the practice or sport of fighting with the fists.

words.tr: v. 连续猛击；反复拳打；捶打
words.ex: The boxer pummels his opponent with fast punches.
words.ex_cn: 拳击手用快速的拳击击打他的对手。
words.en: To pummel someone or something means to hit them many times using your fists.

words.ex: He punched the wall in anger.
words.ex_cn: 他生气地打了墙一拳。
words.en: To punch means to hit someone or something hard with your fist, or to make a hole in something using a tool.

words.ex: He wrote a warm salutation at the start of the letter.
words.ex_cn: 他在信的开头写了一个热情的问候语。
words.en: A salutation is a greeting or an expression of goodwill.

words.tr:
n. 敬礼；致敬；行礼
v. 敬礼；致敬；行礼
words.ex: The soldier gave a salute to the officer.
words.ex_cn: 士兵向军官敬礼。
words.en: If you salute someone, you greet them or show your respect with a formal sign. Soldiers usually salute officers by raising their right hand so that their fingers touch their forehead.

words.ex: He shoved his way through the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他挤过人群。
words.en: To push someone or something in a rough or careless way.

words.ex: A shudder ran through her when she saw the snake.
words.ex_cn: 当她看到蛇时，全身战栗了一下。
words.en: If you shudder, you shake with fear, horror, or disgust, or because you are cold.

words.tr:
v. 吊起；悬挂；投掷
n. 投掷；悬带
words.ex: The nurse slung the arm in a bandage.
words.ex_cn: 护士用绷带吊起手臂。
words.en: To throw or hurl something with force; to suspend or hang something loosely.

words.tr:
n. 短袜；重击
v. 猛打
words.ex: He put on his socks before leaving for school.
words.ex_cn: 他上学前穿上了短袜。
words.en: A sock is a piece of clothing which covers your foot and lower part of your leg, usually made of cotton or wool.

words.tr:
v. 拍（屁股）
n. 拍打
words.ex: The parent will spank the child for lying.
words.ex_cn: 父母会因为孩子撒谎而打他。
words.en: To spank someone means to hit them on their bottom with your hand as a punishment.

words.ex: He squeezed into the small seat.
words.ex_cn: 他挤进了小座位里。
words.en: To squeeze something means to press it firmly, usually with your fingers or hands, often to get liquid out of it or to make it smaller.

words.ex: He changed his stance on climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他改变了对气候变化的立场。
words.en: A stance is a particular way of standing, especially in sports such as golf or baseball, or a person's attitude or opinion about something, especially when it is stated publicly.

words.tr: n. 中风；划水动作；一击；
words.ex: He had a stroke last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年中风了。
words.en: A stroke is a medical condition in which poor blood flow to the brain results in cell death. It can also refer to an act of hitting or striking someone or something, or a gentle movement of the hand over a surface.

words.ex: He swiped his card to pay for the coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他刷卡支付了咖啡的钱。
words.en: If you swipe at a person or thing, you try to hit them with a stick or other object, making a swinging movement with your arm.

words.tr: adj. 拉紧的；绷紧的；紧张的
words.ex: The sail was taut in the strong wind.
words.ex_cn: 帆在强风中绷得紧紧的。
words.en: If something such as a rope or wire is taut, it is stretched very tight. If muscles or parts of the body are taut, they are stretched tight, often because of physical effort or anxiety.

words.ex: He tautened the rope before climbing.
words.ex_cn: 他在爬山前把绳子拉紧了。
words.en: To make or become taut.

words.tr:
v. （使）发痒；胳肢；逗乐
n. 痒；胳肢；呵痒
words.ex: The feather tickles my arm.
words.ex_cn: 羽毛挠得我手臂发痒。
words.en: If something tickles you, it touches you in a way that makes you laugh or feel slightly uncomfortable, usually because it is touching a sensitive part of your body. If something tickles you, it also makes you feel amused or pleased.

words.ex: The movie tries to titillate the audience with spicy scenes.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影试图用煽情的场景来挑逗观众。
words.en: To titillate someone means to excite or stimulate them, often in a sexual way, but it can also refer to arousing interest or curiosity in a non-sexual context.

words.tr:
v. 抽打；连续击打；翻来覆去；击溃
n. 快节奏重金属摇滚乐；聚会；连续击打
words.ex: The teacher used a stick to thrash the naughty boy.
words.ex_cn: 老师用棍子抽打了那个调皮的男孩。
words.en: To beat someone or something violently and repeatedly.

words.ex: He tosses the ball to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他把球扔给他的朋友。
words.en: To throw something, especially something light, with a quick, light motion.

words.tr:
v. 痛打；猛打；颠簸
n. 重击；猛击；冲击力
words.ex: He wallop the ball with his bat.
words.ex_cn: 他用球棒狠狠击打了球。
words.en: To hit someone or something very hard; a heavy blow or punch.

words.tr:
v. 扭动；摆动
n. 扭动；摆动
words.ex: The baby wiggles her toes when she laughs.
words.ex_cn: 当宝宝笑的时候，她会动动脚趾。
words.en: To move or cause to move up and down or from side to side with small rapid movements.

words.tr:
v. 打呵欠
n. 呵欠
words.ex: He yawned during the boring lecture.
words.ex_cn: 他在无聊的讲座上打哈欠。
words.en: If you yawn, you open your mouth very wide and breathe in more air than usual, often because you are tired or bored.

words.tr:
v. 拍；掴；拍击
n. 拍；掴；拍击
words.ex: He slapped the table in anger.
words.ex_cn: 他生气地拍了桌子。
words.en: If you slap someone, you hit them with the palm of your hand.

words.tr: n. 做手势；做示意动作
words.ex: His animated gesticulation made it clear he was very excited about the proposal.
words.ex_cn: 他激动的示意动作表明他对这个提议非常兴奋。
words.en: Gesticulation refers to the act of making gestures, especially while speaking, to emphasize or illustrate what is being said.

chapters.name: Word List 37 语言 抱怨

words.ex: He filed a grievance about the unfair treatment.
words.ex_cn: 他因不公平的对待提出了不满。
words.en: A grievance is a feeling of resentment over something believed to be wrong or unfair.

words.tr:
v. 抱怨；发牢骚；绞痛
n. 抱怨；肠绞痛
words.ex: He always gripes about the weather.
words.ex_cn: 他总是抱怨天气。
words.en: If you gripe, you complain about something in a persistent, irritating way.

words.tr:
n. 爱发牢骚的人；不满；牢骚
v. 闹脾气；发牢骚
words.ex: He is a grouch who complains every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他是个每天早上都抱怨的脾气暴躁的人。
words.en: A grouch is a person who is often in a bad mood and complains a lot.

words.tr:
v. 发牢骚；抱怨；轰鸣
n. 怨言；牢骚；轰隆声
words.ex: He grumbles when he has to wake up early.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不早起时就会抱怨。
words.en: If someone grumbles, they complain about something in a bad-tempered way.

words.tr: adj. 抱怨的；爱发牢骚的
words.ex: She had a querulous tone when she spoke.
words.ex_cn: 她说话时带着一种爱发牢骚的语气。
words.en: If you describe someone as querulous, you mean that they complain about things in a rather bad-tempered way.

words.ex: The committee issued a remonstrance against the proposed changes.
words.ex_cn: 委员会对拟议的变更提出了抗议。
words.en: A remonstrance is a formal statement of protest or complaint.

words.tr:
v. 咕哝地抱怨；嘀咕
n. 咕哝地抱怨；嘀咕
words.ex: He mutters under his breath when he is angry.
words.ex_cn: 当他生气时，他会低声嘟囔。
words.en: To speak or say something in a low voice that is hard to hear, often because you are annoyed or complaining.

chapters.name: Word List 37 语言 嘲笑

words.ex: He taunted his brother for losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 他奚落弟弟比赛输了。
words.en: If someone taunts you, they say unkind or insulting things to you, especially about your weaknesses or failures.

words.ex: They exchanged light-hearted badinage during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他们在会议期间轻松地互相打趣。
words.en: Badinage is light, playful, or humorous conversation or writing.

words.tr:
n. 轻松说笑
v. 轻松说笑
words.ex: They enjoy banter during lunch break.
words.ex_cn: 他们在午餐休息时喜欢开玩笑。
words.en: the playful and friendly exchange of teasing remarks

words.ex: They deride him for wearing old clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他们嘲笑他穿旧衣服。
words.en: If you deride someone or something, you say that they are stupid or have no value.

words.tr:
v. 嘲笑；嘲弄
n. 嘲笑；讥笑的言语
words.ex: The crowd began to jeer at the losing team.
words.ex_cn: 观众开始对落败的队伍嘘声四起。
words.en: To jeer means to laugh at someone or shout rude remarks at them in order to show that you do not respect them.

words.tr:
v. 嘲笑；嘲弄；
adj. 仿制的；
words.ex: They mock him for his accent.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为他口音而嘲笑他。
words.en: To mock someone means to laugh at them, tease them, or make them look foolish, often by imitating their behavior or speech.

words.ex: His persiflage made the meeting feel light and funny.
words.ex_cn: 他的戏谑让会议显得轻松有趣。
words.en: Persiflage is light, slightly mocking talk or writing.

words.tr:
n. 颈手枷
v. 给…上颈手枷；使惹人嘲笑；示众；公开批评
words.ex: The newspaper did not hesitate to pillory the corrupt politician.
words.ex_cn: 这家报纸毫不犹豫地公开谴责那位腐败的政客。
words.en: A pillory is a wooden framework with holes for the head and hands, in which offenders were formerly locked and exposed to public abuse or ridicule. As a verb, to pillory means to expose someone to public scorn, ridicule, or abuse.

words.tr:
v. 戳；刺；捅
n. 戳；刺；捅
words.ex: He poked the fire with a stick.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根棍子戳了戳火。
words.en: To poke means to prod or jab someone or something with a finger or a pointed object, or to move something in a particular direction with a sharp movement. It can also refer to the act of making a hole or opening in something by pushing a pointed object into it.

words.ex: He answered with friendly raillery.
words.ex_cn: 他用友好的调侃回应了。
words.en: Raillery is the act of making good-humored jokes or teasing remarks.

words.ex: He gave a sardonic smile when she told the truth.
words.ex_cn: 当她说出真相时，他露出了讽刺的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as sardonic, you mean they are mocking or scornful in a humorous way.

words.tr:
n. 嘲笑；嘲弄
v. 嘲笑；狼吞虎咽
words.ex: His joke received a scoff from the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他的笑话引来了人群的嘲笑。
words.en: If you scoff at something, you speak about it in a way that shows you think it is ridiculous or inadequate.

words.tr:
v. 嘲笑；讥讽
n. 嘲笑；讥讽
words.ex: He sneered at her simple answer.
words.ex_cn: 他嗤之以鼻地对待她的简单答案。
words.en: If you sneer at someone or something, you express your contempt for them by the expression on your face or by what you say.

words.tr: n. 滑稽地模仿；哄骗；戏弄；讽刺；
words.ex: The movie is a spoof of classic horror films.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是对经典恐怖片的滑稽模仿。
words.en: A spoof is a humorous imitation of something, typically a film or a particular genre of film, in which its characteristic features are exaggerated for comic effect.

words.ex: They tease him because he wears funny hats.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为他戴滑稽的帽子而戏弄他。
words.en: To tease someone means to make fun of them or try to provoke them in a playful way.

words.tr: adj. 疑惑的；嘲弄的；揶揄的
words.ex: He gave a quizzical look when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他露出困惑的表情。
words.en: If you give someone a quizzical look or smile, you look at them or smile at them in a way that shows that you are surprised or amused by their behavior.

words.ex: He told a silly jape to make his friends laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了一个愚蠢的玩笑来逗朋友们笑。
words.en: A jape is a practical joke or a witty remark.

words.tr: n. 嘲笑；愚弄；被嘲笑的对象
words.ex: He laughed in mockery of her mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他嘲笑她的错误。
words.en: Mockery is the act of mocking someone or something or the state of being mocked.

words.ex: The crowd laughed in derision when he fell down.
words.ex_cn: 当他摔倒时，人群发出嘲笑的笑声。
words.en: If you treat someone or something with derision, you express contempt for them; ridicule.

words.tr:
adj. 开玩笑的；风趣的；诙谐的
v. 轻松说笑；“banter”的现在分词
words.ex: His bantering tone made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他风趣的语气让每个人都笑了。
words.en: Bantering refers to the act of exchanging light, playful, teasing remarks.

chapters.name: Word List 37 语言 称赞

words.ex: The actors stood on the proscenium to begin the play.
words.ex_cn: 演员们站在台口开始演出。
words.en: The part of a theater stage in front of the curtain.

words.tr:
adj. 崇高的；壮丽的；极端的；过分的
v. 变高尚；升华
n. 庄严；崇高；顶点
words.ex: The view from the mountain is sublime.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色是壮丽的。
words.en: If you describe something as sublime, you mean that it has a wonderful quality that affects you deeply.

words.ex: The actor received acclaim for his performance.
words.ex_cn: 这位演员因他的表演而受到赞扬。
words.en: If someone or something is acclaimed, they are praised enthusiastically and publicly.

words.ex: He received an accolade for his excellent work.
words.ex_cn: 他因出色的工作而获得了一项荣誉。
words.en: An accolade is something done or given to someone as a special honor or as a sign of approval.

words.ex: I admire my teacher for her patience.
words.ex_cn: 我钦佩我的老师有耐心。
words.en: If you admire someone or something, you like and respect them very much.

words.ex: The crowd applauded after the performance.
words.ex_cn: 演出结束后，观众鼓掌了。
words.en: To applaud means to show approval or praise by clapping the hands.

words.ex: The audience gave applause after the song.
words.ex_cn: 歌曲结束后，观众鼓掌了。
words.en: Applause is the noise made by a group of people clapping their hands to show approval or enjoyment.

words.ex: I appreciate the beauty of nature.
words.ex_cn: 我欣赏大自然的美。
words.en: If you appreciate something, you recognize its value and feel grateful for it.

words.ex: His work finally received the approbation of his peers.
words.ex_cn: 他的工作最终得到了同行的认可。
words.en: Official approval or agreement.

words.tr:
v. 称赞；恭维
n. 称赞；恭维
words.ex: He gave her a compliment on her dress.
words.ex_cn: 他夸了她的裙子。
words.en: A compliment is a polite expression of praise or admiration.

words.ex: He likes to dabble in various hobbies.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢涉猎各种爱好。
words.en: If you dabble in something, you take part in it but not very seriously.

words.ex: His speech was eulogistic, praising the hero with simple words.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满颂扬，用简单的语言赞美了这位英雄。
words.en: If you describe something as eulogistic, you mean that it expresses praise or admiration.

words.ex: The speaker eulogized the bravery of the soldiers.
words.ex_cn: 演讲者颂扬了士兵们的英勇。
words.en: To speak or write in praise of someone or something highly.

words.ex: They exalt their hero with cheers.
words.ex_cn: 他们用欢呼赞美他们的英雄。
words.en: To exalt someone or something means to praise them very highly.

words.ex: He extols the beauty of nature every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天赞美大自然的美。
words.en: If you extol something or someone, you praise them enthusiastically.

words.ex: The movie glorifies violence as heroism.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影美化了暴力，将其视为英雄主义。
words.en: To glorify someone or something means to praise them or make them seem more important or better than they really are.

words.tr: adj. 光辉的； v. “glow”的现在分词；
words.ex: The glowing sun rose over the hills.
words.ex_cn: 光辉的太阳从山上升起。
words.en: If you describe something as glowing, you mean that it is very positive and enthusiastic.

words.ex: The teacher lauded the student for her hard work.
words.ex_cn: 老师称赞了这名学生努力学习。
words.en: If people laud someone, they praise and admire them.

words.ex: The microscope can magnify small objects.
words.ex_cn: 显微镜可以放大微小的物体。
words.en: To magnify something means to make it appear larger than it is, especially by using a lens or microscope. It can also mean to exaggerate or make something seem more important or serious than it really is.

words.tr: adj. 值得嘉奖的；有功的
words.ex: Her work on the project was meritorious and earned her a promotion.
words.ex_cn: 她在项目中的工作是有功的，为她赢得了晋升。
words.en: Deserving reward or praise; having merit.

words.ex: The company values innovation in its products.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司重视产品的创新。
words.en: Innovation is the introduction of new ideas, methods, or things.

words.ex: The actor received a plaudit for his performance.
words.ex_cn: 这位演员因他的表演而获得赞誉。
words.en: Plaudit refers to an expression of praise or approval, often given in the form of applause or enthusiastic commendation.

words.tr: n. 夸大宣传；吹捧的广告
words.ex: The company's marketing campaign is full of puffery, making exaggerated claims about the product.
words.ex_cn: 该公司的营销活动充满了夸大广告，对产品做出了夸张的声明。
words.en: Exaggerated or false praise or publicity, especially in advertising.

words.tr:
n. 坟墓；
adj. 严重的；
words.ex: They visited the grave of their grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 他们参观了祖父的坟墓。
words.en: A grave is a place where a dead person is buried. When used as an adjective, grave means serious or solemn.

words.ex: The composer's rhapsody captured the essence of the wild, untamed landscapes.
words.ex_cn: 作曲家的狂想曲捕捉到了狂野、未驯服的风景的精髓。
words.en: A rhapsody is a piece of music that is full of feeling and is not regular in its form. It can also refer to an expression of great enthusiasm or happiness.

words.tr: v. 兜售；招徕；吹捧；倒卖（高价票）
words.ex: He touts the new phone as the best on the market.
words.ex_cn: 他吹捧这款新手机是市场上最好的。
words.en: If someone touts something, they try to sell it or convince people that it is good, especially in an aggressive or exaggerated way.

words.tr:
v. 把…归因于；由…引起；
n. 品质；属性；特征；属性；
words.ex: He attributes his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you attribute something to an event or situation, you think that it was caused by that event or situation.

words.ex: He lost his job because of his integrity.
words.ex_cn: 他因为正直而失去了工作。
words.en: Integrity is the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles.

words.tr: adj. 赞美的；赞赏的；称赞的
words.ex: The teacher gave a laudatory remark about his effort.
words.ex_cn: 老师对他的努力给予了赞扬的评价。
words.en: If something is laudatory, it expresses praise.

words.tr: v. 鼓舞；激励；“inspire”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 有灵感的；
words.ex: Her speech inspired the students to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 她的演讲鼓舞了学生们更加努力学习。
words.en: If someone or something inspires you, they give you new ideas and a strong feeling of enthusiasm.

chapters.name: Word List 37 语言 诽谤

words.ex: He denied the aspersion on his character.
words.ex_cn: 他否认了对他人格的污蔑。
words.en: An aspersion is a remark or statement that criticizes someone or something and damages their reputation.

words.ex: He tried to calumniate his neighbor with false lies.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用虚假的谎言诽谤他的邻居。
words.en: If someone calumniates you, they make unpleasant and untrue statements about you in order to damage your reputation.

words.ex: He spread calumny about his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他散布了关于他邻居的诽谤。
words.en: A false statement made to damage someone's reputation.

words.tr: v. 诽谤；中伤；损毁名誉
words.ex: He tried to defame his rival with false stories.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用虚假的故事诋毁他的竞争对手。
words.en: To defame someone means to damage their reputation by saying or writing bad things about them that are not true.

words.ex: He tries to denigrate his rival's ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他试图贬低对手的想法。
words.en: If you denigrate someone or something, you criticize them unfairly or insult them.

words.ex: His derogatory remarks hurt her feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他毁谤的言辞伤害了她的感情。
words.en: If you make a derogatory remark or comment about someone or something, you say something that shows you have a low opinion of them.

words.tr:
n. （文字）诽谤
v. 发表文字诽谤（某人）
words.ex: He wrote a false story about her, and it was libel.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一篇关于她的虚假文章，这是诽谤。
words.en: A libel is a published false statement that is damaging to a person's reputation; a written defamation.

words.tr: adj. 诽谤的；损害名誉的
words.ex: The article was filled with libelous accusations.
words.ex_cn: 这篇文章充满了诽谤性的指控。
words.en: If a statement in a book, newspaper, or magazine is libelous, it falsely harms the reputation of a person or organization.

words.tr:
v. 诋毁；诽谤；中伤
n. 诋毁；诽谤；中伤
words.ex: He spread slander about his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他散布了关于他邻居的诽谤。
words.en: Slander is the action or crime of making a false spoken statement damaging to a person's reputation.

words.ex: The article contained slanderous remarks about the company.
words.ex_cn: 这篇文章包含了对公司的诽谤性评论。
words.en: If something is slanderous, it falsely harms someone's reputation by saying something bad about them that is not true.

words.ex: He can translate words into pictures.
words.ex_cn: 他能把词语转化为图画。
words.en: To translate means to change written or spoken words from one language into another, or to explain something in a way that is easier to understand.

words.ex: He did not agree with the policy, but he did not want to vilify those who supported it.
words.ex_cn: 他不同意这项政策，但不想诋毁那些支持它的人。
words.en: To vilify someone means to say or write very unpleasant things about them in order to hurt their reputation.

chapters.name: Word List 37 语言 讽刺

words.tr: adj. 荒唐的；荒唐可笑的；
words.ex: It's absurd to wear a coat in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天穿外套是荒唐的。
words.en: If you say that something is absurd, you are criticizing it because you think that it is ridiculous or that it does not make sense.

words.tr:
n. 连环漫画；
adj. 滑稽的；
words.ex: He reads a comic every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上读一本连环漫画。
words.en: A comic is someone who entertains people by making them laugh, especially a professional comedian.

words.tr:
adj. 离奇可笑的；滑稽古怪的
n. 小丑；滑稽演员
words.ex: His droll sense of humor always lightens the mood.
words.ex_cn: 他滑稽的幽默感总是能缓和气氛。
words.en: If you describe something as droll, you mean that it is amusing, especially in an odd or unusual way.

words.tr: n. 滑稽离奇；古怪可笑
words.ex: The comedian's performance was filled with drollery that kept the audience laughing.
words.ex_cn: 喜剧演员的表演充满了笑话，让观众笑声不断。
words.en: The quality of being amusing or comical, especially in an odd or whimsical way.

words.tr:
v. 调情；轻率地对待
n. 与多人调情的人
words.ex: He flirts with her at the coffee shop.
words.ex_cn: 他在咖啡店向她调情。
words.en: If you flirt with someone, you behave as if you are sexually attracted to them, in a playful or not very serious way.

words.ex: She gave me a book.
words.ex_cn: 她给了我一本书。
words.en: To freely transfer the possession of something to someone; to cause or allow someone to have something.

words.ex: It's ironic that the fire station burned down.
words.ex_cn: 消防站着火了，这真是讽刺。
words.en: If you say that it is ironic that something happens, you mean that it is odd or amusing because it involves a contrast or is the opposite of what you would expect.

words.ex: He told a silly jape to make his friends laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了一个愚蠢的玩笑来逗朋友们笑。
words.en: A jape is a practical joke or a witty remark.

words.tr:
adj. 爱开玩笑的；说着玩的
v. 开玩笑；“jest”的现在分词
words.ex: He was known for his jesting remarks.
words.ex_cn: 他以幽默的言辞而闻名。
words.en: Jesting is the act of making jokes or saying things in a humorous way.

words.tr: adj. 诙谐的；爱开玩笑的；滑稽的
words.ex: He is jocular during breaks, making everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他在休息时很幽默，让大家笑个不停。
words.en: If you say that someone has a jocular manner, you mean that they are cheerful and often make jokes or try to make people laugh.

words.tr: adj. 可笑的；荒谬的；滑稽的
words.ex: It is ludicrous to wear a coat in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天穿外套真是荒谬。
words.en: If you describe something as ludicrous, you are emphasizing that you think it is foolish, unreasonable, or unsuitable.

words.tr:
adj. 尖刻的；刻薄的；尖锐讥讽的
n. 媒染剂
words.ex: His mordant wit made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他尖刻的幽默让大家笑了。
words.en: A mordant remark is one that is critical and sarcastic. In chemistry, a mordant is a substance used to set dyes on fabrics or tissue sections by forming a coordination complex with the dye which then attaches to the fabric or tissue.

words.ex: The village has a quaint old church.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄有一座古色古香的古老教堂。
words.en: Something that is quaint is attractive because it is unusual and old-fashioned.

words.ex: He faced ridicule for wearing old clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他因为穿旧衣服而遭到嘲笑。
words.en: To ridicule someone or something means to make fun of them in an unkind way.

words.tr: adj. 讽刺的；嘲讽的；挖苦的
words.ex: He gave a sarcastic laugh when she said she was perfect.
words.ex_cn: 当她说自己完美时，他讽刺地笑了一声。
words.en: If you describe someone as sarcastic, you mean that they are inclined to say things which are the opposite of what they really mean, especially in order to mock or insult someone.

words.ex: The cartoon satirizes politicians.
words.ex_cn: 这幅漫画讽刺了政治家。
words.en: If you satirize a person or group of people, you use satire to criticize them or make fun of them in a play, movie, or novel.

words.ex: The comedian's performance was so sidesplitting that the audience could hardly catch their breath.
words.ex_cn: 这位喜剧演员的表演非常令人捧腹大笑，观众们几乎喘不过气来。
words.en: If you describe something as sidesplitting, you mean that it is extremely funny.

words.tr:
adj. 讽刺的；刻毒的；卑鄙的
n. 人造宝石；伪币
words.ex: She made a snide comment about his appearance.
words.ex_cn: 她对他的外表进行了暗讽。
words.en: A snide remark or comment is one that criticizes someone in an unkind and indirect way.

words.tr: v. 使无效；使显得愚蠢
words.ex: The boring meeting stultifies his creativity.
words.ex_cn: 这个无聊的会议扼杀了他的创造力。
words.en: To stultify someone or something means to cause them to appear foolish or to be ineffective.

words.tr: adj. 滑稽的；诙谐的；爱恶作剧的
words.ex: His waggish sense of humor often lightened the mood at serious meetings.
words.ex_cn: 他滑稽的幽默感经常在严肃的会议上活跃气氛。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behaviour as waggish, you mean that they are humorous and often make jokes or amusing remarks.

words.tr: adj. 扭歪的；啼笑皆非的；挖苦的；讽刺的
words.ex: He gave a wry smile when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到这个消息时露出了苦笑。
words.en: If someone has a wry expression, it shows that they find a bad situation or a change in a situation slightly amusing.

words.tr:
n. 滑稽模仿；讽刺作品
adj. 滑稽模仿的；讽刺性作品的
v. 模仿嘲弄
words.ex: The burlesque show was a hit with the audience.
words.ex_cn: 滑稽讽刺表演受到了观众的热烈欢迎。
words.en: A burlesque is a performance or a piece of writing that makes fun of something or someone by copying them in an exaggerated way.

words.tr:
n. 漫画；讽刺画；滑稽模仿
v. 画成漫画讽刺
words.ex: He drew a caricature of the teacher with big eyes.
words.ex_cn: 他画了一幅老师大眼睛的漫画。
words.en: A caricature is a drawing or description of someone that exaggerates their appearance or behavior in a humorous or critical way.

words.tr: n. 幽默故事；滑稽短剧
words.ex: The comedy club performed a series of skits that had the audience in stitches.
words.ex_cn: 喜剧俱乐部表演了一系列让观众捧腹大笑的滑稽短剧。
words.en: A skit is a short, usually humorous play or performance, often part of a larger show.

words.ex: He said it with sarcasm, even though he seemed happy.
words.ex_cn: 他说这话时带着讽刺，尽管他看起来很高兴。
words.en: Sarcasm is a sharp, bitter, or cutting expression or remark; a bitter gibe or taunt.

chapters.name: Word List 37 语言 奉承

words.ex: He adulated his boss to get a promotion.
words.ex_cn: 他奉承他的老板以获得晋升。
words.en: To adulate someone means to praise them excessively or slavishly, often in a way that is insincere.

words.ex: She used a lot of blandishment to get what she wanted.
words.ex_cn: 她使用了许多奉承话来达到她的目的。
words.en: Blandishment refers to the act of flattering or coaxing someone in order to persuade them to do something.

words.tr:
n. 爱抚；抚摸；吻
v. 爱抚；抚摸；吻
words.ex: Her caress made the baby feel safe.
words.ex_cn: 她的爱抚让婴儿感到安全。
words.en: A caress is a gentle, loving touch or gesture, often given to show affection.

words.ex: The restaurant caters to vegetarians.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅满足素食者的需求。
words.en: To cater means to provide food and drink at an event, often as a business service, or to provide what is needed or wanted by a particular person or group.

words.tr: n. 彬彬有礼；殷勤；奉承
words.ex: Her complaisance in the face of adversity was admirable.
words.ex_cn: 她在逆境中的顺从态度令人钦佩。
words.en: Willingness to please others by being polite and not causing any disagreement.

words.tr: adj. 殷勤的；顺从的；讨好的
words.ex: He was overly complaisant to his boss, always agreeing with everything he said.
words.ex_cn: 他对老板过于顺从，总是同意他说的每一件事。
words.en: Willing to please others; obliging; agreeable.

words.tr:
adj. 畏缩的；卑躬屈膝的
v. 畏缩；卑躬屈膝；“cringe”的现在分词
words.ex: His cringing behavior made him look weak.
words.ex_cn: 他谄媚的行为让他看起来很软弱。
words.en: Behaving in a way that shows you are very nervous or embarrassed, often because you are trying to please someone or avoid their disapproval.

words.tr:
v. 奉承；讨好
adj. 更平坦的；更扁平的；“flat”的比较级
adv. 更平直地；更直截了当地；“flat”的比较级
words.ex: He flatters his boss to get a raise.
words.ex_cn: 他奉承老板以获得加薪。
words.en: If someone flatters you, they praise you in an exaggerated way that may be sincere or may be intended to persuade you to do something.

words.tr:
n. 正面看台；大看台
v. 哗众取宠；为博取观众喝彩而卖弄技巧
words.ex: The grandstand was filled with cheering fans.
words.ex_cn: 正面看台上挤满了欢呼的粉丝们。
words.en: A grandstand is a large, usually roofed structure for spectators at a sports ground or racecourse. It can also refer to the act of behaving in a way intended to attract attention and impress others.

words.ex: He tries to ingratiate himself with his boss by bringing coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上送咖啡给老板，试图讨好他。
words.en: If someone tries to ingratiate themselves with you, they do things to try and make you like them.

words.tr:
adj. 讨好的；逢迎的
v. 使讨好；使得到…的欢心；“ingratiate”的现在分词
words.ex: His ingratiating manner made him many friends.
words.ex_cn: 他讨好的态度为他赢得了很多朋友。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behaviour as ingratiating, you mean that they try to make people like them by being very pleasant and agreeable, often in a way that seems insincere.

words.tr: adj. 奉承的；逢迎的；谄媚的
words.ex: He was obsequious to his boss to get a promotion.
words.ex_cn: 他为了得到晋升，对老板阿谀奉承。
words.en: If you describe someone as obsequious, you are criticizing them because they are too eager to help or agree with someone more important than them.

words.tr:
v. 空谈；废话；阿谀奉承
n. 谈判；空谈；奉承
words.ex: The negotiators engaged in a lengthy palaver to reach a compromise.
words.ex_cn: 谈判代表们进行了长时间的谈判以达成妥协。
words.en: Palaver is prolonged and idle discussion, often intended to avoid addressing a problem directly.

words.ex: The show pandered to children's tastes.
words.ex_cn: 这个节目迎合了孩子们的口味。
words.en: If you pander to someone or to their wishes, you do everything that they want, often to get some advantage for yourself.

words.tr: v. 劝慰；使息怒；谋求好感
words.ex: He brought flowers to propitiate his angry wife.
words.ex_cn: 他带了花去劝慰他生气的妻子。
words.en: To propitiate someone means to make them less angry or hostile by doing something to please them.

words.tr:
n. 口水；奴隶贩子
v. 淌口水；恭维奉承
words.ex: The dog slavers at the sight of the bone.
words.ex_cn: 狗一看到骨头就淌口水。
words.en: If someone slavers, they let saliva fall from their mouth, often because they are hungry or excited.

words.ex: He gave a smarmy smile as he tried to win her favor.
words.ex_cn: 他试图赢得她的好感，露出了虚情假意的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as smarmy, you are criticizing them for being unpleasantly polite and friendly, especially in a way that seems insincere.

words.tr: adj. 实用的；功利主义的；
words.ex: The chair is utilitarian and comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子实用又舒适。
words.en: Utilitarian means relating to or adhering to the belief that the value of a thing or an action is determined by its utility.

words.ex: He felt uncomfortable with the adulation from his fans.
words.ex_cn: 他对于粉丝们的盲目崇拜感到不舒服。
words.en: Excessive admiration or praise.

words.tr: adj. 奉承的；摇尾乞怜的
words.ex: He is fawning over the boss to get a raise.
words.ex_cn: 他正在讨好老板以获得加薪。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as fawning, you disapprove of it because it shows that they are trying too hard to please someone, often because they are eager for power or approval.

words.tr: v. 自夸；夸耀；自豪地拥有
words.ex: He boasts about his new car.
words.ex_cn: 他夸耀自己的新车。
words.en: If someone boasts about something that they have done or that they own, they talk about it very proudly, in a way that other people may find irritating or offensive.

words.ex: His speech was full of bombast and little truth.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满空洞的豪言壮语，却缺乏真实内容。
words.en: Bombast is speech or writing that sounds grand or important but has little meaning.

words.tr: adj. 夸大的；言过其实的
words.ex: He gave a bombastic speech full of big words.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一篇充满华丽辞藻的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as bombastic, you are criticizing them for trying to impress other people by saying things that sound impressive but have little meaning.

words.tr: n. 冒充内行者；庸医；骗子
words.ex: He is a charlatan who pretends to be a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他是个冒充医生的骗子。
words.en: A charlatan is someone who pretends to have skills or knowledge that they do not really possess.

words.tr: v. 慷慨陈词；高声朗诵
words.ex: He likes to declaim poetry in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在全班面前朗诵诗歌。
words.en: To declaim means to speak or recite something in a dramatic or impassioned way, often in public.

words.ex: The actor's declamation of the monologue was powerful and moving.
words.ex_cn: 演员的独白朗诵有力且感人。
words.en: Declamation is the act or art of declaiming; rhetorical delivery; harangue.

words.ex: He exaggerates his achievements to impress others.
words.ex_cn: 他夸张自己的成就来给别人留下印象。
words.en: If you exaggerate, you indicate that something is, for example, worse or more important than it really is.

words.ex: His story was an exaggeration of the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事是对事实的夸张。
words.en: An exaggeration is a statement that represents something as better or worse than it really is.

words.tr:
v. 喋喋不休；啰唆；唠叨
n. 空谈；唠叨；闲聊
words.ex: She loves to gab about her latest adventures.
words.ex_cn: 她喜欢闲聊她最近的冒险经历。
words.en: If someone gabs, they talk continuously and eagerly, especially about unimportant things.

words.ex: The palace has a grandiose design with tall columns and golden domes.
words.ex_cn: 这座宫殿有着宏伟的设计，配有高大的柱子和金色的圆顶。
words.en: If you describe something as grandiose, you mean it is larger or more elaborate than necessary, or it is intended to seem very impressive or magnificent.

words.tr: adj. 夸大的；言过其实的
words.ex: He gave a magniloquent speech full of big words.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了一篇充满华丽辞藻的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone's language or behaviour as magniloquent, you mean that it is too elaborate and formal.

words.tr: adj. 朗朗的；宏亮的；做作的；夸张的
words.ex: His orotund speech was filled with grandiose phrases.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了夸大的措辞，显得非常做作。
words.en: An orotund voice or style of speaking is clear, full, and impressive.

words.ex: He wore gold chains as a show of ostentation.
words.ex_cn: 他戴金链子是为了炫耀。
words.en: Ostentation is the act of showing off your wealth, possessions, or abilities in a way that is meant to impress others.

words.ex: He overstates his achievements to impress others.
words.ex_cn: 他夸大自己的成就来给别人留下印象。
words.en: If you say that someone is overstating something, you mean they are describing it in a way that makes it seem more important or serious than it really is.

words.tr:
v. 怒吼；激昂地说
n. 喧闹的话；夸口话；叫喊
words.ex: He went on a rant about bad service.
words.ex_cn: 他大肆抱怨服务很差。
words.en: To speak or write in an angry or violent manner, often for a long time.

words.tr:
n. 大言不惭；吹牛 
adj. 吹牛的
v. 大言不惭
words.ex: He was full of rodomontade about his achievements.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的成就大言不惭。
words.en: Boastful or inflated talk or behavior.

words.tr:
adj. 生硬的；不自然的
v. 用高跷行走；“stilt”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: His stilted speech made everyone feel uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他僵硬的演讲让每个人都感到不舒服。
words.en: If someone's way of speaking, writing, or behaving is stilted, they speak, write, or behave in a formal or unnatural way, for example because they are not relaxed.

words.tr: adj. 浮肿的；肿胀的；浮夸的
words.ex: His legs looked turgid after the long walk.
words.ex_cn: 他长时间走路后，双腿看起来浮肿了。
words.en: If you describe something such as a piece of writing or a speech as turgid, you think it is boring and difficult to understand because it is too serious or complicated.

words.tr:
adj. 吹嘘的；自吹自擂的
v. 吹嘘；自夸；“vaunt”的现在分词
words.ex: His vaunting of his achievements only made others dislike him more.
words.ex_cn: 他对成就的自吹自擂使其他人更加不喜欢他。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as vaunting, you are critical of them because they are praising or boasting about themselves or something they have done in an excessive way.

words.tr: adj. 词藻浮华的；夸大的；做作的
words.ex: He gave a grandiloquent speech full of big words.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了一篇充满华丽辞藻的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone's language as grandiloquent, you mean that it is extremely formal, elaborate, or exaggerated, and is used to impress people.

words.tr: adj. 炫耀的；浮华的；卖弄的
words.ex: He wore an ostentatious gold watch to show off his wealth.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一块华丽的金表来炫耀他的财富。
words.en: If you describe something as ostentatious, you disapprove of it because it is expensive and is intended to impress people.

words.ex: They accused him of stealing the money.
words.ex_cn: 他们指控他偷了钱。
words.en: If you accuse someone of doing something wrong or dishonest, you say or tell them that you believe that they did it.

words.ex: The suspect was arraigned in court yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 嫌疑人昨天在法庭上被传讯。
words.en: If someone is arraigned, they are brought to court and formally charged with a crime.

words.tr: v. 攻击；困扰；抨击；袭击
words.ex: The storm assailed the small village.
words.ex_cn: 风暴袭击了这个小村庄。
words.en: If someone assails you, they attack you violently, either physically or with words.

words.ex: The priest anathematized the heretic.
words.ex_cn: 牧师诅咒了异教徒。
words.en: If someone anathematizes something or someone, they formally curse them or declare them to be evil.

words.ex: The fish has a sharp barb on its tail.
words.ex_cn: 这条鱼的尾巴上有一个尖锐的倒刺。
words.en: A barb is a sharp projection near the end of an arrow, fishhook, or similar object, which is angled away from the main point so as to make extraction difficult. It can also refer to a remark that is meant to hurt someone's feelings.

words.ex: The teacher berated the student for being late.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为学生迟到而责备了他。
words.en: To scold or criticize someone angrily.

words.ex: The teacher castigated the student for cheating.
words.ex_cn: 老师因学生作弊而严厉批评了他。
words.en: To castigate someone means to criticize or punish them severely.

words.ex: The teacher gave castigation to the student who cheated.
words.ex_cn: 老师惩罚了作弊的学生。
words.en: Castigation is the act of criticizing or punishing someone severely.

words.ex: The teacher chastised the boy for talking in class.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为男孩在课堂上说话而责备了他。
words.en: To chastise someone means to punish or criticize them severely.

words.ex: My mother chides me for coming home late.
words.ex_cn: 我妈妈因为我回家晚而责备我。
words.en: If you chide someone, you speak to them angrily because they have done something wrong.

words.ex: The public condemned the corrupt politician.
words.ex_cn: 公众谴责了这位腐败的政客。
words.en: If you condemn something, you say that it is very bad and unacceptable.

words.ex: The teacher will critique the student's essay tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天会对学生的作文发表评论。
words.en: A critique is a detailed analysis and assessment of something, especially a literary, philosophical, or political theory.

words.ex: He is culpable for the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他对这起事故负有责任。
words.en: If someone is culpable, they are responsible for something wrong or bad that has happened.

words.tr:
adj. 该死的；可恶的；糟透的
v. 咒骂（某人下地狱）
words.ex: It's a damn good idea.
words.ex_cn: 这是个该死的好主意。
words.en: If you say that someone is damned if they do something, you mean that they will be in a very difficult situation if they do it.

words.tr: v. 公开指责；告发；揭发
words.ex: He denounces corruption in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中谴责腐败。
words.en: If you denounce a person or an action, you criticize them severely and publicly because you feel strongly that they are wrong or evil.

words.tr: v. 公开指责；告发；揭发
words.ex: The politician was quick to denunciate the corruption in the government.
words.ex_cn: 这位政治家迅速谴责了政府中的腐败现象。
words.en: To denunciate means to publicly declare to be wrong or evil.

words.ex: He faced public denunciation for his lies.
words.ex_cn: 他因撒谎而遭到公众的谴责。
words.en: Denunciation is the act of criticizing something or someone strongly and publicly.

words.ex: He gave a loud diatribe against the new law.
words.ex_cn: 他对新法律发表了一通激烈的抨击。
words.en: A diatribe is an angry speech or piece of writing that strongly criticizes something or someone.

words.ex: The child excoriated his knee when he fell on the rough ground.
words.ex_cn: 孩子摔倒在粗糙的地面上，膝盖擦伤了。
words.en: To excoriate someone or something means to criticize them severely.

words.ex: The chef will flay the fish before cooking it.
words.ex_cn: 厨师会在烹饪前剥去鱼皮。
words.en: To strip off the skin or outer covering of; to criticize severely.

words.tr: v. 大声呵斥；强烈谴责
words.ex: He fulminates against unfair laws.
words.ex_cn: 他强烈谴责不公正的法律。
words.en: To fulminate means to express vehement protest. It can also mean to explode or detonate.

words.ex: The president may be impeached for lying.
words.ex_cn: 总统可能因撒谎而被弹劾。
words.en: If a government official is impeached, they are formally charged with a serious crime in a special government court.

words.ex: He will impugn the witness's honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他将质疑证人的诚实性。
words.en: To impugn means to challenge as false or questionable; to cast doubt upon.

words.ex: His speech was full of invective against his opponent.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了对对手的辱骂。
words.en: Invective is rude and unpleasant things that people shout at someone they hate or are angry with.

words.tr: v. 猛烈抨击；痛骂；激烈反对
words.ex: He often inveighs against the corruption in the government.
words.ex_cn: 他经常猛烈抨击政府中的腐败现象。
words.en: If you inveigh against something, you criticize it strongly.

words.ex: The angry father lambasted the bully with his belt.
words.ex_cn: 愤怒的父亲用皮带痛打了那个欺凌者。
words.en: If you lambaste someone, you criticize them severely, usually in public.

words.ex: He faced obloquy for speaking the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他因说出真相而遭受非议。
words.en: Obloquy is strong public criticism or verbal abuse.

words.ex: He put the bread in the pan.
words.ex_cn: 他把面包放进平底锅里。
words.en: A pan is a round metal container with a long handle, which is used for cooking things in, usually on top of a stove.

words.tr:
v. 指责；斥责
n. 指责；谴责
words.ex: The teacher gave him a rebuke for talking in class.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为他上课讲话而责备了他。
words.en: If you rebuke someone, you speak severely to them because they have said or done something that you do not approve of.

words.ex: The teacher reprehended the student for his disruptive behavior.
words.ex_cn: 老师因学生扰乱课堂的行为而责备他。
words.en: If you reprehend someone, you criticize them severely for their actions or behavior.

words.tr: adj. 应受谴责的；应受指责的；
words.ex: His lying to the teacher was reprehensible.
words.ex_cn: 他对老师撒谎是应受谴责的。
words.en: If you think that someone's behavior is reprehensible, you think that it is very bad or unacceptable.

words.tr:
n. 申斥；谴责
v. 斥责；训斥
words.ex: The teacher gave him a reprimand for talking in class.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为他上课讲话而训斥了他。
words.en: A reprimand is a formal or official expression of disapproval, typically by a person in authority.

words.tr:
v. 责备；指责
n. 责备；指责
words.ex: She reproached him for being late.
words.ex_cn: 她责备他迟到了。
words.en: To express disapproval or disappointment towards someone because of their actions or behavior.

words.tr: n. 堕落的人；不道德的人
words.ex: The townspeople shunned the reprobate, fearing his influence.
words.ex_cn: 镇上的人们都避开那个堕落的人，害怕他的影响。
words.en: A reprobate is a person who behaves in a way that is morally wrong and who shows no regret or shame for their actions.

words.ex: His tone was one of gentle reproof.
words.ex_cn: 他的语气带着温和的责备。
words.en: An expression of blame or disapproval.

words.ex: The teacher reproved the student for being late.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为学生迟到而责骂了他。
words.en: If you reprove someone, you speak angrily or seriously to them because they have behaved in a wrong or foolish way.

words.tr:
n. 结构；建筑物；
v. 组织；
words.ex: The structure of the bridge is very strong.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥的结构非常坚固。
words.en: The arrangement of and relations between the parts or elements of something complex.

words.ex: She upbraided him for his carelessness.
words.ex_cn: 她因他的粗心大意而责骂他。
words.en: To criticize or reproach severely; to scold.

words.tr:
v. 谴责；责难；指责
n. 谴责；责难；指责
words.ex: The teacher censured the student for cheating.
words.ex_cn: 老师谴责了那个作弊的学生。
words.en: If you censure someone for something that they have done, you tell them that you strongly disapprove of it.

words.ex: He made an animadversion on his friend's poor choice.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的糟糕选择提出了批评。
words.en: A critical or censorious remark or comment.

words.tr: adj. 应受严厉谴责的；可悲的；极糟糕的
words.ex: The living conditions in the slums were deplorable.
words.ex_cn: 贫民窟的生活条件非常糟糕。
words.en: If you say that something is deplorable, you think that it is very bad and unacceptable.

words.ex: The critic's excoriation of the movie was scathing.
words.ex_cn: 影评人对这部电影的苛责是尖锐的。
words.en: Excoriation refers to the act of excoriating or the state of being excoriated, which can mean either the removal of the surface of the skin by abrasion or severe criticism.

words.ex: The old adage says, 'Slow and steady wins the race.'
words.ex_cn: 这句古老的格言说：'慢而稳者胜。'
words.en: An adage is a short, wise saying which has been used for a long time and is generally accepted as true.

words.tr: n. 宣言；声明；格言；警句
words.ex: The judge's dictum was clear and final.
words.ex_cn: 法官的宣言清晰而最终。
words.en: A dictum is a formal pronouncement from an authoritative source; it can also be a short statement that expresses a general truth or principle.

words.ex: His speech was filled with gnomic phrases.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了精辟的格言。
words.en: A gnomic remark or piece of writing is short and clever, and it is often difficult to understand.

words.tr:
v. 耳语；低语
n. 耳语；低语；沙沙的声音
words.ex: He whispered a secret to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他向朋友低语了一个秘密。
words.en: To speak very quietly using one's breath rather than one's throat, especially for the sake of privacy.

words.tr: n. 表示爱慕的话语；亲热的表示
words.ex: He called her 'sweetheart' as an endearment.
words.ex_cn: 他称她为‘亲爱的’，作为一种亲昵的称呼。
words.en: An endearment is a word or phrase that you use to show affection or love for someone.

words.tr: v. （贸然）上前搭讪；（唐突地）走近谈话
words.ex: He accosted a stranger on the street.
words.ex_cn: 他在街上拦住了一位陌生人。
words.en: If someone accosts another person, they go up to them and speak to them, especially in a way that seems rude or threatening.

words.ex: The baby babbles when she is happy.
words.ex_cn: 当宝宝开心时，她会含糊不清地说话。
words.en: To babble means to talk rapidly and continuously in a foolish, excited, or incomprehensible way.

words.ex: He blurted out the secret by accident.
words.ex_cn: 他不小心说出了秘密。
words.en: If someone blurts something, they say it suddenly, after trying hard to keep quiet or to keep it secret.

words.ex: They had a quiet colloquy after class.
words.ex_cn: 他们课后进行了一次安静的交谈。
words.en: A colloquy is a formal conversation or dialogue.

words.tr:
n. 公社；亲密的会谈
v. 亲密地交谈；与…融为一体
words.ex: The farmers lived in a commune in the 1970s.
words.ex_cn: 这些农民在20世纪70年代住在一个公社里。
words.en: A commune is a group of people who live together and share responsibilities and possessions, or the act of communicating intimately with someone or something.

words.ex: They communicate well with each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们彼此沟通得很好。
words.en: To communicate means to share or exchange information, news, or ideas, especially by speaking or writing.

words.ex: His converse was the opposite of what he said earlier.
words.ex_cn: 他的相反言论与他之前说的话相反。
words.en: To engage in conversation; to talk informally with someone.

words.tr: v. 射精；射出；突然说出
words.ex: He cannot ejaculate due to medicine.
words.ex_cn: 由于药物，他无法射精。
words.en: To ejaculate means to say something suddenly and briefly, or to emit semen from the penis during orgasm.

words.ex: He faltered when asked his name.
words.ex_cn: 当被问到名字时，他犹豫了。
words.en: If you falter, you lose your confidence and stop doing something or start making mistakes.

words.tr:
v. 急促而含混不清地说
n. 急促不清的话
words.ex: The children gabble when they are excited.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们兴奋时会叽叽喳喳地说个不停。
words.en: If you gabble, you say things so quickly that it is difficult for people to understand you.

words.ex: His prevarication during the interview was obvious.
words.ex_cn: 他在面试中的搪塞显而易见。
words.en: The act of avoiding telling the truth by not directly answering a question.

words.ex: The school will equip the lab with new computers.
words.ex_cn: 学校将为实验室配备新电脑。
words.en: To provide someone or something with the necessary items for a particular purpose.

words.tr: v. 反复地说；重申；重述
words.ex: He reiterate that he is sorry.
words.ex_cn: 他反复地说他很抱歉。
words.en: If you reiterate something, you say it again, usually in order to emphasize it.

words.tr:
v. 拖曳；搅乱；洗牌；移来移去
n. 拖着脚走；洗牌；混在一起
words.ex: He shuffle his feet across the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他拖着脚在地板上走。
words.en: To shuffle is to walk by dragging one's feet along or without lifting them fully from the ground. It also means to mix up the order of things, especially cards in a deck.

words.tr:
v. 含混不清地说话；诋毁；诽谤
n. 诽谤；诋毁；污辱
words.ex: He slurrs his words when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 当他累了的时候，说话含糊不清。
words.en: If someone slurs their speech or if their speech slurs, they do not pronounce each word clearly, because they are drunk, ill, or sleepy. A slur is an insulting remark which could damage someone's reputation.

words.ex: She dismissed his comments as mere twaddle.
words.ex_cn: 她认为他的评论不过是废话。
words.en: If you refer to something that someone says as twaddle, you mean that it is silly or untrue.

words.tr: v. 轻描淡写；打折扣地说；少说
words.ex: He understated the cost of the repair.
words.ex_cn: 他轻描淡写了维修的费用。
words.en: If you understate something, you describe it in a way that suggests it is less important or serious than it really is.

words.tr:
adj. 不夸张的；朴素的；简朴的
v. 轻描淡写；打折扣地说；少说；“understate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: She wore an understated dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条低调的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe something as understated, you mean that it is simple and not exaggerated, often in a way that is elegant or effective.

words.tr: n. 保守的说法；不充分的叙述；掩饰；低调
words.ex: His description of the accident was an understatement.
words.ex_cn: 他对事故的描述是轻描淡写的。
words.en: If you say that a statement is an understatement, you mean that it does not fully express the extent to which something is true.

words.tr: adj. 健谈的；滔滔不绝的
words.ex: He is a voluble speaker who talks all day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个健谈的人，整天说个不停。
words.en: If you describe someone as voluble, you mean that they talk a lot with great energy and enthusiasm.

words.ex: He used subterfuge to avoid answering the question.
words.ex_cn: 他用遁词来避免回答问题。
words.en: Deceit used in order to achieve one's goal.

words.ex: She became tongue-tied when she met her idol.
words.ex_cn: 当她见到她的偶像时，她变得结结巴巴。
words.en: If someone is tongue-tied, they are unable to speak because they are shy, nervous, or embarrassed.

words.tr: n. 俏皮话；妙语；诙谐语
words.ex: His speech was filled with witticisms that kept the audience laughing.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲中充满了妙语，让观众笑声不断。
words.en: A witticism is a clever and amusing remark.

words.tr:
v. 慢吞吞地说；拉长语调说话
n. 慢吞吞拉长调子的说话方式
words.ex: He speaks with a slow drawl.
words.ex_cn: 他说话慢吞吞的。
words.en: To speak slowly with vowels greatly prolonged.

words.tr: n. 无稽之谈；胡言乱语
words.ex: He spoke gibberish, making it impossible to understand his message.
words.ex_cn: 他语无伦次，让人无法理解他的意思。
words.en: If you describe someone's words or ideas as gibberish, you mean that they do not make any sense.

words.tr:
v. 咕哝；（猪等）打呼噜
n. 咕哝；呼噜声
words.ex: He grunted when he lifted the heavy box.
words.ex_cn: 他搬起沉重的箱子时咕哝了一声。
words.en: To make a low, short guttural sound, typically to express dissatisfaction or effort.

words.ex: He used a lot of swear words when he got angry.
words.ex_cn: 他生气时用了许多骂人的话。
words.en: A swear word is a word which is considered to be rude or offensive, especially one referring to sex or other bodily functions.

words.ex: He talked nonsense and no one understood him.
words.ex_cn: 他说了一些无意义的话，没人能理解他。
words.en: If you say that something spoken or written is nonsense, you mean that you consider it to be untrue or silly.

words.ex: He spoke a soliloquy alone on stage.
words.ex_cn: 他独自在舞台上说了一段独白。
words.en: A soliloquy is a speech in a play in which a character speaks their thoughts aloud, often when they are alone on stage.

chapters.name: Word List 39 自身行为 爱好

words.ex: He developed a passion for philately at a young age.
words.ex_cn: 他从小就对集邮产生了浓厚的兴趣。
words.en: The collection and study of postage stamps, postmarks, and related materials.

words.ex: He is a cineast who collects rare film prints.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位电影爱好者，收藏了稀有的电影拷贝。
words.en: A cineast is someone who is very interested in and knowledgeable about films.

words.tr:
n. 爱好者
adj. 高档的；“fancy”的比较级
words.ex: He is a bird fancier and has a collection of rare species.
words.ex_cn: 他是个鸟类爱好者，收藏了许多珍稀品种。
words.en: A fancier is someone who has a strong interest in or love for a particular thing or hobby, often collecting items related to it.

words.ex: The trend shows more people are using electric cars.
words.ex_cn: 这个趋势表明越来越多的人在使用电动汽车。
words.en: A trend is a general development or change in a situation or in the way that people are behaving.

words.ex: He is an addict who cannot stop smoking.
words.ex_cn: 他是个无法戒烟的瘾君子。
words.en: An addict is someone who is unable to stop taking harmful drugs, or someone who is very interested in something and spends a lot of time doing it.

words.tr: adj. 兴奋期待的；急切期待的
words.ex: The children were agog at the magic show.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们对魔术表演感到无比惊奇。
words.en: If you are agog, you are very eager or excited to see or hear something.

words.tr: adj. 业余的；外行的；不熟练的
words.ex: The performance was amateurish and lacked professionalism.
words.ex_cn: 这场表演很业余，缺乏专业性。
words.en: If you describe something as amateurish, you mean that it is not skillfully done or made, often because the person who did or made it was not experienced or professional.

words.ex: He has an appetite for spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢辛辣食物。
words.en: A desire or liking for something, especially food.

words.ex: His aspiration is to become a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他的渴望是成为一名医生。
words.en: A strong desire to achieve something high or great.

words.tr: v. 向往；渴望；追求；立志
words.ex: He aspires to be a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他向往成为一名医生。
words.en: If you aspire to something, you have a strong desire to achieve it or attain it.

words.ex: His avocation is painting on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 他的业余爱好是周末画画。
words.en: An avocation is an activity that you do because you are interested in it, rather than as your main job.

words.tr: adj. 弯曲的； v. 弯曲；使弯曲；“bend”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The bent pipe leaked water.
words.ex_cn: 弯曲的管道漏水了。
words.en: Bent is used to describe something that is not straight but has a curve or angle in it. It can also refer to someone's natural talent or inclination towards a particular activity or subject.

words.tr: adj. 嗜酒的；好饮的；吸水的
words.ex: He is a bibulous man who drinks wine every night.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个每晚都喝酒的嗜酒者。
words.en: Bibulous means having a tendency to absorb liquids or being fond of alcoholic beverages.

words.tr: adj. 令人信服的； v. “compel”的现在分词；
words.ex: His story was compelling and made everyone listen.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事令人信服，让所有人都认真聆听。
words.en: A compelling argument or reason is one that makes you believe it or accept it because it is so strong.

words.tr: v. 投入；献身；“devote”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 全心全意的；投入的；
words.ex: He devoted all his time to helping his students.
words.ex_cn: 他把所有时间都投入到了帮助学生上。
words.en: If you are devoted to something, you care about it a lot and are very enthusiastic about it.

words.tr:
adj. 惹人喜爱的
v. 使受喜爱；“endear”的现在分词
words.ex: Her smile is endearing.
words.ex_cn: 她的微笑很可爱。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as endearing, you mean that it causes you to feel very fond of them.

words.ex: He cooked the meal with gusto.
words.ex_cn: 他做这顿饭时很有兴趣。
words.en: If you do something with gusto, you do it with great energy and enthusiasm.

words.ex: Her infatuation with the movie star lasted only a few weeks.
words.ex_cn: 她对那位电影明星的迷恋只持续了几个星期。
words.en: An infatuation is an intense but short-lived passion or admiration for someone or something.

words.ex: He accepted liability for the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他承担了事故的责任。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is a liability, you mean that they cause a lot of problems or embarrassment.

words.ex: He has a penchant for sweet food.
words.ex_cn: 他偏爱甜食。
words.en: A penchant is a strong liking or taste for something.

words.ex: He has a predilection for sweet food.
words.ex_cn: 他偏爱甜食。
words.en: If you have a predilection for something, you have a strong liking for it.

words.ex: He has a predisposition to catch colds easily.
words.ex_cn: 他容易感冒的倾向。
words.en: A predisposition is a tendency to behave in a particular way or to suffer from a particular condition.

words.ex: He has a propensity for telling the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他有说实话的倾向。
words.en: A propensity is a natural tendency to behave in a particular way.

words.ex: They rejoice when the sun comes out.
words.ex_cn: 当太阳出来时，他们欢呼。
words.en: To feel or show great joy or delight.

words.tr:
v. 喜欢；享受；从…获得乐趣
n. 享受；乐趣；调味品
words.ex: He relishes every bite of his favorite food.
words.ex_cn: 他享受着每一口他最喜欢的食物。
words.en: If you relish something, you enjoy it very much.

words.tr: n. 兴致；热情；趣味；（用于调味的）柠檬皮；橙皮
words.ex: He cooks with zest and loves spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他做菜很有激情，喜欢辣的食物。
words.en: Great enthusiasm and energy.

words.ex: He has a proclivity for solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他有解决数学问题的倾向。
words.en: A proclivity is a natural tendency to behave in a particular way or to like a particular thing.

words.tr: v. 使预先有倾向；使易接受；使易于患（病）
words.ex: Genes can predispose a person to diabetes.
words.ex_cn: 基因可能使人更容易患糖尿病。
words.en: If something predisposes you to think or behave in a particular way, it makes it likely that you will think or behave in that way.

words.tr: adj. 慈善的；乐善好施的；
words.ex: He made a philanthropic donation to help poor children.
words.ex_cn: 他捐赠了一笔慈善款项来帮助贫困儿童。
words.en: A philanthropic person or organization freely gives money or other help to people who need it.

chapters.name: Word List 39 自身行为 暗示

words.tr:
v. 声称；意指；意味着
n. 意义；要旨；主要意思
words.ex: The letter purports to be from the president.
words.ex_cn: 这封信声称是总统写的。
words.en: If something purports to be a particular thing or to do a particular thing, it claims or appears to be that thing or to do that thing, even though this may not be the case.

words.tr: adj. 心照不宣的；不作声的
words.ex: They have a tacit understanding about the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他们对规则有一种心照不宣的理解。
words.en: If you refer to someone's tacit agreement or approval, you mean they are agreeing to something or approving it without actually saying so, often because they are unwilling to admit to doing so.

words.tr: n. 象征物；标志；代金券；代币；
words.ex: The dove is a token of peace.
words.ex_cn: 鸽子是和平的象征物。
words.en: A token is something that represents or stands for something else, especially a piece of metal or plastic that you can use instead of money in some machines or as a symbol of a particular feeling or event.

words.ex: The dark clouds indicate rain.
words.ex_cn: 乌云表明要下雨了。
words.en: If one thing indicates another, the first thing shows that the second is true or exists.

words.tr: n. 暗指；影射；间接提及
words.ex: He made an allusion to Shakespeare in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中提到了莎士比亚。
words.en: An allusion is an indirect reference to someone or something.

words.ex: The dark clouds foreshadow a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something foreshadows an event or situation, it suggests that it will happen.

words.tr: n. 含意；可能的影响（或后果）；暗示；
words.ex: The implication of his words was that he was sorry.
words.ex_cn: 他话中的含意是他很抱歉。
words.en: An implication is a possible future effect or result of an action or decision, often one that is not immediately obvious.

words.ex: She had only the faintest inkling of what he was planning.
words.ex_cn: 她对他正在策划的事情只有一点模糊的概念。
words.en: An inkling is a slight knowledge or suspicion of something.

words.ex: He insinuated that she was lying.
words.ex_cn: 他暗示她在撒谎。
words.en: If you say that someone insinuates that something bad is the case, you mean that they say it in an indirect way.

words.ex: Her calm demeanor bespeaks confidence.
words.ex_cn: 她平静的举止表明了自信。
words.en: If someone's action or behaviour bespeaks a particular quality, feeling, or experience, it shows that they have that quality, feeling, or experience.

words.ex: The symbol x denotes an unknown number.
words.ex_cn: 符号 x 表示一个未知数。
words.en: If one thing denotes another, it is a sign or indication of it.

words.ex: The dark clouds are an indication of rain.
words.ex_cn: 乌云是下雨的迹象。
words.en: An indication is a sign which suggests, for example, what people are thinking or feeling.

chapters.name: Word List 39 自身行为 暴露

words.ex: The tree has bare branches in winter.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树在冬天有光秃秃的树枝。
words.en: If part of your body is bare, it is not covered by any clothing.

words.ex: The scientist debunked the myth that sugar makes children hyper.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家揭穿了糖会使孩子多动的谬论。
words.en: If you debunk a widely held belief, you show that it is false. If you debunk something that is widely admired, you show that it is not as good as people think it is.

words.ex: He refused to disclose the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝透露这个秘密。
words.en: To disclose information means to make it known to the public.

words.ex: He won't divulge the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他不会泄露这个秘密。
words.en: If you divulge a piece of secret or private information, you tell it to someone.

words.ex: The worker had long exposure to loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 这名工人长期暴露在噪音中。
words.en: The condition of being exposed to something, especially to something harmful or unpleasant.

words.tr: v. 显露；泄露；透露；“reveal”的现在分词； adj. 有启示作用的；
words.ex: The mirror revealed his true feelings.
words.ex_cn: 镜子显露了他真实的情感。
words.en: Providing interesting or significant information that was not previously known or realized.

words.tr: n. 揭露；被揭示的真相；
words.ex: The letter was a revelation about his secret life.
words.ex_cn: 这封信揭露了他隐秘的生活。
words.en: A revelation is a surprising and previously unknown fact that has been disclosed to others.

chapters.name: Word List 39 自身行为 表演

words.tr:
n. 全体演员；
v. 投掷；扔；投射；
words.ex: The cast of the play performed very well.
words.ex_cn: 这部剧的全体演员表演得非常好。
words.en: To cast something means to throw it forcefully in a particular direction.

words.ex: His histrionic gestures made the play very exciting.
words.ex_cn: 他戏剧性的手势让这场戏非常精彩。
words.en: If you refer to someone's behaviour as histrionic, you are critical of it because it is very dramatic, exaggerated, and insincere.

words.ex: His repertoire includes singing, dancing, and acting.
words.ex_cn: 他的全部才能包括唱歌、跳舞和表演。
words.en: A repertoire is all the plays, songs, pieces of music, etc. that a performer or group knows and can perform.

words.ex: The movie's premiere was held last night.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的首映昨晚举行。
words.en: The first public performance of a play, film, or other form of entertainment.

words.ex: He gave a presentation about climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一个关于气候变化的报告。
words.en: The act of showing or explaining something to an audience.

words.ex: The app rendering free tools for students.
words.ex_cn: 这个应用程序为学生提供免费工具。
words.en: A rendering is a performance, interpretation, or translation of a piece of art, music, or text.

words.ex: The rendition of the song by the singer moved everyone.
words.ex_cn: 歌手对这首歌的演出打动了所有人。
words.en: A rendition of a play, poem, or piece of music is a performance of it.

words.ex: He has a thespian talent for acting.
words.ex_cn: 他有戏剧表演的天赋。
words.en: Relating to drama and the theater; an actor or actress.

words.tr:
n. 首次露面；初次登场
v. 初次登场；首次推出
words.ex: He made his debut on stage last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚在舞台上首次登台。
words.en: The debut of a performer or sports player is their first public performance, appearance, or recording.

chapters.name: Word List 39 自身行为 偿赎

words.ex: He received compensation for his injured leg.
words.ex_cn: 他因腿部受伤获得了赔偿。
words.en: Compensation is something, typically money, awarded to someone in recognition of loss, suffering, or injury.

words.tr: adj. 不能补救的；不能挽回的
words.ex: The damage to the painting was irremediable.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画的损坏是无法挽回的。
words.en: If something is irremediable, it is impossible to correct or improve.

words.tr:
n. 奖励；报酬；
v. 奖励；回报；
words.ex: He got a reward for winning the contest.
words.ex_cn: 他因赢得比赛而得到了奖励。
words.en: Something given or received in return for a deed or service rendered.

words.ex: The company decided to amortize the cost of the new machinery over five years.
words.ex_cn: 公司决定在五年内摊销新机器的成本。
words.en: To amortize a debt or cost means to pay it back or write it off gradually over a period of time.

words.ex: He tried to atone for his mistakes by working harder.
words.ex_cn: 他通过更加努力工作来弥补自己的错误。
words.en: If you atone for something that you have done, you do something to show that you are sorry you did it.

words.ex: The company is bankrupt after losing all its money.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司失去所有钱后破产了。
words.en: If a person or a company is bankrupt, they have been declared by a court of law to be unable to pay their debts.

words.ex: The company will compensate you for the delay.
words.ex_cn: 公司会因延误而补偿你。
words.en: If you compensate for a lack of something or for something you have done wrong, you do something to show that you are sorry or that you are trying to make things better.

words.ex: He got compensatory pay for working overtime.
words.ex_cn: 他因加班获得了补偿性工资。
words.en: Compensatory is used to describe something that is intended to compensate for something else, especially loss or damage.

words.ex: The hotel gave us complimentary breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 酒店免费赠送了我们早餐。
words.en: If something is complimentary, it is given or done free of charge. It can also mean expressing a compliment; praising or approving.

words.ex: He tried to expiate his guilt by helping the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过帮助穷人来赎罪。
words.en: If you expiate guilty feelings or bad behaviour, you do something to show that you are sorry for what you have done.

words.ex: The insurance company agreed to indemnify the victims for their losses.
words.ex_cn: 保险公司同意赔偿受害者的损失。
words.en: To indemnify someone means to compensate them for harm or loss they have suffered.

words.ex: The company paid indemnity for the damaged car.
words.ex_cn: 公司为损坏的汽车支付了保险赔偿。
words.en: If something provides indemnity, it provides insurance or protection against damage or loss, especially in the form of a legal agreement.

words.tr: adj. 不能抵偿的；不能平息的
words.ex: His crimes were deemed inexpiable by society.
words.ex_cn: 他的罪行被社会视为不可赎回的。
words.en: If a crime or sin is inexpiable, it is so bad that it cannot be forgiven or atoned for.

words.ex: The company went bankrupt due to insolvency.
words.ex_cn: 由于资不抵债，这家公司破产了。
words.en: The state of being unable to pay one's debts.

words.ex: He paid the first installment last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周支付了第一期分期付款。
words.en: An installment is one of the amounts, usually equal, into which a debt is divided for payment at stated intervals over a fixed period.

words.tr: adj. 不能赎回的；不能兑现的；不可救药的
words.ex: The bond is irredeemable and will never be paid back.
words.ex_cn: 这种债券是不能赎回的，永远不会被偿还。
words.en: If you describe something as irredeemable, you mean that it is so bad or undesirable that there is no way to improve it or make it acceptable.

words.tr: v. 清算；变卖；消除；铲除
words.ex: The company will liquidate its assets to pay debts.
words.ex_cn: 公司将变卖资产来偿还债务。
words.en: To liquidate a company means to sell its assets in order to pay its debts, or to sell an asset for cash.

words.ex: The government declared a moratorium on new construction.
words.ex_cn: 政府宣布暂停新的建筑项目。
words.en: A moratorium is a temporary prohibition of an activity.

words.ex: We went to the matinee on Saturday.
words.ex_cn: 我们在周六去看午场电影。
words.en: A matinee is a performance of a play or a showing of a movie which takes place in the afternoon.

words.ex: The rain offset the heat yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 昨天的雨抵消了炎热。
words.en: If one thing is offset by another, the effect of the first thing is reduced by the second, so that any advantage or disadvantage is cancelled out.

words.ex: The kidnappers asked for a ransom of $1 million.
words.ex_cn: 绑匪要求一百万美元的赎金。
words.en: A ransom is the money that is demanded for the release of a person who has been kidnapped.

words.tr:
v. 补偿；赔偿；报酬
n. 报偿；回礼；赔偿
words.ex: The company recompense the worker for the lost time.
words.ex_cn: 公司补偿了工人损失的时间。
words.en: If you are given something, usually money, in recompense, you are given it as a reward or because you have suffered.

words.ex: The company will reimburse you for your travel expenses.
words.ex_cn: 公司会报销你的旅行费用。
words.en: If you reimburse someone for something, you pay them back the money that they have spent or lost because of it.

words.ex: The company will remunerate you for your extra work.
words.ex_cn: 公司会为你的额外工作支付报酬。
words.en: To remunerate someone means to pay them for work that they have done.

words.tr: adj. 可补救的；可补偿的
words.ex: The broken bike is reparable.
words.ex_cn: 这辆坏了的自行车可以修好。
words.en: If something is reparable, it is possible to fix or mend it.

words.ex: The preparation for the exam took two weeks.
words.ex_cn: 考试的准备花了两周时间。
words.en: Preparation is the process of getting something ready for use or for a particular purpose.

words.ex: She replenished the water bottle after the hike.
words.ex_cn: 她在徒步后补充了水瓶里的水。
words.en: If you replenish something, you make it full or complete again.

words.tr: n. 归还；赔偿；恢复原状
words.ex: The court ordered restitution for the damaged property.
words.ex_cn: 法院命令对受损财产进行赔偿。
words.en: The act of restoring something to its original state or the act of compensating for loss or damage.

words.tr:
v. 补充；
n. 补充物；附加费；
words.ex: He supplements his income by teaching part-time.
words.ex_cn: 他通过兼职教学来补充收入。
words.en: A supplement is something that is added to something else in order to make it complete or better.

words.ex: He enjoys eating Welsh rarebit on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在周末吃威尔士兔肉。
words.en: To fail to honor a debt or obligation, especially a gambling debt.

words.ex: The court imposed a punitive fine for the violation.
words.ex_cn: 法院对这一违规行为处以惩罚性罚款。
words.en: Punitive actions, laws, or measures are intended to punish someone.

words.ex: The king vouchsafed a generous grant to the university.
words.ex_cn: 国王慷慨地赐予了大学一笔赠款。
words.en: If you vouchsafe something to someone, you give or tell it to them, especially in a gracious or condescending manner.

chapters.name: Word List 39 自身行为 超越

words.ex: He works hard to emulate his older brother.
words.ex_cn: 他努力赶上他的哥哥。
words.en: To emulate someone or something means to try to be like them or to do something in the same way that they do it.

words.ex: He can outshine others with his bright ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他能用他出色的想法胜过别人。
words.en: If you outshine someone, you are much better at doing something than they are.

words.ex: The new car outstrips the old one in speed.
words.ex_cn: 这辆新车在速度上超过了旧车。
words.en: To outstrip means to go faster or to do better than someone or something else.

words.ex: He wants to pursue his dream of becoming a writer.
words.ex_cn: 他想追求成为作家的梦想。
words.en: If you pursue an activity, interest, or plan, you carry it out or follow it.

words.ex: He surpassed his brother in math scores.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学成绩上超过了他弟弟。
words.en: If one person or thing surpasses another, the first is better than, or has more of a particular quality than, the second.

words.tr: adj. 可追踪的；可追溯的；
words.ex: The package is traceable using the tracking number.
words.ex_cn: 使用跟踪号码可以追踪这个包裹。
words.en: If something is traceable, it can be tracked or followed back to its source or origin.

words.tr:
n. 踪迹；轨道；小路；跑道；
v. 追踪；跟踪；
words.ex: The dog followed the track of the rabbit.
words.ex_cn: 狗跟着兔子的踪迹。
words.en: A track is a path or route along which something moves or travels. It can also refer to marks left by something that has passed, or the act of following such marks to find someone or something.

words.ex: He finally acknowledged his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他终于承认了自己的错误。
words.en: If you acknowledge a fact or a situation, you accept or admit that it is true or that it exists.

words.ex: The ticket is your admission to the concert.
words.ex_cn: 这张票是进入音乐会的许可。
words.en: An admission is a statement in which you admit that something bad, unpleasant, or embarrassing is true, or the act of allowing someone to enter a place or organization.

words.ex: My parents give me a weekly allowance.
words.ex_cn: 我父母每周给我零用钱。
words.en: An allowance is money that is given regularly, usually to a child, by their parents, or by the government to someone who is unemployed or ill.

words.tr: v. 承认；公开宣称声明
words.ex: He avows his love for her.
words.ex_cn: 他坦承自己对她的爱。
words.en: If you avow something, you declare it or admit it openly.

words.ex: He finally conceded defeat after the match.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束后，他终于承认失败了。
words.en: If you concede something, you admit, often unwillingly, that it is true or correct.

words.ex: He confesses that he made a mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他承认自己犯了一个错误。
words.en: If you confess to doing something, you admit that you did it.

words.ex: She adores her little brother.
words.ex_cn: 她非常喜爱她的弟弟。
words.en: If you adore someone, you feel great love and admiration for them.

words.ex: He showed deference to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他对老师表示尊敬。
words.en: Deference is a polite and respectful attitude towards someone, often because they are older or more experienced than you.

words.tr: v. 神化；把…奉若神明；崇拜
words.ex: They deify their ancient heroes.
words.ex_cn: 他们崇拜自己的古代英雄。
words.en: To treat someone or something as a god or goddess, or to consider them as if they were divine.

words.tr: adj. 虔诚的；献身的；宗教仪式的
words.ex: She spent her mornings in devotional prayer.
words.ex_cn: 她早上用来进行虔诚的祷告。
words.en: Devotional activities or writings are related to religious worship or prayer.

words.tr: v. 置入神龛中；入庙祀奉；奉为神圣；珍藏
words.ex: They enshrined the ancient statue in a golden shrine.
words.ex_cn: 他们把这尊古代雕像置入了一个金色神龛中。
words.en: If something such as a tradition or a right is enshrined in something such as a constitution or law, it is protected by it.

words.tr: adj. 可估量的；值得尊重的
words.ex: The cost of the project is estimable with current data.
words.ex_cn: 根据当前数据，这个项目的成本是可以估量的。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as estimable, you mean that they deserve admiration because they are extremely good or have a very good quality.

words.ex: She has a fetish for collecting vintage clothing.
words.ex_cn: 她对收集古董衣服有一种恋物情结。
words.en: A fetish is an object that is believed to have magical powers, especially one that is worshipped by people who believe in magic. In psychology, a fetish is a form of sexual desire in which gratification is linked to an abnormal degree to a particular object, item of clothing, part of the body, etc.

words.ex: They hallow the old church on Halloween.
words.ex_cn: 他们在万圣节时敬拜那座老教堂。
words.en: To make holy or set apart as holy; to honor as sacred.

words.ex: The film is an homage to old Hollywood movies.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是对老好莱坞电影的致敬。
words.en: Homage is respect shown towards someone or something you admire, or to a person in authority.

words.tr: v. 奉为偶像；盲目崇拜
words.ex: Many fans idolatrize the famous singer.
words.ex_cn: 许多粉丝崇拜那位著名歌手。
words.en: To idolatrize means to worship or admire someone or something excessively and blindly, often to the point of obsession.

words.tr: v. 偶像化；过分崇拜；奉为神圣
words.ex: He idolizes his older brother.
words.ex_cn: 他崇拜他的哥哥。
words.en: If you idolize someone, you admire them very much.

words.ex: They lionize the famous singer everywhere she goes.
words.ex_cn: 无论她去哪里，人们都把她当作名人追捧。
words.en: To treat someone as a celebrity or hero.

words.ex: He showed obeisance to the king by bowing deeply.
words.ex_cn: 他通过深深鞠躬向国王表示敬意。
words.en: Obeisance is a gesture or movement of the body expressing respect or submission.

words.ex: The tribe honors their totem with a special dance.
words.ex_cn: 部落通过特殊的舞蹈来敬奉他们的图腾。
words.en: A totem is an object, animal, or plant that serves as the emblem or symbol of a family, clan, or tribe, often regarded as a spiritual ancestor or protector.

words.ex: People venerate the ancient sage for his wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 人们因他的智慧而崇敬这位古代圣人。
words.en: To regard with respect or reverence.

words.tr:
n. 地址；演讲；
v. 解决；向…讲话；
words.ex: Please write your address on the form.
words.ex_cn: 请把你的地址写在表格上。
words.en: The particulars of the place where someone lives or an organization is situated; a formal speech delivered to an audience.

words.tr:
n. 方法；接近；靠近；路径；
v. 接近；靠近；临近；处理；
words.ex: He used a new approach to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一种新方法来解决问题。
words.en: To come near or nearer to something or someone in distance or time.

words.tr: v. 解开；解脱；解决（纠纷等）
words.ex: He tried to disentangle the tangled wires.
words.ex_cn: 他试图把缠在一起的电线解开。
words.en: To free something or someone from being tangled or twisted, or to separate things that are twisted together.

words.ex: The disposal of waste is important for the environment.
words.ex_cn: 废物的处理对环境很重要。
words.en: The act or process of getting rid of something, especially by throwing it away or selling it.

words.ex: He disposed of the old books.
words.ex_cn: 他处理了那些旧书。
words.en: To dispose of something means to get rid of it, especially by throwing it away.

words.ex: His disposition is calm and kind.
words.ex_cn: 他的性情平静而善良。
