words.en: A thread is a long, thin strand of cotton, nylon, or other fibers used in sewing or weaving. It can also refer to a theme or idea that connects parts of a story or discussion.

words.ex: She wreathe the flowers around the door.
words.ex_cn: 她把花缠绕在门周围。
words.en: To twist or entwine something around something else, often in a decorative manner.

words.tr: v. 使卷入；使陷入；牵连
words.ex: He didn't want to embroil his friend in the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他不想让朋友卷入这场争吵。
words.en: To involve someone in a difficult or complicated situation.

words.ex: The cat got entangled in the string.
words.ex_cn: 猫被绳子缠住了。
words.en: If something is entangled in something else, it is caught or twisted around it, or mixed with it so that it is difficult to separate the two things.

words.ex: The vines entwine around the tree.
words.ex_cn: 藤蔓缠绕在树上。
words.en: To twist or twine together; interweave.

words.tr: v. 使牵连其中；涉及；暗示；指明起因
words.ex: The evidence may implicate him in the crime.
words.ex_cn: 证据可能使他牵连进这起犯罪中。
words.en: To show or suggest that someone is involved in something illegal or morally wrong.

words.ex: The two stories intertwine in the final chapter.
words.ex_cn: 这两个故事在最后一章交织在一起。
words.en: If two or more things are intertwined, they are closely connected with each other in many ways.

words.tr: v. 不断打扰；纠缠；烦扰
words.ex: The child keeps pestering his mom for candy.
words.ex_cn: 孩子不停地缠着妈妈要糖果。
words.en: If you say that someone is pestering you, you mean that they keep asking you to do something, or keep talking to you, and you find this annoying.

words.tr: adj. 可盘卷的；能抓住的；有理解能力的；贪婪的
words.ex: The monkey has a prehensile tail to grab trees.
words.ex_cn: 这只猴子有一条能抓握的尾巴来抓住树木。
words.en: A prehensile tail or limb is adapted for grasping or holding.

words.tr: v. 解开(~ sth. out)；使更复杂(~ sth. up)
words.ex: She raveled the tangled yarn out slowly.
words.ex_cn: 她慢慢地把缠绕的毛线解开。
words.en: To ravel means to tangle or untangle threads or fibers, or to become tangled or untangled. It can also refer to the process of separating the threads of a woven or knitted fabric, or to confuse or complicate a situation.

words.tr:
v. 咆哮；吼叫；（使）缠结
n. 咆哮（声）；缠结
words.ex: The dog snarls at strangers.
words.ex_cn: 狗对陌生人咆哮。
words.en: If an animal snarls, it makes a fierce, rough noise in its throat, usually to show anger.

words.tr:
n. 螺旋形；陡升或骤降；
v. 螺旋式上升（或下降）；
adj. 螺旋形的；
words.ex: The snail moved along a spiral path.
words.ex_cn: 蜗牛沿着一个螺旋形的路径爬行。
words.en: A spiral is a shape which winds round and round, with each curve above or outside the previous one.

words.tr:
v. （使）纠缠；使陷入；使混乱
n. 纠缠；混乱；纠纷
words.ex: The cat got into a tangle with the yarn.
words.ex_cn: 猫和毛线缠在一起了。
words.en: If something is tangled or tangles, it becomes twisted together in an untidy way.

words.ex: She unfastened her seatbelt before getting out of the car.
words.ex_cn: 她下车前解开了安全带。
words.en: To unfasten something means to open or undo it so that it is no longer fixed or attached.

words.tr: v. （使）吃腻（甜食）；（使）过饱；因过量而厌烦
words.ex: The rich dessert soon cloyed my appetite.
words.ex_cn: 丰富的甜点很快就让我感到腻了。
words.en: If something cloys, it becomes unpleasant because it is too sweet, rich, or sentimental.

words.tr: v. 吞食；吞噬；狼吞虎咽地吃；如饥似渴地看
words.ex: The dog devoured the meat quickly.
words.ex_cn: 狗很快地把肉吃光了。
words.en: To eat something quickly and eagerly, especially because you are very hungry; to destroy something quickly and completely.

words.ex: The fire engulfed the old house.
words.ex_cn: 大火吞噬了那座老房子。
words.en: If one thing engulfs another, it completely covers or hides it, often in a sudden and unexpected way.

words.tr: adj. 贪吃的；暴食的；饕餮的
words.ex: He was a gluttonous eater, consuming vast amounts of food at every meal.
words.ex_cn: 他是个贪吃的人，每顿饭都吃下大量的食物。
words.en: If you describe someone as gluttonous, you mean they eat or consume far more than they need.

words.ex: The mouse is gnawing on the wood.
words.ex_cn: 老鼠正在啃木头。
words.en: To gnaw means to bite or chew something persistently, especially something hard, or to cause persistent worry or discomfort.

words.tr:
v. 狼吞虎咽；吞并；火鸡咯咯叫
n. 火鸡叫声
words.ex: The dog will gobble up its food quickly.
words.ex_cn: 狗会很快把食物狼吞虎咽地吃掉。
words.en: To eat something quickly and eagerly, often making a noise.

words.ex: He was known to gormandize at dinner parties.
words.ex_cn: 他以在晚宴上狼吞虎咽而闻名。
words.en: To eat greedily and to excess.

words.tr:
v. 大口吞咽；喘气；抑制
n. 一大口；吞咽
words.ex: He gulped down his water quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速地吞下了水。
words.en: If you gulp something, you eat or drink it very quickly by swallowing large quantities of it at once.

words.ex: He guttled his food like a starving man.
words.ex_cn: 他像一个饿极了的人一样狼吞虎咽地吃着食物。
words.en: To consume food greedily or in large quantities.

words.tr: v. 狂吃暴饮；大吃大喝；大量消耗
words.ex: He guzzles soda every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都大口喝苏打水。
words.en: If you guzzle something, you drink it quickly and greedily.

words.ex: He imbibes coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都喝咖啡。
words.en: To imbibe means to drink, especially alcohol, or to absorb or take in something, such as knowledge or ideas.

words.tr:
v. 使醉；使陶醉
n. 酒鬼
words.ex: He was inebriated after a few drinks at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上喝了点酒后便醉了。
words.en: To make someone drunk or to exhilarate or stupefy as if with alcohol.

words.ex: The baby ingests milk every few hours.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿每隔几小时喝奶。
words.en: To ingest means to take food, drink, or another substance into your body, usually by swallowing.

words.ex: The ingestion of too much sugar can cause health problems.
words.ex_cn: 摄食过多的糖会导致健康问题。
words.en: The process of taking food, drink, or another substance into the body by swallowing or absorbing it.

words.tr:
v. 轻咬；啃；一点点地吃
n. 一小口；轻咬；少量
words.ex: The dog nibble the biscuit slowly.
words.ex_cn: 狗慢慢地轻咬着饼干。
words.en: To nibble means to take small bites of something, especially food.

words.ex: The dog gave a small nip to his leg.
words.ex_cn: 狗轻轻咬了他的腿一口。
words.en: To nip means to pinch, squeeze, or bite something quickly and sharply. It can also refer to taking a small amount of a drink.

words.ex: Bears are omnivorous animals.
words.ex_cn: 熊是杂食动物。
words.en: An omnivorous animal or person eats both plants and meat.

words.tr:
v. 啄；连续敲击；轻吻
n. 啄痕；啄食；轻吻
words.ex: The bird pecked at the bread on the ground.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿啄地上的面包。
words.en: To peck means to strike or bite something with the beak, or to kiss someone lightly and quickly.

words.tr: adj. 可饮用的；适于饮用的
words.ex: The water is potable.
words.ex_cn: 这水可以饮用。
words.en: Potable water is safe to drink.

words.tr: v. 豪饮；痛饮；开怀畅饮
words.ex: He quaffed the cold drink quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他快速地喝下了那杯冷饮。
words.en: To drink (a beverage) heartily and with gusto.

words.ex: The cool water helped to slake his thirst.
words.ex_cn: 清凉的水帮助他解渴。
words.en: If you slake a thirst, desire, or need, you satisfy it.

words.tr:
v. 出声地吃喝；啧啧地响
n. 啧啧吃的声音；咕嘟声
words.ex: He slurps his soup noisily.
words.ex_cn: 他吧嗒吧嗒地喝汤。
words.en: To drink or eat something noisily.

words.ex: She is a teetotal advocate for healthy living.
words.ex_cn: 她是健康生活的绝对戒酒倡导者。
words.en: Someone who is teetotal does not drink alcohol.

words.ex: I like to browse the internet for fun.
words.ex_cn: 我喜欢上网浏览消遣。
words.en: To look through or glance at reading matter casually or randomly.

words.tr: n. 矛盾心理；正反感情并存
words.ex: He feels ambivalence about moving to a new city.
words.ex_cn: 他对搬到新城市感到矛盾。
words.en: Ambivalence is the state of having mixed feelings or contradictory attitudes about something or someone.

words.ex: He felt ambivalent about accepting the job offer.
words.ex_cn: 他对接受这份工作邀约感到矛盾。
words.en: If you say that someone is ambivalent about something, you mean that they have mixed feelings about it or are unsure whether they want it or not.

words.tr: n. 始终一贯；前后一致；
words.ex: His consistency in studying every day helped him pass the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他每天学习的一贯坚持帮助他通过了考试。
words.en: Consistency is the quality or condition of being consistent, especially in achieving a level of performance or behavior that does not vary greatly in quality over time.

words.ex: There is a discrepancy between the two reports.
words.ex_cn: 这两份报告之间有差异。
words.en: A discrepancy is a difference between two or more things that should be the same.

words.tr: adj. 不能调和的；无法化解的；不兼容的
words.ex: Their views are irreconcilable.
words.ex_cn: 他们的观点无法调和。
words.en: If two things such as opinions or proposals are irreconcilable, they are so different from each other that it is not possible to believe or have both of them.

words.ex: It's a paradox that he is rich but unhappy.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个悖论，他很富有却不快乐。
words.en: A paradox is a statement that seems to contradict itself but may nonetheless be true, or a situation that defies intuition.

words.ex: There is a small rift in the wall.
words.ex_cn: 墙上有一条小裂缝。
words.en: A rift is a major fault or break in the Earth's crust.

words.ex: There is a large variance between the budget and the actual cost.
words.ex_cn: 预算与实际成本之间有很大的差额。
words.en: Variance refers to the fact or quality of being different, divergent, or inconsistent.

words.ex: He is grappled with the math problem for hours.
words.ex_cn: 他花了好几个小时努力解决这道数学题。
words.en: To grapple with something means to try hard to understand or deal with a difficult problem or subject.

words.tr: n. 混乱；混乱的人群；混战；肉搏；近战
words.ex: The two teams got into a melee during the game.
words.ex_cn: 比赛期间，两支球队发生了混战。
words.en: A melee is a confused fight or scuffle, especially one involving many people.

words.ex: There is a dissonance between his words and actions.
words.ex_cn: 他的言行不一致。
words.en: A lack of harmony or agreement between people or things.

words.tr: adj. 不调和的；不一致的；不和谐的
words.ex: The two voices sounded discordant.
words.ex_cn: 这两声音听起来不和谐。
words.en: Something that is discordant is strange or unpleasant because it does not fit in with other things.

words.ex: He was beset by problems at work.
words.ex_cn: 他被工作中的问题困扰。
words.en: If someone or something is beset by problems or fears, they have many problems or fears which affect them severely.

words.ex: He embeds the photo in the document.
words.ex_cn: 他把照片插入到文档中。
words.en: To fix something firmly and deeply in a surrounding mass.

words.tr:
v. 提取；
n. 摘录；提取物；
words.ex: They extract oil from plants.
words.ex_cn: 他们从植物中提取油。
words.en: To remove or take out something, especially by effort or force.

words.ex: The knight was impaled on the spear.
words.ex_cn: 骑士被长矛刺穿了。
words.en: To impale someone or something means to pierce them with a sharp object such as a spear or spike.

words.ex: The thick forest was impenetrable.
words.ex_cn: 这片茂密的森林无法穿越。
words.en: Impenetrable is used to describe something that cannot be passed through, entered, or understood.

words.ex: He inserts a coin into the machine.
words.ex_cn: 他把一枚硬币放进机器里。
words.en: To put or introduce something into something else.

words.ex: The historian interpolated the text with his own opinions.
words.ex_cn: 这位历史学家在文本中插入了自己的观点。
words.en: To interpolate means to insert something between other things or parts, especially to insert words into a text.

words.ex: Water can penetrate the soil slowly.
words.ex_cn: 水可以慢慢渗透进土壤。
words.en: To penetrate means to enter or pass through something, especially when this is difficult or when it is not obvious how to do it.

words.ex: The new app has high penetration in young markets.
words.ex_cn: 这款新应用在年轻市场中普及率很高。
words.en: The act or process of making a way into or through something; the ability to understand or find something out.

words.ex: The needle will pierce the skin.
words.ex_cn: 针会刺穿皮肤。
words.en: If a sharp object pierces something, or if you pierce something with a sharp object, the object goes into it and makes a hole in it.

words.tr:
n. 刺穿；刺孔
v. 刺穿；削弱
words.ex: The bike tire has a puncture.
words.ex_cn: 自行车轮胎有一个漏气孔。
words.en: A puncture is a small hole made by a sharp object, especially in a tire. To puncture something means to make a hole in it with a sharp object.

words.tr: v. （将刀剑）入鞘；放进套里；包；覆盖
words.ex: He sheathes his knife after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后把刀收进刀鞘。
words.en: To put something, especially a weapon, into a sheath; to cover or protect something with a sheath.

words.tr:
n. 串肉扦；烤肉叉
v. 用扦子串住；将…叉住
words.ex: He put the meat on a skewer and grilled it.
words.ex_cn: 他把肉串在串肉扦上烤。
words.en: A skewer is a long pin made of wood or metal, used for holding together pieces of food, especially meat, during cooking.

words.tr: adj. 刺状的； 多刺的
words.ex: The cactus had a spiny exterior that made it difficult to handle.
words.ex_cn: 仙人掌的外表多刺，难以处理。
words.en: Something that is spiny is covered with spines or has many spines.

words.tr:
n. 刺；戳
v. 刺；戳
words.ex: He felt a sharp stab in his side.
words.ex_cn: 他感到侧腹一阵刺痛。
words.en: If someone stabs you, they push a knife or sharp object into your body.

words.ex: The rocket's thrust lifted it into the sky.
words.ex_cn: 火箭的推力将它送上了天空。
words.en: To thrust something somewhere means to push it there quickly and forcefully. A thrust is also a powerful push or movement.

words.ex: That paper was a seminal work in computer science.
words.ex_cn: 那篇论文是计算机科学领域一部影响深远的著作。
words.en: Seminal is used to describe things such as books, works, events, and people that have a great influence in a particular field.

words.tr: adv. 遗传上地；基因上地；
words.ex: The dogs are genetically similar to each other.
words.ex_cn: 这些狗在遗传上彼此相似。
words.en: In a way that relates to genes or heredity.

words.tr:
n. 山；
v. 逐渐增加；
words.ex: He climbed the mount early in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 他一大早爬了那座山。
words.en: To mount something means to go up it or to get on it. It can also refer to the act of organizing and beginning something, such as an event or an exhibition.

words.ex: He tries not to antagonize his brother.
words.ex_cn: 他尽量不惹恼他的弟弟。
words.en: To antagonize someone means to cause them to feel hostile or unfriendly towards you.

words.ex: He is averse to changing his routine.
words.ex_cn: 他反对改变自己的日常安排。
words.en: If you say that someone is averse to something, you mean they dislike it or have a strong opposition to it.

words.tr:
n. 抵制；拒绝参加；
v. 抵制；拒绝参加；
words.ex: The students organized a boycott of the unfair school rule.
words.ex_cn: 学生们组织了对这项不公平校规的抵制。
words.en: If a country, group, or person boycotts a country, organization, or activity, they refuse to be involved with it in any way because they disapprove of it.

words.ex: Two companies compete for the same customers.
words.ex_cn: 两家公司为争夺相同的客户而竞争。
words.en: If you compete with someone for something, you try to get it for yourself and stop the other person getting it. You can also say that two people compete for something that they both want.

words.ex: He must confront his fears.
words.ex_cn: 他必须面对自己的恐惧。
words.en: If you confront a difficult situation or issue, you accept the fact that it exists and try to deal with it.

words.ex: He contradicts what she said.
words.ex_cn: 他反驳了她的话。
words.en: If you contradict someone, you say that what they have just said is wrong, or you suggest that it is wrong by saying something different.

words.ex: His words were contradictory.
words.ex_cn: 他的话是矛盾的。
words.en: If two or more facts, ideas, or statements are contradictory, they state or imply that opposite things are true.

words.ex: He controverts the claim with clear evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他用清晰的证据反驳了这一说法。
words.en: To argue about (a subject) in a formal manner; to dispute or contradict.

words.tr: n. 拒不服从；藐视法庭
words.ex: His contumacy led to a contempt of court charge.
words.ex_cn: 他的拒不服从导致了他被指控藐视法庭。
words.en: Contumacy is the refusal to obey or comply with authority, often characterized by stubborn resistance or disobedience.

words.ex: The boy showed defiance by refusing to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 男孩通过拒绝遵守规则来表现违抗。
words.en: Defiance is behaviour or an attitude which shows that you are not willing to obey someone or something.

words.ex: The boy defied his parents by staying out late.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩因为熬夜不回家而违抗了父母。
words.en: If you defy someone or something, you refuse to obey them or you do something that they do not allow.

words.ex: The experiment demonstrates that water boils at 100°C.
words.ex_cn: 这个实验证明水在100摄氏度时沸腾。
words.en: To demonstrate means to show something clearly by giving proof or evidence.

words.tr:
v. 提出异议；表示反对
n. 异议；反对
words.ex: He demurred when asked to sign the contract.
words.ex_cn: 当被要求签署合同时，他提出了异议。
words.en: If you demur, you express reluctance or objection to something.

words.tr: v. 对…表示极不赞成；强烈反对；轻视
words.ex: They deprecate old software.
words.ex_cn: 他们不推荐使用旧软件。
words.en: If you deprecate something, you criticize it or express your disapproval of it.

words.ex: The lawyer presented a disproof of the defendant's alibi.
words.ex_cn: 律师提出了对被告不在场证明的反驳证据。
words.en: Evidence or an argument that disproves a theory, belief, or statement.

words.ex: He expressed dissent about the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 他对新规定提出了异议。
words.en: Dissent is strong disagreement or dissatisfaction with a decision or opinion, especially one that is supported by most people or by people in authority.

words.ex: He expostulate with his friend about the unfair rule.
words.ex_cn: 他向朋友抱怨这条不公平的规则。
words.en: To expostulate means to reason earnestly with someone in an attempt to dissuade or correct them.

words.ex: The mutinous crew refused to follow the captain's orders.
words.ex_cn: 叛乱的船员拒绝服从船长的命令。
words.en: If someone is mutinous, they are strongly dissatisfied with a person in authority and are likely to stop obeying them.

words.ex: He raised an objection to the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 他对新规定提出了反对。
words.en: An objection is an expression or feeling of disapproval or opposition; a reason for disagreeing.

words.ex: He opposes the new law.
words.ex_cn: 他反对这项新法律。
words.en: If you oppose someone or something, you disagree with them and try to prevent them from doing something, or you try to change what they are doing.

words.tr:
adj. 压倒性的；强烈的；使人无法忍受的
v. 制服；压倒；令人折服；使难以忍受；“overpower”的现在分词
words.ex: The smell of flowers was overpowering.
words.ex_cn: 花的气味非常强烈。
words.en: An overpowering feeling or smell is so strong that you cannot resist it.

words.tr:
v. 抗议；
n. 抗议活动；
words.ex: The students protest against the new school rules.
words.ex_cn: 学生们抗议新的校规。
words.en: A protest is the act of saying or showing publicly that you object to something.

words.tr:
n. 遁词；狡辩；支吾以对；争论的小问题
v. 使用遁词；含糊其辞；吹毛求疵
words.ex: His excuse was just a quibble to avoid blame.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口只是逃避责任的遁词。
words.en: To argue or raise objections about a trivial matter or minor detail.

words.ex: The rebellious boy refused to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这个叛逆的男孩拒绝遵守规则。
words.en: If you think someone is rebellious, you mean that they are deliberately not obeying people in authority or rules of behaviour.

words.ex: He gave a strong rebuttal to the claim.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个说法给出了有力的反驳。
words.en: A rebuttal is a statement or piece of evidence that contradicts or opposes a previous statement or evidence.

words.ex: The recalcitrant student refused to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这个顽抗的学生拒绝遵守规则。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as recalcitrant, you mean that they are unwilling to obey orders or are difficult to deal with.

words.ex: He refuted the claim with clear evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他用清晰的证据驳斥了这一说法。
words.en: To prove a statement or theory to be wrong or false; to deny the truth or accuracy of something.

words.tr: v. 抗议；表示异议；劝诫
words.ex: He remonstrated with his friend for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他因为朋友迟到而责备了他。
words.en: To remonstrate means to make a forcefully reproachful protest.

words.tr:
v. 反驳；回嘴
n. 反驳；顶嘴
words.ex: He gave a quick retort when she criticized him.
words.ex_cn: 当她批评他时，他迅速回了一句。
words.en: If you retort, you reply angrily to someone.

words.ex: The riot broke out after the game.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束后爆发了骚乱。
words.en: A riot is a violent disturbance of the peace by a crowd.

words.ex: The rivalry between the two teams is very strong.
words.ex_cn: 这两支队伍之间的竞争非常激烈。
words.en: Competition for the same objective or for superiority in the same field.

words.ex: There was a hue and cry when the dog went missing.
words.ex_cn: 狗失踪时，人们一片喧哗。
words.en: If there is a hue and cry about something, there is a loud protest about it or opposition to it.

words.ex: He oppugns the decision loudly.
words.ex_cn: 他大声反对这个决定。
words.en: To oppose or argue against; to challenge or dispute.

words.ex: He committed apostasy by leaving his religion.
words.ex_cn: 他因放弃自己的宗教而犯了背教罪。
words.en: Apostasy is the act of abandoning or renouncing a religious or political belief or principle.

words.tr: v. 背叛；出卖；泄露；暴露
words.ex: He betrays his friend by telling the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他通过泄露秘密背叛了朋友。
words.en: If you betray someone who loves or trusts you, your actions hurt and disappoint them.

words.ex: They collaborate to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 他们合作完成这个项目。
words.en: to work jointly with others or together especially in an intellectual endeavor

words.ex: The deviation from the plan caused delays.
words.ex_cn: 偏离计划导致了延误。
words.en: A deviation is a noticeable difference from what is expected or from a standard.

words.tr:
v. 出卖；欺骗
n. 欺骗行为；出卖行为
words.ex: He double-crossed his friend to win the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他背叛了朋友以赢得奖品。
words.en: If someone double-crosses you, they deceive you by doing the opposite of what they said they would do.

words.tr: n. 火把；燃烧的木柴；煽动者
words.ex: He is a firebrand who speaks loudly against injustice.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个大声反对不公的激进分子。
words.en: A firebrand is a person who is passionate about a particular cause, often inciting others to action or rebellion.

words.tr:
n. 起义者；叛乱者；造反者
adj. 叛乱的；起义的
words.ex: The insurgent attacked the village at night.
words.ex_cn: 叛乱分子在夜里袭击了村庄。
words.en: An insurgent is a person who rises in active revolt against an established authority or government.

words.ex: The insurrection failed because people did not support it.
words.ex_cn: 这次起义失败了，因为人们不支持它。
words.en: An insurrection is a violent uprising against an authority or government.

words.tr: adj. 不忠的；背信弃义的
words.ex: The perfidious traitor betrayed his comrades.
words.ex_cn: 那个背信弃义的叛徒背叛了他的同伙。
words.en: If you describe someone as perfidious, you mean that they have betrayed someone or cannot be trusted.

words.ex: His perfidy shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的背信弃义让所有人震惊。
words.en: Perfidy is the act of deliberately betraying someone's trust; treachery.

words.ex: He reneged on his promise to help me.
words.ex_cn: 他背弃了帮助我的承诺。
words.en: If someone reneges on a promise or an agreement, they do not do what they have promised or agreed to do.

words.tr:
v. 叛乱；反叛；（使）厌恶
n. 叛乱；厌恶；反感
words.ex: The people revolt against the unfair rules.
words.ex_cn: 人们反抗不公平的规则。
words.en: If a large number of people revolt, they refuse to be controlled or ruled, and take action against authority, often violent action.

words.ex: The treacherous road made driving very scary.
words.ex_cn: 这条危险的道路让驾驶非常可怕。
words.en: If you describe someone as treacherous, you mean that they are likely to betray you and cannot be trusted. If you say that something is treacherous, you mean that it is very dangerous and unpredictable.

words.tr:
n. 反叛；暴动
v. 反叛；暴动
words.ex: The sailors started a mutiny against the captain.
words.ex_cn: 水手们对船长发动了叛变。
words.en: Mutiny is a situation in which a group of people, especially soldiers or sailors, refuse to obey orders and try to take control away from the person who commands them.

words.tr:
adj. 不满的；不忠的；有叛意的
v. 使不满；使疏远；“disaffect”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The disaffected youth joined the protest.
words.ex_cn: 不满的青年加入了抗议活动。
words.en: If you are disaffected, you no longer support or are satisfied with something or someone, especially a group or organization that you used to support.

words.ex: His defection shocked the whole team.
words.ex_cn: 他的叛逃让整个团队震惊。
words.en: The act of abandoning a cause, party, or nation, especially in favor of an opposing one.

words.tr:
n. 雄鹿；公羊；雄兔；美元
v. （马等）猛然弓背跃起；抵制
words.ex: The buck ran through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 雄鹿在森林中奔跑。
words.en: A buck is a male deer, antelope, rabbit, or hare. It can also refer to a dollar in American slang. As a verb, it means to jump or to resist something.

words.ex: He abnegates his own needs for his family.
words.ex_cn: 他为了家人而放弃自己的需求。
words.en: If you abnegate something, you renounce or reject it.

words.ex: He disavow any connection to the crime.
words.ex_cn: 他否认与这起犯罪有任何关联。
words.en: If you disavow something, you say that you are not responsible for it or you do not agree with it.

words.ex: The website has a disclaimer about errors.
words.ex_cn: 该网站有一个关于错误的免责声明。
words.en: A disclaimer is a statement in which a person says that they did not know about something or that they are not responsible for something.

words.ex: He tried to disprove the theory with new data.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用新数据驳斥这个理论。
words.en: To disprove something means to show that it is not true or correct.

words.ex: No one can gainsay the truth.
words.ex_cn: 没有人能否认这个事实。
words.en: If there is no gainsaying something, it is not possible to deny that it is true or that it exists.

words.tr:
v. 否认；拒绝
n. 否认；拒绝
words.ex: He always naysay when others suggest new ideas.
words.ex_cn: 当别人提出新想法时，他总是反对。
words.en: To say no to something; to deny, refuse, or oppose something.

words.ex: He tries to negate the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图否认事实。
words.en: If someone negates something, they say that it does not exist or is not true.

words.tr: n. 否定；反面；对立面；拒绝
words.ex: He gave a negation of the statement.
words.ex_cn: 他否定了那个陈述。
words.en: A negation is a statement that denies or contradicts another statement.

words.ex: The boss can override the rules if needed.
words.ex_cn: 如果需要，老板可以凌驾于规则之上。
words.en: If one thing in a situation overrides other things, it is more important than them.

words.ex: The judge will overrule the objection.
words.ex_cn: 法官将驳回这个异议。
words.en: If someone in authority overrules a decision or order, they officially decide that it is wrong and change it.

words.tr:
v. 断然拒绝
n. 粗暴回绝；生硬的拒绝
words.ex: He rebuffed her offer with a shake of his head.
words.ex_cn: 他摇了摇头，拒绝了她的提议。
words.en: If you rebuff someone or rebuff a suggestion that they make, you refuse to do what they suggest.

words.tr:
n. 否决；否决权
v. 否决
words.ex: The president used his veto to stop the law.
words.ex_cn: 总统行使否决权阻止了这项法律。
words.en: If someone in authority vetoes something, they forbid it, or they stop it from being put into action.

words.tr: n. 不赞成；持反对意见；非难
words.ex: He felt disapprobation when he saw the messy room.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到凌乱的房间时，他感到不满。
words.en: Disapprobation is a strong feeling of disapproval or condemnation.

words.ex: He gave a disavowal of the false statement.
words.ex_cn: 他否认了那句虚假的言论。
words.en: A disavowal is a statement in which you say that you are not responsible for something, or that you do not agree with or support something.

words.tr: n. 阳否阴述；故抑其词；表面否认要说或正说的话
words.ex: He said, 'I will not mention the mistake,' using apophasis.
words.ex_cn: 他说：‘我不会提到那个错误，’这是用了回避法。
words.en: Apophasis is a rhetorical device wherein the speaker or writer brings up a subject by either denying it, or denying that it should be brought up. It is thus a form of irony, and often used in political speeches and debates.

words.ex: The teacher made an intervention to help the student.
words.ex_cn: 老师进行了干预以帮助学生。
words.en: Intervention is the act of intervening, especially in a situation to prevent something undesirable from happening.

words.ex: The teacher intervened when the students argued.
words.ex_cn: 当学生们争吵时，老师进行了干涉。
words.en: If you intervene in a situation, you become involved in it and try to change it.

words.ex: Don't meddle in my affairs.
words.ex_cn: 别插手我的事情。
words.en: To meddle means to interfere in something that is not one's concern.

words.ex: He felt beholden to his mentor for all the help he had received.
words.ex_cn: 他觉得自己对导师的帮助感激不尽。
words.en: If you are beholden to someone, you are in their debt because they have helped you or given you something.

words.ex: I am grateful for your help.
words.ex_cn: 我感激你的帮助。
words.en: If you are grateful for something that someone has given you or done for you, you have warm, friendly feelings towards them and wish to thank them.

words.ex: He showed gratitude for the help.
words.ex_cn: 他表达了对帮助的感激。
words.en: Gratitude is the feeling of being thankful and appreciative.

words.ex: He is indebted to the bank for a large loan.
words.ex_cn: 他欠银行一大笔贷款。
words.en: If you say that you are indebted to someone for something, you mean that you are very grateful to them for something.

words.tr: v. 回报；报答；往复；来回
words.ex: She helped me, and I will reciprocate.
words.ex_cn: 她帮了我，我会回报她。
words.en: If your feelings or actions towards someone are reciprocated, the other person feels or behaves in the same way towards you as you have felt or behaved towards them.

words.tr: adj. 没有回报的；无报酬的；有仇未报的；单方面的
words.ex: She suffered from unrequited love for many years.
words.ex_cn: 多年来，她一直承受着单恋之苦。
words.en: If you say that something such as love or affection is unrequited, you mean that it is not returned by the person it is directed towards.

words.ex: The old church has strong masonry walls.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的教堂有坚固的石砖结构墙壁。
words.en: Masonry is the craft of building with stone, brick, or similar materials, often using mortar.

words.ex: The boss appointed Tom as the new manager.
words.ex_cn: 老板任命汤姆为新经理。
words.en: If you appoint someone to a job or official position, you formally choose them for it.

words.ex: He learned carpentry from his father.
words.ex_cn: 他从父亲那里学到了木工工作。
words.en: Carpentry is the activity of making and repairing wooden things.

words.tr: v. 罢免；废黜；宣誓证明
words.ex: The people deposed the corrupt leader.
words.ex_cn: 人民推翻了腐败的领导人。
words.en: To depose someone means to remove them from a position of power or authority, especially a monarch or political leader.

words.tr: n. 沉积（物）；革职；宣誓证词；作证书
words.ex: Sediment deposition forms layers on the riverbed.
words.ex_cn: 沉积物在河床上形成层状结构。
words.en: The act of depositing something, especially a layer of a substance formed by natural processes, or the giving of testimony under oath.

words.ex: The teacher designated him as the group leader.
words.ex_cn: 老师指派他为组长。
words.en: If you designate someone or something as a particular thing, you formally give them that description or name.

words.ex: The power will devolve to the local government.
words.ex_cn: 权力将下放给地方政府。
words.en: If you devolve power, authority, or responsibility to a less powerful person or group, or if it devolves upon them, it is transferred to them.

words.tr:
v. 派遣；调遣；发送
n. 快信；发送；派遣
words.ex: He will dispatch the package tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会寄出这个包裹。
words.en: To send someone or something to a particular place for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The manager will empower the team to make decisions.
words.ex_cn: 经理将授权团队做决定。
words.en: To give someone the authority or power to do something.

words.tr: v. 授权；命名；给...权利（或资格）
words.ex: This book entitles you to a free gift.
words.ex_cn: 这本书使你有资格获得一份免费礼物。
words.en: If you are entitled to something, you have the right to have it or do it.

words.tr:
adj. 就职的；开幕的；创立的
n. 就职演说
words.ex: He gave his inaugural speech last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚发表了就职演讲。
words.en: An inaugural event or speech is the first in a series planned to celebrate or introduce something.

words.tr: v. 开创；为（某人）举行就职典礼；为…举行开幕仪式
words.ex: The president will inaugurate the new hospital next week.
words.ex_cn: 总统将于下周为新医院举行揭幕仪式。
words.en: If you inaugurate a new system, service, or project, you start it or introduce it officially.

words.tr: v. 使正式就任；给予职位
words.ex: They inducted the new mayor with a ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他们通过一场仪式使新市长正式就任。
words.en: To induct someone into a position or organization means to formally install them in that position or officially introduce them into that organization.

words.ex: The induction of the new mayor will be held next Monday.
words.ex_cn: 新市长的就职典礼将在下周一举行。
words.en: Induction is the process or action of inducting someone to a position or organization, or the process of reasoning from specific cases to general rules.

words.ex: He will initiate a new project next week.
words.ex_cn: 他将在下周发起一个新项目。
words.en: To initiate something means to start it or cause it to happen.

words.ex: He will install the new software on his computer.
words.ex_cn: 他将在他的电脑上安装新软件。
words.en: To set up or fix in position for use or service.

words.ex: The king will instate a new prime minister next week.
words.ex_cn: 国王下周将任命一位新的首相。
words.en: To instate someone in a position or job means to formally establish them in that position or job.

words.tr: v. 准许入学；被录取入学
words.ex: He will matriculate next fall.
words.ex_cn: 他将在明年秋天入学。
words.en: To matriculate means to enroll at a college or university, or to be accepted as a student by a college or university.

words.ex: They will nominate her for the award.
words.ex_cn: 他们将提名她获得这个奖项。
words.en: If someone is nominated for a job or position, their name is formally suggested as a candidate for it.

words.tr: v. 授予圣职；命令；注定
words.ex: The priest will ordain the new pastor next Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 神父将在下个星期日任命这位新牧师。
words.en: To ordain someone as a priest or minister means to officially make them a priest or minister, usually in a religious ceremony. To ordain something means to order or command it officially.

words.tr: v. 主持；指挥；担任会议主席
words.ex: He presides over the meeting every Monday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周一主持会议。
words.en: To preside means to be in charge of a formal meeting, ceremony, or other event.

words.tr: n. 工作清闲但报酬优厚的职位；闲职；美差
words.ex: He got a sinecure in the government office.
words.ex_cn: 他在政府部门得到了一个闲职。
words.en: A sinecure is a position requiring little or no work but giving the holder status or financial benefit.

words.tr:
v. 转移；转让；调任；
n. 转移；转让；调任；
words.ex: He will transfer the money to his bank account.
words.ex_cn: 他将把钱转到他的银行账户。
words.en: If you transfer something or someone from one place to another, or they transfer from one place to another, they go from the first place to the second.

words.ex: The courier delivered the letter quickly.
words.ex_cn: 信使迅速送来了这封信。
words.en: A courier is a person or company that delivers messages, packages, and mail.

words.ex: The coroner examined the body to find the cause of death.
words.ex_cn: 法医检查了尸体以确定死因。
words.en: A coroner is an official who is responsible for investigating the deaths of people who have died in a sudden, violent, or unusual way.

words.ex: The police investigated the assault on the old man.
words.ex_cn: 警方调查了对那位老人的攻击。
words.en: An assault is a physical attack on someone, or a military attack on a place.

words.ex: This is his first foray into painting.
words.ex_cn: 这是他首次涉足绘画。
words.en: A foray is a sudden and brief incursion or attack into enemy territory, especially to obtain something; a raid. It can also refer to an initial attempt to become involved in a different activity or profession.

words.ex: His iconoclastic ideas changed the way people think about art.
words.ex_cn: 他打破旧习的想法改变了人们对艺术的看法。
words.en: If you describe someone or their ideas as iconoclastic, you mean that they deliberately challenge established beliefs or institutions.

words.ex: The new law impinges on people's privacy.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律侵犯了人们的隐私。
words.en: To impinge means to have an effect or influence, especially a negative one, on someone or something.

words.ex: The army made an inroad into the enemy's territory.
words.ex_cn: 军队对敌方领土发动了一次袭击。
words.en: An inroad is an advance or penetration often at the expense of someone or something, or a hostile incursion or invasion.

words.ex: The onslaught of rain flooded the streets.
words.ex_cn: 大量倾泻的雨水淹没了街道。
words.en: An onslaught is a very powerful, often violent, attack against someone or something.

words.ex: The soldiers raided the enemy camp at night.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在夜间突袭了敌人的营地。
words.en: A raid is a sudden attack on a place by soldiers, police, or other officials, in order to search for something or to arrest someone.

words.ex: Children are vulnerable to colds in winter.
words.ex_cn: 儿童在冬天容易感冒。
words.en: If someone or something is vulnerable, they are weak and without protection, with the result that they are easily hurt physically or emotionally.

words.tr: adj. 可攻击的；有隙可乘的
words.ex: The old wall is assailable by strong winds.
words.ex_cn: 这堵旧墙容易被强风摧毁。
words.en: If something is assailable, it is capable of being attacked or criticized.

words.tr: v. 提出；提议；提出…供考虑
words.ex: He propound a new theory in class.
words.ex_cn: 他在课堂上提出了一种新理论。
words.en: To propound means to suggest or put forward an idea, theory, or point of view for consideration.

words.ex: He adduce evidence to prove his point.
words.ex_cn: 他提出证据来证明自己的观点。
words.en: To cite as evidence or proof; to bring forward in argument or as proof.

words.ex: The teacher will allocate books to students.
words.ex_cn: 老师将给学生分配书籍。
words.en: To allocate something means to give it to a particular person or use it for a particular purpose.

words.tr: n. 救济金；施舍物（复数名词）
words.ex: He gave alms to the poor man.
words.ex_cn: 他施舍给那个穷人。
words.en: Alms are money, food, or other donations given to the poor or needy as an act of charity.

words.ex: The charity helps poor children get food and education.
words.ex_cn: 这个慈善团体帮助贫困儿童获得食物和教育。
words.en: An organization that helps people in need, or the act of giving money, food, or help to those who need it.

words.ex: The nurse will dispense medicine to the patients.
words.ex_cn: 护士将分发药品给病人。
words.en: To dispense means to distribute or provide something, especially in a systematic way, or to prepare and give out medicine.

words.ex: The teacher will distribute the books to students.
words.ex_cn: 老师将把书分发给学生。
words.en: If you distribute things, you hand them or deliver them to a number of people.

words.ex: The teacher endues her students with confidence.
words.ex_cn: 老师赋予学生信心。
words.en: To provide someone or something with a particular quality or ability.

words.tr:
n. 补助金；授予物；
v. 承认；授予；允许；
words.ex: The university received a grant for scientific research.
words.ex_cn: 这所大学收到了一笔用于科学研究的补助金。
words.en: If someone in authority grants you something, or if something is granted to you, you are allowed to have it or do it.

words.tr:
n. 问题；重要议题；发行（物）；
v. 发行；
words.ex: The main issue is lack of money.
words.ex_cn: 主要问题是缺乏资金。
words.en: An issue is an important subject or problem that people are talking about or arguing about.

words.tr:
v. 分配；给予
n. 边界
words.ex: He mete out justice fairly.
words.ex_cn: 他公平地施以正义。
words.en: To distribute or allot something, especially justice or punishment.

words.tr:
v. 献出；拿出；提供
n. 献出；拿出；提供
words.ex: He proffered a cup of tea to his guest.
words.ex_cn: 他递给客人一杯茶。
words.en: If you proffer something to someone, you offer it to them for acceptance.

words.ex: The ship carries a provision of food for the journey.
words.ex_cn: 这艘船为旅程准备了食物供应。
words.en: A provision is a condition or requirement in a legal document. It can also refer to the act of supplying or providing something that is needed.

words.ex: He purveys fresh bread to the local shop.
words.ex_cn: 他向当地商店供应新鲜面包。
words.en: To purvey means to supply or provide something, especially food, as a business.

words.ex: The factory has a quota of 1000 units per day.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂每天有1000件的配额。
words.en: A quota is the limited number or quantity of something which is officially allowed.

words.tr:
n. 定量；配给量
v. 配给；定量供应
words.ex: He gets a small ration of food each day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天得到少量的食物配给。
words.en: A ration is a fixed amount of something such as food or fuel that is officially allowed to each person, especially when there is not enough of it available.

words.ex: The government plans redistribution of wealth to help the poor.
words.ex_cn: 政府计划重新分配财富以帮助穷人。
words.en: The act of distributing something again or differently, especially wealth or resources.

words.ex: The rain rendered the road slippery.
words.ex_cn: 雨水使道路变得滑溜。
words.en: To render something means to cause it to become or to provide it. It can also mean to express or translate something.

words.ex: He won a trophy for first place in the race.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中获得第一名，赢得了一个奖杯。
words.en: A trophy is a prize, such as a gold or silver cup, that is given to the winner of a competition or race.

words.tr: v. 给予选举权；释放（奴隶）
words.ex: The law will enfranchise all adults over 18.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律将赋予所有18岁以上成年人选举权。
words.en: To enfranchise someone means to give them the right to vote in elections.

words.tr: v. 供以服装；供以军用品；装备
words.ex: The soldiers were accoutered with the latest military gear.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们装备了最新的军用装备。
words.en: To equip or outfit someone with the necessary items or clothing for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The ship dropped its anchor in the harbor.
words.ex_cn: 船在港口放下了锚。
words.en: An anchor is a heavy object that is dropped from a boat or a ship into the water to prevent the vessel from moving.

words.tr:
n. 带扣；皮带扣
v. （使）搭扣扣住
words.ex: The belt has a shiny buckle.
words.ex_cn: 这条皮带有一个闪亮的带扣。
words.en: A buckle is a piece of metal or plastic attached to one end of a belt or strap, which is used to fasten it. As a verb, to buckle means to fasten something with a buckle or to bend or collapse under pressure.

words.tr:
n. 带扣；皮带扣
v. （使）搭扣扣住
words.ex: The belt has a shiny buckle.
words.ex_cn: 这条皮带有一个闪亮的带扣。
words.en: A buckle is a piece of metal or plastic attached to one end of a belt or strap, which is used to fasten it. As a verb, to buckle means to fasten something with a buckle or to bend or collapse under pressure.

words.tr:
n. 带扣；皮带扣
v. （使）搭扣扣住
words.ex: The belt has a shiny buckle.
words.ex_cn: 这条皮带有一个闪亮的带扣。
words.en: A buckle is a piece of metal or plastic attached to one end of a belt or strap, which is used to fasten it. As a verb, to buckle means to fasten something with a buckle or to bend or collapse under pressure.

words.ex: The local company is an affiliate of the big global brand.
words.ex_cn: 这家本地公司是这个全球大品牌的分公司。
words.en: If an organization is affiliated with another larger organization, it is officially connected with the larger organization or is a member of it.

words.ex: The club has an affiliation with the university.
words.ex_cn: 这个俱乐部与大学有从属关系。
words.en: An affiliation is a close connection or association with a particular group, organization, or institution.

words.ex: Align your goals with your actions.
words.ex_cn: 让你的目标与行动保持一致。
words.en: To arrange something in a straight line or in the correct position in relation to something else, usually so that it is parallel to it.

words.ex: The two companies will amalgamate next month.
words.ex_cn: 这两家公司下个月将合并。
words.en: If two or more organizations amalgamate, they join together and become one organization.

words.ex: The annexation of the small country by its neighbor caused international protest.
words.ex_cn: 邻国对这个小国的吞并引发了国际抗议。
words.en: The act of annexing, especially territory.

words.tr:
v. 把…联系在一起；
adj. 副的；
n. 同事；伙伴；
words.ex: He associates happiness with family time.
words.ex_cn: 他把幸福与家庭时光联系在一起。
words.en: If you associate someone or something with a particular quality or idea, or if they are associated with it, you connect them in your mind with that quality or idea.

words.tr: v. 聚合；合并；长到一起
words.ex: The small ponds coalesce into a large lake.
words.ex_cn: 小池塘合并成一个大湖。
words.en: If two or more things coalesce, they come together and form a single group or system.

words.ex: The two parties formed a coalition to win the election.
words.ex_cn: 这两个政党联合起来以赢得选举。
words.en: A coalition is a temporary alliance for combined action, especially of political parties forming a government.

words.ex: She concatenates two strings to make one word.
words.ex_cn: 她把两个字符串连接成一个单词。
words.en: To link things together in a chain or series.

words.ex: The confederacy fought against the union in the civil war.
words.ex_cn: 南方联盟在内战中与联邦作战。
words.en: A confederacy is a union of states or groups of people who have joined together for a common purpose or by a common agreement.

words.ex: He conflates happiness with wealth.
words.ex_cn: 他把幸福和财富混为一谈。
words.en: To combine two or more things into one, especially in a way that is confusing or misleading.

words.ex: The rain and the thunder happened in conjunction.
words.ex_cn: 雨和雷声同时发生。
words.en: A conjunction is a word that is used to connect clauses or sentences or to coordinate words in the same clause.

words.ex: They cooperate to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他们合作以按时完成项目。
words.en: If you cooperate with someone, you work with them or help them for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The corporate office is in New York.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司的总部在纽约。
words.en: Corporate relates to large companies or to a particular large company.

words.ex: The new plan incorporates feedback from students.
words.ex_cn: 新计划包含了学生的反馈。
words.en: If one thing incorporates another thing, it includes the other thing.

words.ex: The hospital is a public institution.
words.ex_cn: 这家医院是一家公共机构。
words.en: An institution is a large important organization such as a university, church, or bank.

words.tr:
v. （使）连锁；（使）相互扣住
n. 互锁设备
words.ex: The puzzle pieces interlock tightly.
words.ex_cn: 拼图块紧密地互锁在一起。
words.en: To interlock means to fit together firmly or closely, or to cause things to fit together in this way.

words.tr:
adj. 联锁的；相互扣住的
v. （使）连锁；（使）相互扣住；“interlock”的现在分词
words.ex: The puzzle pieces are interlocking.
words.ex_cn: 这些拼图碎片是相互扣合的。
words.en: Interlocking refers to the process or state of two or more things being connected or joined together in such a way that they move or operate together.

words.ex: The car stopped at the junction.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在交叉路口停了下来。
words.en: A junction is a place where two or more things, especially roads or railways, come together.

words.tr:
v. （使）合并；（使）融合；（使）混合
n. 合并；混合
words.ex: He melds the two ideas into one.
words.ex_cn: 他把这两个想法融合成一个。
words.en: To combine or blend to form a single entity.

words.ex: The net is made of a fine mesh.
words.ex_cn: 这个网是由细密的网状物制成的。
words.en: A mesh is a material made of a network of wire or thread to catch or hold things, or to allow things to pass through it.

words.ex: The internet is a nexus of information.
words.ex_cn: 互联网是信息的联系中心。
words.en: A nexus is a connection or series of connections within a particular situation or system.

words.tr: n. 专家咨询组；嵌板；仪器板；
words.ex: The government formed a panel to advise on health policy.
words.ex_cn: 政府组建了一个专家咨询组来就卫生政策提供建议。
words.en: A panel is a small group of people who are chosen to do something, for example to discuss something in public or to make a decision.

words.ex: He will realign his goals after the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议后将重新调整他的目标。
words.en: To change the way something is organized or arranged in order to make it more effective or suitable for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The cells can recombine DNA to repair damage.
words.ex_cn: 细胞可以重新组合DNA来修复损伤。
words.en: To combine again or differently, especially in the context of genetics, to form new combinations.

words.tr:
v. 捻接；粘接；结合
n. 粘接处；绞接处
words.ex: He spliced the two ropes together.
words.ex_cn: 他把两根绳子捻接在一起。
words.en: To join or unite (ropes or rope ends) by interweaving the strands.

words.tr: adj. 不愿合作的；不愿配合的
words.ex: He was uncooperative during the interview.
words.ex_cn: 他在面试中不配合。
words.en: If you describe someone as uncooperative, you mean that they do not want to help or support other people.

words.ex: The confluence of the two rivers created a fertile valley.
words.ex_cn: 两条河流的汇流形成了一个肥沃的山谷。
words.en: The confluence of two or more things is the junction or merging of them, often forming something greater or more complex.

words.ex: The movie aroused his curiosity.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影激起了他的好奇心。
words.en: If something arouses a particular reaction or attitude in people, it causes them to have that reaction or attitude.

words.tr: v. 使不抱幻想；使不再着迷；使醒悟
words.ex: The truth disenchant him about his hero.
words.ex_cn: 真相让他对他的偶像不再抱有幻想。
words.en: If you are disenchanted with something, you are disappointed with it and no longer believe that it is good or worthwhile.

words.tr:
v. 使不再抱幻想；使理想破灭
n. 幻灭；理想破灭
words.ex: The bad experience disillusioned him about politics.
words.ex_cn: 这次糟糕的经历让他对政治不再抱幻想。
words.en: If a person or thing disillusions you, they make you realize that something is not as good as you thought it was.

words.ex: The music is evocative of childhood memories.
words.ex_cn: 这音乐唤起了童年的回忆。
words.en: If you describe something as evocative, you mean that it is good or interesting because it produces pleasant memories, ideas, emotions, and responses in people.

words.ex: He wants to expedite the process.
words.ex_cn: 他想加快这个过程。
words.en: To expedite something means to make it happen or be done more quickly.

words.tr: v. 搅动；“agitate”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 焦虑不安的；
words.ex: He agitated the water with a stick.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根棍子搅动了水。
words.en: If someone is agitated, they are very worried or upset, and show this in their behavior, movements, or voice.

words.ex: Exercise can bolster your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以增强你的健康。
words.en: If you bolster something such as someone's confidence or courage, you increase it. A bolster is also a long, firm pillow.

words.tr:
n. 浮标；浮筒
v. 使浮起；支撑；鼓励
words.ex: The buoy floats on the water.
words.ex_cn: 浮标漂浮在水面上。
words.en: A buoy is a floating object that is anchored in water to mark a location, warn of danger, or indicate a navigational channel.

words.ex: The speech embolden the protesters to speak up.
words.ex_cn: 这次演讲鼓舞了抗议者们发声。
words.en: To embolden someone means to make them feel more confident or courageous.

words.ex: The teacher exhorts students to study hard.
words.ex_cn: 老师敦促学生努力学习。
words.en: To strongly encourage or try to persuade someone to do something.

words.ex: Parents should foster good habits in children.
words.ex_cn: 父母应该培养孩子的好习惯。
words.en: To foster something means to encourage and promote its development.

words.tr:
n. （赶牲畜的）尖头棒；激励；刺激
v. 刺激；驱使
words.ex: The farmer used a goad to guide the oxen.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用一根尖头棒赶牛。
words.en: If you goad someone, you deliberately make them feel angry or irritated, often causing them to react by doing something.

words.ex: Her smile heartened the tired students.
words.ex_cn: 她的微笑鼓舞了疲惫的学生。
words.en: If someone is heartened by something, it encourages them and makes them cheerful.

words.ex: His words were hortative, urging everyone to try harder.
words.ex_cn: 他的话具有激励性，鼓励大家更加努力。
words.en: If you describe something as hortative, you mean that it is intended to encourage or incite someone to do something.

words.ex: The bonus is an incentive to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 奖金是努力工作的动机。
words.en: Something that encourages a person to do something or to work harder.

words.ex: He tried to incite a riot with his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过演讲煽动暴乱。
words.en: To incite someone to do something means to encourage or persuade them to do it, often in a way that is negative or harmful.

words.ex: The teacher tried to infuse confidence into the students.
words.ex_cn: 老师试图向学生注入信心。
words.en: If you infuse a quality into someone or something, you fill them with it. If a quality infuses something, it is present throughout it.

words.tr: v. 增添活力；振奋；使活跃
words.ex: The fresh air invigorates me every morning.
words.ex_cn: 每天早晨的新鲜空气让我精神焕发。
words.en: If something invigorates you, it makes you feel more energetic and alive.

words.tr:
adj. 精神充沛的；让人神清气爽的
v. 增添活力；振奋；使活跃；“invigorate”的现在分词
words.ex: The morning walk was invigorating.
words.ex_cn: 晨跑让人精神充沛。
words.en: If something is invigorating, it makes you feel more energetic and alive.

words.tr: v. 使恢复精力；使复原；使变新
words.ex: A short nap can refresh you.
words.ex_cn: 小睡一会儿能让你恢复精力。
words.en: To refresh someone means to make them feel less tired or less hot.

words.tr: v. 恳求；征求；（妓女）拉客
words.ex: He solicits donations for the charity.
words.ex_cn: 他为慈善机构募捐。
words.en: If you solicit money, help, support, or an opinion from someone, you ask them for it.

words.ex: The bright light was a stimulus for the baby to open his eyes.
words.ex_cn: 明亮的光线是让婴儿睁开眼睛的刺激物。
words.en: Something that causes growth or activity.

words.ex: Please stir the soup before serving.
words.ex_cn: 请在上菜前搅拌一下汤。
words.en: To mix a substance or move it around using a spoon or other object; to cause to move or act; to arouse or excite.

words.ex: The smell of food whetted his appetite.
words.ex_cn: 食物的香味刺激了他的食欲。
words.en: To whet something means to make it sharper or more intense.

words.tr: adj. 招致不满的；不公平的；难以决定的
words.ex: He made an invidious comparison between his two students.
words.ex_cn: 他对他的两个学生做了令人不快的比较。
words.en: If you describe a task or job as invidious, you mean that it is likely to make you unpopular because it is unpleasant or difficult to do.

words.ex: He felt jealousy when his friend got a new bike.
words.ex_cn: 当他的朋友得到一辆新自行车时，他感到妒忌。
words.en: Jealousy is the feeling of anger or bitterness which someone has when they think that another person is trying to take a lover or friend, or a possession, away from them.

words.ex: This car is economical because it uses little fuel.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车很经济，因为它耗油少。
words.en: Using money, resources, or time in a careful and effective way.

words.tr: n. 否认；自我克制；放弃
words.ex: His abnegation of the truth made everyone sad.
words.ex_cn: 他对真相的否认让每个人都感到难过。
words.en: The act of renouncing or rejecting something, often used in the context of self-denial or the refusal of certain rights or privileges.

words.tr: v. 戒绝；弃权；自我克制
words.ex: He abstains from eating sugar.
words.ex_cn: 他戒食糖。
words.en: If you abstain from something, you deliberately do not do it or have it, especially something you like or enjoy which might be considered bad for you.

words.ex: His abstention helped the bill pass.
words.ex_cn: 他的弃权帮助法案通过了。
words.en: An abstention is a formal act of not voting either for or against a proposal.

words.ex: He is abstentious about eating sweets.
words.ex_cn: 他克制自己不吃甜食。
words.en: Someone who is abstentious avoids excess and practices self-restraint, especially in eating and drinking.

words.ex: He is abstinent from alcohol.
words.ex_cn: 他戒酒了。
words.en: Someone who is abstinent refrains from indulging in something, especially alcohol or sex.

words.tr: v. 约束；“constrain”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The rules constrained his actions.
words.ex_cn: 这些规则约束了他的行为。
words.en: If you feel constrained to do something, you feel that you must do it, even though you would prefer not to.

words.ex: Asia is the largest continent.
words.ex_cn: 亚洲是最大的洲。
words.en: A continent is a very large area of land, such as Africa or Asia, that consists of several countries.

words.ex: He showed forbearance when his friend made a mistake.
words.ex_cn: 当他的朋友犯错时，他表现出了忍耐。
words.en: Forbearance is the quality of being patient and being able to control your temper in difficult situations.

words.tr: n. 清醒；镇定；严肃；节制
words.ex: He values sobriety after his accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后重视清醒。
words.en: The state of being sober, especially in terms of not being under the influence of alcohol.

words.ex: He lives a life of asceticism, eating little and owning few things.
words.ex_cn: 他过着苦行的生活，吃得少，拥有的东西也很少。
words.en: The practice of severe self-discipline and abstention from all forms of indulgence, typically for religious reasons.

words.ex: He showed great continence by not eating the cake.
words.ex_cn: 他通过不吃蛋糕展现了极大的自制力。
words.en: The ability to control oneself, especially one's desires and impulses, particularly in the context of sexual activity.

words.tr: n. 条状物；酒吧；栅栏；棒；
words.ex: He ate a chocolate bar after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后吃了一条巧克力。
words.en: A bar is a place where alcoholic drinks are served, or a long, narrow piece of metal or wood used for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The city has a curfew at 10 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市晚上10点实行宵禁。
words.en: A curfew is an order given by the authorities that people must stay indoors between certain hours, typically at night.

words.ex: He was debarred from entering the building.
words.ex_cn: 他被禁止进入那栋楼。
words.en: To officially prevent someone from doing something or from entering a place.

words.ex: The school forbids students to use phones in class.
words.ex_cn: 学校禁止学生在课堂上使用手机。
words.en: To forbid something means to order that it must not be done.

words.tr:
n. （法庭的）禁令；禁止
v. 禁止（行动）；阻断
words.ex: The court issued an interdict to stop the construction.
words.ex_cn: 法院发布了一项禁令，以停止施工。
words.en: If someone is interdicted from doing something, they are officially prevented from doing it by a law or a rule.

words.ex: He gave an explicit answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了明确的答案。
words.en: Something that is explicit is expressed or shown clearly and openly, without any attempt to hide anything.

words.tr: v. 禁止；使失去法律保护
words.ex: The law proscribes selling alcohol to minors.
words.ex_cn: 法律禁止向未成年人出售酒精。
words.en: If a government or other authority proscribes a group or an activity, it officially forbids it or makes it illegal.

words.ex: It is a taboo to speak his name in this village.
words.ex_cn: 在这个村子里，提到他的名字是禁忌。
words.en: A taboo is a social or religious custom prohibiting or restricting a particular practice or forbidding association with a particular person, place, or thing.

words.tr: n. （政治、商业或社会性）活动；运动；
words.ex: The city launched a campaign to reduce plastic waste.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市发起了一项减少塑料垃圾的活动。
words.en: A campaign is a planned set of activities that people carry out over a period of time in order to achieve something such as social or political change.

words.ex: He contends that education is the key to success.
words.ex_cn: 他主张教育是成功的关键。
words.en: If you contend with someone or contend with something, you have to deal with a difficult situation or problem. If you contend that something is true, you state or argue that it is true.

words.ex: He won the spelling contest.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得了拼写比赛。
words.en: A contest is a competition or a struggle for victory between individuals or groups.

words.ex: He joined a crusade for clean water.
words.ex_cn: 他参加了一场为清洁用水而发起的运动。
words.en: A crusade is a long and determined attempt to achieve something that you strongly believe in, especially to bring about social or political change.

words.ex: They vie for the top prize.
words.ex_cn: 他们争夺最高奖项。
words.en: To compete eagerly with someone in order to do or achieve something.

words.tr:
adj. 竞争的
v. 竞争；争夺；“vie”的现在分词
words.ex: Two teams are vying for the championship.
words.ex_cn: 两支队伍正在争夺冠军。
words.en: If one person or thing is vying with another for something, they are competing with each other to get it.

words.tr: n. 划船比赛；赛艇比赛
words.ex: The boys joined a regatta last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 上周末，这些男孩参加了一场帆船比赛。
words.en: A regatta is a sporting event consisting of a series of boat or yacht races.

words.ex: The speaker will amplify the sound for everyone to hear.
words.ex_cn: 扬声器会放大声音，让每个人都能听到。
words.en: To amplify something means to make it louder, stronger, or more detailed.

words.tr:
n. 膨胀；凸出部分；暴涨
v. 膨胀；凸出；急增
words.ex: The balloon begins to bulge when filled with air.
words.ex_cn: 气球充气时开始鼓起来。
words.en: If something bulges, it sticks out or swells in a rounded shape.

words.ex: The doctor used drops to dilate her pupils.
words.ex_cn: 医生用了滴眼液来扩大她的瞳孔。
words.en: If you dilate something such as a part of your body, or if it dilates, it becomes larger or wider.

words.tr: v. 膨胀；肿大；使扩张；使膨胀；
words.ex: The balloon distend when filled with air.
words.ex_cn: 气球充满空气时会膨胀。
words.en: If a part of your body distends or if you distend it, it becomes larger or swollen, often because of pressure from inside.

words.ex: The balloon shows distension when filled with air.
words.ex_cn: 气球充满空气时会膨胀。
words.en: The act of distending or the state of being distended.

words.ex: The balloon showed distention after being filled with air.
words.ex_cn: 气球充满空气后出现了膨胀。
words.en: The act of distending or the state of being distended, especially the abnormal swelling of a body part due to pressure from within.

words.ex: The argument started small but soon escalate.
words.ex_cn: 争论起初很小，但很快逐步升高。
words.en: If a bad situation escalates or if someone or something escalates it, it becomes greater in size, seriousness, or intensity.

words.tr: v. 扩大；膨胀；更充分地阐述；
words.ex: The company plans to expand its business to other countries.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司计划将其业务扩大到其他国家。
words.en: To increase in size, number, or importance, or to make something increase in this way.

words.ex: He had flatulence after eating beans.
words.ex_cn: 他吃完豆子后放屁了。
words.en: Flatulence is the condition of having an excessive amount of gas in the stomach or intestines, which causes discomfort and can lead to the expulsion of gas from the anus.

words.tr: v. 膨胀；使充气；夸口；吹嘘
words.ex: He tries to inflate the balloon with his mouth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用嘴把气球吹大。
words.en: To inflate something means to cause it to increase in size by filling it with air or gas. It can also refer to increasing the amount of money in circulation, leading to a decrease in its value.

words.ex: The wound showed intumescence after the injury.
words.ex_cn: 受伤后，伤口出现了肿胀。
words.en: Intumescence refers to the process of swelling up or the state of being swollen, often used in medical or scientific contexts to describe abnormal enlargement of a body part or material.

words.tr: v. 使增加至最大限度；最大化；
words.ex: He tries to maximize his profit by selling more.
words.ex_cn: 他通过多卖东西来使利润达到最大。
words.en: To maximize something means to make it as great in amount, size, or importance as possible.

words.ex: The wound began to swell after the insect bite.
words.ex_cn: 被昆虫叮咬后，伤口开始肿胀。
words.en: To increase in size or volume as a result of internal pressure; to expand.

words.tr: adj. 肿大的；肿胀的；浮夸的
words.ex: His tumid face looked swollen after the insect bite.
words.ex_cn: 他的脸在被昆虫叮咬后显得肿胀。
words.en: Swollen or distended; pompous or bombastic in style.

words.tr:
n. 不可知论者
adj. 不可知论的
words.ex: He is agnostic about religion.
words.ex_cn: 他对宗教持不可知论态度。
words.en: An agnostic is someone who believes that it is not possible to know whether God exists or not.

words.ex: He cannot comprehend the simple math problem.
words.ex_cn: 他无法理解这个简单的数学问题。
words.en: To comprehend something means to understand it fully.

words.ex: The teacher spoke in a comprehensible way.
words.ex_cn: 老师用容易理解的方式讲话。
words.en: If something is comprehensible, you can understand it.

words.ex: His silence was an implicit apology.
words.ex_cn: 他的沉默是一种含蓄的道歉。
words.en: Something that is implicit is expressed in an indirect way.

words.tr: adj. 可理解的；明白易懂的；清楚的
words.ex: His explanation was intelligible to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的解释人人都能听懂。
words.en: Capable of being understood; comprehensible.

words.ex: He misperceives her silence as anger.
words.ex_cn: 他误以为她的沉默是生气。
words.en: To perceive incorrectly or misunderstand.

words.ex: His motives are not scrutable.
words.ex_cn: 他的动机无法理解。
words.en: Capable of being understood or interpreted.

words.ex: Children develop cognitive skills as they grow.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在成长过程中发展认知能力。
words.en: Cognitive means relating to the mental process involved in knowing, learning, and understanding things.

words.ex: He misconstrued her smile as anger.
words.ex_cn: 他误解了她的微笑，以为是生气。
words.en: If you misconstrue something that has been said or something that happens, you interpret it wrongly.

words.ex: The availability of free Wi-Fi is important for travelers.
words.ex_cn: 免费Wi-Fi的可用性对旅行者很重要。
words.en: The quality of being able to be used or obtained.

words.tr: adj. 可获得的；有空的；可用的；
words.ex: The books are available in the library.
words.ex_cn: 这些书在图书馆里可以借到。
words.en: If something is available, it is able to be used or obtained.

words.ex: He capitalized on the chance to start a business.
words.ex_cn: 他利用了这个创业的机会。
words.en: To capitalize means to use something to your advantage, especially in a way that brings financial gain. It can also mean to write or print a word with its first letter as a capital letter.

words.tr: adj. 群体的；社区的；公有的；
words.ex: They share a communal kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 他们共用一个群体厨房。
words.en: Communal means relating to or shared by all the members of a community.

words.ex: He used a disposable cup for his coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一次性杯子喝咖啡。
words.en: Something that is disposable is intended to be thrown away after use.

words.ex: He exerted pressure on his team to win.
words.ex_cn: 他给他的团队施加了压力以赢得比赛。
words.en: To exert means to use power, influence, or effort to make something happen.

words.ex: It is feasible to finish the project in one week.
words.ex_cn: 一周内完成这个项目是可行的。
words.en: If something is feasible, it can be done, made, or achieved.

words.tr: adj. 功能的；起作用的；实用的；
words.ex: This chair is functional and comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子功能性强且舒适。
words.en: Relating to the way in which something works or operates.

words.ex: The inexorable flow of time cannot be stopped.
words.ex_cn: 时间不可阻挡地流逝。
words.en: If you describe something as inexorable, you mean that it is impossible to stop or prevent from happening.

words.tr: n. 相互作用；相互影响；互动交流；
words.ex: The interaction between the two chemicals causes a reaction.
words.ex_cn: 这两种化学物质之间的相互作用引起反应。
words.en: An interaction is a situation where two or more people or things communicate with or react to each other.

words.tr: n. 几率；不利条件；不平等；
words.ex: The odds of winning the lottery are very low.
words.ex_cn: 中彩票的几率非常低。
words.en: The odds are the chances that a particular thing will happen.

words.tr: adj. 能用的；耐用的；有用的
words.ex: The old car is still serviceable.
words.ex_cn: 这辆旧车仍然可以使用。
words.en: If something is serviceable, it is in good enough condition to be used.

words.ex: The machine is underutilized because few people know how to use it.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器使用不足，因为很少有人知道如何操作它。
words.en: If something is underutilized, it is not being used as much as it could be.

words.tr: adj. 塞子未开的；未使用的；
words.ex: The untapped bottle of soda still has its cap on.
words.ex_cn: 那瓶未开盖的苏打水还封着盖子。
words.en: If something is untapped, it has not yet been used or exploited.

words.ex: We can utilize solar energy to power the house.
words.ex_cn: 我们可以利用太阳能来为房子供电。
words.en: To utilize something means to use it in a practical or effective way.

words.tr: n. 临时滞留；中途停留；短暂停留
words.ex: We had a short layover in Dubai.
words.ex_cn: 我们在迪拜有一个短暂的中转。
words.en: A layover is a short stay in a place in between parts of a journey, especially a wait between airplane flights.

words.ex: He went on an odyssey to find his lost brother.
words.ex_cn: 他踏上了一段寻找失散兄弟的漫长旅程。
words.en: An odyssey is a long and eventful or adventurous journey or experience.

words.ex: His peregrinations through Europe were filled with adventure and discovery.
words.ex_cn: 他在欧洲的游历充满了冒险和发现。
words.en: A long journey, especially one made on foot.

words.tr:
n. 谜语；费解的事
v. 解谜；出谜；使布满窟窿；打洞
words.ex: He told me a riddle and I solved it.
words.ex_cn: 他给我出了一道谜语，我解出来了。
words.en: A riddle is a question or statement that is deliberately very confusing and has a clever or amusing answer.

words.ex: The depth of the ocean remains unfathomed.
words.ex_cn: 海洋的深度仍未被探明。
words.en: Not fully explored, understood, or known.

words.ex: The old house had a labyrinthine hallway.
words.ex_cn: 这所老房子有一条像迷宫一样的走廊。
words.en: If you describe a place as labyrinthine, you mean that it is like a labyrinth because it has a lot of narrow streets or paths that cross each other, making it difficult to find your way around.

words.ex: The riddle perplexed the children.
words.ex_cn: 这个谜语让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: If something perplexes you, it confuses and worries you because you do not understand it or because it causes you difficulty.

words.tr:
adv. 迷路地；误入歧途地
adj. 迷路的；误入歧途的
words.ex: The little dog went astray in the park.
words.ex_cn: 那只小狗在公园里走丢了。
words.en: If you go astray, you lose your direction when you are trying to go somewhere.

words.tr:
v. 使困惑；难倒；阻碍
n. 挡板；遮护物；阻碍体
words.ex: The magic trick baffled the children.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: If something baffles you, you cannot understand it or explain it.

words.tr: v. 使迷惑；使混乱；使烂醉
words.ex: The complicated instructions befuddle him.
words.ex_cn: 这些复杂的说明让他困惑。
words.en: If something befuddles you, it confuses your mind or thoughts.

words.ex: The strange math problem caused his befuddlement.
words.ex_cn: 这个奇怪的数学题让他感到困惑。
words.en: Befuddlement is a state of confusion or perplexity.

words.tr:
adj. 困惑的；发呆的
v. 使困惑；使茫然；“bemuse”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He looked bemused when the teacher asked a strange question.
words.ex_cn: 当老师问了一个奇怪的问题时，他看起来很困惑。
words.en: If you are bemused, you are puzzled or confused.

words.tr: v. 使迷惑；使...不知所措
words.ex: The strange signs bewilder the children.
words.ex_cn: 这些奇怪的符号让孩子们感到迷惑。
words.en: If something bewilders you, it is so confusing or difficult that you cannot understand it.

words.tr:
adj. 令人困惑的；使人糊涂的
v. 使迷惑；使昏乱；“bewilder”的现在分词
words.ex: The maze was bewildering.
words.ex_cn: 这个迷宫令人困惑。
words.en: If something is bewildering, it is very confusing and difficult to understand or to make a decision about.

words.ex: The magic show captivates the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演吸引了孩子们。
words.en: If you are captivated by someone or something, you find them fascinating and attractive.

words.ex: The strange noise confounded the children.
words.ex_cn: 奇怪的声音让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: To confuse and surprise someone, especially by being difficult to understand or deal with.

words.tr:
v. 使发昏；使迷乱
n. 恍惚； 晕眩
words.ex: The loud noise dazed him for a moment.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让他一时发昏。
words.en: If someone is in a daze, they are feeling confused and unable to think clearly, often because they have had a shock or surprise.

words.tr: adj. 神志不清的；极度兴奋的；发狂的
words.ex: He was delirious after the fever.
words.ex_cn: 他发烧后神志不清。
words.en: If someone is delirious, they are not able to think or speak in a sensible and reasonable way, usually because they are very ill and have a fever.

words.tr:
adj. 困惑的；尴尬的
v. 使为难；使挫折；使窘迫；“discomfit”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He felt discomfited when he couldn't answer the simple question.
words.ex_cn: 当他无法回答这个简单的问题时，他感到很困惑。
words.en: If you are discomfited by something, it makes you feel slightly anxious, embarrassed, or upset.

words.ex: The magic show enthralls the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演让孩子们着迷。
words.en: If you are enthralled by something, you are so interested and excited by it that you give it all your attention.

words.tr: v. 强烈吸引住；使着迷；
words.ex: The magic show fascinated the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演深深吸引了孩子们。
words.en: If something fascinates you, it interests and delights you so much that your thoughts tend to concentrate on it.

words.ex: The mirage in the desert is an illusive image.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠中的海市蜃楼是一个虚幻的景象。
words.en: If something is illusive, it is based on an illusion and is not real or true.

words.tr: n. 迷宫；难解的事件；错综复杂；
words.ex: The child got lost in the labyrinth.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在迷宫里迷路了。
words.en: A labyrinth is a complicated irregular network of passages or paths in which it is difficult to find one's way; a maze.

words.tr: n. 迷宫；错综复杂的曲径；
words.ex: The children got lost in the maze.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在迷宫里迷路了。
words.en: A maze is a complex system of paths or passages in which it is easy to get lost.

words.tr:
v. 使迷惑；使不知所措
n. 迷惑；困惑；为难
words.ex: The tricky question nonplused the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 这个棘手的问题让老师不知所措。
words.en: To cause to be at a loss as to what to say, think, or do; perplex.

words.tr: v. （故意地）混淆；使混乱；使困惑
words.ex: He tries to obfuscate the truth with complicated words.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用复杂的词语混淆真相。
words.en: To obfuscate something means to deliberately make it unclear or difficult to understand.

words.tr: v. 蔓延；散乱地分布；落伍
words.ex: Weeds straggle across the garden.
words.ex_cn: 杂草蔓延在整个花园里。
words.en: If people straggle, they move along slowly, spread out over a wide area, and are not in a group.

words.tr:
v. 使惊慌失措；使慌张
n. 慌张；慌乱
words.ex: He got flustered when the teacher asked him a question.
words.ex_cn: 当老师问他问题时，他变得慌乱了。
words.en: If you fluster someone, you make them feel nervous and confused by rushing them or by making it difficult for them to concentrate on what they are doing.

words.ex: The witch bewitches the prince with her song.
words.ex_cn: 女巫用她的歌声迷住了王子。
words.en: To bewitch someone means to attract them so strongly that they seem to be under a spell.

words.ex: He used an adhesive to stick the paper on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 他用黏合剂把纸贴在墙上。
words.en: An adhesive is a substance used for sticking objects or materials together.

words.ex: He affixed a stamp to the envelope.
words.ex_cn: 他把邮票贴在信封上。
words.en: To attach, fasten, or join something to something else.

words.ex: Please attach the file to the email.
words.ex_cn: 请将文件附加到邮件中。
words.en: To attach something to something else means to fasten or join it to the other thing.

words.ex: The child clings to his mother's leg.
words.ex_cn: 孩子紧贴着妈妈的腿。
words.en: If you cling to someone or something, you hold onto them tightly.

words.ex: The glutinous rice sticks together when cooked.
words.ex_cn: 糯米煮熟后会粘在一起。
words.en: Something that is glutinous is sticky and often thick.

words.ex: The tackiness of the glue made it difficult to remove from the surface.
words.ex_cn: 胶水的粘着性使得它很难从表面去除。
words.en: The quality of being sticky or of lacking style or good taste.

words.ex: The syrup is very viscid and flows slowly.
words.ex_cn: 这种糖浆很粘稠，流动得很慢。
words.en: A viscid substance is thick and sticky.

words.ex: Honey is a viscous liquid.
words.ex_cn: 蜂蜜是一种黏稠的液体。
words.en: A viscous liquid is thick and sticky and does not flow easily.

words.tr: v. 黏合；连结；附着；连贯；形成整体
words.ex: The pieces cohere to form a complete picture.
words.ex_cn: 这些碎片组合在一起形成一幅完整的图画。
words.en: If the different elements of a piece of writing, a theory, or a policy cohere, they fit together well so that they form a united whole.

words.ex: The old wall began to crumble after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 旧墙在雨后开始坍塌。
words.en: If something crumbles, or if you crumble it, it breaks into a lot of small pieces.

words.tr: adj. 脆弱的；易碎的；不牢固的；
words.ex: The glass is fragile and might break easily.
words.ex_cn: 这个玻璃很脆弱，容易碎。
words.en: If something is fragile, it is easily broken or damaged.

words.ex: The ancient pottery was so friable that it crumbled in our hands.
words.ex_cn: 这件古老的陶器非常易碎，在我们手中就碎了。
words.en: Easily crumbled or reduced to powder.

words.tr:
v. 切碎；剁碎；装腔作势地小步走
n. 绞碎的肉
words.ex: He minces garlic for the sauce.
words.ex_cn: 他把大蒜剁碎用来做酱。
words.en: To mince means to cut food, especially meat, into very small pieces, or to walk or speak in an affected manner.

words.ex: The scrappy room was full of clothes and toys on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 这个不整洁的房间里到处都是衣服和玩具。
words.en: If you describe someone as scrappy, you mean that they are determined and unwilling to give up, even in a difficult situation.

words.tr:
n. 球类运动（squash）；
v. 压碎；
words.ex: He plays squash every weekend with his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他每周末和朋友打壁球。
words.en: To squash something means to press or squeeze it so that it becomes flat, soft, or out of shape. It can also refer to the sport of squash or a type of vegetable.

words.ex: The machine extrudes plastic into long tubes.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器将塑料挤出成长管状。
words.en: To force or push out through a small opening.

words.ex: This tool can obviate the need for manual work.
words.ex_cn: 这个工具可以避免手动工作的需要。
words.en: To obviate means to remove a need or difficulty, especially so that action to deal with it becomes unnecessary.

words.ex: The rain precludes a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 下雨阻止了野餐。
words.en: If something precludes an event or action, it prevents it from happening.

words.tr: n. 厌恶；嫌弃；排斥；斥力
words.ex: The sight filled her with repulsion.
words.ex_cn: 那景象让她感到厌恶。
words.en: A feeling of intense distaste or disgust.

words.ex: Smartphones supplanted landline phones.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机取代了固定电话。
words.en: To supplant someone or something means to take the place of them, often by being more powerful or effective.

words.ex: His supposition is that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他的假设是明天会下雨。
words.en: A supposition is a guess or a theory that you have about something, which may not be true.

words.ex: The judge will adjudicate the dispute next week.
words.ex_cn: 法官将在下周裁决这场纠纷。
words.en: To adjudicate means to make an official decision about a problem or dispute.

words.ex: The teacher will appraise my essay next week.
words.ex_cn: 老师下周会评价我的作文。
words.en: If you appraise something or someone, you consider them carefully and form an opinion about them.

words.ex: The judge will arbitrate the dispute between the two neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 法官将调解这两个邻居之间的纠纷。
words.en: To arbitrate means to officially settle a dispute by making a decision that both sides accept.

words.ex: The teacher will assess your homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天会评估你的作业。
words.en: to judge or decide the amount, value, quality, or importance of something

words.ex: The teacher gave an assessment of the students' work.
words.ex_cn: 老师对学生的作品进行了评估。
words.en: An assessment is a judgment about something, especially about how good or bad it is, or an amount that is calculated for something, especially for tax purposes.

words.ex: The teacher gave an evaluation of the student's work.
words.ex_cn: 老师对学生的作业进行了评估。
words.en: An evaluation is a judgment about how good, useful, or successful something is.

words.ex: He inferred that she was tired from her yawns.
words.ex_cn: 他从她的哈欠推断出她很累。
words.en: If you infer that something is the case, you decide that it is true on the basis of information that you already have.

words.tr: adj. 可衡量的；可估计的；值得考虑的
words.ex: The question of ethics is a ponderable issue in this debate.
words.ex_cn: 道德问题是这场辩论中值得考虑的问题。
words.en: Capable of being weighed or assessed.

words.ex: The umpire blew the whistle when the player broke the rule.
words.ex_cn: 当球员犯规时，裁判吹响了哨子。
words.en: An umpire is a person whose job is to make sure that a game is played fairly and that the rules are not broken.

words.tr: adj. 低能的；意志薄弱的；精神薄弱的
words.ex: He was considered feebleminded and unfit to make important decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他被认为意志薄弱，不适合做重要决定。
words.en: If you describe someone as feebleminded, you mean that they are not very intelligent or are not able to make sensible decisions.

words.ex: The small boat capsize in the storm.
words.ex_cn: 小船在风暴中倾覆了。
words.en: If a boat capsizes or if you capsize it, it turns over in the water.

words.tr: v. 倾倒；摇摇欲坠；将…推翻；使…跌倒
words.ex: The strong wind toppled the old tree.
words.ex_cn: 大风把那棵老树吹倒了。
words.en: If someone or something topples, or if someone or something topples them, they become unsteady or unstable and fall over.

words.tr: n. 恶作剧；淘气；伤害；损害
words.ex: The boy caused mischief by letting the cats out.
words.ex_cn: 那个男孩放出了猫，惹了麻烦。
words.en: Mischief is behavior, especially by children, that is slightly bad but is not intended to cause serious harm or damage.

words.ex: He feared perdition for his wicked deeds.
words.ex_cn: 他因自己的恶行而害怕堕入地狱。
words.en: Perdition is a state of eternal punishment and damnation into which a sinful and unrepentant person is believed to pass after death.

words.tr: v. 大批杀死；大量毁灭
words.ex: The storm decimated the village.
words.ex_cn: 风暴摧毁了这个村庄。
words.en: To decimate something such as a group of people or animals means to destroy a very large number of them.

words.tr: v. 损伤…的外观；在…上乱涂乱画
words.ex: They deface the wall with graffiti.
words.ex_cn: 他们用涂鸦破坏了墙壁。
words.en: To deface something means to spoil its appearance by writing or drawing on it, or by damaging it in some other way.

words.ex: They will demolish the old building next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们下周会拆掉那座旧建筑。
words.en: To demolish something such as a building means to destroy it completely. It can also mean to defeat someone completely in a discussion, argument, or competition.

words.tr: n. 摧毁；拆毁；拆除；大败；
words.ex: The demolition of the old building started last week.
words.ex_cn: 那座旧楼的拆除上周开始了。
words.en: The act of demolishing something, especially a building.

words.tr: adj. 可破坏的；易被摧毁的
words.ex: The building was made of destructible materials.
words.ex_cn: 这座建筑是用易损坏的材料建造的。
words.en: Capable of being destroyed.

words.ex: The earthquake devastated the small town.
words.ex_cn: 地震摧毁了这个小镇。
words.en: To devastate means to destroy or ruin something completely, or to cause someone to feel extreme sadness or shock.

words.tr: v. 损毁…的外形；使变丑
words.ex: The accident disfigured his face.
