words.ex_cn: 那次事故使他的脸变形了。
words.en: To disfigure someone or something means to spoil their appearance.

words.ex: The stain on the carpet is a mar.
words.ex_cn: 地毯上的污渍是一个污点。
words.en: To mar something means to spoil or damage it.

words.tr: v. 破坏；毁坏；“mar”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The painting was marred by a large scratch.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画被一道大划痕损毁了。
words.en: If something is marred, it is spoiled or made less enjoyable by something.

words.tr:
v. 推翻；颠覆；打倒
n. 推翻；颠覆；打倒
words.ex: The court will overturn the old law.
words.ex_cn: 法院将推翻这项旧法律。
words.en: If a decision, result, etc. is overturned, it is officially changed so that it becomes the opposite of what it was before.

words.tr: v. 使夷为平地；彻底摧毁
words.ex: They will raze the old building next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们下周将把那座旧建筑夷为平地。
words.en: To raze a building, town, or forest means to completely destroy it, especially by knocking it down or burning it.

words.tr:
n. 蓄意破坏
v. 蓄意破坏；暗中破坏
words.ex: He tried to sabotage the project.
words.ex_cn: 他试图破坏这个项目。
words.en: Sabotage is the act of deliberately destroying, damaging, or obstructing something, especially for political or military advantage.

words.tr: v. 使粉碎；使破碎；使破灭；“shatter”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The stone shattered when it hit the ground.
words.ex_cn: 石头撞到地面时碎裂了。
words.en: If something is shattered, it is broken into many small pieces, or it is extremely tired or shocked.

words.tr:
adj. 颠覆性的；破坏性的
n. 颠覆分子；危险分子
words.ex: The subversive poster tried to break the government's rules.
words.ex_cn: 那张颠覆性的海报试图破坏政府的规则。
words.en: A subversive person or activity is one that is intended to weaken or destroy a political system or government.

words.ex: They tried to subvert the government.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图颠覆政府。
words.en: To subvert means to undermine the power and authority of an established system or institution.

words.ex: The cows trample the grass in the field.
words.ex_cn: 牛在田野里践踏草地。
words.en: If someone tramples something or tramples on it, they step heavily and carelessly on it and damage it.

words.tr: v. 逐渐削弱；暗中损害；
words.ex: Constant criticism can undermine your confidence.
words.ex_cn: 不断的批评会逐渐削弱你的信心。
words.en: To undermine something means to weaken it or make it less effective, often in a gradual or sneaky way.

words.tr: adj. 没有受伤的；未受损害的；
words.ex: He walked away from the crash unscathed.
words.ex_cn: 他从车祸中安然无恙地走开了。
words.en: If someone is unscathed after a dangerous experience, they have not been injured or harmed by it.

words.tr: n. 恣意毁坏他人财产罪
words.ex: The boys did vandalism by breaking the windows.
words.ex_cn: 那些男孩通过砸坏窗户实施了破坏行为。
words.en: The crime of deliberately damaging or destroying public or private property.

words.tr: v. 肆意破坏（尤指公共财物）
words.ex: They vandalize the park with graffiti.
words.ex_cn: 他们用涂鸦破坏公园。
words.en: To vandalize something means to deliberately damage or destroy property belonging to others.

words.ex: He violated the school rule by using his phone in class.
words.ex_cn: 他上课使用手机，违反了校规。
words.en: If someone violates an agreement, law, or promise, they break it.

words.ex: The government raised the excise on tobacco.
words.ex_cn: 政府提高了烟草的货物税。
words.en: Excise is a tax that is charged on goods produced within a country, or on goods that are brought into a country from abroad, especially on goods such as alcohol and tobacco. It can also refer to the act of cutting out or removing something, especially in a surgical operation.

words.ex: The artist incised the design into the wood.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家将设计雕刻在木头上。
words.en: To cut into a surface with a sharp tool; to carve or engrave.

words.ex: The two lines intersect at point A.
words.ex_cn: 两条线在点A相交。
words.en: If two or more lines or roads intersect, they meet or cross each other.

words.tr: v. 用薄片覆盖；压成薄片；
words.ex: They laminate the table with plastic to make it waterproof.
words.ex_cn: 他们用塑料薄片覆盖桌子，使其防水。
words.en: To laminate something means to cover it with a layer of plastic or another material for protection or to make it stronger.

words.tr: v. 使残废；使残缺不全；毁伤
words.ex: The accident mutilated his hand.
words.ex_cn: 事故使他的手残废了。
words.en: To mutilate something or someone means to damage them severely, for example by cutting off or destroying part of them.

words.tr:
v. 使成锯齿状
adj. 锯齿状的
words.ex: The leaf has a serrate edge.
words.ex_cn: 这片叶子的边缘是锯齿状的。
words.en: Having a notched or toothed edge, especially in reference to the edges of leaves or other plant parts.

words.ex: The serration on the edge of the blade made it difficult to cut smoothly.
words.ex_cn: 刀刃边缘的锯齿状突起使得切割变得困难。
words.en: A serration is a series of small, sharp points or notches on the edge of an object, resembling the teeth of a saw.

words.tr: v. 卸货；（使）下船（或飞机，车等）
words.ex: The passengers began to debark as soon as the ship docked.
words.ex_cn: 船一靠岸，乘客们就开始下船。
words.en: To leave a ship or airplane; to disembark.

words.ex: They will dismantle the old bridge next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们下周将拆除这座旧桥。
words.en: To dismantle something means to take it to pieces.

words.ex: He tried to dispel the fear with calm words.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用平静的话语消除恐惧。
words.en: To dispel something such as a fear, belief, or idea means to make it disappear or to make people stop believing it.

words.tr: v. 除去表面上的污渍
words.ex: The workers need to deseam the metal sheets before they can be used in construction.
words.ex_cn: 工人们需要去除金属板的焊缝，然后才能用于建筑。
words.en: To remove the seam from (a metal object), especially by grinding or cutting.

words.ex: We must eliminate the waste to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 我们必须消除浪费以保护环境。
words.en: To eliminate something, especially something you do not want or need, means to remove it completely.

words.tr: v. 驱（魔）；除去（痛苦的想法等）
words.ex: The priest tried to exorcise the demon from the house.
words.ex_cn: 牧师试图将恶魔从房子里驱逐出去。
words.en: To exorcise means to drive out or attempt to drive out (a supposed evil spirit) from a person or place.

words.ex: The court decided to expunge his record.
words.ex_cn: 法院决定删除他的记录。
words.en: If you expunge something, you get rid of it completely, because it causes problems or bad feelings.

words.tr: v. 删去（书籍中不合适之处）
words.ex: The teacher expurgated the old book to remove bad words.
words.ex_cn: 老师删改了这本旧书，去掉了不好的词语。
words.en: To remove material that is considered improper or offensive from (a book, movie, etc.).

words.ex: The new law will supersede the old one.
words.ex_cn: 新法律将取代旧法律。
words.en: If something is superseded by something newer, it is replaced because it has become old-fashioned or unacceptable.

words.ex: The camera will unmask the hidden face.
words.ex_cn: 摄像头将揭开隐藏的脸。
words.en: To reveal the true nature of someone or something, especially when it has been hidden.

words.ex: The wizard conjure a fireball with ancient words.
words.ex_cn: 巫师用古老的咒语召唤出一个火球。
words.en: If you conjure something out of nothing, you make it appear as if by magic.

words.ex: He submitted his application for the job last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周提交了那份工作申请。
words.en: An application is a formal request, often written, for something such as a job, a place at a university, or permission to do something. It can also refer to the act of putting something to a special use or purpose, or a program or piece of software designed to perform a specific function.

words.ex: She beseeched him to stay with her.
words.ex_cn: 她恳求他留下来陪她。
words.en: If you beseech someone to do something, you ask them very eagerly and anxiously.

words.ex: He entreats his friend to help him.
words.ex_cn: 他恳求朋友帮助他。
words.en: To ask someone earnestly or anxiously to do something.

words.ex: She made an earnest entreaty for forgiveness.
words.ex_cn: 她真诚地恳求原谅。
words.en: An entreaty is a serious and often emotional request for something, especially for help or mercy.

words.ex: She implored him to stay.
words.ex_cn: 她恳求他留下。
words.en: If you implore someone to do something, you ask them to do it in a forceful, emotional way.

words.tr: v. 不断请求；胡搅蛮缠
words.ex: He importunes his boss for a raise.
words.ex_cn: 他不断向老板请求加薪。
words.en: To importune someone means to ask them for something repeatedly and in a way that is annoying or troublesome.

words.ex: He muttered imprecations under his breath.
words.ex_cn: 他低声念着咒语。
words.en: An imprecation is a curse or a swear word.

words.ex: He will intercede for his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他会为他的朋友出面说情。
words.en: If you intercede with someone, you try to persuade them to forgive someone or end their disagreement with them.

words.ex: He invoked the law to protect his rights.
words.ex_cn: 他援引法律来保护自己的权利。
words.en: If you invoke a law, rule, or principle, you refer to it as a reason or justification for something.

words.tr: v. 恳求；辩护；答辩；以…为理由
words.ex: He pleaded for help when he was lost.
words.ex_cn: 当他迷路时，他恳求帮助。
words.en: If you plead with someone to do something, you ask them in an intense, emotional way to do it.

words.tr:
adj. 恳求的
n. 恳求者
words.ex: The suppliant knelt before the king.
words.ex_cn: 恳求者在国王面前跪下。
words.en: A suppliant is someone who asks for something in a very humble or earnest way, often by kneeling or bowing.

words.ex: He supplicated for mercy.
words.ex_cn: 他恳求宽恕。
words.en: to ask for something in a humble way; to beg earnestly and humbly

words.ex: He would often cadge cigarettes from strangers.
words.ex_cn: 他经常向陌生人乞讨香烟。
words.en: To cadge means to ask for and obtain something without paying for it, often by persuading someone to give it to you.

words.tr: adj. 未被要求的；未经邀请的；自发的
words.ex: She felt a sense of intrusion as the unbidden thoughts flooded her mind.
words.ex_cn: 当这些未受邀请的想法涌入她的脑海时，她感到一种被侵犯的感觉。
words.en: Not invited or asked for; spontaneous.

words.tr: adj. 引起兴趣的； v. 吸引；“appeal”的现在分词；
words.ex: The book has an appealing story.
words.ex_cn: 这本书有一个引人入胜的故事。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as appealing, you mean that you like them or they make you want to have or do something.

words.ex: He made an adjuration to tell the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他恳切地要求说实话。
words.en: An adjuration is a solemn urging or a formal command, often invoking a sacred or authoritative source to compel someone to act or to refrain from acting.

words.tr: v. 驱逐出境；使举止得体
words.ex: They will deport him for breaking the law.
words.ex_cn: 他们将因他违法而驱逐他。
words.en: If a government deports someone, usually someone who is not a citizen of that country, it sends them out of the country because they have committed a crime or because it believes they do not have the right to be there.

words.ex: The man faced deportation for breaking the law.
words.ex_cn: 这个人因违法而面临驱逐。
words.en: The act of expelling a person from a country, typically because they do not have the legal right to be there or because they have committed a crime.

words.ex: He used a stick to dislodge the rock from the path.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根棍子把石头从路上移出。
words.en: To dislodge something means to remove it from a place where it is fixed or held.

words.ex: The landlord will evict the tenant for not paying rent.
words.ex_cn: 房东会因为租客不付房租而将他驱逐。
words.en: To evict someone means to force them to leave a house or piece of land, usually because they have not paid the rent or have broken the law.

words.tr: n. （尤指依法从房屋或土地上）驱逐；
words.ex: The landlord filed for eviction after the tenant refused to pay rent.
words.ex_cn: 租客拒绝支付租金后，房东申请了驱逐。
words.en: The act of expelling someone, especially a tenant, from a property; expulsion.

words.ex: The rule excludes children under 12.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则排除了12岁以下的孩子。
words.en: To exclude someone or something means to prevent them from entering a place or taking part in an activity.

words.ex: He faced ostracism from his classmates for speaking up.
words.ex_cn: 他因为发声而遭到同学的排斥。
words.en: Ostracism is the act of excluding someone from a group or society by common consent.

words.ex: They ostracize him for being different.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为他与众不同而排斥他。
words.en: To ostracize someone means to exclude them from a society or group.

words.ex: The team will oust the coach after the loss.
words.ex_cn: 球队在输球后将撤换教练。
words.en: If someone is ousted from a position of power, job, or place, they are forced to leave it.

words.tr:
v. 击退；回绝；憎恶
n. 拒斥；击退；严拒
words.ex: The soldiers repulse the enemy attack.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们击退了敌人的进攻。
words.en: If you repulse someone, you reject them or make them feel disgusted.

words.tr:
v. 放电；放出；
n. 排放；
words.ex: The battery will discharge if left unused for a long time.
words.ex_cn: 如果长时间不使用，电池会放电。
words.en: If someone is discharged from a hospital, prison, or the armed forces, they are officially allowed to leave, or told that they must leave. If something is discharged from inside a place, it comes out.

words.ex: The body expels waste through the kidneys.
words.ex_cn: 身体通过肾脏排出废物。
words.en: If someone is expelled from a school or organization, they are officially told to leave because they have behaved badly or broken the rules.

words.ex: He faced expulsion for breaking the school rules.
words.ex_cn: 他因违反校规而被开除。
words.en: Expulsion is the act of forcing someone to leave a place, especially a school or a country, as a punishment or because they are not wanted there.

words.ex: He dismissed her advice and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他不理会她的建议，走开了。
words.en: If you dismiss someone, you send them away or allow them to leave.

words.ex: The priest was defrocked after being found guilty of misconduct.
words.ex_cn: 牧师因行为不当被判有罪后被解除僧职。
words.en: To remove someone from their position as a priest or minister, often as a punishment for doing something wrong.

words.tr:
n. （下反对命令）取消（前一命令）；调回；取消（定货）
v. （下反对命令）取消（前一命令）；调回；取消（定货）
words.ex: The general countermanded the order to attack.
words.ex_cn: 将军取消了进攻的命令。
words.en: If you countermand an order, you cancel it, usually by giving a different order.

words.tr: adj. 无法改变的；不能取消的
words.ex: The decision was irrevocable.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定是不可撤销的。
words.en: If a decision, action, or process is irrevocable, it cannot be changed or reversed.

words.tr: v. 删节猥亵不当的部分
words.ex: The publisher decided to bowdlerize the novel to make it suitable for younger readers.
words.ex_cn: 出版商决定删改这本小说，使其适合年轻读者阅读。
words.en: To bowdlerize a book or film means to remove parts of it that are considered offensive or improper, especially in order to make it suitable for children or for people who might be offended.

words.ex: The drought depletes the water supply.
words.ex_cn: 干旱耗尽了水源。
words.en: If you deplete something, you reduce the amount of it that is available or that exists.

words.ex: He tried to disabuse her of the idea that money solves everything.
words.ex_cn: 他试图让她明白，钱并不能解决所有问题。
words.en: If you disabuse someone of something, you tell them or persuade them that what they believe is in fact not true.

words.ex: The government wants to eradicate poverty.
words.ex_cn: 政府希望消灭贫困。
words.en: To eradicate something means to get rid of it completely.

words.tr: v. （因抵押人未如期还贷）取消赎回权；排除；妨碍
words.ex: The bank foreclosed on the house after the owner defaulted on the mortgage.
words.ex_cn: 房主在抵押贷款违约后，银行取消了房屋的赎回权。
words.en: If the person or organization that lent someone money forecloses, they take possession of a property that was bought with the borrowed money, for example because regular repayments have not been made.

words.ex: She is weaning her baby off milk.
words.ex_cn: 她正在让宝宝戒掉牛奶。
words.en: To wean someone off something means to make them gradually stop using or depending on it, especially something harmful or unnecessary.

words.ex: They tried to extirpate the weeds from the garden.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图把花园里的杂草彻底清除。
words.en: To destroy or remove something completely, especially a problem or an organization.

words.ex: He will delete the old file.
words.ex_cn: 他会删除那个旧文件。
words.en: To delete something means to remove it or erase it.

words.ex: You must abide by the rules.
words.ex_cn: 你必须遵守规则。
words.en: If you can't abide someone or something, you dislike them very much.

words.ex: His countenance showed surprise.
words.ex_cn: 他的面容流露出惊讶。
words.en: A person's face or facial expression; support or approval.

words.ex: He had to endure the cold winter without a coat.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不在没有外套的情况下忍受寒冷的冬天。
words.en: To endure means to suffer something difficult, unpleasant, or painful, or to continue to exist for a long time.

words.ex: He ate too much and his stomach hurt.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多了，胃疼。
words.en: The stomach is the organ in your body where food is digested after you have eaten it.

words.ex: The farmer works hard to sustain his crops.
words.ex_cn: 这位农民努力维持他的庄稼。
words.en: To sustain something means to continue it or maintain it for a period of time.

words.ex: He swallowed the pill with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水吞下了药片。
words.en: To swallow means to make food or drink go down your throat and towards your stomach. It can also mean to accept something without protest or to believe something too easily.

words.ex: His tolerance for different opinions is impressive.
words.ex_cn: 他对不同观点的宽容令人印象深刻。
words.en: The ability or willingness to tolerate the existence of opinions or behaviour that one dislikes or disagrees with.

words.ex: The weather is sunny today.
words.ex_cn: 今天天气晴朗。
words.en: The condition of the atmosphere at a particular place and time, especially with regard to temperature, precipitation, and wind.

words.ex: The bridge can withstand strong winds.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥能经受住强风。
words.en: If something or someone withstands a force or action, they survive it or do not give in to it.

words.ex: He forbears from yelling when he is angry.
words.ex_cn: 他生气时忍住不喊叫。
words.en: If you forbear from doing something, you do not do it although you have the opportunity or the right to do it.

words.ex: He has great stamina for running long distances.
words.ex_cn: 他有很强的耐力来跑长距离。
words.en: Stamina is the physical or mental energy needed to do a tiring activity for a long time.

words.ex: The king will bestow a medal on the hero.
words.ex_cn: 国王将把奖章授予这位英雄。
words.en: To bestow something on someone means to give or present it to them.

words.ex: Clean water is a boon to the village.
words.ex_cn: 干净的水对这个村庄是有益的。
words.en: A boon is something that is very helpful and improves the quality of life.

words.ex: The university conferred an honorary degree on him.
words.ex_cn: 大学授予他一个荣誉学位。
words.en: To confer something such as a degree or an honor on someone means to give it to them in a formal way. To confer with someone means to discuss something with them in order to make a decision.

words.ex: He donate money to the poor children.
words.ex_cn: 他向贫困儿童捐赠钱。
words.en: To donate means to give something, especially money, to a person or organization that needs help.

words.tr:
n. 花环
v. 给…戴上花环
words.ex: She put a garland on the door for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对在门上挂了一个花环。
words.en: A garland is a circular decoration made from flowers and leaves, which is worn on the head or hung up as a decoration.

words.ex: The company showed its largess by donating to several charities.
words.ex_cn: 公司通过向几家慈善机构捐款展示了它的慷慨。
words.en: Largess refers to the generous giving of gifts or money, often by a person of high status, such as a king or noble, to their subjects or followers.

words.ex: He won a gold medal in the Olympics.
words.ex_cn: 他在奥运会上赢得了一枚金牌。
words.en: A medal is a small metal disc which is given as an award for bravery or as a prize in a sporting event.

words.ex: The law obliges drivers to wear seat belts.
words.ex_cn: 法律迫使司机系安全带。
words.en: If you are obliged to do something, you have to do it because the situation, the law, a duty, etc., makes it necessary.

words.tr: adj.  施舍的；慈善的；接受接济的
words.ex: The eleemosynary organization provided food and shelter to the homeless.
words.ex_cn: 这个慈善组织为无家可归者提供了食物和住所。
words.en: Relating to or dependent on charity; charitable.

words.ex: He decided to embark on a new career.
words.ex_cn: 他决定从事一份新职业。
words.en: To embark on something means to start it, especially something new, difficult, or exciting.

words.ex: He is the beneficiary of his father's will.
words.ex_cn: 他是他父亲遗嘱的受益人。
words.en: A beneficiary is someone who receives money or other benefits as a result of something, especially a will or insurance policy.

words.ex: He alleges that the manager stole money.
words.ex_cn: 他声称经理偷了钱。
words.en: If you allege that something bad is true, you say it but do not prove it.

words.tr: v. 断言；宣称；坚持；维护
words.ex: He asserts that the answer is correct.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持认为答案是正确的。
words.en: To state a fact or belief confidently and forcefully.

words.ex: The candidate's avowal of support for the new policy was met with mixed reactions.
words.ex_cn: 候选人公开支持新政策的声明引起了褒贬不一的反应。
words.en: An avowal is a statement in which you say or admit something that you believe, support, or intend to do.

words.tr:
v. 声称；索赔；
n. 声称；索要；
words.ex: He claims that he saw a UFO last night.
words.ex_cn: 他声称自己昨晚看到了不明飞行物。
words.en: If you say that someone claims that something is true, you mean they say that it is true but you are not sure whether or not they are telling the truth.

words.tr: n. 解说词；评论；实况报道；
words.ex: The commentator gave live commentary during the soccer match.
words.ex_cn: 解说员在足球比赛期间进行了现场解说。
words.en: A commentary is a spoken or written description of an event or situation that is broadcast or published as it occurs.

words.tr: v. 解释；把…逐字译出；作句法分析
words.ex: He construes her silence as a yes.
words.ex_cn: 他把她的沉默理解为同意。
words.en: If you construe something in a particular way, you interpret it in that way.

words.ex: He tried to decipher the secret code.
words.ex_cn: 他试图破译那个秘密代码。
words.en: To decipher something means to convert it from a code into normal language or to understand something that is difficult to understand or that is not obvious.

words.ex: He can decode the secret message.
words.ex_cn: 他能译解这个秘密信息。
words.en: To convert coded data into intelligible form.

words.tr: n. 精心制作；详尽的细节；
words.ex: The chef gave an elaboration to the dish with fresh herbs.
words.ex_cn: 厨师用新鲜香草对这道菜进行了精心制作。
words.en: The process of developing or presenting a theory, policy, or system in detail.

words.ex: The teacher elucidated the math problem with a simple diagram.
words.ex_cn: 老师用一个简单的图表阐明了这道数学题。
words.en: To make something clear or easy to understand by explaining or giving reasons.

words.ex: His smile evinces joy.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑流露出快乐。
words.en: To show clearly that you have a particular quality, feeling, or ability.

words.tr: adj. 可说明的；可解释的
words.ex: The mistake is explicable because she was new.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误是可以解释的，因为她是个新手。
words.en: If something is explicable, it can be explained and understood because it is logical or there is a clear reason for it.

words.tr: v. 举例说明；给书籍、杂志等加插图；
words.ex: The teacher illustrated the point with a simple story.
words.ex_cn: 老师用一个简单的故事来举例说明这个观点。
words.en: To illustrate something means to explain or demonstrate it clearly, often by giving examples or by using pictures or diagrams.

words.ex: He iterate the importance of honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他反复说诚实的重要性。
words.en: To say or do something again or several times.

words.ex: The legend says a dragon lives in the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 传说有一条龙住在山里。
words.en: A legend is a very old and popular story that may be true or may be imaginary.

words.ex: He wrote a manifesto to explain his ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一份宣言来解释他的观点。
words.en: A manifesto is a written statement of the beliefs, aims, and policies of an organization, especially a political party.

words.ex: He paraphrased the poem in simple words.
words.ex_cn: 他用简单的语言意译了这首诗。
words.en: To paraphrase means to express the meaning of something written or spoken using different words, especially to achieve greater clarity.

words.ex: The king proclaimed a new law.
words.ex_cn: 国王宣告了一项新法律。
words.en: If you proclaim something, you formally announce it or declare it publicly.

words.ex: The king made a proclamation about peace.
words.ex_cn: 国王发布了一项关于和平的公告。
words.en: A proclamation is a public announcement about something important, often made by a king, queen, or government.

words.ex: The government will promulgate new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将公布新规则。
words.en: To promulgate means to make a new law or rule known officially and publicly.

words.ex: He wants to publicize his new book.
words.ex_cn: 他想宣传他的新书。
words.en: To publicize something means to make it widely known to the public, especially by using the media.

words.tr: adj. 规定的；指定的；约定俗成的；
words.ex: The teacher gave a prescriptive rule for writing essays.
words.ex_cn: 老师给出了一个关于写论文的规定性规则。
words.en: If something is prescriptive, it involves making rules or giving instructions about what should be done.

words.ex: The teacher will announce the results tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天将宣布结果。
words.en: To announce something means to make it known publicly or officially.

words.ex: He apprised her of the change.
words.ex_cn: 他通知了她这个变化。
words.en: If you are apprised of something, someone tells you about it.

words.tr: adj. 有说服力的；令人信服的
words.ex: His argument was cogent and easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点有说服力且容易理解。
words.en: A cogent argument, reason, etc. is clearly expressed and persuades people to believe it.

words.ex: The city hosted an exposition last summer.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市去年夏天举办了一场博览会。
words.en: An exposition is a detailed explanation or description of an idea or theory. It can also refer to a large public exhibition of art or trade goods.

words.ex: He wrote an exegesis of the ancient text.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一篇对古文的阐释。
words.en: Exegesis is the explanation and interpretation of a text, especially a religious one.

words.tr: v. 考虑；深思；凝视；思考…的可能性
words.ex: He contemplates quitting his job.
words.ex_cn: 他正在考虑辞去工作。
words.en: If you contemplate an action, you think about whether to do it or not.

words.tr: v. 想出；研究出；设计；发明
words.ex: He excogitate a new plan to fix the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他想出了一个新计划来解决这个问题。
words.en: To think carefully and deeply about something; to ponder or meditate.

words.tr: n. 意识形态；思想体系；
words.ex: His ideology is based on equality and justice.
words.ex_cn: 他的意识形态基于平等与正义。
words.en: An ideology is a set of beliefs, especially one held by a particular group, that influences the way people think and behave.

words.tr: adj. 无思虑的；考虑不周的
words.ex: His incogitant remarks hurt her feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他无心的话语伤了她的感情。
words.en: Lacking thought or consideration; thoughtless.

words.ex: He is introspective and often thinks about his feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他善于内省，经常思考自己的感受。
words.en: If you describe someone as introspective, you mean that they spend a lot of time examining their own thoughts, ideas, and feelings.

words.tr: v. 沉思；冥想；考虑；仔细计划
words.ex: He meditates every morning to feel calm.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上冥想以保持平静。
words.en: To meditate means to spend time in quiet thought for religious purposes or relaxation.

words.ex: He does meditation every morning to relax.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上冥想以放松。
words.en: Meditation is the act of remaining in a silent and calm state for a period of time, as part of a religious training, or so that you are more able to deal with the problems of everyday life.

words.tr:
v. 沉思
n. （作家、画家等的）灵感；缪斯
words.ex: He often muses about the meaning of life.
words.ex_cn: 他常常沉思生命的意义。
words.en: In Greek mythology, the Muses are the goddesses of the inspiration of literature, science and the arts. As a verb, to muse means to think about something carefully and for a long time.

words.ex: He opined that the new policy would benefit the company.
words.ex_cn: 他认为新政策将对公司有利。
words.en: To opine means to express an opinion.

words.ex: He sat by the window to ponder his future.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在窗边深思自己的未来。
words.en: If you ponder something, you think about it carefully.

words.ex: He did not premeditate the crime; it happened in the moment.
words.ex_cn: 他没有预谋犯罪；那是当场发生的。
words.en: If you premeditate an action, especially a crime, you plan it or think about it before you do it.

words.tr: adj. 预谋的；事先策划的； v. “premeditate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The theft was premeditated, not random.
words.ex_cn: 这次盗窃是预谋的，不是随机的。
words.en: If you describe an action as premeditated, you mean that it has been planned or thought about before it is done.

words.tr:
v. 回忆起；召回；
n. 记忆力；
words.ex: I recall my first day at school.
words.ex_cn: 我想起了我上学的第一天。
words.en: If you recall something, you remember it and tell others about it.

words.ex: We sit together and reminisce about old times.
words.ex_cn: 我们坐在一起回忆过去的时光。
words.en: If you reminisce about something from your past, you write or talk about it, often with pleasure.

words.tr: v. 折回；追溯；沿原路返回；追想
words.ex: He retraced his steps to find the lost key.
words.ex_cn: 他折回原路寻找丢失的钥匙。
words.en: To go back over the same path or route that one has just taken.

words.ex: He sits quietly to ruminate on his choices.
words.ex_cn: 他静静地坐着沉思自己的选择。
words.en: To ruminate means to think deeply about something or to chew the cud, as a cow does.

words.ex: He spent the evening in a ruminative mood, pondering the meaning of life.
words.ex_cn: 他整个晚上都在沉思，思考生命的意义。
words.en: If you are ruminative, you are thinking deeply and carefully about something.

words.ex: He speculates that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他推测明天会下雨。
words.en: If you speculate about something, you make guesses about its nature or identity, or about what might happen.

words.tr: adj. 推测的；推理的；思索的；投机的
words.ex: He made a speculative guess about the weather.
words.ex_cn: 他对天气做了一个推测性的猜测。
words.en: Based on conjecture rather than knowledge; involving a high risk of loss.

words.tr: adj. 非预谋的；非事先策划的
words.ex: The response was completely unpremeditated.
words.ex_cn: 这个回答完全是即兴的。
words.en: Not planned or thought out in advance; spontaneous.

words.tr: adj. 回顾的；回想的；溯及既往的
words.ex: He made a retrospective look at his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他回顾了自己的童年。
words.en: A retrospective is an exhibition or compilation showing the development of an artist's work over a period of time. It can also refer to a look back at past events or situations.

words.ex: He felt a warm reminiscence of his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他感受到了对童年的温馨回忆。
words.en: The act or process of recalling past experiences, events, etc.

words.tr:
n. 顾虑；顾忌；踌躇
v. 顾虑；有顾忌
words.ex: He had a scruple about lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他对于对朋友撒谎感到不安。
words.en: A scruple is a feeling of doubt or hesitation with regard to the morality or propriety of a course of action.

words.ex: He is doing cerebration to solve the math problem.
words.ex_cn: 他正在动脑筋解决这道数学题。
words.en: The process of thinking or mental activity.

words.ex: He contravenes the school rules by using his phone in class.
words.ex_cn: 他上课使用手机，违反了校规。
words.en: To contravene a law or rule means to do something that is forbidden by it.

words.ex: He infringes the rules by arriving late.
words.ex_cn: 他因迟到而违反了规则。
words.en: To infringe means to violate or break a law, agreement, or right.

words.ex: He was punished for transgressing the law.
words.ex_cn: 他因违法而受到惩罚。
words.en: To transgress means to go beyond the limits of what is morally, socially, or legally acceptable.

words.tr: adj. 产生相反效果的；适得其反的；事与愿违的；
words.ex: Yelling at him is counterproductive.
words.ex_cn: 对他大喊大叫会产生相反的效果。
words.en: Something that is counterproductive achieves the opposite result from the one that you want to achieve.

words.tr: v. 听取（执行任务的）情况汇报
words.ex: The officer was debriefed after returning from the mission.
words.ex_cn: 这名军官在任务返回后接受了盘问。
words.en: To question someone in order to obtain information, especially after a mission or task.

words.ex: The teacher gave me feedback on my essay.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了我关于我作文的反馈。
words.en: Feedback is comments in the form of opinions about and reactions to something, intended to provide useful information for future decisions and development.

words.ex: The police opened an inquiry into the accident.
words.ex_cn: 警方对这起事故展开了调查。
words.en: An inquiry is a question which you ask in order to get some information.

words.ex: The police will interrogate the suspect tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 警察明天会审问嫌疑人。
words.en: To interrogate someone means to ask them a lot of questions for a long time in order to get information, sometimes using threats.

words.tr:
n. 窥探；杠杆；爱打探的人
v. 打听；窥探；用杠杆撬开
words.ex: His pry into my private messages made me angry.
words.ex_cn: 他窥探我的私信让我很生气。
words.en: To try to find out private information about someone or something in a way that is annoying or rude.

words.tr:
n. 询问；疑问；问号
v. 询问；怀疑
words.ex: He made a query about the bus schedule.
words.ex_cn: 他询问了公交车的时刻表。
words.en: A query is a question, especially one that you ask in order to check that something is true or correct.

words.ex: He rejoin the team after his injury healed.
words.ex_cn: 他伤愈后重新加入了队伍。
words.en: To become a member of a group again after leaving it; to reply to a remark or accusation.

words.ex: He gave a quick rejoinder to her question.
words.ex_cn: 他对她的问题迅速做出了回应。
words.en: A rejoinder is a reply, especially a quick or witty one, to a question or remark.

words.tr: n. 敏捷的回答；机智的回答
words.ex: The witty repartee between the two comedians kept the audience laughing.
words.ex_cn: 两位喜剧演员之间的机智对话让观众笑声不断。
words.en: A repartee is a quick, witty reply or a conversation full of such replies.

words.tr: adj. 角的；有角的；尖角的；
words.ex: The angular shape of the triangle is clear.
words.ex_cn: 三角形的角形很清晰。
words.en: having angles or sharp corners; lean and bony

words.ex: The responsiveness of the touchscreen is very good.
words.ex_cn: 这个触摸屏的敏感性很好。
words.en: The quality of reacting quickly and positively.

words.ex: The priest used the catechism to teach the children about the faith.
words.ex_cn: 牧师使用教义问答书来教导孩子们关于信仰的知识。
words.en: A catechism is a summary of the principles of Christian religion in the form of questions and answers, used for the instruction of Christians.

words.ex: The sponge absorbs water quickly.
words.ex_cn: 海绵很快吸收水。
words.en: If something absorbs a liquid, gas, or other substance, it soaks it up or takes it in.

words.ex: I saw an advert on TV for new shoes.
words.ex_cn: 我在电视上看到一双新鞋的广告。
words.en: An advert is a notice or announcement in a public medium promoting a product, service, or event.

words.tr:
adj. 迷人的；令人沉醉的
v. 施魔法于；蛊惑；“bewitch”的现在分词
words.ex: She had a bewitching smile that could light up any room.
words.ex_cn: 她有一个迷人的微笑，能让任何房间都亮起来。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as bewitching, you mean they are so attractive or interesting that they seem to have a magical effect on you.

words.tr: n. 注意的焦点； 引人注目的事物；北极星
words.ex: The new museum became the cynosure of all eyes in the city.
words.ex_cn: 这座新博物馆成为全城瞩目的焦点。
words.en: A cynosure is someone or something that is the center of attention or admiration.

words.tr: adj. 值得拥有的；令人渴望的；称心如意的；
words.ex: A quiet neighborhood is desirable for families.
words.ex_cn: 安静的社区对家庭来说是值得拥有的。
words.en: Something that is desirable is worth having or doing because it is useful, necessary, or popular.

words.tr: v. 使着迷；使陶醉；对…施魔法
words.ex: The magic show enchants the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演让孩子们着迷。
words.en: If you are enchanted by someone or something, they cause you to have feelings of great delight or pleasure.

words.ex: The shop tries to entice customers with cheap prices.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店试图以低价吸引顾客。
words.en: If you entice someone, you attract them to a particular place or activity by making it seem attractive or interesting.

words.ex: The entrance to the building is on the left.
words.ex_cn: 这座建筑的入口在左边。
words.en: An entrance is a way into a place, such as a door or gate. It can also refer to the act of entering a place or the right to enter.

words.ex: The music was so entrancing that we lost track of time.
words.ex_cn: 音乐如此迷人，以至于我们忘记了时间。
words.en: If you describe something as entrancing, you mean that it is very beautiful or charming and holds your attention completely.

words.ex: The dog fetches the ball every time I throw it.
words.ex_cn: 每次我扔出球，狗都会把它拿来。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as fetching, you think that they are very attractive.

words.tr: adj. 扣人心弦的； v. “grip”的现在分词；
words.ex: The movie had a gripping plot that kept me awake all night.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影情节扣人心弦，让我整晚都没睡。
words.en: If something is gripping, it holds your interest or attention because it is exciting or intense.

words.tr:
v. 注意；留心
n. 注意；留心
words.ex: He did not heed the warning.
words.ex_cn: 他没有理会那个警告。
words.en: If you heed someone's advice or warning, you pay attention to it and do what they suggest.

words.ex: The ad induced him to buy the product.
words.ex_cn: 这则广告诱使他购买了该产品。
words.en: To induce a state or condition means to cause it.

words.tr:
adj. 热恋着的；冲昏头脑的；入迷的
v. 使冲昏头脑；使着迷；“infatuate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: She was infatuated with the new pop star.
words.ex_cn: 她对这位新晋流行歌手非常着迷。
words.en: If you are infatuated with someone, you have a very strong feeling of love or attraction for them, which usually does not last very long.

words.ex: He is the liaison between the two departments.
words.ex_cn: 他是两个部门之间的联络人。
words.en: A liaison is a person who acts as a link to assist communication between different groups or organizations.

words.tr:
v. 吸引；诱惑；引诱
n. 诱惑；诱饵；吸引力
words.ex: The bright colors lure the birds to the feeder.
words.ex_cn: 鲜艳的颜色吸引鸟类来到喂食器。
words.en: If you lure someone, you tempt them to do something or to go somewhere, especially by offering some form of reward.

words.tr:
n. 柩衣；棺罩；帷幕；遮盖物
v. 使人厌倦；变得枯躁无味
words.ex: The pall of smoke from the factory hung over the town.
words.ex_cn: 工厂的烟幕笼罩着整个城镇。
words.en: A pall is a dark cloud of smoke, dust, or similar, or a feeling of fear, sadness, or depression.

words.tr:
adj. 令人销魂的；极其迷人的
v. 强奸；抢夺；使着迷；“ravish”的现在分词
words.ex: The sunset was so ravishing that it took everyone's breath away.
words.ex_cn: 日落美得令人陶醉，让人叹为观止。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as ravishing, you mean that they are extremely beautiful or attractive.

words.ex: The magic show riveted the children's attention.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演吸引了孩子们的注意力。
words.en: A rivet is a short metal pin or bolt for holding together two plates of metal, its headless end being beaten out or pressed down when in place. As a verb, to rivet means to attract and hold the attention of someone completely.

words.tr:
adj. 吸引人的；引人入胜的
v. （用铆钉）固定；吸引住；“rivet”的现在分词
words.ex: The movie was riveting from start to finish.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影从头到尾都扣人心弦。
words.en: If you describe something as riveting, you mean that it is extremely interesting and exciting, and that it holds your attention completely.

words.ex: The sunset was spectacular.
words.ex_cn: 日落非常壮观。
words.en: Something that is spectacular is very impressive or dramatic.

words.tr: adj. 不讨人喜欢的；不吸引人的；
words.ex: He has an unprepossessing appearance, but he is very kind.
words.ex_cn: 他外表不讨人喜欢，但他非常善良。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as unprepossessing, you mean that they look rather plain or ordinary, and not at all impressive or attractive.

words.tr: v. 邀请；“invite”的现在分词； adj. 诱人的；吸引人的；
words.ex: He is inviting his friends to dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他正在邀请他的朋友来吃晚饭。
words.en: If you describe something as inviting, you mean that it has good qualities that attract you or make you want to experience it.

words.tr:
adj. 撩拨人的；让人非常着急的
v. （以可望而不可即之物）逗引；使干着急；“tantalize”的现在分词
words.ex: The smell of fresh bread was tantalizing.
words.ex_cn: 新鲜面包的香味令人垂涎。
words.en: If you describe something as tantalizing, you mean that it is very attractive, interesting, or desirable.

words.ex: He accepted the job because of the financial inducement.
words.ex_cn: 他因为经济诱因接受了这份工作。
words.en: Something that is offered to someone to persuade them to do something.

words.tr: v. （以可望而不可及之物）逗引；使干着急
words.ex: The smell of cookies tantalize him.
words.ex_cn: 饼干的香味让他垂涎欲滴。
words.en: If someone or something tantalizes you, they make you feel hopeful and excited about getting what you want, usually before disappointing you by not letting you have it.

words.ex: The allure of money made him take the risky job.
words.ex_cn: 金钱的诱惑让他接受了这份高风险的工作。
words.en: The quality of being powerfully and mysteriously attractive or fascinating.

words.ex: She confides in her best friend.
words.ex_cn: 她向最好的朋友倾诉。
words.en: If you confide in someone, you tell them a secret.

words.ex: He tried to convince her to stay.
words.ex_cn: 他试图说服她留下。
words.en: If someone or something convinces you of something, they make you believe that it is true or that it exists.

words.ex: The witness gave credence to the story by crying.
words.ex_cn: 证人通过哭泣使这个故事显得可信。
words.en: Credence is a belief in or acceptance of something as true.

words.ex: The movie was incredible.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影太棒了。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as incredible, you like them very much or are impressed by them, because they are extremely or unusually good.

words.tr:
n. 信用；赊账；赞扬；贷款；荣誉；
v. 相信；
words.ex: He has good credit with the bank.
words.ex_cn: 他在银行有良好的信用。
words.en: If you are allowed credit, you are allowed to pay for goods or services several weeks or months after you have received them.

words.ex: His credo is to always tell the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他的信条是永远说真话。
words.en: A credo is a set of beliefs, principles, or opinions that strongly influence the way a person lives or works.

words.ex: He is credulous and believes every story he hears.
words.ex_cn: 他很轻信，相信他听到的每一个故事。
words.en: If you describe someone as credulous, you have a low opinion of them because they are too ready to believe what people tell them and are easily deceived.

words.ex: The church teaches its doctrine to all members.
words.ex_cn: 教会向所有成员传授它的教义。
words.en: A doctrine is a set of beliefs or principles that are taught or accepted by a particular group, especially in religion or politics.

words.ex: He refuses to accept the dogma of the church.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝接受教会的教条。
words.en: A principle or set of principles laid down by an authority as incontrovertibly true.

words.ex: The concert was fabulous!
words.ex_cn: 这场音乐会太棒了！
words.en: If you describe something as fabulous, you are emphasizing that you like it a lot or think that it is very good.

words.tr: adj. 难以置信的；不像真实的；
words.ex: It seems implausible that he won the lottery twice.
words.ex_cn: 他中了两次彩票，这似乎难以置信。
words.en: If you describe something as implausible, you believe that it is unlikely to be true.

words.ex: Children have reliance on their parents for food and shelter.
words.ex_cn: 孩子依赖父母提供食物和住所。
words.en: Reliance is the state of depending on or trusting in someone or something.

words.ex: Honesty is the main tenet of his life.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是他生活的宗旨。
words.en: A tenet is a principle or belief, especially one that is part of a larger system of beliefs.

words.ex: He is a trustworthy friend who always keeps his promises.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个值得信赖的朋友，总是信守承诺。
words.en: If you describe someone as trustworthy, you mean they are reliable, honest, and truthful.

words.tr: adv. 不可能地；无法可想地
words.ex: The task was impossibly difficult.
words.ex_cn: 这项任务几乎是不可能完成的。
words.en: In a manner that is not possible or is extremely difficult to believe or achieve.

words.tr: v. 旋转；螺旋形地运转；剧烈起伏
words.ex: The dancer gyrated to the rhythm of the music.
words.ex_cn: 舞者随着音乐的节奏旋转。
words.en: If something or someone gyrates, they move around in a circle, especially very quickly.

words.tr:
n. 枢；中心；旋转
v. 在枢轴上转动；以…为中心
words.ex: The door pivots on a hinge.
words.ex_cn: 门围绕一个铰链旋转。
words.en: A pivot is the central point, pin, or shaft on which a mechanism turns or oscillates. It can also refer to the central or most important person or thing in a situation.

words.ex: He wound the fishing line onto the reel.
words.ex_cn: 他把鱼线绕在卷筒上。
words.en: A reel is a cylinder on which film, wire, thread, or other flexible materials can be wound. It can also refer to a lively Scottish or Irish dance, or to the act of staggering or lurching violently.

words.ex: The wheel rotates slowly.
words.ex_cn: 轮子缓慢地转动。
words.en: To rotate means to turn or cause to turn around an axis or center.

words.ex: The car slued around on the icy road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在结冰的路面上旋转。
words.en: To turn or slide suddenly or violently in a particular direction, especially in an uncontrolled way.

words.tr:
n. 摇摆；
v. 摇摆；
words.ex: The child enjoyed the swing at the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子喜欢在公园里荡秋千。
words.en: If something swings or if you swing it, it moves repeatedly backwards and forwards or from side to side from a fixed point. If you swing somewhere, you move there by holding onto something and moving your body through the air.

words.tr:
n. 摇摆；
v. 摇摆；
words.ex: The child enjoyed the swing at the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子喜欢在公园里荡秋千。
words.en: If something swings or if you swing it, it moves repeatedly backwards and forwards or from side to side from a fixed point. If you swing somewhere, you move there by holding onto something and moving your body through the air.

words.tr:
n. 摇摆；
v. 摇摆；
words.ex: The child enjoyed the swing at the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子喜欢在公园里荡秋千。
words.en: If something swings or if you swing it, it moves repeatedly backwards and forwards or from side to side from a fixed point. If you swing somewhere, you move there by holding onto something and moving your body through the air.

words.ex: She abhors violence.
words.ex_cn: 她憎恶暴力。
words.en: If you abhor something, you hate it very much, especially because you think it is immoral or disgusting.

words.ex: She abominates cruelty to animals.
words.ex_cn: 她痛恨对动物的残忍行为。
words.en: If you abominate something, you hate it very much.

words.tr: adj. 对（享乐）感到厌倦的；（因司空见惯而）无动于衷的
words.ex: He is blase about the new phone because he has one every year.
words.ex_cn: 他对新手机无动于衷，因为他每年都换一部。
words.en: If you describe someone as blasé, you mean that they are not easily impressed, excited, or worried by things, usually because they have seen or experienced them before.

words.ex: The smell was disagreeable.
words.ex_cn: 这气味令人不愉快。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as disagreeable, you mean that they are rather unpleasant.

words.ex: His exceptionable behavior upset the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他令人反感的行为让老师很生气。
words.en: If you describe something as exceptionable, you mean that it is open to objection or criticism.

words.ex: I loathe waking up early.
words.ex_cn: 我讨厌早起。
words.en: If you loathe something or someone, you dislike them very much.

words.ex: The loud music was obnoxious and made everyone leave.
words.ex_cn: 那刺耳的音乐非常讨厌，让所有人都离开了。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as obnoxious, you think that they are very unpleasant because of being aggressive, loud, or offensive.

words.tr: adj. 可憎的；讨厌的；令人作呕的
words.ex: The smell of the garbage was odious.
words.ex_cn: 垃圾的气味令人讨厌。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as odious, you think that they are extremely unpleasant, horrible, or disgusting.

words.tr: adj. 冒犯的；令人不快的；进攻性的；
words.ex: His offensive words made her cry.
words.ex_cn: 他冒犯的话让她哭了。
words.en: If you describe someone's language or behavior as offensive, you mean that it is rude or insulting.

words.tr: adj. 令人讨厌的；令人厌恶的
words.ex: The rebarbative odor made it difficult to concentrate.
words.ex_cn: 那令人讨厌的气味让人难以集中注意力。
words.en: If you describe something as rebarbative, you mean that you find it unattractive and unpleasant.

words.ex: The smell repels insects.
words.ex_cn: 这种气味能击退昆虫。
words.en: If something repels you, it is so unpleasant or offensive that you want to avoid it or push it away.

words.ex: We use a repellent to keep mosquitoes away.
words.ex_cn: 我们使用驱虫剂来驱赶蚊子。
words.en: A repellent is a substance that is used to keep insects or animals away from something. It can also refer to something that is extremely unpleasant or disgusting.

words.tr: adj. 令人厌恶的；讨厌的；抵触的
words.ex: The smell was repugnant.
words.ex_cn: 那气味令人厌恶。
words.en: If you think that something is horrible and disgusting, you can say that it is repugnant.

words.tr:
adj. 过度满足的
v. 充分满足；使饱享；“sate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: She felt sated after the large meal.
words.ex_cn: 她在大餐后感到饱足。
words.en: If you are sated with something, you have had more than enough of it and do not want any more.

words.tr: adj. 不合意的；不想要的；
words.ex: The weather is undesirable for a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 这种天气不适合野餐。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as undesirable, you think they will have harmful effects or cause problems.

words.ex: His behavior scandalized the community.
words.ex_cn: 他的行为让社区感到震惊。
words.en: To scandalize someone means to shock or outrage them by something considered immoral or improper.

words.tr: adj. 味道不佳的；令人讨厌的；声名狼藉的；不道德的
words.ex: The fish had an unsavory smell.
words.ex_cn: 这条鱼有一种难闻的气味。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as unsavory, you mean that they are unpleasant or morally unacceptable.

words.tr: adj. 讨厌的；可恶的；令人憎恶的
words.ex: The smell of the rotten food was loathsome.
words.ex_cn: 腐烂食物的气味令人作呕。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as loathsome, you are indicating that they are extremely unpleasant and disgusting.

words.tr: n. 对抗；对立；敌对状态（行为）
words.ex: There is antagonism between the two neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 这两个邻居之间有敌意。
words.en: Antagonism is a strong feeling of dislike or opposition towards someone or something.

words.ex: He felt antipathy toward the loud neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对那个吵闹的邻居感到反感。
words.en: A deep-seated feeling of dislike; aversion.

words.ex: He has a disinclination to speak in public.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意在公众场合讲话。
words.en: A disinclination to do something is a feeling of not wanting to do it.

words.tr: n. 所愿望之物；迫切需要之物
words.ex: A clean environment is the desideratum for a healthy society.
words.ex_cn: 清洁的环境是健康社会的迫切需要之物。
words.en: Something that is needed or wanted.

words.ex: Running a business entails hard work.
words.ex_cn: 经营企业必然需要努力工作。
words.en: If one thing entails another, it involves it or causes it.

words.tr:
adj. 极重要的；
n. 紧急的事；
words.ex: It is imperative to drink water every day.
words.ex_cn: 每天喝水非常重要。
words.en: If it is imperative that something is done, that thing is extremely important and must be done.

words.ex: You need basic math as a prerequisite for this course.
words.ex_cn: 你学习这门课程的前提是掌握基础数学。
words.en: A prerequisite is something that must exist or happen before something else can exist or happen.

words.tr: adj. 紧迫的； v. 按；“press”的现在分词；
words.ex: The pressing issue is finding clean water.
words.ex_cn: 紧迫的问题是找到干净的水。
words.en: If something is pressing, it needs to be dealt with immediately because it is important or urgent.

words.ex: The procrustean approach to education enforces a standardized curriculum.
words.ex_cn: 这种强求一致的教育方式强制推行标准化课程。
words.en: If you describe something as procrustean, you mean that it is based on the idea that everyone or everything must be made to fit a particular standard, even if this means ignoring individual differences or needs.

words.tr:
n. 请求；要求的事；
v. 要求；请求；
words.ex: He made a request for help.
words.ex_cn: 他提出了一个帮助的请求。
words.en: If you request something, you ask for it politely or formally.

words.tr: adj. 必需的；必备的；必不可少的；
words.ex: A passport is a requisite for international travel.
words.ex_cn: 护照是国际旅行所必需的。
words.en: Something that is necessary for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The contract stipulates that payments must be made monthly.
words.ex_cn: 合同规定付款必须按月进行。
words.en: If you stipulate a condition or stipulate that something must be done, you say clearly that it must be done.

words.tr: adj. 再三要求的；纠缠不休的
words.ex: He was importunate in asking for money.
words.ex_cn: 他不停地要求给钱。
words.en: persistent to the point of annoyance

words.tr:
n. 露营；野营
v. 野营；临时露营
words.ex: The soldiers set up a bivouac for the night.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们为过夜搭建了露营地。
words.en: A bivouac is a temporary camp or shelter, often used by soldiers or mountaineers, that does not use tents or other structures.

words.tr:
n. 营地；
v. 宿营；露营；
words.ex: The children set up a camp near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在湖边搭了一个营地。
words.en: A camp is a place where people live temporarily in tents or other temporary structures.

words.ex: The cat creeps slowly toward the bird.
words.ex_cn: 猫蹑手蹑脚地向鸟靠近。
words.en: To move slowly and quietly, especially in a way that does not attract attention.

words.tr: v. 取代；迫使…离开家园；
words.ex: The new robot will displace the workers on the assembly line.
words.ex_cn: 这个新机器人将取代装配线上的工人。
words.en: To displace something or someone means to take their place or to force them to leave their usual place or role.

words.ex: He wants to emigrate to Canada for a better life.
words.ex_cn: 他想移民到加拿大过更好的生活。
words.en: To leave one's own country in order to settle permanently in another.

words.ex: The book is 10 inches long.
words.ex_cn: 这本书长10英寸。
words.en: An inch is a unit of length equal to one twelfth of a foot.

words.ex: The child learns locomotion by crawling.
words.ex_cn: 孩子通过爬行学习移动。
words.en: The ability to move from place to place.

words.ex: The locomotive pulled the train down the track.
words.ex_cn: 机车拉着火车沿着轨道行驶。
words.en: A locomotive is a powered rail vehicle used for pulling trains.

words.ex: Birds are migratory in winter.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类在冬天是迁徙的。
words.en: Relating to or characterized by migration; tending to migrate.

words.ex: The mobile table can be moved easily.
words.ex_cn: 这个可移动的桌子很容易搬动。
words.en: A mobile is something that can move or be moved easily.

words.tr: adj. 能动的；有自动力的
words.ex: The sperm cells are highly motile and can swim towards the egg.
words.ex_cn: 精子细胞非常活跃，能够游向卵子。
words.en: A motile organism is capable of moving independently, using metabolic energy.

words.ex: The procession moved slowly down the street.
words.ex_cn: 行列缓缓沿着街道行进。
words.en: A procession is a group of people who are walking, riding, or driving in a line as part of a public event.

words.ex: Please remove the trash from the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 请把厨房的垃圾去掉。
words.en: To take something or someone away from a place or off a surface.

words.tr: n. 往返移动之物；航天飞机；
words.ex: The bus is a shuttle between the hotel and the airport.
words.ex_cn: 这辆巴士是酒店和机场之间的往返交通工具。
words.en: A shuttle is a vehicle that travels frequently between two places. In weaving, a shuttle is a device used to carry the weft thread back and forth across the loom.

words.ex: The snake slithered through the grass.
words.ex_cn: 蛇在草丛中滑行。
words.en: To move smoothly and quietly with a twisting or oscillating motion, like a snake.

words.ex: The hospital performed a kidney transplantation last week.
words.ex_cn: 医院上周进行了肾脏移植手术。
words.en: The act or process of moving an organ, tissue, or living thing from one place or person to another.

words.tr: v. 使掉换顺序；使转移；使换位
words.ex: You need to transpose the elements to solve the equation.
words.ex_cn: 你需要调换元素来解这个方程。
words.en: To transpose something means to change its order, position, or nature, especially in mathematics or music.

words.tr:
n. 滨螺；玉黍螺
v. 挑出；剔出；设法搞到；逐出
words.ex: He found a winkle on the rocky beach.
words.ex_cn: 他在岩石海滩上发现了一只滨螺。
words.en: To winkle means to move slowly or with difficulty, or to extract information from someone with difficulty. As a noun, it refers to a small edible sea snail.

words.tr:
n. 马笼头；缰绳；约束
v. 套笼头；表示恼怒；抑制
words.ex: He pulled the bridle to stop the horse.
words.ex_cn: 他拉了一下缰绳让马停下来。
words.en: A bridle is a set of straps that fits around a horse's head and is used to control the horse. As a verb, to bridle means to put a bridle on a horse or to restrain or control something.

words.ex: The box contains five apples.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子包含五个苹果。
words.en: If something such as a box, bag, room, or place contains things, those things are inside it.

words.ex: The containment of the fire took three hours.
words.ex_cn: 控制火势花了三个小时。
words.en: The act of keeping something harmful under control or within limits.

words.ex: The price of the phone is prohibitive for most students.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机的价格对大多数学生来说太贵了。
words.en: If the cost of something is prohibitive, it is so high that it prevents people from buying it or doing it.

words.tr:
n. 经常重复的评价（或抱怨）；叠句；
v. 克制；
words.ex: His constant refrain is that the food is too expensive.
words.ex_cn: 他经常抱怨食物太贵。
words.en: If you refrain from doing something, you deliberately do not do it.

words.ex: He tries to restrain his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他努力克制自己的愤怒。
words.en: If you restrain someone, you stop them from doing what they intended or wanted to do, usually by using your physical strength.

words.ex: He showed restraint when he stayed calm during the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持冷静，表现出了克制。
words.en: Restraint is a measure or condition that keeps someone or something under control or within limits.

words.ex: The smoke began to stifle her breathing.
words.ex_cn: 烟雾开始让她窒息。
words.en: To stifle something means to prevent it from happening, continuing, or developing.

words.tr:
n. 埋伏；伏击
v. 埋伏；伏击
words.ex: The soldiers set an ambush at night.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在夜间设下埋伏。
words.en: An ambush is a surprise attack by people lying in wait in a concealed position.

words.tr:
n. 藏物处；隐藏物；
v. 匿藏；
words.ex: The hunters found a cache of food under the rocks.
words.ex_cn: 猎人们在石头下发现了一个食物藏匿处。
words.en: A cache is a hidden store of things such as weapons or a supply of food.

words.ex: He tried to conceal the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图隐藏真相。
words.en: If you conceal something, you prevent it from being seen or known about.

words.ex: He dissembles when he is nervous.
words.ex_cn: 当他紧张时，他会假装。
words.en: To dissemble means to conceal one's true motives, feelings, or beliefs.

words.ex: He dissimulated his anger to keep the peace.
words.ex_cn: 他掩饰了自己的愤怒以维持和平。
words.en: To dissimulate means to hide your real feelings, character, or intentions.

words.ex: The soldier lay doggo in the bushes.
words.ex_cn: 士兵趴在灌木丛中隐蔽不动。
words.en: A term of endearment or informal reference to a dog.

words.tr: v. 厚厚地覆盖；使…窒息；闷死
words.ex: He tried to smother the fire with a blanket.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用毯子把火闷灭。
words.en: To smother someone or something means to kill them by covering their face so that they cannot breathe, or to put out a fire by covering it.

words.tr: adj. 独自的；单独的；孤寂的；
words.ex: He lives in a solitary house far from the town.
words.ex_cn: 他住在离城镇很远的独自一人的房子里。
words.en: A solitary person or thing is the only one in a place.

words.tr:
n. 茎；柄；梗
v. 跟踪；偷偷接近；昂首阔步地走
words.ex: The stalk of the sunflower is very tall.
words.ex_cn: 向日葵的茎很高。
words.en: The main stem of a plant, typically rising above ground but occasionally subterranean. Also, to pursue or approach stealthily.

words.tr: adj. 私下参与的；私下的；秘密的
words.ex: He is privy to the secret plan.
words.ex_cn: 他知道这个秘密计划。
words.en: If you are privy to something secret, you have been allowed to know about it.

words.tr:
adj. 僻静的；隐僻的； 退隐的
v. 隔离；隔绝；隐居；“seclude”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The cabin is secluded in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 小木屋坐落在树林中，十分僻静。
words.en: A secluded place is quiet, private, and not near people or things that disturb you.

words.ex: She led a reclusive life in the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 她在山中过着隐居的生活。
words.en: If you describe someone as reclusive, you mean that they live alone and do not like seeing or talking to other people.

words.tr: adj. （适用于）步行的；非固定的；可移动的；流动的
words.ex: The hospital has an ambulatory care unit for patients needing less intensive treatment.
words.ex_cn: 这家医院设有一个流动护理单元，供需要较少密集治疗的患者使用。
words.en: Relating to or adapted for walking; able to walk about and not bedridden.

words.tr: n. 航班；飞行；（阶梯的）一段；
words.ex: The flight to Beijing leaves at 8 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 飞往北京的航班早上8点起飞。
words.en: A flight is a journey made by flying, usually in an aircraft.

words.ex: The old man walked with a slow gait.
words.ex_cn: 老人走路步伐缓慢。
words.en: A person's manner of walking.

words.ex: The bird glide smoothly over the lake.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在湖面上滑行。
words.en: To move smoothly and continuously along, as if without effort or resistance.

words.ex: He jogs every morning to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上慢跑以保持健康。
words.en: To run at a slow, steady pace, especially as a form of exercise.

words.ex: The sudden jolt woke me up.
words.ex_cn: 突然的震动把我惊醒了。
words.en: If something jolts or if something jolts it, it moves suddenly and quite violently.

words.ex: The kinetic energy of the moving ball is high.
words.ex_cn: 运动的球的动能很高。
words.en: Relating to or resulting from motion.

words.ex: The bacteria show high motility in warm water.
words.ex_cn: 这种细菌在温水中具有很高的运动能力。
words.en: The ability of an organism or fluid to move or be moved.

words.ex: The apple plummeted from the tree.
words.ex_cn: 苹果从树上垂直落下。
words.en: If an amount, rate, or price plummets, it decreases quickly by a large amount.

words.tr: v. 腾跃；阔步行走；神气地快速走动
words.ex: The horse prances across the field.
words.ex_cn: 那匹马在田野上欢快地跳跃。
words.en: If a horse prances, it moves with high, springy steps.

words.ex: The light pulsates slowly in the dark.
words.ex_cn: 灯在黑暗中缓慢地脉动。
words.en: If something pulsates, it beats, moves in and out, or shakes with strong, regular movements.

words.ex: The doctor checked his pulse with his fingers.
words.ex_cn: 医生用手指检查了他的脉搏。
words.en: A pulse is the regular beating of the heart, especially when it is felt at the wrist or neck. It can also refer to a single vibration or short burst of sound, electric current, light, etc.

words.tr:
v. 拖足而行；（使）磨损
n. 拖着脚走；磨损
words.ex: He scuffed his shoes on the pavement.
words.ex_cn: 他在人行道上拖着脚走，把鞋子磨坏了。
words.en: To scuff means to drag your feet along the ground as you walk, or to make a mark or scratch on the surface of something by rubbing it against something rough.

words.ex: The rope caused slippage on the wet surface.
words.ex_cn: 绳子在湿滑的表面上发生了滑动。
words.en: Slippage refers to the act or process of slipping or the amount by which something slips.

words.tr:
n. 猛跌；衰退；萧条期
v. 急剧下降；暴跌；重重地坐下（或倒下）
words.ex: The company's sales went into a slump last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月，这家公司的销售额下滑了。
words.en: If something such as the value of something slumps, it falls suddenly and by a large amount.

words.ex: The price of oil soared last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月石油价格骤升。
words.en: To rise or increase dramatically in amount or level.

words.tr:
v. 大步行走；跨一大步
n. 大步；步伐
words.ex: He takes a long stride when he walks.
words.ex_cn: 他走路时迈着大步。
words.en: To walk with long, decisive steps in a specified direction.

words.tr:
v. 神气十足地走；大摇大摆地走
n. 大摇大摆；神气十足
words.ex: He walks with swagger down the street.
words.ex_cn: 他大摇大摆地走在街上。
words.en: If someone swaggers, they walk in a very proud and confident way, often in a way that annoys other people.

words.ex: The drummer changed the tempo of the song.
words.ex_cn: 鼓手改变了这首歌的拍子。
words.en: The speed at which a piece of music is played or the rate or speed of motion or activity.

words.ex: They traverse the forest to reach the village.
words.ex_cn: 他们横穿森林去到达村庄。
words.en: To traverse something means to move or travel across it, often with some difficulty.

words.tr:
v. 踩；踏；践踏
n. 脚步声；胎面
words.ex: He tread carefully on the icy path.
words.ex_cn: 他小心地走在结冰的小路上。
words.en: If you tread on something, you put your foot on it when you are walking. The tread of a tyre is the pattern of lines on its surface that prevent it from slipping.

words.tr:
v. 摇摇摆摆地走；蹒跚
n. 摇摆的步子；蹒跚而行
words.ex: The duck waddle across the pond.
words.ex_cn: 鸭子摇摆着走过池塘。
words.en: To walk with short steps, swaying from side to side, like a duck.

words.tr: n. 体育运动；田径运动；竞技；
words.ex: He loves athletics and runs every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他热爱体育运动，每天早上跑步。
words.en: Athletics refers to sports in general, especially those that involve physical strength, speed, or endurance, such as running, jumping, and throwing.

words.ex: The horse canter around the field.
words.ex_cn: 马在田野里慢跑。
words.en: If a horse canters, it moves at a speed that is slower than a gallop but faster than a trot.

words.ex: He worked hard to accomplish his goal.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以实现自己的目标。
words.en: To accomplish something means to succeed in doing it, especially after a lot of effort.

words.ex: His attainment of the goal took many years.
words.ex_cn: 他达到这个目标花了多年时间。
words.en: The act of achieving something, especially through effort; a skill or accomplishment that has been achieved.

words.ex: Climbing the mountain without oxygen was a great feat.
words.ex_cn: 在不吸氧的情况下爬山是一项伟大的壮举。
words.en: A feat is an act or achievement that shows great courage, skill, or strength.

words.ex: The soil has been treated to fructify the plants.
words.ex_cn: 土壤经过处理，使植物多结果实。
words.en: To fructify means to make something fruitful or productive, especially in a literal sense such as causing plants to bear fruit, or in a figurative sense such as making an idea or project successful.

words.ex: The language barrier was insuperable for him.
words.ex_cn: 语言障碍对他来说是难以克服的。
words.en: If you describe a problem or obstacle as insuperable, you mean that it is impossible to overcome.

words.ex: The general managed to outmaneuver the enemy forces.
words.ex_cn: 这位将军设法用计谋胜过了敌军。
words.en: To outmaneuver someone means to use clever tactics to gain an advantage over them, especially in a military context or in any kind of strategic competition.

words.tr: adj. 占优势的；主要的；压倒性的
words.ex: The preponderant influence of the older generation is still evident.
words.ex_cn: 老一代的占优势的影响仍然明显。
words.en: If something is preponderant, it is more important, powerful, or numerous than other things in a particular situation.

words.ex: The advantages of the new system preponderate over its disadvantages.
words.ex_cn: 新系统的优势超过了它的劣势。
words.en: To be greater in number, influence, or importance than something else.

words.ex: He surmounted his fears to speak in public.
words.ex_cn: 他克服了恐惧，在公众面前发言。
words.en: If you surmount a problem or difficulty, you deal successfully with it.

words.ex: She transcended her fears to speak on stage.
words.ex_cn: 她超越了自己的恐惧，在舞台上发言。
words.en: If something transcends normal limits or boundaries, it goes beyond them, because it is more significant than them.

words.tr: n. 胜利；赢得（物）； adj. 获胜的；赢的； v. 赢；获得；“win”的现在分词；
words.ex: Her winning was celebrated by the whole team.
words.ex_cn: 她的胜利得到了全队的庆祝。
words.en: A winning person or thing is one that wins or has won something, such as a competition, game, or election.

words.ex: He used a roller to flatten the dirt.
words.ex_cn: 他用滚筒把泥土压平。
words.en: To flatten something means to make it flat or flatter, or to knock it down to the ground.

words.tr: v. 粉碎；磨成粉；彻底击败；摧毁
words.ex: The machine will pulverize the rocks into dust.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器会把岩石碾成粉末。
words.en: To pulverize something means to crush it into a fine powder or to defeat someone or something completely.

words.tr:
v. 斗嘴；闪烁
n. 口角
words.ex: They bicker over small things every day.
words.ex_cn: 他们每天为小事争吵。
words.en: If people bicker, they argue or quarrel about unimportant things.

words.ex: The brawl started over a simple misunderstanding.
words.ex_cn: 这场争吵源于一个简单的误解。
words.en: A brawl is a rough or noisy fight or quarrel.

words.ex: They had a discord about the movie ending.
words.ex_cn: 他们对电影的结局有分歧。
words.en: Disagreement or strife between people or groups.

words.tr:
v. （使）磨损；（使）烦躁；（使）紧张
n. 磨损处；吵闹；争吵
words.ex: The rope began to fray after years of use.
words.ex_cn: 这根绳子用了多年后开始磨损。
words.en: If something such as cloth or rope frays, or if something frays it, its threads or fibres start to come apart from each other and it becomes weaker. A situation of conflict or intense competition can also be referred to as a fray.

words.tr:
v. （使）生气
n. 发脾气；微怒
words.ex: She got a miff when I forgot her birthday.
words.ex_cn: 我忘记了她的生日，她有点恼火。
words.en: To cause to be annoyed or offended.

words.ex: His article was a polemic against government corruption.
words.ex_cn: 他的文章是对政府腐败的抨击。
words.en: A polemic is a very strong written or spoken attack on, or defence of, a particular belief or opinion.

words.tr: adj. 好战的；好斗的；爱滋事的
words.ex: He is pugnacious and always argues with his classmates.
words.ex_cn: 他好斗，总是和同学争吵。
words.en: Someone who is pugnacious is eager to argue or fight.

words.tr:
n. 小规模战斗；小争斗；小冲突
v. 进行一场小冲突
words.ex: The two boys had a small skirmish over the ball.
words.ex_cn: 两个男孩为了球发生了一场小冲突。
words.en: A skirmish is a minor battle or fight, often one that is part of a larger conflict.

words.tr:
n. 争吵
v. 争吵
words.ex: The two boys squabble over toys every day.
words.ex_cn: 这两个男孩每天为玩具争吵。
words.en: A squabble is a noisy disagreement about something unimportant.

words.ex: They had a tiff over the last piece of cake.
words.ex_cn: 他们为了最后一块蛋糕拌了几句嘴。
words.en: A tiff is a small unimportant quarrel, especially between two people who are usually friends or who are married to each other.

words.tr:
v. 争论；争执；吵架
n. 争吵；口角
words.ex: They wrangle over the price every day.
words.ex_cn: 他们每天为价格争执。
words.en: If you wrangle with someone, you argue with them in a noisy or angry way.

words.tr:
n. 轻拳出击；争论
v. 轻拳出击；拌嘴；“spar”的现在分词
words.ex: They engaged in some light sparring during the training session.
words.ex_cn: 他们在训练期间进行了一些轻度的对打。
words.en: Sparring refers to the practice of fighting with an opponent in a controlled way, especially in boxing, or to argue with someone in a friendly or competitive way.

words.ex: There is strife between the two neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 这两个邻居之间有争执。
words.en: Strife is angry or violent conflict between two people or groups.

words.tr: adj. 爱争吵的；好争论的
words.ex: He was a quarrelsome man who always started arguments.
words.ex_cn: 他是个爱争吵的人，总是挑起争论。
words.en: If you describe someone as quarrelsome, you mean that they are bad-tempered and often become involved in arguments.

words.tr:
adj. 吵闹的；粗暴的
n. 凶暴的人；无赖
words.ex: The rowdy kids made noise in the library.
words.ex_cn: 那些吵闹的孩子在图书馆里制造噪音。
words.en: If you describe someone as rowdy, you mean that they are noisy, rough, and likely to cause trouble.

words.ex: They had an altercation over the parking space.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为停车空间发生了争吵。
words.en: An altercation is a noisy argument or disagreement, especially in public.

words.tr: adj. 展开争论的；爱争论的
words.ex: He was known for his disputatious nature in the office.
words.ex_cn: 他在办公室里以爱争辩的性格而闻名。
words.en: A disputatious person is someone who likes to argue or disagree with others.

words.tr:
adj. 交战的；寻衅的；好战的
n. 交战国；交战团体
words.ex: The two belligerent nations signed a peace treaty.
words.ex_cn: 这两个交战国家签署了和平条约。
words.en: A belligerent person or country is aggressive and eager to fight.

words.ex: He apologizes for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他因为迟到而道歉。
words.en: To express regret for something that one has done wrong.

words.ex: There was a contention between the two students about the answer.
words.ex_cn: 两个学生对答案发生了争论。
words.en: A contention is a strong disagreement or argument about something. It can also refer to a point or statement that someone argues is true.

words.tr: adj. 好争吵的；有争议的
words.ex: The plan is contentious because many people disagree.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划有争议，因为很多人不同意。
words.en: If you describe something as contentious, you mean that it is the subject of intense argument and disagreement.

words.ex: The movie is controversial because it shows violence.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影因为展示暴力而有争议。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as controversial, you mean that they are the subject of intense public argument, disagreement, or disapproval.

words.tr:
v. 辩论；争论
n. 辩论；争论
words.ex: The students had a debate about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学生们就作业进行了一场辩论。
words.en: A debate is a discussion about a subject on which people have different views.

words.tr:
n. 纠纷；争端；
v. 对（某事）有异议；
words.ex: The dispute between the two neighbors was about the fence.
words.ex_cn: 两个邻居之间的纠纷是关于篱笆的。
words.en: A dispute is a disagreement or argument about something important.

words.tr:
v. 争论；讲价
n. 讨价还价；争论
words.ex: They haggle over the price of the car.
words.ex_cn: 他们为汽车的价格争论。
words.en: If you haggle, you argue about something, especially about the price of something you want to buy.

words.tr:
n. 麻烦；困难；争吵
v. 烦扰；纠缠
words.ex: It's not worth the hassle to change your plans.
words.ex_cn: 改变计划不值得这么麻烦。
words.en: If you describe something as a hassle, you mean that it is inconvenient and annoying. As a verb, to hassle someone means to annoy or trouble them persistently.

words.tr: adj. 可协商的；可转让的；可通行的
words.ex: The price is negotiable.
words.ex_cn: 价格可以商量。
words.en: If you describe something as negotiable, you mean that it can be changed or agreed upon through discussion.

words.ex: They will negotiate the price with the seller.
words.ex_cn: 他们会与卖家协商价格。
words.en: If people negotiate with each other or negotiate an agreement, they talk about a problem or a situation such as a business arrangement in order to solve the problem or complete the arrangement.

words.tr: adj. 辩论的；引起争论的；争议的
words.ex: His polemical article sparked strong debates.
words.ex_cn: 他那篇有争议的文章引发了激烈争论。
words.en: A polemical piece of writing or speech is one that strongly argues against or in favor of a particular opinion, person, or idea, often in a way that is intended to provoke controversy.

words.ex: His argument was full of sophisms that obscured the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点充满了诡辩，掩盖了真相。
words.en: A sophism is a clever but false argument, especially one used deliberately to deceive.

words.ex: The sophistication of the machine allows it to work very precisely.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器的精密使其能够非常精确地工作。
words.en: Sophistication refers to the quality of being sophisticated, which includes complexity, refinement, and worldly experience.

words.ex: His argument was full of sophistry, making it difficult to discern the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点充满了诡辩，让人难以分辨真相。
words.en: Sophistry is the use of clever but false arguments, especially with the intention of deceiving.

words.tr:
n. 扭打；斗争
v. 扭打；打斗
words.ex: They had a tussle over the last piece of cake.
words.ex_cn: 他们为了最后一块蛋糕扭打起来。
words.en: A tussle is a rough physical struggle or fight.

words.ex: He attests that the document is true.
words.ex_cn: 他证明这份文件是真实的。
words.en: To attest something means to declare or affirm that it is true or genuine, often in a formal or legal context.

words.ex: He received a certification for completing the course.
words.ex_cn: 他完成了课程后获得了证明。
words.en: Certification is the act of certifying or the state of being certified, often involving the issuance of a certificate or official document attesting to a status or level of achievement.

words.ex: The test results confirm he has the disease.
words.ex_cn: 检测结果证实他患有这种疾病。
words.en: To confirm something means to establish its truth or validity by providing evidence or proof.

words.tr:
adj. 明白表示的；证实的；公然表示情绪的
n. 指示词
words.ex: He is demonstrative with his love for his family.
words.ex_cn: 他对家人表达爱意时很外露。
words.en: If you are demonstrative, you show your feelings or behave in a way that shows your love for someone.

words.tr:
n. 文件；公文；文献；
v. 记录；为…提供证明；
words.ex: He submitted the document to the office.
words.ex_cn: 他把文件提交给了办公室。
words.en: A document is a piece of text or graphics, for example a letter, that is stored as a file on a computer and that you can access in order to read it or change it.

words.ex: He needs to substantiate his claim with evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他需要用证据来证实他的说法。
words.en: To substantiate a statement or a story means to supply evidence which proves that it is true.

words.ex: He testified that he saw the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他证明自己看到了那起事故。
words.en: To testify means to make a statement based on personal knowledge or belief, especially in a court of law, or to serve as evidence or proof of something's existence or truth.

words.ex: His testimony proved the suspect was innocent.
words.ex_cn: 他的证词证明了嫌疑人是无辜的。
words.en: A formal written or spoken statement, especially one given in a court of law.

words.ex: Please verify your email address.
words.ex_cn: 请核实你的电子邮件地址。
words.en: To verify something means to check or prove that it is true, accurate, or justified.

words.ex: He proved his innocence to vindicate his name.
words.ex_cn: 他证明了自己的清白以洗清自己的名声。
words.en: To clear someone of blame or suspicion.

words.ex: He felt vindication when the truth came out.
words.ex_cn: 当真相大白时，他感到被证实了。
words.en: Vindication is the act of proving that someone is not guilty of a crime or that something is true.

words.tr: v. 证明…是真实的；鉴别
words.ex: He must authenticate his identity with a password.
words.ex_cn: 他必须用密码验证自己的身份。
words.en: To authenticate something means to prove or confirm that it is genuine or true.

words.ex: He supports advocacy for clean water.
words.ex_cn: 他支持清洁用水的倡导。
words.en: The act of pleading or arguing in favor of something, such as a cause, idea, or policy; active support.

words.ex: He swore allegiance to his country.
words.ex_cn: 他向自己的国家宣誓效忠。
words.en: Loyalty or commitment to a superior or to a group or cause.

words.tr:
n. 扶墙；拱壁
v. 支持
words.ex: The old wall needs a buttress to stay standing.
words.ex_cn: 这面旧墙需要一个支撑物来保持不倒。
words.en: A buttress is a structure built against or projecting from a wall which serves to support or reinforce the wall. As a verb, to buttress means to support or strengthen something.

words.ex: The old temple has a long colonnade with white pillars.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老寺庙有一排长长的白色柱子组成的柱廊。
words.en: A colonnade is a row of columns which are usually evenly spaced and support a roof or a series of arches.

words.ex: The politician's espousal of environmental policies gained him many supporters.
words.ex_cn: 这位政治家对环保政策的拥护为他赢得了许多支持者。
words.en: The act of adopting or supporting a cause, belief, or way of life.

words.ex: He espouses simple ideas about justice.
words.ex_cn: 他拥护关于正义的简单理念。
words.en: If you espouse a particular policy, cause, or belief, you become very interested in it and give your support to it.

words.ex: The climbers found a foothold on the rocky wall.
words.ex_cn: 登山者在岩壁上找到了一个立足点。
words.en: A foothold is a secure position from which further progress or development may be made.

words.ex: The fulcrum is the point on which a lever rests or is supported and on which it pivots.
words.ex_cn: 支点是杠杆所依靠或支撑的点，也是它旋转的中心。
words.en: A fulcrum is the support about which a lever turns, or something that plays a central role in or is in the center of a situation or activity.

words.ex: The statue was placed on a marble pedestal.
words.ex_cn: 雕像被放置在大理石底座上。
words.en: A pedestal is the base or support on which a statue, obelisk, or column is mounted.

words.ex: The statue was mounted on a marble plinth.
words.ex_cn: 雕像被安置在大理石底座上。
words.en: A plinth is a square block, usually made of stone or concrete, on which a statue or pillar is placed.

words.tr:
n. 支撑物；支柱；道具
v. 支撑；靠
words.ex: He uses a prop to support the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个道具来支撑架子。
words.en: A prop is an object or piece of furniture that is used in a play or film to make a scene look more realistic, or something that is used to support or hold up another object.

words.tr:
n. 购买；采购；
v. 购买；采购；
words.ex: The purchase of a new car took all his savings.
words.ex_cn: 买一辆新车花光了他所有的积蓄。
words.en: To purchase something means to buy it. It can also refer to something that has been bought.

words.ex: The doctor put a splint on his broken arm.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他骨折的手臂上了夹板。
words.en: A splint is a long, thin piece of wood or metal that is used to hold a broken bone in place while it heals.

words.ex: He put the camera on a tripod.
words.ex_cn: 他把相机放在三脚架上。
words.en: A tripod is a three-legged stand or support, especially for a camera or telescope.

words.tr: n. 一捆；一束（干草、稻草）；
words.ex: He carried a truss of hay to the barn.
words.ex_cn: 他扛了一捆干草到谷仓。
words.en: To tie up or bind tightly; to support or strengthen with a framework.

words.ex: Strong foundations undergird the old bridge.
words.ex_cn: 坚固的地基加强了这座旧桥。
words.en: To provide a strong foundation or support for something.

words.tr: v. 求爱；求婚；寻求支持
words.ex: He tried to woo her with flowers and chocolates.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用鲜花和巧克力追求她。
words.en: If you woo someone, you try to persuade them to marry you or to have a relationship with you, or you try to gain their support or favor.

words.tr: n. 阐述者；拥护者；代表者；指数
words.ex: He is the exponent of modern education reform.
words.ex_cn: 他是现代教育改革的阐述者。
words.en: An exponent is someone who supports and explains a particular idea, theory, or system, or a symbol that shows how many times a number is to be multiplied by itself.

words.tr:
n. 提倡者；
v. 提倡；
words.ex: He is an advocate for clean water.
words.ex_cn: 他是清洁用水的提倡者。
words.en: If you advocate a particular action or plan, you recommend it publicly.

words.tr:
n. 支撑物；支架；牙箍
v. 支撑；绷紧；紧靠；准备好
words.ex: The old bookshelf needs a brace to stay steady.
words.ex_cn: 旧书架需要一个支撑物来保持稳定。
words.en: To brace oneself means to prepare oneself for something difficult or unpleasant.

words.tr:
v. 吊起；悬挂；投掷
n. 投掷；悬带
