words.ex: The nurse slung the arm in a bandage.
words.ex_cn: 护士用绷带吊起手臂。
words.en: To throw or hurl something with force; to suspend or hang something loosely.

words.tr: n. 公共卫生；卫生设施；
words.ex: The city improved sanitation to keep people healthy.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市改善了公共卫生以保障人民健康。
words.en: The conditions and processes that help maintain health and prevent disease, especially through cleanliness.

words.ex: He moved up to a higher bracket after his promotion.
words.ex_cn: 他升职后进入了更高的等级。
words.en: A bracket is a piece of metal, wood, or plastic that is fastened to a wall in order to support something such as a shelf. In writing, brackets are symbols that are used to separate words or numbers.

words.ex: The witness corroborated his story with photos.
words.ex_cn: 证人用照片证实了他的说法。
words.en: To corroborate something that has been said or reported means to provide evidence or information that supports it.

words.ex: He spoke to his friend yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 他昨天和他的朋友说了话。
words.en: A spoke is one of the rods or bars that connect the center of a wheel to its outer edge, helping to support the wheel's structure.

words.ex: He made a commitment to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他承诺按时完成这个项目。
words.en: A commitment is something that regularly takes up some of your time because of an agreement you have made or because of responsibilities that you have.

words.ex: The car's chassis was damaged in the accident.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的底盘在事故中受损了。
words.en: The chassis is the framework of a vehicle, supporting the body and mechanical components.

words.ex: The fallen tree was a roadblock on the highway.
words.ex_cn: 倒下的树是高速公路上的路障。
words.en: A roadblock is a temporary barrier or obstacle placed across a road to stop or slow down traffic, often used by police or military for control or security purposes.

words.ex: The fence is a barrier to animals.
words.ex_cn: 这道围栏是动物的障碍。
words.en: A barrier is something such as a rule, law, or policy that makes it difficult or impossible for something to happen or be achieved.

words.ex: The members blackballed his application for membership.
words.ex_cn: 成员们对他的入会申请投了反对票。
words.en: To blackball someone is to prevent them from joining a club or group by voting against them.

words.tr:
n. 阻塞；封锁
v. 封锁
words.ex: The blockade stopped all ships from entering the port.
words.ex_cn: 封锁阻止了所有船只进入港口。
words.en: A blockade is an action to prevent goods or people from entering or leaving a place.

words.ex: The blockage in the pipe caused water to stop flowing.
words.ex_cn: 管道中的堵塞导致水停止流动。
words.en: A blockage is a situation in which something is preventing movement or flow in a passage or pipe.

words.tr:
n. 厚木底皮鞋；木屐
v. 堵塞；妨碍
words.ex: She wore wooden clogs to work in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 她穿着厚木底皮鞋去花园干活。
words.en: If something clogs a hole or place, it blocks it so that nothing can pass through.

words.ex: The heavy snow cumbered our progress.
words.ex_cn: 大雪阻碍了我们的前进。
words.en: To hinder or obstruct the movement or progress of someone or something.

words.ex: The two teams are in a deadlock over the budget.
words.ex_cn: 两个团队在预算上陷入了僵局。
words.en: A deadlock is a situation in which no progress can be made or no agreement is reached, especially because of a disagreement between two or more parties.

words.ex: The high fine will deter people from breaking the law.
words.ex_cn: 高额罚款会制止人们违法。
words.en: If something deters you from doing something, it makes you not want to do it or continue doing it.

words.ex: He tried to dissuade her from quitting her job.
words.ex_cn: 他试图劝她不要辞掉工作。
words.en: If you dissuade someone from doing something, you persuade them not to do it.

words.ex: He is encumbered by too many debts.
words.ex_cn: 他被太多的债务拖累。
words.en: To encumber someone or something means to weigh them down or to block or hinder them.

words.tr: v. 预先阻止；抢先一步
words.ex: He forestalls problems by planning ahead.
words.ex_cn: 他通过提前计划来防止问题。
words.en: To forestall something means to prevent it from happening or to act before someone else does in order to prevent them from doing something.

words.tr:
v. 阻碍；妨碍
n. （带盖）篮子
words.ex: Rain hampered our picnic plans.
words.ex_cn: 雨妨碍了我们的野餐计划。
words.en: If something hampers you, it makes it difficult for you to do something.

words.ex: Rain can hinder our plan to go hiking.
words.ex_cn: 雨天会妨碍我们去徒步旅行的计划。
words.en: If something hinders you, it makes it more difficult for you to do something or make progress.

words.tr: n. 绝境；僵局；死路；死胡同
words.ex: The talks reached an impasse and no one could move forward.
words.ex_cn: 谈判陷入了僵局，没有人能继续前进。
words.en: An impasse is a situation in which no progress can be made or no advancement is possible, especially because of disagreement; a deadlock.

words.ex: The fallen tree impeded the car's path.
words.ex_cn: 倒下的树阻碍了汽车的前进。
words.en: To impede something means to make its movement, development, or progress difficult.

words.ex: His speech impediment made it hard for him to talk clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他的口吃使他难以清晰地说话。
words.en: An impediment is something that makes it difficult to do or achieve something.

words.ex: The police intercepted the stolen car.
words.ex_cn: 警察拦截了那辆被盗的汽车。
words.en: If you intercept someone or something that is going from one place to another, you stop them before they get there.

words.ex: The negotiations reached a logjam when neither side would compromise.
words.ex_cn: 谈判陷入僵局，因为双方都不愿意妥协。
words.en: A logjam is a situation in which there is a deadlock or a complete lack of progress, often due to an impasse in negotiations or decision-making processes.

words.ex: The fallen tree obstructs the road.
words.ex_cn: 倒下的树挡住了道路。
words.en: If something obstructs a road or path, it blocks it, stopping people or vehicles from getting past.

words.ex: The fallen tree was an obstruction on the road.
words.ex_cn: 倒下的树是路上的障碍。
words.en: An obstruction is something that blocks a road, passage, or entrance, or the act of blocking something.

words.ex: The leaf occluded the pipe.
words.ex_cn: 叶子堵住了管道。
words.en: To occlude means to block or stop up a passage, opening, or vessel.

words.tr:
n. 僵局；和棋；僵持状态
v. 使陷入僵局
words.ex: The two players are in a stalemate.
words.ex_cn: 两位选手陷入了僵局。
words.en: A situation in which further action or progress by opposing parties seems impossible.

words.tr: n. 特技表演；噱头；发育不良的动植物；
words.ex: The actor performed a dangerous stunt in the movie.
words.ex_cn: 这位演员在电影中表演了一个危险的特技。
words.en: A stunt is a dangerous feat that is done to entertain people, especially in a film.

words.ex: The rain stymied our plan to go hiking.
words.ex_cn: 雨水阻碍了我们去远足的计划。
words.en: To stymie someone or something means to prevent them from achieving their aims.

words.tr:
v. 陷入（困境）；设圈套；
n. 圈套；陷阱；困境；
words.ex: He trapped himself in debt by spending too much.
words.ex_cn: 他因花钱太多而陷入债务困境。
words.en: A trap is a device or enclosure designed to catch and retain animals, typically by allowing entry but not exit or by catching hold of a part of the body.

words.tr:
v. 畏缩不前；犹豫；妨碍
n. 阻碍，妨碍
words.ex: He balks at paying high prices.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意支付高价。
words.en: If you balk at something, you hesitate to do it or agree to it, often because it is unpleasant or difficult.

words.ex: The car had a malfunction in the engine.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的发动机出现了故障。
words.en: If a machine or device malfunctions, it fails to work properly.

words.tr:
n. 马梏；量规；束缚物；渔网
v. 束缚；妨碍；用网捕捉
words.ex: The horse wore a trammel to control its legs.
words.ex_cn: 这匹马戴着马梏来控制它的腿。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is trammeled, you mean that their freedom of action or movement is restricted.

words.tr:
n. 路障；栅栏；阻碍
v. 设路障；阻挡
words.ex: The police put up a barricade to stop the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 警察设了一个路障来阻止人群。
words.en: A barricade is a temporary structure that is built across a road, entrance, or other route to prevent people from passing. It can also refer to the act of creating such a structure.

words.tr:
n. 跨栏；障碍；难关
v. 越过障碍；克服
words.ex: He jumped over the hurdle quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速跳过了跨栏。
words.en: A hurdle is a problem or difficulty that you must deal with before you can achieve something.

words.tr: n. 木栅；打桩; v. 用桩篱把……围起；包围（pale 的 ing 形式）
words.ex: The sky is paling as the sun rises.
words.ex_cn: 随着太阳升起，天空渐渐变亮。
words.en: A paling is a fence made from wooden stakes or boards.

words.ex: The train runs on the rail.
words.ex_cn: 火车在铁轨上行驶。
words.en: A rail is a horizontal bar, typically made of metal or wood, used as a support or barrier; or a track made of steel rails along which trains run.

words.tr:
n. 栅栏；围栏
v. 用栅栏围住；用栅栏防卫
words.ex: The prisoners were locked in a wooden stockade.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯们被关在木制栅栏里。
words.en: A stockade is a defensive barrier made from upright wooden posts or stakes, especially as a temporary defense against attack.

chapters.name: Word List 50 物体行为 促进

words.ex: The car will accelerate when you press the gas.
words.ex_cn: 当你踩油门时，汽车会加速。
words.en: To accelerate means to start to go faster or to make something start to go faster.

words.tr: v. 开动（机器等）；驱使；激励
words.ex: The button actuates the machine.
words.ex_cn: 这个按钮启动机器。
words.en: To actuate something means to make it move or operate, especially by means of a mechanism.

words.tr: v. 促进；使便利；使容易；
words.ex: The teacher facilitates learning by asking questions.
words.ex_cn: 老师通过提问来促进学习。
words.en: To make an action or process easier or more likely to happen.

words.ex: He hastened to finish his homework before dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他赶紧在晚饭前写完作业。
words.en: If you hasten to do something, you quickly do it or quickly go somewhere.

words.ex: He hie to the store after school.
words.ex_cn: 他放学后急忙去商店。
words.en: To go quickly; hasten.

words.ex: The danger impels him to act quickly.
words.ex_cn: 危险驱使他迅速行动。
words.en: If something impels you to do something, it makes you feel very strongly that you must do it.

words.ex: The new law gave impetus to environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 新法律为环境保护提供了推动力。
words.en: Something that gives a process impetus or an impetus makes it happen or progress more quickly.

words.ex: He tried to instigate a fight at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在聚会上挑起争斗。
words.en: If someone instigates an event or situation, they cause it to happen by their actions or behavior.

words.ex: The team gained momentum after scoring the first goal.
words.ex_cn: 球队在进第一个球后获得了势头。
words.en: Momentum is the ability of something to keep increasing, developing, or being more successful.

words.ex: Mother's milk nourishes the baby.
words.ex_cn: 母乳滋养婴儿。
words.en: To nourish someone or something means to provide them with the food and other substances they need in order to live, grow, and be healthy.

words.tr: v. 促进；推动；宣传；推销；
words.ex: Exercise can promote good health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以促进健康。
words.en: To promote means to help something to happen, develop, or increase, or to raise someone to a higher position or rank.

words.tr:
n. 提示；
v. 促使；
adj. 迅速的；准时的；
words.ex: The teacher gave a prompt to help students start writing.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个提示，帮助学生开始写作。
words.en: If you prompt someone when they stop speaking, you encourage or help them to continue. If you are prompt to do something, you do it without delay or you are not late.

words.ex: The wind propels the sailboat forward.
words.ex_cn: 风推动帆船前进。
words.en: To propel something in a particular direction means to cause it to move in that direction.

words.ex: The boat has a large propeller at the back.
words.ex_cn: 这艘船后面有一个大的螺旋桨。
words.en: A propeller is a device with blades that is used to propel a vehicle such as a ship or an airplane.

words.ex: The rocket uses chemical propulsion to fly into space.
words.ex_cn: 火箭使用化学推进力飞入太空。
words.en: Propulsion is the force that moves something forward, especially in vehicles like cars, planes, or spacecraft.

words.tr:
v. 触发；引起；发动；
n. 诱因；触发；
words.ex: The loud noise triggered the alarm.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音触发了警报。
words.en: A trigger is a device that activates a mechanism when it is pulled or pressed. It can also refer to something that causes a particular reaction or development.

words.ex: Good teachers motivate students to learn.
words.ex_cn: 好老师激励学生学习。
words.en: To motivate someone means to provide them with a reason for doing something, especially something that requires effort.

words.ex: His rude words provoked her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话激怒了她。
words.en: If you provoke someone, you deliberately annoy them and try to make them behave aggressively.

chapters.name: Word List 50 物体行为 雕刻

words.ex: He etches a design on the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他在玻璃上刻了一个图案。
words.en: To etch means to cut into a surface, especially metal or glass, using acid or a sharp tool, in order to create a design or pattern.

words.ex: He carved beautiful fretwork on the wooden chair.
words.ex_cn: 他在木椅上雕刻了精美的透雕图案。
words.en: Ornamental work consisting of interlacing parts, especially in wood or metal.

words.ex: He is an icon of pop music.
words.ex_cn: 他是流行音乐的偶像。
words.en: An icon is a small picture or symbol on a computer screen that represents a program or a file.

words.ex: The boy pulled the strings of the marionette.
words.ex_cn: 男孩拉了木偶的线。
words.en: A marionette is a puppet whose movements are controlled by strings.

words.ex: The machine can perforate the paper quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器可以快速地在纸上打孔。
words.en: To make a hole or holes through something, especially by piercing or drilling.

words.ex: He bought a porcelain cup at the market.
words.ex_cn: 他在市场上买了一个瓷杯。
words.en: A hard, white, translucent ceramic that is made by firing a pure clay and then glazing it.

words.ex: The statue has a strong torso.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像有一个强壮的躯干。
words.en: The main part of the human body, not including the head, arms, or legs.

chapters.name: Word List 50 物体行为 躲避

words.ex: He absconded with the money last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚携款逃跑了。
words.en: If someone absconds from somewhere, they leave there quickly and secretly because they have something to hide or are afraid of being caught.

words.ex: His absenteeism caused the team to lose points.
words.ex_cn: 他的缺勤导致团队丢了分数。
words.en: Absenteeism is the habitual non-presence of an employee at their job.

words.ex: He turned his head to avert the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他转过头去避免了事故。
words.en: If you avert something unpleasant, you prevent it from happening.

words.ex: He avoids eating sugar to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他避免吃糖以保持健康。
words.en: If you avoid something, you take action in order to prevent it from happening to you.

words.ex: He was arrested for bilking investors out of millions of dollars.
words.ex_cn: 他因诈骗投资者数百万美元而被捕。
words.en: To bilk someone means to cheat them, especially out of money.

words.ex: The mechanic tightened the bolt with a wrench.
words.ex_cn: 机械师用扳手拧紧了螺栓。
words.en: A bolt is a type of fastener consisting of a threaded pin or rod with a head at one end, designed to be inserted through holes in assembled parts and tightened by a nut from the other end. It can also refer to a sudden dash or run, or to eat food quickly and without chewing.

words.tr: v. 绕行；设法避开；智胜；围住
words.ex: He circumvented the traffic by taking a small road.
words.ex_cn: 他通过走一条小路绕过了交通拥堵。
words.en: If someone circumvents a rule or restriction, they avoid having to obey it, usually in a clever and dishonest way.

words.tr:
v. 避开；躲避
n. 躲避；诡计
words.ex: He dodged the ball quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速躲开了球。
words.en: If you dodge, you move quickly, often to avoid being hit, caught, or seen.

words.ex: The tricky question eluded even the best students.
words.ex_cn: 这道难题难倒了即使是最优秀的学生。
words.en: If something that you want eludes you, you fail to obtain it. If you elude someone or something, you avoid them or escape from them.

words.ex: He reads fantasy books for escapism.
words.ex_cn: 他读奇幻小说来逃避现实。
words.en: Escapism is the tendency to seek distraction and relief from unpleasant realities, especially by seeking entertainment or engaging in fantasy.

words.ex: He tries to eschew sugar for health reasons.
words.ex_cn: 他为了健康尽量避免吃糖。
words.en: If you eschew something, you deliberately avoid doing it or becoming involved in it.

words.ex: He tried to evade the police by driving fast.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过高速驾驶来逃避警察。
words.en: If you evade something, you find a way of not doing something that you really ought to do.

words.ex: He tried evasion to avoid paying taxes.
words.ex_cn: 他试图逃避缴税。
words.en: The act of avoiding something that you are supposed to do or deal with.

words.tr: adj. 逃避的；推托的；闪烁其辞的
words.ex: He gave an evasive answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个回避的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone as evasive, you mean that they deliberately avoid giving clear direct answers to questions.

words.tr:
v. 偷懒；称病；欺诈
n. 假金砖；懒汉；赝品
words.ex: He is goldbricking instead of working.
words.ex_cn: 他正在偷懒而不工作。
words.en: To avoid work or responsibility, especially by pretending to be busy or by shirking duties.

words.tr: adj. 不可避免的；必然发生的
words.ex: The outcome was ineluctable.
words.ex_cn: 结果是不可避免的。
words.en: Something that is ineluctable cannot be avoided or escaped from.

words.ex: He was accused of malingering to avoid military service.
words.ex_cn: 他被指控装病以逃避兵役。
words.en: If someone is malingering, they pretend to be ill in order to avoid work or duties.

words.tr:
v. 挡开；避开；回避
n. 挡开；闪避
words.ex: He parries the punch with his arm.
words.ex_cn: 他用胳膊格挡了这一拳。
words.en: If you parry a question or argument, you cleverly avoid answering it or dealing with it. In fencing, if you parry a blow, you defend yourself against it by pushing it away with your weapon.

words.tr:
n. 撤退；退却；静居处；
v. 撤退；退却；
words.ex: The army ordered a retreat after the battle.
words.ex_cn: 战斗后，军队下令撤退。
words.en: If you retreat, you move away from something or someone, often because you are frightened or because you want to be alone. A retreat is also a quiet, isolated place that you go to in order to rest or to do things in private.

words.ex: He shirks his homework every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天逃避作业。
words.en: If someone shirks their duties or responsibilities, they deliberately avoid doing them.

words.ex: He shuns loud parties because he is shy.
words.ex_cn: 他因为害羞而避开热闹的派对。
words.en: If you shun someone or something, you deliberately avoid them or keep away from them.

words.tr:
v. 向旁侧避让；回避
n. 向侧方跨步
words.ex: He sidestepped the question during the interview.
words.ex_cn: 他在采访中回避了这个问题。
words.en: If you sidestep a problem or question, you avoid answering it or dealing with it.

words.ex: She wore a red skirt to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条红色短裙去参加派对。
words.en: A skirt is a piece of clothing that hangs from the waist and covers part or all of the legs. It can also refer to the edge or border of something, or to the act of moving along the edge of something.

words.tr: n. 逃学；旷课；玩忽职守
words.ex: He was punished for truancy last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周因为逃学被惩罚了。
words.en: The action of staying away from school without permission.

words.tr:
n. 皱眉蹙额；退缩
v. 皱眉蹙额；退避
words.ex: He let out a wince when he touched his sore arm.
words.ex_cn: 当他碰触到疼痛的手臂时，他皱了一下眉。
words.en: If you wince, you make a slight, sudden movement of your face, especially when you are in pain or when you see or hear something unpleasant.

words.tr: v. 潜伏；偷偷隐躲；鬼鬼祟祟地活动
words.ex: The cat skulked behind the bushes.
words.ex_cn: 猫躲在灌木丛后面鬼鬼祟祟地走。
words.en: If someone skulks somewhere, they move there in a quiet, secretive way, often because they are involved in something dishonest or because they do not want to be seen.

words.tr: n. 避难所；庇护所；庇护；
words.ex: The birds found sanctuary in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这些鸟在森林里找到了避难所。
words.en: A sanctuary is a place where people or animals are protected from danger or trouble.

chapters.name: Word List 50 物体行为 发生

words.ex: His pride begets conflict.
words.ex_cn: 他的骄傲招致了冲突。
words.en: To beget means to cause something to happen or exist.

words.ex: Poverty can engender crime.
words.ex_cn: 贫困会引起犯罪。
words.en: To cause a feeling, situation, or condition to exist.

words.ex: The song evokes happy memories of childhood.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌唤起了对童年的美好回忆。
words.en: To evoke a particular memory, idea, emotion, or response means to cause it to occur.

words.ex: The wind generates electricity.
words.ex_cn: 风产生电力。
words.en: To generate something means to cause it to begin and develop.

words.ex: The incidence of flu increased last winter.
words.ex_cn: 去年冬天流感的发生率上升了。
words.en: The incidence of something is the frequency with which it occurs or the rate at which it happens.

words.ex: The occurrence of rain surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 下雨这件事让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: An occurrence is something that happens or takes place.

words.ex: The onset of winter brought heavy snow.
words.ex_cn: 冬天的开始带来了大雪。
words.en: The onset of something is the beginning of it, especially something unpleasant.

words.ex: His spontaneity made the party fun.
words.ex_cn: 他的自发性让派对变得有趣。
words.en: The condition of being spontaneous; impulsive or natural action or behavior.

words.tr: adj. 自发的；自然产生的；
words.ex: The children gave a spontaneous cheer.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们自发地欢呼起来。
words.en: Something that is spontaneous is not planned but happens or is done because of a sudden impulse or natural feeling.

words.tr: adj. 即将发生（或出版等）的；准备好的；
words.ex: The forthcoming book will be released next month.
words.ex_cn: 即将出版的这本书将在下个月发布。
words.en: If something is forthcoming, it is happening or coming soon.

chapters.name: Word List 50 物体行为 复活

words.ex: There was a resurgence of interest in classical music last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年古典音乐的兴趣再次兴起。
words.en: A resurgence is a process in which something becomes active or popular again after a period of inactivity or unpopularity.

words.tr: v. 使复生；使重新出现
words.ex: The magic spell can resurrect the dead.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔法咒语可以让死者复活。
words.en: To resurrect something means to bring it back to life or to bring it back into use or existence after it had disappeared or ended.

words.tr: v. （使）复活；（使）恢复知觉；（使）复兴
words.ex: The paramedics tried to resuscitate the man after he collapsed.
words.ex_cn: 当这位男子晕倒后，急救人员试图救活他。
words.en: To resuscitate someone means to bring them back to consciousness or to make them start breathing again after they have stopped.

words.ex: The city plan will revitalize the old town.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市计划将使老城区复兴。
words.en: To revitalize something means to give it new life or energy.

chapters.name: Word List 50 物体行为 过失

words.tr: adj. 不注意的；疏忽的；非故意的
words.ex: He made an inadvertent mistake while typing.
words.ex_cn: 他在打字时不小心犯了个错误。
words.en: If something bad is inadvertent, it is done without realizing that it is wrong or that it could have bad consequences.

words.ex: His flippancy annoyed the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他的轻率惹恼了老师。
words.en: Flippancy is a lack of seriousness or respect, especially in a situation where it is not appropriate.

words.tr: v. 错误地计算或估计；失算；对…判断错误
words.ex: He miscalculate the cost of the trip.
words.ex_cn: 他算错了旅行的费用。
words.en: If you miscalculate, you make a mistake in judging a situation or in making a calculation.

words.tr:
adv. 有毛病地；出差错地；不合适地
adj. 有毛病的；出差错的；不合适的
words.ex: Something is amiss with the machine.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器有些不对劲。
words.en: If something is amiss, there is something wrong.

words.ex: The boy's delinquency worried his parents.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩的犯罪行为让他的父母很担心。
words.en: Delinquency refers to minor crimes, especially those committed by young people.

words.tr:
adj. 失职的；违法的；拖欠债务的
n. 违犯者；少年罪犯；违法者
words.ex: The delinquent worker ignored his duties.
words.ex_cn: 这位失职的员工忽视了他的职责。
words.en: A delinquent is someone, especially a young person, who commits a crime or breaks the law.

words.tr:
n. 漠视；忽视；
v. 漠视；不理会；不顾；
words.ex: His advice was met with disregard.
words.ex_cn: 他的建议遭到了漠视。
words.en: If you disregard something, you ignore it or do not take account of it.

words.ex: He made an error in his math homework.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学作业中犯了一个错误。
words.en: An error is a mistake.

words.ex: His argument is fallacious because it ignores the facts.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点是错误的，因为它忽略了事实。
words.en: If an idea, argument, or reason is fallacious, it is wrong because it is based on a fallacy.

words.ex: His argument is based on a fallacy.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点基于一个谬误。
words.en: A fallacy is an idea which many people believe to be true, but which is in fact false because it is based on incorrect information or reasoning.

words.ex: Everyone has fallibility and makes mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 每个人都有缺点，都会犯错。
words.en: The state of being liable to make mistakes or be wrong.

words.ex: Everyone is fallible, even teachers.
words.ex_cn: 每个人都会犯错，即使是老师。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is fallible, you mean that they are not perfect and are likely to make mistakes or to fail in what they are doing.

words.ex: He was faulted for missing the deadline.
words.ex_cn: 他因错过截止日期而受到责备。
words.en: To find fault with someone or something means to criticize them or to point out their mistakes or weaknesses.

words.ex: He made a gaffe when he called the boss by the wrong name.
words.ex_cn: 他叫错老板的名字，犯了个错误。
words.en: A gaffe is a mistake that a person makes in public, especially something embarrassing that they say or do.

words.ex: The computer had a small glitch during the presentation.
words.ex_cn: 演示过程中电脑出现了一个小故障。
words.en: A glitch is a small problem or fault that prevents something from working correctly.

words.tr:
n. 倒塌；崩溃；暴跌；
v. 倒塌；崩溃；
words.ex: The collapse of the old bridge caused many problems.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧桥的倒塌引起了诸多问题。
words.en: If a building or other structure collapses, it falls down very suddenly.

words.tr: adj. 没注意到的；未觉察的；忘却的；
words.ex: He was oblivious to the noise around him.
words.ex_cn: 他对周围的噪音毫无察觉。
words.en: If you are oblivious to something or oblivious of it, you are not aware of it.

words.ex: His rude words were an offense to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话冒犯了所有人。
words.en: An offense is a crime or a violation of the law; it can also refer to a feeling of being upset or annoyed by something perceived as insulting or disrespectful.

words.ex: He omitted the last word in the sentence.
words.ex_cn: 他省略了句子中的最后一个词。
words.en: If you omit something, you do not include it in an activity or piece of work, deliberately or accidentally.

words.ex: His oversight caused the project to fail.
words.ex_cn: 他的疏忽导致项目失败。
words.en: An oversight is a mistake that is made by not noticing something or by forgetting to do something.

words.ex: He committed a peccadillo by arriving a few minutes late.
words.ex_cn: 他因迟到几分钟而犯了一个小错误。
words.en: A peccadillo is a small, unimportant fault or sin.

words.tr: adj. 疏忽的；怠慢的；不留心的
words.ex: It would be remiss of me not to mention the importance of regular exercise.
words.ex_cn: 不提及定期锻炼的重要性，我会感到疏忽。
words.en: If someone is remiss, they are careless and do not do the things they are expected to do.

words.tr: n. 打字（或排印）文稿的小错误
words.ex: He found a typo in his email.
words.ex_cn: 他在邮件里发现了一个拼写错误。
words.en: A typo is a mistake in the way something is printed or written.

words.tr: n. 时代错误；不合时代的事；过时的事或人
words.ex: The knight in the movie uses a smartphone, which is an anachronism.
words.ex_cn: 电影中的骑士使用智能手机，这是不合时宜的。
words.en: An anachronism is something that is out of place in terms of time or chronology, such as an object, a custom, or an idea that belongs to a different time period than the one in which it is placed.

words.tr: adj. 游历的；游离不定的；行为不当的；出轨的
words.ex: The errant knight traveled far across the land.
words.ex_cn: 这位游历的骑士穿越了广袤的土地。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as errant, you mean that they have strayed from the proper course or standards.

words.ex: His answer was erroneous because he added wrong.
words.ex_cn: 他的答案是错误的，因为他加错了。
words.en: If you describe someone's beliefs or opinions as erroneous, you mean that they are incorrect and based on false information.

words.ex: I assume it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我假定明天会下雨。
words.en: If you assume that something is true, you accept that it is true without proof.

words.ex: His assumption was that the train would be on time.
words.ex_cn: 他的假设是火车会准时。
words.en: An assumption is something that you assume to be the case, even without proof.

words.ex: His conjecture was that the missing key was in the drawer.
words.ex_cn: 他猜测丢失的钥匙在抽屉里。
words.en: A conjecture is a conclusion that is based on information that is not certain or complete.

words.ex: He extrapolates the trend from last year's data.
words.ex_cn: 他从去年的数据中推断出趋势。
words.en: To extrapolate is to estimate or conclude something by extending or projecting known information.

words.ex: He made a hypothesis that plants grow faster in light.
words.ex_cn: 他提出一个假设，认为植物在光照下长得更快。
words.en: A hypothesis is an idea which is suggested as a possible explanation for a particular situation or condition, but which has not yet been proved to be correct.

words.ex: It is a hypothetical situation.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个假设的情况。
words.en: A hypothetical situation, idea, or explanation is based on possible ideas or situations rather than actual ones.

words.ex: He posits that the earth is round.
words.ex_cn: 他提出地球是圆的。
words.en: To posit something is to suggest it as a basic fact or principle from which a further idea is formed or developed.

words.tr:
v. 假定；要求
n. 假定；假设
words.ex: He postulates that all humans are equal.
words.ex_cn: 他假定所有人都是平等的。
words.en: If you postulate something, you suggest it as the basis for a theory, argument, or calculation.

words.ex: It is presumable that he will arrive tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天可能会到。
words.en: If you say that something is presumable, you mean that you think it is true or likely, although you are not certain.

words.ex: I presume he will arrive tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我假设他明天会到。
words.en: If you presume that something is the case, you think that it is the case, although you are not certain.

words.ex: His plan is based on a presupposition that everyone will agree.
words.ex_cn: 他的计划基于一个所有人都会同意的假设。
words.en: A presupposition is something that you assume to be true, especially something which you must assume is true in order to continue with a line of argument or a course of action.

words.ex: I reckon it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我认为明天会下雨。
words.en: If you reckon that something is true, you think that it is true.

words.tr:
v. 臆测；猜想
n. 臆测；猜度
words.ex: He surmises that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他推测明天会下雨。
words.en: If you surmise that something is true, you guess it from the available evidence, although you do not know for certain.

words.ex: He made an extrapolation from the data to predict the future.
words.ex_cn: 他根据数据做出了外推以预测未来。
words.en: Extrapolation is the act of estimating or concluding something by assuming that existing trends will continue or a current method will remain applicable.

words.ex: The team went on a fact-finding trip to the village.
words.ex_cn: 团队去村庄进行了一次调查事实的旅行。
words.en: Fact-finding is used to describe activities or missions that are intended to discover the facts about a situation.

words.ex: The team canvass voters for their opinions.
words.ex_cn: 团队征询选民的意见。
words.en: To canvass means to ask people for their votes or opinions, especially in a political context, or to examine something carefully.

words.tr:
n. 审查员；检查员
v. 检查；审查
words.ex: The censor removed the bad words from the movie.
words.ex_cn: 审查员从电影中删除了粗俗用语。
words.en: A censor is a person who supervises conduct and morals: in particular, one who examines books, films, or other material for objectionable matter.

words.ex: The mother won custody of her child.
words.ex_cn: 母亲获得了孩子的监护权。
words.en: Custody is the legal right or duty to care for someone or something, especially a child after its parents have separated or died.

words.ex: The detection of smoke triggered the alarm.
words.ex_cn: 烟雾的探测触发了警报。
words.en: The act of detecting something, especially something that is not easy to see, hear, etc.

words.ex: The police will investigate the accident.
words.ex_cn: 警方将调查这起事故。
words.en: If someone, especially an official, investigates an event, situation, or claim, they try to find out what happened or what is the truth.

words.ex: The teacher will invigilate the exam.
words.ex_cn: 老师将监考这场考试。
words.en: To supervise candidates during an examination to prevent cheating.

words.ex: The manager oversees the team's daily work.
words.ex_cn: 经理监督团队的日常工作。
words.en: To oversee means to watch and direct a piece of work, the people doing it, or the way it is done in order to ensure that it is done correctly.

words.ex: The poll showed that most people support the new law.
words.ex_cn: 这项民意调查表明，大多数人支持这项新法律。
words.en: A poll is a survey in which people are asked their opinions about something, usually in order to find out how popular something is or what people intend to do in the future.

words.ex: He will proofread the letter before sending it.
words.ex_cn: 他在发送这封信之前会校对。
words.en: To read and mark corrections on a text before it is published.

words.ex: The thermostat helps regulate the room temperature.
words.ex_cn: 恒温器有助于调节室温。
words.en: To regulate something means to control or manage it, especially by means of rules or laws.

words.tr: v. 详细检查；仔细察看
words.ex: The teacher scrutinizes every student's homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师仔细检查每位学生的作业。
words.en: If you scrutinize something, you examine it very carefully, often to find out some information from it or about it.

words.tr: v. 监督；管理；主管；指挥
words.ex: He superintends the construction site every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天监督建筑工地。
words.en: To be in charge of something and make sure that it is working as it should.

words.ex: The teacher supervises the students during the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 老师在实验期间指导学生。
words.en: If you supervise an activity or a person, you make sure that the activity is done correctly or that the person is doing a task or behaving correctly.

words.ex: The police used surveillance to watch the building.
words.ex_cn: 警察使用监视来观察那栋大楼。
words.en: The careful watching of a person or place, especially by the police or army, because of a crime that has happened or is expected.

words.ex: He will assemble the toy for his son.
words.ex_cn: 他将为儿子组装玩具。
words.en: If people assemble or if someone assembles them, they come together in a group, usually for a particular purpose such as a meeting.

words.tr: v. 招手示意；举手召唤；引诱
words.ex: He beckoned to the boy to come closer.
words.ex_cn: 他向那个男孩招手示意过来。
words.en: If you beckon to someone, you signal to them to come to you, usually by a gesture of your hand.

words.ex: The smoke made him choke.
words.ex_cn: 烟让他窒息。
words.en: If you choke, or if something chokes you, you cannot breathe properly because there is not enough air or because something is blocking your throat.

words.ex: The team's cohesion helped them win the match.
words.ex_cn: 团队的凝聚力帮助他们赢得了比赛。
words.en: Cohesion refers to the action or fact of forming a united whole, especially in the context of a group of people or the parts of a substance.

words.ex: He compiles data from many surveys.
words.ex_cn: 他汇编来自许多调查的数据。
words.en: To compile means to collect information from different places and arrange it in a book, report, or list.

words.ex: The committee will convene tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 委员会明天将召开会议。
words.en: If someone convenes a meeting or conference, they arrange for it to take place. They can also be said to convene when they meet.

words.ex: The convergent series gets closer to a final number.
words.ex_cn: 这个会聚级数逐渐接近一个最终数值。
words.en: Convergent refers to the process or state of coming together or moving toward union or uniformity, especially in the context of ideas, cultures, or scientific phenomena.

words.ex: The president convoked an emergency meeting.
words.ex_cn: 总统召集了一次紧急会议。
words.en: To call together for a meeting or assembly.

words.ex: Dolphins are gregarious animals that swim in groups.
words.ex_cn: 海豚是群居动物，成群游泳。
words.en: Someone who is gregarious enjoys being with other people.

words.ex: His gregariousness makes him popular at parties.
words.ex_cn: 他的外向性格让他在派对上很受欢迎。
words.en: The quality of being fond of company; sociability.

words.ex: The judge will summon him tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 法官明天将传唤他。
words.en: If you summon someone, you order them to come to you.

words.tr: v. 重新集合；重新召集
words.ex: The committee will reconvene next Monday.
words.ex_cn: 委员会将在下周一重新召开。
words.en: To reconvene means to come together again after a break or to cause a group to come together again.

words.ex: He accumulates coins from different countries.
words.ex_cn: 他收集来自不同国家的硬币。
words.en: To accumulate means to gradually gather or acquire an increasing number or quantity of something.

words.tr:
n. 总计；集合体
adj. 合计的；总的
v. （使）聚集；聚合；总计为
words.ex: The aggregate of all sales this month is $50,000.
words.ex_cn: 本月所有销售额的总计是5万美元。
words.en: An aggregate is a number of things or people that are considered as a group or a whole.

words.ex: He amass wealth by working hard.
words.ex_cn: 他通过努力工作积累财富。
words.en: If you amass something such as money or information, you gradually collect a large amount of it.

words.ex: They had a big banquet after the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 婚礼后他们举办了一场盛大的宴会。
words.en: A banquet is a large formal meal for many people, often followed by speeches in honor of someone.

words.ex: The team showed cohesive behavior during the project.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队在项目期间表现出有凝聚力的行为。
words.en: If something is cohesive, it consists of parts that fit together well and form a united whole.

words.ex: The global climate conference was held in Paris.
words.ex_cn: 全球气候大会在巴黎举行。
words.en: A conference is a meeting of people who share the same interests or profession.

words.tr:
adj. 砾岩的；成球状的；结成团块的
n. 砾岩；企业集团；联合大公司；合成物
v. （使）结聚成一团
words.ex: The rock layer is conglomerate, made of small stones stuck together.
words.ex_cn: 这层岩石是砾岩，由小石头粘合而成。
words.en: A conglomerate is a large business firm consisting of several different companies.

words.ex: People congregate in the park on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 人们在周末聚集在公园里。
words.en: To congregate means to come together in a group or crowd.

words.ex: The milk turned into curd after sitting overnight.
words.ex_cn: 牛奶放了一夜后变成了凝乳。
words.en: A soft, white substance formed when milk coagulates, used as the basis for cheese.

words.ex: You need to pay a 40-yuan deposit to rent the bike.
words.ex_cn: 租自行车需要支付40元押金。
words.en: A deposit is a sum of money which is part of the full price of something, and which you pay when you agree to buy it. It is also a sum of money that you pay into a bank account.

words.ex: He garnered food for the winter.
words.ex_cn: 他贮藏了过冬的食物。
words.en: To gather or collect something, especially information or support.

words.ex: The old woman gleaned wheat from the field after the harvest.
words.ex_cn: 这位老妇人在收割后从田里拾落穗。
words.en: To gather information or material bit by bit.

words.tr:
n. 组；群；集团；
v. （使）形成组；
words.ex: The students are in a group of five.
words.ex_cn: 这些学生组成一个五人小组。
words.en: A group is a number of people or things that are located, gathered, or classed together.

words.tr:
n. 化妆舞会；伪装
v. 伪装；冒充
words.ex: We went to a masquerade last night.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨晚去参加了一个化妆舞会。
words.en: A masquerade is a party or dance where people wear masks and costumes, or it refers to the act of pretending to be someone or something else.

words.tr:
v. 鼓起；集合；召集
n. 集合；集合的人群
words.ex: He must muster courage to speak in public.
words.ex_cn: 他必须鼓起勇气在公众面前发言。
words.en: To muster means to gather or assemble (troops, etc.), especially for inspection or in preparation for battle. It can also mean to summon up (a feeling, attitude, or response).

words.tr:
v. 集合起来；振作；复苏
n. 集会
words.ex: The crowd rallied to support their team.
words.ex_cn: 人群聚集起来支持他们的球队。
words.en: A rally is a large public meeting that is held in order to show support for something such as a political party or a sports team. It can also mean to come together again in order to continue fighting or arguing after a defeat or a period of confusion.

words.tr: n. 专题讨论会；研讨会
words.ex: He spoke at a symposium about climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他在一个关于气候变化的研讨会上发言。
words.en: A symposium is a conference or meeting to discuss a particular subject.

words.ex: He won the chess tournament last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周赢得了国际象棋锦标赛。
words.en: A tournament is a competition in which players who win a match continue to play further matches in the competition until just one person or team is left.

words.ex: The dust formed an agglomeration on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 灰尘在地板上形成了结块。
words.en: An agglomeration is a mass or collection of things; especially a cluster of disparate elements.

words.tr: n. 混合物；聚集物；集团化
words.ex: The conglomeration of small shops made a big mall.
words.ex_cn: 小商店的聚集形成了一家大型商场。
words.en: A conglomeration is a mixture of different things that are found all together.

words.ex: The cumulative score is the total of all previous points.
words.ex_cn: 累积得分是所有之前分数的总和。
words.en: If a series of events have a cumulative effect, each event makes the effect greater.

words.tr: v. 改编为戏剧；渲染；使戏剧化
words.ex: They dramatize the novel for the stage.
words.ex_cn: 他们将这部小说改编成舞台剧。
words.en: If a book or story is dramatized, it is written or presented as a play, film, or television drama.

words.tr:
v. 大声宣布；装饰
n. 徽章
words.ex: He blazoned his name on the flag.
words.ex_cn: 他在旗帜上醒目地写下了自己的名字。
words.en: To blazon something means to describe, depict, or display it prominently or vividly, often in a heraldic context.

words.tr: n. 特性描述；人物性格塑造；
words.ex: The characterization of the hero shows his bravery.
words.ex_cn: 对英雄的特性描述展现了他勇敢的品质。
words.en: The act of describing or representing the qualities or peculiarities of a person or thing.

words.tr: v. 描述…的特性；以…为特征；
words.ex: This book characterizes the hero as brave and kind.
words.ex_cn: 这本书将主人公描述为勇敢而善良的。
words.en: To describe the character or qualities of someone or something.

words.ex: He gave a citation from the book.
words.ex_cn: 他引用了这本书中的一段话。
words.en: A citation is a reference to a published or unpublished source (not always the original source). More precisely, a citation is an abbreviated alphanumeric expression embedded in the body of an intellectual work that denotes an entry in the bibliographic references section of the work for the purpose of acknowledging the relevance of the works of others to the topic of discussion at the spot where the citation appears.

words.ex: He cited a book in his essay.
words.ex_cn: 他在文章中引用了一本书。
words.en: To cite something means to quote it or mention it as evidence or proof of what you are saying.

words.ex: He will delineate the plan clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他将清晰地描述这个计划。
words.en: To delineate something means to describe or portray it precisely.

words.ex: The painting depicts a quiet village at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画描绘了一个宁静的村庄在日落时分的景象。
words.en: To depict someone or something means to show or represent them in a work of art such as a drawing or painting.

words.tr:
v. 乱写；乱画；涂鸦
n. 乱画；乱写；涂鸦
words.ex: He doodled on his notebook during class.
words.ex_cn: 他在上课时在笔记本上乱画。
words.en: If you doodle, you draw small, simple pictures or patterns on a piece of paper, often while you are thinking about something else.

words.ex: He will enumerate the steps clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他将清晰地列出这些步骤。
words.en: To enumerate means to mention things one by one.

words.tr:
n. 摘录；摘要
v. 摘录；引用
words.ex: He read an excerpt from the book.
words.ex_cn: 他读了这本书的一段摘录。
words.en: An excerpt is a short piece of writing or music which is taken from a larger piece.

words.ex: He expatiated on the importance of education.
words.ex_cn: 他详细阐述了教育的重要性。
words.en: To expatiate means to speak or write about something in great detail or at considerable length.

words.ex: The artist limned the scene with great detail.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家非常详细地描绘了那个场景。
words.en: To depict or describe in painting or words.

words.tr:
n. 叙述；叙事；
adj. 叙述性的；
words.ex: He told a simple narrative about his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了一个关于他童年的简单故事。
words.en: A narrative is a story or an account of a series of events.

words.ex: Can you particularize your request?
words.ex_cn: 你能详细说明你的要求吗？
words.en: To particularize means to describe or consider something in detail, often by listing its individual parts or aspects.

words.ex: The GPS can pinpoint your exact location.
words.ex_cn: GPS可以精准定位你的准确位置。
words.en: To pinpoint something means to locate or identify it precisely.

words.ex: The painter portrays a happy family in the photo.
words.ex_cn: 这位画家在画中描绘了一个幸福的家庭。
words.en: To portray someone or something means to show or represent them in a painting, film, book, or other artistic work.

words.tr:
v. 引用；报价；
n. 引用；引文；报价；
words.ex: He quoted Shakespeare in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中引用了莎士比亚的话。
words.en: To repeat or copy out (a group of words from a text or speech), typically with an indication that one is not the original author or speaker.

words.ex: He stipple the paper with small dots.
words.ex_cn: 他用小点点缀了纸张。
words.en: To stipple means to paint, engrave, or draw by means of dots or small touches.

words.ex: The word 'buzz' is an example of onomatopoeia.
words.ex_cn: 单词'buzz'是拟声的一个例子。
words.en: The formation of a word from a sound associated with what is named.

words.ex: The parrot can say hello.
words.ex_cn: 这只鹦鹉会说你好。
words.en: A parrot is a tropical bird with a curved beak and brightly colored feathers. Parrots are often kept as pets because they can be taught to copy human speech.

words.tr: n. （名人）雕像；（丑化的）模拟像
words.ex: They burned an effigy of the king.
words.ex_cn: 他们烧了一个国王的雕像。
words.en: An effigy is a sculpture or model of a person, often made to be destroyed as a protest or as part of a ceremony.

words.tr: n. 复制本；摹本；仿制品；传真
words.ex: He sent a facsimile of the document to his office.
words.ex_cn: 他把文件的传真发到了办公室。
words.en: An exact copy of a document, picture, or piece of writing, especially one that has been made by a machine.

words.ex: The necklace is an imitation made of plastic.
words.ex_cn: 这条项链是用塑料做的仿制品。
words.en: An imitation of something is a copy of it.

words.ex: The child made an imitative sound of the bird.
words.ex_cn: 孩子模仿鸟的声音。
words.en: If you describe someone's actions as imitative, you mean that they are copying someone else's actions, rather than being original.

words.ex: He tried to impersonate a police officer.
words.ex_cn: 他试图冒充一名警察。
words.en: To impersonate someone means to pretend to be that person, either to deceive people or to entertain them.

words.tr: adj. 无法仿效的；不可比拟的
words.ex: Her inimitable style of writing has captured the hearts of many readers.
words.ex_cn: 她那独特的写作风格赢得了许多读者的心。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as inimitable, you mean that they are so good or unusual that it is unlikely that anyone or anything else could be like them.

words.ex: He bought a replica of the ancient statue.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一件古代雕像的复制品。
words.en: A replica of something such as a statue, building, or weapon is an accurate copy of it.

words.ex: The game simulates real traffic conditions.
words.ex_cn: 这个游戏模拟了真实的交通状况。
words.en: To simulate is to create a model or representation of a situation, process, or system for the purpose of study, analysis, or training. It involves imitating the conditions of a real event or environment to understand its effects or to practice responses to it.

words.tr: n. 自动装置；机器人；机器人似的人
words.ex: The factory was filled with automatons that performed repetitive tasks.
words.ex_cn: 工厂里满是执行重复任务的自动机。
words.en: An automaton is a machine that operates on its own without the need for human control, especially a robot in the form of a human.

words.ex: They tried to coerce him into signing the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图强迫他签署那份文件。
words.en: If you coerce someone into doing something, you make them do it, even though they do not want to.

words.ex: The law compels drivers to wear seat belts.
words.ex_cn: 法律强迫司机系安全带。
words.en: If a situation, a rule, or a person compels you to do something, they force you to do it.

words.ex: The law constrains companies from polluting rivers.
words.ex_cn: 法律约束公司不得污染河流。
words.en: To constrain someone or something means to limit their development or force them to behave in a particular way.

words.ex: The budget is a constraint on our project.
words.ex_cn: 预算是我们项目的限制。
words.en: A constraint is something that limits or controls what you can do.

words.ex: He signed the paper under duress.
words.ex_cn: 他在胁迫下签了那张纸。
words.en: Duress is a situation in which someone is forced to do something against their will, typically by the use of threats or force.

words.ex: The government imposed a new tax on sugar.
words.ex_cn: 政府对糖征收了一项新税。
words.en: To impose means to officially force a rule, tax, punishment, etc. to be obeyed or received.

words.ex: The bully tried to intimidate the new student.
words.ex_cn: 那个霸凌者试图恐吓新生。
words.en: If you intimidate someone, you deliberately make them frightened enough to do what you want them to do.

words.ex: He does not want to intrude on their conversation.
words.ex_cn: 他不想插话他们的谈话。
words.en: To intrude means to enter somewhere or become involved in a situation where you are not wanted or are not supposed to be.

words.tr: adj. 强制性的；义务的；必须的；
words.ex: Wearing a helmet is obligatory for cyclists.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔是强制性的。
words.en: If something is obligatory, you must do it because of a rule or law.

words.tr: v. 强使接受；打扰；闯入
words.ex: He tried to obtrude his opinions on the group.
words.ex_cn: 他试图强使组里接受他的观点。
words.en: To force something on someone in a way that is unwelcome or intrusive.

words.tr: v. 征募；征用；强占；霸占
words.ex: The soldiers commandeer the truck for their mission.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们征用了那辆卡车用于任务。
words.en: If the army, police, or any other group in authority commandeers a vehicle or building, they officially take charge of it so that they can use it.

words.ex: The child loves to play with fantasy stories about dragons.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子喜欢玩关于龙的幻想故事。
words.en: A fantasy is a pleasant situation or event that you imagine, which is unlikely to happen.

words.ex: He saw a mirage in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 他在沙漠中看到了海市蜃楼。
words.en: An optical illusion caused by atmospheric conditions, especially the appearance of a sheet of water in a desert or on a hot road caused by the refraction of light from the sky by heated air.

words.ex: The phantom appeared in the mist near the old house.
words.ex_cn: 幻影出现在老房子附近的薄雾中。
words.en: A phantom is a ghost or a figment of the imagination.

words.ex: His opinion is subjective and not based on facts.
words.ex_cn: 他的观点是主观的，不是基于事实的。
words.en: Based on or influenced by personal feelings, tastes, or opinions.

words.ex: He dreams of a perfect utopia where everyone is happy.
words.ex_cn: 他梦想一个每个人都很幸福的完美乌托邦。
words.en: An imagined place or state of things in which everything is perfect.

words.tr: adj. 乌托邦的；空想完美主义的；
words.ex: His plan for a perfect society is utopian.
words.ex_cn: 他关于完美社会的计划是乌托邦式的。
words.en: If you describe a plan or idea as utopian, you are criticizing it because it is unrealistic and shows a belief that things can be improved much more than is possible.

words.tr: adj. 可想象得出的；可信的；可能的
words.ex: It is conceivable that he will arrive late.
words.ex_cn: 他可能会迟到，这是可以想象的。
words.en: Capable of being imagined or grasped mentally.

words.ex: He waited in the foyer before the show started.
words.ex_cn: 演出开始前，他在门厅里等候。
words.en: A foyer is an area at the front of a building, especially a hotel or theater, where people can wait or meet others.

words.tr: n. 间歇；插曲；幕间节目
words.ex: He took an interlude to drink water.
words.ex_cn: 他休息了一下喝水。
words.en: An interlude is a short period of time that comes in the middle of something, or a short piece of music, talk, or entertainment that comes between the main parts of a performance or event.

words.ex: We waited in the hotel lobby for our friend.
words.ex_cn: 我们在酒店的大厅里等我们的朋友。
words.en: A lobby is a large room or hall in a building, often used for meetings or as a waiting area. As a verb, to lobby means to try to influence politicians or officials on a particular issue.

words.tr: v. 施以催眠术；迷住；迷惑
words.ex: The dancer mesmerized the crowd with her slow movements.
words.ex_cn: 舞者用她缓慢的动作对观众施以催眠术。
words.en: If you are mesmerized by something, you are so interested in it or so attracted to it that you cannot think about anything else.

words.ex: He is prone to colds in winter.
words.ex_cn: 他冬天容易感冒。
words.en: If you are prone to a particular problem or characteristic, you are likely to be affected by it or to have it.

words.tr: v. 躺；靠在；向后倾斜（坐椅）
words.ex: He reclines on the sofa after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后躺在沙发上。
words.en: To recline means to lean or lie back in a relaxed position with the body supported.

words.tr: adj. 斜躺的；斜靠的；侧卧的
words.ex: The old man sat in a recumbent chair.
words.ex_cn: 那位老人坐在一张躺椅上。
words.en: A recumbent position or posture is one in which a person is lying down or leaning back in a relaxed manner.

words.ex: Reading a book gives me relaxation.
words.ex_cn: 读书让我放松。
words.en: Relaxation is the state or process of becoming less tense, anxious, or stressed.

words.ex: After work, she found repose in her garden.
words.ex_cn: 下班后，她在花园里休息。
words.en: A state of rest, sleep, or tranquility. To lie or be placed in a particular position or manner.

words.tr:
n. 度假胜地；手段；
v. 求助于；
words.ex: They went to a beach resort for their vacation.
words.ex_cn: 他们去一个海滨度假胜地度假。
words.en: If you resort to a particular course of action, you do it because you cannot see any other way of achieving what you want.

words.ex: The wind began to slacken after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 风暴过后，风速开始减缓。
words.en: If something slackens or if you slacken it, it becomes slower, less active, or less intense.

words.tr:
v. 睡眠
n. 睡眠（常复数）
words.ex: The baby fell into a deep slumber after feeding.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝喂完奶后进入了深深的睡眠。
words.en: Slumber is a state of sleep, especially one that is peaceful and restful.

words.tr: adj. 昏昏欲睡的；困倦的；催眠的
words.ex: The somnolent boy nodded off during class.
words.ex_cn: 那个昏昏欲睡的男孩在课堂上睡着了。
words.en: If you are somnolent, you feel sleepy.

words.ex: He compresses the file to save space.
words.ex_cn: 他压缩文件以节省空间。
words.en: To compress something means to press it or squeeze it so that it takes up less space.

words.tr: v. 充塞；充血；使拥挤；充满
words.ex: The traffic congests the city center during rush hour.
words.ex_cn: 高峰时段，交通堵塞了市中心。
words.en: If a place is congested, it is extremely crowded and blocked with traffic or people.

words.ex: The snake constricts its prey.
words.ex_cn: 蛇缠住它的猎物。
words.en: If something constricts you, it limits your actions so that you cannot do what you want to do.

words.ex: The rope constringe around the box.
words.ex_cn: 绳子紧紧缠绕在盒子上。
words.en: To make or become narrower or tighter by squeezing or pressing.

words.tr: v. 装入胶囊；压缩；简述；概括
words.ex: The pharmacist encapsulate the medicine into small capsules.
words.ex_cn: 药剂师把药物装入小胶囊中。
words.en: To encapsulate something means to express or show the most important facts about it in a very short and clear form.

words.tr:
v. 挤作一团
n. 挤作一团
words.ex: The team huddled together to plan their next move.
words.ex_cn: 团队聚在一起规划下一步行动。
words.en: If people huddle together, they stand, sit, or lie close to each other because they are cold or frightened.

words.tr:
n. 新闻界；出版社；
v. 按；压；
words.ex: The press reported the news quickly.
words.ex_cn: 新闻界迅速报道了这则新闻。
words.en: To press something is to push it firmly, often with your fingers or hand, in order to operate a device or machine, or to make something flat or smooth. It can also mean to urge someone to do something or to make a strong demand for something.

words.ex: The sweater shrinks in hot water.
words.ex_cn: 这件毛衣在热水中会收缩。
words.en: If something shrinks or you shrink it, it becomes smaller.

words.ex: He put a stamp on the envelope.
words.ex_cn: 他在信封上贴了一张邮票。
words.en: A stamp is a small piece of paper which you stick on an envelope or package before you post it to pay for the cost of the postage. It can also mean to bring down your foot heavily on the ground or to impress a pattern or mark on a surface.

words.ex: The teacher gave formative feedback to help students improve.
words.ex_cn: 老师给出了影响形成的学习反馈，以帮助学生改进。
words.en: Relating to or characterized by the formation or development of something.

words.tr:
n. 影响力；冲击（力）；
v. 对…产生影响；
words.ex: The new law had a big impact on education.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律对教育产生了重大影响。
words.en: The effect or influence of one person, thing, or action, on another.

words.ex: He is impressionable and easily believes what others say.
words.ex_cn: 他容易受影响，很容易相信别人说的话。
words.en: Someone who is impressionable is easily influenced by other people's opinions or actions.

words.ex: The interplay between light and shadow creates beauty.
words.ex_cn: 光与影的相互作用创造了美。
words.en: The way in which two or more things have an effect on each other.

words.ex: Several factors militate against his success.
words.ex_cn: 有几个因素对他的成功产生不利影响。
words.en: If something militates against a particular thing, it makes it less likely to happen or be successful.

words.tr: adj. 身心失调的；身心的
words.ex: His headache is psychosomatic, not from illness.
words.ex_cn: 他的头痛是心理作用引起的，不是因为生病。
words.en: Relating to or involving both the mind and the body, especially in the context of illness or psychological stress.

words.ex: The old house has a mysterious aura.
words.ex_cn: 这所老房子有一种神秘的氛围。
words.en: An aura is a distinctive atmosphere or quality that seems to surround and be generated by a person, thing, or place.

words.tr: v. 预想；事先想好；预先形成
words.ex: He preconceives that all teachers are strict.
words.ex_cn: 他先入为主地认为所有老师都很严格。
words.en: To form an opinion or idea about something before having enough information or experience.

words.ex: The fate was preordained by the gods.
words.ex_cn: 命运早已由神明注定。
words.en: If something is preordained, it is decided by God or fate in advance.

words.tr: adj. 预知的；有先见之明的
words.ex: His prescient warning saved many lives.
words.ex_cn: 他那有先见之明的警告挽救了许多生命。
words.en: Having or showing knowledge of events before they take place.

words.tr: v. 简述；预示；勾画轮廓
words.ex: He adumbrated the plan in a few words.
words.ex_cn: 他用几句话简述了这个计划。
words.en: To give a faint indication or suggestion of something; to outline or sketch.

words.ex: The dark clouds bode a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something bodes ill, it makes you think that something bad will happen in the future. If something bodes well, it makes you think that something good will happen.

words.tr:
n. 凶兆；前兆；预兆
v. 预示；是…的兆头；“bode”的现在分词
words.ex: He is boding about the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他正在为考试担忧。
words.en: A feeling that something bad is going to happen; an omen or foreboding.

words.ex: The temple is a divine place.
words.ex_cn: 这座寺庙是神的圣地。
words.en: Something that is divine relates to a god or goddess.

words.ex: He envisions a world without war.
words.ex_cn: 他想象一个没有战争的世界。
words.en: To envision something is to imagine it as a future possibility; it is often used to describe the act of foreseeing or planning for the future.

words.ex: The dark clouds forebode a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something forebodes a future event, it suggests that it is going to happen.

words.tr:
n. 预测；预报；
v. 预测；预报；
words.ex: The weather forecast says it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 天气预测说明天会下雨。
words.en: If you forecast future events, you say what you think is going to happen in the future.

words.ex: He had foreknowledge of the storm.
words.ex_cn: 他事先知道会有风暴。
words.en: Knowledge of something before it happens or exists.

words.ex: The horse-drawn carriage was a forerunner of the car.
words.ex_cn: 马车是汽车的先驱。
words.en: A forerunner is someone or something that comes before another and is often considered as a sign of what is to follow.

words.ex: The dark clouds are a harbinger of storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云是暴风雨的预兆。
words.en: A harbinger is something that shows that something is going to happen soon, especially something bad.

words.ex: The cat hunched its back when it saw the dog.
words.ex_cn: 猫看到狗时，背部拱了起来。
words.en: A hunch is a feeling or guess based on intuition rather than known facts.

words.ex: The painting gave me inspiration.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画给了我灵感。
words.en: Inspiration is a feeling of enthusiasm you get from someone or something, which gives you new and creative ideas.

words.ex: The dark clouds looked ominous before the storm.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨来临前，乌云显得不祥。
words.en: If you describe something as ominous, you mean that it worries you because it makes you think that something unpleasant is going to happen.

words.ex: Dark clouds portend a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something portends something else, it indicates that it is likely to happen in the future.

words.ex: The bicycle was a precursor to the car.
words.ex_cn: 自行车是汽车的先驱。
words.en: A precursor is something that happened or existed before another thing, especially if it either developed into it or had an influence on it.

words.ex: The dark clouds prefigure a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If one thing prefigures another, it is a sign that the other thing will happen or exist in the future.

words.ex: She had a premonition that something bad was going to happen.
words.ex_cn: 她有一种不祥的预感，觉得会有坏事发生。
words.en: A premonition is a feeling that something, especially something unpleasant, is going to happen.

words.tr:
n. 预示；前兆；预感
v. 预示；预兆
words.ex: The dark clouds presage a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something presages a situation or event, it is considered to be a warning or sign of what is about to happen.

words.ex: He showed prescience by predicting the storm.
words.ex_cn: 他通过预测风暴展现了先见之明。
words.en: The ability to know or predict what will happen in the future.

words.ex: She had a presentiment that something bad was going to happen.
words.ex_cn: 她有一种不祥的预感，觉得会有坏事发生。
words.en: A presentiment is a feeling that something is about to happen, especially something unpleasant.

words.ex: He gave a quick preview of the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他简要预看了这部电影。
words.en: A preview is an opportunity to see something such as a film or a collection of works of art before it is open to the public.

words.ex: He made a prevision of the storm.
words.ex_cn: 他预见到这场风暴。
words.en: The ability to foresee or predict future events or developments.

words.tr: n. 预断病情；预后；预测
words.ex: The prognosis for patients with this disease is generally poor.
words.ex_cn: 这种疾病的患者预后通常不佳。
words.en: A prognosis is an estimate of the future course and outcome of a disease, especially of the chances of recovery.

words.ex: He tries to prognosticate the weather tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他试图预测明天的天气。
words.en: To prognosticate means to foretell or predict something based on present signs or symptoms.

words.ex: The old woman made a prophecy about the rain.
words.ex_cn: 那位老妇人预言了会有雨。
words.en: A prophecy is a statement that something will happen in the future, especially one made by someone with religious or magical powers.

words.tr: adj. 预言的；预示的；先知的
words.ex: His words were prophetic when the storm came.
words.ex_cn: 当风暴来临时，他的话应验了。
words.en: If something was prophetic, it described or suggested something that did actually happen later.

words.ex: The actors had a rehearsal before the play.
words.ex_cn: 演出前，演员们进行了一次排练。
words.en: A rehearsal of a play, dance, or piece of music is a practice of it in preparation for a performance.

words.ex: The actors rehearse their lines every evening.
words.ex_cn: 演员们每天晚上排练他们的台词。
words.en: To rehearse means to practice a play, piece of music, or other work for later public performance.

words.ex: The dark clouds foreshadow a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something foreshadows an event or situation, it suggests that it will happen.

words.ex: She had a premonitory feeling that something bad was about to happen.
words.ex_cn: 她有一种不祥的预感，觉得有不好的事情即将发生。
words.en: Serving as a warning or indication of a future event.

words.ex: A sense of foreboding filled the room as the storm approached.
words.ex_cn: 随着暴风雨的临近，房间里充满了不祥的预感。
words.en: A foreboding is a feeling that something bad is going to happen.

chapters.name: Word List 52 普通状态 安静

words.ex: The volcano is quiescent now.
words.ex_cn: 这座火山现在处于休眠状态。
words.en: Someone or something that is quiescent is quiet and inactive.

words.ex: The chair is stationary and does not move.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子是固定的，不会移动。
words.en: not moving or not intended to be moved

words.ex: He kept his equanimity during the storm.
words.ex_cn: 他在风暴中保持了冷静。
words.en: If you face a difficult situation with equanimity, you remain calm and do not get upset or angry.

words.ex: He remembers those halcyon days of childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他怀念那些童年的宁静时光。
words.en: A halcyon time is a time in the past that was peaceful or happy.

words.tr:
v. 使安静；使肃静
n. 安静
words.ex: Please hush, the baby is sleeping.
words.ex_cn: 请安静，宝宝在睡觉。
words.en: If you hush someone or if they hush, they stop speaking or making a noise.

words.tr:
adj. 哑的；无声的
n. 哑巴；沉默的人
v. 减弱…的声音
words.ex: He stayed mute during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议期间保持沉默。
words.en: If someone is mute, they are unable to speak.

words.ex: The pastoral man tends his sheep on the hill.
words.ex_cn: 这位牧人在山上照看他的羊。
words.en: Relating to the countryside or to the work of a shepherd; idyllically rural.

words.tr: adj. 平静的；宁静的；温和的；
words.ex: The lake was placid in the morning light.
words.ex_cn: 清晨的阳光下，湖面平静无波。
words.en: A placid person or animal is calm and does not easily become excited, angry, or upset.

words.tr:
n. 保护区；储备；保留；
v. 预订；
words.ex: The wildlife reserve is home to many endangered animals.
words.ex_cn: 这个自然保护区是许多濒危动物的家园。
words.en: If you reserve something such as a table, ticket, or magazine, you arrange for it to be kept for you and not given to anyone else.

words.tr: adj. 沉默寡言的；讳莫如深的
words.ex: He is reticent about his feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的感受很沉默。
words.en: If you are reticent about something, you are unwilling to talk about it or make your feelings known.

words.tr: adj. 平静的；宁静的；安详的
words.ex: The lake is serene in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 清晨的湖面很宁静。
words.en: Calm, peaceful, and untroubled; tranquil.

words.ex: He is taciturn and rarely speaks.
words.ex_cn: 他沉默寡言，很少说话。
words.en: A taciturn person does not say very much and can seem unfriendly.

words.ex: The lake at dawn offers perfect tranquility.
words.ex_cn: 黎明时分的湖泊带来完全的宁静。
words.en: A state of peace and quiet.

words.ex: The lake offers quietude at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 湖面在日出时带来宁静。
words.en: A state of stillness, calmness, and quiet in a place or person.

chapters.name: Word List 52 普通状态 吵闹

words.tr:
v. 大叫；大哭；大声训斥
n. 叫骂声；放声痛哭
words.ex: The baby began to bawl when he saw the dog.
words.ex_cn: 当宝宝看到狗时，开始大哭。
words.en: To shout or cry loudly and often for a long time.

words.tr: n. 混乱；骚乱情景；疯人院
words.ex: The classroom was a bedlam during the fire drill.
words.ex_cn: 火灾演习时，教室里一片混乱。
words.en: A scene of uproar and confusion.

words.tr:
v. 发出（响亮而刺耳的声音）
n. 响亮刺耳的声音
words.ex: The car alarm blares loudly at night.
words.ex_cn: 汽车警报在夜里大声响着。
words.en: If something such as a siren or radio blares or if you blare it, it makes a loud, unpleasant noise.

words.tr:
v. 咆哮；“bluster”的现在分词
adj. 狂暴的
words.ex: He is blustering about his big achievements.
words.ex_cn: 他正在夸夸其谈自己的伟大成就。
words.en: If you say that someone is blustering, you mean that they are speaking aggressively but without authority, often because they are angry or offended.

words.ex: The children were boisterous at the party.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在聚会上喧闹不已。
words.en: Someone who is boisterous is noisy, lively, and full of energy.

words.ex: The bird made a soft chirp in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在早晨发出轻柔的唧唧声。
words.en: If a bird or an insect chirps, it makes short high-pitched sounds.

words.tr:
n. 喧嚷；大声的要求
v. 喧嚷；大声地要求
words.ex: The crowd made a loud clamor for justice.
words.ex_cn: 人群为正义发出大声喧哗。
words.en: If people are clamoring for something, they are demanding it in a noisy or angry way.

words.tr:
n. 嘈杂声；喧闹声
v. 喧闹；喋喋不休地说
words.ex: The children made a loud din in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在教室里发出很大的嘈杂声。
words.en: A din is a loud, unpleasant, and prolonged noise.

words.ex: The fracas at the party scared everyone.
words.ex_cn: 派对上的骚乱吓到了所有人。
words.en: A fracas is a noisy quarrel or fight.

words.ex: The hubbub in the market made it hard to think.
words.ex_cn: 市场里的喧闹让人难以集中思想。
words.en: A hubbub is a loud, confused noise, especially one caused by a large crowd of people.

words.tr: n. 欢乐的集会；喧闹的集会；庆祝会
words.ex: The kids joined a big jamboree last summer.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们去年夏天参加了一个盛大的集会。
words.en: A jamboree is a large, festive gathering or celebration, often involving music, dancing, and other forms of entertainment.

words.ex: The obstreperous crowd made it difficult to hear the speaker.
words.ex_cn: 吵闹的人群使得演讲者的话难以听清。
words.en: If you say that someone is obstreperous, you are annoyed because they are noisy and difficult to control.

words.tr: adj. 不安宁的； 焦躁不安的；难驾驭的；倔强的
words.ex: The audience grew restive as the speaker droned on.
words.ex_cn: 演讲者喋喋不休，听众开始焦躁不安。
words.en: If you are restive, you are impatient or bored with a situation and you want it to change.

words.ex: The child was restless during the long meeting.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在漫长的会议中坐立不安。
words.en: If you are restless, you are unable to stay still or to be calm and happy, because you are bored or worried.

words.ex: The students roistered through the streets after the football victory.
words.ex_cn: 足球胜利后，学生们在大街上狂欢。
words.en: To engage in noisy, boisterous, or drunken revelry.

words.tr:
adj. 欢闹的；嬉戏耍闹的
v. 嘻嘻哈哈地闹着玩；“rollick”的现在分词
words.ex: The party was a rollicking affair with lots of laughter and dancing.
words.ex_cn: 派对是一场充满欢笑和舞蹈的欢乐活动。
words.en: If you describe an activity as rollicking, you mean that it is lively and enjoyable.

words.tr: n. 骚动；骚乱；心烦意乱
words.ex: The crowd caused a tumult after the game.
words.ex_cn: 比赛后，人群引起了混乱。
words.en: A tumult is a state of confusion, noise, and excitement, often involving a large group of people.

words.ex: The announcement caused an uproar in the town.
words.ex_cn: 这个公告在小镇上引起了轩然大波。
words.en: A loud and impassioned noise or disturbance.

words.tr: adj. 喧嚣的；吵闹的；令人捧腹大笑的
words.ex: The party became uproarious as the night went on.
words.ex_cn: 随着夜晚的深入，派对变得喧嚣起来。
words.en: If something is uproarious, it is very noisy and loud, often because people are laughing or shouting.

words.tr: adj. 大声喊叫的；喧嚷的
words.ex: The vociferous crowd shouted for change.
words.ex_cn: 喧闹的人群大声要求变革。
words.en: If you describe someone as vociferous, you mean that they speak with great energy and determination, because they want their views to be heard.

chapters.name: Word List 52 普通状态 吃惊

words.tr:
adj.  张口发呆的；目瞪口呆的
adv. 张口发呆地；目瞪口呆地
words.ex: The child stood agape at the magic show.
words.ex_cn: 孩子目瞪口呆地看着魔术表演。
words.en: If you describe someone as being agape, you mean that their mouth is open wide, often because they are very surprised by something.

words.ex: She was aghast when she saw the mess.
words.ex_cn: 她看到那片狼藉时惊呆了。
words.en: If you are aghast, you are filled with horror and surprise.

words.ex: The magic trick astounded the children.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术让孩子们惊呆了。
words.en: If something astounds you, it surprises or shocks you very much.

words.ex: The violent news appalls her.
words.ex_cn: 这起暴力新闻令她震惊。
words.en: to fill with horror or dismay; shock deeply

words.ex: Her sudden resignation caused great consternation among her colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 她的突然辞职让她的同事们非常震惊。
words.en: A feeling of anxiety or dismay, typically at something unexpected.

words.ex: The nation was convulsed by political scandal.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家因政治丑闻而剧烈震动。
words.en: If someone convulses or if they are convulsed by or with something, their body moves suddenly and violently, often in an uncontrolled way.

words.tr: v. 使说不出话来；使目瞪口呆
words.ex: The magic trick dumbfound everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术让所有人都惊呆了。
words.en: If someone or something dumbfounds you, they surprise you so much that you cannot think or speak for a moment.

words.ex: The new song caused a furor among teenagers.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌在青少年中引起了狂热。
words.en: A furor is a very angry or excited reaction by people to something.

words.tr: n. 城河；壕坑; n. （Foss）人名；（德、英、法、西、瑞典）福斯
words.ex: The castle is surrounded by a deep foss.
words.ex_cn: 城堡被一条深城河环绕。
words.en: A fossilized remnant or trace of an organism from a past geological age.

words.tr:
adj. 可怕的；恐怖的；惨白的；令人不快的
adv. 可怖地；惨白地
words.ex: The ghost looked ghastly in the dark.
words.ex_cn: 那个幽灵在黑暗中看起来吓人极了。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as ghastly, you mean that they are extremely unpleasant or shocking.

words.ex: She stored jam in a glass jar.
words.ex_cn: 她把果酱存放在一个玻璃罐里。
words.en: A jar is a glass or clay container with a wide opening at the top and a lid, used especially for storing food.

words.tr: adj. 非常亮的；浓艳的；苍白的；血红的；可怕的；（故意地）骇人听闻的
words.ex: The lurid neon signs lit up the night street.
words.ex_cn: 鲜艳的霓虹灯照亮了夜晚的街道。
words.en: If you say that something is lurid, you are critical of it because it involves a lot of violence, sex, or shocking detail.

words.tr:
v. 惊异于；惊异；
n. 令人惊异的人（或事）；
words.ex: I marvel at how fast she runs.
words.ex_cn: 我惊异于她跑得有多快。
words.en: If you marvel at something, you express your great surprise, wonder, or admiration.

words.tr: v. 使石化；使僵化；吓呆
words.ex: The lightning petrified the tree into stone.
words.ex_cn: 闪电把树变成了石头。
words.en: To petrify means to make someone so frightened that they are unable to move or think.

words.ex: The cold water gave her a sudden sensation.
words.ex_cn: 冷水给了她一种突然的感觉。
words.en: A sensation is a physical feeling or a reaction of interest or excitement that something causes in a person or in a group of people.

words.tr: adj. 易恶心的；易受惊的；神经质的；过于拘谨的
words.ex: She was too squeamish to watch the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 她太容易呕吐了，不敢看手术过程。
words.en: If you are squeamish, you are easily upset by unpleasant sights or situations.

words.ex: The loud noise startle the bird.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音惊动了那只鸟。
words.en: If something or someone startles you, they surprise and frighten you slightly.

words.ex: The earthquake caused tremendous damage.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了巨大的破坏。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as tremendous, you mean that they are very great in amount, extent, or intensity.

words.ex: The view from the mountain is marvelous.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色极好。
words.en: If you describe something as marvelous, you are emphasizing that it is extremely good.

chapters.name: Word List 52 普通状态 充满

words.tr: adj. 充满（不愉快事物）的；
words.ex: The journey was fraught with delays.
words.ex_cn: 这次旅程充满了延误。
words.en: If a situation or activity is fraught with problems or risks, it is full of them.

words.ex: The table was replete with food.
words.ex_cn: 桌子上摆满了食物。
words.en: If you are replete with something, you have a lot of it and it fills you up.

chapters.name: Word List 52 普通状态 繁忙

words.tr: v. （使）参与；从事于；雇佣；“engage”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 忙着的；
words.ex: The teacher engaged the students in a group discussion.
words.ex_cn: 老师让学生们参与了一次小组讨论。
words.en: If you are engaged in an activity, you are doing it or involved in it. If you are engaged to someone, you have agreed to marry them.

words.tr: adj. 匆忙的；草率的；急躁的
words.ex: He made a hasty decision and regretted it.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一个仓促的决定，后来后悔了。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behavior as hasty, you mean that they are acting too quickly, without thinking carefully, often with unwanted results.

words.ex: Her mornings are hectic with work and kids.
words.ex_cn: 她的早晨因为工作和孩子而紧张忙碌。
words.en: If you describe a situation as hectic, you mean that it is very busy and involves a lot of rushed activity.

words.ex: The onerous workload made her tired every day.
words.ex_cn: 繁重的工作量让她每天都很累。
words.en: If you describe a task as onerous, you dislike having to do it because you find it difficult or unpleasant.

words.tr: adv. 概括地；草率地；立即地
words.ex: The case was dismissed summarily.
words.ex_cn: 这个案件被立即驳回。
words.en: If something is done summarily, it is done quickly and without considering all the details.

words.tr:
adj. 繁重的；费力的；伤脑筋的
v. 对...征税；使负重荷；“tax”的现在分词
words.ex: The math test was taxing for the students.
words.ex_cn: 这次数学考试让学生们感到很吃力。
words.en: If you describe a task as taxing, you mean that it requires a lot of mental or physical effort.

chapters.name: Word List 52 普通状态 方便

words.ex: The store is open 24 hours for your convenience.
words.ex_cn: 商店24小时营业，以方便您。
words.en: The state of being able to proceed with something with little effort or difficulty.

words.tr: n. 权宜；与目的相称；私利
words.ex: He ignored the rules for expediency.
words.ex_cn: 他为了方便而忽略了规则。
words.en: Expediency is the quality of being convenient and practical despite possibly being improper or immoral.

words.ex: This portable charger works well on trips.
words.ex_cn: 这个便携式充电器在旅行时很好用。
words.en: Capable of being carried or moved about with ease.

chapters.name: Word List 52 普通状态 费解

words.ex: The profundity of his insights left the audience speechless.
words.ex_cn: 他见解的深刻让观众无言以对。
words.en: Profundity refers to the quality of being profound, which means having deep insight or understanding, or being very intense or extreme.

words.ex: The abstruse math problem confused the students.
words.ex_cn: 这个深奥的数学问题让学生们感到困惑。
words.en: Difficult to understand; obscure.

words.ex: No example sentences
words.ex_cn: 没有例句
words.en: A conundrum is a confusing and difficult problem or question.

words.tr:
adj. 旋绕的；费解的
v. 盘旋；卷绕；“convolute”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The path through the garden was convoluted.
words.ex_cn: 花园里的小路蜿蜒曲折。
words.en: If you describe something such as a story, explanation, or system as convoluted, you mean that it is complicated and difficult to understand.

words.tr: adj. 难以捉摸的；不易被抓获（觉察、理解或记忆）的；
words.ex: The truth remained elusive.
words.ex_cn: 真相难以捉摸。
words.en: Difficult to find, catch, or achieve; difficult to remember or understand.

words.ex: The book contains esoteric ideas that only experts understand.
words.ex_cn: 这本书包含了只有专家才能理解的深奥思想。
words.en: Intended for or likely to be understood by only a small number of people with a specialized knowledge or interest.

words.tr: adj. 无法触及的；摸不着的；难解的
words.ex: The concept of infinity is often considered impalpable.
words.ex_cn: 无限的概念常常被认为是难以理解的。
words.en: Impalpable means something that cannot be perceived by touch or is very difficult to understand or define.

words.tr: adj. 无法解释的；费解的
words.ex: His sudden silence was inexplicable.
words.ex_cn: 他突然的沉默无法解释。
words.en: If something is inexplicable, you cannot explain why it happens or why it is true.

words.tr: adj. 难以捉摸的；难以理解的；神秘莫测的
words.ex: His expression was inscrutable.
words.ex_cn: 他的表情难以捉摸。
words.en: If someone or something is inscrutable, it is impossible to understand or know what they are thinking or feeling.

words.ex: The intricacy of the clock made it very special.
words.ex_cn: 这座钟的复杂精细让它非常特别。
words.en: The quality of being intricate; complexity.

words.ex: The lock has an intricate design.
words.ex_cn: 这个锁有复杂的结构。
words.en: You use intricate to describe something that has many small parts or details.

words.ex: The meaning of the poem is obscure.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗的意思不清楚。
words.en: If something is obscure, it is not well known or not easily understood.

words.ex: The artist lived in obscurity for most of his life.
words.ex_cn: 这位艺术家一生大部分时间都默默无闻。
words.en: The state of being unknown, inconspicuous, or unimportant.

words.tr: adj. 不透明的；难懂的；晦涩的
words.ex: The glass is opaque, so I cannot see through it.
words.ex_cn: 这扇玻璃是不透明的，所以我看不到它后面的东西。
words.en: If an object or substance is opaque, you cannot see through it.

words.ex: The children enjoyed solving the rebus puzzles.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们喜欢解画谜。
words.en: A rebus is a puzzle in which words are represented by combinations of pictures and individual letters; for instance, 'i' might be represented by an eye.

words.ex: The recondite math problem confused most students.
words.ex_cn: 这道深奥的数学题让大多数学生感到困惑。
words.en: Recondite knowledge or information is known and understood by very few people.

words.ex: The old man gave an enigmatic smile.
words.ex_cn: 那位老人露出了一个神秘的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as enigmatic, you mean they are mysterious and difficult to understand.

words.ex: The ancient symbol remains an enigma.
words.ex_cn: 这个古代符号仍然是一个谜。
words.en: An enigma is something that is mysterious and difficult to understand.

chapters.name: Word List 52 普通状态 疯狂

words.ex: His political speeches were often filled with zealotry and fanaticism.
