words.ex: The old man was doddering as he walked down the street.
words.ex_cn: 老人走在街上时蹒跚而行。
words.en: If you describe someone as doddering, you mean they are old and weak, and they walk in a way that is not steady.

words.ex: He worked hard to fulfill his dream.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以实现自己的梦想。
words.en: To fulfill a task, role, or function means to do or perform it as required or expected.

words.tr: v. 容纳；适应；为...提供住宿；
words.ex: The hotel can accommodate 200 guests.
words.ex_cn: 这家酒店能容纳200位客人。
words.en: If a building or space can accommodate someone or something, it has enough room for them.

words.tr: adj. 不对称的；不均匀的
words.ex: The two sides of the box are asymmetric.
words.ex_cn: 盒子的两边不对称。
words.en: An asymmetric object does not have the same shape, size, or arrangement on both sides of a central line.

words.ex: His opinion coincides with mine.
words.ex_cn: 他的观点与我的一致。
words.en: If one event coincides with another, they happen at the same time.

words.ex: His salary is commensurate with his experience.
words.ex_cn: 他的薪水与他的经验相称。
words.en: If the level of one thing is commensurate with another, the first level is in proportion to the second.

words.tr: adj. 符合的；一致的；全等的
words.ex: The two shapes are congruent in size.
words.ex_cn: 这两个形状大小相符。
words.en: If one thing is congruent with another, they are similar or fit together well.

words.ex: The colors are congruous with the room's design.
words.ex_cn: 这些颜色与房间的设计相协调。
words.en: If one thing is congruous with another, there is a harmonious agreement or consistency between them.

words.tr: adj. 一致的；始终如一的；
words.ex: His answers are consistent with the data.
words.ex_cn: 他的答案与数据一致。
words.en: Someone who is consistent always behaves in the same way, has the same attitudes towards people or things, or achieves the same level of success in something.

words.ex: The correspondent reported the news from the city.
words.ex_cn: 记者从城市报道了新闻。
words.en: A correspondent is someone who reports news from a particular place or on a particular subject for a newspaper, magazine, or television or radio station.

words.ex: The team works in harmony.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队合作得很和谐。
words.en: Harmony is the pleasant combination of different notes of music played at the same time. It can also refer to a situation in which people are peaceful and agree with each other, or when things seem right or suitable together.

words.ex: The butterfly has perfect symmetry.
words.ex_cn: 这只蝴蝶有完美的对称性。
words.en: Symmetry is the quality of being made up of exactly similar parts facing each other or around an axis.

words.tr:
n. 记数；
v. 合计；
words.ex: He kept a tally of how many goals he scored.
words.ex_cn: 他记录了自己进了多少球。
words.en: A tally is a record of amounts or numbers which you keep changing and adding to as the activity which affects it progresses.

words.ex: The unification of the two countries brought peace.
words.ex_cn: 两个国家的统一带来了和平。
words.en: The process of making or becoming a single unit.

words.tr:
adj. 一致的；统一的；
n. 制服；
words.ex: The students wear a uniform shirt to school.
words.ex_cn: 学生们穿一致的衬衫去学校。
words.en: A uniform is a special set of clothes which some people, for example soldiers or the police, wear to work in and which some children wear at school. It is also used to describe something that is the same in all parts and does not vary.

words.tr: v. （使）统一；（使）联合；（使）成一体；
words.ex: The two teams decided to unify their efforts.
words.ex_cn: 这两个团队决定统一他们的努力。
words.en: To unify means to make or become united, uniform, or whole.

words.ex: The two shirts are identical.
words.ex_cn: 这两件衬衫是一样的。
words.en: Exactly the same, or very similar.

words.ex: There is a resemblance between the two brothers.
words.ex_cn: 这两兄弟之间有相似之处。
words.en: If there is a resemblance between two people or things, they are similar to each other.

words.tr:
v. 抵消；使平衡
n. 衡重体；平衡力
words.ex: The weight acts as a counterbalance to the arm.
words.ex_cn: 这个重量作为手臂的平衡物。
words.en: A counterbalance is a weight or force that balances or counteracts another.

words.tr:
n. 平衡；砝码
v. 平衡；平均
words.ex: The weight acts as a counterpoise to the arm.
words.ex_cn: 这个重量作为手臂的平衡物。
words.en: A counterpoise is a force or influence that balances or offsets another, maintaining stability or equilibrium.

words.ex: The two kids stayed in equilibrium on the seesaw.
words.ex_cn: 两个孩子在跷跷板上保持了平衡。
words.en: A state in which opposing forces or influences are balanced.

words.ex: The machine will homogenize the milk.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器会将牛奶均质化。
words.en: To homogenize something means to make it the same throughout, or to make it uniform.

words.ex: These two words are interchangeable in this sentence.
words.ex_cn: 这两个词在这个句子中可以互换使用。
words.en: If one thing is interchangeable with another, the first can be used instead of the second because it has the same function or meaning.

words.tr:
v. 嘲讽；嘲弄；相匹配
n. 嘲弄；挖苦
words.ex: His story doesn't jibe with the facts.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事与事实不符。
words.en: If one thing jibes with another, they agree or are very similar.

words.tr:
n. 平方；广场；正方形；四方形；
adj. 正方形的；四方形的；平方的；成直角的；
v. 与...一致；
adv. 成直角地；
words.ex: The area of the room is 16 square.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间的面积是16平方米。
words.en: A square is a shape with four sides of equal length and four angles of 90 degrees. It can also refer to an open area in a town, often used for public events, or to the result of multiplying a number by itself.

words.ex: The leaf is asymmetrical.
words.ex_cn: 这片叶子是不对称的。
words.en: Something that is asymmetrical has two sides or halves that are different in shape, size, or style.

words.tr: adj. 脱离正道的；脱离常轨的
words.ex: His aberrant behavior surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他反常的行为让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: An aberrant person or thing is one that is unusual or unexpected, especially in an unwelcome way.

words.tr: adj. 偏离规则的；反常的
words.ex: The temperature was anomalous for this season.
words.ex_cn: 这个季节的温度异常。
words.en: Deviating from what is standard, normal, or expected.

words.tr: n. 异常事物；反常现象；
words.ex: The strange weather this month is an anomaly.
words.ex_cn: 这个月奇怪的天气是一个异常现象。
words.en: Something that deviates from what is standard, normal, or expected.

words.ex: An apparition appeared in the dark hallway.
words.ex_cn: 一个幽灵出现在黑暗的走廊里。
words.en: An apparition is a ghost or ghostlike image of a person.

words.tr: adj. 离奇的；奇特的；奇怪的；
words.ex: The clown wore a bizarre hat with three eyes.
words.ex_cn: 小丑戴着一顶有三只眼睛的离奇帽子。
words.en: Something that is bizarre is very odd and strange.

words.tr:
adj. 不正常的；离经叛道的
n. 不正常的人
words.ex: His deviant behavior surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他不正常的行为让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: Deviant behavior or thinking is different from what people normally consider to be acceptable.

words.tr: adj. 功能失调的；出现障碍的；
words.ex: The dysfunctional family rarely ate meals together.
words.ex_cn: 这个功能失调的家庭很少一起吃饭。
words.en: Not operating normally or properly.

words.ex: He is an eccentric man who wears socks with sandals.
words.ex_cn: 他是个古怪的人，穿着袜子配凉鞋。
words.en: If you say that someone is eccentric, you mean that they behave in a strange way, and have habits or opinions that are different from those of most people.

words.tr: adj. 外来的；外国来的；奇异的；
words.ex: The market sells exotic fruits from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个市场出售来自其他国家的外来水果。
words.en: Something that is exotic is unusual and interesting because it comes from or is related to a distant country.

words.ex: The trial was a farce.
words.ex_cn: 这场审判是一场闹剧。
words.en: A farce is a comedy that aims at entertaining the audience through situations that are highly exaggerated, extravagant, and thus improbable.

words.tr:
n. 怪诞行为；
adj. 不正常的；怪异的；
words.ex: His freak of wearing socks with sandals surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他穿袜子配凉鞋的怪诞行为让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: A freak is a person who is considered to be unusual because of their behaviour or interests, or a sudden and unexpected event or situation.

words.tr:
adj. 怪诞的；丑陋奇异的；奇形怪状的
n. 奇形怪状的东西；奇异风格
words.ex: The painting showed a grotesque face with twisted eyes.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画上有一个扭曲眼睛的怪诞面孔。
words.en: If you say that something is grotesque, you mean that it is extremely unattractive, exaggerated, and often shocking or disturbing.

words.ex: His heterodox ideas shocked the traditional scholars.
words.ex_cn: 他的非正统观点让传统学者感到震惊。
words.en: Heterodox ideas, opinions, or practices are different from the accepted or official ones.

words.ex: The child's recovery was a miracle.
words.ex_cn: 孩子的康复是个奇迹。
words.en: A miracle is an event that cannot be explained by the laws of nature and is therefore considered to be the work of a divine agency.

words.tr: adj. 奇迹般的；不可思议的；神奇的
words.ex: The sick boy made a miraculous recovery.
words.ex_cn: 那个生病的男孩奇迹般地康复了。
words.en: If you describe a good event as miraculous, you mean that it is very surprising and unexpected.

words.tr: adj. 畸形的；奇形怪状的；扭曲变形的；
words.ex: The misshapen toy looked strange to the children.
words.ex_cn: 那个畸形的玩具让孩子们觉得奇怪。
words.en: If something is misshapen, it has a shape that is not the normal or natural one, often because it has been damaged or has not developed correctly.

words.ex: The toy store sells many novelty items for children.
words.ex_cn: 玩具店出售许多为儿童设计的新奇物品。
words.en: The quality of being new, original, or unusual; something new, original, or unusual.

words.tr: adj. 不寻常的；非传统的；不落俗套的
words.ex: He likes offbeat movies that no one else understands.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢那些别人都不理解的古怪电影。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as offbeat, you mean that they are different from what is usual or expected in an unusual and appealing way.

words.ex: He wore an outlandish hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶奇异的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe something as outlandish, you mean that it is very unusual, strange, or exaggerated.

words.tr: adj. 不寻常的；超自然的；难以解释的
words.ex: The psychic claimed to have preternatural abilities.
words.ex_cn: 这位通灵者声称自己拥有超自然的能力。
words.en: Beyond what is normal or natural; supernatural.

words.ex: The boy is a piano prodigy at age six.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩六岁时就是一位钢琴奇才。
words.en: A prodigy is someone who is unusually young and has a great natural ability in a particular area.

words.ex: The singularity of the black hole confuses scientists.
words.ex_cn: 黑洞的特异性让科学家感到困惑。
words.en: The state, fact, quality, or condition of being singular.

words.tr: adj. 非尘世的；怪异的；可怕的；时间过早或不便的
words.ex: The unearthly glow of the northern lights was mesmerizing.
words.ex_cn: 北极光那神秘的光辉令人着迷。
words.en: If you describe something as unearthly, you mean that it seems strange and unnatural, not like anything that exists in the natural world.

words.tr: n. 奇想；异想天开；怪异多变
words.ex: His plans change with every vagary of mood.
words.ex_cn: 他的计划随着情绪的每个变化而改变。
words.en: A vagary is an unexpected and inexplicable change in a situation or in someone's behavior.

words.tr:
v. 缓行；溜蹄
n. 溜蹄；缓行漫步
words.ex: He amble through the park after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后在公园里缓行。
words.en: To walk at a slow, relaxed pace, especially for pleasure.

words.tr: n. （短暂的）情事；调情；短暂参与
words.ex: He had a short dalliance with a singer.
words.ex_cn: 他与一位歌手有过一段短暂的恋情。
words.en: Dalliance refers to a casual involvement with something, especially a romantic or sexual relationship, without serious intentions.

words.ex: He dawdled away the afternoon at the park.
words.ex_cn: 他在公园里混掉了整个下午。
words.en: If you dawdle, you spend more time than is necessary going somewhere or doing something.

words.tr: n. 道德败坏；堕落；沉湎酒色（或毒品）
words.ex: He lost his job because of debauchery.
words.ex_cn: 他因为放荡不羁而丢了工作。
words.en: Excessive indulgence in sensual pleasures.

words.tr: adj. 无能的；软弱的；不中用的
words.ex: His feckless attempts to solve the problem only made it worse.
words.ex_cn: 他试图解决问题的无效尝试反而使问题变得更糟。
words.en: If you describe someone as feckless, you mean that they lack determination or strength, and are unable to do anything properly.

words.ex: He is loitering near the park.
words.ex_cn: 他正在公园附近闲逛。
words.en: If someone loiters somewhere, they remain there or walk up and down without any real purpose.

words.tr: adj. 巡游的；到处走的；兼职的
words.ex: He is a peripatetic teacher who moves from town to town.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位四处奔波的老师，从一个城镇搬到另一个城镇。
words.en: If you have a peripatetic job or way of life, you travel around a lot, living or working in different places for short periods of time.

words.ex: We walked along the promenade by the sea.
words.ex_cn: 我们在海边的步行区散步。
words.en: A promenade is a leisurely walk, especially one taken in a public place for pleasure or display.

words.ex: He likes to ramble about his travels.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢漫谈他的旅行经历。
words.en: To walk for pleasure, especially in the countryside, without a definite route or destination.

words.tr:
v. 闲逛；漫步
n. 闲逛；漫步
words.ex: We decided to saunter along the beach.
words.ex_cn: 我们决定沿着海滩漫步。
words.en: If you saunter somewhere, you walk there in a slow, relaxed way.

words.tr:
v. 闲逛；散步；漫步；
n. 闲逛；散步；漫步；
words.ex: They stroll in the park after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他们晚饭后在公园里闲逛。
words.en: If you stroll somewhere, you walk there in a slow, relaxed way.

words.tr:
adj. 用柏油覆盖的
v. 耽搁；逗留
words.ex: The workers tarry at the road, waiting for the asphalt to dry.
words.ex_cn: 工人们在道路上耽搁，等着沥青变干。
words.en: To tarry means to stay longer than intended or to delay leaving a place.

words.tr:
v. 疲惫地行走；闲荡
n. 漫步；闲逛；疲惫地走
words.ex: They traipse through the mud to find the hidden path.
words.ex_cn: 他们踩着泥巴跋涉，寻找那条隐蔽的小路。
words.en: If you traipse somewhere, you go there unwillingly or with difficulty, often because you are tired or uninterested.

words.ex: He was arrested for vagrancy after sleeping on the street.
words.ex_cn: 他因在街上睡觉而因流浪罪被捕。
words.en: The state or condition of wandering from place to place without a home or job.

words.tr: v. 生长；植物似地生长；过单调呆板的生活
words.ex: The plants vegetate quickly in spring.
words.ex_cn: 这些植物在春天生长得很快。
words.en: To vegetate means to live in a monotonous, passive, or mentally inactive way; to grow or sprout as a plant does.

words.ex: The study found a causal link between smoking and lung cancer.
words.ex_cn: 这项研究发现了吸烟与肺癌之间的因果关系。
words.en: A causal factor or event is one that causes or leads to something else.

words.tr: adj. 不容置疑的；无可否认的
words.ex: The evidence is incontrovertible.
words.ex_cn: 证据是无可辩驳的。
words.en: If something is incontrovertible, it is definitely true and cannot be disputed.

words.ex: His genius is indubitable.
words.ex_cn: 他的天才是不容置疑的。
words.en: If you describe something as indubitable, you mean that it is definitely true.

words.tr: adj. 可辩解的；可证明为正当的；有理的
words.ex: His action was justifiable because he protected his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他的行为是合理的，因为他保护了他的朋友。
words.en: If something is justifiable, there is a good reason for it.

words.ex: He gave a justification for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他为迟到提供了一个正当的理由。
words.en: A justification for something is an acceptable reason or explanation for it.

words.tr: adj. 说得过去的；站得住脚的；可防守的
words.ex: His excuse was a little weak, but still tenable.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口有点牵强，但还是说得过去的。
words.en: If an idea, argument, or plan is tenable, it is reasonable and could be successfully defended against criticism.

words.ex: The evidence is undisputable.
words.ex_cn: 证据是无可争议的。
words.en: If you describe a fact or statement as undisputable, you mean that it is definitely true and cannot be doubted.

words.tr: adj. 无懈可击的；无可指责的
words.ex: Her performance was unexceptionable.
words.ex_cn: 她的表现无可挑剔。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as unexceptionable, you mean that they are unlikely to be criticized or objected to, because they are very good, standard, or normal.

words.tr: adj. 无懈可击的；无可指责的；可靠的
words.ex: His unimpeachable honesty earned everyone's trust.
words.ex_cn: 他无可挑剔的诚实赢得了每个人的信任。
words.en: If you describe someone as unimpeachable, you mean that they are completely honest and reliable.

words.tr: adj. 保证的； v. “warrant”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The repair was warranted by the store.
words.ex_cn: 这次维修由商店保证。
words.en: If something is warranted, there is a good reason for it and it can be accepted.

words.ex: The story has plausibility because it feels real.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事有合理性，因为它感觉真实。
words.en: The quality of seeming reasonable or probable.

words.ex: This is a commonplace event in big cities.
words.ex_cn: 这在大城市里是件普通的事。
words.en: Something that is commonplace is ordinary and not very interesting.

words.ex: The book uses demotic language to reach ordinary people.
words.ex_cn: 这本书使用通俗的语言来吸引普通人。
words.en: Relating to or denoting the form of a language used by ordinary people; vernacular.

words.ex: He follows the orthodox religious practices.
words.ex_cn: 他遵循正统的宗教习俗。
words.en: Orthodox beliefs, methods, or systems are ones which are accepted or used by most people.

words.ex: His performance was unexceptional.
words.ex_cn: 他的表现很平常。
words.en: If you describe something as unexceptional, you mean that it is ordinary, not very interesting, or not especially good.

words.ex: He suffered from asphyxia after breathing in smoke.
words.ex_cn: 他吸入烟雾后因窒息而受苦。
words.en: Asphyxia is a condition arising when the body is deprived of oxygen, causing unconsciousness or death; suffocation.

words.ex: Breathing deeply helps with respiration.
words.ex_cn: 深呼吸有助于呼吸。
words.en: The process of breathing, which involves inhaling oxygen and exhaling carbon dioxide.

words.ex: The accident caused strangulation.
words.ex_cn: 这次事故导致了窒息。
words.en: The act of killing someone by squeezing their throat so that they cannot breathe.

words.ex: The mechanic checked the throttle on the car engine.
words.ex_cn: 机械师检查了汽车发动机的节流阀。
words.en: To throttle someone means to kill or injure them by squeezing their throat or tightening something around it and preventing them from breathing. A throttle is a device that controls the amount of fuel going into an engine.

chapters.name: Word List 55 状态变化 变化

words.ex: He adapted to the new school quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他很快就适应了新学校。
words.en: To make suitable to or fit for a specific use or situation.

words.ex: Children are often adaptable to new environments.
words.ex_cn: 孩子通常能适应新环境。
words.en: If someone or something is adaptable, they are able to change their ideas or behaviour in order to deal with new situations.

words.ex: He will alter the plan tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会改动计划。
words.en: To alter something means to change it, usually slightly, or to cause the characteristics of something to change.

words.ex: The new policy will ameliorate living conditions.
words.ex_cn: 新政策将改善生活条件。
words.en: To make something better or improve a situation.

words.ex: He amended the letter before sending it.
words.ex_cn: 他在发送信件之前修正了它。
words.en: To amend something means to make changes to it in order to improve it or make it more accurate.

words.ex: He couldn't budge the heavy box.
words.ex_cn: 他无法让那个重箱子稍微移动一下。
words.en: If someone will not budge on a matter, or if nothing budges them, they refuse to change their mind or to come to an agreement.

words.tr: n. 反复无常；任性；怪想
words.ex: Her decision to quit the job was a sudden caprice.
words.ex_cn: 她决定辞职是突如其来的任性之举。
words.en: A sudden and unaccountable change of mood or behavior.

words.tr: adj. 变化无常的；任性的
words.ex: He is capricious and changes his mind every day.
words.ex_cn: 他喜怒无常，每天都会改变主意。
words.en: Someone who is capricious often changes their mind unexpectedly.

words.ex: The coach chastened the team for their poor performance.
words.ex_cn: 教练因球队表现不佳而惩罚了他们。
words.en: If you are chastened by something, it makes you regret that you have behaved badly or stupidly.

words.tr: adj. 分成方格的； v. “checker”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The table has a checkered cloth.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子上有块方格布。
words.en: Something that is checkered has a pattern of squares, usually of two different colors, or has had a lot of different experiences or events, often both good and bad.

words.ex: He drives a red convertible on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 他周末开一辆红色敞篷车。
words.en: A convertible is a car with a roof that can be folded down or removed.

words.ex: The weather will deteriorate tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天天气会恶化。
words.en: If something deteriorates, it becomes worse in some way.

words.ex: The school values diversity in its students.
words.ex_cn: 学校重视学生的多样性。
words.en: The state of being diverse; variety.

words.ex: He will emend the report tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会修改这份报告。
words.en: To emend something means to correct or improve it by changing it slightly.

words.ex: Exercise can enhance your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提高你的健康。
words.en: To enhance something means to improve its value, quality, or attractiveness.

words.tr: adj. 不稳定的；飘忽不定的；
words.ex: The weather has been erratic this month.
words.ex_cn: 这个月的天气一直不稳定。
words.en: Something that is erratic does not follow a regular pattern, but happens at unexpected times or moves in unexpected directions.

words.tr: adj. 易变的；无常的；感情不专的
words.ex: He is fickle and changes his mind every day.
words.ex_cn: 他善变，每天都会改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as fickle, you disapprove of them because they keep changing their mind about what they like or want.

words.ex: The price of oil fluctuates every day.
words.ex_cn: 油价每天都在波动。
words.en: To fluctuate means to change or vary frequently and unpredictably.

words.tr:
n. 流量；流动；变动
v. 熔化；熔解；流出
words.ex: The flux of water through the pipe is very high.
words.ex_cn: 管道中水的流量非常高。
words.en: Flux is a state of constant change or a flow of liquid.

words.ex: The fusion of music and technology creates new sounds.
words.ex_cn: 音乐与技术的融合创造了新的声音。
words.en: The process or result of joining two or more things together to form a single entity.

words.tr: v. 混淆；曲解；断章取义
words.ex: He garbled the message so no one understood it.
words.ex_cn: 他把消息说得乱七八糟，没人能听懂。
words.en: If you garble something, you distort or confuse it so that it is difficult to understand.

words.tr:
adj. 混乱不清的；引起误解的
v. 混淆；曲解；断章取义；“garble”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The phone call was garbled and hard to understand.
words.ex_cn: 电话声音杂乱，很难听清楚。
words.en: If something is garbled, it is confused and difficult to understand, often because it has been communicated in a way that is unclear or distorted.

words.ex: The pollution caused the degradation of the river.
words.ex_cn: 污染导致了河流的恶化。
words.en: The process by which something is reduced in quality, value, or status.

words.tr: n. 反复无常；不忠；不专一
words.ex: His inconstancy made her sad.
words.ex_cn: 他的不忠让她伤心。
words.en: The quality of being inconstant; lack of stability or uniformity.

words.ex: The company values innovation in its products.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司重视产品的创新。
words.en: Innovation is the introduction of new ideas, methods, or things.

words.tr: adj. 革新的；富有革新精神的；
words.ex: The company made an innovative phone.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司推出了一款革新的手机。
words.en: Something that is innovative is new and original, especially in the way that it is done.

words.tr: adj. 万花筒似的；千变万化的；五花八门的
words.ex: The kaleidoscopic lights made the room look magical.
words.ex_cn: 五彩缤纷的灯光让房间看起来像魔法一样。
words.en: If you describe something as kaleidoscopic, you mean that it consists of a lot of very different parts, such as different colors, patterns, or shapes.

words.ex: The clay is malleable and easy to shape.
words.ex_cn: 这种黏土是可塑的，容易塑形。
words.en: If you say that someone is malleable, you mean that they are easily influenced or controlled by other people.

words.ex: He will mend his broken shoe.
words.ex_cn: 他将修补他破掉的鞋子。
words.en: If you mend something that is broken or damaged, you repair it, so that it works properly or so that it looks like new again.

words.tr:
adj. 多汞的；含汞的；易变的；灵活的；反复无常的
n. 汞制剂；水银剂
words.ex: His mercurial mood changes from happy to angry quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他多汞的情绪很快从高兴变到生气。
words.en: If you describe someone as mercurial, you mean that they frequently change their mind or mood without warning.

words.ex: The caterpillar metamorphose into a butterfly.
words.ex_cn: 毛毛虫变成了蝴蝶。
words.en: To change completely in form or nature.

words.ex: He will modify the plan tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会更改计划。
words.en: To change something slightly, especially in order to make it more suitable for a particular purpose.

words.ex: He is working on optimization of the system.
words.ex_cn: 他正在改进系统的优化。
words.en: Optimization refers to the process of making something as good or as effective as possible.

words.tr: adj. 变化多端的；千变万化的
words.ex: He is protean in his interests, changing often.
words.ex_cn: 他对兴趣变化多端，经常改变。
words.en: Able to change frequently or easily; versatile.

words.tr: v. 撤回声明；放弃信仰
words.ex: He recanted his statement after seeing the evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他在看到证据后撤回了他的话。
words.en: If you recant, you say publicly that you no longer hold a set of beliefs that you had in the past.

words.tr: v. 重铸；改写；更换（演员）
words.ex: The director decided to recast the play with a different set of actors.
words.ex_cn: 导演决定用另一组演员重新排演这出戏。
words.en: To recast something means to change it by organizing it in a different way or presenting it in a different form.

words.tr: v. 要求归还；收回；开垦；感化
words.ex: He wants to reclaim his lost wallet.
words.ex_cn: 他想要要求归还他丢失的钱包。
words.en: If you reclaim something that you have lost or that has been taken away from you, you succeed in getting it back. If you reclaim land, you make it suitable for use, for example by draining it or by getting rid of unwanted buildings or plants.

words.ex: He will rectify the mistake tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会纠正这个错误。
words.en: If you rectify something that is wrong, you change it so that it becomes correct or satisfactory.

words.ex: The sign helped redirect the traffic away from the accident.
words.ex_cn: 这个标志帮助将车流改道，避开事故现场。
words.en: To direct something to a new or different place or purpose.

words.ex: The government must redress the unfair law.
words.ex_cn: 政府必须纠正这部不公平的法律。
words.en: If you redress something such as a wrong or a complaint, you do something to correct it or to improve things for the person who has been wronged.

words.tr:
v. 重新洗牌；改组
n. 改组；重新安排
words.ex: The coach will reshuffle the team for the next game.
words.ex_cn: 教练将为下一场比赛重新调整阵容。
words.en: to change the positions of people or things within a group, especially in order to improve the way it works

words.ex: He revised his answer to make it correct.
words.ex_cn: 他修正了他的答案，使其正确。
words.en: To revise something means to alter or amend it, especially in order to correct or improve it.

words.tr: v. 拨弄；玩弄；篡改；收买
words.ex: Don't tamper with the machine.
words.ex_cn: 不要拨弄这台机器。
words.en: If someone tampers with something, they interfere with it or make unauthorized changes to it, often in order to cause damage or make it work differently.

words.ex: The transition from school to work was hard for him.
words.ex_cn: 从学校到工作的转变对他来说很难。
words.en: The process or a period of changing from one state or condition to another.

words.ex: The wizard can transmute lead into gold.
words.ex_cn: 巫师可以把铅变成金子。
words.en: To change something completely, especially into something different and better.

words.ex: The storm caused an upheaval in the town.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴给小镇带来了混乱。
words.en: A very large change in something that often causes confusion or problems.

words.tr:
v. 改变方向；转向
n. 转向
words.ex: The car veers to the left when the driver turns too fast.
words.ex_cn: 当司机转得太快时，汽车会向左偏转。
words.en: If something veers in a certain direction, it suddenly changes direction and moves in that direction.

words.ex: Life is full of vicissitude.
words.ex_cn: 生活充满起伏。
words.en: A change of circumstances or fortune, typically one that is unwelcome or unpleasant.

words.ex: His life has been vicissitudinous, full of ups and downs.
words.ex_cn: 他的一生充满起伏，变幻无常。
words.en: Marked by or full of vicissitudes; subject to change or variation.

words.ex: The alcohol is volatile and evaporates quickly.
words.ex_cn: 酒精是易挥发的，会迅速蒸发。
words.en: A volatile situation or person is one that is likely to change suddenly and unexpectedly, especially by getting worse.

words.ex: He bought the car on a whim.
words.ex_cn: 他一时兴起买了这辆车。
words.en: A whim is a sudden desire or change of mind, especially one that is unusual or unexplained.

words.tr: adj. 异想天开的；古怪的；反复无常的
words.ex: The little girl wore a whimsical hat with flowers.
words.ex_cn: 小女孩戴着一顶带有花朵的古怪帽子。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as whimsical, you mean that they are unusual, playful, and unpredictable, often in a way that you find charming or amusing.

words.tr: n. 古怪行为；异想天开；怪念头
words.ex: His whimsy made him wear socks with sandals.
words.ex_cn: 他的古怪行为让他穿着袜子配凉鞋。
words.en: A whimsy is a sudden and arbitrary idea or desire, especially one that is unusual or fanciful.

words.ex: The loud music distract me from my homework.
words.ex_cn: 嘈杂的音乐让我无法专心做作业。
words.en: If something distracts you or your attention, it makes you stop concentrating on what you are doing.

words.ex: The two cultures have a lot of interchange.
words.ex_cn: 这两种文化有很多交流。
words.en: The act or process of exchanging things with each other, especially ideas or information.

words.ex: They will remodel their kitchen next month.
words.ex_cn: 他们下个月要重新装修厨房。
words.en: To remodel something means to change its structure or form, often to improve it.

words.tr: v. 重铸；改写；更换（演员）
words.ex: The director decided to recast the play with a different set of actors.
words.ex_cn: 导演决定用另一组演员重新排演这出戏。
words.en: To recast something means to change it by organizing it in a different way or presenting it in a different form.

words.tr: v. 调整；使适合；使适应；
words.ex: He adjusted the chair to sit comfortably.
words.ex_cn: 他调整了椅子以便坐得舒服。
words.en: To adjust something means to change it so that it is more effective or appropriate, or so that it fits better.

words.ex: I watched a clip of the movie on YouTube.
words.ex_cn: 我在YouTube上看了这部电影的一个片段。
words.en: A clip is a small device, usually made of metal or plastic, that is specially shaped for holding things together. As a verb, to clip means to cut something, especially to make it shorter or neater.

words.tr:
n. 通勤；
v. 通勤；
words.ex: His daily commute takes an hour by train.
words.ex_cn: 他每天的通勤坐火车要一个小时。
words.en: If you commute, you travel a long distance every day between your home and your place of work.

words.ex: The road was diverted around the park.
words.ex_cn: 这条路被改道绕过公园。
words.en: If you divert someone or something, you cause them to change direction or to go somewhere different.

words.tr: n. 屡教不改；难望矫正
words.ex: His incorrigibility made the teacher give up on him.
words.ex_cn: 他的不可救药让老师放弃了他。
words.en: The quality or state of being incorrigible, which means not able to be corrected or reformed.

words.ex: They will renovate the old house next month.
words.ex_cn: 他们下个月将翻新那栋老房子。
words.en: To renovate means to restore something to a good state of repair or to make it as good as new.

words.ex: He will restore the old bike.
words.ex_cn: 他将修复这辆旧自行车。
words.en: To restore something means to bring it back to its original condition or to a state of health, efficiency, or good management.

words.tr: v. 恢复；“restore”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 恢复的；复原的；
words.ex: The old house was restored to its original state.
words.ex_cn: 这座老房子被恢复到了原来的状态。
words.en: If something that has been lost or stolen is restored to its owner, it is returned to them.

words.ex: The restoration of the old house took two years.
words.ex_cn: 这座老房子的修复花了两年时间。
words.en: The act of returning something to its original condition, or the state of being returned to its original condition.

words.tr:
v. 使转轨；使分流；转向一边
n. 转轨；分流器
words.ex: The train was shunted to a side track.
words.ex_cn: 火车被调到了侧线。
words.en: If a train or a railway carriage is shunted, it is moved from one track to another, usually in order to make space for another train or carriage.

words.ex: She snip the paper with scissors.
words.ex_cn: 她用剪刀剪纸。
words.en: To cut something with scissors in a quick, small movement.

words.tr:
v. 突然转向；改变方向
n. 转向
words.ex: He swerved to avoid the dog.
words.ex_cn: 他为了避开狗而转向。
words.en: If a vehicle or other moving thing swerves, it suddenly changes direction, often in order to avoid hitting something.

words.ex: The contortion bent her body into a small box.
words.ex_cn: 这个柔术演员把身体弯进了一个小盒子里。
words.en: A contortion is a twisted or bent shape or position, often of the body.

words.ex: The loud music was a diversion from his worries.
words.ex_cn: 那嘈杂的音乐分散了他对烦恼的注意力。
words.en: A diversion is an action or event that attracts your attention away from what you are doing or should be doing.

words.ex: He reverted to his old habits after the holiday.
words.ex_cn: 假期后，他恢复了旧习惯。
words.en: To return to a former state, practice, topic, etc.

words.ex: Mom reassured me that everything would be fine.
words.ex_cn: 妈妈让我安心，一切都会好起来的。
words.en: If you reassure someone, you comfort them and stop them from worrying.

words.tr: v. 故态复萌；退步；再犯
words.ex: He backslid into old habits after quitting smoking.
words.ex_cn: 他戒烟后又回到了旧习惯。
words.en: To revert to bad habits or undesirable activities after a period of improvement.

words.tr: v. 恢复；修复；改造（罪犯）
words.ex: The hospital will rehabilitate the injured athlete.
words.ex_cn: 医院将帮助受伤的运动员康复。
words.en: To rehabilitate someone who has been ill or in prison means to help them to live a normal life again. To rehabilitate a building or an area means to improve its condition.

words.ex: The program offers rehabilitative care for injured workers.
words.ex_cn: 该项目为受伤工人提供康复护理。
words.en: Relating to or designed to promote rehabilitation.

words.ex: The company will reinstate his job next month.
words.ex_cn: 公司下个月将恢复他的工作。
words.en: If you reinstate someone, you give them back a job or position which had been taken away from them.

words.ex: He took a recuperative nap after the long walk.
words.ex_cn: 他走了很长的路后，小睡了一会儿来恢复。
words.en: If something is recuperative, it helps you to recover your health and strength after an illness or injury.

words.tr: v. 使年轻； 使恢复精神； 使复原
words.ex: The new sleep routine helps rejuvenate her energy.
words.ex_cn: 新的睡眠习惯帮助她恢复精力。
words.en: To rejuvenate someone or something means to make them look or feel young, fresh, or lively again.

words.ex: The renascent town began to grow again.
words.ex_cn: 这个复兴的小镇开始再次发展。
words.en: Experiencing a revival or renewal; being reborn.

words.ex: The resilient child bounced back quickly after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 这个适应力强的孩子在事故后很快恢复了。
words.en: Something that is resilient is strong and not easily damaged by being hit, stretched, or squeezed.

words.ex: The idea of a resurgence in national pride began to take hold.
words.ex_cn: 民族自豪感复兴的想法开始深入人心。
words.en: If something resurges, it becomes stronger or more popular again after a period of being weak or not popular.

words.ex: After the treatment, there was a reversion to his normal health.
words.ex_cn: 经过治疗后，他的健康恢复了正常。
words.en: The act of returning to a previous state or condition, especially in law, the return of an estate to the grantor or his heirs after the expiry of the grant.

words.ex: His curly hair and strong jaw are a throwback to his grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 他卷曲的头发和强壮的下巴是来自他祖父的返祖现象。
words.en: A throwback is something that is similar to something that existed or happened in the past.

words.ex: The wind began to abate after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 风暴过后，风开始减弱。
words.en: If something bad or undesirable abates, it becomes much less strong or severe.

words.ex: He abbreviates the word 'example' as 'ex.'.
words.ex_cn: 他把单词 'example' 缩写为 'ex.'。
words.en: To abbreviate something means to make it shorter, especially by using a particular word or phrase to represent it.

words.ex: The wind abrades the rock slowly.
words.ex_cn: 风慢慢磨损岩石。
words.en: To scrape or wear away by friction or erosion.

words.ex: The editor abridged the long story for children.
words.ex_cn: 编辑删节了这个长故事，以便适合儿童阅读。
words.en: To abridge a book, play, or other text means to make it shorter by leaving parts out.

words.ex: The school will curtail recess time during exams.
words.ex_cn: 学校在考试期间将缩短课间休息时间。
words.en: If you curtail something, you reduce or limit it.

words.tr:
adj. 潮湿的；减震的；压低（声音）的 
v. 使潮湿；“damp”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The damped clothes hung on the line all day.
words.ex_cn: 潮湿的衣服一整天都挂在晾衣绳上。
words.en: Reduced in amplitude or intensity by the presence of a damping material or device.

words.tr: v. 缓和；减弱（感觉）；降低（声音）
words.ex: The noise deadened after the door closed.
words.ex_cn: 门关上后，噪音减弱了。
words.en: If something deadens a feeling or a sound, it makes it less strong or loud.

words.ex: The illness debilitates him every winter.
words.ex_cn: 每年冬天，这场疾病都会使他虚弱。
words.en: To make someone weak and infirm.

words.tr:
n. 下降；衰退；
v. 下降；衰退；
words.ex: There was a sharp decline in sales last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月销售额大幅下降。
words.en: If something declines, it becomes less in quantity, importance, or strength.

words.ex: He deducts tax from his salary every month.
words.ex_cn: 他每月从工资中扣除税款。
words.en: If you deduct an amount from a total, you subtract it from the total.

words.ex: The music becomes softer with a diminuendo.
words.ex_cn: 音乐通过渐弱变得越来越轻柔。
words.en: A diminuendo is a gradual decrease in loudness in a piece of music.

words.ex: The ship arrived at the dock at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 船在日出时到达了码头。
words.en: A dock is an enclosed area of water in a port where ships go to be loaded, unloaded, and repaired.

words.ex: The water in the pond dwindles in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天时，池塘里的水逐渐减少。
words.en: If something dwindles, it becomes smaller, weaker, or less in number.

words.ex: The injury impaired his ability to walk.
words.ex_cn: 这次受伤损害了他走路的能力。
words.en: If something impairs something such as an ability or the way something works, it damages it or makes it worse.

words.ex: The old building will implode if the explosives go off.
words.ex_cn: 如果炸药引爆，这座旧楼会坍塌。
words.en: If something implodes, it collapses into itself in a sudden and violent way.

words.tr: v. 衰弱；凋萎；憔悴；受折磨
words.ex: The prisoner languishes in a dark cell.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯在黑暗的牢房中饱受煎熬。
words.en: If someone languishes somewhere, they are forced to remain and suffer in an unpleasant situation.

words.tr: v. 减到最少；使最小化；
words.ex: Try to minimize waste in the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 尽量减少厨房里的浪费。
words.en: To minimize something means to reduce it to the smallest possible amount or degree.

words.tr: v. 使声音降低；压抑（声音）；蒙住；裹
words.ex: He muffled his laugh with a pillow.
words.ex_cn: 他用枕头捂住笑声。
words.en: To muffle a sound is to make it quieter or less clear, often by covering it or wrapping it in something.

words.tr:
adj. 沉闷的；压抑的；模糊不清的
v. 使声音降低；压抑（声音）；蒙住；裹；“muffle”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The sound was muffled by the thick door.
words.ex_cn: 声音被厚门挡住了。
words.en: A muffled sound is not loud because it is blocked by something.

words.ex: He wore a wool muffler in winter.
words.ex_cn: 他在冬天戴了一条羊毛围巾。
words.en: A muffler is a piece of cloth worn around the neck for warmth or a device used to reduce the noise emitted by an engine.

words.tr: adj. 减弱的；变得轻柔的
words.ex: The muted sound came from the old TV.
words.ex_cn: 微弱的声音来自那台旧电视。
words.en: If something is muted, it is less intense or less noticeable than usual.

words.ex: He will pare the apple with a knife.
words.ex_cn: 他将用刀削苹果。
words.en: To pare something means to cut off its outer layer or to reduce its size or amount by cutting or trimming.

words.ex: He can permute the numbers to find a new pattern.
words.ex_cn: 他可以重新排列这些数字来找到一个新的模式。
words.en: To permute things means to change the order in which they are arranged.

words.tr: v. 发慈悲；动怜悯心；缓和
words.ex: The teacher finally relented and gave the students more time.
words.ex_cn: 老师终于发慈悲，给了学生们更多时间。
words.en: If you relent, you allow someone to do something that you had previously refused to allow them to do.

words.tr: v. 心软；缓和；“relent”的现在分词
words.ex: He kept asking, but she was not relenting.
words.ex_cn: 他一直请求，但她没有让步。
words.en: Becoming less severe or intense; softening in attitude or determination.

words.ex: The rain will retard the construction of the road.
words.ex_cn: 雨水会延迟道路的建设。
words.en: To retard something means to delay it or make it happen more slowly than it would otherwise.

words.ex: The company announced retrenchment to save money.
words.ex_cn: 公司宣布削减以节省资金。
words.en: The act of reducing costs or spending in order to become more financially stable.

words.ex: The police tried to subdue the angry man.
words.ex_cn: 警察试图制服那个愤怒的人。
words.en: To subdue someone or something means to bring them under control by using force or persuasion.

words.ex: Subtract 5 from 10 to get 5.
words.ex_cn: 从10中减去5得到5。
words.en: If you subtract one number from another, you take the first number away from the second.

words.tr: v. 逐渐变细；逐渐减少；
words.ex: The candle tapers toward the top.
words.ex_cn: 蜡烛向顶部逐渐变细。
words.en: A taper is a long thin candle or a gradual decrease in width or thickness.

words.ex: The software allows you to truncate long filenames.
words.ex_cn: 该软件允许你截断过长的文件名。
words.en: To shorten something by cutting off the top or the end.

words.tr: v. 轻描淡写；表演不充分
words.ex: He underplays his talent to avoid jealousy.
words.ex_cn: 他故意低估自己的才华，以避免引起嫉妒。
words.en: To represent something as being less important or significant than it really is.

words.tr: v. 使变质；损害；使失效
words.ex: The poison vitiated the water supply.
words.ex_cn: 这种毒物使水源变质。
words.en: To vitiate something means to impair or reduce the quality, value, or effectiveness of it.

words.tr:
v. 衰落；减弱；缺；亏
n. 衰退；减弱；缺；亏
words.ex: The moon begins to wane after the full moon.
words.ex_cn: 满月之后，月亮开始变暗。
words.en: If something wanes, it becomes gradually weaker or less, often so that it eventually disappears.

words.tr:
n. 垃圾；废物；浪费；
v. 浪费；白费；糟蹋；
adj. 荒芜的；废弃的；
words.ex: The children threw waste into the bin.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们把垃圾扔进了垃圾桶。
words.en: If you waste something such as time, money, or energy, you use too much of it doing something that is not important or necessary, or you do not use it in a sensible way.

words.ex: He whittled a small bird from wood.
words.ex_cn: 他用木头削出了一只小鸟。
words.en: To whittle means to cut or shape a piece of wood by repeatedly cutting small slices from it, or to reduce something in size, amount, or extent by a gradual series of steps.

words.ex: The noise will diminish after midnight.
words.ex_cn: 午夜后噪音会减少。
words.en: If something diminishes, or if something diminishes it, it becomes reduced in size, importance, or intensity.

words.ex: The car decelerate when it sees the red light.
words.ex_cn: 当汽车看到红灯时，它减速了。
words.en: If a vehicle or machine decelerates or if you decelerate it, it slows down.

words.tr:
v. 抑制；降低；减弱
n. （制革用的）软化剂
words.ex: The hawk bated its wings in anticipation.
words.ex_cn: 鹰在期待中鼓翅躁动。
words.en: To lessen the force or intensity of something; to restrain or hold back.

chapters.name: Word List 56 物理形态改变

words.tr: v. 使减细；使减小；使减弱
words.ex: The wire attenuates as it gets longer.
words.ex_cn: 这根电线随着变长而变细。
words.en: To reduce the force, effect, or value of something.

words.tr:
adj. 不锋利的；耿直的
v. 使变钝
words.ex: The knife is blunt and cannot cut paper.
words.ex_cn: 这把刀不锋利，切不动纸。
words.en: If you are blunt, you say exactly what you think without trying to be polite.

words.ex: He tried to loosen the tight screw.
words.ex_cn: 他试图拧松那颗紧的螺丝。
words.en: If you loosen something or if it loosens, it becomes less tight, less firmly fixed, or less strongly attached.

words.ex: The brewery uses fresh mash to make beer.
words.ex_cn: 酿酒厂使用新鲜的麦芽浆来酿造啤酒。
words.en: To crush or smash something into a soft, pulpy mass.

words.tr:
v. （使）成核
adj. 有核的
words.ex: Bubbles begin to nucleate when the water boils.
words.ex_cn: 当水沸腾时，气泡开始形成。
words.en: To form or cause to form a nucleus.

words.ex: They decided to prolong the meeting by one hour.
words.ex_cn: 他们决定将会议延长一小时。
words.en: To prolong something means to make it last longer.

words.ex: He tries to protract the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他试图延长会议。
words.en: To protract something means to make it last longer than usual or necessary, often in a way that is annoying or inconvenient.

words.ex: The artist elongated the figure to create a sense of grace.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家拉长了人物形象，以创造出一种优雅的感觉。
words.en: To elongate something means to make it longer, especially by stretching it.

words.ex: They will extend the deadline by one week.
words.ex_cn: 他们将截止日期延长一周。
words.en: To extend something means to make it longer or larger, or to spread it over a larger area.

words.tr: n. 女用小包；钱包；资金；
words.ex: She put her keys in her purse.
words.ex_cn: 她把钥匙放进她的女用小包里。
words.en: A purse is a small bag used especially by women to carry everyday personal items.

words.ex: The teacher will stratify the students by age.
words.ex_cn: 老师会按年龄将学生分层。
words.en: To arrange or form into layers or strata.

words.tr:
v. 伸展；延伸；持续；
n. 一段；伸展；
words.ex: He stretches his arms every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上伸展手臂。
words.en: To stretch is to extend your body or a part of your body to its full length, or to extend something else to its full length or beyond its normal limits.

words.ex: He unfolded the map on the table.
words.ex_cn: 他把地图在桌子上展开。
words.en: To open or spread out something that is folded; to develop or be revealed.

words.ex: The caterpillar's metamorphosis into a butterfly takes weeks.
words.ex_cn: 毛毛虫变成蝴蝶的变形需要几周时间。
words.en: Metamorphosis is a process of transformation from an immature form to an adult form in two or more distinct stages.

words.ex: The air rarefies at high altitudes.
words.ex_cn: 在高海拔地区，空气会变稀薄。
words.en: To make or become less dense or solid; to purify or refine.

words.ex: Sediments accrete on the ocean floor.
words.ex_cn: 沉积物在海底堆积。
words.en: To grow by accumulation or coalescence; to increase by external addition or growth.

words.tr: n. 自然增加；增加之物；增值
words.ex: The accretion of sand formed a small beach.
words.ex_cn: 沙子的堆积形成了一个小海滩。
words.en: Accretion is the process of growth or increase, typically by the gradual accumulation of additional layers or matter.

words.ex: The addition of a new chair made the room more comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 增加一把新椅子让房间更舒适了。
words.en: An addition is something that is added to something else, often to improve it or make it larger.

words.ex: The augmentation of data helps the model learn better.
words.ex_cn: 数据的增加帮助模型学得更好。
words.en: The act or process of making or becoming greater in size or amount.

words.tr: n. 气球；热气球；玩具气球；球状物；
words.ex: The child held a red balloon at the party.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在派对上拿着一个红色的气球。
words.en: A balloon is a small, thin, rubber bag that you blow air into so that it becomes larger and rounder or longer. Balloons are used as toys or decorations.

words.tr: n. 上升；改进；改善；进步
words.ex: The economy is showing an upswing after the recession.
words.ex_cn: 经济在衰退后出现了回升。
words.en: An upswing is a sudden or rapid improvement or increase in something.

words.tr:
n. 蜡；
v. 给…上蜡；
words.ex: Bees make wax to build their hives.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂用蜡建造蜂巢。
words.en: Wax is a solid, slightly shiny substance made of fat or oil that is used to make candles, polish, and other products. It can also refer to the process of applying wax to something or the natural substance found in the ear.

chapters.name: Word List 56 正向状态 自由

words.tr: adj. 自由自在的；无拘束的
words.ex: He is footloose after quitting his job.
words.ex_cn: 他辞掉工作后变得自由自在。
words.en: If you describe someone as footloose, you mean that they have no responsibilities or commitments, and are therefore free to do what they want and go where they want.

words.tr: adj. 散漫的；不连贯的；断续的
words.ex: He gave a desultory answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个漫无目的的回答。
words.en: Something that is desultory is done in an unplanned and disorganized way, and without enthusiasm.

words.tr: adj. 散漫的；不着边际的
words.ex: He gave a discursive speech about many topics.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一篇关于许多主题的散漫演讲。
words.en: If a style of writing or speech is discursive, it includes a lot of information that is not relevant to the main subject.

words.ex: He used to rove through the forests when he was young.
words.ex_cn: 他年轻时常常在森林里漫游。
words.en: To rove means to travel constantly without a fixed destination; wander.

words.tr: adj. 无原则的；无道德的；
words.ex: He is an unprincipled man who lies for money.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个为了钱就撒谎的无原则的人。
words.en: If you describe a person or their actions as unprincipled, you are criticizing them for their lack of moral principles and because they do things which are wrong or dishonest.

words.ex: He made an unscrupulous deal to save money.
words.ex_cn: 他为了省钱做了不道德的交易。
words.en: If you describe someone as unscrupulous, you are critical of them because they are prepared to act in a dishonest or immoral way in order to get what they want.

words.tr: adj. 无忧无虑的；轻松愉快的；
words.ex: The children played carefree in the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在公园里无忧无虑地玩耍。
words.en: If you are carefree, you have no worries or responsibilities, and you are happy and relaxed.

chapters.name: Word List 56 负向状态 不幸

words.ex: The earthquake was a catastrophe.
words.ex_cn: 这场地震是一场灾难。
words.en: An event causing great and often sudden damage or suffering; a disaster.

words.ex: The earthquake caused a big disaster.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了一场大灾难。
words.en: A disaster is an unexpected event causing great damage, destruction, or distress.

words.ex: The play ended in a tragedy when the hero died.
words.ex_cn: 当英雄去世时，这部戏剧以悲剧收场。
words.en: A tragedy is an extremely sad event or situation.

words.ex: The aftermath of the storm left many trees down.
words.ex_cn: 风暴过后，许多树被吹倒了。
words.en: The aftermath of an important event, especially a harmful one, is the situation that results from it.

words.ex: The movie shows an apocalyptic future after a big war.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影描绘了大战之后预示未来灾难的景象。
words.en: Relating to or predicting the end of the world, especially as described in the Bible.

words.tr:
n. 包；捆
v. 捆成大包
words.ex: He tied the hay into a bale.
words.ex_cn: 他把干草捆成一捆。
words.en: A bale is a large quantity of something such as hay, paper, wool, or cloth that has been tied tightly into a rectangular shape.

words.ex: The earthquake was a terrible calamity.
words.ex_cn: 这场地震是一场巨大的灾难。
words.en: A calamity is an event that causes great harm or damage, such as a flood or a fire.

words.ex: The earthquake was a sudden cataclysm.
words.ex_cn: 这场地震是一场突如其来的灾难。
words.en: A cataclysm is an event that causes great damage or makes a big change to something.

words.ex: His infelicitous remark made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他那不恰当的言论让所有人都感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe something as infelicitous, you mean that it is inappropriate or unsuitable in some way.

words.tr: n. 不恰当的言行；不幸
words.ex: The infelicity of his words made her sad.
words.ex_cn: 他话语的不妥让她感到难过。
words.en: The state or quality of being infelicitous; inappropriateness or unhappiness.

words.ex: The political situation in the country was like a maelstrom.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家的政治局势就像一个大漩涡。
words.en: A maelstrom is a powerful whirlpool in the sea or a river, or a situation in which there is great confusion, violence, and destruction.

words.tr: adj. 邪恶的；险恶的；不祥的
words.ex: The old house looked sinister in the moonlight.
words.ex_cn: 那座老房子在月光下显得阴森可怖。
words.en: Something that is sinister seems evil or harmful.

words.tr: adj. 命运不佳的；背运的
words.ex: They were a star-crossed couple who could never be together.
words.ex_cn: 他们是一对命运多舛的情侣，永远无法在一起。
words.en: If someone is described as star-crossed, they are considered to be unlucky because they seem to be doomed to failure or bad luck.

words.ex: The tribulations of war left many families devastated.
words.ex_cn: 战争的苦难使许多家庭陷入了绝望。
words.en: A tribulation is a cause of great trouble or suffering.

words.tr: adj. 不利的；麻烦的；异常的；意外的；棘手的
words.ex: He faced untoward remarks from his classmates.
words.ex_cn: 他遭到了同学的不友好的评论。
words.en: If you say that something is untoward, you mean that it is unexpected and causes difficulties.

words.ex: He set a tickler to remind him of the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他设置了一个提醒器来提醒自己参加会议。
words.en: A tickler is something that causes a light, often pleasurable sensation of being tickled, or a problem that is difficult to solve.

words.ex: He stayed strong through adversity.
words.ex_cn: 他在逆境中保持坚强。
words.en: Adversity refers to a difficult or unlucky situation or event.

words.ex: He lost his job, which was a great misfortune.
words.ex_cn: 他丢了工作，这是一场巨大的不幸。
words.en: An unfortunate condition or event.

words.tr: n. 不幸之事；灾祸；恶运
words.ex: He had a little mishap when he dropped his coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他不小心把咖啡洒了，出了点小差错。
words.en: A mishap is an unlucky accident.

chapters.name: Word List 56 负向状态 乏味

words.tr: adj. 沉闷乏味的；忧郁的；凄凉的
words.ex: The weather was dreary and rainy all day.
words.ex_cn: 天气一整天都阴沉沉的，还下着雨。
words.en: If you describe something as dreary, you mean that it is dull, lifeless, or depressing.

words.ex: The farmer used a drone to check his crops.
words.ex_cn: 农民用无人驾驶飞机检查他的庄稼。
words.en: A drone is a male bee that does not work and exists solely to mate with the queen bee. It can also refer to an unmanned aircraft or ship guided by remote control or onboard computers. Additionally, 'drone' can describe a continuous low humming sound or to speak in a monotonous tone.

words.ex: He grinds the coffee beans into powder.
words.ex_cn: 他把咖啡豆碾成粉末。
words.en: To reduce something to small particles or powder by crushing it.

words.ex: His daily routine is humdrum.
words.ex_cn: 他的日常生活很单调。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as humdrum, you mean that they are ordinary, dull, or boring.

words.tr: adj. 淡而无味的；枯燥乏味的
words.ex: The soup was insipid and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这汤淡而无味，很无聊。
words.en: If you describe food or drink as insipid, you mean that it is very weak, tasteless, or uninteresting.

words.tr: adj. 单调乏味的；毫无变化的；
words.ex: The work is monotonous and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作单调乏味。
words.en: Something that is monotonous is very boring because it has a regular, repeated pattern which never changes.

words.tr:
v. 唠叨；喋喋不休；不断困扰
n. 老马；驽马；矮小马
words.ex: She nagged him to clean his room.
words.ex_cn: 她不停地催他打扫房间。
words.en: If someone nags you, they keep asking you to do something you have not done yet or do not want to do.

words.tr: adj. 枯燥的；乏味的；平淡无奇的
words.ex: His prosaic speech bored everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他平淡无奇的演讲让所有人都感到无聊。
words.en: If you describe something as prosaic, you mean that it is ordinary and not at all interesting or unusual.

words.tr: adj. 难消化的，使人胀饱的；古板的；枯燥乏味的
words.ex: The stodgy pudding made him feel full and uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 这道难消化的布丁让他感到胀满不适。
words.en: If you describe something as stodgy, you mean that it is dull, boring, and rather formal.

words.tr: adj. 同义反复的；类语叠用的
words.ex: The statement was tautological and added no new information.
words.ex_cn: 这个陈述是同义反复的，没有提供新的信息。
words.en: If you describe something as tautological, you mean that it is a tautology or is like a tautology.

words.tr:
n. 媒介；方法；
adj. 中等的；适中的；
words.ex: TV is a popular medium for advertising.
words.ex_cn: 电视是一种流行的广告媒介。
words.en: A medium is a method or way of expressing something.

words.tr: adj. 乏味的；无味的；枯燥的
words.ex: The movie was vapid and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影乏味又无聊。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as vapid, you are criticizing them because they are dull and uninteresting.

words.ex: The aridity of the desert makes it hard for plants to grow.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠的干旱使植物难以生长。
words.en: Aridity is the state of being extremely dry, especially due to lack of rainfall.

words.tr:
adj. 老牛拖破车似的；沉重缓慢的
v. 艰难地行走；吃力地行进；“plod”的现在分词
words.ex: The plodding pace of the lecture made it difficult to stay focused.
words.ex_cn: 单调乏味的讲座节奏让人难以集中注意力。
words.en: Moving or progressing slowly and laboriously.

words.tr: n. 困倦；昏昏欲睡；嗜睡
words.ex: After taking the medication, she experienced a deep state of somnolence.
words.ex_cn: 服用药物后，她进入了深深的困倦状态。
words.en: Somnolence is a state of near-sleep, a strong desire for sleep, or sleeping for unusually long periods.

chapters.name: Word List 56 负向状态 尴尬

words.tr: v. 使羞惭；使不安；使窘迫
words.ex: He was abashed when he forgot his lines.
words.ex_cn: 当他忘记台词时，他感到尴尬。
words.en: If someone is abashed, they feel embarrassed and ashamed.

words.tr: adj. 腼腆的；怕羞的；忸怩的
words.ex: She gave a coy smile when asked about her new boyfriend.
words.ex_cn: 当被问及她的新男友时，她露出了腼腆的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as coy, you mean they are pretending to be shy about something in order to attract attention or to deceive people.

words.ex: His discomfiture was evident as he tried to explain his actions.
words.ex_cn: 他试图解释自己的行为时，显得十分狼狈。
words.en: A feeling of unease or embarrassment.

words.ex: He embarrassed himself in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他在全班同学面前让自己丢脸了。
words.en: If you embarrass someone, you make them feel shy, ashamed, or guilty about something.

chapters.name: Word List 56 负向状态 枯燥

words.ex: The aridness of the desert makes it difficult for plants to grow.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠的干燥使得植物难以生长。
words.en: The state or quality of being extremely dry, especially of the climate or land.

words.ex: The insipidity of the dish was a disappointment to the guests.
words.ex_cn: 这道菜的清淡无味让客人们感到失望。
words.en: The quality of being insipid; lack of flavor, interest, or excitement.

words.tr: adj. 无聊的；令人厌倦的； v. “bore”的现在分词；
words.ex: The movie was boring.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影很无聊。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as boring, you mean that they are not interesting and make you feel tired or impatient.

words.ex: The movie had a corny plot that felt outdated.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影有一个感觉过时的陈腐情节。
words.en: If you describe something as corny, you mean that it is sentimental or old-fashioned, and therefore not very interesting or original.

words.ex: The walls were painted a drab color.
words.ex_cn: 墙壁被刷成了土褐色。
words.en: If you describe something as drab, you think that it is dull and boring to look at or experience.

words.ex: He feels ennui while doing the same job every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天做同样的工作时感到厌倦。
words.en: A feeling of listlessness and dissatisfaction arising from a lack of occupation or excitement.

words.tr: adj. 无精打采的；萎靡的；懒洋洋的；不热心的
words.ex: She approached the task with a lackadaisical attitude.
words.ex_cn: 她以一种无精打采的态度来处理这项任务。
words.en: If you say that someone is lackadaisical, you mean that they are rather lazy and do not show much interest or enthusiasm in what they do.

words.tr:
n. （发声）单调
adj. 单调的
words.ex: He spoke in a monotone voice.
words.ex_cn: 他用单调的声音说话。
words.en: A monotone sound or voice does not change in pitch and is therefore considered boring or uninteresting.

words.tr: n. 单调；枯燥；千篇一律
words.ex: He felt bored because of the monotony of his daily work.
words.ex_cn: 他因为日常工作的单调而感到无聊。
words.en: If you refer to the monotony of something, you are criticizing it because it is boring and has no variety.

chapters.name: Word List 56 负向状态 虚弱

words.ex: His debility was due to a long illness.
words.ex_cn: 他的虚弱是由于长期患病。
words.en: Debility is a state of physical weakness, especially as a result of illness.

words.tr: v. 使衰弱；使虚弱；“debilitate”的现在分词；
words.ex: The illness was debilitating her strength.
words.ex_cn: 这场疾病正在使她的体力衰弱。
words.en: If you say that a disease or condition is debilitating, you mean that it makes people physically or mentally weak.

words.tr: adj. 衰弱的；衰败的；软弱的
words.ex: The old king was effete and could not lead.
words.ex_cn: 这位老国王虚弱无能，无法领导。
words.en: No longer productive or effective; lacking the power or will to achieve or succeed.

words.ex: The illness had enfeebled her to the point of immobility.
words.ex_cn: 疾病使她衰弱到几乎不能动弹的地步。
words.en: To make someone or something very weak.

words.tr: adj. 虚弱的；衰弱的；无力的；
words.ex: The old man gave a feeble smile.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人露出虚弱的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as feeble, you mean that they are weak.

words.tr: v. 用旗标记；“flag”的现在分词；
words.ex: They were flagging the trail with colorful flags.
words.ex_cn: 他们用彩色旗帜标记了小径。
words.en: If something is flagging, it is becoming tired or less active or lively.

words.ex: The old man is infirm and needs help to walk.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人身体虚弱，需要帮助才能走路。
words.en: If someone is infirm, they are weak or ill, and often old.

words.tr: n. 身体不适；不快；萎靡不振；痼疾
words.ex: She felt a general malaise after the long flight.
words.ex_cn: 长途飞行后，她感到全身不适。
words.en: A general feeling of discomfort, illness, or unease whose exact cause is difficult to identify.

chapters.name: Word List 56 负向状态 阴郁

words.ex: The basement was dank and cold.
words.ex_cn: 地下室又潮又冷。
words.en: Unpleasantly damp and cold.

words.tr: adj. 绝望的；孤立无助的；被弃置的
words.ex: The forlorn dog sat by the door, waiting for its owner.
words.ex_cn: 那条孤单的狗坐在门边，等待它的主人。
words.en: If someone is forlorn, they feel alone and unhappy.

words.ex: He enjoys solitude in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在森林中独处。
words.en: The state or situation of being alone.

words.tr:
v. 痛哭；嚎啕；尖叫
n. 痛哭；哀号；尖啸
words.ex: The baby wails when she is hungry.
words.ex_cn: 当宝宝饿的时候，她会哭喊。
words.en: To wail means to make a long, high cry, usually because you are in pain or very sad.

words.ex: His whine about the food made everyone annoyed.
words.ex_cn: 他对食物的抱怨让所有人都感到厌烦。
words.en: If someone or something whines, they make a long, high-pitched noise, especially one which sounds sad or unpleasant.

words.tr: adj. 扭曲的；弯曲的；复杂的
words.ex: The twistful road made driving difficult.
words.ex_cn: 这条弯曲的道路让驾驶变得困难。
words.en: Characterized by twists or turns; winding.

words.tr: n. 喜怒无常；情绪化；闷闷不乐
words.ex: His moodiness makes it hard to talk to him.
words.ex_cn: 他的情绪化让他很难相处。
words.en: The state of being moody; frequent changes in mood.

words.tr: adj.  忧郁的；阴沉的；阴暗的
words.ex: The room had a somber mood.
words.ex_cn: 房间里有一种阴郁的气氛。
words.en: If someone is somber, they are serious or sad.

words.tr: adj. 忧郁的；郁郁不乐的
words.ex: He sat disconsolate after losing his dog.
words.ex_cn: 失去狗后，他悲伤地坐着。
words.en: If someone is disconsolate, they are very unhappy and cannot be comforted.

chapters.name: Word List 56 负向行为 犯罪

words.ex: The country will extradite the suspect to Canada.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家将把嫌疑人引渡到加拿大。
words.en: If someone is extradited, they are officially sent back to their own or another country to be tried for a crime that they have been accused of.

words.tr: v. 遣送回国；调回国内；
words.ex: The government decided to repatriate the refugees.
words.ex_cn: 政府决定将难民遣送回国。
words.en: To repatriate someone means to send or bring them back to their own country.

words.tr: adj. 适当的；合适的；恰当的；
words.ex: This dress is appropriate for a wedding.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子适合参加婚礼。
words.en: Something that is appropriate is suitable or acceptable for a particular situation.

words.ex: He tried to bribe the officer with money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用钱贿赂官员。
words.en: A bribe is a sum of money or something valuable that one person offers or gives to another in order to persuade them to do something, usually something dishonest.

words.tr: n. 违禁品；禁运品；走私货
words.ex: The police seized a large amount of contraband in the raid.
words.ex_cn: 警方在突击搜查中查获了大量走私货。
words.en: Goods that are illegally imported or exported.

words.tr: v. 盗用公款；挪用公款
words.ex: He did defalcate money from the company.
words.ex_cn: 他从公司挪用了资金。
words.en: To defalcate means to embezzle or misappropriate funds that one has been entrusted with.

words.ex: He was jailed for embezzlement from his company.
words.ex_cn: 他因盗用公司公款而入狱。
words.en: Embezzlement is the act of dishonestly taking or using money that belongs to someone else, especially when it is in your care or belongs to the organization you work for.

words.tr: v. 偷（尤指小的或不贵重的物品）
words.ex: He managed to filch a few apples from the market.
words.ex_cn: 他设法从市场上偷了几个苹果。
words.en: To steal something, especially something of little value or in a sneaky manner.

words.ex: He speculates that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他推测明天会下雨。
words.en: If you speculate about something, you make guesses about its nature or identity, or about what might happen.

words.tr: v. 小偷小摸；偷窃（小东西）
words.ex: He was caught pilfering from the store.
words.ex_cn: 他因在商店里小偷小摸被抓。
words.en: To pilfer means to steal things of little value or in small quantities, often in a stealthy way.

words.ex: He plagiarized the essay from the internet.
words.ex_cn: 他从网上抄袭了这篇论文。
words.en: To plagiarize means to use someone else's ideas or work and pretend that it is your own.

words.ex: He was accused of poaching ideas from his colleague.
words.ex_cn: 他被指控盗用同事的想法。
words.en: To poach means to illegally hunt or catch animals or fish, or to cook something such as an egg without its shell in or over boiling water.

words.ex: He was accused of purloining company funds.
words.ex_cn: 他被指控偷窃公司资金。
words.en: To purloin means to steal something, especially in a sneaky or stealthy manner.

words.ex: The old west was full of rustlers stealing cattle.
words.ex_cn: 旧西部到处都是偷牛的偷马贼。
words.en: A rustler is someone who steals cattle.

words.ex: He tried to shoplift a shirt from the store.
words.ex_cn: 他试图从商店偷一件衬衫。
words.en: To steal goods from a shop while pretending to be a customer.

words.tr:
v. 告密；告发；偷窃
n. 告密者；告发者
words.ex: He was caught snitching money from the register.
words.ex_cn: 他因从收银机里偷钱被抓了。
words.en: To snitch means to secretly tell someone in authority that someone else has done something wrong, often in order to cause trouble for them. It can also mean to steal something, especially something small or not very valuable.

words.ex: He committed a transgression by stealing the money.
words.ex_cn: 他偷钱犯了过错。
words.en: A transgression is an act that goes against a law, rule, or code of conduct; an offense.

words.tr: n. 轻罪；品行不端；轻刑罪
words.ex: He committed a misdemeanor by parking illegally.
words.ex_cn: 他因非法停车而犯下轻罪。
words.en: A misdemeanor is a less serious crime than a felony, punishable by less than a year of imprisonment.

words.ex: The country agreed to extradition of the suspect.
words.ex_cn: 该国同意引渡这名嫌疑人。
words.en: The act of officially sending someone back to their own country to be tried for a crime that they have been accused of in another country.

words.tr: n. 海盗；不择手段的投机者；冒险家
words.ex: The buccaneer's ship was heavily armed.
words.ex_cn: 那名海盗的船装备精良。
words.en: A buccaneer is a person who sails the seas attacking and robbing ships, especially in the 17th and 18th centuries.

words.ex: He bought a luxury car as an extravagance.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一辆豪华汽车作为奢侈品。
words.en: Extravagance refers to the spending of more money than is reasonable or than you can afford, or the use of more of something than is necessary.

words.tr: n. 奢华；奢侈品；难得的享受；
words.ex: She bought a luxury dress for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对买了一件奢华的裙子。
words.en: Luxury is very great comfort, especially among beautiful and expensive surroundings.

words.ex: The hotel has a plush lobby with velvet chairs.
words.ex_cn: 这家酒店有一个豪华的大堂，配有丝绒椅子。
words.en: Plush refers to something that is luxurious and expensive, or a type of fabric that is very soft and thick.

words.tr: adj. 大量的；不吝惜的；浪费的
words.ex: He was profuse in thanks after the rescue.
words.ex_cn: 获救后，他表达了深深的感谢。
words.en: If you describe something as profuse, you mean that it is very plentiful or abundant.

words.tr:
adj. 挥霍的；丰富的；慷慨的；不吝惜的
n. 浪子
words.ex: The prodigal son returned home after years.
words.ex_cn: 那个浪子多年后回到了家。
words.en: A prodigal person spends money or resources in a way that is not careful and is too generous.

words.tr: n. 放荡；不检点；肆意挥霍
words.ex: His profligacy led to the loss of all his money.
words.ex_cn: 他的放荡导致他失去了所有的钱。
words.en: Profligacy refers to reckless extravagance or wastefulness in the use of resources, or to licentiousness or dissoluteness in behavior.

words.tr:
n. 挥霍；乱花钱；糟蹋钱
v. 挥霍；乱花（钱）；糟蹋（钱）
words.ex: He made a splurge on a new car.
words.ex_cn: 他花大钱买了一辆新车。
words.en: If you splurge on something, you spend a lot of money on it, often more than you can afford or more than is necessary.

words.ex: He squandered all his money on games.
words.ex_cn: 他把所有的钱都浪费在游戏上了。
words.en: If you squander money, resources, or opportunities, you waste them in a foolish or careless way.

words.ex: The king ate a sumptuous meal in his palace.
words.ex_cn: 国王在他的宫殿里享用了一顿丰盛的饭菜。
words.en: Something that is sumptuous is very impressive and expensive, especially in a way that involves large amounts of money.

words.ex: The police confiscate illegal drugs.
words.ex_cn: 警察没收非法毒品。
words.en: If you confiscate something from someone, you take it away from them, usually as a punishment.

words.ex: The government will expropriate the land for the new road.
words.ex_cn: 政府将征用这块土地用于新建道路。
words.en: If a government or other authority expropriates someone's property, they take it away from them for public use or benefit.

words.tr:
n. 没收物；罚金
v. 丧失；被没收
words.ex: He had to pay a forfeit for breaking the rule.
words.ex_cn: 他因违反规定不得不支付没收物。
words.en: If you forfeit something, you lose it or are forced to give it up because you have broken a rule or done something wrong.

words.ex: The court sequestrated the debtor's assets to repay the creditors.
words.ex_cn: 法院扣押了债务人的资产以偿还债权人。
words.en: To sequestrate means to take temporary possession of someone's property until they have paid what they owe or until a legal dispute has been resolved.

words.ex: The storm deprived us of electricity.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴剥夺了我们的电力。
words.en: If you deprive someone of something that they want or need, you take it away from them, or you prevent them from having it.

words.tr: v. 使失去勇气；使身心交疲；使气馁
words.ex: The loud noise unnerves her.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让她心神不宁。
words.en: If something unnerves you, it makes you feel worried or uncomfortable.

words.tr: v. 消灭；歼灭；彻底击败
words.ex: The bomb will annihilate the building.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹会摧毁那栋大楼。
words.en: To annihilate something means to destroy it completely.

words.tr: v. 非法霸占；僭越；盗用
words.ex: He arrogated the right to make decisions without consulting the team.
words.ex_cn: 他擅自决定，未经团队商议。
words.en: To claim or seize without justification; to assume or appropriate to oneself without right.

words.ex: The storm bereaved the village of its power.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴使村庄失去了电力。
words.en: To deprive someone of a loved one through death.

words.tr:
adj. 被剥夺的；丧失的；失去亲人的
v. 夺去；使丧失；“bereave”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He was bereft of words after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他一句话也说不出来。
words.en: If someone is bereft of something, they have lost it and feel its loss keenly.

words.ex: Wear a helmet to counteract the risk of head injury.
words.ex_cn: 戴头盔以对抗头部受伤的风险。
words.en: If you counteract something, you reduce its effect by doing something that produces an opposite effect.

words.tr: v. 滥伐…的森林；乱砍…的树木
words.ex: They deforest the land to build houses.
words.ex_cn: 他们砍伐森林来建造房屋。
words.en: To deforest means to remove the trees from an area of land.

words.tr: n. 采伐森林；森林开伐；
words.ex: Deforestation is killing many animals.
words.ex_cn: 采伐森林正在杀死许多动物。
words.en: The act of cutting down or burning all the trees in an area.

words.ex: The storm denuded the trees of their leaves.
words.ex_cn: 风暴把树上的叶子都刮掉了。
words.en: To strip something of its covering, possessions, or assets; to make bare.

words.ex: The depredation of forests harms wildlife.
words.ex_cn: 森林的破坏危害了野生动物。
words.en: The act of preying upon or plundering; the act of laying waste; as, the depredations of an army on the country.

words.ex: The prisoners suffered from sleep deprivation.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯们因睡眠剥夺而受苦。
words.en: Deprivation is the lack or denial of something considered to be a necessity.

words.ex: The government's policy aimed to deracinate the rebel group.
words.ex_cn: 政府的政策旨在根除叛乱组织。
words.en: To deracinate someone or something means to remove them from their natural environment or culture, especially in a way that causes them to lose their identity or characteristics.

words.tr: v. 抢劫；掠夺；蹂躏；破坏
words.ex: The invaders despoiled the village.
words.ex_cn: 入侵者抢劫了村庄。
words.en: To despoil something means to steal from it or damage it, especially in a violent or destructive way.

words.ex: The new law disfranchised many citizens.
words.ex_cn: 新法律剥夺了许多公民的选举权。
words.en: To deprive someone of a privilege, right, or power, especially the right to vote.

words.ex: The cows graze in the enclosure.
words.ex_cn: 奶牛在围场里吃草。
words.en: An enclosure is an area that is surrounded by a barrier or fence, often used to keep animals in or to protect something.

words.tr: v. 侵入；侵占；侵犯；侵蚀
words.ex: The new building encroaches on the park.
words.ex_cn: 新建筑侵占了公园。
words.en: To gradually take something such as power or authority from someone else, often in a way that is not fair or legal.

words.ex: The farmer tried to exterminate the rats.
words.ex_cn: 农夫试图消灭老鼠。
words.en: To exterminate means to kill all the members of a group of people or animals, or to destroy something completely.

words.tr: adj. 灭绝的；熄灭的；绝种的；
words.ex: The dodo is an extinct bird.
words.ex_cn: 渡渡鸟是一种灭绝的鸟。
words.en: If a species of animals or plants is extinct, it no longer has any living members, either in the world or in a particular place.

words.ex: The government's goal is the extirpation of poverty in the region.
words.ex_cn: 政府的目的是在该地区消灭贫困。
words.en: The act of completely destroying or getting rid of something.

words.tr: adj. 不可剥夺（或分割）的
words.ex: Freedom is an inalienable right.
words.ex_cn: 自由是不可剥夺的权利。
words.en: An inalienable right or quality is one that cannot be taken away from you.

words.tr: adj. 不能根除的；根深蒂固的
words.ex: The pain of loss is irradicable.
words.ex_cn: 失去的痛苦是无法根除的。
words.en: If something is irradicable, it is impossible to remove or destroy.

words.tr: n. 重型卡车；不可抗拒的强大力量；无法控制的强大机构；使人盲目牺牲（或崇拜）的事物
words.ex: The juggernaut rolled down the highway, carrying heavy cargo.
words.ex_cn: 这辆重型卡车沿着高速公路行驶，载着沉重的货物。
words.en: A juggernaut is something or someone that is extremely large, powerful, and unstoppable.

words.tr:
v. 抢劫；掠夺
n. 袭击
words.ex: The soldiers marauded through the village, taking whatever they wanted.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在村庄里四处掠夺，拿走了他们想要的一切。
words.en: To maraud means to roam around in search of things to steal or people to attack.

words.ex: The big company tries to monopolize the market.
words.ex_cn: 这家大公司试图垄断市场。
words.en: If a company or person monopolizes something, they have complete control over it, so that other people cannot share it.

words.ex: He has a monopoly on selling ice cream in this town.
words.ex_cn: 他在这座小镇上垄断了冰淇淋的销售。
words.en: If a company, person, or state has a monopoly on something such as an industry, they have complete control over it, so that it is impossible for others to become involved in it.

words.ex: The occupation of the city by foreign troops lasted for years.
words.ex_cn: 外国军队对这座城市的占领持续了多年。
words.en: An occupation is a job or profession, or a way of spending your time.

words.tr:
n. 掠夺；抢劫；掠夺物
v. 抢劫；掠夺
words.ex: The soldiers committed pillage after winning the battle.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在赢得战斗后进行了掠夺。
words.en: If a group of people pillage a place, they steal a lot of things from it and often cause a lot of damage, especially in a war.

words.tr:
v. 掠夺；抢劫
n. 掠夺物；掠夺；赃物
words.ex: The pirates plundered the ship.
words.ex_cn: 海盗劫掠了那艘船。
words.en: If someone plunders a place or plunders things from a place, they steal things from it.

words.tr: adj. 贪婪的；贪得无厌的；劫掠的
words.ex: The rapacious wolf ate all the food.
words.ex_cn: 贪婪的狼吃掉了所有食物。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as rapacious, you disapprove of their greedy or selfish behaviour.

words.ex: The woman was ravished by a stranger.
words.ex_cn: 这名女子被一名陌生人强奸了。
words.en: If you are ravished by something, you are filled with delight and wonder by it.

words.tr:
n. 袋子；
v. 劫掠；
words.ex: He carried the apples in a burlap sack.
words.ex_cn: 他把苹果装在一个麻布袋里。
words.en: A sack is a large bag made of rough woven material, used for storing or carrying goods. It can also refer to the act of dismissing someone from employment or the act of looting a place.

words.ex: There was a scramble for the last ticket.
words.ex_cn: 大家争相抢购最后一张票。
words.en: If you scramble over rocks or up a hill, you move quickly over them or up it using your hands to help you. Scramble can also mean to compete or struggle with others for something that is in short supply.

words.ex: The new policy undercut the company's profits.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策削弱了公司的利润。
words.en: To undercut means to sell something at a lower price than a competitor, or to weaken something or someone.

words.tr: v. 脱去…的法衣；免去…的圣职
words.ex: The priest was unfrocked for his misconduct.
words.ex_cn: 这位牧师因行为不端而被解除僧职。
words.en: To remove someone from their position as a priest or minister, especially as a punishment.

words.ex: He tried to usurp the throne from his brother.
words.ex_cn: 他试图从他兄弟手中篡夺王位。
words.en: If you say that someone usurps a job, role, title, or position, they take it from someone when they have no right to do this.

words.tr: v. 剥夺…的权利（尤指选举权）
words.ex: The law disenfranchises many poor people.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律剥夺了许多穷人的投票权。
words.en: To disenfranchise someone means to take away their right to vote or to deprive them of a privilege or a right.

words.ex: He embezzled money from his company.
words.ex_cn: 他从公司贪污了钱。
words.en: To embezzle means to steal or misappropriate money placed in one's trust or belonging to one's employer.

words.ex: The encroachment of the desert is destroying farmland.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠的侵蚀正在摧毁农田。
words.en: Encroachment refers to the act of gradually taking something, especially someone else's rights or property, without permission.

words.tr: n. 飞地；被包围的领土
words.ex: The village is an enclave surrounded by forest.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄是一个被森林包围的飞地。
words.en: An enclave is a part of a country or a group of people that is surrounded by another country or group of people.

words.ex: She showed great affection for her little dog.
words.ex_cn: 她对她的小狗非常钟爱。
words.en: A feeling of liking and caring for someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 讨厌的（小孩）；被惯坏的；不懂事的；无礼的
words.ex: His brattish behavior annoyed everyone at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他那被惯坏的行为让聚会上的每个人都感到讨厌。
words.en: If you describe someone, especially a child, as brattish, you mean that they are badly behaved in a way that is typical of a spoilt child.

words.ex: She coddles her little brother too much.
words.ex_cn: 她太宠着她的弟弟了。
words.en: To treat someone in an indulgent or overprotective way.

words.tr:
v. 宠爱；娇养；纵容
n. 宠儿
words.ex: She cosseted her baby with soft blankets and gentle songs.
words.ex_cn: 她用柔软的毯子和轻柔的歌声呵护她的婴儿。
words.en: To cosset someone means to treat them with great care and attention, often in a way that is excessive or indulgent.

words.tr:
adj. 溺爱的；宠爱的
v. 溺爱；宠爱；过分喜爱；“dote”的现在分词
words.ex: Her doting parents always buy her toys.
words.ex_cn: 她溺爱的父母总是给她买玩具。
words.en: If you say that someone is, for example, a doting mother, husband, or friend, you mean that they show a lot of love for someone.

words.tr:
adj. 倾心的；被迷住的
v. 迷住；使迷恋；“enamor”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He was enamored with the idea of traveling the world.
words.ex_cn: 他迷恋上了环游世界的想法。
words.en: If you are enamored of something or someone, you are very fond of them or very interested in them.

words.tr: adj. 慈善的；乐善好施的；
words.ex: He made a philanthropic donation to help poor children.
words.ex_cn: 他捐赠了一笔慈善款项来帮助贫困儿童。
words.en: A philanthropic person or organization freely gives money or other help to people who need it.

words.ex: The beach is unspoiled and clean.
words.ex_cn: 这片海滩未被破坏，很干净。
words.en: If you describe a place as unspoiled, you think it is beautiful because it has not been changed or built on for a long time.

words.tr: adj. 过分宠爱妻子的；怕老婆的
words.ex: He was known for his uxorious nature, always putting his wife's needs before his own.
words.ex_cn: 他以怕老婆著称，总是把妻子的需求放在自己的需求之前。
words.en: If you describe a man as uxorious, you mean that he is extremely fond of his wife and shows it in his behavior towards her.

words.ex: He tried to bamboozle me with his elaborate story.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用他精心编造的故事来欺骗我。
words.en: To deceive or trick someone, often in a playful or mischievous manner.

words.tr: v. 诱骗；消遣；迷住；消磨
words.ex: He beguiles her with sweet words.
words.ex_cn: 他用甜言蜜语哄骗她。
words.en: If someone beguiles you, they charm you in a way that makes you trust them or like them, often so that they can deceive you.

words.tr: v. 以甜言蜜语哄骗；勾引
words.ex: He tried to cajole his sister into lending him money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图哄骗妹妹把钱借给他。
words.en: If you cajole someone into doing something, you persuade them to do it by flattery or by making promises.

words.ex: The story was a complete canard, spread by those with vested interests.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事完全是一个谣言，是由那些有既得利益的人散布的。
words.en: A canard is a false or baseless story or piece of information, especially one that is deliberately misleading.

words.tr:
n. 凿子
v. 雕；凿；欺骗
words.ex: He used a chisel to carve the stone.
