words.ex_cn: 他用凿子雕刻石头。
words.en: A chisel is a tool with a long metal blade which has a sharp edge for cutting wood, stone, or metal.

words.tr: v. 哄；用好话劝诱；哄骗
words.ex: He tried to coax the cat out from under the bed.
words.ex_cn: 他试图哄猫从床底下出来。
words.en: To coax someone means to persuade them to do something by gentle persuasion or flattery.

words.ex: He cozens his friend into lending him money.
words.ex_cn: 他哄骗朋友借给他钱。
words.en: To deceive or trick someone.

words.ex: His deceit made his friends lose trust in him.
words.ex_cn: 他的欺骗让朋友们失去了对他的信任。
words.en: Deceit is behaviour that is intended to make someone believe something that is not true.

words.ex: His deception fooled everyone at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他的欺骗骗过了派对上的所有人。
words.en: Deception is the act of deceiving someone or the state of being deceived.

words.tr:
n. 诱饵；（诱捕鸟兽的）动物
v. 引诱
words.ex: The hunter used a decoy to attract ducks.
words.ex_cn: 猎人用假鸭子来吸引鸭子。
words.en: A decoy is a person, thing, or action that is used to trick someone into doing something or going somewhere, especially by making them think they are going to get something they want.

words.ex: He tried to defraud the bank with a fake check.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用一张假支票诈骗银行。
words.en: If someone defrauds you, they take something away from you or stop you from getting what is rightfully yours by deceiving you.

words.ex: He deluded himself into thinking he would win.
words.ex_cn: 他欺骗自己，以为自己会赢。
words.en: If you delude yourself, you let yourself believe that something is true, even though it is not true.

words.ex: He has a delusion that he is a famous singer.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种错觉，认为自己是一位著名歌手。
words.en: A delusion is a belief or impression that is firmly maintained despite being contradicted by what is generally accepted as reality or rational argument, typically a symptom of mental disorder.

words.ex: He told a falsehood to avoid punishment.
words.ex_cn: 他说了一个谎言来避免惩罚。
words.en: A falsehood is a statement that is not true; a lie.

words.ex: He tried to falsify the report.
words.ex_cn: 他试图篡改报告。
words.en: To falsify means to change something in order to deceive people, or to make a false statement.

words.ex: The company made fraudulent claims about its product.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司对其产品做出了欺诈性的声明。
words.en: A fraudulent activity is deceitful or dishonest.

words.ex: The party tried to gerrymander the voting districts.
words.ex_cn: 这个政党试图操纵选区划分。
words.en: To manipulate the boundaries of an electoral constituency so as to favor one party or class.

words.ex: The ad used a cheap gimmick to attract customers.
words.ex_cn: 这个广告用了一个廉价的噱头来吸引顾客。
words.en: A gimmick is a trick or device intended to attract attention, publicity, or trade.

words.ex: He is gullible and believes every story he hears.
words.ex_cn: 他很容易受骗，相信每一个他听到的故事。
words.en: If you describe someone as gullible, you mean they are easily tricked because they are too trusting.

words.tr: n. 传闻；谣传；道听途说
words.ex: He believed the hearsay without checking the facts.
words.ex_cn: 他没有核实事实就相信了这些流言。
words.en: Information received from other people that one cannot adequately substantiate; rumor.

words.tr:
n. 骗局；恶作剧；戏弄
v. 愚弄
words.ex: The news was a hoax to scare people.
words.ex_cn: 这则新闻是个骗局，为了吓唬人。
words.en: A hoax is a plan to deceive someone, such as telling the police there is a bomb somewhere when there is not, or a trick in which someone tells people a lie.

words.ex: He tried to hoodwink her with a fake story.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用一个虚假的故事欺骗她。
words.en: To deceive or trick someone.

words.tr: n. 冒名顶替；冒名欺骗
words.ex: He was caught in an imposture pretending to be a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他冒充医生，结果被揭穿了。
words.en: The act of deceiving others by pretending to be someone else.

words.ex: He tried to inveigle her into lending him money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图哄骗她借钱给他。
words.en: If you inveigle someone into doing something, you cleverly persuade them to do it when they do not really want to.

words.tr:
v. 绑架；劫持；诱拐
n. 绑架罪
words.ex: The man tried to kidnap the little girl.
words.ex_cn: 这个人试图绑架那个小女孩。
words.en: To take someone away illegally by force, typically to obtain a ransom.

words.tr: adj. 撒谎的；不真实的；捏造的
words.ex: She was known for her mendacious stories.
words.ex_cn: 她以编造虚假故事而闻名。
words.en: If someone is mendacious, they are not telling the truth.

words.ex: He prevaricates when asked about the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 当被问到错误时，他回避回答。
words.en: If you prevaricate, you avoid giving a direct answer or making a firm decision.

words.tr:
adj. 据称的；传言的
v. 声称；意指；意味着；“purport”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The purported owner of the car was not the real one.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的所谓主人并不是真正的主人。
words.en: If you say that something purports to be true or to have a particular quality, you mean that it claims to be true or to have that quality, although it may not be.

words.tr:
n. 索具装备；钻探设备；装备
v. 配备索具；操纵；舞弊
words.ex: He uses a rig to hold the camera steady.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个支架来固定相机。
words.en: To rig something means to arrange or set it up in a particular way, often in a temporary or makeshift manner. It can also refer to the equipment used in drilling for oil or gas, or the sails and ropes on a ship.

words.tr:
v. 诈骗；骗取
n. 诈取；骗局
words.ex: He tried to swindle money from old people.
words.ex_cn: 他试图欺骗老人的钱。
words.en: To swindle means to deceive someone in order to get money or possessions from them dishonestly.

words.ex: He resisted the temptation to eat cake.
words.ex_cn: 他抵制了吃蛋糕的诱惑。
words.en: If you feel you want to do something or have something, even though you know you really should avoid it, you can refer to this feeling as temptation.

words.ex: The trickster fooled the old man with a simple lie.
words.ex_cn: 这个骗子用一个简单的谎言愚弄了那位老人。
words.en: A trickster is someone who deceives or cheats people, often in a playful or mischievous way.

words.tr:
v. 骗取；伪造
n. 哄骗
words.ex: She managed to wangle an invitation to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她设法弄到了派对的邀请。
words.en: If you wangle something that you want, you manage to get it by being clever or persuading someone.

words.ex: He tried to wheedle money from his parents.
words.ex_cn: 他试图哄骗父母给他钱。
words.en: If someone wheedles, they try to persuade someone to do or give them something, often by flattery or by being very nice.

words.tr: v. 以网或陷阱捕捉；俘获；诱获；诱捕
words.ex: The hunter used a net to entrap the bird.
words.ex_cn: 猎人用网捕捉了那只鸟。
words.en: To catch someone or something in a trap or to trick someone into doing something they would not normally do.

words.tr: adj. 迷惑的；误导的；虚妄的
words.ex: The promise of quick riches is often delusive.
words.ex_cn: 迅速致富的承诺往往是欺瞒的。
words.en: Something that is delusive gives a false impression or leads you to believe something that is not true.

words.ex: The aliens abduct the man at night.
words.ex_cn: 外星人在晚上绑架了那个男人。
words.en: To take someone away illegally by force or deception; kidnap.

words.tr:
n. 勒索；敲诈
v. 勒索；讹诈
words.ex: He threatened to tell the truth unless she paid him money — that's blackmail.
words.ex_cn: 他威胁说，除非她付钱，否则就说出真相——这就是敲诈。
words.en: Blackmail is the action of threatening to reveal a secret about someone, unless they do something you want, such as give you money.

words.ex: The gang tried to extort money from the shop owner.
words.ex_cn: 这个帮派试图向店主敲诈钱财。
words.en: To extort is to obtain something, especially money, through force, threats, or other unfair means.

words.tr:
n. 弧口凿；半圆凿；凿成的槽（或孔、洞）
v. 凿；挖出；敲竹杠；诈骗
words.ex: He used a gouge to carve the wooden bowl.
words.ex_cn: 他用弧口凿雕刻木碗。
words.en: To gouge means to make a hole or groove in something using a sharp tool or object, or to charge someone too much money for something.

words.ex: He was mulcted for parking illegally.
words.ex_cn: 他因非法停车被罚款。
words.en: To mulct means to fine someone or to defraud them of money.

words.tr:
n. 滥用；虐待；辱骂；
v. 滥用；虐待；辱骂；
words.ex: The abuse of power led to many problems.
words.ex_cn: 权力的滥用导致了许多问题。
words.en: Abuse is the improper usage or treatment of a thing, often to unfairly or improperly gain benefit. Abuse can come in many forms, such as physical or verbal maltreatment, injury, assault, violation, rape, unjust practices, crimes, or other types of aggression.

words.ex: He gave her an abusive shout.
words.ex_cn: 他对她大喊大叫，态度虐待。
words.en: If someone is abusive, they use rude and insulting words or behave violently towards someone else.

words.ex: He execrates lies and dishonesty.
words.ex_cn: 他痛恨谎言和不诚实。
words.en: To express great loathing for; to curse or denounce vehemently.

words.ex: He hurled the ball across the field.
words.ex_cn: 他猛地把球投过球场。
words.en: To throw something with great force; to shout something loudly.

words.ex: He took an oath to tell the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他发誓要说出真相。
words.en: An oath is a formal promise, especially one made in a court of law or a religious ceremony, or a swear word.

words.ex: He swore he didn't steal the money.
words.ex_cn: 他发誓他没有偷钱。
words.en: If someone swears, they use language that is considered to be rude or offensive, usually because they are angry.

words.ex: He was reviled by his opponents for his controversial views.
words.ex_cn: 由于他的有争议的观点，他受到了对手的辱骂。
words.en: To revile someone means to criticize them in an abusive or angrily insulting manner.

words.ex: He vituperates his boss for unfair treatment.
words.ex_cn: 他因为不公平的待遇而痛骂他的老板。
words.en: To criticize or blame someone harshly and angrily.

words.tr: adj. 充满辱骂的；责骂的
words.ex: His vituperative remarks were uncalled for.
words.ex_cn: 他那些责骂的话是多余的。
words.en: If you describe something that is said or written as vituperative, you mean that it is full of bitter criticism or anger.

words.ex: He shouted an expletive when he dropped the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他摔碎玻璃时骂了一句脏话。
words.en: An expletive is a word or phrase that people sometimes say when they are angry or in pain, or to add force to what they are saying, especially when it is not polite.

words.tr: v. 擦伤；挫伤；出现伤痕；
words.ex: He bruised his knee when he fell off the bike.
words.ex_cn: 他从自行车上摔下来时擦伤了膝盖。
words.en: A bruise is a mark that appears on your skin after you have been injured, but the skin is not broken.

words.tr: v. 使关节脱位；使脱臼；使混乱
words.ex: He dislocated his shoulder while playing basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他在打篮球时脱臼了肩膀。
words.en: To dislocate something means to force it out of its proper position or place, especially a bone in a joint.

words.tr: adj. 两败俱伤的；内讧的；互相残杀的
words.ex: The two brothers had an internecine fight over money.
words.ex_cn: 这两兄弟为了钱发生了激烈的内斗。
words.en: If you describe something as internecine, you mean that it involves conflict or struggle within a group or organization.

words.ex: The main reason for his success is hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他成功的主要原因是努力工作。
words.en: The most important part or aspect of something.

words.tr:
n. 痂；疥癣；拒罢工的工人
v. 结疤；当工贼
words.ex: The wound healed and a scab formed.
words.ex_cn: 伤口愈合了，结了痂。
words.en: A scab is a hard, dry covering that forms over a wound or sore as it heals. It can also refer to a person who continues working while others are on strike, often viewed negatively by the strikers.

words.ex: He has a scar on his arm from the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他手臂上有一道事故留下的伤疤。
words.en: A mark left on the skin after a wound or injury has healed, or the act of causing such a mark.

words.tr:
v. 扭伤
n. 扭伤
words.ex: He sprained his ankle while running.
words.ex_cn: 他跑步时扭伤了脚踝。
words.en: If you sprain a joint such as your ankle or wrist, you accidentally damage it by twisting it or bending it violently.

words.ex: The army stopped the incursion at the border.
words.ex_cn: 军队在边境阻止了入侵。
words.en: An incursion is a sudden attack on or invasion of a place.

words.ex: Smoking is detrimental to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is detrimental has a harmful or damaging effect on something else.

words.ex: The accident left him with a serious trauma on his leg.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故使他的腿受了严重的伤。
words.en: A trauma is a very distressing or disturbing experience.

words.ex: He had a contusion on his arm after the fall.
words.ex_cn: 他摔倒后手臂上有了一个挫伤。
words.en: A contusion is a bruise that appears on your skin after an injury.

words.ex: The welt on his arm hurt after the burn.
words.ex_cn: 他手臂上的烧伤疤痕很疼。
words.en: A welt is a raised mark on the skin caused by a blow, especially from a whip or stick.

words.ex: He adulterates milk with water to make more money.
words.ex_cn: 他往牛奶里加水以赚更多钱。
words.en: To make something poorer in quality by adding another substance to it.

words.tr: adj. 真实性可疑的；杜撰的
words.ex: The story about the ghost is apocryphal.
words.ex_cn: 关于鬼魂的故事是不可信的。
words.en: An apocryphal story is one that is probably not true or did not happen, although it is often told and believed by some people to be true.

words.ex: The flowers in the garden are artificial.
words.ex_cn: 花园里的花是人造的。
words.en: Made or produced by human beings rather than occurring naturally, especially as a copy of something natural.

words.ex: The email was bogus and tried to steal my password.
words.ex_cn: 这封邮件是假的，试图窃取我的密码。
words.en: If you describe something as bogus, you mean that it is not genuine, true, or real.

words.ex: He concocted a story to explain his absence.
words.ex_cn: 他编了一个故事来解释他的缺席。
words.en: If you concoct an excuse or explanation, you invent one that is not true.

words.ex: He tried to counterfeit money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图伪造货币。
words.en: Made in exact imitation of something valuable with the intention to deceive or defraud.

words.ex: The store sells ersatz coffee made from chicory.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店出售用菊苣制成的代用咖啡。
words.en: An ersatz product is a substitute for another product, especially one that is not as good as the original.

words.ex: He fabricates excuses to avoid work.
words.ex_cn: 他编造借口来逃避工作。
words.en: To fabricate means to invent or produce something false in order to deceive someone.

words.tr: adj. 人为的；非自然产生的
words.ex: The success of the movie was attributed to factitious marketing strategies.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的成功归因于人为的营销策略。
words.en: If you describe a situation or emotion as factitious, you mean that it has been created or developed deliberately, rather than happening naturally.

words.tr:
v. 伪造；假装；冒充；
adj. 假的；冒充的；伪造的；
words.ex: He faked a signature to get the money.
words.ex_cn: 他伪造了一个签名来拿到钱。
words.en: If something is fake, it is not real, genuine, or true, but is made to appear so.

words.ex: The character is fictitious and does not exist in real life.
words.ex_cn: 这个角色是虚构的，现实中不存在。
words.en: Fictitious means invented and not true or not existing.

words.tr:
n. 锻造车间；
v. 建立（联系等）；
words.ex: The blacksmith works in the forge every morning.
words.ex_cn: 铁匠每天早上都在锻造车间工作。
words.en: To forge something means to create it, especially by using considerable effort or skill. It can also mean to make or produce something, especially with some difficulty or effort. Additionally, it refers to the act of making a copy or imitation of something with the intent to deceive.

words.tr: n. 伪造；伪造罪；伪造物
words.ex: He was arrested for forgery.
words.ex_cn: 他因伪造被逮捕了。
words.en: Forgery is the crime of making or altering a document or signature with the intent to deceive or defraud.

words.ex: Her constant mendacity made it difficult to trust her.
words.ex_cn: 她不断的谎言让人难以信任她。
words.en: The quality of being untruthful; lying.

words.tr:
adj. 假的；冒充的；欺骗的
n. 骗子；伪君子；假货
words.ex: He gave a phony excuse for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他编了一个虚假的借口来解释迟到。
words.en: If you describe something as phony, you disapprove of it because it is false rather than genuine.

words.tr: adj. 似乎合理的；看似真实的；似乎可信的；看似真实的；
words.ex: His excuse sounded plausible.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口听起来似乎合理。
words.en: An explanation or statement that is plausible seems likely to be true or valid.

words.tr:
n. 假象；假冒者；冒牌货
adj. 虚假的
v. 假装
words.ex: The gift was a sham, not real.
words.ex_cn: 这份礼物是假的，不是真的。
words.en: A sham is something that is not what it appears to be and is intended to deceive people.

words.tr: n.  欺骗；作假；使诈；诡计
words.ex: The company was involved in various acts of skullduggery to gain an unfair advantage.
words.ex_cn: 该公司为了获得不公平的优势，参与了各种欺骗行为。
words.en: Underhanded or unscrupulous behavior; trickery.

words.tr: adj. 假的；伪造的；欺骗性的；谬误的
words.ex: The data is spurious and cannot be trusted.
words.ex_cn: 这些数据是虚假的，不可信。
words.en: Something that is spurious seems to be genuine, but is false.

words.tr:
n. （当众）侮辱；冒犯
v. （当众）侮辱；冒犯
words.ex: He felt an affront when they laughed at his idea.
words.ex_cn: 当他们嘲笑他的想法时，他感到受到了冒犯。
words.en: If something is an affront to you, it is an action or remark that insults or offends you.

words.ex: His blasphemous remarks offended many people in the congregation.
words.ex_cn: 他的亵渎神明的言论激怒了教会中的许多人。
words.en: If you describe something as blasphemous, you mean that it is very offensive to people who are religious.

words.ex: They tried to desecrate the holy church.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图亵渎那座神圣的教堂。
words.en: To desecrate something means to spoil or damage something that is considered to be holy or very important.

words.ex: He tried to hector the little boy into giving up his toy.
words.ex_cn: 他试图威吓那个小男孩，让他交出玩具。
words.en: If you say that someone is hectoring you, you do not like the way they are trying to make you do something by bothering you and talking to you aggressively.

words.tr: v. 使屈辱；使丢脸；使蒙羞
words.ex: He tried to humiliate her in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在全班面前羞辱她。
words.en: To humiliate someone means to make them feel ashamed or stupid, especially in front of other people.

words.tr: n. 耻辱；屈辱；名誉受损
words.ex: He faced ignominy after lying to the court.
words.ex_cn: 他在法庭上撒谎后遭到了耻辱。
words.en: Ignominy is a situation or event that causes you to feel ashamed or embarrassed, especially when this is public.

words.ex: He suffered an indignity at the hands of the guards.
words.ex_cn: 他受到了守卫的羞辱。
words.en: An indignity is a situation or event that causes you to feel ashamed or embarrassed because it involves something that is unfair or insulting.

words.tr: n. 屈辱感；窘迫感；坏疽
words.ex: The mortification of his public failure was almost unbearable.
words.ex_cn: 他因公开失败而感到的屈辱几乎难以忍受。
words.en: A feeling of shame, humiliation, or wounded pride.

words.ex: He offended the law by stealing.
words.ex_cn: 他偷窃触犯了法律。
words.en: If you offend someone, you upset or embarrass them by saying or doing something that they think is rude or insulting.

chapters.name: Word List 57 其他 伴随

words.ex: The music accompanies the dance.
words.ex_cn: 音乐伴随舞蹈。
words.en: To go somewhere with someone as a companion or escort; to play a musical accompaniment for.

words.ex: The rain was a concomitant of the storm.
words.ex_cn: 雨水是这场风暴的同时发生的事。
words.en: Something that is concomitant with something else, especially something undesirable, happens at the same time as it or is connected with it.

words.tr:
n. 女监护人
v. 监护
words.ex: A chaperon is often required for young women attending formal events.
words.ex_cn: 年轻女性参加正式活动时通常需要一位年长女伴陪同。
words.en: A chaperon is a person who accompanies and looks after another person or group of people, especially in a social situation.

chapters.name: Word List 57 其他 本质

words.ex: The texture of the bread is soft and fluffy.
words.ex_cn: 这种面包的质地柔软蓬松。
words.en: The feel, appearance, or consistency of a surface or a substance.

words.ex: Honesty is an inherent quality of a good leader.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是好领导固有的品质。
words.en: Existing in something as a permanent, essential, or characteristic attribute.

words.ex: The plasticity of the clay made it ideal for sculpting.
words.ex_cn: 黏土的可塑性使其非常适合雕塑。
words.en: The quality of being easily shaped or molded.

words.ex: His idiosyncrasy is talking to himself while reading.
words.ex_cn: 他的怪癖是读书时自言自语。
words.en: An idiosyncrasy is a peculiar or unusual habit, way of behaving, or feature that someone or something has.

chapters.name: Word List 57 其他 命运

words.ex: She believed that their meeting was kismet.
words.ex_cn: 她相信他们的相遇是天命。
words.en: Kismet is a term used to express the concept of destiny or fate, often implying that events are predetermined.

chapters.name: Word List 57 其他 情感

words.ex: They plant trees to commemorate the fallen soldiers.
words.ex_cn: 他们种树以纪念阵亡的士兵。
words.en: To commemorate an important event or person means to remember them by means of a special action, ceremony, or specially created object.

words.ex: He bought a commemorative coin for the event.
words.ex_cn: 他为这个活动买了一枚纪念币。
words.en: Something that is commemorative is intended to honor or remember someone or something.

words.tr:
adj. 偏远的；久远的；
n. 遥控器；
words.ex: The village is in a remote area far from the city.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄位于远离城市的偏远地区。
words.en: Remote areas are far away from cities and places where most people live, and are therefore difficult to get to.

words.ex: He felt nostalgia when he saw his old toy.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到自己的旧玩具时，感到怀旧。
words.en: A sentimental longing or wistful affection for the past, typically for a period or place with happy personal associations.

words.ex: His sentiment about the new policy is positive.
words.ex_cn: 他对新政策的看法是积极的。
words.en: A sentiment is a thought, opinion, or idea based on a feeling about a situation, or a way of thinking about something.

words.tr: adj. 色情的； 多情的； 爱情的
words.ex: The movie showed amorous scenes that shocked the audience.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了让观众震惊的色情场景。
words.en: If you describe someone's feelings or actions as amorous, you mean that they involve sexual desire.

chapters.name: Word List 57 其他 确定

words.ex: The concept of inerrancy is often debated in theological circles.
words.ex_cn: 无差错的概念在神学界经常被讨论。
words.en: The quality or state of being free from error; infallibility.

words.tr: adj. 不可避免的；必定的；
words.ex: It is inevitable that the sun will rise tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 太阳明天一定会升起。
words.en: If something is inevitable, it is certain to happen and cannot be prevented or avoided.

words.ex: The pope is considered infallible in matters of faith by some Catholics.
words.ex_cn: 一些天主教徒认为教皇在信仰问题上是一贯正确的。
words.en: If a person or thing is infallible, they are never wrong or never fail.

words.ex: He affirm that the plan will work.
words.ex_cn: 他断言这个计划会成功。
words.en: If you affirm that something is true or that something exists, you state firmly and publicly that it is true or that it exists.

words.tr: adj. 确定的； v. 向…保证；“assure”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He was assured that the package would arrive tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他确定包裹明天会到。
words.en: If you are assured of something, you are certain to get it or achieve it.

words.ex: He turned his head to avert the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他转过头去避免了事故。
words.en: If you avert something unpleasant, you prevent it from happening.

words.ex: There is no certainty that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天是否会下雨还没有确定。
words.en: Something that is certain is sure to happen or is definitely true.

words.ex: He spoke with certitude about the answer.
words.ex_cn: 他对于这个答案说话时充满确信。
words.en: A feeling of being certain or convinced about something.

words.tr: adj. 无可置疑的；决定性的；
words.ex: The evidence was conclusive.
words.ex_cn: 证据是无可置疑的。
words.en: If something is conclusive, it means that it proves something in a way that is certain and leaves no doubt.

words.ex: The weather is a determinant of whether we go hiking.
words.ex_cn: 天气是我们是否去远足的决定因素。
words.en: A determinant is a factor which decisively affects the nature or outcome of something.

words.ex: His determination helped him finish the race.
words.ex_cn: 他的决心帮助他完成了比赛。
words.en: Determination is the quality that you show when you have decided to do something and you will not let anything stop you.

words.tr: adj. 自由决定的；酌情行事的；便宜行事的
words.ex: He spent his discretionary money on a new phone.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的可自由支配的钱花在了一部新手机上。
words.en: If something is discretionary, it is available for use as someone chooses, rather than according to a set plan or rule.

words.tr: v. 使根深蒂固；使处于牢固地位；用壕沟围住
words.ex: The habit entrenches itself over time.
words.ex_cn: 这个习惯随着时间的推移变得根深蒂固。
words.en: To establish something very firmly so that it is very difficult to change.

words.ex: There is uncertainty about the weather tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天的天气还不确定。
words.en: Uncertainty is a situation in which something is not known, or something that is not known or certain.

words.tr: adj. 不确定的；不明确的
words.ex: The result is indeterminate.
words.ex_cn: 结果是不确定的。
words.en: If something is indeterminate, you cannot say exactly what it is.

words.ex: He used the sun to orient himself.
words.ex_cn: 他用太阳来确定方向。
words.en: To orient means to align or position something in relation to the points of a compass or other specified positions, or to familiarize someone with a new situation or environment.

words.ex: Her positiveness about the future was contagious.
words.ex_cn: 她对未来的信心具有传染性。
words.en: The quality or state of being positive; assurance, confidence, or certainty.

words.ex: Some people believe that their lives are predestined by fate.
words.ex_cn: 有些人认为他们的生活是由命运预先注定的。
words.en: If you say that something is predestined, you mean that it seems certain to happen, usually because it has been decided by God or by fate.

words.tr: adj. 推定的；假定的；一般认为的
words.ex: The putative father was asked to take a DNA test.
words.ex_cn: 被推定的父亲被要求做DNA测试。
words.en: Generally believed to be or to exist, but not proved to be so.

words.ex: They settled in a small village after retirement.
words.ex_cn: 他们退休后在一个小村庄安顿下来。
words.en: To settle means to resolve or come to an agreement about a dispute, to establish a permanent home in a particular place, or to come to rest in a particular position.

words.tr: adj. 无计谋的；得过且过的；无能的
words.ex: He was lazy and shiftless, never willing to put in the effort.
words.ex_cn: 他很懒惰且无能，从不愿付出努力。
words.en: If you describe someone as shiftless, you mean that they are lazy and have no intention of working hard or improving their life.

words.ex: The jury gave a guilty verdict.
words.ex_cn: 陪审团作出了有罪裁决。
words.en: A verdict is a decision made after a lot of consideration, especially one made by a jury in a court of law.

words.tr: v. 证实；“verify”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The scientist verified the results with a second test.
words.ex_cn: 科学家用第二次实验证实了结果。
words.en: Confirmed as true or accurate by evidence or testimony.

words.ex: He gave her a loud affirmation.
words.ex_cn: 他给了她一个大声的肯定。
words.en: An affirmation is a statement or sign that something is true.

words.ex: The rules give a determinate answer.
words.ex_cn: 这些规则给出了一个明确的答案。
words.en: If something is determinate, it is fixed, definite, and not subject to change.

chapters.name: Word List 57 其他 首尾

words.ex: The book begins with a prefatory note from the author.
words.ex_cn: 这本书以作者的前言开始。
words.en: Serving as an introduction or preface; introductory.

words.ex: His opening gambit was a simple question.
words.ex_cn: 他的开场白是一个简单的问题。
words.en: A gambit is a clever action in a game or other situation that is intended to achieve an advantage and usually involves taking a risk.

words.tr: n. 结尾；总结；冗长乏味的演说
words.ex: The speaker's peroration was filled with grandiose promises.
words.ex_cn: 演讲者的结束语充满了夸张的承诺。
words.en: The concluding part of a speech, typically intended to inspire enthusiasm in the audience.

words.ex: The court followed the precedent set in 1995.
words.ex_cn: 法院遵循了1995年确立的先例。
words.en: A precedent is an action or decision that is used as an example when someone wants to do a similar thing in the future.

words.tr: adj. 原始的；远古的；最初的
words.ex: The primordial soup formed the first life on Earth.
words.ex_cn: 原始汤形成了地球上的最初生命。
words.en: Primordial means existing at or from the beginning of time; primeval.

words.ex: The primacy of the Pope is a significant aspect of the Catholic Church.
words.ex_cn: 教皇的首位是天主教会的一个重要方面。
words.en: The state of being the most important or first in position or rank.

words.tr: adj. 最后部的；在最后面的；“hind”的最高级
words.ex: The hindmost child in the line could not see the stage.
words.ex_cn: 队列最后面的孩子看不到舞台。
words.en: Situated at the very end; farthest back.

chapters.name: Word List 57 其他 屠杀

words.ex: The king was killed in a regicide.
words.ex_cn: 国王在一次弑君事件中被杀。
words.en: The act of killing a king or queen; a person who kills a king or queen.

chapters.name: Word List 57 其他 循环

words.ex: Blood circulates in the body.
words.ex_cn: 血液在体内循环。
words.en: To move or cause to move continuously or freely through a closed system or area.

words.ex: The circulation of blood keeps us alive.
words.ex_cn: 血液的循环让我们活着。
words.en: The movement of something such as money or goods from place to place or from person to person; the number of copies of a newspaper or magazine that are sold.

words.ex: The economy has a cyclical pattern of growth and decline.
words.ex_cn: 经济有增长和衰退的周期性模式。
words.en: Relating to or occurring in cycles; regularly repeated.

words.tr:
adj. 与安息日有关的
n. （大学教师每七年一次的）公休假
words.ex: He took a sabbatical from university to write a book.
words.ex_cn: 他从大学请假一年去写书。
words.en: A sabbatical is a period of paid leave granted to a university teacher or other worker for study or travel, traditionally one year for every seven years worked.

chapters.name: Word List 57 其他 责任

words.ex: He felt an obligation to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他感到有义务帮助他的朋友。
words.en: An obligation is something that you must do because you have promised, because of a law, etc.

words.ex: The onus is on you to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 完成这个项目是你的职责。
words.en: The responsibility for something, especially a duty or task.

words.ex: The manager showed accountability for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 经理对这个错误承担了责任。
words.en: The fact or condition of being accountable; responsibility.

words.ex: It behooves us to be cautious in our decisions.
words.ex_cn: 我们在做决定时理应谨慎。
words.en: If it behooves you to do something, it is right, necessary, or useful for you to do it.

words.tr: adj. 不负责任的；无责任感的；
words.ex: He is irresponsible because he never pays his bills.
words.ex_cn: 他从不付账单，所以是不负责任的。
words.en: If you describe someone as irresponsible, you are criticizing them because they do things without properly considering their possible consequences.

chapters.name: Word List 57 其他 祝福

words.ex: The priest gave a benediction at the end of the service.
words.ex_cn: 牧师在仪式结束时给予了祝福。
words.en: A benediction is a prayer asking for God's blessing, especially one at the end of a religious service.

words.ex: The priest gave his benison to the newlyweds.
words.ex_cn: 牧师为新婚夫妇送上祝福。
words.en: A benison is a blessing or a prayer asking for divine favor and protection.

words.ex: He sent her a card with congratulations.
words.ex_cn: 他给她寄了一张写有祝贺的卡片。
words.en: an expression of pleasure at someone's success or good fortune

chapters.name: Word List 57 其他 其他

words.ex: The advent of smartphones changed how we communicate.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机的到来改变了我们的交流方式。
words.en: The arrival of a notable person, thing, or event.

words.ex: The security guard checked the ID of everyone attempting ingress.
words.ex_cn: 保安检查了每一个试图进入的人的身份证。
words.en: Ingress refers to the act of entering or the means by which one enters.

words.ex: The nomadic family moves with their sheep every season.
words.ex_cn: 这个游牧家庭每季都随着羊群迁移。
words.en: A nomadic way of life is one in which people move from place to place instead of living in one place all the time.

words.tr:
n. 奖赏；奖品；奖金；
v. 珍视；
words.ex: He won a prize for the best science project.
words.ex_cn: 他因最好的科学项目获得了奖赏。
words.en: A prize is something valuable, such as money or a trophy, that is given to someone who wins a competition or who has done outstanding work.

words.ex: The family reduced their monthly expenditure.
words.ex_cn: 这个家庭减少了每月的开支。
words.en: Expenditure is the spending of money on something, or the money that is spent on something.

words.tr: n. 直线；捷径；最短距离
words.ex: The bee made a beeline for the flower.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂径直飞向花朵。
words.en: A direct, straight course or path.

words.ex: He needs time to acclimate to the new climate.
words.ex_cn: 他需要时间来适应新气候。
words.en: When you acclimate or are acclimated to a new situation, place, or climate, you become used to it.

words.ex: The company improved data retention after upgrading its system.
words.ex_cn: 公司在升级系统后提高了数据保留能力。
words.en: The action of retaining something; the continued possession, use, or control of something.

words.ex: He painted a beautiful seascape at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 他在日落时画了一幅美丽的海景画。
words.en: A seascape is a view or picture of the sea.

words.ex: Farmers protect the topsoil to grow healthy crops.
words.ex_cn: 农民保护表土以种植健康的作物。
words.en: Topsoil is the upper layer of soil, usually the top 2 inches (5.1 cm) to 8 inches (20 cm). It has the highest concentration of organic matter and microorganisms and is where most of the Earth's biological soil activity occurs.

words.tr: adj. 未用铅垂线测量的；深不可测的
words.ex: The depths of the ocean remain unplumbed.
words.ex_cn: 海洋的深处仍未经探测。
words.en: If something is unplumbed, it has not been fully explored or understood.

words.ex: He passed the test, albeit with a low score.
words.ex_cn: 他通过了考试，尽管分数很低。
words.en: You use albeit to introduce a fact or comment which reduces the force or significance of what you have just said.

words.ex: He incurred a fine for speeding.
words.ex_cn: 他因超速而招致了一笔罚款。
words.en: If you incur something unpleasant, it happens to you because of something you have done.

words.tr: n. 自由空间；回旋余地
words.ex: The boss gave us some leeway to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 老板给了我们一些余地来完成这个项目。
words.en: Leeway refers to the amount of freedom to move or act that is available.

words.ex: The light output is measured in lumens.
words.ex_cn: 光输出以流明为单位进行测量。
words.en: A unit of luminous flux in the International System of Units, equal to the amount of light emitted per second in a unit solid angle of one steradian by a uniform point source of one candela.

words.tr:
v. 交叠；使部分重叠；
n. 重叠部分；
words.ex: The two colors overlap on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 两种颜色在墙上交叠。
words.en: If one thing overlaps another, or if you overlap them, a part of the first thing occupies the same area as a part of the other thing. You can also say that two things overlap.

words.tr:
adj. 不拘一格的；兼收并蓄的；折中的
n. 折中主义者
words.ex: He has an eclectic taste in music.
words.ex_cn: 他对音乐的品味很广泛多样。
words.en: An eclectic collection or group is a wide range of different things or people.

words.tr: adj. 自我中心的；利己的；
words.ex: He is egocentric and only talks about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他以自我为中心，只谈论自己。
words.en: If you describe someone as egocentric, you mean that they are only concerned with their own needs and desires, and not with those of other people.

words.tr: v. 安顿；安居；安卧；坐落于
words.ex: The baby nestles close to her mother.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿依偎在妈妈身边。
words.en: To settle or lie comfortably within or against something.

words.ex: The car has a streamlined shape to reduce wind resistance.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车具有流线型的外形以减少风阻。
words.en: Designed or arranged to offer the least resistance to fluid flow; made efficient by simplifying or eliminating unnecessary elements.

words.ex: The new manager introduced a high level of regimentation to improve efficiency.
words.ex_cn: 新经理引入了高度的纪律性以提高效率。
words.en: The act of regimenting or the state of being regimented; strict control or organization.
